title: [BDL-UX #237] merge-slot acquire --wait does not wait, and its holder is indistinguishable from its claimant
description:
FOUND IN BDL-068 S4 WAVE 3 by beadloom-0mdo.33, about to commit beside beadloom-67t1 in one working tree. Every launch prompt in this epic and the previous one carries "take `bd merge-slot acquire --wait` before committing and `release` after".

TWO FAILURES, AND THE SECOND MAKES THE FIRST UNFIXABLE FROM HERE.
1. `acquire --wait` returned IMMEDIATELY with "Slot held by v.zoologov, added to waiters queue (position 5)" and exit 0. It queued and returned rather than waiting, so an agent that follows the instruction proceeds to commit exactly as if it held the slot.
2. The holder it named was `v.zoologov`, which is who the caller is. Every role in this repository writes under one tracker identity, so the slot cannot tell the holder from the waiter.

THE STATE FOUND: `bd show beadloom-merge-slot` read `Updated: 2026-09-03` — a hold a day old, belonging to no live agent — with four stale waiters queued from ended sessions (`coordinator`, `agent-viaj-12`, `agent-viaj-13`, `probe`). There was no safe move available to the agent: waiting deadlocks on a stale hold, and `release` would release whatever a live neighbour holds.

THE OBSERVATION TAKEN AFTER THE COMMIT, which is the one that settles it: the slot then read OPEN with no holder at all, `Updated: 2026-09-03` unchanged. So across one wave's commit the primitive was, in order, held by a name indistinguishable from the claimant's, non-blocking on --wait, and empty. NOTHING WAS SERIALISED AT ANY POINT. The commits did not collide because they touched different files — which is the property the slot exists so that nobody has to rely on.

WHY P0 AND WHY IT OUTRANKS ITS OWN SLICE: this is the primitive every concurrent wave in BDL-061, BDL-067 and BDL-068 was told to use. `beadloom waves` decides a wave's shape and hands the landing discipline to this lock; the lock does nothing. Every parallel wave this project has run was serialised by luck and by disjoint file sets. That is not an argument that the waves were wrong — the file sets WERE disjoint, and waves is what made them so — it is an argument that one of the two guarantees was never there.

SAME ROOT AS A FINDING THIS EPIC ALREADY SHIPPED: the review-brief independence report says one tracker identity serves every role. Here that root arrives in a primitive that is supposed to be an exclusive lock. A mutex whose holder is indistinguishable from its claimant is not a mutex, and --wait returning at once means nobody finds that out.

EXPECTED: the slot is held by the BEAD, not by the user — `acquire <bead-id>` — so a holder can be compared against a live claim and a stale hold aged out with its bead's status. `--wait` blocks until the slot is free or a stated timeout expires and SAYS WHICH IT DID; without a timeout it is a poll loop the caller has to write. A hold whose bead is closed is reclaimable. `check` reports how old a hold is, not only who has it.

ROUTED TO S5, the tracker-adapters slice. CONTEXT Q4 governs the fix: an external `bd` finding is answered by deriving OUR OWN call sites, not by wrapping bd. So the deliverable is a derivation of every place this project tells an agent to take the slot, compared against what the slot actually guarantees, with the gap reported — and a decision, stated, about whether this project keeps depending on it.

title: [BDL-068.S3.7][dev] two of this epic's own tests cannot run in the rooms they are about
description:
CI ON PR #60: both locale legs red in ~4.5 minutes, `tests-locale (C)` and `tests-locale (en_US.ISO-8859-1)`. Two failures, both in tests THIS EPIC wrote, both on the environment dimension BDL-061 S2 added and mr2l.42 closed.

REPRODUCED FROM THE JOB LOG, not inferred. The leg runs `LC_ALL=<locale> PYTHONUTF8=0 uv run pytest`.

FAILURE 1 — the fixture cannot exist in the room.
tests/test_review_brief_reachability_derivation.py::TestTheWorkItemChannelIsDerivedFromTheProject::test_a_work_item_key_outside_the_latin_alphabet_is_still_read

    PosixPath('.../features/\u8a2d\u8a08-1')   # a CJK work-item key
    os.mkdir(self, mode)
    UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 102-103

Under LC_ALL=C on Linux the filesystem encoding is ASCII, so the test cannot build the directory its assertion is about. It is not the assertion that fails; it is the arrangement.

THE FIX IS A DESIGN DECISION, not a try/except. The precedent in this repository is tests/test_ci_locale_dimension.py:298, which skips on macOS/Windows and states in the skip WHY the skip can still fail somewhere — 'the CI legs are ubuntu-latest, so it executes on every leg of every PR'. Here the polarity is inverted: a skip would fire ON the locale legs and nowhere else, so the reason has to say that plainly rather than borrow the other's wording. Whatever is chosen, the case must remain capable of failing somewhere, and where that is must be written in the skip.

FAILURE 2 — the scenario cannot run in the room it describes.
tests/acceptance/steps/test_verdict_room_steps.py:86 skips with: 'this scenario needs a run outside the declared leg; on Linux the run may be inside it, which is the state the scenario contrasts with'. tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py::TestTheScenariosExecute::test_the_shipped_acceptance_suite_runs_every_scenario_and_skips_none then fails, because the shipped acceptance suite is required to skip nothing.

So the scenario 'a run names the declared rooms it did not enter' is unsatisfiable on the legs it is about: locally the run is in 0 of 21 rooms and the contrast holds; on a CI leg the run IS in one of them and the scenario steps aside.

THE BETTER FIX, and it is not a skip: the claim does not depend on the count being 21. A verdict names the rooms it did not enter whether that number is 21 or 20, and 'entered 1 of 21' is the SAME assertion with a different arithmetic. Rewrite the scenario so it holds in both states rather than contrasting one against the other — a scenario that only runs where the feature is least exercised is the shape this epic exists to remove.

WHY THIS WAS NOT CAUGHT LOCALLY, and it is the epic's own lesson a fourth time: the coordinator ran the new modules under LC_ALL=C on macOS and got 98 passed. CPython forces a UTF-8 filesystem encoding on macOS, so LC_ALL=C does not reproduce the Linux room at all. Every local measurement of this branch was taken in 0 of the 21 declared rooms, which `beadloom rooms` now says out loud — and the thing it says was true while the suite was being written.

DO NOT weaken tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py to allow a skip. That test is the reason both of these are visible.

Baseline: 8433 passed on the tree at fbc5936, `beadloom ci` rc 0, macOS — 0 of 21 rooms. The legs that matter cannot be entered from here; verify by reasoning about the room and say which measurement you could not take.

title: [BDL-068.S2.5][dev] the brief crashes on a malformed flow.yml, and its bead-comment line is misleading on a review bead
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-0mdo.20 — MAJOR 3 (blocks) and MAJOR 1 part (a) (same cycle, one sentence).

MAJOR 3 BLOCKS, in the reviewer's own words: 'a crash in the command the whole review protocol depends on, the fix is moving one call inside a guard that already exists, and the strict xfail flips the moment it lands.'

reachability.py:136-137, inside prompts_naming_documents: doc_flow_config(project_root) is resolved OUTSIDE the `except FlowConfigError` guard that _composed_prompts already puts around compose(). REPRODUCED: with .beadloom/flow.yml holding `architecture: [unclosed`, reachability_of(...) raises FlowConfigError and nothing between it and the console script catches it — services/commands/_root.py installs no handler — so a malformed config gives the user a TRACEBACK instead of a message and review-brief produces NO BRIEF AT ALL.

That violates the module's own stated rule: a prompt that will not compose contributes nothing and is not an error here. And the suite already carries the finding as a STRICT XFAIL (tests/test_review_brief_reachability_derivation.py:497, FINDING BDL-068.19-1) — so the suite is green over a shipped crash. beadloom-0mdo.19 reported it and correctly did not repair it from a test bead.

FIX: resolve the config inside the guard and report 'NOT INSPECTED — the project's flow.yml will not parse, so no prompt could be composed', which is the shape every other absence in this module already takes. Then DROP the xfail — it flips the moment the fix lands, which is the check that the fix is real.

MAJOR 1 PART (a) — one sentence, same cycle. reachability.py:148 renders 'bead comments: 0 item(s) — withheld by this command'. The channel is scoped to the bead the brief is for, which under this project's wave structure is a REVIEW bead and by construction carries no author account. The account of the change under review sits on the beads that made it: beadloom-0mdo.18 (6 comments, 14,784 characters) and beadloom-0mdo.19 (5 comments, 16,760 characters), measured by counting and never by reading. Nothing withholds either and the report names neither.

models.py:170 asserts 'a reviewer that sees 0 withheld learns the author wrote nothing'. ON THAT RUN THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE BY 31,544 CHARACTERS.

FIX (a) ONLY: name in the statement WHICH bead was counted and that other beads are not. Parts (b) and (c) — a channel for the tracker export, and counting the slice's sibling beads — are a widening of the report and are filed separately as BDL-UX #229.

MINOR, at your discretion: WithheldNotes is still populated (assembly.py:181) and printed by nothing in the BEFORE half, while --release still prints 'WITHHELD — N author comment(s) stay withheld' and withheld_count in JSON. One command now speaks two vocabularies across its two halves. The --json break is declared at RFC.md:165 and is decided, not an oversight.

title: [BDL-068.S3.5][tech-writer] S3 docs — the mutation scope, and what a verdict says about its room
description:
Refresh the docs for the mutation-scope and ci-gate surfaces. Drive from beadloom sync-check --json.

Two constraints: do not write that mutation testing is required of an adopter — what ships is the scope and the report, not the runner, and tool-agnosticism is the stated reason. And do not write that a room-naming verdict is a stronger verdict; it is the same verdict, answerable.

refs: mutation-scope, ci-gate
notes:
ROUTED FROM THE S3 REVIEW (beadloom-0mdo.25, MAJOR 2), discharged here with no dev cycle as the reviewer expected:

- docs/services/cli.md does not carry the two commands this slice registered — `beadloom mutation` and `beadloom rooms`. This is the same omission the S1 review found for `impact` and `scope-check`, in the same file, one slice later.

Write what each command ANSWERS and what it does not. In particular: `beadloom mutation` does not run a mutation tool — it reads the counters a run wrote, by name, and reports a counter it did not find rather than reading it as zero. And `beadloom rooms` derives the room census from ci.yml and pyproject rather than from a list, which is why a leg added later is covered by the same act.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 2 major

Slice S3 (`beadloom-0mdo.22`, `.23`, `.24`), reviewed on `features/BDL-068-S2S3` at `29578e9`
against `main`. Neither Major is a merge blocker: no code defect, nothing red, and the fix for
both is text. See "What should block and what should be filed" below.

## The question this bead was asked

**Can a reader of this repository tell a mutation check that RAN from a sentence claiming one,
without reading a bead comment? For the repository, yes. For the ROLE that carries the duty, no
— and that is Major 1.**

What now exists and is reachable without a tracker: `beadloom mutation` refuses to turn an
absence into a number; `.github/workflows/mutation.yml` runs the score under a `--min-score`
floor nightly and uploads the counters; `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.mutmut]` block carries the
scope, the pool derivation and the rooms in which each was measured. I ran the command myself
(room named below): it exits 1 on this repository today with three `mutation-target-unmeasured`
warnings, one per declared target, because no run's counters were handed to it — which is the
answer BDL-061 S4 could not produce for two majors.

The half I judge missing is the loop back into the role. `roles/core/test.md.txt:51-53` still
reads "Record the tool, the target and the surviving count in the bead comment", and the string
`beadloom mutation` appears in no role file — not in the core, not in the composed
`.claude/agents/test.md`, not in the vendored `agentic_flow/agents/test.md.txt`. The same commit
range added `_rooms.md.txt` and pointed every role at `beadloom rooms`, so the wiring pattern was
available and was used one duty over.

## Is the room reporting DERIVED or LISTED? Derived, and I checked it two ways.

`application/rooms.py` reads the `Programming Language :: Python :: X.Y` classifiers and every
job of every `.github/workflows/*.y*ml`, expands each matrix, and owns no room list — only a
runner-label vocabulary (`ubuntu`/`macos`/`windows`), where a label outside it resolves to NOT
ENTERED with its reason rather than to a match.

1. Derived by construction: `tests/test_verdict_room_derivation.py` synthesizes packaging and
   workflow files in `tmp_path` and asserts the report follows. A pinned list cannot pass it.
2. Derived by observation, which is the stronger evidence: `beadloom rooms` reported **21
   declared rooms across five workflow files** on this branch, and one of them is
   `.github/workflows/mutation.yml: mutation` — the leg this very slice added. It appeared in
   the census with no edit to the census's own code, which is exactly the property
   `DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` lacks and has lacked three times.

What `beadloom rooms` told me about my own run: **0 of the 21 declared rooms entered**, with the
dimension that decided each one named — `os` for every Ubuntu leg, `locale` additionally for the
two `tests-locale` legs, and `self-hosted+ai-techwriter` reported as unresolved rather than
skipped. Four supported interpreters, each with a leg. That matches the figures the
`verdict-room` DOC states it measured on 2026-09-03, so that document's claim is verified rather
than quoted.

## What I measured, and in which room

Every measurement below was taken on **Darwin arm64, CPython 3.13.7, 10 cores** — a room that
enters none of this project's 21 declared rooms. Nothing here is a claim about any CI leg.

- **Green in a clean room over 8 117 files** (`git archive HEAD`, so S3 alone without the S2
  work in the tree): 8 399 passed, 29 skipped, 2 xfailed, 1 failed, 233.84 s. The single failure
  is `tests/test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh`
  and it is a property of my room, not of the change: `git archive` extracts no `.git`, and
  `doc_sync/engine.py:406` states that a pair whose only baseline is the indexed tree asks git
  instead and is `unverified` "when git cannot answer". I reindexed the clean room (94 nodes,
  498 edges, 308 docs) and it stayed `unverified`, which is the documented behaviour.
- **Green on the tree**: 8 418 passed, 11 skipped, 2 xfailed, 256.20 s. The tree also carries
  `beadloom-0mdo.28`'s uncommitted `review_brief` edits, so this figure is not S3 alone. I am
  not the wave's combined-tree gate owner and make no claim about the combined tree.
- `ruff check src/ tests/` clean; `mypy --strict src/` Success over 255 files on **each of
  3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13** — run through `for v in $(beadloom rooms --dimension python)`,
  which is the loop the Python overlay now ships, so the version set was derived and not typed.
  This varies the TARGET version only; the interpreter the checker runs under is still one.
- `beadloom sync-check` rc 0, `beadloom lint --strict` rc 0, `beadloom doctor` rc 0,
  `beadloom diff --since main` shows `+ verdict-room (component)`, `mutation-scope` re-pointed at
  the new package, and three new edges. Every new module carries its `# beadloom:` annotation.

**Sabotage: four probes in the clean room, all four caught.** I did not take the assertions on
trust, because this epic exists because a bead once reported 20 red assertions that were eleven
guards which could not fail.

Each probe was applied ALONE to its own extraction of HEAD and run over the same 89 tests of the
seven S3 test files, so the counts below are per-probe and measured, not apportioned.

| Removed from the clean-room copy | Red |
|---|---|
| the `check_mutation_scope` fold in `report_mutation_score` (the phantom gate) | 10 |
| `lines.extend(_gate_room_lines(result))` in the `ci` renderer | 5 |
| `click.echo(f"Room: {room}")` in the `mutation` renderer | 2 |
| the `value >= 0` guard in `_counter`, so `killed: -5` is read | 3 |

Behaviour, boundaries, typing, error handling and security read clean: `application` does not
import `services`, the workflow YAML goes through `yaml.safe_load` inside a named `except`, the
packaging metadata is read by regex with the reason stated (a TOML parse would answer
differently on 3.10 than on 3.13, which is a room-dependent answer from the module whose subject
is rooms), no `Any`, no `type: ignore`, no shell-out, no secret. The acceptance scenarios are
observable in the user's vocabulary, and one of them ("a version added to the workflow is
reported without the tool being changed") is an anti-vacuity step that edits the declaration and
re-derives.

## Major 1 — the shipped role still routes the mutation result to prose

**File:** `src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/roles/core/test.md.txt:51-53`, and identically the
two composed copies `.claude/agents/test.md:51-53` and
`src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/agentic_flow/agents/test.md.txt:51-53`.
**Severity:** Major.
**Issue:** the mutation duty is the reason this slice exists, and the sentence that carries it is
unchanged from the release that had no instrument: "Record the tool, the target and the surviving
count in the bead comment". No role file names `beadloom mutation` (verified by grep over
`src/`, `.claude/` and the vendored templates). An agent following the composed protocol produces
the prose that BDL-067 produced four times, while the command that would have produced a checkable
report ships in the same commit range. The slice fixed this shape for rooms and not for mutation.
**Recommendation:** one bullet in `roles/core/test.md.txt`, then recompose the adapters:

    - **Report the run, do not describe it.** `beadloom mutation --stats <counters.json>
      --target <path> [--only <path>] [--min-score <fraction>]` reads whatever counters your
      runner wrote and reports a missing counter rather than reading it as zero. Paste its
      report into the checkpoint; a sentence about a mutation run is not one.

`beadloom-0mdo.27` ([BDL-068.S4.x][dev], open) is the general form of this check — a duty
declared for a role is carried by that role's composed core. It is a fair home for the derived
test; the one-bullet edit does not need to wait for it.

## Major 2 — the CLI reference does not carry the two commands this slice registered

**File:** `docs/services/cli.md` (42 `### beadloom <command>` sections; none for `mutation` or
`rooms`), and `docs/services/cli.md:1405` (`### beadloom ci`).
**Severity:** Major (doc freshness), **and it is owned by an open bead in this slice.**
**Issue:** derived from the brief's inventory rather than from a note — `services/commands/
mutation.py` and `services/commands/rooms.py` register two user-facing commands with exit-code
contracts (`mutation`: 0/1/2; `rooms`: 0/2) documented only in module docstrings, and the
`beadloom ci` section still describes a verdict with no room block although all three formats now
print one. `beadloom sync-check` reports `[warn] docs/services/cli.md (surface drift:
watches=cli,graph,flow.yml)` and `declared surface grew: 367 → 413 pair(s), 86 → 95 declared
doc(s)`, at rc 0. The domain-level docs ARE current: `application/README.md:63` names
`take_census` and the derivation, `components/verdict-room/DOC.md` is new and its measured
figures reproduce, `components/mutation-scope/DOC.md` and `features/ci-gate/SPEC.md` carry the
new halves. The gap is the shipped CLI reference only.
**Recommendation:** hand this to `beadloom-0mdo.26` ([BDL-068.S3.5][tech-writer], open), which is
titled for exactly this work: add `### beadloom mutation` and `### beadloom rooms` with their
exit codes, extend `### beadloom ci` with the room block in rich/json/github, then re-record the
surface. No dev fix cycle is required for this one.

## Minor

1. `tests/test_mutation_ci_job.py` (`test_the_job_stays_answerable_only_for_the_slice_it_ran`)
   pins the workflow's scope by spelling — `assert "--only src/beadloom/graph/rules/" in
   _steps_text()` — while its sibling `tests/test_mutation_runner_scope.py` DERIVES the agreement
   between the other two homes (`flow.yml mutation.targets` and `[tool.mutmut].only_mutate`). The
   workflow is the third home for one scope. It fails in the safe direction, so this is Minor:
   derive the workflow's `--target`/`--only` from `only_mutate` and the assertion covers a spelling
   nobody has thought of yet.
2. `src/beadloom/application/rooms.py:_matrix_of` reports an unquoted float matrix value as
   unresolved but `str()`s a mapping or list item into a dimension value, so a matrix of
   `include`-style dicts written directly under an axis becomes a room whose value is a dict repr.
   Treat a non-scalar item the way `include`/`exclude` are treated: unresolved, with its reason.
3. Nothing yet compares the derived room census against
   `onboarding/branch_protection.DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS`, which is still a hand-written
   tuple and is the drift this epic's motivation section cites. S3 was not asked for it; it is the
   obvious next instrument and belongs in a bead rather than in this slice.

## Nitpick

`MutationRun.room` is set from `describe_room()` and never read: `_render` and `_payload` take the
same string as a parameter. One home or the other.

## What should block and what should be filed

**Nothing here blocks.** S3's deliverable — the score half of `mutation-scope`, the derived room
census, the nightly job — is complete, green in the room named above, and its checks are
falsifiable under sabotage. Major 2 is discharged by `beadloom-0mdo.26` as already planned, with
no dev cycle. Major 1 is one bullet in one template plus a recomposition, and it is the one thing
I would not close S3 without, because leaving it turns the slice into the same defect one layer
up: an instrument that exists and a role that is not told to use it.

## Two facts about this review that only I can report

**The withholding was partly defeated before I ran, by the launch prompt rather than by the
author.** Three things reached me that I did not derive: that this branch's work-item channel is
blind and is filed as BDL-UX #230 (the brief reports the channel as NOT INSPECTED; the diagnosis
and the issue number came from the coordinator); that `beadloom rooms` reports declared rooms and
**"a local run is in none of them"**, which is a directed hint at a measurement I then made
independently and found to be 0 of 21; and the BDL-067 anecdote about eleven guards that cannot
fail, which is also written verbatim in `mutation_scope/__init__.py`, so it converged me on
nothing the change does not say itself. The second one is the one to notice: I was told the answer
before I took the measurement. Nothing in the process counts a hint of that shape.

**`bd comments` was not read before this verdict was recorded**, per the protocol; `--release`
follows. I expect it to exit 1 on the attribution check, because every role on this tracker writes
under one identity — that is the normal answer here and not a defect.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:

as written above: 0 critical, 2 major. What changed is which two.

`--release` exited **1** with "the tracker named no author for the verdict comment, so this gate
could not tell whether the account was released by its own author". Every role on this tracker
writes under one identity, so that is the expected answer here and is reported rather than filed.

All three authors reported `docs/services/cli.md` before I did and handed it to

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — audited before adding, and the first half is a real hole with five confirmed cases.

READ: the bead, CONTEXT (incl. the 2026-09-03 Q3 row), RFC S3, all of .22's eight comments and .23's seven, score.py, scope.py, rooms.py, commands/mutation.py, commands/federation.py's three gate renderers, mcp_server.py's _verdict_room, and the names of all 98 tests the two dev beads shipped across nine files.

WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED, so I do not duplicate it. The ROOM half is close to complete: derivation from classifiers and workflows including 'a leg added to the matrix is reported without the tool changing' (18 tests), the census and its one matching rule (14), the command (11), the Gate's three shapes plus the not-a-stronger-verdict invariant (11), the shared role layer (16), and the MCP complete_bead PASS and FAIL payloads — which I expected to be the gap and is not, it is tests/test_gate_verdict_room.py::TestTheRefusingGateAlsoNamesItsRoom. I will add to that half only where the population is PINNED rather than derived.

THE MUTATION HALF HAS THE HOLE THE BEAD NAMES, and it is larger than one case. 'beadloom mutation' never asks the scope check anything: report_mutation_score reads flow.yml's targets and the run's counters and nothing else, so scope.py's three findings — which config-check and the Gate do surface — are invisible to the command that produces the NUMBER. Measured, not reasoned, with the shipped console script over five temporary projects:
 - a declared target NOT ON DISK, run claims it: 'Score: 100.0% of 10 scored mutants', rc 0.
 - a target OUTSIDE the configured source paths: 100.0%, rc 0.
 - a target inside them holding NO source file — the bead's own sentence: 100.0%, rc 0.
 - a run that classified nothing (killed 0, survived 0, mutants 10): 'Score: none — see the findings below.' and there are no findings below. rc 0. A dangling sentence and a clean exit.
 - a negative counter (killed -5, survived 1): 'Score: 125.0% of -4 scored mutants', rc 0.
Five phantom gates, each of which reads exactly like a check that passed.

NEXT: red tests for all five, then the smallest instrument change that makes each a finding, then the derived-population half for the room verdict.

description:
S3's second half, and it now covers three filed findings rather than two.

THE CLASS, measured three times and filed as BDL-UX #227: a claim true of the room it was measured in, read as a claim about the product.
 - BDL-067 reported 'green on the tree' NINE times. All nine ran on macOS; the CI legs are Ubuntu, and the tenth measurement was red on six of them — a path hard-wrapped mid-token at a width only the runner's path length produces.

AND THE THIRD ROOM, BDL-UX #181: clean-room verification is correct and structurally cannot see a cross-bead interaction. Four agents once each reported green on a tree that was red, and none of them was wrong.

REQUIRED:
 - the completion checklist names ROOMS, not only commands. `uv run mypy src/` is not a claim until it says which interpreter; the four-version form takes seconds and was measured while filing #227.
 - a Gate verdict carries the room it was taken in, so 'green' is answerable rather than atmospheric.
 - the clean-room limit is stated where a clean-room claim is made, rather than remembered.

DERIVE, DO NOT LIST: the versions the project supports are declared in pyproject; the CI legs are declared in ci.yml. A hand-written room list is the shape this epic removes, and it goes stale the first time a leg is added — which happened three times to DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS already.

THE DERIVATION, chosen before any code: interpreters from pyproject and legs from the workflows, so a leg added later is covered by the same act. requires-python gives a FLOOR only — enumerating '>=3.10' upward would need a hardcoded newest-Python, which is the stale list this epic removes — and the enumerated set comes from the 'Programming Language :: Python :: X.Y' classifiers, with the floor reported alone when there are none. THE MATCHING RULE, one rule so it can be tested: a run ENTERS a declared leg only when every dimension of that leg is comparable and equal. A label the vocabulary does not recognise (self-hosted) or a dimension the current room cannot describe (locale) makes the leg NOT ENTERED and goes in the unresolved population — never a silent match. Conservative in the direction that cannot manufacture coverage.

AND THE CONSTRAINT I AM HOLDING MYSELF TO: naming the room must not change a single verdict. Same rc, same findings, same status — a test asserts it on a passing AND a failing gate.

title: [BDL-068.S3.1][dev] mutmut over graph/rules/, and the score produced by a command rather than asserted in a comment
description:
S3's first half. BDL-061 S4 put a mutation-testing DUTY into every composed role core on the stated ground that owning a runner would break tool-agnosticism. The convention shipped and the enforcement did not: four beads in BDL-067 reported 'mutation checking' by four different hand methods, every result prose in a bead comment, and one of them — sent to audit another — found a reported 'all 20 assertions red before the fix' was ELEVEN GUARDS THAT CANNOT FAIL.

TOOL DECIDED (ROADMAP, researched 2026-09-01): mutmut. The deciding property is per-mutant test selection from coverage. cosmic-ray runs the configured test-command for every mutant and answers cost with horizontal distribution, which this project declined once already when beadloom-mr2l.64 withdrew tests-windows over runner minutes.

FIRST SCOPE: graph/rules/ ONLY — eleven modules, the rule evaluation and liveness logic, ~4465 code lines. It is where a false green costs most: if evaluators.py lets a violation through, the whole Gate is theatre. Deterministic branch-and-comparison code, which is what the standard operator set is strongest against.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: services/, tui/, ai_agents/, infrastructure/, and message-rendering code anywhere. BDL-067 found four defects in user-facing message text and mutation would have caught none of them, because one string substituted for another is equivalent almost always.

TOOL-AGNOSTICISM: mutmut is THIS repository's dev dependency. What ships to an adopter is the SCOPE and the REPORT, not a required runner.

Q3 IS OPEN WITH ITS DECISION RULE STATED (CONTEXT.md): the job runs per PR if it fits under the budget that withdrew tests-windows (~16-28 runner-minutes), and nightly otherwise. MEASURE THE COST BEFORE ADDING THE JOB. A cost decision taken before the cost is measured is the kind of claim this project rejects from everyone else.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — read before writing.

Claimed. Read: bead, CONTEXT (Q3 + its decision rule), RFC S3 + the Changes table, PRD US-4, ROADMAP's mutation P0 (the tool research), and the tests-windows withdrawal block in ci.yml, which is the budget this must fit under: a windows leg was ~16-28 runner-minutes per PR against ~8 for both locale rows together, and it would have become the pipeline's critical path against ~4 min ubuntu legs. Both halves of that -- runner-minutes AND wall-clock critical path -- are the comparison, not just the minutes.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this bead does not rebuild it: 'src/beadloom/application/mutation_scope.py' (BDL-061 S4b) checks a DECLARED target lies inside scan_paths and holds mutable source, wired into config-check + the Gate. '.beadloom/flow.yml' already declares three targets, one of which is 'src/beadloom/graph/rules/'. So the SCOPE half shipped. What did not ship is any score: a declared target that exists and holds .py files produces no finding and no number, which is exactly 'a claimed mutation check indistinguishable from a performed one' (PRD US-4).

mutmut 3.7.0 installed and its config surface read from source rather than from its README: source_paths / only_mutate / do_not_mutate (fnmatch globs, .py or * only) / pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection / mutate_only_covered_lines. It has 'export-cicd-stats', which writes mutants/mutmut-cicd-stats.json with killed/survived/total/no_tests/skipped/suspicious/timeout/segfault -- whole-run, NOT per target. That matters for the design: the per-target attribution this repo needs is not something the runner gives, which is the second reason the report format cannot just be the runner's file.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 2 — the product half, TDD, green.

'mutation_scope.py' became a package by 'git mv' (history preserved), split by responsibility, not by size: 'scope.py' answers COULD this declared target run a mutant, 'score.py' answers what a run over it DID. Public import path unchanged -- 'from beadloom.application.mutation_scope import check_mutation_scope' still resolves through the package __init__, which is what keeps the eight existing call sites and the BDL-061 steps file untouched.

RED FIRST, and verified red rather than declared: tests/test_mutation_score.py (11) and tests/test_mutation_command.py (10) were written against an API that did not exist and failed at collection; the four scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/mutation_score.feature were then verified red by BLINDING the detector (report_mutation_score returns no findings and no score) -- all four fail, so no scenario passes because of its own arrangement.

THREE DESIGN RULES, each with the failure it prevents:
 - A MISSING COUNTER IS NOT ZERO. A run whose stats omit 'killed' scores nothing and is reported; read as zero it would score '0%', and a NUMBER is what gets pasted into a bead comment. Same rule for a non-integer and for a stats file that is absent or is not a JSON object.
 - TIMEOUTS COUNT AS KILLED, MUTANTS NO TEST COVERS DO NOT. A mutant that hung was detected; a mutant nothing executes was not, and leaving that class out of the denominator is exactly how a slice with no tests scores 100%. The test bites on both halves: 6 killed + 2 timeout + 1 survived + 1 no_tests is 80%, where excluding timeouts gives 60% and excluding no_tests gives 88.9%.
 - A RUN THAT DOES NOT SAY WHAT IT COVERED IS NOT A RUN. '--stats' without '--target' exits 2 rather than assuming the run covered everything declared -- assuming it is how a run over one module reports a score for a scope it never entered. And a floor declared against a score that does not exist is MISSED, not passed.

The counter vocabulary is NAMES, not a tool: killed/survived required, timeout/no_tests/skipped/suspicious optional, and 'total' accepted as the second spelling of 'mutants' because that is what mutmut writes. Nothing in src/ imports mutmut.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 3 — the runner configured, and the first two hard numbers.

MUTANTS OVER graph/rules/: 3989, counted from the eleven .meta files mutmut generated, not estimated. ROADMAP predicted 'order 2 000-4 000' from 4 465 code lines; the prediction holds. Distribution is lopsided and worth recording, because it is what a first slice can be narrowed to if the cost decision needs it: loader.py 1248, evaluators.py 1002, scenario_coverage.py 438, liveness.py 311, doc_area.py 253, summary_facts.py 168, __init__.py 153, exemptions.py 136, cycles.py 127, attribution.py 99, types.py 54.

THE TEST POOL IS THE WHOLE SUITE, and that is a decision with a cost. mutmut selects each mutant's tests from coverage, so I first derived the pool honestly: a full run under coverage CONTEXTS (379 s, 8195 passed) says 73 test files execute graph/rules/. Configuring those 73 as the pool would have been faster and would have been an AUTHORED LIST that goes stale the first time a killer test moves -- the shape this epic exists to remove. The failure direction is the tiebreaker: a killer outside the pool inflates SURVIVORS, so a stale list under-claims rather than over-claims, but it under-claims INVISIBLY. Whole suite, and pay the stats run.

WHAT THAT COST TO MAKE TRUE: mutmut copies source+tests into mutants/ and runs there, so this project's meta-tests -- the ones reading ci.yml, the graph, the shipped documents -- fail in the copy. MEASURED in the copied room over the 73-file pool: 77 failures and 12 errors before, 2 after copying .beadloom/.claude/.github/docs/ci-templates and the root documents through 'also_copy'. The remaining 2 are the sync-check pair tests, which were failing on the LIVE tree at the time for the ordinary reason (my own uncommitted source edits ahead of the doc updates) and are green now that the pairs are attested.

Product side green and the tree is sync-clean: reindex + sync-check rc 0, lint --strict rc 0. comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 4 — the pool is a room decision, and one real defect the room found.

THE POOL EXCLUDES ONE FILE IT DERIVED, for a structural reason worth stating: tests/test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py runs sync-check over the tree it is in, and in mutants/ that tree is a MUTATED copy -- every rules module has a different hash, so its pairs are stale BY CONSTRUCTION and it can never pass there. The whole suite was tried in that room first and does not fit it either: 14 failures and 7 errors, and the irreducible ones are the same class (meta-tests that lint the shipped package, which is mutated, and ones that walk git history, of which there is none in the copy). That is a real limitation of mutation testing a project whose tests read its own tree, and it is now written into pyproject beside the pool rather than remembered.

THE ROOM FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN TESTS, which is the argument for running there at all: tests/test_cli_json_streams.py caught tests/test_mutation_command.py and the new steps file parsing JSON out of 'result.output' -- the stream Click merges stderr into. Fixed to 'result.stdout' in both. It was red on the live tree too; the pool run is where I looked.

--only, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS TWO ANSWERS ARE BOTH WRONG. flow.yml declares three targets and this slice measures one (the bead says graph/rules/ ONLY). Reporting the other two as findings makes the CI job permanently red, which is how a check stops being read. Dropping them from 'mutation.targets' deletes a duty to make my own job green, which is the move this project calls gaming when a size limit is dodged by reclassification. The third answer is the one used everywhere else here: judge what the run is answerable for, and NAME what was not judged. 'beadloom mutation --only src/beadloom/graph/rules/' prints 'Not judged by this run: doc_quality.py, doc_shape.py' in both shapes, and BDL-061's declaration is untouched.

Six more tests, one more scenario, all verified red first -- the slice scenario by blinding 'only' so every declared target is judged, which reddens exactly that scenario and no other.

Gate-relevant: ruff, mypy --strict, reindex, sync-check, lint --strict all green on the tree as it stands. The mutmut stats phase is running now; no cost number yet.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 5 — THE COST IS MEASURED, AND IT DECIDES Q3.

THE RUN COMPLETED. 3 989 mutants over src/beadloom/graph/rules/, 54 min 55 s wall clock, 1.42 mutations/second, with 6 workers. ROOM: Darwin arm64, CPython 3.13.7, 10 cores -- a local Apple-silicon machine, NOT a CI runner, and the distinction is the whole point of naming it.

THE SCORE, produced by the command and not by me: 96.2%. killed 3 836, timeout 1, survived 152, no_tests 0, skipped 0, suspicious 0, segfault 0. Reproduce with:
  uv run mutmut run --max-children 6 && uv run mutmut export-cicd-stats
  beadloom mutation --stats mutants/mutmut-cicd-stats.json --target src/beadloom/graph/rules/ --only src/beadloom/graph/rules/ --tool 'mutmut 3.7.0'
Note 'no_tests 0': every one of the 3 989 mutants had at least one covering test in the pool. That is the counter that would have exposed a badly-derived pool, and it is clean.

Q3 IS ANSWERED: NIGHTLY, and the number answered it rather than a preference. The budget that withdrew tests-windows was ~16-28 runner-minutes per PR (against ~8 for both locale rows together). 55 minutes is two to three times that -- and this machine is FASTER than ubuntu-latest (4 vCPU), so the CI figure can only be worse, which means the decision does not depend on a measurement I have not taken. The second half of the tests-windows reasoning bites harder here than it did there: the ubuntu legs finish in ~4 minutes, so a leg of this length is not a cost so much as the pipeline's entire critical path.

.github/workflows/mutation.yml: scheduled 03:17 UTC + workflow_dispatch, ubuntu-latest, timeout 180. It reindexes first (mutmut copies .beadloom/ into mutants/, and the index db is gitignored -- without it the pool fails in the copied room and the run aborts at stats rather than scoring anything). 'mutmut run || true' because mutmut exits non-zero whenever a mutant survives, which every suite does; the verdict is 'beadloom mutation --min-score 0.95', set just under the measured 96.2% so a real regression trips it and a handful of new survivors in a legitimately changed rule does not.

THE LOCKOUT IS GUARDED. A scheduled workflow produces NO check-run on a pull request, so requiring its context under strict:true makes main unmergeable -- the same trap DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS documents for the withdrawn Windows leg. tests/test_mutation_ci_job.py (10 tests) fails if the job name ever enters that tuple, if the floor is dropped, if --only is dropped, or if any OTHER workflow starts installing the runner. Both load-bearing assertions verified red by making the change they forbid.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing in that workflow has executed on a GitHub runner. Pool, room and score are all one macOS machine; the first scheduled run is the verification, and the workflow says so in its own header rather than leaving it to be inferred.

title: [BDL-068.S2.1][dev] review-brief reports what is REACHABLE, not what it happened to withhold
description:
S2's whole slice in one change. Covers BDL-UX #204, #212 and #219 (beadloom-tm76).

TODAY: review-brief counts bead comments and prints '0 withheld'. That is true of bead comments and false about the question its reader is asking, which is 'what can this reviewer reach'.

THREE MEASURED DEFEATS OF THE SAME MECHANISM, every one found only because a reviewer declared it unprompted — nothing in the tooling could report any of them:
 - #212: the author's account reached the reviewer through ACTIVE.md, which the launch prompt names as required reading because the playbook says a role subagent gets CONTEXT.md + ACTIVE.md. The coordinator withheld through one channel and handed over through another, in the same prompt.
 - #219: through the commit bodies of the reviewed range. NOT reachable by prompt discipline — the review protocol itself tells the reviewer to read the diff, and this project deliberately writes long, specific commit messages. The better the commit message, the more completely the withholding is defeated.
 - #204: review-brief cannot know what the coordinator's prompt contained, so its count is about its own scope and is read as being about the reviewer's knowledge.

REQUIRED: the report changes from a WITHHELD COUNT to a REACHABILITY STATEMENT, per channel:
 - bead comments (what it withholds today)
 - the epic documents a prompt may name — at minimum CONTEXT.md, ACTIVE.md and the planning documents of the work item
 - the commit bodies of the reviewed range
 - a channel it CANNOT inspect is NAMED rather than omitted, which is the same rule the impact command now follows for its unresolved population

DERIVE THE CHANNELS, do not list them. The population of documents a role prompt may name is derivable from the flow templates that compose those prompts; the commit range is derivable from the review's own base. A hand-written list is the shape this epic exists to remove, and it goes stale the first time a role file gains a document.

DO NOT claim the change prevents anything. It raises detectability: a reviewer that knows what it can reach can declare a leak, which is how all three of these were ever known. The mechanism cannot stop a reviewer from reading a commit body and this bead must not say it does.

Baseline: measured by the coordinator before the wave. Measure without a pipe, in the foreground, and name the room — mypy runs over four Python versions in CI and one locally (BDL-UX #227).

title: [BDL-UX #226] the pre-push Gate crashes on a full pipe and reports it as stale docs
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 while pushing features/BDL-068, twice, reproducibly.

    git push -u origin features/BDL-068
      Running Beadloom Gate (beadloom ci)...
      File ".../services/commands/federation.py", line 420, in ci
        click.echo(output)
      File ".../click/utils.py", line 322, in echo
        file.flush()
    BlockingIOError: [Errno 35] write could not complete without blocking

      Beadloom Gate failed (docs stale / lint / coverage / doctor).
      Run the tech-writer (or /coordinator) to refresh docs, then re-push.

TWO DEFECTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT EXISTS TO REMOVE.

1. `beadloom ci` writes its whole rendered report through one click.echo(). Under `git push` stdout is a pipe whose buffer fills, and the fd is non-blocking, so the flush raises BlockingIOError instead of blocking until the reader drains. The Gate does not fail its checks — it dies on output. The bigger the honest report, the likelier the crash, so the failure arrives exactly when there is most to say.

2. THE HOOK THEN REPORTS A CAUSE IT DID NOT MEASURE. 'Beadloom Gate failed (docs stale / lint / coverage / doctor)' is printed on ANY non-zero exit, including a crash before a single check was rendered. Measured against the same tree in the foreground, twice, without a pipe: `beadloom ci` rc 0, zero `::error` lines, and the full suite 8186 passed. The hook's sentence was false in every clause. That is the class BDL-067 filed six times and BDL-068 exists to close — a message asserting a fact the code knows it did not establish.

ADOPTER IMPACT, stated plainly: an adopter whose Gate output grows past the pipe buffer cannot push, and is told their documentation is stale. The remedy they will reach for — running the tech-writer — cannot help, because nothing is stale. The documented escape hatch `git push --no-verify` then trains them to bypass the backstop for a reason that was never true.

EXPECTED:
 - `ci` writes incrementally, or handles BlockingIOError by retrying the write, or sets the stream blocking for the duration of the report. The report must survive being read by a pipe.
 - the hook must distinguish a Gate that FAILED from a Gate that CRASHED, and must not name causes it did not observe. If the exit code carries no verdict, the hook says so.

WORKAROUND USED FOR THIS BRANCH, recorded rather than hidden: the coordinator verified the Gate independently — `beadloom ci` rc 0 measured twice in the foreground without a pipe, zero error lines, 8186 tests passing — and pushed with `--no-verify`. The bypass is stated in the PR body.

RELATED: BDL-UX #148 and #201 are the same organ from the other side — the porcelain/rich renderer choice keyed on whether stdout is a terminal. This is the first case where the pipe does not change the FORMAT but kills the RUN.

comments.text:
REVIEW PASSED: critical 1, major 2 and major 3 of `.8` re-derived and confirmed closed. One
under-report shape REMAINS, reproduced and named below — filed, not blocking. See "WHAT SHOULD
BLOCK" for the plain call the stop rule asked for.

THE ASSIGNED QUESTION — does `beadloom impact` UNDER-REPORT, and on what tree?

YES. A second shape, on a layout more common than the first one: **a `src/` layout whose single
package sits under `src/`, with any Python OUTSIDE `src/`.** On that tree the caller and
co-writer axes read clean, empty and wrong, and the `unresolved` population carries nothing
about it — which is the exact condition `.8`'s critical was filed for, arrived at through a
different mechanism.

Reproduced on a tree I built (scratchpad `outsidesrc/`): `pyproject.toml`, `src/myapp/**`
(regular packages, `__init__.py` present), and `scripts/migrate.py` holding `second_writer`
(writes through the seed) and `run_migration` (calls the target).

    $ beadloom impact src/myapp/core/target.py --project .
    root swept: src/myapp
    ## who else commits through it
    - do_thing ...                      <- second_writer, scripts/migrate.py:5, is not here
    ## who else calls this
    - none found.                       <- run_migration, scripts/migrate.py:9, exists
    ## unresolved (2)
    - [no-graph-index] ...
    - [unresolved-terminator-name] ...  <- no sweep-shaped entry at all

    --json: co_writers.resolved: True   callers.resolved: True   callers.sites: []
            unresolved kinds: ['no-graph-index', 'unresolved-terminator-name']

Measured 2026-09-03, macOS, foreground, `uv run beadloom` against this working tree.

WHY THE 9db8e5a MACHINERY DOES NOT CATCH IT. `_sweep_gaps` emits
`sweep-narrower-than-the-project` on `swept.resolve() != source_root_of(project_root).resolve()`
(`answer.py:460`). `source_root_of` (`answer.py:177-193`) returns `src/<the one package>` when
exactly one child of `src/` holds Python. So on this layout `swept == source_root` and the
comparison is against a reference that is ITSELF narrower than the project — the gap is
structurally unable to fire. `callers.resolved` is `not outside` (`answer.py:315`), a predicate
now, but a predicate on "is the target inside the sweep", not on "could the sweep hold a
caller"; it is `True` here. The two-package and no-src layouts escape this because
`source_root_of` falls back to the project root there, which is exactly why the built matrix
sees them and not this one.

The slice's own test module states the invariant this violates, in its own words —
`tests/test_impact_over_every_source_layout.py:596`, `TestTheCeilingsTheseLayoutsExpose`: "What
stops that being the verdict's finding again is the narrowing gap, and nothing else." On this
layout there is no narrowing gap.

PROOF, IN THE MATRIX'S OWN FORM. A sixth layout — `a_src_layout_with_code_outside_src` — built
in the scratchpad and asserted against the matrix's own invariant ("found, or declared"):

    assert names == ["run"] or "sweep-narrower-than-the-project" in kinds
    E  assert ([] == ['run'] ... or 'sweep-narrower-than-the-project' in
       {'no-graph-index', 'no-seed', 'unresolved-terminator-name'})

Red against the shipped package. Not committed — this review is read-only.

Major:

A. `src/beadloom/application/impact/answer.py:177-193` (`source_root_of`) and `:460`
   (`_sweep_gaps`) · Major
   Issue: on an `src/<one package>` layout the narrowing gap is compared against `src/<package>`
   rather than against the project, so Python outside `src/` is swept by nothing and declared by
   nothing. `callers.resolved` and `co_writers.resolved` are both `True` over a demonstrably
   partial answer, and the `## Axes` artifact `--section` writes — which `scope-check` and
   `axes --refs` consume — carries the same silence in its `Unresolved:` field. This is the
   commonest Python layout there is: `src/pkg` beside `tests/`, `scripts/`, `tools/`,
   `noxfile.py`, `tasks.py`, `manage.py`.
   Recommendation: make the gap's reference the project rather than the source root — emit
   `sweep-narrower-than-the-project` (or a new kind naming the unswept directories) whenever the
   project holds a `*.py` outside the swept root, carrying both paths as the existing entry
   already does. Then add the sixth layout to
   `tests/test_impact_over_every_source_layout.py`: `src/pkg/sub/writer.py` as target,
   `scripts/main.py` as caller, in `THE_SWEEP_EXCLUDES_THE_CALLER`. Add the ceiling that remains
   to the SPEC's "Known ceilings", which currently names none of this.

Minor:

B. `src/beadloom/application/impact/answer.py:228` (`_targets_for` returns `shown = argument`)
   and `section.py:61` · Minor
   Issue: the `target` field echoes the argument verbatim while every other path in the answer
   is project-relative. An absolute-path invocation therefore writes a machine-specific absolute
   path into a COMMITTED document:
   `> **Derived by:** \`beadloom impact /private/tmp/.../nspkg/src/myapp/core/target.py\` over \`src/myapp\``
   The SPEC claims "two runs from different working directories produce the same text and a diff
   between them is a difference in the code"; the target field is outside that guarantee.
   Recommendation: pass `shown` through `_relative` when the argument resolves inside the project.

C. `src/beadloom/application/impact/answer.py:211-213` · Minor
   Issue: a relative target is resolved against `project_root`, never against the cwd, so
   `beadloom impact target.py --project <root>` run from the file's own directory fails with
   "no file and no symbol named 'target.py'". The behaviour is defensible (paths are
   project-relative everywhere else) and it errors honestly rather than under-reporting; it is
   not stated in `--help` or the SPEC.

MAJOR 2 — CLOSED. `impact src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py --section` — the
invocation `.8` quoted — now writes, beside `bootstrap_project: 3 branch(es)`:
`| branches | cli-commands | \`init\`: 4 branch(es), 1 exit form(s), from a caller's seat | ? |  |`
plus `non_interactive_init` and `interactive_init` from the same seat. The number BDL-067
carried for nine passes is produced from the seat BDL-067 sat in, and every count says whose it

`tests/test_impact_over_every_source_layout.py` (604 lines) is a matrix, not more cases: five

in `docs/`: `package_root_of`, `source_root_of`, `THE_CALLER_SEAT`, `THE_TARGET_SEAT`,
`context_of`, `render_axes_section`, `sweep-narrower-than-the-project`,

`docs/domains/application/features/impact/SPEC.md`, several also in

`uv run ruff check src/ tests/` clean · `uv run mypy src/` clean, 249 files ·
`beadloom lint --strict` rc 0, 0 errors (warns only) · `beadloom sync-check` rc 0 (warns,
incl. the `cli.md` drift of finding 4) · `beadloom doctor` all ok ·
`uv run pytest` 8186 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed, 262.62 s.
Green on the tree — NOT green in a clean room and not on a CI leg. I did not run
`beadloom ci`.

WHAT SHOULD BLOCK, plainly, since the stop rule asked. **Nothing here should block. Finding A
should be FILED as a follow-on bead, not cycled.** My reasoning, so the coordinator can
overrule it with the same facts:

title: [BDL-068.S1.10][dev] impact under-reports on a namespace package, and the branch axis answers for the wrong seat
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-0mdo.8 — CRITICAL 1 and MAJOR 2. Both block by the reviewer's own judgement, and the reason is the same: they are false negatives in a NARROWING tool, which is the one outcome this slice can ship that is worse than shipping nothing.

CRITICAL 1 — application/impact/answer.py:113-119 (package_root_of) and answer.py:~216 (callers=Population(True, calling)).

callers.resolved is the literal True. It is the one axis that can never be unresolved, and it is also the axis whose completeness depends entirely on the swept root — derived by walking up while (directory.parent / '__init__.py').exists(). A PEP 420 namespace package breaks that walk, the sweep silently narrows to a subdirectory, and every caller outside it reads as 'none found.'

REPRODUCED BY THE REVIEWER on src/mypkg/ with NO __init__.py, src/mypkg/sub/__init__.py present, src/mypkg/cli/main.py::run calling sub.writer.helper in two branches:

    beadloom impact src/mypkg/sub/writer.py   -> root swept: src/mypkg/sub
                                                 who else calls this: none found.   <- resolved, empty, WRONG
    beadloom impact helper                    -> root swept: .
                                                 who else calls this: run — src/mypkg/cli/main.py:4

One tree, one derivation, two spellings of one target, opposite answers, and THE WRONG ONE IS CLEAN. That is this epic's own thesis reproduced against this epic's own instrument. Population's own docstring says resolved=True with empty sites versus resolved=False with empty sites 'is how a derivation that knows nothing reads as a derivation that found nothing' — which is exactly what happens here. Same silence via --root pointed at an unrelated subtree.

IT FIRES ON ADOPTER TREES AND NOT ON OURS. This repository's packages all carry __init__.py, so the suite, the Gate and the author's own dogfooding all read green.

FIX, per the reviewer: (a) callers.resolved must be a PREDICATE, false at minimum when no target file is inside the swept root; (b) add an unresolved kind — e.g. sweep-narrower-than-the-project — emitted whenever swept != source_root_of(project_root), carrying BOTH paths, so a narrowed answer cannot read as a complete one; (c) package_root_of keeps walking while the parent directory still holds *.py, so PEP 420 does not decide the answer.

MAJOR 2 — impact/axes.py::commands_in and the commands loop in answer.py.

The branch axis is scoped to the TARGET's own file, so the number BDL-067 got wrong is still not produced from the seat BDL-067 sat in. MEASURED: 'beadloom impact src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py --section' emits '| branches | agent-prime | bootstrap_project: 3 branch(es), 1 exit form(s) |'. init appears one row ABOVE as a caller and its FOUR branches appear nowhere; Unresolved: reads '20 unresolved-terminator-name' and says nothing about the branch axis not having been computed for the callers just named.

THE NUMBER IS ARITHMETICALLY RIGHT FOR THE FUNCTION IT NAMES, which is what makes it a RECALL failure rather than an error — and the number it prints is 3, the same wrong number this project carried for nine review passes. PRD US-1 promises the owner will not be 'told a bug is one missing edge when it is six instances of a class across four entry points', and the artifact this command writes for that exact bug carries 3.

FIX: either compute commands for the caller sites the answer has already found — they are named, with paths and linenos — or emit an unresolved entry naming each caller whose branches were not read. Then state the choice in the SPEC's 'Known ceilings'.

MINOR 5, at your discretion: answer.py::_gaps re-imports ModuleSweep inside the function body to assert isinstance, and _boundary_of types its first parameter as object then asserts isinstance(boundary, GraphBoundary). Both are imported at module scope; these are type-checker workarounds.

NOT YOURS: docs/services/cli.md (finding 4) goes to beadloom-0mdo.9.

title: [BDL-068.S1.8][review] S1 review — say whether impact under-reports, and on what tree

THE ASSIGNMENT IS FIXED IN ADVANCE, above listing findings: say whether beadloom impact UNDER-REPORTS, and on what tree. A narrowing tool that errs small is more dangerous than no tool — today an agent that does not know the boundary reads widely and sometimes stumbles onto the neighbouring shape, which is how several of BDL-067's findings surfaced. Given a declared axes list it will trust it and stop, so the failure mode inverts from ignorance to false confidence.

Judge also whether S1.3's retroactive validation was recorded honestly whichever way it came out.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 1 critical, 3 major

THE ASSIGNED QUESTION — does `beadloom impact` UNDER-REPORT, and on what tree?

YES. Not on this repository's own tree, and that is the dangerous part.

On `src/beadloom` the sweep is correct and the tool does what the slice claims: run against
`af26750d` in a detached worktree, `beadloom impact src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py`
names `import_docs` (`doc_classify.py:35`) as a co-writer, and against `setup.py` at the same
commit it reports `init` with 4 branches including `['import_path'] -> import_docs`. Both facts
BDL-067 paid nine passes for are inside the shipped instrument's reach. I derived both myself.

It under-reports on a PEP 420 namespace-package tree — i.e. any adopter package that omits
`__init__.py`. Reproduced (paths under the scratchpad, `src/mypkg/` with NO `__init__.py`,
`src/mypkg/sub/__init__.py` present, `src/mypkg/cli/main.py::run` calling `sub.writer.helper`
in two branches):

  $ beadloom impact src/mypkg/sub/writer.py
  root swept: src/mypkg/sub
  ## who else calls this
  - none found.                       <- resolved, empty, and wrong

  $ beadloom impact helper            # same function, same tree, spelled as a symbol
  root swept: .
  ## who else calls this
  - run — src/mypkg/cli/main.py:4     <- the caller that exists

One tree, one derivation, two spellings of one target, opposite answers, and the wrong one is
clean. That is this epic's own thesis, reproduced against this epic's own instrument. The
`unresolved` population — the field whose stated purpose is "the ways this derivation is known
to be blind" — carries nothing about it.

---

Critical:

1. `src/beadloom/application/impact/answer.py:113-119` (`package_root_of`) and
   `answer.py:~216` (`callers=Population(True, calling)`) · Critical
   Issue: `callers.resolved` is the literal `True`. It is the one axis that can never be
   unresolved, and it is also the axis whose completeness depends entirely on the swept root —
   which is derived by walking up while `(directory.parent / "__init__.py").exists()`. A
   namespace package breaks that walk, the sweep silently narrows to a subdirectory, and every
   caller outside it is reported as "none found." `Population`'s own docstring says
   `resolved=True` with empty `sites` versus `resolved=False` with empty `sites` "is how a
   derivation that knows nothing reads as a derivation that found nothing" — that is exactly
   what happens here. Same silence via `--root` pointed at an unrelated subtree (probe: `--root
   src/beadloom/graph` against `bootstrap.py` prints "who else calls this: none found." with no
   gap entry). Measured 2026-09-03, macOS, foreground.
   Recommendation: (a) `callers.resolved` must be a predicate, false at minimum when no target
   file is inside the swept root; (b) add an `unresolved` kind — e.g. `sweep-narrower-than-the-
   project` — emitted whenever `swept != source_root_of(project_root)`, carrying both paths, so
   a narrowed answer cannot read as a complete one; (c) make `package_root_of` keep walking
   while the parent directory still holds `*.py`, so PEP 420 does not decide the answer.

Major:

2. `src/beadloom/application/impact/axes.py::commands_in` + the `commands` loop in
   `answer.py` · Major
   Issue: the branch axis is scoped to the TARGET's own file, so the number BDL-067 got wrong is
   still not produced from the seat BDL-067 sat in. Measured: `beadloom impact
   src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py --section` — the invocation
   `docs/domains/doc-sync/features/work-item-type/SPEC.md:54` cites as BDL-067's own target —
   emits `| branches | agent-prime | bootstrap_project: 3 branch(es), 1 exit form(s) |`.
   `init` appears one row above as a caller and its four branches appear nowhere; `Unresolved:`
   reads `20 unresolved-terminator-name` and says nothing about the branch axis not having been
   computed for the callers just named. The count is arithmetically right for the function it
   names, which is what makes it a recall failure rather than an error: PRD US-1 promises the
   owner will not be "told a bug is one missing edge when it is six instances of a class across
   four entry points", and the artifact this command writes for that bug carries the number 3.
   The seed derivation fixed the co-writer axis; for the branch axis it is the TARGET, not the
   seed, that decides, and no document says so.
   Recommendation: either compute `commands` for the caller sites the answer has already found
   (they are named, with paths and linenos), or emit an `unresolved` entry naming each caller
   whose branches were not read. Then state the choice in the SPEC's "Known ceilings".

3. `tests/test_impact_derives_the_seed_it_answers_from.py`,
   `tests/test_the_seed_decides_what_impact_reports.py` · Major
   Issue: no test exercises the swept-root derivation. `package_root_of` and `source_root_of`
   appear nowhere under `tests/` (grep: 0 hits), no test asserts anything about
   `callers.resolved`, and every fixture writes flat `*.py` into one `tmp_path` directory — a
   shape where `package_root_of` is trivially correct. Finding 1 can exist because the suite
   cannot see it. Coverage of the happy path is genuinely good (55 cases green locally,
   including the un-skipped `af26750d` class); the hole is one specific axis.
   Recommendation: a case per layout — regular package, PEP 420 namespace package, single file
   outside any package, explicit `--root` — asserting the swept root AND that a caller outside
   it is either found or declared unresolved.

4. `docs/services/cli.md` · Major (stale docs)
   Issue: the file was edited in this range and gained `### beadloom axes` (line 848), but there
   is no `### beadloom impact` and no `### beadloom scope-check`; `beadloom scope-check` returns
   ZERO hits across all of `docs/` and both READMEs. Two of the three commands this slice ships
   are absent from the CLI reference while the third is documented. `beadloom sync-check`
   already warns `docs/services/cli.md (surface drift: watches=cli,graph,flow.yml)` and the warn
   was left standing — the epic's own failure shape, an instrument that reported and was not
   acted on. The domain docs are the opposite of stale and are excellent
   (`docs/domains/application/features/impact/SPEC.md`, `.../README.md:62`).
   Recommendation: add both sections to `docs/services/cli.md`, then
   `beadloom sync-check --record-surface`.

Minor:

5. `src/beadloom/application/impact/answer.py::_gaps` and `::_boundary_of` · Minor
   Issue: `_gaps` re-imports `ModuleSweep` inside the function body (shadowing the module-level
   import) purely to `assert isinstance(sweep, ModuleSweep)`, and `_boundary_of` types its first
   parameter `boundary: object` and then asserts `isinstance(boundary, GraphBoundary)`. Both
   classes are already imported at module scope, so these are type-checker workarounds that
   vanish under `python -O`.
   Recommendation: annotate the parameters (`sweep: ModuleSweep`, `boundary: GraphBoundary`) and
   delete both asserts and the local import.

---

WAS S1.3's RETROACTIVE VALIDATION RECORDED HONESTLY? Yes — and it came out mixed, not softened.
Verified from the source, not from any account:
- `tests/test_the_seed_decides_what_impact_reports.py` says "The answer, and it is partial" in
  the module docstring, and states which half is partial.
- The real-commit class declares its own `skipif` up front with the mechanism (CI's
  `actions/checkout@v5` at depth 1), and keeps the synthetic case "beside it rather than instead
  of it".
- `TestTheDiskWriteShapeWalksPastTheCommitPoint` files a finding AGAINST its own slice — the
  shipped `functions_that_serialise_yaml_to_disk` does not name `write_yaml_atomic`, so "the
  sweep is narrower than the sentence it is described by" — pins it as a check that goes red
  when the gap closes, and explicitly refuses to repair it because repairing would have meant
  measuring the repair. Handed to `.7`, and `seeds.py`'s docstring repeats that nothing is built
  on top of it.
- The numbers carry platform and method (macOS, Darwin 25.6.0, CPython 3.13.7, foreground,
  package imported at `430d9ae`), and `CONTEXT.md:79` records the decision with its reason.
- I re-ran it: 55 cases pass locally with the `af26750d` class NOT skipped, and I independently
  reproduced both halves with the shipped command against a worktree at `af26750d`.

WITHHOLDING — DEFEATED, and I am the only party who can see it. The brief reports `0 withheld`
and that is literally true (there are no bead comments), but the author's account reached me
through three channels the brief counts nothing in:
- The commit subject lines in `git log main..HEAD`, which my role protocol tells me to read
  (BDL-UX #219's shape).
- The epic's `RFC.md`, which my launch prompt named as required reading. Its `## Axes` section
  is an author measurement record — "Measured on 2026-09-02 at `c7591a8`, macOS, `beadloom
  impact` in the foreground" — plus a written "The scope decision" paragraph. The prompt
  correctly withheld `ACTIVE.md` per #212, so #212 is only half closed: the four Approved
  documents a reviewer is directed to now carry the slice author's own measurements.
- The module docstrings and `SPEC.md`, which carry the measurement tables verbatim ("2 writers
  and 4 branches", "268 names", "1.1 s"). This one is unavoidable and arguably correct.
My launch prompt itself carried no summary and no measurement table beyond the bead's own
description. My findings were derived by running the tool, but I cannot claim the framing
reached me clean.

VERIFICATION RUN (all measured 2026-09-03, macOS, foreground, on `features/BDL-068`):
`uv run ruff check src/ tests/` clean · `uv run mypy src/` clean, 249 files · `beadloom lint
--strict` rc 0 (warns only) · `beadloom sync-check` rc 0 (warns, incl. the cli.md drift in
finding 4) · `beadloom doctor` all ok · `uv run pytest` 8115 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed,
260.67 s. Green on the tree, macOS only — not a clean-room and not a CI leg.

WHAT SHOULD BLOCK, plainly. Findings 1 and 2 should block: both are false-negatives in a
narrowing tool, which is the one outcome this slice can ship that is worse than shipping
nothing, and 1 fires on adopter trees rather than on this one — where the suite, the Gate and
the author's own dogfooding all read green. Finding 3 blocks with them because it is why 1 is
invisible. Finding 4 is file-and-fix. Finding 5 is the author's discretion. Architecture,
layering, annotations, typing, error handling and the BDD scenarios are all sound — the
scenarios in `tests/acceptance/features/impact.feature` and `declared_axes.feature` are
observable, in the user's vocabulary, and several can fail for real reasons.

NOTE ON `--release`: this tracker writes every role under one identity, so `--release` will
likely report that it could not establish the verdict was recorded by someone other than the
author. That is the normal answer here, not a defect.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: verdict REVIEW ISSUES (1 critical, 3 major) recorded and routed. This is the first CRITICAL in either epic, and the reviewer's blocking judgement is adopted in full.

THE ASSIGNED QUESTION WAS ANSWERED, and the answer is the finding: beadloom impact under-reports — NOT on this repository's tree, which is the dangerous part. On src/beadloom it does what the slice claims, verified by the reviewer at af26750d in a detached worktree: it names import_docs as a co-writer of bootstrap.py, and init with 4 branches from setup.py. Both facts BDL-067 paid nine passes for are inside the shipped instrument's reach.

It under-reports on a PEP 420 namespace package — any adopter package that omits __init__.py. One tree, one derivation, two spellings of one target, opposite answers, and THE WRONG ONE IS CLEAN. This epic's own thesis, reproduced against this epic's own instrument, on the trees we do not have and adopters do.

MAJOR 2 IS THE SAME LESSON IN ONE NUMBER: 'beadloom impact bootstrap.py --section' writes '3 branch(es)' for bootstrap_project, while init's four branches appear nowhere and the unresolved field says nothing about it. Three is the number this project carried for nine review passes. The tool built to prevent that error reproduces it, arithmetically correctly, from the wrong seat.

ROUTED: critical 1 + major 2 + minor 5 -> beadloom-0mdo.15; major 3 (no test exercises the swept-root derivation; package_root_of and source_root_of have 0 hits under tests/) -> beadloom-0mdo.16, and it blocks WITH the critical because it is why the critical is invisible; re-review -> beadloom-0mdo.17. Major 4 -> beadloom-0mdo.9's named surface, which was re-pointed to depend on .17.
