comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: bead claimed. Read .1-.6 comments in full plus CONTEXT/RFC/PLAN. This is an AUDIT, so the first act is a census of what is ALREADY pinned, and three of the four things the bead owes are partly covered already:
- PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK: .3 pinned the GAP (the commit point's own callees are disjoint from the set; the shipped sweep does not name it) and .2 pinned the EXCLUSION (no declared effect rule uses the set) plus the consequence on a synthetic tree. NOT pinned: the three verbs individually -- .1 measured that narrowing {write_text,write_bytes,open} to {write_text} survives the whole suite -- and nothing states the shape that DOES hold, so a widening of the vocabulary re-answers every impact target silently.
- unresolved direction: .2 has 2 cases (co_writers.resolved False + no-seed kind) on the ANSWER. Not yet checked whether the two RENDERERS (text, json) and the section renderer can make a seedless target read as an empty list -- that is where the bead's clause 3 actually bites.
- .5 and .6's new checks: verified red by their own mutants; the bead asks me to RE-DERIVE rather than adopt, on a named tree.
Not duplicating what is covered. Next: the census of assertions that cannot fail (.1's dangling==[] property) across the lifted package's consumers.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: the census is measured, not argued. macOS Darwin 25.6.0, CPython 3.13.7, foreground, no pipe.

(1) THE VACUITY AUDIT, .1's method run over every real-tree finding list in the lifted package's eight consumer modules. Each finding list was blinded (the variable set to [] / set() immediately before its assertion) and ITS OWN MODULE re-run:
  test_every_caller_of_the_skeleton_writer.py wrong -> 11 passed; stale -> 11 passed
  test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py elsewhere -> 43 passed
  test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py unguarded (2 sites) -> 30; silent -> 30; stale -> 30; bypassing -> 30
  test_one_parent_post_condition_over_every_writer.py dangling -> 27 passed
All eight survive, which is expected and is NOT by itself the defect: blinding the ASSERTION does not blind the DETECTOR. The property .1 named is that no case anywhere demonstrates the detector can REJECT. Checked one by one:
  wrong / stale -> demonstrated (test_it_reads_the_argument_a_call_site_hands_over, test_it_reports_a_caller_that_re_indexes_only_before)
  elsewhere -> demonstrated (five positive spellings + the half-shape negatives)
  unguarded -> demonstrated (five cases assert a non-empty reaches_marker=False set)
  silent / stale -> demonstrated (TestTheDeferralChecksStillBite)
  bypassing -> demonstrated (test_the_declared_exception_still_exists), as .1 recorded
  dangling -> NOT demonstrated. So .1's finding reproduces and NOTHING ELSE in the package's consumers has that property. That is the answer to the bead's clause 2 second half, and it is a negative result stated as one.

(2) PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK, measured on this tree with the real sweep: the commit point's own callees are ['Path','dump','fdopen','fileno','flush','fsync','mkstemp','replace','str','suppress','unlink','write'] -- intersect SERIALISES_YAML = {dump} (why the declared rule finds it) and intersect PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK = {} (why the disk rule does not). Per-verb over the real tree: write_text names persist_flow_config, write_bytes names NOTHING, open names NOTHING. That is exactly why narrowing to {write_text} survives -- two of three verbs are exercised by no case at all. Widening the set with {fdopen, write, replace} names the commit point (2 bodies instead of 1), so the exclusion is a live choice and not an accident.

(3) A SECOND SITE OF THE SAME 'silently omits' DIRECTION, found while auditing .5's routing derivation and measured: a routing row whose Flow cell spells neither 'simplified' nor 'full' is DROPPED by _routes_in with no note. Measured on a three-row table (epic Full / bug Simplified / spike 'Lightweight: NOTE'): routes = 2, notes = (), flow_of('spike') = None -- indistinguishable from a type nobody declared. Routing.notes exists for exactly this and is only used for 'no table at all'. Not repaired here (the naive repair fires on the table's own alignment row, which is why .5 has a mutant for it); it is pinned as a gap class with the instruction to delete rather than repair, and reported.

(4) ONE ASSERTION THAT CANNOT FAIL, in .2's acceptance steps: 'assert "unresolved" in world["human"].output' for the seedless target. render_impact always emits a '## unresolved (N)' heading, so the word is in every output. Strengthening it to the line that actually distinguishes the two populations.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: written, green, and every case demonstrated capable of failing.

BUILT. tests/test_the_derivations_hold_as_shapes.py, 21 cases in four classes, plus four cases appended to tests/test_one_parent_post_condition_over_every_writer.py (27 -> 31) and one strengthened assertion in tests/acceptance/steps/test_impact_steps.py.

(a) THE GAP .3 HANDED OVER BY NAME. TestEveryDiskWriteVerbIsExercisedByACase: one synthetic writer per verb in PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK (write_text / write_bytes / open), so all three are load-bearing where two were carried by nothing; the conjunction from the other side (a body that writes and serialises nothing is not named); and the SHAPE THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS, which was nowhere stated -- the commit point's own body names fdopen, write and replace, and PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK spells none of the three. The message on that assertion names the re-measurement a widening owes (.2's two acceptance targets at af26750d, and .3's gap class deleted rather than repaired). A fourth case pins that the WIDENED set does name the commit point, so the exclusion cannot pass over a vocabulary that excludes nothing.

(b) THE PROSE SCANNER .1 REFUSED TO LIFT. Its finding computation is now _dangling_in(package), a package parameter defaulting to the real one -- the convention _writers_that_create_nodes already uses in that module. Four cases over trees built to dangle: a docstring naming a symbol the sibling lost, the same as a COMMENT (the surviving cross-reference this check exists for was a comment), a reference that resolves and is silent, and prose naming something that is not a sibling module at all. VERIFIED: replacing the computation with [] was 0 red before and is 2 red now.

(c) THE DIRECTION OF THE UNRESOLVED REPORT, at the renderers rather than at the answer. ONE answer carries both populations -- for a module that reaches no sink and that nothing calls, co_writers is UNRESOLVED and callers is RESOLVED AND EMPTY -- so the case is a shape and not two fixtures. Text: '- unresolved: <reason>' against '- none found.'. JSON: sites == [] on BOTH sides, asserted, so resolved+reason carry the whole difference and a consumer reading the list alone sees one fact where there are two.

(d) .5'S HANDED SPELLINGS. Four spellings of the launch (an Agent call, a bare prose mention, an assignment in single quotes, a colon with loose spacing) all found; two near-misses refused, including 'explorer', the one a prefix match accepts; and the heading renamed under a found launch, so the step is still found.

ELEVEN MUTANTS, each a run of the real suite over a deliberately weakened production tree, tree restored after each (git diff --stat src/ empty before and after):
  disk-write set narrowed to {write_text} -> 2 red (the gap .1 measured, now closed)
  disk-write set widened with the commit point's verbs -> 2 red
  the shape read as a disjunction -> 2 red
  an unresolved population rendered like an empty one -> 1 red in the unit module AND 1 red in .2's acceptance scenario, which is the strengthening earning its place
  a seedless answer rendering no seed line -> 1 red
  the reason dropped from the JSON population -> 1 red
  the launch matched only as an Agent call argument -> 3 red
  the role matched by prefix -> 1 red
  an unreadable flow cell defaulting to simplified -> 2 red
  the routing stating a note it has no reason to state -> 5 red
  the prose finding computation blinded -> 2 red
ONE MUTANT WAS RE-APPLIED because the first form did not run: 'a dropped row reported as a note' referenced a name the edit never defined, so it failed with a NameError rather than as a weakening. .6 recorded that a mutant that did not run is not a mutant that passed; it was re-stated as two edits that do run.

title: [BDL-068.S1.6][dev] the commit-scope check: a change outside the work item's declared axes is a finding
description:
sync-check --staged and the commit-scoped hook already judge a commit by its paths. This compares those paths against the axes the work item declared.

DONE WHEN:
- a commit touching a path outside the declared axes is REPORTED, verified on a commit that does
- a commit inside them is SILENT, verified on one that is — an always-red check is an ignored check
- the finding names WHICH axis the path fell outside, not merely that it did

Q2 IS DECIDED (CONTEXT): compare against the WORK ITEM's axes, not the bead's. The work item's axes are what the human approved; a bead may narrow freely inside them. A commit leaving the work item's axes means the approval no longer covers the change, which is exactly the re-plan trigger. Comparing against the bead would fire constantly on legitimate cross-bead work inside one approved scope.

WHY THIS IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: a section the Gate can see missing is advice with a checkbox. This project has watched a prompt input be ignored or routed around three times — the mutation duty with no runner, the withholding defeated through ACTIVE.md and then through commit bodies. Each was correct as written and none of them held.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: read .2, .4 and .5's comments in full, CONTEXT/RFC/PLAN, and the six modules the premise names. Bead claimed. THE PREMISE IS HALF-TRUE AND THE ACCEPTANCE'S SECOND POINT IS ALREADY MEASURABLY BROKEN BY THE OBVIOUS DESIGN.

CLAUSE 1 -- 'sync-check --staged and the commit-scoped hook already judge a commit by its paths'. TRUE. doc_sync/commit_scope.scope_to_commit narrows the pair list by git_baseline.staged_paths, and the installed pre-commit hook runs ruff, mypy and sync-check over the staged paths only. But what it narrows is a list of INDEXED DOC-CODE PAIRS: a staged path that belongs to no pair is invisible to it. The axes name graph NODES, not pairs, so nothing of scope_to_commit's answer can be reused -- the comparison this bead needs runs over the staged paths themselves.

CLAUSE 2 -- 'this is the comparison they were missing'. The comparison does not exist. What is missing beyond it is WHICH work item to compare against: pre-commit runs before the message is finalised, so the '[BDL-068]' prefix is not readable there, and only the branch name features/<ISSUE-KEY> answers it at that moment. An unnamed work item is NOT CHECKED with a reason, never a pass.

THE ALWAYS-RED TRAP IS REAL AND I MEASURED IT ON THIS EPIC'S OWN TABLE, before designing anything. Rule 'a staged path's owning node must be a node a kept axis row names', run against BDL-068's RFC Axes section (kept nodes: ci-gate, cli-commands, config-check, flow-guards, impact, planning-report, role-adapters, work-item-type) over this branch's three code commits:
  c7591a8 (36 paths): OUTSIDE agentic-flow-setup, axes-section, doc-shape, onboarding, role-composer, work-item-routing -- 11 paths
  3f68442 (35 paths): OUTSIDE axes-section, doc-shape, doc-shape-requirements, doc-templates, onboarding -- 5 paths
  2f9e343 (27 paths): OUTSIDE cli, source-derivation -- 6 paths
Three of three. The node-level rule is red on every commit the approval DOES cover, which is docs_audit.ignore's shape exactly.

WHY, and it is a fact about the section rather than about the rule: the table records what a change RANGES OVER (the callers axis), and the surfaces the change IS live in the 'Derived by' field as prose paths. Adding the derivation targets clears axes-section and role-composer and leaves c7591a8 red on four.

MEASURED SECOND RULE, at the BOUNDED CONTEXT the declared axes reach (application, cli, doc-sync, onboarding): all three commits SILENT, and over the 250 commits before this branch, 115 of the 155 that touch an owned path (74 percent) fall outside it. So it is specific to this epic's own work and still fires on three quarters of unrelated work -- the profile a signal has.

DESIGN, two clauses and one reported fault. INSIDE when the path's owning node is named by a KEPT row, or when no row names the node and its bounded context is reached by a kept row or by a derivation target. OUTSIDE when a row names the node and every such row was ruled OUT of scope (the finding names that axis by name), or when no declared axis reaches the context (the finding names the contexts they do reach). An UNDECIDED row neither widens nor narrows -- it is not kept, and the count is printed beside the verdict, because axis-without-a-scope-decision already owns that fault and a second reporter is a second thing to keep in step. A path no node owns is not a call site: it is counted as the unjudged population, never reported, the way CommitScope already states its remainder.

One measurement of mine corrupted one of its own: tests/test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation failed in the baseline run because I ran a script that opened .beadloom/beadloom.db read-only while the suite was running. It passes alone. The baseline will be re-measured in the foreground with nothing else touching the index.

comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: green on the parts, and both of the acceptance points that decide the check are verified on REAL commits against this epic's REAL table rather than on fixtures.

RED FIRST: the 9 scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/commit_scope.feature were written and run before any production code existed and failed at collection. 9 pass now.

BUILT, one mechanism per fact.
- doc_sync/scope_check.py -- the check, pure: paths + a DeclaredScope + an ownership mapping in, a ScopeVerdict out. No git, no index, no filesystem, because the domain has none of them.
- doc_sync/axes_section.py gains derived_targets(): the paths the 'Derived by' field names, over a SHAPE -- any whitespace-separated word inside a code span that carries a path separator. That reads the RENDERED field (target and sweep root in one span) and a hand-written one (three files in three spans) without either being a case. A target given as a symbol carries no separator and is not returned; the gap is stated.
- doc_sync/git_baseline.py gains paths_changed_since() and current_branch(), rather than a second subprocess call to git elsewhere in the product. The three-dot form ref...HEAD, not two-dot, and that is a measurement rather than a preference -- see below.
- application/impact/boundary.py gains context_of(node): the same part_of walk owner_of already performs, exposed because a caller starting from a DECLARED node has no path to look it up by.
- application/declared_scope.py -- the join, the way work_item_routing does it for work-item-type. The work item is found by the BRANCH, and it has to be: pre-commit runs before the commit message is finalised, so the [BDL-068] prefix is unreadable at the moment the commit is judged. The population is DERIVED from planning_documents(), so a project configuring its own doc_quality.paths is judged over its own corpus. A folder matches when its name is one of the branch's /-separated SEGMENTS -- not a substring.
- services/commands/impact.py gains 'beadloom scope-check' (--since, --branch, --porcelain, --json), and its module docstring now states the responsibility it actually has: the Axes family, one document written by impact, read by axes and enforced by scope-check.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, CPython 3.13.7, foreground, no pipe. Read off BDL-068's own RFC: 8 kept nodes, 3 derivation targets (axes-section, cli-commands, role-composer), 4 bounded contexts, 0 undecided rows.
  SILENT on this branch's own work: 2f9e343 judged 14 owned paths -> 0; 3f68442 judged 10 -> 0; c7591a8 judged 14 -> 0; and 'beadloom scope-check --since origin/main' judges 36 owned paths across the whole branch and reports nothing.
  REPORTED on a commit that leaves: a4738b7c, BDL-067's landed fix, judged 10 owned paths -> 1 finding, src/beadloom/graph/linter.py.
  THE FINDING NAMES THE AXIS: 'outside every axis the work item declared -- callers (application, cli, doc-sync, onboarding) -- and outside the 4 bounded context(s) they reach'.

ONE DEFECT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND, and it is why paths_changed_since uses the three-dot form. Run with --since main it reports graph/linter.py; with --since origin/main it is silent. Local main here is two commits behind the remote, so a4738b7 is 'on HEAD and not on main' and another work item's LANDED change reads as this branch's. The three-dot form asks what the branch changed since it left the ref, which is what a pull request contains and what the approval was given for.

THE UNDECIDED ROW, treated deliberately rather than by default -- the coordinator's caution. An undecided row neither WIDENS the scope nor NARROWS it: it is not kept, so it cannot authorise a commit, and it is not a ruling, so it does not condemn one. Its node therefore falls to the bounded-context clause like any other. The count travels with the verdict and is printed, because axis-without-a-scope-decision already owns that fault and a second reporter is a second thing to keep in step. BDL-068's own table has 0 undecided rows today; the case is a scenario.

Reading a section needs no index. The absence is now reported first, so a work item that declares no scope gets the reason that names its own fault rather than one about this machine's cache. TESTS. 9 scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/commit_scope.feature, written and run RED at collection before any production code existed, plus 54 cases in tests/test_a_commit_is_judged_against_the_declared_axes.py. EVERY CASE DEMONSTRATED CAPABLE OF FAILING by sixteen mutants, each a run of the real suite over a deliberately weakened derivation: the bounded-context clause dropped -> 6 red; a ruled-out node judged like any other -> 3; the derivation targets not counted as inside -> 1; an undecided row counted as kept -> 3; a path no node owns reported instead of counted -> 7; the ruling finding not naming the axis -> 2; a node kept by one row and ruled out by another treated as ruled out -> 1; staged paths not deduplicated -> 1; the whole Derived by field read rather than its code spans -> 1; a target needing no path separator -> 3; the branch matched by substring rather than by segment -> 1; the missing section reported after the missing index -> 1; the local trunk preferred over the remote-tracking ref -> 1; the branch compared with two dots -> 1; the branch read through rev-parse so a detached HEAD names one -> 1; the bounded context taken as the node itself rather than walked -> 4. title: [BDL-068.S1.4][dev] ## Axes as a required section, reported by doc-quality when absent or empty
description:
Add the heading to the BRIEF and RFC core templates. doc_templates.required_sections already DERIVES a document's required sections from the composed template's literal '## ' headings, so adding the heading makes the section required by the same act, and doc-quality reports its absence exactly as missing_sections reports any other. This is why the cheap half is cheap.

DONE WHEN:
- a BRIEF without ## Axes is a doc-quality finding, verified on a document that lacks it
- an ## Axes section that is PRESENT AND EMPTY is also a finding
- the section records the derivation's output AND the human's scope decision, and the bead's refs: is generated from it

Q1 IS DECIDED (CONTEXT): the axes are DERIVED by beadloom impact; the document records the derivation's output and the human's scope decision; the bead's refs: is generated from the document. A disagreement between the three is a finding. Do not create a second AUTHORED home — two authored homes are two things that can disagree, which is the class this epic exists to remove.

refs: doc-quality, flow-composer

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: read .2's comments in full, CONTEXT/RFC/PLAN, and the four modules the premise names. THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD AS WRITTEN, measured before designing anything else.

`doc_templates.required_sections` derives sections from the composed `docs` artifact kind, whose DOC_KINDS are overview/domain/service/feature/beadloom-readme -- GRAPH NODE documents. BRIEF and RFC have no template in that family at all: their skeletons are fenced blocks inside the composed `commands/templates` artifact. And `missing_sections` is a SYNC-CHECK reason over paired node documents (doc_sync/doc_shape.check_section_shape, read from the nodes/docs tables), not a doc-quality finding: planning documents are not in that table and doc-quality has no section check at all. So 'add the heading and it is required by the same act' is false today in two places.

WHAT I AM DOING INSTEAD, and it is one mechanism rather than two: EXTEND the same derivation to the planning kinds. The kinds and their sections are read from the composed /templates command's fenced skeletons -- the artifact `shipped_placeholders` already composes and reads for exactly this reason -- through the SAME heading extraction `required_sections` uses. And the peer policy that decides what is required is doc_shape's existing one, extracted into a pure function and used over both corpora rather than reimplemented.

MEASURED FIRST, because the choice of policy is a corpus question. Over the 259 planning documents this repository holds, requiring every template heading of every document of that kind gives 767 findings (the archive is largely pre-`language: en` and carries none of today's headings). Under doc_shape's MAJORITY policy the same requirement gives 6 kind-level statements and 102 document-level findings. Both numbers are true; the second is the policy this project already declared for this exact class, so it is the one I am using, and the 102 will be reported with their number rather than hidden.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: green on the parts, built by responsibility, one mechanism per fact.

BUILT.
- doc_templates gains section_titles (the ONE heading extraction, now shared), planning_skeletons and required_sections_by_document_kind -- the same derivation required_sections performs for node documents, over the composed /templates command's fenced skeletons. A project layer appending '## RUNBOOK.md' with its own headings makes them required by the same act; that is a case, not a claim.
- The templates gain '## Axes' in the BRIEF and the RFC. In the RFC it REPLACES the authored '### Affected Areas' list, because two homes for 'what this change touches' is the class this epic removes.
- doc_shape: the peer-majority policy extracted into peer_section_shape and used over BOTH corpora -- check_section_shape is re-expressed over it and its 31 existing cases still pass. New: read_sections (fence-aware, depth-aware) and the two planning checks missing-section and empty-section.
- doc_sync/axes_section.py: the section's GRAMMAR, in the domain whose subject is documents, so the renderer (application/impact/section.py) and the reader are one text read in two directions. Checks: axes-without-a-seed and axis-without-a-scope-decision.
- application/planning_report.py: ONE composition of all nine checks. The gate step and 'docs quality' both render it, because two assemblies of one report is two things that can disagree -- which is what they were before this bead.
- CLI: 'beadloom impact --section' renders the section; 'beadloom axes <document>' reads one back, with --refs generating the bead's refs: line from the rows kept in scope.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY after wiring, foreground, no pipe: missing-section 102 over 256 read, empty-section 0 over 256, and 17 kind-level conventions including 'BRIEF Axes (0/12)' and 'RFC Axes (0/48)'. empty-section was 155 before a defect I found by running it: a section whose content lives in its subsections read as empty, so '## Code Standards' over four '###' was reported 155 times. read_sections now propagates content up the heading depth, and the case is in the suite.

THE 102 ARE TRUE AND THEY ARE THE ARCHIVE. They are old RFCs with no '## Overview' and old PRDs with no '## Impact'. Every one is a real departure from the shape its peers keep, the check is warn, and the gate stays green on it. I am reporting the number rather than suppressing it: whether the archive gets revised or the corpus gets scoped is the owner's call, not a dev bead's.

TESTS: 9 scenarios in two feature files + 29 cases. Mutants next, then the epic's own RFC gets its Axes section derived by the command.

comments.text:

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED.

WHAT. `## Axes` is a required section of the BRIEF and the RFC because those two skeletons carry it, and for no other reason. `beadloom docs quality` and the `docs-quality` Gate step now report NINE checks from ONE composition.

THE PREMISE, MEASURED FIRST AND FOUND FALSE, which is the finding this bead hands up. `doc_templates.required_sections` derives over the `docs` artifact kind, whose kinds are graph NODE documents; BRIEF and RFC have no template in that family, and their skeletons are fenced blocks inside the composed /templates command. `missing_sections` is a sync-check reason over paired node documents, not a doc-quality finding. So 'add the heading and it is required by the same act' was false in two places. I EXTENDED the derivation rather than building a second mechanism: section_titles is now the one heading extraction, and required_sections_by_document_kind runs it over the planning skeletons. A project fragment appending '## RUNBOOK.md' with its own headings makes them required by the same act -- a case, not a claim.

THE THREE ACCEPTANCE POINTS.
1. A BRIEF without '## Axes' is a doc-quality finding, verified on a document that lacks it: three briefs of which two carry the section, the third reported as missing-section. The policy is doc_shape's OWN peer-majority rule, extracted into peer_section_shape and used over both corpora, so below a majority the KIND is reported once with its ratio instead of every document.
2. A present-and-empty section is also a finding, and empty-section is deliberately NOT peer-gated: a heading with nothing under it is a defect whatever the peers do, and it is the one a presence check is satisfied by. It fires on a single document with no peers at all.
3. The section records the derivation's output AND the scope decision, and the refs: is generated from it. `beadloom impact <target> --section` writes the first half and leaves every row undecided; `beadloom axes <document> --refs` reads it back and prints 'refs: a, b' from the rows kept in scope, deduplicated in the table's order. The checks report a section that records axes with no seed, and a row with no decision.

THE SEED IS CARRIED, per .3's measurement. axes-without-a-seed exists because the same derivations report 2 writers and 4 branches under one seed and 0 and 3 under another. A stated 'none' IS naming the seed and satisfies the check; a missing field does not. The renderer keeps the same distinction: an absent seed renders as 'none' with the co-writers row reading 'unresolved', never as a zero.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, macOS Darwin 25.6.0, CPython 3.13.7, foreground, no pipe: missing-section 102 over 256 read; empty-section 0 over 256; 17 kind-level conventions including 'BRIEF Axes (0/12)' and 'RFC Axes (0/48)'. A non-peer-relative policy over the same requirement gives 767, which is why the peer one was chosen -- the archive predates `language: en`. empty-section read 155 until the run exposed a real defect: a section whose content lives in its subsections read as empty, so '## Code Standards' over four '###' was reported 155 times. read_sections now records heading DEPTH and propagates content upward, and that is a case.

DECISIONS WORTH THE REVIEW'S ATTENTION.
(1) The 102 are TRUE and are the archive -- old RFCs with no '## Overview', old PRDs with no '## Impact'. All nine checks are warn and the Gate is rc 0 on them. I am reporting the number rather than suppressing it; whether the archive is revised or the corpus scoped by doc_quality.paths is the owner's call, and it is in ACTIVE.md so it is not discovered later as a surprise.
(2) BDL-068's own RFC deliberately does NOT get an Axes section from this bead. An epic is not an `impact` target, its axes span six slices and several runs, and .6 measures every commit against the work item's declared axes -- so a guessed table would make its first run wrong. Consequence, stated rather than hidden: the two axes checks read 0 documents today and the Gate says 'NOT CHECKED' for them.
(3) The section's GRAMMAR lives in doc_sync (the domain whose subject is documents) and the RENDERER in application/impact, which imports it. One grammar, two directions, held together by a round-trip case -- doc_sync may not import upward, and a second grammar in the renderer is exactly the disagreement this epic removes.
(4) document_sections() now skips fenced blocks. A '## ' inside a fence is a quoted template, and a BRIEF quoting its own skeleton would otherwise be credited with every section it names. The 31 existing cases pass unchanged.

TESTS. 9 scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/{axes_section,planning_document_shape}.feature -- two of them under the exact names BDL-068's PRD already referenced, so those two scenario-coverage warnings are now resolved -- plus 29 cases in tests/test_the_axes_section_is_required_by_the_template.py. title: [BDL-068.S1.3][dev] validate the derivations against BDL-067 retroactively, before anything consumes them
description:
Run the lifted derivations against the tree as it stood at BDL-067's first dev bead (2026-08-31, before acf4066) and answer ONE question: would they have listed BOTH writers of graph nodes and FOUR entry points of init?

DONE WHEN:

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS: the claim that this feature would have prevented BDL-067 is currently unmeasured, and it is the whole case for ranking this epic first. A feature justified by an argument where a measurement was available is the defect this epic exists to remove. This project asks that of every claim it reviews.

refs: application

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: bead claimed; the tree under measurement is af26750d ([BDL-065] docs: rerun the guide without the heading lock I had added (#56), 2026-08-31 22:29 +0300) -- the parent of acf4066 and an ancestor of main, reached through a detached worktree rather than a checkout. comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
MEASURED (2): is the seed that produces the right answer DERIVABLE from the input, or does a human have to already know it? Same room, same tree. Rule stated before it was run: the commit point of a target file is a name its own bodies call that reaches a body doing X. Two values of X, both already shipped in the lifted package:

  X = SERIALISES_YAML ({dump, safe_dump}): 3 bodies directly, 58 names reach one.
      From onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py -> 2 candidates: write_yaml_atomic, generate_rules. The right seed is one of two, and the other is itself a graph writer, so it can only widen the answer.
      From services/commands/setup.py -> 8 candidates, and write_yaml_atomic is NOT among them: it is two hops away, so a rule that stops at the target's own callees returns the first hop and not the sink.

So the seed is derivable under one of the package's two shapes and unreachable under the other, and the difference is a spelling -- which is the exact defect class this epic exists to remove, now measured inside the epic's own instrument. NOT REPAIRED HERE, by the bead's own clause: repairing it would mean measuring the repair. It is handed to .7, which already owns the PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK gap that .1 recorded (narrowing it to {write_text} survives the whole suite); this is that gap's concrete consequence rather than a second one.

title: [BDL-068.S1.2][dev] beadloom impact <path|symbol>, with the unresolved population in the answer
description:
Four questions answered from the source: who else writes these files, who else calls these symbols, how many branches the enclosing command has, and how many ways it terminates. Plus the boundary from the graph — which domain each found site belongs to, and therefore when a change leaves one.

Human output and --json.

DONE WHEN — REWRITTEN BY .3's MEASUREMENT, which found the answer to the two criteria that were here is a property of the SEED and not of the tree:
- impact DERIVES its seed from the target and NAMES it in the answer. No invocation takes the commit point as an argument and no literal names it. MEASURED at af26750d (the parent of acf4066, the tree BDL-067's first dev bead started from): seeded with `write_yaml_atomic` the lifted derivations list 2 writers and 4 branches of `init`; seeded with `bootstrap_project`, the function that bead was changing, they list 0 writers and 3 branches. Three is the number the epic carried throughout. The two criteria below are satisfied by a tool that hardcodes `write_yaml_atomic`, which is the authored list this epic exists to remove, so they are worth nothing without this one
- the answer NAMES THE RULE the seed came from, and a target the rule finds no seed for puts that in the unresolved population rather than answering over an empty set. A clean list is trusted and stopped at
- the answer NAMES the population it could not resolve (unparseable module, dynamic dispatch, call through a variable) as a FIELD, not an omission. Recall over precision: the failure mode we are moving toward is false confidence, which is worse than the ignorance we have now
- run against onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py AT af26750d, with no argument naming a commit point, it lists BOTH writers of graph nodes
- run against services/commands/setup.py at the same commit, on the same terms, it lists FOUR entry points of init and the exit forms including sys.exit. MEASURED there: the commit point is TWO HOPS from that file, so a seed rule that stops at the target's own callees returns eight first-hop names and not the sink
- the seed rule is NOT stated over PUTS_BYTES_ON_DISK. MEASURED at af26750d: write_yaml_atomic is not among the 268 names that reach a body in that set, because it puts its bytes down through os.fdopen(...).write and Path.replace while the set spells write_text, write_bytes and open. Over SERIALISES_YAML it is one of two candidates from bootstrap.py
- it is NOT a graph walk: a node whose axes live entirely inside it still produces an answer

THE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS HELPS OR HARMS: impact is not `why` at a new name. Not one axis BDL-067 needed is a fact of the graph — the writers of .beadloom/_graph/, the branches of init, its exit forms, the modes, the renderers, the YAML readers and their policies all live INSIDE one node. A graph walk would answer confidently and miss all of them: a green describing the checker's ignorance, shipped as a feature. The graph supplies the boundary and nothing else.

THE SECOND CONSTRAINT, added by .3: a wrong seed produces a CLEAN, CONFIDENT, WRONG answer. That is the same failure mode as an omitted unresolved population, one level up, and it is the one thing this command can do that is worse than not existing.

COMPLETED.

WHAT. `beadloom impact <path|symbol>` answers four questions from the source -- who else commits through the sink this target reaches, who else calls what it defines, how many branches each of its commands has and how many ways each ends -- plus the boundary from the graph and the population the derivation could not resolve. The seed is DERIVED under a rule the answer names -- `reaches-an-effect-sink`: a name the target reaches through the call graph TRANSITIVELY whose OWN body performs a declared effect directly. title: [BDL-068.S1.1][dev] lift the three AST derivations out of tests/ into a production package
description:
BDL-067 wrote three derivations that answer 'who else writes this, who else calls this, how many branches does this have' from the SOURCE rather than from a list. They live in the test suite and production code cannot import tests.

  tests/test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py      30 cases — a command's writing branches, from its own source
  tests/test_one_parent_post_condition_over_every_writer.py 25 cases — the graph writers, by shape
  tests/test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py       15 cases — the readers as a SHAPE (lists a directory AND parses YAML), over six listing verbs and six loaders

Move the derivation logic into a production package under application/. The tests keep their assertions and import the lifted code.

DONE WHEN:
- no derivation logic remains in tests/, and each test still fails on the shape it was written to catch — verified by re-running the mutants those modules already carry (.22 proved five evasion spellings red against the narrower detector; those cases must still go red)
- a derivation with no test that fails on a fifth body is NOT lifted; report it instead
- beadloom lint --strict rc 0 with the new package placed inside the layer rules

CONSTRAINT FROM CONTEXT: the derivation is over a SHAPE, never a spelling. A check that asks for one way of writing something is a check five other spellings walk past, and that is measured on this repository rather than supposed.

title: [BDL-068] The flow's rules are advice; make them instruments
description:
Six ordered slices converting this project's multi-agent flow from rules an agent is asked to follow into instruments that report when it did not. S1 builds the instrument the other five are measured by.

Docs: .claude/development/docs/features/BDL-068/ (PRD, RFC, CONTEXT, PLAN all Approved 2026-09-02).

THE THESIS, measured rather than argued: every existing flow check reads a channel it declares and is read as answering a question about all channels. review-brief counts bead comments and prints '0 withheld'. The commit hook judges the paths a commit stages and is blind to a neighbour's hunk. mutation-scope reports a target outside the source paths, and no runner produces the score that target was declared for.

FOUR PROOFS: a duty shipped with no runner (BDL-061 S4, and four BDL-067 beads reporting four hand methods as prose); the review's independence defeated through ACTIVE.md (#212) and then through commit bodies (#219), both found only because the reviewers declared them; a guard bound to Edit|Write that does not see a write through Bash (#170); nine 'green on the tree' measurements all taken on macOS while the CI legs are Ubuntu, where the tenth was red on all six.

BEADS ARE CREATED PER SLICE, not for the epic. Writing 24 beads now means writing 20 before the first slice has taught anything — the re-plan rule expressed as structure rather than discipline.

NOT IN SCOPE: #214, #215, #216, #217, #218, #220, #221, #222 (init/Gate product defects); the docs-audit classifier family (#173, #180, #205, #206, #209); BDL-066 (observability — this epic is about HOLDING a rule, that one about SEEING what an agent was told); patches to bd upstream.

title: [BDL-067 follow-up][bug] the wizard's Edit: path is hard-wrapped mid-token, and CI caught it where nine local runs did not
description:
FOUND BY CI ON PR #58 — six legs red, one test, on ubuntu where nine consecutive local runs on macOS were green.

    FAILED tests/test_every_wizard_answer_is_judged.py::TestEveryAnswerThatLeavesAGraphFileIsJudged::test_the_answer_names_the_files_it_left_in_what_it_says_last[edit]
    assert '.beadloom/_graph' in '... /tmp/pytest-of-runner/pytest-0/test_the_answer_names_the_file1/edit/.beadloom/_g\nraph/services.yml ...'

ROOT CAUSE, and it is in the PRODUCT rather than in the test. init_flow.py:279 prints an absolute path through rich: console.print(f"\n[bold]Edit:[/bold] {graph_path}"). rich hard-wraps at the console width (80 when not a terminal) and inserts a real newline MID-TOKEN. An adopter on a deep directory is handed a path broken across two lines that cannot be copy-pasted — in a message whose entire purpose is to tell them which file to open.

WHY MACOS NEVER SAW IT, and this is the epic's own class one more time: the wrap position depends on the path length. The runner's prefix is 68 characters, leaving 12 before the 80-column break, which splits `.beadloom/_g` from `raph/`. macOS tmp paths are LONGER, so the whole token moves to the next line intact and the assertion passes. The test was true of one shape while a neighbouring shape existed.

REPRODUCED LOCALLY, byte for byte, by matching the runner's path length rather than by guessing:
    uv run pytest --basetemp=/private/tmp/pytest-of-runnerX <the test>
    -> the same assertion, the same split at `.beadloom/_g`.
COLUMNS does not reproduce it: the value never reaches the Console under CliRunner.

FIX: print the path without hard wrapping (soft_wrap), so the emitted text carries no inserted newline. The terminal may still fold it visually; the string an adopter copies stays whole. Do NOT fix this by normalising newlines in the test — the defect is that the product emits a broken path.

COORDINATOR NOTE, recorded because it is the measurement failure behind this: I reported "green on the tree" nine times over this epic and every one of those runs was macOS. The CI legs are ubuntu-latest. Clean-room discipline caught file-scope problems and nothing in this epic ever measured a second platform. That is what `beadloom-mr2l.61` already records from the other direction (fifteen tests skip on Linux that do not skip on macOS).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED. Fixed in the product, not in the test.

FIX: init_flow.py:279 prints the `edit` answer's path with soft_wrap=True, so rich emits no inserted newline and the terminal folds it visually instead. An adopter can copy the path out of the message whose only purpose is to name it.

RED FIRST, against a reproduction rather than against a theory. COLUMNS does not reach the Console under CliRunner, so width could not be forced; the wrap position is a function of the PATH LENGTH. The runner's prefix is 68 characters and the console is 80, which splits `.beadloom/_g` from `raph/`. Reproduced byte for byte locally by matching that length:
    uv run pytest --basetemp=/private/tmp/pytest-of-runnerX   (30 chars, the runner's own)
    -> assert '.beadloom/_graph' in '... /edit/.beadloom/_g\nraph/services.yml ...'
With soft_wrap reverted, BOTH the original test and the new one fail; with it in place, 15 passed.

NEW TEST: test_the_path_it_names_survives_the_render_whole asserts `.beadloom/_graph/services.yml` CONTIGUOUSLY in the output. The old assertion took a substring that a wrap can leave intact by accident, which is why nine macOS runs were green; the contiguous form is the only shape a wrap cannot satisfy by coincidence. It reuses THE_ANSWER_THAT_IS_NOT_JUDGED rather than adding a second name for the same answer.

DOCS: the change is described in docs/domains/onboarding/features/agent-prime/SPEC.md, in the list where this epic records what it learned. docs/domains/onboarding/README.md was re-attested for that one pair only, after reading its init_flow paragraph and confirming it claims nothing about the message's rendering — `--pair` scoped, 35 pairs left explicitly unclaimed (BDL-UX #163: a bare re-baseline is a doc nobody read).

MEASURED: 7866 passed, 0 failed, at the runner's own path length; beadloom ci rc 0; sync-check rc 0; ruff clean; mypy clean over 227 files. Green on the tree AND at the path length that produced the failure — the second is the one that matters here, and it is the measurement this epic never took.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 2 major

Ninth pass, scoped as instructed. Major 1 and minor 1 of `.26` are CLOSED, verified by my own
measurement on the tree `.26` measured. Cycle 9 introduced no regression. NOTHING BELOW BLOCKS
THE MERGE: both majors are documentation-and-test defects with no adopter-facing falsehood, and
under the stop rule both should be FILED as their own work items rather than fixed here. If the
question is "merge or tenth cycle", the answer is merge.

## PROCESS FACTS, FIRST

**The withholding did not run, and my launch prompt carried `.27`'s two reports.**
`review-brief` reported 0 comments withheld. Beyond that, my prompt named both of `.27`'s
findings before I had read a line — the unfalsifiable headline, and the cross-check computing at
the FILE grain — and told me which one to judge carefully. I re-derived both by my own
measurement before writing anything below, and both turned out sharper than the prompt stated
(the cross-check's module docstring states the OLD rule as its invariant, which the prompt did
not say). But I cannot claim I would have found either unaided, and the second major below is
one I did find unaided, which is the only part of this comment the withholding failure does not
touch. I read the commit bodies of `dcdfdb6` and `5f46c4f` (BDL-UX #219 — they carry the
authors' full accounts and nothing counts them). I did not read ACTIVE.md (#212). Nothing from
`beadloom-6i5q`/#218, `beadloom-l22o`/#220, `beadloom-0mb5`/#221, `beadloom-gv0z`/#217 or the
two `.5` doc drifts is re-filed.

**Measured by me, on this tree at `5f46c4f`:** `uv run pytest` 7865 passed, 11 skipped,
1 xfailed, 0 failed (216.71 s); `ruff check src/ tests/` clean; `mypy src/` clean over 227
files; `beadloom lint --strict` rc 0; `beadloom doctor` rc 0; `beadloom sync-check` rc 0 (the
same six warns `.26` recorded); `beadloom ci` rc 0; `beadloom diff --since main` = 1 node added
(`graph-files`), 1 edge, 0 changed, 0 removed. Working tree clean apart from
`.beads/interactions.jsonl`, so all of this is HEAD's source.

**THE CLEAN-ROOM MEASUREMENT `.27` COULD NOT TAKE, TAKEN.** `git archive HEAD` into a temp
directory, 1047 files, fresh `uv` environment: **7678 passed, 197 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 FAILED
in 210 s** — `tests/test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh`.
It is NOT this branch's: the same file run in a clean room built from `main` fails the same case
(`1 failed, 42 passed`). The cause is environmental — `REPO_ROOT` is the tree the test file sits
in, `.beadloom/index.db` is gitignored, so `sync-check` runs against an index with no recorded
baselines and reads the pairs as not-`ok`. So the honest claim is: **green in a clean room over
1047 files, except one pre-existing case that fails identically on `main`.** The higher skip
count (197 vs 11) is the optional language grammars and `graphql` being absent there, which is
the clean room's limit and not a result.

## THE FIX — MAJOR 1 OF `.26` IS CLOSED, MEASURED

`_ATTRIBUTION[(False, True)]` and `[(False, False)]` now deny writing the NODE. I rebuilt the
tree `.26` measured (`_a_tree_whose_annotated_node_is_not_the_failing_one`) and ran
`init --bootstrap` on it. `legacy.yml` IS rewritten by that run (I measured the bytes), and the
report now prints:

    The scaffold above was written, but the check that follows it did not pass.
    Error: the graph already in .beadloom/_graph/ does not pass the rules this command wrote alongside it.
      domain-needs-parent: ledger (.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml)
    This command did not write the node(s) named above — they were already in .beadloom/_graph/
      — so the rule(s) this command wrote are meeting a graph that predates them.

The false sentence is gone and the property is restored: that corner is selected by the failing
node's entry being byte-identical to the one that was there, so the denial cannot disagree with
its key. All three green pins moved with it — the `.feature` step, the step function
(`_then_init_says_the_failing_node_predates_it`, with the reason in its docstring), and the
class assertions. Grepped `docs/`, `src/`, `tests/` for `graph file(s) named beside`,
`was already on disk` and `did not write the graph file`: zero hits outside ACTIVE.md.
`TestEachSentenceSpeaksAtTheGrainItsKeyIsReadAt` is a good class — it checks the table AS a
table, carries an anti-vacuity case over the selection, and its end-to-end case MEASURES its own
premise instead of assuming it.

**Minor 1 of `.26` is closed at the location it was filed** — `graph-files/DOC.md` now states
the shape the test class states, with the `.25` widening and its reason. See major 2 for where
the same sentence survives.

## MAJOR 1 — the independent cross-check states, and computes, the rule the implementation stopped using

`tests/test_init_one_table_over_every_axis.py:41-46` (module docstring, invariant 3),
`:462-478` (`RunOutcome.wrote_the_failing_graph_file` / `.corner`), `:788-800` (the class
docstring).

Issue. The module's own statement of invariant 3 reads: "The bug-report request appears exactly
where THIS run wrote both the rules and **the graph file the failing node came from**." That was
the key until `.24`. The shipped key is `_this_run_wrote_the_node_that_fails` — the NODE.
`RunOutcome.corner` computes the file-grain answer and the three cases then require the report to
agree with it, under a docstring saying "the report is then required to agree with the
measurement ... it FAILS if the report and the tree disagree". Both claims are now false: the
report and the tree can disagree at the node grain in a way this measurement cannot see.

MEASURED by me, over all ten red runs the table performs, computing both grains side by side:
they AGREE in every cell (`--yes-bootstrap-ours` (True,True), `--bootstrap-bootstrap-theirs`
(True,False), `--import-import-theirs` (False,False), `wizard-both-theirs` (True,False), and so
on). The agreement is a consequence of the arrangements, not of the rules: since `.21`,
`generate_skeletons` annotates every node on disk, so whenever a cell rewrites `legacy.yml` it
also rewrites the failing node `ledger`'s own entry. The one tree where the two rules diverge —
the file moves for a SIBLING while the failing node does not — is exactly the tree `.26`
measured, and no cell of this table builds it.

So this is the answer to the question the assignment posed about it: it is a coincidence, not
the strongest test in the suite, **because the divergence is not stated anywhere in the module**
— the module states the superseded rule as its invariant. Two consequences, in the order of
their cost:
- It cannot fail if the implementation regresses to the file grain, which is the defect `.24`
  and `.27` were both spent on. (The epic is not uncovered: the sibling
  `TestTheGraphHalfIsAskedOfTheNodeAndNotOfTheFile` and the new
  `TestEachSentenceSpeaksAtTheGrainItsKeyIsReadAt` do build the divergence tree and would go
  red. That is why this is not Critical and does not block.)
- It will fail FALSELY, blaming a correct implementation, the first time an arrangement stops
  annotating the failing node.

Recommendation. Either compute the corner at the node grain here as well — the module already
digests `.beadloom/_graph/` before and after, and a `{ref_id: node}` digest is the same walk —
or keep the file-grain digest as a deliberately coarser instrument and SAY so: rename
`wrote_the_failing_graph_file`, correct invariant 3's wording to name the node, and add one case
asserting that on THIS table the two grains coincide, so the day they stop coinciding is the day
the case reports it. The second option is cheaper and keeps the independence, which is worth
keeping — an expectation derived by a different route is the right shape; an expectation derived
by a superseded route and described as the current one is not.

## MAJOR 2 — the stale detector sentence minor 1 closed in the DOC is still live one directory away

`docs/domains/onboarding/features/agent-prime/SPEC.md:85`.

Issue. It reads: "`tests/test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py` derives the readers from
the source — **every function that both globs `*.yml` and calls `yaml.safe_load`** — and fails
when a fifth body appears". That is `.24`'s detector verbatim, and it is the exact sentence
minor 1 of `.26` was filed against. `.25` replaced it after measuring five spellings it let
through; the shipped detector is `LISTS_A_DIRECTORY = {glob, rglob, iterdir, listdir, scandir,
walk}` crossed with six loaders (`tests/test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py:271`).
Cycle 9 corrected the sentence in `graph-files/DOC.md` and left the twin in the SPEC. Found by
grepping the docs for the symbols the changed files define, not from any note.

The error direction is the mild one — the SPEC understates the check, so a maintainer would
believe an `iterdir` reader escapes a check that in fact catches it — which is why this is
Major-but-not-blocking rather than Critical. It is still a doc making a false statement about a
guard this epic built, in a file this branch edited.

Recommendation. Replace with the DOC's own corrected sentence: "a function that both LISTS a
directory and PARSES YAML, by any name the standard library or PyYAML offers for either".

## THE JUDGEMENT ASKED FOR: are the remaining user-facing sentences true of every corner?

**No, and yes — the answer splits cleanly, and the split is the useful part.**

TRUE OF EVERY CORNER THAT CAN SELECT THEM, by construction, after cycle 9:
- all four `_ATTRIBUTION` sentences. The two node-chosen corners deny writing a node and the
  key is the node; the `rules.yml` corner denies writing a file and the key is that file's
  bytes. The bug-report request — the one sentence that costs an adopter something — is now
  sound on every corner: I checked the fallback route too, and a nodeless finding cannot reach
  `(True, True)`, because the only rules `generate_rules` writes (`domain-needs-parent`,
  `feature-needs-parent`) are both node-bearing, so nodeless findings only arise from an
  adopter's own `rules.yml`, which forces the rules half to False.
- `WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM`, guarded by the `if not written: return` precondition.
- the `beadloom ci` line, which is BUILT from `step.name` and `step.summary`. This is the model
  the others should follow: it is the one sentence in the report that cannot be wrong because it
  is derived rather than written beside its key, and it survived every renderer for that reason.

NOT TRUE OF EVERY CORNER, OR NOT CHECKABLE AT ALL — three sentences, and they need DERIVING:

**Minor 1 — the headline halves, `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:906-913.**
`_GRAPH_HALF` says "the graph this command just wrote" / "the graph already in
.beadloom/_graph/" while the key is one node. I confirm `.27`'s report and put it at the same
grain: on the tree above, this run wrote `services.yml` fresh, rewrote `legacy.yml`, and the
headline says "the graph already in .beadloom/_graph/". That is not FALSE — "the graph" is a
definite description whose extent the sentence never fixes, so no tree can refute it. It is one
step milder than the four defects already fixed: not a sentence that is true of one shape while
a neighbouring shape exists, but a sentence with no shape at all. Two further corners make it
concrete: `_this_run_wrote_the_node_that_fails` falls back to `bool(files_this_run_wrote)` when
no finding names an attributable node, and at this call site that is unconditionally True
(the precondition guarantees it), so a rule-level finding about the adopter's own tree still
opens "the graph this command just wrote". Recommendation: derive it from the key — name the
node(s) below rather than "the graph", e.g. "the node(s) below, which this command wrote" /
"which were already in .beadloom/_graph/". The rule lines follow immediately, so the reference
is unambiguous and, unlike today's wording, an adopter can check it.

**Minor 2 — `_REPAIR_ADVICE`, `:952-956`, whose comment claims "true of every corner of the
table above".** It says "the graph file named beside each node above". `_failing_rule_lines`
(`:1077-1094`) deliberately emits two other line shapes — the bare rule name for a finding about
no single node, and `rule: node` with no file for a node no graph file claims — and its own
docstring defends them ("an unattributed line is still true, and a guessed file is not"). On
those lines no file is named beside anything, so the advice describes the output it is printed
under incorrectly. Reachable through an adopter's hand-written `module_coverage` or
`forbid_import` rule. Recommendation: build the advice from the lines actually printed.

**Minor 3 — `_report_rules_that_would_not_load`, `:1189-1192`:** "so the graph this command
wrote was not checked against it". This branch consults no attribution key at all, yet asserts
authorship of "the graph" — on an `--import` run over an inherited tree, what this command wrote
is `imported.yml` and what went unchecked is the whole graph. Same unfalsifiable shape as the
headline, and it should be keyed or narrowed for the same reason.

So: **this is the fifth wording instance of the same class, and it will not be the last while
the sentences are written beside their keys instead of built from them.** The `_ATTRIBUTION`
table has now been corrected three times (`.16`, `.24`, `.27`) and each correction restored the
"true by construction" property by hand. The `ci` line has never been corrected once, because it
is generated from the two fields every renderer reads. That contrast is the finding under the
finding, and it is worth one work item stating it as a rule for this report: a sentence that
names a fact the code measures must be built from the value that measures it.

plus `docs/services/cli.md` and `docs/guides/parallel-waves.md`, which are `beadloom-e8s4.5`'s

Issue. `.24` moved the graph half of the key from "this run wrote the FILE the failing node
came from" to "this run created or changed the NODE" and left both sentences saying
`file(s)`. Before `.24` those sentences were true by construction: the corner was SELECTED
by the file's bytes being unchanged, so a claim about the file could not be wrong. `.24`
selects the corner by the node and still prints a claim about the file, so the claim is now
independent of what selected it.

MEASURED by me, twice, on a project with `src/index.ts` and an inherited
`.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml` holding `ledger` (orphan, documented, untouched) and
`warehouse` (parented, undocumented). `beadloom init --bootstrap` prints:

    Error: the graph already in .beadloom/_graph/ does not pass the rules this command
      wrote alongside it.
      domain-needs-parent: ledger (.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml)
    This command did not write the graph file(s) named beside the node(s) above — they
      were already on disk — so the rule(s) this command wrote are meeting a graph that
      predates them.

and `diff` against a copy taken before the run shows `.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml` — the
one file the message names — was rewritten by that command: `warehouse` gained
`docs: [docs/domains/warehouse/README.md]`, and every entry in the file was
re-serialised (the adopter's two-space list indentation is flattened). An adopter who runs
`git diff` sees the file modified and the sentence denying it.

The node-grain answer is right and is an improvement; the sentence is what did not move.
This is the same class this epic has filed three times — an instrument whose words name one
fact while the code measures another (the review of `.11` major 1, of `.16` major 2, of
`.23` major 4) — introduced this cycle by the fix for the last of them.

It is pinned green in three places, so all three move with the fix:
- `tests/test_init_report_says_whose_failure_it_is.py:781`
  `test_the_failing_node_is_the_earlier_runs_though_its_file_moved` asserts `(False, True)`
  is printed on the tree whose sibling premise case at `:766` has just asserted the file
  moved. The two cases in one class assert contradictory facts about one file.
- `tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature`, last step of
  "a failing node an earlier run wrote is not blamed on this one":
  `And the command says the graph file was already there` — a scenario in the user's
  vocabulary asserting a statement that is false about the user's tree.
- `tests/acceptance/steps/..._steps.py:849-860` `_then_init_says_the_graph_file_predates_it`,
  whose own docstring reads "a run that met an inherited graph said the opposite of the
  truth about it".

Recommendation. Move the sentences to the grain the fact is now at, and the scenario step
with them:

    (False, True)  "This command did not write the node(s) named above — they were
                    already in .beadloom/_graph/ — so the rule(s) this command wrote are
                    meeting a graph that predates them."
    (False, False) "This command wrote neither the rule(s) above nor the node(s) they
                    name — both were already in .beadloom/_graph/ — so nothing this run
                    produced is what fails."

and rewrite `:922-926` to key the table on "this run wrote the failing NODE", which is what
`_this_run_wrote_the_node_that_fails` now returns. Rename the acceptance step to "the
command says the failing node was already there". This is the one finding I would put in a
fix cycle rather than re-plan: it is entirely inside cycle 8's own change, it is small, and
it ships a false sentence to an adopter.

## MAJOR 2 — the open question, answered: NO, and the corner it was decided to close is still open on the commonest shape

`src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:796-833` (`_graph_nodes_now`), `:1086-1122`
(`_this_run_wrote_the_node_that_fails`).

**Is a node whose `docs:` field this run wrote a node this run wrote? No — not for this
instrument, and the grain was never the axis that decides it.** The instrument exists to
answer one question: did this run produce the property that makes this node fail. The
failing rule is `domain-needs-parent`, which reads `kind` and `part_of` edges. `docs:` is
not a field any rule in the failing finding can see. A run that annotated a node did not
write anything the rule read, so answering "yes" attributes to Beadloom a failure Beadloom
did not cause. `.23` moved from file to node believing the annotation was a property OF THE
FILE; `.24` measured that it is a property of the NODE as well and said so. The variable
that actually separates the two cases is not how coarse the sample is — it is whether the
part of the node that changed is a part the rule reads.

MEASURED by me, on `.23`'s own two trees: they do not swap. An inherited `legacy.yml`
holding one undocumented orphan still prints `(True, True)` — "This is a defect in
Beadloom's bootstrap rather than in your project — please report it with the rule name(s)
above" — about a node no writer in this run produced. That is a single-node inherited graph
file, which is at least as ordinary as the two-node one `.24` did close, so the cost `.23`
named ("paid by the adopter in a bug report and by this project in triage") is still being
paid on a common path.

Recommendation, and it is deliberately not the option `.23` rejected. Do NOT exempt a
`docs:`-only diff: `.23` was right that a filter over one field is the shape
`init_flow.py`'s own docstring argues against, and it goes stale the next time the block
gains a writer. Instead key the node sample on a RULE-RELEVANT PROJECTION of the node,
derived rather than hand-listed: digest the node restricted to the fields the rule engine
can read, taken from `graph/rules/loader.py`'s own authoring surface. Then a `docs:`-only
annotation is not a change the failing rule can see and the corner stops firing for it,
while a `kind`, `source` or edge rewrite still reads as ours — so the error direction
`.24` correctly insisted on (`created-or-changed`, never `created`) is preserved rather
than traded away. This project already holds the precedent for exactly that derivation:
`test_every_authoring_key_the_loader_accepts_has_a_type` holds `_detect_rule_type` to
`graph.rules.loader.AUTHORING_KEYS`, so a rule dimension added later widens the projection
by the same act instead of leaving a filter behind. A rule that one day reads `docs:` would
then make a `docs:`-only annotation attributable to this run, which is the right answer and
the one a hand-written exemption would get wrong.

This is NOT a defect in `.24`'s execution. `.24` was told to implement a decision, it
implemented it, measured that the decision's stated outcome did not follow, refused to
write that it had, and put the measurement in the class docstring. Filing this against the
bead's work would punish exactly the behaviour that made it visible. The right disposition
is a new work item alongside `beadloom-6i5q` and `beadloom-l22o`, carrying this answer and
the projection above — not a re-open of cycle 8.

## MINOR 1 — the component DOC describes `.24`'s detector, which `.25` widened

`docs/domains/onboarding/components/graph-files/DOC.md`, "Tests" section: "a function that
both globs `*.yml` and calls `yaml.safe_load` is a graph-file reader". The shipped detector
matches six listing verbs (`glob`, `rglob`, `iterdir`, `listdir`, `scandir`, `walk`) and six
loaders. As written, the DOC names the escape hatch `.25` measured and closed — a reader
spelled with `iterdir` would read as out of reach of the check that is in fact designed to
catch it. Recommendation: restate the shape as "a function that both LISTS a directory and
PARSES YAML, by any name the standard library or PyYAML offers for either", which is the
sentence the test class already uses.

## MINOR 2 — one acceptance scenario names implementation scope

`tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature`: "Then no reader in init's
own modules raised on the file it could not parse". An observer cannot see "init's own
modules". The comment above it explains why the true observable claim ("the command does
not traceback") would be false today, so the phrasing is honest rather than ceremonial and
the step is non-vacuous — it checks frames and is paired with an explicit anti-vacuity step
("the scaffold is written from the graph files that do parse"). Recommendation: when
`beadloom-l22o` lands, replace it with the observable sentence rather than leaving the
implementation-shaped one in place.

## OBSERVED, NOT FILED

The four new surface-drift warns (`README.md`, `README.ru.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
`docs/guides/bdd-scenarios.md`) follow from the graph gaining the `graph-files` node.
`sync-check --record-surface` was deliberately not run because it is all-or-nothing and
would also clear `docs/services/cli.md` and `docs/guides/parallel-waves.md`, which belong
to the open `beadloom-e8s4.5`. That is the right call — masking another bead's drift to
clear your own is worse than four warns — and it means `.5` now has six drifts to clear,
not two. Those two remain open, as the sixth consecutive review to find them; recorded,
not re-filed.

`--release` is expected to report that it could not establish the verdict was recorded by
anyone other than the bead's author: every role on this tracker writes under one identity.
That is the normal answer here and not a defect.

title: [BDL-067.24][dev] the three regressions this epic introduced, and the attribution instrument
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.23 majors 3, 4, 5 + one minor. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-02: cycle 8 fixes ONLY what this epic broke or was asked to decide. Majors 1 and 2 (the step-sequence class) are re-planned into their own work item — the first application of the re-plan rule this project ranked P0 in the ROADMAP an hour earlier.

MAJOR 3 — init now tracebacks, and we did it. .21 removed generate_skeletons' node-list parameter, so --bootstrap always calls _load_graph_from_yaml (doc_generator.py:40, reached from setup.py:1219), which calls yaml.safe_load with no try. Before .21 that branch passed its own nodes and never read the tree. MEASURED: on a project carrying one hand-edited .beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml that does not parse, `beadloom init --bootstrap` prints a raw yaml.parser.ParserError traceback at the adopter. THE SAME COMMIT added exactly this guard to the two sibling readers (_existing_graph at doc_classify.py:82-87, which also guards isinstance(data, dict), and _graph_file_of_each_node at setup.py:1000-1005) and listed 'the unreadable-YAML guards' in its own message as delivered. The reading side was hardened and the writing side was not, one wave after that exact split was diagnosed.
  FIX: give _load_graph_from_yaml both guards its siblings carry — except (yaml.YAMLError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError), and the isinstance(data, dict) check (a graph file holding a top-level list raises AttributeError on data.get).
  AND THE SHAPE: there are now FOUR readers of .beadloom/_graph/*.yml with four skip policies — _load_graph_from_yaml, _existing_graph, _graph_file_of_each_node, _patch_docs_field. This is the one-invariant-in-N-bodies shape .21 consolidated for the WRITERS, standing on the READERS. Consolidate it the same way; do not add a fifth policy.

MAJOR 4 — the attribution instrument. The reviewer decided it and the decision is adopted: (True, True) — 'This is a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap ... please report it' — is printed for a node no writer in this run produced, whenever this run merely ANNOTATED the file that node sits in. That is the exact defect bead .9 was created to remove.
