comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 5 major

Seventh pass. The three converted axes hold. The divergence moved off all three.

## THE ASSIGNMENT, ANSWERED FIRST

**Is the writing side converted?** Yes, on the three symbols the sixth pass named, and
each conversion is sound.

- The post-condition is one function (`src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/parent_edges.py`),
  both writers import it, and the writer population is DERIVED (calls `write_yaml_atomic`
  and builds a payload holding `nodes`). I checked the derivation's own blind spot: every
  `yaml.dump` / `safe_dump` site in the product is `atomic_io`, `doc_sync/surface.py` and
  `flow_config.py`, so the single-commit-point premise is true today and
  `test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py:813` holds it there. The three
  `write_yaml_atomic` callers outside `onboarding` (`graph/loader.py:203`,
  `services/commands/index_ops.py:280,296`) are patchers and are correctly excluded.
- `generate_skeletons(project_root)` takes one parameter and the signature assertion
  cannot go stale.
- `_this_run_wrote_a_graph_file` asks the tree, not the branch, and the wizard's `cancel`
  is judged.

**Did the prediction hold?** No. Not a third writer of nodes, not a fifth exit from
`init`. The fourth caller of `generate_skeletons` (`docs_generate`) exists, is declared,
and its vacuity claim survives measurement — I ran `docs generate` over a patched graph
with no reindex and `beadloom ci` was green, because `ci` re-indexes as its own first
step.

**The divergence is somewhere neither side names, and it is not about a symbol at all.**
Every instrument this epic has built ranges over ONE symbol's callers. Nothing ranges
over one entry point's STEPS. `init` holds three hand-written step sequences — the
`--bootstrap` branch inline in `setup.py`, `non_interactive_init`, `interactive_init` —
and no artifact states what the sequence is. So the next divergence was a step that two
sequences run and the third does not (major 1), and a step that runs once over one
writer's output and is never revisited (major 2). Both were reachable through the whole
epic; six reviews and two derived enumerators did not see them, because the question
"which steps does this entry point run" has never been asked of the source.

That is the finding above the list. `.21`'s three fixes are each correct and each is the
last fix of its kind that a per-symbol enumeration can produce.

## THE DECISION THAT IS MINE: THE ATTRIBUTION INSTRUMENT

Reproduced first, on two trees differing by one field, `init --bootstrap`:

    inherited node without `docs:` -> (True, True)  "This is a defect in Beadloom's
                                                     bootstrap ... please report it"
    inherited node with `docs:`    -> (False, True) "the rule(s) this command wrote are
                                                     meeting a graph that predates them"

Same rule, same node, same file. `.22`'s report is accurate and its pair of cases is the
right pair.

**Decision: split the question, and move the GRAPH half to per node, created-or-changed.**
Keep `_graph_files_now`'s byte digest for the two questions it answers correctly — the
verdict PRECONDITION (`_this_run_wrote_a_graph_file`: did this run change the adopter's
tree at all — a run that only patched `docs:` did, and should be judged) and the RULES
half (`rules.yml` holds no nodes, so the file is the grain). Replace the graph half of
`_ATTRIBUTION`'s key with a before/after sample of `{ref_id: node-as-written}`, taken in
the same one place `graph_before` is taken. "This run wrote the node" becomes: the ref_id
was absent before, or its content differs.

What each option costs:

- **Per FILE and per BYTES, as it stands.** Zero code. Cost: the `(True, True)` corner —
  the only one that asks for a bug report — fires for a node no writer in this run
  produced, and it fires on the COMMON path, not an edge case: `generate_skeletons`
  writes a README for every docs-less node in the tree and patches the field back, so an
  inherited orphan is annotated by default. This re-creates the defect `.9` was created
  to remove, one level down. That cost is paid by the adopter in a bug report and by this
  project in triage.
- **Per node CREATED.** Fixes the corner. Cost: it mis-attributes the opposite way — a
  node this run REWROTE into failing (a kind or source change on a pre-existing ref_id)
  reads as "your project's", so the instrument's error direction becomes "hide our own
  defect". This epic exists because a green exit hid one; buying the fix in that currency
  is the wrong trade.
- **Per node CREATED-OR-CHANGED (recommended).** Fixes the corner and keeps the rewrite
  case ours. Cost: one before-sample that parses rather than digests (a handful of small
  files, taken where `graph_before` already is); the "unreadable file is skipped"
  limitation carries over at a finer grain and must be re-stated; and the module keeps
  two instruments. That last is not a regression against `.17` — `.17` removed a boolean
  read off a WRITER'S RETURN VALUE, and both instruments here are read off the tree, so
  the property that made `.17` right is preserved.
- **Exempt a `docs:`-only diff.** Reject, on this repository's own stated grounds:
  `init_flow.py` argues "THE ORDER RATHER THAN A FILTER ... a filter removes only today's
  consequence, and goes stale the next time this block gains a writer." A filter over one
  field is that, exactly.

**Was pinning it rather than fixing it the right call? Yes.** Three reasons, and I would
not have said yes without the third. It is a product decision with a cost on both sides,
and a test bead that changes the product to make its own assertion read better is worse
than one that records the answer. The pin is falsifiable in the right direction: both
corners are asserted, so whoever moves the instrument must come here and re-state them.
And `test_the_two_trees_fail_the_same_rule_on_the_same_node` is the anti-vacuity case
that makes the pair mean something — without it, two different sentences would not be
evidence of anything. The finding is carried in the test file's own docstring, not only
in the commit message, which is where a future reader looks. Filed as major 4 because
the decision now needs implementing, not because pinning was wrong.

## MAJOR 1 — `auto_link_docs` is run by two of the three entry points; doc-sync is off on the third

`src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1210-1219` (the `--bootstrap` branch) ·
`src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py:83,290` (the only two callers).

Issue. `auto_link_docs(project_root, nodes)` links an adopter's pre-existing documents to
graph nodes and patches `docs:` back. `non_interactive_init` and `interactive_init` call
it; the `--bootstrap` branch does not. It also still takes a node list — the exact
parameter shape `.21` removed from `generate_skeletons`, on that function's sibling, and
both call sites hand it one writer's output.

MEASURED, on two identical ordinary adopter trees (`src/orders/a.ts`, and
`docs/domains/orders/README.md` written by the adopter before init ran — no inherited
graph file, nothing hand-edited):

    beadloom init --yes --mode bootstrap  -> node `orders` carries
                                             docs: [docs/domains/orders/README.md]
                                             sync-check: 1 pair tracked
    beadloom init --bootstrap             -> node `orders` carries no `docs:`
                                             sync-check: "No sync pairs found."

One command, one declared mode, two flags, and on one of them the product's core function
is silently off. This is BDL-UX #216's shape on a second function. `.21` closed the
`generate_skeletons` half of the same gap and left this half, because the enumeration was
over one symbol's callers.

The instrument that should have caught it exists and is one fixture property short.
`test_init_one_table_over_every_axis.py::test_every_branch_offering_the_mode_leaves_the_same_graph`
compares all three entry points at mode `bootstrap`, and passes because its fixture
(`_a_project_with_code_and_docs`, `test_init_agrees_across_its_modes.py:241`) is a flat
`src/index.ts` plus documents at `docs/<name>.md` — none of which is at a path
`auto_link_docs` matches for the node `src`. On a virgin tree the divergence is invisible:
`generate_skeletons` creates the document and patches the field itself. It needs an
adopter document at a path the node would be linked to.

Recommendation. Two parts, and the second is the one that matters. (a) Give the
`--bootstrap` branch the same step sequence as the other two, or route it through
`non_interactive_init` so there is one sequence rather than three. (b) State the sequence
where it can be checked: derive, per entry point, the ordered list of graph-touching steps
it reaches, and assert the three agree — the same move `.22` made for one symbol's
callers, made for one entry point's steps. Add an adopter document at a matched path to
the shared fixture so the existing three-way comparison can fail.

## MAJOR 2 — `generate_rules` is the second whole-graph artifact rendered from one writer's node list

`src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/rules_gen.py:29` (`kinds = {n["kind"] for n in nodes}`) ·
`src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py:261-262` (`if nodes and not rules_path.exists()`).

Issue. `rules.yml` is a statement about the WHOLE graph. It is written from
`bootstrap_project`'s own node list, inside `bootstrap_project`, before `import_docs` runs
— and never revisited, because the guard is `not rules_path.exists()`. So the rule set is
derived from one writer's output. That is the sentence `.21` wrote into
`generate_skeletons`' docstring, still true of the other generated whole-graph artifact.

MEASURED, twice:

    monolith, src/orders/ + docs/checkout.md + docs/adr-1.md, `init --yes --mode both`
      -> graph holds nodes of kind `feature` and `adr` (imported.yml)
      -> rules.yml holds `domain-needs-parent` only; no `feature-needs-parent`
      -> an unparented `feature` node added by hand: lint --strict rc 0, "1 rules
         evaluated". The same node as `kind: domain`: rc 1. Same absence of a parent.

    microservices (services/gateway, services/billing) + docs/runbook.md,
    `init --yes --mode both`
      -> bootstrap classifies both dirs as `service`, so `generate_rules` writes NOTHING
         and rules.yml is never created
      -> `import_docs` then writes a `domain` node (`runbook`)
      -> lint --strict: "0 violations, 0 rules evaluated", rc 0. `beadloom ci` rc 0.

The second measurement is the sharp one. The adopter's scaffold has domain nodes and no
rules file at all, and every check is green because nothing is checked. The verdict
machinery cannot see this by construction: it asks "does the graph pass the rules", and a
graph with zero rules always passes. `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph`'s docstring says
"the next divergence between what `init` writes and what `init` requires is visible here";
a divergence in which `init` requires nothing is not.

This is the shape the BRIEF rejected as a fix arriving through the ordering instead:
"ships every adopter one structural rule weaker than this project runs, with nothing that
later reminds a human to restore it". It is also the BRIEF's own diagnosis of
`test_lint_zero_violations_after_init` — an assertion that cannot fail reporting green —
one level up, in the product.

Recommendation. Make the rule set a function of the finished graph, not of one writer:
generate or top up `rules.yml` after the last graph writer in the run, reading the node
kinds off `.beadloom/_graph/` (`_graph_file_of_each_node` already walks it). Adding a rule
to a file that exists is a change to the adopter's file and needs deciding — at minimum
`init` should say "the graph holds kinds K for which no rule was written" rather than
print nothing. State the post-condition where it can fail: every node kind present in the
graph on disk after `init` is either covered by a generated rule or named in a declared
exemption with a reason.

## MAJOR 3 — `.21` gave `--bootstrap` a tree read with no unreadable-YAML guard; `init` now tracebacks

`src/beadloom/onboarding/doc_generator.py:40` (`_load_graph_from_yaml`), reached from
`src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1219`.

Issue. `.21` removed `generate_skeletons`' node-list parameter, so the `--bootstrap`
branch now always calls `_load_graph_from_yaml`, which calls `yaml.safe_load` with no
`try`. Before `.21` that branch passed its own nodes and never read the tree
(`git show 64f575f3^:.../doc_generator.py:943` — `if nodes is None or edges is None`).

MEASURED, on a project carrying one hand-edited `.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml` that does
not parse: `beadloom init --bootstrap` prints a raw `yaml.parser.ParserError` traceback
through `setup.py:1219 -> doc_generator.py:955 -> doc_generator.py:40`.

The same commit added exactly this guard to the two sibling readers — `_existing_graph`
(`doc_classify.py:82-87`, which also guards `isinstance(data, dict)`) and
`_graph_file_of_each_node` (`setup.py:1000-1005`) — and its own message lists "the
unreadable-YAML guards" as delivered. The reading side was hardened and the writing side
was not, one wave after that was diagnosed. `_load_graph_from_yaml` is also missing the
`isinstance(data, dict)` guard: a graph file holding a top-level list raises
`AttributeError` on `data.get`.

Recommendation. Give `_load_graph_from_yaml` the same two guards its siblings carry
(`except (yaml.YAMLError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError): continue`, and the `isinstance`
check). Better: there are now four readers of `.beadloom/_graph/*.yml` with four
skip policies (`_load_graph_from_yaml`, `_existing_graph`, `_graph_file_of_each_node`,
`_patch_docs_field`) — this is the same one-invariant-in-N-bodies shape `.21` consolidated
for the writers, on the readers.

  - `_graph_files_now` digests every file under `.beadloom/_graph/` before any writer and
    again at verdict time, so attribution covers writers `setup.py` does not know about.
  - `_GRAPH_HALF` / `_RULES_HALF` / `_ATTRIBUTION` are a table over the full 2x2 product; a
    corner cannot be left unwritten. I hit three of the four corners on live trees and each
    printed the corner the tree was in (transcripts below).
  - `WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM` is printed by the verdict itself, so no caller can decline it.
  - `lint_step` and `gate_step_line` are shared with the Gate, so there is one verdict and one
    step line rather than two spellings.
  - `_graph_file_of_each_node` reads the files rather than a writer's return value.
  - `tests/test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py` finds `init`'s writing branches in
    `init`'s own source, seeded from every graph writer rather than from `bootstrap_project`.

Not converted:
  - The parent post-condition is stated once per WRITER, over that writer's own output:
    `bootstrap._missing_parent_edges` over `bootstrap_project`'s nodes,
    `doc_classify._missing_parent_edges` over `import_docs`'s nodes. Nothing states it over
    the tree. #217 is the consequence and is deliberately deferred (judged below); Major 3 is
    the shape.
  - `generate_skeletons` is called per BRANCH: two of three entry points read the tree, the
    third passes a node list. Major 1.
  - The branch enumerator's termination set is `{Return, Raise}`, and `init` terminates one
    writing path with `sys.exit(0)`. Major 2.

So the prediction this pass makes is narrow: the next divergence will not be a new report
corner or a missed attribution. It will be a third writer of graph nodes, a fourth caller of
`generate_skeletons`, or a fifth way out of `init` that is not `return`.

The one genuinely new thing in `.19` is worth saying plainly, because it is the first time in
six passes an instrument caught its own blind spot instead of the next reviewer catching it:
`TestTheEntryPointsLeaveOneGraphForOneDeclaredMode` states its limit, records the
`--bootstrap` divergence in the module docstring with a measurement, and routes it. That is
the behaviour the epic has been trying to buy. It did not extend to the two axes below,
which is why the count is 3 and not 0.

Major:

1. `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1190` — `--bootstrap` calls `generate_skeletons`
   with a node list where the other two entry points read the tree, so one declared mode
   leaves two different graphs on a tree that is not virgin.
   `non_interactive_init` and `interactive_init` both call `generate_skeletons(project_root)`,
   which loads every `_graph/*.yml`; this branch calls
   `generate_skeletons(project_root, result["nodes"], result["edges"])`.
   MEASURED, two identical trees (`src/orders/index.ts`, `docs/payments.md`, package name
   `orders-web`), each carrying `.beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml` with a service root and a domain
   `ledger` left by an earlier run:

     - `docs/domains/onboarding/features/agent-prime/SPEC.md:73` — heading "One order for

     - `docs/domains/onboarding/README.md:26` — same claim inside the `scanner/` paragraph.

2. `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1281-1282` and
   `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py:255-262` — the wizard's `cancel` answer at
   the graph review writes `services.yml` and `rules.yml` and then exits 0 without a verdict.
   BDL-UX #192's exact shape, sixth instance, on the branch a human adopter meets first.
   `interactive_init` calls `bootstrap_project` — which has already written both files — and
   only THEN prompts "Proceed with this graph?". `cancel` sets `mode = "cancelled"` and
   returns; `init` answers `sys.exit(0)` above the verdict.
   MEASURED, one tree (`src/orders/index.ts`, package name `orders-web`) carrying an adopter's
   own `rules.yml` with one error-severity `require` rule the bootstrap graph fails:
       wizard answering overwrite/bootstrap/CANCEL  ->  init rc 0
       .beadloom/_graph/ holds rules.yml + services.yml
       beadloom lint --strict on the same tree      ->  rc 1
       the same tree, answering YES instead         ->  init rc 1, full report
   The wizard also prints "Cancelled." over a graph and a rules file it has already written,
   which is the second false user-facing statement on this path.
   WHY THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT SEE IT, which is the finding rather than a detail.
   `tests/test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py:318` `_verdict_follows` walks what
   runs after a writing call and stops at `ast.Return | ast.Raise`. `sys.exit` is neither, so
   the walk steps over `if result["mode"] == "cancelled": sys.exit(0)` and finds the verdict
   below it. Proven with that module's own helpers, against its own fixture text:
       A_VERDICT_BELOW_THE_RETURN     -> [('non_interactive_init', False), ...]
       the same shape with sys.exit(0) -> [('non_interactive_init', True), ...]
   The identical defect reads guarded when the terminator is `sys.exit` and unguarded when it
   is `return`. `setup.py:1282` is uncovered by the ENTIRE suite (whole-suite coverage of
   `setup.py`, missing lines include 1282).

     - `docs/domains/onboarding/README.md:167` — "EVERY branch that writes a file under

   terminator set, with a mutant beside `A_VERDICT_BELOW_THE_RETURN` that proves it red.
   (b) Decide `cancel` explicitly: either take the verdict there too, or make it a named
   carve-out with the reason `edit` has — and if it is a carve-out, the honest fix is that
   `interactive_init` should not have written the files before asking, since "Cancelled." over
   a written graph is the same class of false message this epic has now filed four times.
   (c) Correct the three documents to whatever (b) decides; they currently certify a coverage
   the code does not have.

3. `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py:35` and
   `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/doc_classify.py:96` — one post-condition, two
   implementations, the same private name in two modules, and the docstring that binds them
   names a symbol that no longer exists.
   The two bodies are the same loop: skip a ref_id that is already parented, skip the root's
   own ref_id, otherwise emit `{src, dst: root, kind: part_of}`. They differ only in where
   `parented` comes from and in a `str()` call, and their parameter orders disagree
   (`(nodes, edges, root_ref_id)` against `(nodes, root_ref_id, parented)`).
   This is not a hypothetical drift risk: they have already drifted once and were repaired by
   editing both — `.16` minor 2 recorded that one covered every kind and the other only
   `domain`, "the two writers now disagree about their own shared invariant".
   `doc_classify.py:111` states the binding as "The same post-condition `bootstrap_project`
   holds over its own output (`bootstrap._missing_domain_parent_edges`)". That symbol does not
   exist anywhere in `src/` or `tests/`; `.17` renamed it to `_missing_parent_edges` and left

   form of the binding these two functions depend on.

   called by both writers, with the `parented` set computed by each caller from what it can
   see. Then the invariant is edited once. Repair the dangling reference in the same change.
   NOT re-filed here, and named only so this finding is not mistaken for it: `beadloom-gv0z` /
   BDL-UX #217 is the behavioural consequence of this scoping and is deliberately deferred.

Minor:

- `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:974, 978-979, 1008` — the node-less-finding path
  and the attribution fallback are reached by nothing in the suite. Measured over the WHOLE
  suite, not only the epic's modules: `setup.py` is at 91% and those lines are in `Missing`.
  Judged rather than adopted from the prompt: this is untested code, not dead code, and not
  wrong code. It is reachable in production — `forbid_import` violations carry
  `from_ref_id=None` (`graph/rules/evaluators.py:396`), and `bootstrap_project` writes
  `rules.yml` only when absent, so an adopter's own error-severity `forbid_import` rule
  survives into an `init --bootstrap` and produces exactly a node-less error finding. I could
  not stage that end to end in this environment (no tree-sitter Python grammar installed, so
  the `from:` glob matched nothing and the rule went inert — `rule_liveness:warn`); that is the
  one measurement I could not complete. Reasoning about the consequence: `_failing_rule_lines`
  emits the bare rule name and `_this_run_wrote_the_graph_that_fails` falls back to "did this
  run write any graph file", which on a virgin bootstrap is True; combined with
  `rules_are_this_run_s == False` that selects `_ATTRIBUTION[(True, False)]` — "the rule(s)
  above are your project's" — which is the correct sentence. The corner that would misattribute,
  `(True, True)` with a node-less finding, is unreachable because `generate_rules` writes only
  `require` rules whose findings name a node.
  RECOMMENDATION: one case in `tests/test_init_report_says_whose_failure_it_is.py` with a
  hand-written error-severity `forbid_import` rule on disk before `init --bootstrap`, asserting
  the bare rule name and the `(True, False)` sentence. Also 953-954/956, the unreadable-YAML
  guards in `_graph_file_of_each_node`, are unexercised; a temp file with invalid YAML would
  cover both.

- `docs/services/cli.md` surface drift (`sync-check` warns `watches=cli,graph,flow.yml`). This
  is major 3 of `.13`, routed to `beadloom-e8s4.5`, and this is the fourth review to find it
  open. Recorded, not re-filed.

JUDGEMENT ON `beadloom-gv0z` / BDL-UX #217 — asked for, not re-filed.

Stating it was the right call, for a reason the bead itself gets right and which none of the
other five deferrals in this epic could claim: every other fix in BDL-067 constrains what
Beadloom writes about its own output, and this one would have Beadloom rewrite a graph file
the adopter may have authored. That is a different kind of act and a fix cycle is the wrong
place to decide it. The bead names three options with the trade-off on each, which is what
makes it a decision rather than a deferral.
Two qualifications. First, the adopter is left with a tree that two individually green
commands made red, and no `init` invocation repairs it — I re-ran the wizard on that tree and
got rc 1 again. The report is honest and the state is still a dead end, so option (b) is not
free. Second, the bead frames the gap as a limit of the VERDICT. It is a limit of the WRITER:
option (a) is precisely "make the bootstrap's pass range over the tree instead of over its own
nodes", which is Major 3's recommendation seen from the other side. Deciding #217 and Major 3
separately is how the two copies drift again.

Process:
- `beadloom review-brief --release` on this tracker cannot establish that the verdict was
  recorded by anyone other than the bead's author, because every role writes under one
  identity. That is the expected answer here, not a defect.
- The brief's `changed-outside-scope` finding (`application/gate.py`, `graph/linter.py`) is an
  artefact of measuring since `main`; both changes are this epic's and both are documented in
  `docs/domains/application/README.md` and `docs/domains/graph/features/rule-engine/SPEC.md`.
- The brief's `no-bound-scenario` finding is correct as stated and not a defect of the work:
  `tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature` carries 20+ scenarios in the
  adopter's vocabulary, bound to the dev beads rather than to this review bead. The three the
  BRIEF names as acceptance criteria are all present. Neither of my majors has a scenario,
  which is the expected state for a finding rather than a fix.

title: [BDL-067.19][test] one enumeration over branches x modes x renderers
description:
Cover beadloom-e8s4.17 and beadloom-e8s4.18.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DEFINES THIS BEAD: the suite already enumerates BRANCHES (.7), then MODES (.15), and the fifth review still found four majors — three of them on axes no enumeration covers: which branch withdraws the completion claim, which renderer the quoted ci line matches, and which run wrote the failing node.

So do not add a third one-axis enumeration. Build ONE table over the axes that actually vary: entry point (wizard / --yes / --bootstrap) x mode (bootstrap / import / both) x output renderer (rich / github), and assert the invariants that must hold in every cell:
- no init that wrote a graph file terminates 0 over a graph failing the rules on disk
- a success claim is withdrawn wherever one was made before a failing verdict
- the 'please report it' sentence appears only when THIS run wrote the file the failing node came from
- any shape quoted from another command matches what that command emits in the renderer that will run
- the two entry points agree on the graph they leave for the same declared mode

Verify every new assertion FAILS against the pre-.17 tree, and declare any that cannot fail with its reason.

Baseline: measured by the coordinator after .17 and .18 land. Measure without a pipe.

refs: onboarding, cli

title: [BDL-067.18][dev][BDL-UX #216] --yes --mode both imports the skeletons it generated seconds earlier
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.16 Major 4. Filed as its own bead inside this epic by owner decision, with a UX number, because it is a behaviour change beyond #192's reproduction AND because this branch changed its character.

MEASURED on src/orders/, src/catalog/, docs/payments.md:

    init --yes --mode both   ->  Imported: 4 documents; imported.yml holds
                                 architecture, readme, readme, payments
    wizard answering both    ->  Classified 1 documents; imported.yml holds payments

Three of the four are Beadloom's OWN skeletons. non_interactive_init runs generate_skeletons INSIDE the bootstrap block and import_docs after it (init_flow.py:78-101); interactive_init imports first and offers skeletons last (:255-307).

Two consequences the reviewer measured: docs/domains/orders/README.md and docs/domains/catalog/README.md both become a node with ref_id 'readme' (the ref_id is the file stem), and on a project with services the same run produced a node 'core' of kind domain duplicating the bootstrap's 'core' of kind service. beadloom doctor on that tree then warns "Node 'catalog' has no doc linked" for nodes whose docs: field names those files.

WHY IT IS OURS EVEN THOUGH IT PREDATES US: it is pre-existing on main, but this branch changed its character. _missing_parent_edges now gives those nodes a part_of edge to the root, so what used to be a VISIBLE ORPHAN is now structurally valid and green. We did not create the defect; we hid it. That is the exact class this epic exists to remove, reproduced by the epic itself, and it must not reach main hidden.

DECISION, from the review and adopted: one command with one declared mode must not leave two different graphs, and a graph whose nodes are named after Beadloom's own scaffolding is not a description of the adopter's project.

FIX: import before generating skeletons in non_interactive_init, matching the wizard's order, or exclude the run's own generated files from the import scan. State which you chose and why.

Add the case to the mode-agreement suite: the two entry points must produce the same imported.yml for the same declared mode.

title: [BDL-067.17][dev] consolidation: replace the per-shape instruments with tree-level ones
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.16 Majors 1, 2, 3 + the Minor. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-01: fix the COMMON CAUSE, not four instances.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS IN THIS FORM. Five review passes returned 2, 1, 1, 3, 4 majors — rising. Each cycle fixed an instance by introducing a NEW instrument that was itself scoped to one shape, and the next review found the neighbouring shape. That is the thing to stop, not the individual findings.

The four findings are one cause seen four times:
- bootstrap_wrote_the_rules is an instrument for WHO WROTE THE RULES with no counterpart for WHO WROTE THE FAILING NODE
- the root guard counts NODE OCCURRENCES where it means DISTINCT ref_ids
- WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM is bound to ONE of three branches, and its docstring asserts the other two never make the claim (they do)
- the 'ci will report this as' line quotes ONE of three renderers

FOUR PARTS:

(1) MAJOR 1 — BLOCKER. doc_classify.py:79-84: roots is a list of ref_ids and len(roots) == 1 is tested over occurrences. bootstrap_project writes the root service node, and the attachment loop skips a top-level cluster whose sanitized name equals the project name (bootstrap.py:266), so a project named after one of its own service dirs yields roots == ['core','core'], the guard returns None, and import_docs attaches nothing. Measured: package.json name 'core', src/core/a.ts, src/orders/b.ts, docs/payments.md -> init --yes --mode both exits 1 on every run. Repo names core/api/web/app are the common case. FIX: range the uniqueness test over DISTINCT ref_ids (sorted(set(...))). Add the case to tests/test_import_docs_parents_what_it_writes.py:183, whose existing test uses two DISTINCT ref_ids and therefore cannot see this.

(2) MAJOR 2 — the --mode import carve-out is safe only until the next init on the same tree. The wizard's re-init does not delete .beadloom/ (init_flow.py:146-157), so imported.yml survives into a later bootstrap, which then writes the rule. Measured: init --yes --mode import -> rc 0; then the wizard -> rc 1 naming billing and payments from imported.yml, with 'the graph this command just wrote' (it did not) and 'a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap - please report it' (import_docs did not run this time). FIX, two parts: (a) decide the carve-out on the TREE rather than on one writer's output — take the verdict at the end of every init that wrote ANY graph file, so an unparented node is reported by the run that created it; (b) gate the 'defect in Beadloom's bootstrap / please report it' sentence on THIS RUN having written the graph file the node came from — source_of already names the file per node at _report_rules_the_graph_fails.

(3) MAJOR 3 — all three branches announce success before the verdict; only one withdraws it. WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM's docstring says the --bootstrap branch 'takes its verdict first and never makes it'. It makes it: four check marks, then the error, no withdrawal. --yes is the same (setup.py:1032). FIX: pass claim_to_withdraw from all three call sites, or move the verdict above the success lines in the two flag branches.   no errors. The `docs/services/cli.md` surface drift is `.13`'s Major 3, routed to `.5`.
- The domain/feature docs carry the new symbols (`lint_step`, `RULES_CONFIG_ERROR`,
  `gate_step_line`, `_missing_domain_parent_edges`, `_missing_parent_edges`, the `node` key
  on a finding) and the reindex move. One doc sentence is wrong; it is inside Major 2.
- The acceptance scenarios are observable and in the adopter's vocabulary
  (`Then the lint reports no error-severity violation`), not restatements of the implementation.

Major:

1. `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/doc_classify.py:79-84` — the root guard counts ONE root
   twice, and the bootstrap produces exactly that shape.
   `roots` is a list of ref_ids, and `len(roots) == 1` is tested over it. `bootstrap_project`
   writes the root service node, and the attachment loop skips a top-level cluster whose
   sanitized name equals the project name (`bootstrap.py:266`), so a project named after one
   of its own service directories yields two nodes with ref_id `core`, both `kind: service`,
   neither parented. `roots == ["core", "core"]`, the guard returns None, and `import_docs`
   attaches nothing.
   Measured — `package.json` name `core`, `src/core/a.ts`, `src/orders/b.ts`, `docs/payments.md`:

       beadloom init --yes --mode both
       Initialized beadloom (mode: both)
         Graph: 3 nodes, 1 edges (preset: monolith)
         Imported: 3 documents
       Error: the graph this command just wrote does not pass the rules this command wrote alongside it.
         domain-needs-parent: architecture (.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml)
         domain-needs-parent: payments (.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml)
       rc=1

   The stated post-condition ("every node written here carries an outgoing `part_of` edge to
   the graph's root, unless the graph has no single root") does not hold on a graph that has
   one root named twice. The docstring's justification does not cover this case either:
   "naming a parent by guessing between candidates" presumes two candidates, and there is one
   candidate ref_id here. `init` is unusable on that project shape — every run ends rc 1 and
   asks the adopter to file a bug.
   Recommendation: make the uniqueness test range over ref_ids rather than over node
   occurrences — `roots = sorted({...})` — and add the case to
   `tests/test_import_docs_parents_what_it_writes.py:183`, whose
   `test_two_unparented_services_are_two_candidates_and_neither_is_chosen` uses two DISTINCT
   ref_ids and therefore cannot see this. Repo names like `core`, `api`, `web` and `app` are
   the common case, not a corner.

2. `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1044-1051` and
   `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/doc_classify.py:158-166` — the `--mode import` carve-out
   is safe only until the next `beadloom init` on the same tree, and the message it then
   produces asserts two facts the code knows to be false.
   The carve-out's stated reason, in the code comment, in
   `docs/domains/onboarding/features/agent-prime/SPEC.md` ("no rule the command wrote is on
   disk to fail") and in `tests/test_init_agrees_across_its_modes.py:712`, is scoped to the
   end of the import run. The wizard's re-init does NOT delete `.beadloom/`
   (`init_flow.py:146-157` sets `reinit` and proceeds), so `imported.yml` survives into a
   later bootstrap, which then writes the rule.
   Measured, two commands on one tree — virgin project, `src/index.ts`, `docs/billing.md`,
   `docs/payments.md`:

       beadloom init --yes --mode import            -> rc 0; imported.yml holds
                                                       `billing` and `payments`, kind domain,
                                                       no edges; no rules.yml; `ci` rc 0
       beadloom init   (overwrite / bootstrap / yes / n)
                                                    -> rc 1
       The scaffold above was written, but the check that follows it did not pass.
       Error: the graph this command just wrote does not pass the rules this command wrote alongside it.
         domain-needs-parent: billing (.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml)
         domain-needs-parent: payments (.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml)
       ... This is a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap rather than in your project — please
       report it with the rule name(s) above.

   Two false assertions, both of which the run has the facts to avoid. The graph this command
   just wrote is `services.yml`; `billing` and `payments` were written by a different run, and
   `_graph_file_of_each_node` had already located them in a file this run did not touch. And
   the run ran no `import_docs` at all — `result` carries no `import` key, mode was `bootstrap`
   — so "a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap ... please report it" sends an adopter to file a bug
   about a writer that did not run. This is the named class in both directions:
   `bootstrap_wrote_the_rules` is an instrument for WHO WROTE THE RULES with no counterpart
   for WHO WROTE THE FAILING NODE, and #192's shape is deferred by one command rather than
   prevented.
   Recommendation, two parts. (a) Decide the carve-out on the tree rather than on one writer's
   output: either give an import-only run a root to attach to, or take the verdict at the end
   of every `init` that wrote any graph file, so an unparented node is reported by the run that
   created it. (b) Gate the "defect in Beadloom's bootstrap / please report it" sentence on this
   run having written the graph file the node came from — that fact is already in hand at
   `_report_rules_the_graph_fails`, since `source_of` names the file per node.

3. `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:725-745, 1032, 1120` — the completion claim is
   withdrawn on one branch of three, and the reason given for the other two is false.
   `WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM`'s docstring says "the `--bootstrap` branch takes its verdict
   first and never makes it". It makes it.
   Measured, `--bootstrap` over an adopter's own `rules.yml`:

       ✓ Graph: 2 nodes, 1 edges (preset: monolith)
       ✓ Docs: 2 skeletons created
       ✓ MCP: configured for claude-code (.mcp.json)
       ✓ Index: 0 symbols, 0 imports
       Error: the graph this command just wrote does not pass the rules already in ...
       rc=1

   Four check marks, then an error, with no withdrawal line. `--yes` is the same: it prints
   `Initialized beadloom (mode: both)` at line 1032 and the summary lines, then the error
   (see finding 1's transcript, where no withdrawal line appears). All three branches announce
   success before the verdict; the instrument that withdraws it is bound to one.
   Recommendation: pass `claim_to_withdraw` from all three call sites, or move the verdict
   above the success lines in the two flag branches so there is nothing to withdraw. Either
   way the docstring's "never makes it" has to go — it is the reason the omission looked
   deliberate.

4. `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py:78-101` — `--mode both` writes a different
   graph through `--yes` than through the wizard, and the difference is that `--yes`
   classifies the documents it generated seconds earlier.
   `non_interactive_init` runs `generate_skeletons` inside the bootstrap block and
   `import_docs` after it; `interactive_init` imports first and offers skeletons last
   (`init_flow.py:255-307`). Measured on one project (`src/orders/`, `src/catalog/`,
   `docs/payments.md`):

       init --yes --mode both       -> Imported: 4 documents; imported.yml holds
                                       `architecture`, `readme`, `readme`, `payments`
       wizard answering `both`      -> Classified 1 documents; imported.yml holds `payments`

   Three of the four are Beadloom's own skeletons. `docs/domains/orders/README.md` and
   `docs/domains/catalog/README.md` both become a node with ref_id `readme`, because the
   ref_id is the file stem; on a project with services the same run produced a node `core`
   (kind domain) duplicating the bootstrap's `core` (kind service). `beadloom doctor` on that
   tree then warns `Node 'catalog' has no doc linked` and `Node 'orders' has no doc linked`
   for nodes whose `docs:` field names those files.
   `tests/test_init_agrees_across_its_modes.py:36-48` records the divergence and routes the
   decision here rather than deciding it. The decision: it is a defect. One command with one
   declared mode must not leave two different graphs, and a graph whose nodes are named after
   Beadloom's own scaffolding is not a description of the adopter's project. It is
   pre-existing on `main` rather than introduced here — but this branch changes its
   character: `_missing_parent_edges` now gives those nodes a `part_of` edge to the root, so
   what used to be a visible orphan is now structurally valid and green.
   Recommendation: import before generating skeletons in `non_interactive_init`, matching the
   wizard's order, or exclude the run's own generated files from the import scan. Either is a
   behaviour change beyond this bug's reproduction, so it belongs on its own bead in this
   epic with a BDL-UX number, not folded into a fix cycle here.

Minor:

- `src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:834` — "`beadloom ci` will report this as:
  [FAIL] lint: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)" quotes one of the Gate's three renderings.
  `ci` chooses `rich` only on a TTY and `github` otherwise (`federation.py:409`), and the
  github renderer builds its own step line (`federation.py:485`) rather than calling
  `gate_step_line`. Measured in one non-TTY shell: `init` promised
  `[FAIL] lint: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)`; `beadloom ci` on the same tree printed
  `::notice::lint FAIL: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)`. The instrument introduced to stop this line
  drifting is scoped to one shape while a second exists — the named class again — and it is
  wrong in exactly the scripted context `--yes` serves. Recommendation: state the fact rather
  than the rendering ("`beadloom ci` will fail its lint step: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)"), or
  route the github renderer through `gate_step_line` too.

- `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py:68` — `_missing_domain_parent_edges` is scoped
  to `kind == "domain"`, while `generate_rules` also writes `feature-needs-parent` for
  `kind == "feature"` (`rules_gen.py:53-66`). The sibling in `doc_classify` attaches every kind
  and states why: "a post-condition that tracked the current rule set would go stale the next
  time a rule is added." The two writers now disagree about their own shared invariant. Not
  reachable today — no preset has `default_kind = "feature"` and every cluster node is attached
  by the loop above — so this is a Minor, not a Major. Recommendation: widen the bootstrap's
  pass to every kind and delete the asymmetry, or say in the docstring why the bootstrap's
  post-condition is narrower than the importer's.

- `src/beadloom/services/commands/federation.py:485` — the github Gate renderer emits
  `::notice::` for every step regardless of status, so a failing step is annotated as a notice
  (`::notice::lint FAIL: 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)` on a run whose rc was 1). Pre-existing and
  outside this epic's scope; worth a BDL-UX number rather than a fix here.

Process:
- `beadloom review-brief --release` exits 1 when it cannot establish that the verdict was
  recorded by someone other than the bead's author. On this tracker every role writes under
  one identity, so that is the expected answer and not a defect.
- The brief's `changed-outside-scope` finding (`application/gate.py`, `graph/linter.py`) is
  the branch measured since `main`; both changes are this epic's and both are documented.

title: [BDL-067.15][test] parametrise over --mode, and seed the enumerator from every graph writer
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.13 Major 2. Cover beadloom-e8s4.14.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS: 112 tests across this epic's seven files pass, and NONE of them can see Major 1. Every test and every scenario pins --mode bootstrap. THE_BRANCHES (test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py:60-75) varies flags and monkeypatch bindings and never the --mode value.

TWO PROPERTIES OF THE ENUMERATOR KEPT IT GREEN, and both are in scope:

1. Its reachability scan is seeded from bootstrap_project ALONE, so import_docs — the other writer of domain nodes — is outside the instrument. Its docstring claims 'a fourth branch fails these tests on the day it is written'; that does not hold for a fourth WRITER. Seed the scan from every function that writes a graph file under .beadloom/_graph/, not from bootstrap_project alone. Correct the docstring to what the instrument actually covers.

2. The check is SYNTACTIC: it asserts a call to _verdict_on_the_generated_graph follows the branch, which its own 'Known limits' concedes answers 'could this branch report' rather than 'does it report'. '--yes --mode both' HAS the call and passes the test while the verdict is blind. Add at least one behavioural assertion that would fail on a blind verdict.

3. Parametrise the behavioural cases over --mode (bootstrap, import, both) as well as over the flag. Add a scenario over --mode both to bootstrap_self_consistency.feature.

THE ASSERTION THE REVIEWER NAMED as the one that would have caught this: the wizard answering 'both' and '--yes --mode both' must agree. Today they do not.

Verify every new assertion FAILS against the pre-.14 tree and say how you verified it. Declare any that cannot fail.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TESTS: 75 new cases across 3 files (63 unit/integration in a new module, 10 in the enumerator, 2 acceptance scenarios). Tree: 7425 -> 7500 passed, 0 failed. ruff clean, mypy src/ clean over 225 files, beadloom lint --strict rc 0, sync-check rc 0, doctor rc 0, beadloom ci rc 0. No pipes; rc read directly.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THE BEAD NAMED, each closed and each measured.

1. THE SEED. tests/test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py seeded its reachability scan from bootstrap_project alone while its docstring claimed to cover a fourth BRANCH of the graph. It is now seeded from write_yaml_atomic -- the one commit point every graph YAML routes through, which infrastructure/atomic_io.py states as its own purpose -- so 'this function writes a graph file' is derived from the source rather than listed. The scan rediscovers exactly the six writers .14's sweep found by hand (bootstrap_project, import_docs, generate_rules, update_node_in_yaml, _patch_docs_field, link) and a SEVENTH fails a case, which is the question .14 had to run a manual sweep to answer. The seed's soundness is checked rather than trusted: TestNoGraphFileIsWrittenPastTheCommitPoint fails if any function ever serialises YAML and writes it itself, because such a writer would be invisible to every scan in the module (one declared exception, persist_flow_config, which writes .beadloom/flow.yml and holds no node). The scan also widened from the onboarding package to the whole beadloom package, which retires the old 'another package would not be seen' limit -- link and update_node_in_yaml are writers outside onboarding -- and was measured not to change the bootstrap-seeded call sites.

THE ONE DEFERRAL IS DECLARED AND CHECKED. With the wide seed, exactly one branch of init writes a graph file and takes no verdict: --import. THE_DEFERRED_BRANCHES carries its guard, the reason (it re-indexes nothing and hands the work back, the same shape as the wizard's edit answer) and a string its own remaining source must still contain ('beadloom reindex'), read off the branch by unparsing what follows the call. A deferral that stops telling the adopter what to do next stops being a deferral and fails a case; a deferral naming a branch that no longer exists fails another.

MEASURED, on the shipped pre-.15 module rather than on a story about it: over a synthetic command whose fourth branch writes a graph file WITHOUT bootstrapping, the old seed reports unguarded=[] and the new seed reports [('rescan',)]. That gap is the one that kept import_docs outside the instrument for five waves, and it is now a test (test_the_writer_seed_reports_a_branch_the_bootstrap_seed_calls_clean) stated as the difference between the two seeds rather than as a claim about one.

2. THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF. The syntactic check answers 'could this branch report' and --yes --mode both had the call while the verdict was blind. tests/test_init_agrees_across_its_modes.py runs the command. 13 of its 63 cases FAIL against the pre-.14 tree, all in --mode both.

3. THE MODE AXIS. Parametrised over --mode {bootstrap, import, both} -- read off the flag's own click.Choice, so a fourth mode joins the parametrisation on the day it is declared -- crossed with the two entry points that pick a mode. A companion case asserts the wizard can be answered with every mode the flag accepts (parsed out of interactive_init's four choices lists), because a mode with one entry point is a mode the agreement below cannot be asked about.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
THE ASSERTION THE REVIEWER NAMED, and how it was verified.

TestTheWizardAndTheFlagAgree builds the fixture twice from the same code and the same documents and runs one copy through each entry point. Neither run is asserted to be right; what is asserted is that they say the same thing. Measured against the pre-.14 tree (975b87f, with .14's test files copied in so the imports resolve), with NO SABOTAGE AT ALL:

  --mode bootstrap  --yes rc 0 / lint --strict rc 0   wizard rc 0 / rc 0
  --mode import     --yes rc 0 / rc 0                 wizard rc 0 / rc 0
  --mode both       --yes rc 0 / lint --strict rc 1   wizard rc 1 / rc 1   <- disagreement

A virgin project with a docs/ directory produced that on its own. On the current tree all six read rc 0 / rc 0.

VERIFICATION METHOD: git worktree at 975b87f, uv sync, the new test files copied in, run. 13 red / 50 green.

THE 13 THAT FAIL PRE-.14 (all --mode both):
  TestEveryModeAgreesWithTheLintTheAdopterRunsNext: test_the_run_reports_success[wizard-both]; test_the_verdict_agrees_with_lint_strict_on_the_tree_it_leaves[--yes-both]
  TestEveryDomainAnyWriterWroteCarriesAParent: test_no_domain_is_left_without_a_part_of_edge[--yes-both], [wizard-both]
  TestTheWizardAndTheFlagAgree: test_they_report_the_same_verdict[both]; test_they_leave_the_same_domains_unparented[both]
  TestTheWizardAndTheFlagAgreeOverAGraphTheRulesReject: test_they_report_the_same_verdict[both]; test_each_agrees_with_the_lint_on_the_tree_it_left[both]
  TestAViolationTheRunIntroducedIsReportedInEveryModeItCanReach: test_the_verdict_agrees_with_lint_strict[--yes-both-the-import-adds-an-orphan]
  TestARunThatWroteItsOwnRulesReportsTheGraphThatFailsThem: test_the_command_does_not_report_success and test_it_names_the_rule_the_gate_will_name, both at [--yes-both-the-import-adds-an-orphan]
  TestTheReportNamesTheNodeTheSecondWriterLeftUnparented: test_the_orphan_is_named_in_the_report[--yes-both-...], [wizard-both-...]

Both new acceptance scenarios also fail pre-.14 (5 failed / 11 passed in that file; the other 3 are .14's own).

DECLARED, BECAUSE IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT COSTS -- what does NOT fail pre-.14 and cannot:

- The 10 new enumerator cases. None of them can be red there: .14's defect was a blind verdict, not a missing one, and no branch of init at that commit reached a writer without a verdict call. They would have caught a THIRD WRITER, which that tree did not have either. Their bite is demonstrated on synthetic mutants (TestTheEnumeratorItself), which is the only honest way to test an instrument against a defect that does not exist yet, plus the old-seed-vs-new-seed measurement above.
- The 50 green legs of the behavioural module: --mode bootstrap and --mode import were correct pre-.14 and are the controls that stop the module from being a matrix that is red everywhere.
- TestWhatABlindVerdictWouldReport. It characterises rather than accuses: gate.lint_step reads the index without re-indexing, so a graph file written after the reindex is invisible to it. Green on both trees by construction -- what .14 changed was WHEN init calls it. It is what makes the agreement cases claims rather than tautologies: on this exact fixture a stale reader passes and lint --strict does not. Its assertion message says that if lint_step ever gains a reindex the right answer is to retire the case, not to weaken it.
- The 4 derivation cases (modes off click.Choice, wizard choices off init_flow's source, the two 'which modes write which file' bindings): they guard the axis, and an axis that silently derived nothing would collect zero cases and report a green file.

MUTATION TESTING: not run. Beadloom ships no mutation runner and this bead added no domain code; the equivalent evidence here is the pre-.14 measurement above (13 of 63 red on an unmutated older tree) and the old-seed/new-seed measurement on the enumerator. Reported as zero mutants run, not as clean.

comments.text:
TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE MEASURING, REPORTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY ABSORBED.

(a) THE TWO ENTRY POINTS DO NOT LEAVE THE SAME GRAPH UNDER --mode both, and it is not the defect this bead closes. --yes generates its doc skeletons INSIDE the bootstrap block, so the import step that follows classifies the skeletons the same run just wrote: the graph gains 'architecture' (domain) and 'readme' (feature) nodes that the wizard's graph does not have, because the wizard imports first and offers skeletons afterwards. Both graphs pass their own rules and every domain in both is parented, so nothing here is red. It is why the agreement cases assert the VERDICT and the invariant rather than node-set equality -- choosing the weaker assertion silently would have been this epic's own failure mode. Whether a run should classify documents it generated in the same run is a question for the review; I did not decide it.

(b) --mode import ON A VIRGIN PROJECT LEAVES ITS DOMAINS UNPARENTED, by .14's stated decision (no single root, so no parent is guessed). My first draft asserted 'no domain on disk lacks a part_of edge' over all six combinations and it went red on the two import legs -- correctly, against a claim that was too wide. title: [BDL-067.14][dev] --mode both and --import: the second writer of domain nodes, and a verdict judging a stale index
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.13 Major 1 + Minors 1, 2, 3 + the nitpick. Owner decision 2026-09-01: fix inside BDL-067 rather than filing separately, because the approved BRIEF's acceptance criterion is not met for these modes and three documents ALREADY SHIPPED ON THIS BRANCH assert the opposite.

MEASURED by the reviewer on a project with src/index.ts, docs/payments.md, docs/billing.md:

    beadloom init --yes --mode both      -> rc 0    "Imported: 4 documents"
    beadloom lint --strict --no-reindex  -> rc 0    "1 rules evaluated"    <- what init judged
    beadloom lint --strict               -> rc 1    domain-needs-parent x3 <- what the adopter sees
    beadloom ci                          -> lint FAIL: 3 error(s)

Violating nodes: architecture, billing, payments, all in .beadloom/_graph/imported.yml. Reproduced again: on an already initialised project, 'beadloom init --import docs/' exits 0 and the next lint --strict exits 1.

TWO CAUSES, BOTH IN SCOPE:

(a) SECOND WRITER. import_docs writes every document it cannot classify as kind: domain with NO part_of edge (doc_classify.py:57-65), while the same run writes domain-needs-parent at error severity. Bead .1 stated the domain-parent post-condition over bootstrap_project's output only. import_docs is a second writer of domain nodes and never received the invariant. Give it the same post-condition (a part_of edge to the root), or stop defaulting an unclassifiable document to kind: domain.

(b) STALE INDEX. In non_interactive_init the reindex sits INSIDE the bootstrap block (init_flow.py:97-104) and the import block writes imported.yml AFTER it (:106-112). gate.lint_step reads the index read-only (gate.py:239-241, linter.py:163-168, reindex=None), so _verdict_on_the_generated_graph judges an index predating the last graph file init wrote. The comment 'reindex already ran (or was intentionally skipped); do not redo it' is true inside the Gate and false at this call site. Move the reindex to the end of non_interactive_init, or reindex inside the verdict before judging.

PROOF THE TWO HALVES DISAGREE: on the same project the WIZARD answering 'both' exits 1 and names domain-needs-parent (interactive_init imports before it reindexes, init_flow.py:243-256, :265-272) while --yes --mode both exits 0. That is the exact condition lint_step was made public to make 'unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely' (gate.py:229-234). It is still representable.

ALSO IN SCOPE:
- Minor 2 (setup.py:980-983): the --yes branch calls the verdict for EVERY mode, including --mode import where no graph was written, and both headlines begin 'the graph this command just wrote'. Unreachable today only because an import-only run leaves no rules.yml. Gate the call on 'bootstrap' in result.
- Minor 1 (setup.py:846-874): the evaluated-rules report points the adopter at services.yml and rules.yml for a node that came from imported.yml. Fixing Major 1 removes the case; naming the file each violating node came from removes the SHAPE. Do the latter.
- Minor 3 (setup.py:827): the line says ci will report 'lint — {summary}'. ci actually renders '[FAIL] lint: <summary>' (federation.py:439) or '::notice::lint FAIL: <summary>' (:481). Quote a shape the command emits.
- Nitpick (setup.py:734-742): _wrote_the_rules_file's docstring says rules_generated is 0 'exactly when the file was already there'. It is also 0 when the bootstrap wrote no nodes and when generate_rules finds no domain or feature kind (rules_gen.py:72-73). No false message follows today, but the stated equivalence is not the one the code holds. State what is actually true.

DO NOT touch docs/services/cli.md — that is Major 3 and belongs to beadloom-e8s4.5.
Also correct docs/services/mcp.md:426, which asserts 'All three branches that write a graph ... exit 1 when it does not pass' — false as measured, and --import is a FOURTH writer.

Baseline: 7403 passed, 0 failed, beadloom ci rc 0. Measure without a pipe, in the foreground.

comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: both causes closed and measured on a scratch adopter (orders-web, flat src/index.ts + docs/payments.md + docs/billing.md).

(a) SECOND WRITER. import_docs now holds the same post-condition .1 gave bootstrap_project: every node it writes carries an outgoing part_of edge to the graph's root. Two helpers in doc_classify.py -- _existing_graph(graph_dir) finds the root by reading the graph on disk (the one node of kind service that no part_of edge leaves, ref_id read off the node as written, not recomputed from the project name) and _missing_parent_edges(nodes, root_ref_id, parented) states the invariant over the writer's whole output. It attaches EVERY kind, not only the two the generated rules require a parent for, because a post-condition that tracked today's rule set goes stale the next time generate_rules gains a rule -- an imported kind: feature node was already one classification away from the same defect via feature-needs-parent. Carve-outs: a ref_id that already carries a part_of edge keeps its parent; a ref_id equal to the root's gets nothing; with no single root (import-only on a virgin project, or two unparented services) no parent is named rather than one guessed.

(b) STALE INDEX. The reindex moved out of the bootstrap block to the end of non_interactive_init, so it runs after every block that writes a graph file -- the same order interactive_init already used, which is why the wizard exited 1 where --yes exited 0.

comments.text:
THE SWEEP THE BEAD ASKED FOR — reported, not silently widened.

Every writer into .beadloom/_graph/ enumerated from src/ (write_yaml_atomic call sites + every _graph path reference). SIX writers; exactly TWO create nodes:

  1. bootstrap_project (scanner/bootstrap.py:281) -> services.yml — CREATES nodes. Has the invariant since .1.
  2. import_docs (scanner/doc_classify.py) -> imported.yml — CREATES nodes. LACKED it. Fixed here.

The other four cannot produce an unparented node, because none of them creates a node:
  3. generate_rules (scanner/rules_gen.py:77) -> rules.yml — writes rules, no nodes.
  4. update_node_in_yaml (graph/loader.py:171-205) — patches summary/source on a node that already exists; cannot add a node and cannot change kind.
  5. _patch_docs_field (onboarding/doc_generator.py:511-551) — adds docs: to an existing node.
  6. the link command (services/commands/index_ops.py:280,296) — adds/removes links: on an existing node.

So the class has no third instance on this tree. What it does have is no instrument: nothing in the suite would notice a third node-writer on the day it is added. test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap seeds its reachability scan from bootstrap_project alone, so import_docs was outside the instrument the whole time — that is .15's bead, and this comment is the enumeration it can seed from rather than re-derive.

ALSO IN SCOPE, all four done:
- Minor 2 (setup.py): the --yes verdict is gated on 'bootstrap' in result. --mode import wrote no graph and no rules, and both headlines open with 'the graph this command just wrote'. It had been harmless only because an import-only run leaves no rules.yml — an accident of another module, not a decision at that call site.
- Minor 1 (setup.py): each failing line now names the rule, the violating node, and the graph file the node was written into (_graph_file_of_each_node reads .beadloom/_graph/*.yml; _failing_rule_lines composes). The advice sends the adopter to those files instead of naming services.yml by habit. A finding about no single node keeps the bare rule name; a node no graph file claims keeps rule+node rather than a guessed file.
- Minor 3 (setup.py:827): the quoted line is now rendered by the Gate's own formatter. Extracted application.gate.gate_step_line(step) -> '[STATUS] name: summary'; _format_gate_rich renders it and init quotes it, so the line init attributes to 'beadloom ci' cannot drift from the line 'beadloom ci' prints. It said 'lint — <summary>'; ci prints '[FAIL] lint: <summary>'.
- Nitpick (setup.py:734-742): _wrote_the_rules_file's docstring no longer claims rules_generated is 0 'exactly when the file was already there'. It is also 0 when the bootstrap wrote no nodes and when generate_rules found no domain or feature kind; the docstring now states the only claim the value supports (this run did not author the rules) and why no false message follows.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED beadloom-e8s4.14.

WHAT: (a) import_docs holds the domain-parent post-condition; (b) the reindex moved to the end of non_interactive_init so the verdict judges every graph file the run wrote; plus minors 1, 2, 3 and the nitpick; plus docs/services/mcp.md's false 'All three branches' claim.

DECISIONS, with reasons:
- Chose 'give import_docs the invariant' over 'stop defaulting an unclassifiable document to kind: domain'. The default is not the only unsafe kind: an imported kind: feature node violates feature-needs-parent the moment a bootstrap writes any feature, so re-labelling the fallthrough would have moved the defect one classification sideways. The edge is written for EVERY kind for the same reason — a post-condition scoped to today's two ruled kinds goes stale the next time generate_rules gains a rule.
- The root is discovered by import_docs itself from the graph on disk, not passed in by callers. Three callers reach it (non_interactive_init, interactive_init, the --import branch) and only two have a bootstrap result to pass; a post-condition that depends on caller cooperation is the failure mode this bead exists to close.
- With no single root (import-only on a virgin project, two unparented services) no parent is named. A guessed destination is a claim the graph does not make, and in that state no rules.yml this command wrote is on disk to fail.
- The --import branch still takes NO verdict, deliberately and out of scope: it re-indexes nothing and tells the adopter to run beadloom reindex, so there is no index of its own output to judge. Fix (a) closes its reported reproduction. Stated as fact in mcp.md rather than papered over.

TESTS (RED first, each proven to bite):
- 3 acceptance scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature, tagged @bead:beadloom-e8s4.14. All three failed before the fix: the first on ['architecture','billing','payments'], the second on 'assert 0 != 0' (the stale index), the third on the same orphans via --import. The stale-index sabotage ADDS a parentless domain to imported.yml rather than removing edges from it, so the instrument says the same thing before and after the post-condition landed — a strip-the-edges sabotage would have been a no-op on the pre-fix tree and gone green for the wrong reason.
- tests/test_import_docs_parents_what_it_writes.py, 11 cases. Measured with the fix reverted: 8 of 11 red. The 3 that stay green are the negative claims about a graph with no root (no edges written), which held trivially before and now guard the new behaviour from over-reaching. Stated rather than counted as coverage.
- 4 new cases in tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py for minors 1, 2 and 3, all red before their fixes; 3 more that cover the verdict over both graph files.
- tests/test_linter.py's exact-key assertion updated for the new 'node' key.

MEASURED:
- tree: 7425 passed, 0 failed (baseline 7403), ruff clean, mypy src/ clean over 225 files, beadloom lint --strict rc 0, sync-check rc 0, doctor rc 0, beadloom ci rc 0. No pipes; rc read directly.
- scratch adopter, before -> after: init --yes --mode both rc 0 -> rc 0; lint --strict rc 1 (3 errors) -> rc 0; beadloom ci lint FAIL 3 error(s) -> rc 0. init --import on an initialised project: rc 0 then rc 1 -> rc 0 then rc 0.
- CLEAN ROOM: green in a clean room over 24 files — git archive HEAD + only my files, fresh uv sync, 7418 passed, 1 failed. The one failure is tests/test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh, and it is NOT this change: a pristine clean room built from HEAD with none of my files fails that same class (2 failed there). A fresh checkout has no sync baseline — every pair reads no_baseline/unverified — and the test asserts status == ok.

FILES: src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/{doc_classify,init_flow}.py, src/beadloom/services/commands/{setup,federation}.py, src/beadloom/application/gate.py, src/beadloom/graph/linter.py; tests/test_import_docs_parents_what_it_writes.py (new), tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py, tests/test_linter.py, tests/acceptance/{features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature,steps/test_bootstrap_self_consistency_steps.py}; 11 docs; ACTIVE.md. Commit b68ebb2 on features/BDL-067.

ON THE COMMIT SCOPE: staged by explicit path, never git add -A. The pre-commit hook (beadloom active-sync) ADDED .beads/issues.jsonl to the commit on its own for ACTIVE/tracker coherence — recorded here because it was not my path and the coordinator had staged it before this bead started. The hook also printed two mypy warnings in tests/test_linter.py at lines 35 and 40; they are a pre-existing fixture, my diff in that file starts at line 543, and mypy src/ — the project's declared type check — is clean.

title: [BDL-067.13][review] fourth-pass review after the withdrawal-wording fix
description:
Run 'beadloom review-brief beadloom-e8s4.13' for your input. Read-only.

Confirm Major 1 of beadloom-e8s4.11 is closed and that no new instance of its class remains. That class is: a user-facing message asserting a fact the code knows to be false. It has now been found three times in this epic, each time on the branch a previous bead did not carry its reasoning across to. Sweep for a fourth rather than only confirming the third is fixed.

Do NOT read ACTIVE.md (BDL-UX #212).

refs: onboarding, cli

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 3 major

Fourth-pass review of BDL-067, read-only, on `features/BDL-067` (975b87f). Every number below is
measured on a scratch adopter project that is not this repository, with the wheel built from this
branch.

## The two things the bead asked for

**1. Major 1 of `.11` is closed. Measured.** Wizard over a `rules.yml` the loader refuses:

    The scaffold above was written, but the check that follows it did not pass.
    Error: .beadloom/_graph/rules.yml could not be read, so the graph this command wrote was
      not checked against it.
      Invalid rules configuration: Rule 'broken': 'require' must be a mapping
    No rule was evaluated, so the graph is unchecked rather than wrong.

The withdrawal line no longer asserts that a rule failed, and nothing under it contradicts it.
The original defect is closed too: `init --yes --mode bootstrap` on a flat `src/index.ts`
TypeScript project gives rc 0, `Graph: 2 nodes, 1 edges`, then `lint --strict` rc 0 and
`beadloom ci` green. BDL-UX #192's reproduction no longer reproduces on that path.

**2. The sweep found a fourth instance, and it is inside `init`.** It is not BDL-UX #215 — see
Major 1 below. Filed here rather than separately because it is the epic's own acceptance
criterion ("`init` does not report success over a graph that fails the rules it just wrote")
failing on a branch this epic declares covered.

## Major

### Major 1 — `init` still reports success over a graph that fails the rules it just wrote, on `--mode both` and on `--import`

File: `src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/doc_classify.py:57-65`,
`src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py:76-104`,
`src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:980-983`.

Measured on a project with `src/index.ts`, `docs/payments.md` and `docs/billing.md`:

    beadloom init --yes --mode both       -> rc 0    "Imported: 4 documents"
    beadloom lint --strict --no-reindex   -> rc 0    "1 rules evaluated"   <- what init judged
    beadloom lint --strict                -> rc 1    domain-needs-parent x3 <- what the adopter sees
    beadloom ci                           -> lint FAIL: 3 error(s), 0 warning(s)

The three violating nodes are `architecture`, `billing` and `payments`, all in
`.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml`. Reproduced a second time on a different branch: on an already
initialised project, `beadloom init --import docs/` exits 0 and the next `lint --strict` exits 1
on `domain-needs-parent` for `architecture` and `payments`. This is BDL-UX #192's signature,
unchanged, on the branches the epic did not carry its reasoning to.

Two causes, both fixable:

- `import_docs` writes every document it cannot classify as `kind: "domain"` with no `part_of`
  edge (`doc_classify.py:57-65`), while `bootstrap_project` writes `domain-needs-parent` at error
  severity in the same run. `.1` stated the domain-parent post-condition over `bootstrap_project`'s
  output. `import_docs` is a **second writer of `domain` nodes** and never received it.
- In `non_interactive_init` the reindex sits **inside** the bootstrap block (`init_flow.py:97-104`)
  and the import block writes `imported.yml` after it (`:106-112`). `gate.lint_step` reads the
  index read-only (`gate.py:239-241`, `linter.py:163-168`, `reindex=None`), so
  `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph` judges an index that predates the last graph file `init` wrote.
  The comment "reindex already ran (or was intentionally skipped); do not redo it" is true inside
  the Gate and false at this call site.

The two halves of one command disagree, measured. On the same project shape the **wizard** answering
`both` exits 1 and names `domain-needs-parent`, because `interactive_init` imports before it
reindexes (`init_flow.py:243-256`, `:265-272`), while `--yes --mode both` exits 0. That is the exact
condition `lint_step` was made public to make "unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely"
(`gate.py:229-234`). It is still representable, and it is happening.

Documents shipped on this branch that assert the opposite, and are false as measured:

- `docs/services/mcp.md:426` — "All three branches that write a graph ... exit 1 when it does not
  pass, so the command cannot report success over a graph that fails the rules on disk". It can, and
  `--import` is a fourth branch that writes a graph (`imported.yml`) and takes no verdict at all.
- `docs/domains/onboarding/README.md` — "`init` does not report success over a graph that fails
  those rules."
- `docs/services/components/cli-commands/DOC.md` — "exiting 1 when the graph fails the rules on disk".
- `BRIEF.md:147` acceptance criterion — not met for `--mode both`.

Recommendation: give `import_docs` the same post-condition `.1` gave the bootstrap (a `part_of` edge
to the root, or stop defaulting an unclassifiable document to `kind: domain`), and take the verdict
over an index that includes everything `init` wrote — move the reindex to the end of
`non_interactive_init`, or reindex inside `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph` before judging. Add a
scenario over `--mode both`; the wizard/`--yes` disagreement is the assertion that would have caught
this.

### Major 2 — the suite never varies `--mode`, and the branch enumerator cannot see the second writer

Files: `tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py:98,674`,
`tests/test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py:60-75`,
`tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature`.

Every test and every scenario in this epic pins `--mode bootstrap`. `THE_BRANCHES` varies flags and
monkeypatch bindings and never the `--mode` value; no test in the changed set passes `both` or
`import`. 112 tests in the epic's seven files pass, and none of them can see Major 1.

`test_init_branches_that_reach_the_bootstrap.py` is a real improvement over counting bindings by
hand, but two of its properties keep it green here. Its reachability scan is seeded from
`bootstrap_project` alone, so `import_docs` — the other writer of `domain` nodes — is outside the
instrument, and its docstring's claim that "a fourth branch fails these tests on the day it is
written" does not hold for a fourth *writer*. And the check is syntactic: it asserts a call to
`_verdict_on_the_generated_graph` follows the branch, which its own "Known limits" concedes answers
"could this branch report" rather than "does it report". `--yes --mode both` has the call and passes
the test while the verdict is blind.

Recommendation: parametrise the behavioural cases over `--mode` as well as over the flag, and seed
the reachability scan from every function that writes a graph file under `.beadloom/_graph/`, not
from `bootstrap_project` alone.

### Major 3 — `docs/services/cli.md` still documents the pre-BDL-067 `init`

`docs/services/cli.md:19-56` is the `cli` node's reference doc and is in this bead's specification
set. It was not touched on this branch. It describes `init`'s four invocations and its flags and
says nothing about the largest behaviour change in the epic: `init` can now exit 1, and prints one
of two failure reports when it does. An adopter reading the CLI reference is told the old contract.
The change is documented in `docs/services/mcp.md` and in the `cli-commands` component doc, which is
what makes the omission easy to miss rather than acceptable.

Recommendation: add the non-zero exit and the two report shapes to the `beadloom init` section, and
state which paths take the verdict.

## Minor

1. `setup.py:846-874` — the evaluated-rules report names the wrong files when the failing node came
   from the import step. Measured on the wizard `both` run: the violating node is `payments`, from
   `.beadloom/_graph/imported.yml`, and the message says "This is a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap"
   and points the adopter at `.beadloom/_graph/services.yml` and `rules.yml`, neither of which
   contains it. Fixing Major 1 removes the case; naming the file each violating node came from would
   remove the shape.
2. `setup.py:980-983` — the `--yes` branch calls the verdict for every mode, including
   `--mode import`, where the command wrote no graph, and both headlines begin "the graph this
   command just wrote". It is unreachable today only because an import-only run leaves no
   `rules.yml`, so `run_lint` returns clean before reading the index. Gate the call on
   `"bootstrap" in result`.
3. `setup.py:827` — "`beadloom ci` will report this as: lint — {summary}." `ci` renders
   `[FAIL] lint: <summary>` (`federation.py:439`) or `::notice::lint FAIL: <summary>` (`:481`).
   Neither is `lint — <summary>`. The line exists to pre-empt the adopter's next command, so it
   should quote a shape that command emits.

## Nitpick

`setup.py:734-742` — `_wrote_the_rules_file`'s docstring says `rules_generated` is 0 "exactly when
the file was already there". It is also 0 when the bootstrap wrote no nodes and when
`generate_rules` finds no `domain` or `feature` kind (`rules_gen.py:72-73`). No false message
follows today, because in both of those cases no `rules.yml` exists and lint returns clean, but the
stated equivalence is not the one the code holds.

## Facts to report rather than defects

- **BDL-UX #215 was derived independently before the issue log was read, and is not re-filed.**
  Measured: `beadloom ci --no-reindex` on a scratch adopter with a valid `rules.yml` and no index
  prints `lint FAIL: rules configuration error`, while every other step in the same output says
  `database missing` — `gate.py:242-248` stamps `RULES_CONFIG_ERROR` on all three `LintError` raise
  sites in `graph/linter.py` and two of them are index problems. Its corollary, that
  `docs/domains/application/README.md` and `ci-gate/SPEC.md:23` now document the wrong summary as the
  behaviour, is named in #215's own "Expected" and is not filed here either.
- **The withholding was partly defeated, and by the launch prompt.** `review-brief` reported 0
  comments withheld. The prompt then told me that a fourth instance of the class had been found
  outside `init` and filed as #215. That is a fact about this change that I did not derive, and it
  is directional: it says where the answer already was, which shapes where a sweep looks next. It
  prevented a duplicate file, and it cost independence on the same axis it protected. I reached #215
  by my own measurement anyway, which is the only reason I can say the cost was survivable this time.
