title: [BDL-067.12][dev] the withdrawal line claims a rule failed on the branch where none was evaluated
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.11 Major 1, routed from .10 and re-derived independently by the reviewer on five scratch adopter projects.

On the wizard + unloadable-rules.yml path the failure report opens by asserting what the next two lines deny. Measured verbatim, rc 1:

    The scaffold above was written, but it does not pass the rules it is checked against:
    Error: .beadloom/_graph/rules.yml could not be read, so the graph this command wrote was not
      checked against it.
      Invalid rules configuration: rules.yml: missing required 'version' field
    No rule was evaluated, so the graph is unchecked rather than wrong. Repair ...

Line 1 says the graph does not pass; line 2 says it was not checked; line 4 says nothing was evaluated. Reproduced with two different unloadable files (missing 'version', and a rule missing 'name'), so it is the BRANCH and not one parse error.

THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS. This epic has now found the same defect three times — a message asserting a fact the code knows to be false — and each time by the same route: a bead reasons about one shape and does not carry the reasoning across to the neighbouring shape. .6 counted bindings and called them branches; .9 reasoned about WHOSE rules failed; this one reasons about whether any were evaluated. WITHDRAWN_COMPLETION_CLAIM's own docstring shows the gap: it records that the line is 'deliberately silent about who wrote the rules' — having considered whose rules failed and not whether any ran.

It is also load-bearing for the reader: the withdrawal is the headline and ends in a colon promising a list of failing rules, and what follows the colon is a parse error. _report_rules_the_graph_fails supplies a list; _report_rules_that_would_not_load correctly does not.

FIX (the reviewer's preferred option, and the reason is sound): reword the SHARED constant to say only what is true of both shapes — e.g. 'The scaffold above was written, but the check that follows it did not pass:' — dropping the colon if what follows is a sentence rather than a list. Do NOT give _report_rules_that_would_not_load its own withdrawal string: a second string to keep in step with the first is exactly the drift RULES_CONFIG_ERROR was made a shared constant to avoid.

TEST WORK IS IN THIS BEAD, not a separate one (coordinator decision, stated rather than silent — a separate test bead for one assertion and one scenario would be the quota failure .10 was re-scoped to avoid):
- tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py:617-643 asserts only the line's POSITION and never its text, so it currently pins the wrong wording in place. Its own docstring calls the line 'the same false claim' and stops there. Add the missing assertion: THE_WITHDRAWAL must not claim a rule failed.
- tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature covers the unloadable file only on the --bootstrap branch, where no withdrawal is printed and the contradiction cannot appear. Add the wizard + unloadable case.

comments.text:
SWEEP RESULT — A FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE CLASS. Reported here rather than fixed, per the assignment: not in this commit, route it.

**Finding: `RULES_CONFIG_ERROR` is the summary for three different causes, and two of them have nothing to do with the rules configuration.**

`graph/linter.py` raises `LintError` from THREE sites:
  :154  Invalid rules configuration: <loader complaint>          <- genuinely a rules problem
  :182  index not found at <db_path> — nothing to lint against    <- NOT a rules problem
  :229  index cannot be read (<err>) — it predates the schema     <- NOT a rules problem
`application/gate.py:242-248` catches `LintError` and stamps ALL THREE with
`summary=RULES_CONFIG_ERROR` ('rules configuration error'). The true reason is carried in the
finding's `why` and is then contradicted by the summary printed above it.

MEASURED, not read. Scratch adopter project, valid loadable rules.yml, no index:
    $ beadloom ci --no-reindex          -> rc 1
    ::notice::lint FAIL: rules configuration error
    ::error::lint: index not found at .../.beadloom/beadloom.db — nothing to lint against.
                  Run `beadloom reindex` first, or drop --no-reindex.
Also measured directly: `lint_step(root)` over that project returns
`summary == RULES_CONFIG_ERROR` while `findings[0]['why']` is the index message. So the Gate
tells an adopter their rules configuration is broken while holding, one line down, the fact that
it is not — the same class this epic has now found four times.

SECOND-ORDER REACH, in `init`. `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph` branches on
`step.summary == RULES_CONFIG_ERROR`, so any LintError that is not a rules-config error is
rendered by `_report_rules_that_would_not_load`, which prints '.beadloom/_graph/rules.yml could
not be read' and 'Repair .beadloom/_graph/rules.yml' — pointing the adopter at a file that is
fine. I could NOT construct that reach from `init` itself (every init branch reindexes before
the verdict, so the index exists), so I am reporting the `ci`/`lint_step` reach as measured and
the `init` reach as latent — it becomes live the moment a fourth LintError site is added or the
schema branch fires after a reindex.

THE PROSE SAYS IT TOO — three copies, all written by this epic, all false for two of three sites:
  - src/beadloom/application/gate.py:61 — 'the lint step's summary when rules.yml could not be
    loaded at all'
  - docs/domains/application/README.md (RULES_CONFIG_ERROR bullet) — same sentence
  - docs/domains/application/features/ci-gate/SPEC.md:23 — 'Its LintError branch — rules.yml
    present and unloadable — is the one place a finding's rule is this step's own name'
The name `RULES_CONFIG_ERROR` is itself the smallest carrier of the false claim.

WHY IT IS THE SAME CLASS AND ARRIVED THE SAME WAY. `.6` reasoned about ONE LintError cause — the
hand-edited rules file it was fixing — and named the constant, the summary and the prose after
that one cause, without carrying the reasoning to the other two raise sites in the same `except`.
`.6` counted bindings and called them branches; `.9` reasoned about whose rules failed; `.12`
reasoned about whether any ran; this one reasons about WHICH FAILURE it was.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not taken here): the branch is on the wrong thing. `lint_step` should distinguish
the causes — either a summary derived from the exception rather than one constant, or a typed
`LintError` subclass per raise site — and `init` should branch on the cause rather than on a
summary string. Naming the current constant more honestly (e.g. 'lint could not run') would close
the false claim without closing the conflation, so it is half a fix.

CHECKED AND CLEARED in the same sweep, so the coordinator knows the sweep's extent:
  - '`beadloom ci` will report this as: lint — {step.summary}.' — TRUE as a prediction on both
    branches; measured, `ci` really does print that summary. It inherits the untruth above but
    adds none, so it stays as it is and is fixed by fixing the summary.
  - `_report_rules_the_graph_fails`, both arms — re-measured today on the wizard over an
    adopter's own `service-needs-parent` and over a bootstrap-authored rules.yml. Correct.
  - `_report_rules_that_would_not_load`, all three lines — correct whenever the cause really is
    an unloadable rules.yml; false only via the mis-summary above.
  - `_wrote_the_rules_file` / the blame split — checked against the case where the bootstrap
    authors rules.yml but a node from another _graph/*.yml fails. Blame on Beadloom is still
    defensible there (the RULE is ours), so this is inside `.9`'s decision, not a new false claim.
  - The five docs this epic edited: agent-prime/SPEC.md, onboarding/README.md, mcp.md and
    cli-commands/DOC.md carry no claim falsified by a reachable branch. application/README.md and
    ci-gate/SPEC.md do, and they are the two listed above.

title: [BDL-067.9][dev] the failure message blames Beadloom for the adopter's own rules
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-e8s4.8 Major 1, measured by the reviewer on a scratch adopter project.

When the graph fails an EVALUATED rule, init prints:
    Error: the graph this command just wrote does not pass the rules this command wrote alongside it.
      service-needs-parent
      This is a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap rather than in your project — please report it with the rule name(s) above.

That is true ONLY when the bootstrap authored rules.yml. bootstrap_project writes the file only if it does not already exist (bootstrap.py:288-293). So on a re-init, or on a project whose rules.yml came from an earlier Beadloom or from a hand edit, the failing rule is the ADOPTER'S OWN and Beadloom is told to be blamed for it. Measured: a scratch TypeScript project carrying a hand-written service-needs-parent rule — both 'beadloom init' (wizard) and 'beadloom init --bootstrap' print the above over a rule this command did not write.

The docstring at setup.py:738-742 carries the same false premise: 'the only rules generate_rules writes for an adopter are the two the bootstrap's own post-condition satisfies: a red verdict over evaluated rules can only mean Beadloom contradicted itself'. It reads as verified and is not.

NOTE THAT .6 ALREADY KNEW THIS FACT and wrote it down for the OTHER branch — setup.py:790-793, 'bootstrap_project leaves an existing rules file alone, so the file that did not load is usually the adopter's own edit' — without carrying it across to the branch it invalidates. Two neighbouring messages, one correct.

FIX: the information is already in hand. bootstrap_project returns rules_generated (bootstrap.py:333), which is 0 exactly when the rules file was already there. Thread it to _verdict_on_the_generated_graph. Print the 'defect in Beadloom's bootstrap' sentence ONLY when the bootstrap authored the file; otherwise say the graph fails a rule already present in .beadloom/_graph/rules.yml, and DROP the request to report it. Correct the docstring premise in the same edit. The --yes/--bootstrap sites can pass the value directly; the wizard reads it from result['bootstrap'].

ALSO IN SCOPE — Minor 2 (setup.py:1005-1006): the wizard prints 'Initialization complete!', 'Generated:' and 'Next steps:' and THEN reports failure and exits 1, because interactive_init prints its own tail before returning. The --bootstrap branch takes the verdict before its Next steps, so the two branches read differently and the wizard makes a success claim it immediately withdraws. Cheapest correct fix: one line before the error that withdraws the claim explicitly, e.g. 'The scaffold above was written, but it does not pass its own rules:'. Do NOT move the check inside interactive_init — that crosses a layer.

   project — please report it with the rule name(s) above." That is only true when the bootstrap
   authored `rules.yml`. `bootstrap_project` writes the file **only if it does not already exist**
   (bootstrap.py:288-293), so on a re-init, or on a project whose `rules.yml` was written by an
   earlier Beadloom or edited by hand, the rule that failed is the adopter's own and Beadloom is
   told to be blamed for it. Measured: a scratch TypeScript project carrying a hand-written

   their own rules, and the review cost is a docstring premise that reads as verified and is not.

   `rules_generated` (bootstrap.py:333), which is `0` exactly when the rules file was already there.

   already in `.beadloom/_graph/rules.yml`, and drop the request to report it. Correct the docstring
   premise in the same edit, and note that the `--yes`/`--bootstrap` sites can pass the value
   directly while the wizard reads it from `result["bootstrap"]`.

Minor:

2. src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:1005-1006 vs onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py
   The wizard prints `Initialization complete!`, `Generated:` and `Next steps:` and *then* reports
   the failure and exits 1, because `interactive_init` prints its own tail before returning. The

title: [BDL-067.4][review] read-only verification of the BDL-067 fix
description:
Run 'beadloom review-brief beadloom-e8s4.4' for your input. Read-only: post findings to bead comments, do not edit code.

Verify in particular:
- the deliverable is an INVARIANT over bootstrap_project, not a patch to the single reported branch
- the emitted edge uses the root node's ref_id AS WRITTEN, not a recomputed project name
- rules_gen.py was NOT weakened (option (b) was rejected by the owner; a silently smaller rule set for adopters is the defect being fixed, not a permissible alternative)
- every new test assertion was verified to FAIL against the pre-fix code
- the reproduction from BDL-UX #192 was re-run end to end on a project that is not us

refs: onboarding, cli

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 2 major

Scope reviewed: git diff main...HEAD over the 23 files the brief lists. Verified independently
before reading any author comment; the launch prompt carried no author summary. One caveat I am
the only party who can see: the brief withheld 0 comments, but ACTIVE.md — which the launch prompt
named as required reading — carries a per-bead Results table with the authors' own accounts
(`API change: gate._step_lint -> public lint_step`, the red-verification and coverage numbers).
The ordering held for bead comments and was defeated through the epic document.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED GREEN (measured by me, not taken on report)

- The #192 reproduction, end to end, on a project that is not us. Scratch TypeScript adopter
  (`package.json` name `scratch-adopter`, one flat `src/index.ts`):
  `init --yes --mode bootstrap` -> rc 0, `Graph: 2 nodes, 1 edges`; `lint --strict` -> rc 0;
  `beadloom ci` -> rc 0 (measured without a pipe). Same fixture against `git archive af26750 src`
  imported via PYTHONPATH (`gate.lint_step` absent there, so the override was real): 2 nodes,
  0 edges, no `edges:` key. The fix is the difference.
- The deliverable IS an invariant, not a branch patch. `_missing_domain_parent_edges`
  (bootstrap.py:35-72) runs over the whole node list at bootstrap.py:274, after every edge
  producer and before the YAML write, so a future branch that forgets the edge is closed too.
- The edge uses the root ref_id AS WRITTEN: `root_node[\"ref_id\"]` is passed in, not a recomputed
  project name. Asserted for a parenthesised name in two places, and I confirmed no dangling dst.
- rules_gen.py was NOT weakened: `git diff main...HEAD -- src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/rules_gen.py`
  is empty. Option (b) was not taken.
- Test assertions verified capable of failing: pre-fix bootstrap reproduced 0 edges (above), and
  the `.2` scenarios construct the divergence rather than await it, which is the right call once
  `.1` landed. Anti-vacuity guards are present (`fixture produced no {kind} node`,
  `fixture produced no classified parent`) — those are the difference between a scenario and
  ceremony, and they are there.
- ruff rc 0, `mypy --strict` clean over 225 files, `beadloom lint --strict` rc 0, `sync-check`
  rc 0, `doctor` rc 0, `beadloom diff --since main` reports no graph change. The 6 files under
  tests/ + acceptance run 55 passed.
- BDD: the five scenarios say something an observer sees, in the adopter's vocabulary, and the
  `.2` sabotage is honest about what it fakes (the graph half only; the real `generate_rules`
  still writes the rule). The brief's `no-bound-scenario` finding is against a review bead and is
  not a defect.

Major:

1. src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:944 (and setup.py:724, tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py:40-47)
   Issue: the class-prevention half of the fix is applied at two of the three branches of `init`
   that write a bootstrap graph. `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph` has exactly two call sites
   (setup.py:853 `--yes`, setup.py:921 `--bootstrap`). The default interactive wizard — plain
   `beadloom init`, no flags — falls through to `interactive_init`, which calls
   `bootstrap_project` for mode `bootstrap`/`both` (init_flow.py:201-206), reindexes, prints
   `Initialization complete!` and returns with no verdict. Reproduced read-only, sabotaging the
   same binding the shipped tests sabotage (`init_flow.bootstrap_project`, `part_of` edges
   stripped back out of services.yml after the real bootstrap and the real generate_rules):
       WIZARD `beadloom init` exit_code = 0   names domain-needs-parent: False
       lint --strict exit_code = 1   domain-needs-parent:require:error:::src:
       ci exit_code = 1
   That is #192's exact shape, unguarded, on the branch a human adopter meets first. Coverage
   over the six changed test files confirms setup.py:930-944 is never entered.
   The test module's own comment states \"The two ways `init` reaches the bootstrap\" — true of
   monkeypatch BINDINGS (the wizard shares the `--yes` binding), false of branches, and the
   wording is what hides the third one.
   Recommendation: call `_verdict_on_the_generated_graph(project_root)` after `interactive_init`
   returns, guarded on `result[\"mode\"] in (\"bootstrap\", \"both\")` and skipped when
   `result.get(\"review\") == \"edit\"` (that branch hands the graph to the user on purpose).
   Add a third leg to `BOOTSTRAP_BINDINGS`-style parametrisation, or a wizard-specific case, and
   fix the comment to say \"the two bindings\" rather than \"the two ways\".

2. docs/services/cli.md:19-60
   Issue: stale. This is the adopter-facing CLI reference for `beadloom init`, it is listed in
   the brief's SPECIFICATION set, and it still describes a command that cannot fail. The change
   alters the command's exit-code contract — `init` now exits 1 and prints
   `Error: the graph this command just wrote does not pass the rules this command wrote alongside
   it.` — and the section says nothing about it, though it spends a full paragraph on the
   `.gitignore` side effect. `sync-check` also flags `docs/services/cli.md` with surface drift
   (`watches=cli,graph,flow.yml`). Six other docs were updated by the dev beads, so this one is
   an omission rather than a deferral.
   Recommendation: add the exit-code contract to the `beadloom init` section, naming which
   branches take the verdict (do not write \"init exits 1\" unqualified while finding 1 stands).
   Natural owner is `.5`, so this can be routed rather than run as a dev fix cycle.

Minor:

3. src/beadloom/onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py:69 vs BRIEF.md and docs/domains/onboarding/README.md
   The stated post-condition is absolute — \"every node the bootstrap writes with kind: domain
   carries at least one outgoing part_of edge\" — while the implementation carves out a domain
   whose ref_id equals the root's. The carve-out is right (a self-edge is not a parent), but it
   lands on the classic Python src-layout. Measured on a fresh `ledger` project with
   `src/ledger/`: `init --yes --mode bootstrap` rc 0, `Graph: 2 nodes, 0 edges`, services.yml
   holding TWO nodes with ref_id `ledger` (one service, one domain) and no `edges:` key; the
   loader keeps one, so `lint --strict` reports `domain-needs-parent:rule_liveness:warn` and
   `ci` is rc 0. Not a regression — pre-fix behaviour is identical, and `.1`'s guard is not the
   cause — but the graph silently loses a node on a very common layout.
   Recommendation: state the exception in the BRIEF/README sentence as the docstring already
   does, and log the ref_id collision to UX-Issues.md as its own defect (its fix is a distinct
   ref_id, not an edge).

4. src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py:748-751
   When `lint_step` fails through its `LintError` branch (gate.py:234-239) the finding's `rule`
   is the literal `\"lint\"` and its `why` carries the parse error. The init message then prints
   `  lint` and drops the text, so an adopter with a hand-edited unparseable rules.yml is told a
   rule named `lint` failed and not what is wrong with the file.
   Recommendation: print `f[\"why\"]` when it is present, or special-case the
   `summary == \"rules configuration error\"` step.

5. docs/domains/onboarding/README.md:167
   The bullet opens \"`init` does not report success over a graph that fails those rules\" and
   qualifies to two branches only in the next sentence. The opening clause is broader than the
   code while finding 1 stands.

Note on `--release`: this tracker writes every role under one identity, so it cannot establish
that the verdict was recorded by someone other than the bead's author. That is the expected
answer here, not a defect.

title: [BDL-067.2][dev] init must not report success over a graph that fails the rules it just wrote
description:
The half that prevents the CLASS rather than the instance. Independent of .1: after .1 lands, a future divergence between what init writes and what init requires must be visible at init time, not at the adopter's first ci run.

TODAY: services/commands/setup.py:781-804 (the --yes branch) prints 'Initialized beadloom (mode: ...)' + 'Graph: N nodes, M edges' and returns bare -> click exit 0. No lint, no validation, no rc computation. non_interactive_init (onboarding/scanner/init_flow.py:40-117) reindexes (:96-103) but never lints. The --bootstrap non---yes branch (setup.py:806-870) is the same shape, and its own closing advice at :866 tells the user to run lint afterwards.

REQUIRED: after the graph is written, init evaluates it with the SAME semantics the Gate uses — application/gate.py:217-233, 'passed = not result.has_errors', i.e. lint --strict semantics, NOT the bare lint that stays 0 on error-severity violations (services/commands/federation.py:331-343). Then either exit non-zero, or state the incompleteness in the words the gate will use — the rule name the adopter will see. Silence is what is being fixed; a green that describes the checker's ignorance is not acceptable here.

SITE: setup.py:793-798, right after the 'Graph: N nodes, M edges' line where the counts are in hand. Precedent for naming a known-weak green: services/commands/federation.py:333-343.

COVER BOTH BRANCHES: --yes and interactive --bootstrap.

DONE WHEN: an init that writes a graph failing its own generated rules cannot terminate with a silent rc 0.

comments.text:
COMPLETED beadloom-e8s4.2 — commit e52aa06.

WHAT. init evaluates the graph it just wrote with the Gate's own semantics and exits 1 rather than reporting success. services/commands/setup.py:_verdict_on_the_generated_graph(project_root) runs application.gate.lint_step and, when the step does not pass, prints to stderr: the headline, one line per error-severity rule name, the exact line 'beadloom ci' will show for that step (the GateStep summary), and where the scaffold is on disk; then sys.exit(1). Called at the end of the --yes branch (after the Graph/Index summary lines) and of the --bootstrap branch (after the missing-parser warning, before 'Next steps' — which therefore never prints over a red graph).

DECISIONS.
1. Share the Gate's step, do not restate it. _step_lint became the public lint_step instead of copying 'passed = not result.has_errors' to the init site. The defect being closed is two halves of one command disagreeing about whether a tree is green; a second copy of the predicate is how they would disagree again. Bare 'lint' was rejected as the bead required: federation.py:331-343 keeps rc 0 on error-severity violations by design.
2. Exit non-zero, not a loud rc 0. generate_rules (rules_gen.py:18-78) writes an adopter exactly two rules, domain-needs-parent and feature-needs-parent, and .1's post-condition satisfies both — so a red verdict here can only mean Beadloom contradicted itself, and no healthy adopter path is turned red. A loud zero would still let a scripted 'init && ci' run on to where the cause is out of view.
3. The scaffold is NOT withdrawn on a red verdict. Asserted in test_the_graph_is_still_on_disk_to_be_repaired: the rc reports the defect, the adopter keeps an editable graph.
4. Import-only init needs no special case: linter.lint returns an empty result before touching the database when rules.yml is absent (linter.py:145-149), so the verdict passes rather than erroring on a missing index.

HOW THE FAILING CASE WAS CONSTRUCTED (the bead's central requirement). After .1 a virgin bootstrap is self-consistent, so the divergence is injected, not awaited: a wrapper round the real bootstrap_project lets it write the real graph and the real rules, then removes the part_of edges from .beadloom/_graph/services.yml (dropping the edges: key entirely, which is the shape bootstrap_project itself produced before .1). rules_gen is untouched, so domain-needs-parent is still written and is still error severity by loader default. The result is BDL-UX #192 verbatim — 'Graph: 2 nodes, 0 edges' — on a bootstrap no longer capable of producing it. The two init branches bind bootstrap_project differently and are sabotaged separately: 'beadloom.onboarding.scanner.init_flow.bootstrap_project' for --yes (module-level import) and 'beadloom.onboarding.bootstrap_project' for --bootstrap (imported inside the command body).

TESTS. tests/test_init_verdict_over_its_own_rules.py — 14 cases, every one parametrised over both branches. Sabotaged tree: rc != 0; the output names domain-needs-parent (not merely 'failed'); the verdict agrees with 'lint --strict' on the same tree; the graph and rules files survive. Clean tree: rc 0; no rule named; agrees with 'lint --strict' again. The clean-path cases exist so the check cannot pass by being permanently red. RED before GREEN was observed: 6 of the 14 failed on the pre-change tree (the four sabotage cases per branch minus the two that were already true), with lint --strict rc 1 on the same trees. Acceptance: one scenario added to tests/acceptance/features/bootstrap_self_consistency.feature under @bead:beadloom-e8s4.2 (node agent-prime inherited), 'init does not report success over a graph that fails the rules it just wrote', red as an unbound step before its implementation.

Clean room (git archive HEAD + my 11 files): 7334 passed, 1 failed — tests/test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh reports 40 pairs 'unverified', and it fails identically on a pristine HEAD archive with none of my files, so it is a property of a checkout with no committed sync baseline rather than of this change. title: [BDL-067.1][dev] bootstrap post-condition: no domain node is written without a part_of edge (fallback branch attaches to the root service)
description:
Fix (a), as a stated post-condition of bootstrap_project rather than a patch to one branch.

INVARIANT: every node bootstrap_project writes with kind=domain carries at least one outgoing part_of edge — to its classified parent where one exists, to the root service node otherwise.

THE BROKEN PATH: onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py:133-145 (the 'if not nodes and scan["source_dirs"]' fallback) creates one node per source dir at preset.default_kind (= domain under MONOLITH) and adds no edge; the root-attachment loop at :226-229 iterates 'clusters', which is empty on that path, so those nodes never reach the root either. services.yml then omits the edges: key entirely (:232-235, 'if edges').

USE THE ROOT'S ACTUAL ref_id AS WRITTEN (bootstrap.py:171-179), do not recompute the project name: cluster refs pass through _sanitize_ref_id (:227-228, onboarding/scanner/constants.py:149-154) and the root ref does not, so a recomputed dst silently stops resolving for a project whose name contains parentheses.

ALSO CHECK the preset.infer_part_of=False path (:125-131) for the same hole — the invariant is the deliverable, not the single branch.

DO NOT touch rules_gen.py: option (b) was considered and rejected by the owner.

DONE WHEN: bootstrap_project over tests/adopter_project.py::typescript_project produces a graph where lint --strict has no errors, and the invariant holds for every preset the module can select.

WHAT: bootstrap_project now carries a stated post-condition — every node it writes with kind=domain leaves the function with at least one outgoing part_of edge, to its classified parent where one exists and to the root service node otherwise. The guard is "if not claims.is_live" over the whole loop followed by continue, which looks total, but .9's distinction -- total carries declared severity, partial stays advisory -- is the entire basis of the fix. title: [BDL-062] .9 dev: one node vetoes the source root, and the stand-down is silent
description:
Found by .4 answering a coordinator challenge on #195. Two defects, one trigger, and the second is the class this whole feature exists to eliminate.

TRIGGER: _common_prefix runs over ALL paired sources. A single node whose source shares nothing with the rest -- here site/ -- collapses the source root to empty for all 85 others. min_support guards the dominant-mapping half; NOTHING guards the prefix. One pair vetoes the derivation for the entire graph.

Then _area_depth votes only on doc paths containing a vocabulary word, and the two outcomes diverge:

  doc at site/vitepress-site/DOC.md   -> depth 0    -> 84 compared -> 7 FALSE errors
  doc at guides/vitepress-site.md     -> depth None -> 86 unnamed  -> rule reports CHECKED NOTHING

DEFECT 2, the dangerous one: that stand-down is emitted through liveness_finding, which hardcodes rule_type = LIVENESS_RULE_TYPE and severity = warn. So lint --strict stays rc 0 while the rule silently stops checking all 86 pairs -- EVEN THOUGH this repository escalates doc-area-coherence to error. A rule the project declared blocking can stand down over 100% of its population and the Gate stays green.

That is a green gate describing the checker's ignorance, shipped inside the release about green gates describing the checker's ignorance.

NOT EXOTIC: any adopter with a site/, scripts/, tooling/ or a second source root meets this on first contact.

SCOPE:
1. The prefix must tolerate a minority root -- one pair must not veto 85. Whatever the mechanism, state the population and the threshold in the output the way .2 already does for the dominant mapping.
2. A rule standing down over its WHOLE population must not be silently downgraded to warn when the project escalated it. Decide and record: does liveness follow the declared severity, or does total stand-down differ from an inert exclusion? Either is defensible; silence is not.
3. Rewrite #195 -- it is inaccurate on trigger and FALSE on evidence ('4 true findings become 6 false' compares against a baseline of 4 that did not exist; the measured baseline was 0). The vitepress-site docs_absent reason inherits the same framing.

BLOCKS THE RELEASE. Shipping doc_area_coherence with a silent stand-down is shipping the defect 3.0.1 is about.

title: [BDL-UX #192][bug] a virgin `beadloom init --yes` leaves `beadloom ci` red — the bootstrap writes a domain with no part_of edge and a rule that requires one
description:
MEASURED ON THE BUILT 3.0.0 WHEEL, in a fresh venv, against a scratch adopter project (a TypeScript service at 0.4.1 with one file under src/) — `beadloom-mr2l.90`'s artifact verification.

    beadloom init --yes --mode bootstrap   ->  rc 0   Graph: 2 nodes, 0 edges
    beadloom lint                          ->  rc 0
    beadloom lint --strict                 ->  rc 1   domain-needs-parent:require:error:::src:
    beadloom ci                            ->  rc 1

THE TWO HALVES OF ONE COMMAND DISAGREE. The classifier writes a `src` node of kind `domain` and NO EDGES AT ALL (the generated services.yml has no `edges:` key), while `generate_rules` writes `domain-needs-parent` whenever any node is a domain. So the scaffold fails the rules the same command wrote one step earlier, on a repository nobody has touched.

NOT INTRODUCED BY 3.0.0: `onboarding/scanner/rules_gen.py` and the bootstrap classifier both predate it. It had never been measured because everything this project measures runs on THIS project, whose graph has been hand-authored since BDL-008. That is the epic's own thesis arriving from the outside.

WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DOES NOT COVER IT. `rules_gen.py` carries this exact worry for `feature`: BDL-UX #71 made `has_edge_to` an empty matcher so a feature nested under a service is not flagged, and the comment says requiring a domain parent 'makes a clean bootstrap fail its own lint --strict gate out of the box'. An empty matcher relaxes WHERE the edge may point; it does not excuse a node with no edge. `service-needs-parent` was removed outright for the same class. The fix was applied twice, to the two neighbours, and the middle case is what ships.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, AND THE CHOICE IS A DECISION:
(a) the bootstrap emits `part_of` edges from every classified domain to the root service node. Structurally complete, and it is what a hand-authored graph looks like. Against it: it states a parent relationship the classifier did not verify.
(b) `generate_rules` omits `domain-needs-parent` when the bootstrap produced no `part_of` edge to require. Honest about what was inferred. Against it: the project ships with one fewer structural rule, and nothing later reminds the human to add it.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN: `init` must not print rc 0 over a graph that fails the rules it just wrote. If the graph is knowingly incomplete, init should say so in the words the gate will use.

TEST IT ON A PROJECT THAT IS NOT US: `tests/adopter_project.py` builds the fixtures; the reproduction above used `typescript_project`.

title: [BDL-061.18c][dev] S5: a WORKING root means two different things to its two readers
description:
FINDING BDL-061.18-4, filed by the test bead .18; two xfail(strict=True) statements in tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py::TestAWrongWorkingDeclarationIsDetectable, each with a passing control beside it.

WHAT. check_sync classifies the DOCS-DIR-RELATIVE doc_path the indexer writes ('guides/ci-setup.md'); check_spaces classifies the PROJECT-RELATIVE path ('docs/guides/ci-setup.md'). Kind agrees on both spellings because a stem has no prefix — which is why every shipped case works and why this has been invisible. Roots do not agree, and the WORKING exemption is the one knob where a root decides whether a gate applies.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE WRONG. (a) A working root spelled the way every other root in doc_roots is spelled — project-relative, 'docs/guides/*.md' — has NO EFFECT on freshness. (b) The docs-dir-relative spelling DOES silence freshness, and the check built to catch a wrong WORKING declaration cannot see it: working_documents classifies the file project-relative, finds AS-IS, and reports no working_declaration_contradicted for the very document check_sync just excused.

MEASURED in a clean-room git worktree at f67fc36, through the real CLI: three stale documents under node 'beadloom'; with doc_roots.as_is.roots=[docs/**/*.md] and doc_roots.working.roots=[*.md, guides/*.md] plus a reason, 'beadloom sync-check' went rc 2 -> rc 0, six pairs became exempt, and 'beadloom docs spaces --json' reported zero contradiction findings. Where the project-relative spelling matches nothing at all the liveness leg does fire — and then says 'the WORKING exemption excused nothing' while freshness was excusing six pairs, which is worse than silence because it invites the reader to conclude the declaration is inert.

RELATED, and stated so it is not rediscovered: index_docs walks the docs directory alone, so nothing outside it enters sync_state. The shipped ACTIVE.md lives under the planning tree, so the shipped exemption excuses 0 of 330 pairs on this repository while docs spaces prints '55 WORKING document(s) exempt' — a count of documents, not of excused pairs. It is true and it is not the number a reader will take from it.

SHAPE OF THE FIX: one spelling. Either check_sync resolves its doc_path to project-relative before asking, or DocSpaces takes the docs directory and normalises. Whichever is chosen, the two callers must be shown to classify one file identically — that is the assertion in TestAWrongWorkingDeclarationIsDetectable.

DONE WHEN: both xfail(strict=True) tests turn green and .71/.72 inherit the single spelling.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COORDINATOR — raised P2 -> P0. This is a gate defeat, not a classification inconsistency.

The measurement in .18 is that a root-declared WORKING exemption took `beadloom sync-check` from rc 2 to rc 0 with ZERO `working_declaration_contradicted` findings, because `check_sync` classifies a docs-dir-relative path while `check_spaces` classifies a project-relative one. Two readers, two meanings, one declaration.

What that amounts to for an adopter: declaring the docs root WORKING silently switches off the freshness gate. CONTEXT's own words for this family are 'an unnamed exclusion is how a gate is quietly switched off' — and here it is worse, because the exclusion IS named, in a file we tell people to edit, and the naming simply does not reach the reader that would object.

It is also the exact shape S5 was built to prevent. WORKING is exempt BY DECLARATION rather than by inference precisely so a wrong declaration can be detected; the detector exists, and the two paths never meet, so it detects nothing. A capability with no reachable caller is not a capability.

Fix the classification seam, not the symptom: one path vocabulary, established once, with a test that fails if the two readers ever disagree again — the shape .66 used for the three composed kinds ('same deletion, three artifacts, they must answer alike').

comments.text:
COMPLETED — one spelling, and the declaration now reaches the reader that objects.

WHAT. `DocSpaces.project_path(doc_path)` is the single translation from the docs-dir-relative path a `sync_state` row carries to the project-relative spelling every root glob is written in; `check_sync` asks it before classifying. `resolve_docs_dir(project_root)` in `infrastructure/doc_roots.py` is now the single reader of the `docs_dir` key — three readers held it before (`reindex/indexing._resolve_docs_dir`, `engine._resolve_reference_docs_dir`, and a hardcoded `docs` inside `check_sync`), and every `Path("docs")` in `doc_sync/engine.py` + `doc_shape.py` now goes through it.

ROOT PRECEDENCE, and why it is not arbitrary. Roots are consulted WORKING → TO-BE → AS-IS (`_ROOT_PRECEDENCE`, separate from `SPACES`, which stays the report's reading order). WORKING ships with an empty root list, so the only way a document reaches it by root is a project DECLARING it, while the AS-IS default is the catch-all `docs/**/*.md`. If the catch-all won, a declaration written in the file we tell adopters to edit would be silently inert — the same defect one layer down. Kind still wins over root, unchanged.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, through the real CLI on an incremental reindex (#175), each run reverted and `sync-check` rc 0 again afterwards:
- `docs/architecture.md` edited (2 pairs stale, rc 2). With `doc_roots.working.roots: [docs/architecture.md]`: `sync-check` rc 0 — the exemption still applies, which is the point of a declaration — and `beadloom docs spaces --json` reports **1 `working_declaration_contradicted` naming `docs/architecture.md`**, where the same configuration reported **0** before.
- The whole tree declared (`docs/**/*.md`): 28 of 330 pairs exempt and **6** contradictions named, previously 0. The 28 are the documents whose stem is not SPEC/DOC/README, because kind still wins over root.
- Exit codes and `--json` throughout (#148); no line counts.

TWO MORE HOLES CLOSED WHILE THE SEAM WAS OPEN, each with its own test:
1. `working_exemption_inert` only ever looked at declared KINDS, so an exemption declared by ROOT that matched nothing reported nothing — an exclusion that quietly stops applying, which is the finding's own sentence. It now fires on either half and names which.
2. `check_sync` returned `exempt` BEFORE hashing, so a declared document that had been DELETED read as excused rather than `missing`. That is BDL-UX #174's equation reached through the one verdict that never blocks. Existence is now established first; the exemption covers freshness and nothing else.

TESTS. 16 new in tests/test_bead75_one_path_vocabulary.py + 1 acceptance scenario (`@bead:beadloom-mr2l.75`, doc_spaces.feature). The invariant that bites: over four configurations (kind route, project-relative root, docs-dir-relative root, and a configured `docs_dir`), every pair freshness excuses must be a document the report calls WORKING — the comparison is spelled by the test from the docs directory it wrote, not built from the code under test. TESTS MUST BITE, measured: reverting the one-line seam fix (`spaces.project_path(doc_path)` → `doc_path`) reddens 4 unit tests + the acceptance scenario; restored by byte-identical copy (sha256 verified, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT).

TWO FIXTURES CORRECTED, and stated rather than hidden.
(a) `.18`'s pin `test_a_root_declared_exemption_that_silences_a_pair_is_contradicted` had `working.roots: [guides/*.md, *.md]` — the BROKEN vocabulary written down. Under one spelling that string means a top-level `guides/`, so it correctly excuses nothing under `docs/`. The ASSERTION is untouched (silences ⇒ contradicted); the roots are re-spelled `docs/**/*.md`, which is the gate defeat itself. The old configuration is kept as a passing test in TestADocsDirRelativeRootMeansWhatItSays, so the measurement stays executable.
(b) `.17`'s acceptance step wrote a `sync_state` row whose `doc_path` was PROJECT-relative — a spelling `index_docs` never writes. It passed only because the exemption short-circuited before the file was looked for. It now carries both spellings explicitly.

title: [dev] one non-UTF-8 document takes down the whole gate, and four populations are silently empty
description:
Review `.15`: 1 critical + the population majors. S4 ship-blocker.

=== CRITICAL - ONE DOCUMENT TAKES DOWN THE WHOLE RUN.
`doc_sync/doc_quality.py::check_documents` catches only `OSError`. A single non-UTF-8 planning document raises `UnicodeDecodeError` out of the `docs-quality` gate step and takes down the entire `beadloom ci` - measured by the reviewer: rc 1, a traceback, and NO step results at all. Not a wrong verdict; no verdict, for every check in the gate.

THIS IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE OF ONE FAMILY IN THIS EPIC: a handler narrower than what its call can raise, around text decoded without an explicit rule. `.36` (two), `.37` (the probes), `.40` (four call sites), `.42` (the ~40-site sweep) - and now a module written AFTER all four. That is the finding, not the missing except clause: the knowledge did not reach the next author. Say in the SPEC what the rule is, and check whether a lint rule or a test can make the next instance fail rather than ship.
Note `.42`'s decision framework: decide per site whether the stream is a UTF-8 CONTRACT (planning documents are) or the user's locale, and make the handler as wide as the call. And per CONTEXT: an undecodable document is `unverified`, never silently absent - `.14` already filed `beadloom-mr2l.62` for the reference leg's version of this.

=== MAJOR - POPULATIONS THAT ARE SILENTLY EMPTY.
- **All 11 `BRIEF.md` contribute ZERO to all four content checks, by template construction.** A whole document kind never enters the population and nothing says so. `checks_that_read_nothing` is a global OR and structurally cannot see a per-kind hole - so the anti-vacuity guard `b0xl` built has exactly the blind spot it was built to prevent, one level down. Report coverage per kind, not per check.
- Two more silent exits beyond `beadloom-mr2l.63`: a **reasonless `for.exclude`** (CONTEXT requires every exclusion to carry `reason` and `until`; this one is accepted bare) and a **live `non_behavioural` that is never reported** (PLAN's own criterion was "a chore MAY declare itself non-behavioural with a NAMED REASON and is accepted" - accepted silently is not accepted with a reason).
- `rules_inert` does not count `scenario_coverage` while the SPEC says it does. `.14` measured that repointing the path takes lint 68 -> 1 liveness finding; verify that still holds after you fix the count, because that behaviour is the proof the rule cannot be silently zeroed.
- The deliberate-silence note names ONE leg where the code skips FOUR. An honesty note understating what the code does - the sixth occurrence in this epic.

=== ALSO
`tests/test_doc_quality.py::test_our_approved_rfc_still_carries_pending_questions` is RED because commit `2ddbcf9` paid the debt it pins. That is the coordinator's doing and is correct: the pin characterised a defect that no longer exists. Rewrite it to assert the mechanism (a `Pending` row in an `Approved` document is reported) rather than the instance, so it keeps biting after the instance is gone.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — the critical is closed and MEASURED, and the population hole is now visible.

C1 REPRODUCED FIRST, on the working tree, not taken from the report: a cp1251 PRD under the default glob takes `beadloom docs quality` to rc 1 with 'UnicodeDecodeError: utf-8 codec cant decode byte 0xd6 in position 3', out of check_documents. RED before GREEN.

FIX, per .42's framework rather than a new one: a planning document is a UTF-8 CONTRACT (we choose the codec), so it is decoded with an explicit encoding and the handler is as wide as what read_text can raise — (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError). The document is COUNTED and carries a named 'unreadable' finding: per CONTEXT an undecodable document is unverified, never silently absent, and the old `continue` dropped it from `N documents read` as well.
- UNREADABLE is deliberately OUTSIDE CHECK_NAMES: it reads no population of its own, so counting it there would print a permanent 'NOT CHECKED: unreadable' on every clean run. SELECTABLE_CHECKS = CHECK_NAMES + UNREADABLE is what --check accepts.

TWO MORE SITES OF THE SAME FAMILY IN THE SAME CALL PATH, both found by measuring rather than by reading:

title: [dev] config-check --fix destroys a hand edit one line after promising it will not
description:
BDL-UX #186, found by `.12`. MERGE BLOCKER for S3 — not because of the data loss, which is older than this slice, but because of what S3 adds on top of it.

MEASURED BY THE COORDINATOR, twice:
  On features/BDL-061-S3: append a hand edit to .claude/agents/dev.md (sha 77dfc84f -> f40b584e).
    `beadloom config-check` says: "hand-edited: the body differs from the composition AND from what
    Beadloom last wrote. It will NOT be rewritten"
    `beadloom config-check --fix` -> sha back to 77dfc84f, the edit GONE, and it reports
    "Agent-config in sync - no blocking drift", exit 0. It does not mention deleting anything.
  On main (git worktree, same probe): the edit is destroyed there too, exit 1.

SO THE DESTRUCTION IS PRE-EXISTING AND IS NOT AN S3 REGRESSION. What S3 adds is the PROMISE. Before this slice `--fix` overwrote silently and claimed nothing; now the tool states "It will NOT be rewritten" and then rewrites it. A reader who trusts that sentence is exactly the reader who will run `--fix` feeling safe. Shipping a false promise in the slice whose subject is honest reporting is the part I will not merge.

TWO WAYS TO MAKE IT TRUE, and the choice needs its reason:
  (a) Honour the sentence: `--fix` refuses to overwrite a file classified hand-edited, fixes everything else, and reports what it declined and why. This matches CONTEXT's decision that a hand-edited vendored file is reported with migration guidance and NEVER rewritten - which is the decision the message is quoting.
  (b) Qualify the sentence: "...will not be rewritten by this check; `--fix` WILL overwrite it - move your additions to the project layer first." Cheaper, honest, and worse: it leaves a documented data-loss path in a command whose name promises repair.
(a) is the recommendation. If you take (b), say why (a) was rejected.

WHATEVER YOU CHOOSE, two things are required:
  - `--fix` must NEVER destroy content while reporting "in sync ... no blocking drift". A destructive action that reports success is the same defect class as a check that reports clean without checking - #174, #175, #172 - and it is worse, because those only misinformed.
  - Say what it did. If a file is rewritten, name it and say what was lost, in the output, not in a doc.

SCOPE: this bead is the message-and-behaviour contradiction only. The other three defects `.12` found (#187 virgin setup-agentic-flow leaves config-check at exit 1, #188 orphans/migration notes have no caller so #137 does not close, #189 `sync-update <doc> --check` WRITES) stay with `.58` - do not absorb them.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, REPORTS ARE NOT EVIDENCE. The test that matters: a hand-edited file survives `--fix`, or the loss is named in the output; and a run that changed a file may not report "no blocking drift".

title: [BDL-061.58][dev] project-local facts still reach adopters, and a red project turns green on upgrade
description:
Two findings from review `.11` that are the reviewer's own, not routed from an earlier bead. Both are about what an ADOPTER experiences, which is the population none of our checks can see.

=== 1. BDL-UX #183 — every adopter's CLAUDE.md states BEADLOOM's version as the project's own.
`onboarding/scanner/claude_md.py:125` calls `application.doctor.get_actual_version()`, which returns `beadloom.__version__`. That function is CORRECT and should not change - it exists to diagnose Beadloom's own version drift (#92). The defect is the caller: that value is rendered into the composed `CLAUDE.md` as `- **Current version:** ...` inside the section describing the ADOPTER's project. Reproduced by the coordinator: our own line 117 reads 2.2.0. A JavaScript project at 0.4.1 renders 2.2.0.

WHY IT SURVIVED FOUR SLICES OF SCRUTINY, and this is the part that matters: on this repository the fact is TRUE BY COINCIDENCE. We are Beadloom, so the project's version and Beadloom's version are the same string. Every check, every review and every dogfood run has read a correct line.

SO THE FIX THAT MATTERS IS NOT THIS LINE. It is (a) read the adopter's version from the adopter's project, rendering NOTHING rather than something false when it cannot be determined - unknown is not zero, the rule this epic applied everywhere else; (b) sweep the whole composed output for other facts computed about Beadloom rather than about the project - one was found by reading and nobody has looked at the rest; and (c) **a fixture project that is not Beadloom**, rendered in a test. Without (c) the next instance survives exactly as this one did.

=== 2. A RED PROJECT SILENTLY TURNS GREEN ON UPGRADE.
The reviewer measured hand-edited role files going error -> warn across an upgrade. That is precisely the #139/#151 population - adopters who edited a vendored file because there was nowhere else to put their additions.

An upgrade that WEAKENS a verdict is worse than one that strengthens it: a project that was correctly failing now passes, nobody is told, and the evidence that it was ever failing is gone. CONTEXT's constraint is 'no adopter's green project turns red on upgrade'; the inverse was never stated because nobody expected to need it. State it now, and decide whether a downgrade across an upgrade should be reported as its own finding.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, ONE PLATFORM IS NOT VERIFIED (a non-Beadloom fixture is the same idea one axis over: a claim measured only on this repo is true here and unknown everywhere else).

title: [BDL-061.57][dev] S3: config-check is partly sighted — eight measured blind spots, one of them a clock-driven time bomb
description:
Found by `.10` and pinned as nine strict-xfail tests, which are the specification. `.9` made `config-check` see the `CLAUDE.md` body at all (before it was totally blind: replacing the file with `# gone` gave 0 drifts). These are what it still cannot see.

THE TIME BOMB, and it should be fixed first because it fails without anyone touching the repo: `describe()` calls `date.today()`, so the composition is a function of the CLOCK. An untouched repository goes from 0 findings to 1 ERROR overnight, under a reason that blames the composition. A gate that turns red while everyone is asleep, for a reason that names the wrong cause, will be worked around rather than debugged - and the workaround will be to disable the check.

DISABLING BY DELETION, three ways, none of them reported:
- `rm .beadloom/flow-manifest.json` downgrades a hand-edited `CLAUDE.md` from error to warn (CLI exit 1 -> 0).
- Deleting the `<!-- beadloom:composed` line as well gives ZERO findings.
- Deleting ONE scaffolded file switches the flow checks off for ALL the others, and that is itself never reported.
  Same equation as #174: the gate is not satisfied by having less to check. Whatever `.46`/`.47` established for sync-check pairs, config-check must establish for its own inputs - a missing manifest is `unverified`, never absent-and-therefore-fine.

SUPPRESSIONS ACCEPTED IN SILENCE, which is the CONTEXT decision failing at its own promise: a suppression naming a rule that exists NOWHERE is accepted, and an EXPIRED suppression is accepted. CONTEXT says suppressing a core rule requires a named reason and an exit condition and is itself reported. S2b's `.49` already made expiry a finding for lint exemptions and shares the deadline logic - so suppressions should inherit it rather than re-implement it. A suppression that suppresses nothing is `.48`'s rule-liveness question one layer up.

HELD, reported so a clean result is not mistaken for a shallow one: fake auto-region markers hide nothing; append-only holds at line level (all 34 fragments end with a newline, now pinned by a test); and the awkward upgrade case - the shipped CORE moving underneath an existing overlay - passes.

The nine xfail(strict) tests fail the moment each is fixed, so they are the acceptance criteria. Do not delete one to make the suite green.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT.

title: [BDL-061.49][dev] an exemption's until: is prose, and a suppressed violation is never counted
description:
Review .7 MAJOR 2. An honesty note that overstates - the fourth recurrence of that shape in this epic, and this time the mechanism was ADDED BY THIS SLICE (`.43`).

THE CLAIM, `.beadloom/_graph/rules.yml:141-144`: "each exemption carries the reason it exists and the condition that retires it. An exemption that stops suppressing anything is itself reported, which is how the exit condition announces itself instead of waiting to be remembered."

WHAT IS TRUE: only a DEAD exemption is reported. An EXPIRED one is not, because `until` is never parsed as anything. `graph/rules/loader.py:241-243` requires a non-empty string and nothing more; `types.py:118` stores `until: str`; the only consumer is `evaluators.py:419`, inside the dead-exemption message. No date parsing exists anywhere in `graph/` or `guards/`. `application/guards/config.py` has the same shape.

MEASURED by the reviewer: adding to `tui-no-direct-infra` an exemption `to: "*" / from: "*" / reason: "review probe" / until: "1999-01-01"` and injecting a real tui -> infrastructure import gives `lint --strict` -> "0 violations, 12 rules evaluated", rc 0, saying NOTHING about a suppression. A wildcard exemption 26 years expired swallows a real error-severity crossing in silence. This repo's own lint likewise prints 0 violations while six onboarding crossings sit behind exemptions, and the suppressed count is never surfaced.

WHY IT IS FILED AT P0 RATHER THAN AS A DOC FIX: fixing one silent gate-defeat while adding another is precisely what S2 exists to stop. The exemptions `.43` wrote are exemplary - visible, reasoned, dated - and are NOT the problem. The problem is a sentence promising a guarantee the code does not provide.

TWO ACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES, and the choice needs its reason: (i) report the suppressed count on every lint run and make an expired `until` a finding - the anti-false-green move; (ii) correct the comment to say what is true today - "a DEAD exemption is reported; an EXPIRED one is not, because `until` is prose" - the minimum honest move. Leaving the current wording is not an option.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT.

comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit e244568 on features/BDL-061-S2b).

THE CHOICE, with its reason: OUTCOME (i). (ii) would have committed a sentence saying that a mechanism THIS EPIC ADDED is decoration — the fourth recurrence of the shape S2 exists to stop, written down as policy. (i) costs one module and one clause per renderer.

WHAT: (a) THE COUNT — LintResult.suppressed carries the crossings themselves (not a number), violations_suppressed counts them, and the clause appears wherever a run can read as clean: rich (both branches), the piped '0 violations, N rules evaluated' line, --format json (summary.violations_suppressed + a 'suppressed' array naming each crossing with its exemption, until and expired flag), and the Gate's lint line. This repo now reports '12 rules, 0 violations, 6 crossings suppressed by an exemption'. Absent at zero, so the everyday line keeps its shape — .48's rules_inert treatment, applied to the second counter. (b) THE DEADLINE — exit_condition_deadline(until): a DATE when the value leads with YYYY-MM-DD (optionally followed by the prose that explains it), an EVENT otherwise. A passed deadline on an entry still suppressing something is a finding.

SEVERITY warn, decided the way .48 decided its own, and honoured harder: not only is the finding warn, expiry does not CHANGE what is suppressed. A crossing reappearing at error severity because a calendar day passed would redden a build with no commit behind it — worse than the silence being fixed. --fail-on-warn is the lever for a project that wants the deadline enforced. Kept as rule_type rule_liveness rather than a new kind: the consumer's question is 'is my check doing its job', which is one bucket; splitting it would have meant editing the helper in test_s2_false_green_residue.py that PINS this defect, and bending a defect's own pin to make a fix land is not a trade worth 'nicer JSON filtering'.

GRAMMAR, the detail worth keeping: pinned by regex, NOT by date.fromisoformat, which widened in 3.11 (20260101 and week dates parse there, raise on 3.10). Delegating would have made the same until: enforceable on one supported interpreter and prose on another. A date must LEAD — 'some time after 2026-01-01' is an event.

WHY EVENT-SHAPED until STAYS LEGAL, measured rather than assumed: all six of .43's own exemptions retire on a landed re-scope, not a day. Requiring a date would have forced six fabricated deadlines and broken every adopter's config on upgrade at rc 2. So the mechanism these entries rely on is the COUNT; the date is for entries that have one.

NO GAP LEFT BEHIND for a blanket exemption, and this is why no extra check was added: an entry either suppresses crossings (counted) or suppresses none (already reported dead). from: '*' / to: '*' cannot hide either way.

GUARDS FIXED TOO — asked for as 'fix both or say why not'. Fixed: GuardExclusion.expired(), describe() appending ' — EXPIRED', GuardLiveness.expired_exclusions + to_dict + a fourth --liveness flag. It imports exit_condition_deadline from beadloom.graph.rules (application -> domain, layer-legal; guards already import onboarding) rather than restating the grammar — a restated promise is how two surfaces come to mean different things. The count half is deliberately NOT ported: a guard names its exclusion in the skip reason at the moment it applies, so suppression there was never silent. Lint had no such channel.

COHESION: graph/rules/exemptions.py is a NEW module ('what an exemption is doing: what it swallows, and whether it has run out'), not more weight on the 1183-line evaluators.py, which LOSES ~35 lines to it. matches_import_target / import_path_as_path / MATCHING_FORM_HINT moved to types.py beside the ImportBoundaryRule docstring that defines the two vocabularies — three modules state them now, and the move is what breaks the evaluators<->exemptions cycle. Every public import path unchanged.

OUT OF MY DECLARED SURFACE, declared rather than hidden: application/gate.py. It was the concurrent agent's file when I started and I filed beadloom-mr2l.54 for it; their commit 189d92f landed while I worked and left it uncontended, so I took the one line rather than defer a third time (.48 named the same gap and deferred). MEASURED while doing it, and it corrects .54's own premise: the Gate needs NO inert clause, because an inert rule always emits a finding and therefore always flips the summary to the '0 error(s), N warning(s)' branch — the clean branch is unreachable while rules_inert > 0. A suppressed crossing is the only counter that can be non-zero with nothing to report. .54 closed with that measurement.

title: [BDL-061.47][dev] a clean-DB rebuild adopts the tree as its own baseline, so the freshness gate is blind
description:
BDL-UX #175. Found by review `.7`, reproduced by the coordinator through the real CLI, pre-existing at `main` (7c5fa7d) - NOT introduced by S2.

MEASURED, one modified source file (graph/linter.py), its paired doc untouched, by exit code (never by line count - see #148):
  incremental reindex      -> sync-check exit 2   (stale, correct)
  rm beadloom.db; reindex  -> sync-check exit 0   (blind)
                           -> beadloom ci  exit 0

A fresh database holds no prior baseline, so the rebuild records the CURRENT hashes as the baseline. Nothing can be stale relative to a baseline created a second ago.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST INSTRUCTIVE DEFECT IN THE EPIC. The blindness is produced by following this project's own advice. Standing rule CLEAN-DB LINT instructed every agent to lint on a clean database, because incremental reindex did not refresh import edges (#142). That workaround silently made the FRESHNESS leg vacuous. A workaround for one lying check created another. The coordinator ran the gate that way throughout BDL-061 S1 and S2 and reported each result as authoritative verification - so this defect also explains why the other members of its family (#146, #172, #173, #174) went unnoticed for so long.

WHAT THE FIX MUST ESTABLISH:
- A rebuild must not silently establish a baseline. Either preserve the prior baseline where one exists, or have sync-check report "no baseline - not checked" instead of "fresh". This is the same distinction #174 and #146 turn on: UNVERIFIABLE IS NOT CLEAN, and the two must not print the same word.
- `beadloom ci` should know whether the index it just built has a usable baseline and say so on the sync-check line, rather than printing a pair count that means nothing.
- Decide where the baseline should live. If it belongs in the database, a rebuild destroys evidence by design and that is the deeper defect; if it belongs beside the docs (committed), a rebuild cannot lose it. State the choice with its reason - this is the load-bearing decision of the bead, not the reporting.
- **Retire the practice as part of the fix.** With #142 closed in S2, "lint on a clean DB" is no longer needed. Leaving the habit documented keeps the hazard alive, and habits outlive the defects that justified them.

RELATED AND LIKELY THE SAME ROOT: #174 (`beadloom ci` exits 0 when a declared SPEC is deleted). Check whether one fix covers both before treating them as separate.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, REPORTS ARE NOT EVIDENCE. The test that matters: a stale pair must be reported as stale after a full rebuild, or explicitly reported as unverifiable - never as fresh.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT (.46+.47, one fix): implemented + green locally. ONE FIX COVERED BOTH — the shared sentence is 'unverifiable is not clean'; they diverge only in the VERDICT each state earns: a deleted doc is `missing` (a failure, exit 2, gate FAIL) and a rebuilt index with no baseline is `unverified` (reported by name, never counted fresh, gate step WARN, exit code unchanged so no adopter goes red on upgrade).

WHERE THE BASELINE LIVES (the load-bearing decision): NOT in the database. .beadloom/beadloom.db is a derived cache — gitignored, per-machine, dropped by every rebuild and ABSENT ON EVERY FRESH CI CHECKOUT, so a baseline kept there is destroyed by the act that most needs it. Freshness baseline = GIT (committed by construction, a rebuild cannot erase it); surface-size baseline = a COMMITTED ledger (.beadloom/sync-surface.json). The DB keeps only a cache of both.

Mechanism: sync_state.baseline_source records provenance (index_build | carried | attested), carried VERBATIM across reindex and never promoted — a fabricated baseline does not become earned by being copied. A pair whose baseline is index_build and would read ok is corroborated against git HEAD (one `git status --porcelain -z -uall`); if git cannot answer -> unverified/no_baseline. Legacy '' rows read as 'carried', so this repo and every existing adopter keep today's behaviour: measured, all 283 live pairs still report baseline=index.

Files so far: src/beadloom/doc_sync/{git_baseline,declared_docs,surface_ledger}.py (new), doc_sync/engine.py, application/{gate.py,reindex/{sync_state,indexing,full,incremental,models}.py}, infrastructure/db.py (declared_docs table + baseline_source column + four-verdict status CHECK rebuild), services/commands/{docsync,federation}.py. comments.text:
COMPLETED (.46 + .47, ONE fix, commit bb716ed on features/BDL-061-S2b).

  * a doc that is GONE -> status=missing -> exit 2, gate FAIL. Someone must restore the file or remove the declaration; there is a defect in the tree.
  * a pair with NO BASELINE -> status=unverified -> named, counted separately, NEVER counted fresh, gate step prints WARN, exit code unchanged. Making this red would turn every non-git or freshly-cloned adopter red on upgrade, which CONTEXT forbids and which is how gates get switched off.
Same mechanism, same result dicts, same finding shapes, one test module.

DECISION — WHERE THE BASELINE LIVES: not in the database, and that IS the deeper defect .47 pointed at. .beadloom/beadloom.db is a derived cache (gitignored, per-machine, dropped by every rebuild, ABSENT ON EVERY FRESH CI CHECKOUT), so a baseline kept there is destroyed by the act that most needs it — which also means the CI gate has been structurally blind since it existed, not only when an agent typed rm. Two baselines now live outside it, both committed:
  1. FRESHNESS -> git. Not a new artifact: git is already the only committed record of what the code and docs said before, and check_sync_since already relied on it. sync_state.baseline_source records provenance (index_build|carried|attested), carried VERBATIM across reindex and never promoted; an index_build pair that would read ok is corroborated against HEAD via one `git status --porcelain -z -uall`; if git cannot answer -> unverified.

Added test_a_second_reindex_does_not_launder_the_fabricated_baseline; sabotage 6 re-run -> 1 reddened.

Changed: doc_sync/engine.py, application/{gate,doctor,status,site,architecture_view}.py, application/reindex/{full,incremental,indexing,models,sync_state}.py, infrastructure/db.py, services/commands/{docsync,federation}.py, graph/rules/evaluators.py, 13 docs, CONTEXT.md, ACTIVE.md, BDL-UX #174/#175 marked fixed with the measurements. title: [BDL-061.46][dev] S2: the documentation gate is defeated by DELETING documentation — beadloom ci exits 0 with every step PASS
description:
Found by `.6`; independently reproduced by the coordinator through the real CLI before filing. This is the most serious defect the BDL-061 epic has produced.

MEASURED, on `features/BDL-061-S2` at 004487a, clean DB:
  rm docs/domains/graph/features/rule-engine/SPEC.md   (a SPEC declared in the graph)
  beadloom ci
    reindex      PASS
    lint         PASS: 12 rules, 0 violations
    sync-check   PASS: 269 pair(s) fresh      <- was 275
    docs-audit   PASS: 13 mention(s) fresh
    config-check PASS
    doctor       PASS: 21 check(s) clean      <- was 20
    exit 0
Six declared pairs VANISHED and the gate called the result fresh. The doctor check count went UP by one while a file was being deleted. File restored, sha256 13300daa… verified, tree clean.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS EVERYTHING ELSE IN S2. Beadloom's whole promise is "no code reaches main without current docs". The cheapest way to satisfy that gate is now to DELETE the document instead of updating it - and nothing anywhere reports it. An agent under time pressure, or a careless rebase, or a bad merge that drops a file, all produce a green gate. Every other S2 defect made a check unreliable about what it examined; this one lets the thing being examined disappear.

IT IS ALSO THE EXACT SHAPE OF STANDING RULE 2, one level up. That rule said: for `component` nodes, "clean" means "no pairs exist", not "docs are fresh". `.5` fixed it for node kinds. The same confusion survives at the level of whole DOCUMENTS: a pair whose doc is gone is not fresh, it is unverifiable, and the two must not both print PASS. `.6` also measured the adjacent case - `sync-check` calls a pair `ok` when the FILE is gone - which is the same equation from the other side.

WHAT THE FIX MUST ESTABLISH, and only the third item makes it durable:
- A declared doc that does not exist is a FAILURE, not an absence. Decide the honest verdict (missing vs stale are different facts and should read differently) and state the reason.
- The pair COUNT is part of the contract. A run whose declared-pair count fell since the last run must say so; a silent drop from 275 to 269 is the signal that was available and discarded. Consider recording the expected count the way `config-check` records agent-config state.
- **Nothing may pass by having less to check.** Every check in the gate should be audited against this sentence, not just sync-check: `doctor`'s count rose while a file vanished, and `.6` separately measured that `20 check(s) clean` counts 9 warnings and 1 "not verified". A count that grows when the tree shrinks is not a count of anything.

Related: `#172` (a rule that cannot match reads clean), `#173` (docs-audit affirms one fact thirteen times), standing rules A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT and REPORTS ARE NOT EVIDENCE.

Standing rules apply, by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT. The test that matters: deleting any declared doc must redden the suite AND fail the gate.

title: [BDL-061.44][dev] S2: docs-audit reads a number out of an identifier — a bead reference now blocks the Gate
description:
BDL-UX #169, filed on 2026-08-22 after `docs audit` read the string `BDL-061.29` as a `cli_command_count` claim. It has now happened a second time and is BLOCKING the Gate on the S2 branch.

MEASURED by the coordinator on the final S2 wave-2 tree:
  ::error file=docs/services/cli.md,line=645::doc-fact-stale: mcp_tool_count:
  doc says 33 but project state is 18
The `33` is the tail of `(BDL-061.33)` - a bead reference in prose, written by the `.33` agent in commit 71e31eb. It is not a claim about anything. `beadloom ci` is rc 1 for it; everything else in the Gate is green.

WHY THE OBVIOUS WORKAROUND IS FORBIDDEN. Rewording the sentence makes the Gate green and teaches every author to write around the checker - which is the outcome #169 explicitly names as the thing to avoid. Note that `.4`'s tech-writer met this same trap and correctly refused it, reporting `#169 did not fire and nothing was reworded around it`. So the fix is the extractor, not the prose.

THE FIX. Do not extract a number that is part of a larger token. `BDL-061.33`, `v2.2.0`, `Python 3.10`, `PR #33` are identifiers, versions and references - not facts. Tokenize before matching rather than scanning for digits near a keyword, and decide what a token boundary is with the reason written down.

DO NOT SOLVE THIS WITH A TOLERANCE OR AN IGNORE ENTRY in `docs_audit`. That silences a true positive channel to hide a false one, and the next real staleness in that file goes unreported.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, judge and report rather than fix silently: how many OTHER extracted facts in this repo rest on the same digits-near-a-keyword heuristic? A false POSITIVE announces itself by failing the Gate; a false NEGATIVE - a real count that drifted while the extractor matched some other number in the line - is silent, and nobody has looked for one. That asymmetry is the same shape as every other finding in S2, so the sweep matters more than this one fix.

Every behaviour changed needs a test proving it fails on the condition it guards - specifically, a doc line containing an identifier whose tail looks like the fact's value must NOT be read as that fact, and a genuine drift in the same line must still be caught.

Standing rules 1, 5, 9.

title: [BDL-061.43][dev] S2: four lint rules cannot match anything — the glob is compared against a path that never has the src/ prefix
description:
Found by `.5` while fixing #142/#146/#147, correctly NOT absorbed into it. Independently reproduced end to end by the coordinator on 2026-08-22 through the real CLI; the measurements below are mine, not the reporting agent's.

THE DEFECT. All four `forbid_import` rules in `.beadloom/_graph/rules.yml` write their `from:`/`to:` globs with a `src/` prefix. The evaluator compares them against a path that never carries `src/`, so no import can ever match and `lint --strict` reports `0 violations, 12 rules evaluated` while four of the twelve are incapable of firing.

REPRODUCTION, in the order that separates the hypotheses:
1. Injected `from beadloom.infrastructure import db` into `src/beadloom/tui/app.py` - a textbook instance of exactly what `tui-no-direct-infra` forbids. Clean-DB reindex: 1323 imports (up from 1322, so the injected import IS indexed). `lint --strict` -> **0 violations, exit 0**.
2. Rewrote the globs without the `src/` prefix (`beadloom/tui/**` -> `beadloom/infrastructure/**`). Still **0 violations**. So the naive repair does not revive them either.
3. Widened rule 1 to `from: "**"` / `to: "**"`. It FIRES, many rows. So the mechanism is alive and the glob FORM is the whole problem.
4. `from: "**/tui/**"` / `to: "**/infrastructure/**"` fires correctly.
5. Removed the injection, kept the corrected form, clean-DB reindex: exactly ONE real pre-existing violation, `src/beadloom/tui/data_providers.py:284` - tui reaching into infrastructure directly, sitting in the repository uncaught for as long as the rule has existed.
All edits reverted; `rules.yml` back to sha256 b06604628d49… and `tui/app.py` to bec7e32276b6…, `git diff` clean.

WHY THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING OF S2. `beadloom lint --strict` is the architecture gate - a required CI check, a pre-commit hook, a pre-push hook, and the check the review role leans on. It has been printing a green count computed over rules that cannot fire. Every "12 rules, 0 violations" in this epic, including every gate run I performed and reported myself, was partly vacuous. That is S2's own theme - a check reporting success without checking - in S2's own instrument, and it outranks #142/#146/#147 because those three make lint UNRELIABLE while this one makes a third of it INERT.

`.5` measured 0 of 1322 imports matchable and reported that repairing surfaces 7 violations; my repair form surfaces 1 for rule 1. Reconcile the two numbers rather than picking one - the difference is probably which glob form each of us used and which rules it revived, and knowing that IS the fix.

WHAT THE FIX MUST INCLUDE, beyond correcting four lines of YAML:
- **Decide and document what `from:`/`to:` are matched against**, in one sentence, in the rules reference. Two engineers wrote `src/`-prefixed globs into this file and neither noticed; a form nobody can predict from the docs is the root cause, not the four lines.
- **Make a rule that cannot match a diagnosable state.** A rule whose glob matches zero candidate imports across the whole graph should be REPORTED - `warn` at least - exactly as `--liveness` reports a guard that never fires. This is the S1 lesson (`a check that can never fail is not a check`) applied to the linter, and it is what makes this fix permanent rather than a one-time correction.
- Fix `tui/data_providers.py:284` or record it as a deliberate exemption with a reason and an exit condition, per CONTEXT's exclusion decision. Do not make the rule green by weakening it.
- Re-check the other three rules under the corrected form and report what they surface; `.5`'s 7 suggests there is more than my 1.

Standing rules 1, 5, 9. The test that matters: a rule whose glob matches nothing must fail the suite.
