title: [BDL-061.40][dev] S2: the Gate itself lies on a non-UTF-8 image — four call sites with a measured wrong answer
description:
From the 17-call-site sweep delivered by `.37` (see `bd comments beadloom-mr2l.37`, section DELIVERABLE - THE SWEEP). Each verdict there was MEASURED by driving the real module through a double that re-implements CPython's documented text-mode rule with the ambient codec as a parameter (utf-8 / latin-1 / ascii) - not by reading the code, and not by arranging an exotic environment.

COORDINATOR'S HONESTY NOTE: I have NOT independently reproduced these four. The method is sound and the numbers are specific, but per standing rule 6 an agent's report is not evidence. Re-measure each one before fixing it, and say if any verdict does not hold.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DEFECT, in all four: the CURRENT content is read with an explicit `encoding=\"utf-8\"`, while the AT-REF / subprocess content is decoded by whatever the image says. So the two sides of a comparison are decoded by different rules, and the comparison then reports a difference that is an artefact of the environment.

1. P0-SHAPED - THE GATE LIES. `doc_sync/engine.py:307,323` (`_validate_git_ref`, `_file_content_at_ref`): `text=True`, NO handler at all. Current file read at engine.py:98 with `encoding=\"utf-8\"`. MEASURED on this repo with `docs/architecture.md` unchanged at HEAD: ambient utf-8 -> hashes match; ambient latin-1 -> hashes DO NOT match, i.e. `sync-check --since` reports drift in a file nobody touched; ambient ascii -> uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError` out of a command that runs INSIDE `beadloom ci`. On a non-UTF-8 image the Gate therefore either crashes or reports stale docs that are not stale - for any document containing one non-ASCII byte, which is every doc in this repo that uses an em dash. This is S2's own theme turned on S2's own instrument.

2. THE DIFF LIES. `graph/diff.py:64,79,134`: `text=True`, NO handler, same asymmetry (current read at diff.py:177 with utf-8, previous via `git show` under the ambient codec). MEASURED against HEAD expecting zero changes: utf-8 -> 0 node / 0 edge changes; latin-1 -> uncaught yaml `ReaderError` ('unacceptable character #x0086'); ascii -> uncaught `UnicodeDecodeError`. `beadloom diff --since` is the review role's instrument, so a reviewer on such an image gets a crash or a fabricated change set.

3. A CONTRIBUTOR WHO DOES NOT EXIST. `infrastructure/git_activity.py:190`: `text=True` plus `except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)` - the identical two lines `.37` just fixed. The content is `git log --format=%H %aI %aN`, i.e. AUTHOR NAMES. MEASURED on a repo authored by 'Иван Петров': utf-8 -> the name; latin-1 -> mojibake shown in the dashboard as a real contributor; ascii -> `UnicodeDecodeError` past the handler. Clean on THIS repo only because every author and filename in the last 90 days is ASCII - the same 'true on the machine that ran it' that produced .36.

4. SILENT PROVENANCE LOSS. `graph/federation/export.py:214,261`: `text=True` with `except (FileNotFoundError, OSError)` - an enumeration that is also redundant, since `FileNotFoundError` IS an `OSError`. `.37` calls that redundancy the tell: it was written without checking the hierarchy. MEASURED with the repo at a path containing Cyrillic: utf-8 -> a sha; latin-1 -> None; ascii -> `UnicodeDecodeError`. The `None` is the 'honest unknown HEAD' branch (#103) being taken for a DISHONEST reason - a federation export silently loses its commit provenance while looking like a legitimate unknown.

FIX SHAPE: the same as `.36` and `.37`. Decode deliberately - explicit `encoding=\"utf-8\"` with a stated `errors=` choice, or read bytes and decode where the meaning is known - and make each handler as wide as what its call can actually raise. Where two sides of a comparison are decoded, they must be decoded by the SAME rule; say so in the code, because the asymmetry is what made three of these invisible.

SCOPE NOTE: `.37` deliberately did not fix these, and was right not to - three of the four are in the surface of the agent working `.5` in the same tree, and 'a sweep is a check, not a licence to sprawl'. This bead therefore depends on `.5`.

RELATED: `.38`'s CI locale leg would catch every one of these on the first PR that runs it. That is the argument for `.38` earning its wall-clock, and it should be recorded as such.

title: [BDL-061.37][dev] S2: the subprocess probes decode with the ambient locale, and the handler misses the failure that causes
description:
Item 1 of the environment-dependence deliverable in `bd comments beadloom-mr2l.36`. This is defects 1 and 2 of .36 in a SINGLE call, and unlike them it is still live.

`services/guard_probes.py:101` (git) and `services/bd_seam.py:71` (bd) both run subprocess with `text=True`. `text=True` decodes with `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)` - NOT UTF-8 - and the handler is `except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)`, which does not include `UnicodeDecodeError` (it is a `ValueError`, and neither of those). So on an image whose preferred encoding is not UTF-8, a branch name or a bead title carrying a non-ASCII byte makes the probe raise straight past its own handler.

DIRECTION OF FAILURE, and it matters: fail-CLOSED but WRONG. The invocation boundary from .29/.31 catches it and turns it into an `error` verdict at exit 2, which BLOCKS the edit. The designed answer for 'the probe cannot answer' is `skip` with a stated reason. So the guard does not lie and does not crash - it blocks work for a reason that is not the real one, and the operator's remediation will be aimed at the wrong thing.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON THE OWNER'S MACHINE, and .36 says so rather than claiming it verified: measured there, `LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0` still reports preferred encoding 'utf-8' because of PEP 538/540 coercion, and a branch named with Cyrillic came back correct. Reproducing it needs a Linux image with a genuinely non-UTF-8 locale. Do not conclude it is absent because this machine cannot produce it - that inference is exactly what put .36's two defects into CI.

FIX SHAPE, the same as .36's: pass `encoding=\"utf-8\"` explicitly with a decided `errors=` value, or read bytes and decode deliberately; and widen the handler to what the call can actually raise. State the `errors=` decision with its reason - `strict` makes an undecodable branch name a refusal, `surrogateescape` makes it a name the probe can still compare - and note which direction each fails in.

Then check whether any OTHER subprocess call in the codebase has the same pair of defects. These two were found by reading the guard package; nobody has swept the rest.

comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.37] — commit 61bf722 on features/BDL-061-S2 (9 files, +571/-18; the 9th is .beads/issues.jsonl, added by the pre-commit coherence hook, tracker state only).

=== 1. THE FIX, AS THE PROPERTY IT RESTORES
Both probes now state their codec: encoding='utf-8', errors='surrogateescape'. The ENCODING is not negotiable (text=True consults locale.getpreferredencoding(False), which is the image speaking, not the tool). The errors= choice is decided by direction of failure, not by outcome: strict makes a branch name that is legal on POSIX but not UTF-8 unreadable -> probe None -> working-branch SKIPS = an exemption nobody declared, and one stray byte in one bead's TITLE would unplug bead-claimed for the whole project (display text switching off a gate); replace is not injective, so two distinct names can collapse to one string = a comparison handed a wrong answer; surrogateescape is the only one of the three that round-trips to the exact bytes the tool holds, so ids/statuses/names stay distinct and nothing a guard COMPARES can be corrupted by a byte. Its cost, named: such a name reaches the message with \udcff escapes — verified harmless because working-branch interpolates with !r and repr escapes lone surrogates, so the verdict still encodes on an ASCII-only stdout (asserted).
Both handlers are now as wide as their sentence, .36's lesson applied to an except clause: guard_probes -> 'a probe that cannot answer returns None' -> Exception (never BaseException: an interrupt is the process stopping, not git declining). bd_seam -> 'a BdResult, or BdUnavailableError' -> Exception, with FileNotFoundError kept separate because it is the one failure with an actionable remedy. Nothing is swallowed: the class is named via exception_detail (the .36 helper, one definition) and the original is chained.

=== 2. WHAT I FOUND THAT THE BEAD DID NOT NAME
run_bd caught FileNotFoundError ALONE. So a bd wedged past its 60 s timeout (TimeoutExpired) and a REAL non-executable bd on PATH (PermissionError — an OSError, not a FileNotFoundError) escaped the seam, escaped BdWorkTracker (which catches only BdUnavailableError) and hit the boundary as error/exit 2. Same family, same direction, reachable with no locale and no injection at all.

=== 3. VERIFICATION — WHICH HALF IS REAL AND WHICH IS CONSTRUCTED
Undecodable-bytes half: REPRODUCED HERE, through the real git. 'git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/features/<0xff>-bad' (HEAD is file CONTENT, so APFS's refusal of non-UTF-8 FILENAMES is bypassed) -> 'git branch --show-current' emits bytes text=True cannot decode -> UnicodeDecodeError past the handler.
Ambient-locale half: NOT reproducible here and not faked as if it were. Measured: patching locale.getpreferredencoding to 'ascii' left the decode utf-8, because TextIOWrapper resolves the locale codec below Python — so the environment cannot be arranged from a test either, on top of PEP 538/540 coercion. It is CONSTRUCTED: a double re-implements CPython's documented text-mode rule ('...or locale.getpreferredencoding(False) if neither is given') with the ambient codec as a parameter, rows utf-8/ascii/latin-1. Rule 4 is answered rather than argued around — every claim the double makes is also made against the real git and against a real child process on PATH.
Also fixed a vacuous test OF MY OWN before it could ship: PATH-prepending a non-executable bd passes even unfixed, because execvp remembers EACCES and keeps searching until it finds the real bd. PATH is now replaced, not prepended; the trace is in the docstring.

=== 4. SABOTAGES (rule 5: FAILED never ERROR; numbers; reverse edit; sha256)
(a) git codec -> text=True: 4 FAILED / 15 passed (the ascii+latin-1 ambient rows and both real-git rows).
(b) git handler -> (OSError, SubprocessError): 2 FAILED / 17 passed (the injected decode-failure and the 'class nobody has enumerated yet' rows — exactly the two the enumeration misses).
(c) bd codec -> text=True: 4 FAILED / 24 passed (both ambient title rows, the undecodable-title row, and the structural row in test_bd_seam).
(d) bd handler -> RuntimeError only: 4 FAILED / 15 passed (three injected rows + the real non-executable bd).
All restored by reverse edit; shasum -a 256 -c OK on both files; no sabotage produced an ERROR or 'no tests ran'.

title: [BDL-061.36][dev] S1 hotfix: the refusal depends on the ambient locale, and a symlink loop raises the one exception the handler does not catch
description:
CI on PR #33 failed on all four Python versions while the local macOS suite was 5574/5574 green. Two defects, both in code written in this slice, both diagnosed by the coordinator through local reproduction - not inferred from the CI log. Do NOT re-diagnose; verify and fix.

=== DEFECT 1 (fails on 3.10-3.13; 4 tests) - THE REFUSAL IS CLOSED FOR ONE LOCALE

`tests/test_guards_adversarial.py:1050` and `tests/test_guards_invocation.py:1489` assert rc 2 for an undecodable hook payload and get rc 0 with empty stderr.

REPRODUCED LOCALLY on macOS, with the same binary that passes under my normal environment:
  beadloom guard bead-claimed --hook claude-code < badbytes.bin
    default locale -> ERROR "the claude-code hook payload could not be read as text" (correct)
    LC_ALL=C       -> WARN "no bead is in progress while editing src/\udcff\udcfe.py", rc 0
    PYTHONUTF8=1   -> same

CAUSE: with LC_CTYPE C/POSIX, Python enables UTF-8 Mode, which sets `sys.stdin`'s error handler to `surrogateescape`. The undecodable bytes become lone surrogates instead of raising, the JSON parses, and the guard EVALUATES a path it was built to refuse. C is the default locale in most CI images and most containers, so this is not an edge case - it is the common deployment.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE: `.27` narrowed path input precisely so that a spelling could not exempt a file, and `.31` closed the same family again. This is the same defect once more, one dimension over: the refusal is closed for one AMBIENT ENVIRONMENT rather than for one spelling. Note also that the shape gate did not refuse the surrogate-bearing path either - it reached evaluation and produced a WARN - so this is two layers failing, not one.

FIX DIRECTION (judge it, do not just apply it): read the harness payload as BYTES and decode explicitly with errors=\"strict\", so the behaviour does not depend on how the process was started. Then decide separately whether `rejection_reason` should refuse a lone surrogate wherever it arrives from, as defence in depth - .30 already observed that a surrogate from argv survives. Do NOT fix this by pinning a locale in CI: that hides the defect from us while shipping it to adopters.

=== DEFECT 2 (fails on 3.10-3.12, passes on 3.13; 2 tests) - THE UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION IS NAMED IN A COMMENT THAT CALLS IT UNREACHABLE

`src/beadloom/application/guards/paths.py:220-227`:
    try:
        target = candidate.resolve()
        root = project_root.resolve()
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        # Unreachable for every input the shape gate admits today - which is
        # exactly why it is here. The property this module exists to hold is
        # \"no supplied path ends in a traceback\" ...

`Path.resolve()` raises `RuntimeError(\"Symlink loop from ...\")` on a symlink loop, and `RuntimeError` is neither `OSError` nor `ValueError`. Measured: Python 3.9 and 3.10-3.12 raise (CI shows both `RuntimeError` at pathlib.py:1074 and `OSError` ELOOP 40 at pathlib.py:1097); Python 3.13 returns the path unresolved and raises nothing, which is the only reason the local macOS run is green. So the local suite passes for a reason that has nothing to do with the code being correct.

The comment asserts unreachability and the CI log falsifies it. That is an understating honesty note for the FOURTH time in this slice (m3 in .28, the project_root docstring in .30, the .32 'cost today is zero' that I wrote myself, and now this). Fix the comment to say what is true, and treat the recurrence as a signal about how these comments get written, not as four unrelated slips.

FIX DIRECTION: catch what the operation can actually raise. The stated property is \"no supplied path ends in a traceback\" - so the handler should be as wide as that sentence, which is exactly the cycle-five lesson applied to an except clause instead of to a pin.

=== VERIFICATION BAR - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE BEAD

My verification was thorough and single-platform, and that is why this reached CI. Every claim I made was true on macOS 3.13.

- Reproduce BOTH defects before fixing, and prove each fix by re-running the reproduction under the failing condition, not only under the passing one.
- Add a test that runs the undecodable-payload case with `LC_ALL=C` (or an env that forces UTF-8 Mode) in the child process, so the locale dimension is covered by the suite rather than by CI.
- For the loop: make the test independent of whether the installed Python raises, so it does not silently become vacuous on 3.13 - assert the module's property (a verdict, never a traceback) by INJECTING the exception if the platform will not produce it.
- Standing rules 1, 5, 9 apply. A sabotage reddening must be FAILED, never ERROR.

Then say plainly which other guard behaviours are environment-dependent and were never checked under anything but a UTF-8 macOS - that list is a deliverable, not an aside.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
DELIVERABLE — WHICH OTHER GUARD BEHAVIOURS ARE ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT AND HAVE ONLY EVER BEEN CHECKED ON A UTF-8 macOS WITH 3.13. Ordered by how badly a wrong answer would land, not by likelihood. Each says the mechanism, the direction it fails in, and whether I measured it.

1. THE SUBPROCESS PROBES DECODE WITH THE LOCALE ENCODING, AND THE HANDLER DOES NOT CATCH A DECODE FAILURE. This is defects 1 and 2 in ONE call, and it is live.
   services/guard_probes.py:101 (git) and services/bd_seam.py:71 (bd) both run subprocess with text=True. text=True decodes with locale.getpreferredencoding(False) — NOT UTF-8 — and the handler is except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError), which does not include UnicodeDecodeError (verified: UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, neither of those). So on an image whose preferred encoding is not UTF-8, a branch name or a bead title carrying a non-ASCII byte makes the probe RAISE past its own handler. Direction: fail-CLOSED but wrong — the invocation boundary converts it into an 'error' verdict at exit 2 and BLOCKS the edit, where the designed answer for 'the probe cannot answer' is SKIP with a stated reason.
   NOT REPRODUCIBLE ON THIS MACHINE, and that is the point: measured here, LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 still reports preferred encoding 'utf-8' (PEP 538/540 coercion), and a branch named 'features/тест' came back correct. It needs a Linux image with a non-UTF-8 locale. Fix shape, same as this bead's: pass encoding='utf-8' explicitly (plus an errors= decision), or read bytes; and widen the handler to what the call can raise.

2. THE SHAPE GATE'S OWN CRITERION IS AMBIENT. paths.rejection_reason accepts a target iff os.fsencode(raw) succeeds, and fsencode uses sys.getfilesystemencoding() + surrogateescape. Under UTF-8 that accepts exactly the surrogates DC80-DCFF (which denote real bytes and round-trip) and refuses the rest — measured. Under a non-UTF-8 filesystem encoding the accepted SET changes, and no test has ever run under one. Direction: unknown either way, which is why it is #2. (This is also where I judged the bead's open question: no, rejection_reason should NOT refuse lone surrogates. On POSIX a DC80-DCFF surrogate is the faithful name of a real byte sequence and the writer will create exactly that file, so the guard and the writer look at the same file — refusing it would refuse legitimate non-UTF-8 names in the blocking direction. A PAYLOAD that is not UTF-8 denotes nothing (JSON is UTF-8 by definition), which is why the refusal belongs at the transport and only there. Both halves are now stated in the SPEC.)

3. WINDOWS IS NOT TESTED AT ALL, AND IT READS AS GREEN. Six guard tests carry skipif(sys.platform == 'win32') and CI has no Windows leg, so every Windows claim rests on reasoning. The backslash refusal exists FOR Windows harnesses and has never executed on one; Path.resolve, the documented 'C:/... is read as a relative directory called C:' behaviour, and case-insensitivity all differ there. A skip that can never fail is the same shape as the vacuous loop test this bead just fixed.

4. EXCLUSION MATCHING IS CASE-SENSITIVE; THE FILESYSTEM MAY NOT BE. MEASURED on macOS: with 'scripts/**' declared, 'SCRIPTS/deploy.sh' names the SAME existing file as 'scripts/deploy.sh' (names_an_existing_file=True) and does NOT match the exclusion. Direction: over-guarding — a declared exemption silently stops applying — so it is not a bypass, but the same edit gets one verdict on a developer's mac and a different one in CI on Linux, and no test says so.

5. UNICODE NORMALISATION, same shape. MEASURED on macOS: the NFC and NFD spellings of 'src/café.py' both name the same existing file and resolve to two DIFFERENT strings (equal_strings=False), so an exclusion written in one form does not cover the other. On Linux they are genuinely two files and the same code is correct. Never tested either way.

6. Path.resolve() DIVERGES BEYOND THE LOOP. The loop is now asserted as a property rather than as a branch, but ENAMETOOLONG, a permission-denied parent and a dangling chain have no test at all, and WHICH branch runs (INSIDE vs MALFORMED) is version- and platform-dependent — so any future test that asserts one of them is a single-platform test by construction. The handler covers them as a class; the coverage does not.

7. THE bd/git BINARIES ARE THE ENVIRONMENT TOO. 'bd list --status in_progress --json --limit 0' has only ever been answered by bd 1.0.4 on macOS. A bd that renames the status, drops --limit or changes the JSON shape yields either None (probe unavailable -> SKIP, honest) or an EMPTY TUPLE (a false 'no bead is in progress' -> WARN, and BLOCK under the RFC's own example config). The empty-tuple branch is fail-closed against the developer and is indistinguishable from the true answer.

8. CHECKED AND CLEAN, said so the list is not only bad news: firing.py timestamps use datetime.now(timezone.utc) (no TZ dependence); liveness.project_files skips symlinks explicitly, so a loop cannot make the walk hang; the verdict RENDER survives a hostile stdout — measured under PYTHONIOENCODING=latin-1, the em dash printed as a \\u2014 escape and the exit code stayed 2, which is .31's 'the render cannot choose the exit code' holding under a condition nobody had tried.

9. NOT A GUARD BEHAVIOUR BUT THE SAME BLINDNESS, FOUND EN ROUTE: the suite leaks sqlite connections across tests. test_guards_parity's '-wal' assertion blamed a guard for a connection opened by test_bead15_s3b_coverage's lint-on-the-real-repo test (traced with a teardown hook; fixed in this bead by stating the assertion relative to the state before the evaluation), and test_db.py::test_no_resource_warning surfaces the same leaks as PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning under random ordering (1 warning in fixed order, up to 15 in random). Both are order-dependent assertions about global state.

RECOMMENDATION, one line: the cheapest structural defence is a CI matrix leg that runs the existing suite with LC_ALL=C (varying the locale, NOT pinning it — pinning would have hidden this bead's defect). Everything above except #3 would have been caught by an environment DIMENSION rather than by a new test.

comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.36] S1 hotfix — both defects fixed as consequences of the property each was supposed to hold, both verified UNDER THE FAILING CONDITION rather than under the passing one.

=== 1. WHAT THE FIX IS, IN ONE SENTENCE EACH
D1 (locale): read_payload now yields BYTES and the boundary decodes them itself with errors='strict', so the ambient interpreter configuration no longer participates in the refusal. _read_stdin takes the stream's binary layer when it has one, and re-encodes with surrogateescape when it does not (an in-process double) — the exact inverse of the decoding that would otherwise hide the bad bytes.
D2 (loop): the handler is now as wide as its sentence — Exception, not a list of classes — and stops short of BaseException with a stated reason: an interrupt mid-resolution is the PROCESS being stopped, not this PATH being refused, and the boundary already has a distinct answer for it. The comment that called the case unreachable is replaced by the measurement that falsifies it.
Also, DRY: the two identical 'exception as one clause' helpers became guards.models.exception_detail, one definition, with the reason in its docstring.

=== 2. THE VERIFICATION, WHICH IS WHAT THE BEAD WAS ABOUT
REPRODUCED FIRST, through the real binary: 'beadloom guard bead-claimed --hook claude-code < badbytes.bin' -> ERROR/rc2 under the inherited locale, WARN/rc1 'no bead is in progress while editing src/\\udcff\\udcfe.py' under LC_ALL=C and under PYTHONUTF8=1. AFTER: ERROR/rc2 under all four of '', LC_ALL=C, PYTHONUTF8=1, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8.
Path.resolve MEASURED on real interpreters (uv run --python X), 'a -> b -> a', for the link and for a path through it: 3.10.1, 3.11.13, 3.12.12 raise RuntimeError('Symlink loop from ...'); 3.13.7 returns unresolved and raises nothing. The CI log's ELOOP OSError is the same condition from the other layer; the widened handler covers both.
THE FAILING PLATFORM, RUN LOCALLY: a 3.10.1 venv with the dev extras. Guard subset 820 passed under the default locale AND under LC_ALL=C. Full suite on 3.10: 5442 passed, 4 failed — all four environmental to that ad-hoc venv and none of them a guard test (2 x test_ai_techwriter_seams: FileNotFoundError 'python' is not on PATH there; 2 x the live sync-state pair tests, re-baselined since).
LOCALE IS NOW A SUITE DIMENSION, not a CI accident: 4 ambient decoders x the undecodable-payload matrix, run through the real binary. The fourth row (PYTHONIOENCODING=latin-1) was ADDED because the first sabotage passed 302/302 without it — a decoder that accepts every byte escapes nothing, so the surrogateescape round-trip cannot see it. That row is what makes the binary-layer branch load-bearing.
THE LOOP TEST CANNOT GO VACUOUS ON 3.13: the real-loop test asserts the property (a scope, never an exception) and accepts either branch, and four INJECTED refusals — RuntimeError, ELOOP OSError, ValueError, and LookupError ('a class nobody has enumerated yet', which a three-class handler would fail) — cover the raising branch on an interpreter that will not produce it.

title: [BDL-UX #236] a clean room's verdict is decided by which optional extras it installed, and the convention never names them
description:
FOUND IN BDL-068 S4 WAVE 3 by beadloom-0mdo.33. See the log entry for the measurement; the headline is that one code base produced 0, 1 and 82 mypy errors depending on which optional extras the room had installed.

WHY IT BELONGS BESIDE #235 AND #237: those three are the whole isolation story of a wave, and all three were ASSUMED rather than checked. #235 — the room may contain a neighbour. #236 — the room's dependency set is unstated, so its verdict is not reproducible from the convention alone. #237 — the lock that was supposed to serialise the landings does nothing.

THE SHAPE THIS PROJECT KEEPS MEETING: a measurement whose population nobody stated. "Green in a clean room over N files" names the file count and not the environment, so two correct agents following the same convention can return different verdicts and neither is wrong.

EXPECTED: the room states its extras the way a verdict now states its room (BDL-068 S3). A clean-room report that cannot be reproduced from what it prints is a claim, not a measurement.

ROUTED TO S6 with #235 — same convention, same slice.

title: [BDL-UX #235] the clean-room convention names a fixed directory, so two agents in one wave build one room and both call it clean
description:
FOUND IN BDL-068 S4 WAVE 1 by beadloom-0mdo.31, independently observed by beadloom-0mdo.27, and reconstructed from mtimes: .31's `git archive HEAD | tar -x` at 22:53, .27's untracked files copied in at 23:16, .31's at 23:26. One room, two occupants.

WHAT IT COST AND WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COST: .31's run in that room reported 8 failures; five were .27's — its acceptance steps and two annotation-consistency checks over a graph node HEAD does not carry. None was a defect in either bead. Rebuilding under a bead-unique name gave 1 failure, itself a stated property of the room (no `.git`, so sync-check has no baseline). The cost was one five-minute suite run. The cost avoided was a WRONG VERDICT: had .31 written its report from that room, it would have attributed .27's work to itself, in the one measurement whose entire purpose is to separate them.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A NAMING SLIP: the gate-owner rule exists because a clean room cannot see interactions between beads ON THE TREE. Nobody said the rooms themselves could interact. An agent that follows the convention exactly and correctly gets a room containing its neighbour's work, and every check it runs there is honest about a tree that exists nowhere.

THE PROMPT-LEVEL MITIGATION IS ALREADY IN USE and is not the fix: every launch prompt since wave 2 says the room's directory must carry the bead id. That is the #228 shape — a rule carried by the coordinator's typing.

EXPECTED, and the second form is the one this project prefers: not "name the directory differently", but a command that DERIVES the room path from the claimed bead and REFUSES a directory it did not create empty, so "is this room mine" is answered rather than assumed. A room that cannot say whose it is is not a clean room; it is a shared directory with a reassuring name.

ROUTED TO S6, not S4. S4's contents are fixed and its stop rule is the point. The clean-room convention is a flow document-and-role matter, which is S6's subject. beadloom-67t1 carries the DUTY TEXT for it in S4 because it is writing that text anyway; the machine half is here.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
POINTER from beadloom-67t1 (BDL-UX #228), closed 2026-09-04 — do not redo the convention half.

ALREADY SHIPPED, in commits a5bf5ae and 204fc95: room_for(bead_id) returns 'room-<bead-id>' and is exported from beadloom.application.waves; beadloom waves prints 'clean room: <bead> -> room-<bead>' per bead for EVERY wave, including a wave of one, beside the combined-tree gate owner; the working-tree medium's statement carries the rule and cites 'BDL-UX #181, #235'; and the five role cores carry it under the clean-room duty, which config-check blocks on. A test binds the role prose to room_for's own output, so renaming the room in the planner reddens the text that promises it.

WHAT IS LEFT, which is this bead's whole remaining scope: no command CREATES the room. #235's Expected asks for the stronger form — a command that derives the path from the claimed bead and REFUSES a directory it did not create empty — so 'is this room mine' is still answered by a human reading a path rather than by the tool. That is the clause the UX log entry was left open on.

ONE MEASURED TRAP such a command should close, found while building the room for 67t1: with an editable install, running pytest inside the room with the project venv imports the TREE's source, not the room's. The first attempt did exactly that and it was caught from a warning path in the output, not from a failure. PYTHONPATH=<room>/src fixes it, and 'import beadloom' printing a path inside the room is the check. A room-creating command that does not also hand back the invocation leaves this trap open, and it produces a green that is a measurement of the tree wearing a room's name.

title: [BDL-068.S4][test] the guards' surface, as shapes: every write path, every duty, every refusal rule
description:
Tests for S4's dev beads. The slice's technique is "derive the enforcement surface from the instrument's own matcher, compare it against what exists, report the gap", so the tests are written over a SHAPE and never over a spelling — the standing rule from S1, restated here because S4 is where a hand-written list is most tempting.

WHAT THAT MEANS CONCRETELY, per bead:
- `.31` — the write-path population is ENUMERATED from the harness settings the flow emits, not listed. A test that asserts "Bash, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit" passes forever after a fifth write path is added. Assert instead that every tool the emitted settings can route a write through appears in the guard's matcher, or is named in the surface report as uncovered.
- `.32` — the exempt set is measured against real commits on this branch, and the test states the population it measured over. An exempt set validated against zero commits is a phantom gate.
- `.33` — every new refusal rule is exercised through `PureWindowsPath`; anything it cannot settle is a written residual, and the suite already forbids re-pinning it as an xfail (`test_no_platform_xfail_waits_for_a_runner_that_will_not_come`).
- `.27` / `67t1` — the duty check runs in BOTH directions over the composed role cores, and the test is the thing that keeps the two halves from separating.
- `gsal` / `nn4c` / `en0x` — each has its own reproduction already written into its bead; the test is that reproduction, red before the fix.

STANDING RULES, unchanged and not negotiable per bead:
- A new test file landing on an existing path DELETES its scenarios and the suite goes green over the wreckage (BDL-UX #224, unfixed). Check the filename before writing it.
- Report the measurement in the words that name it: "green in a clean room over N files" is a different claim from "green on the tree" (#181).
- Name the room. `beadloom rooms` says a local run is in 0 of the 21 this project declares; `tests/room_simulation.py` can fabricate one, and S3 shipped it for exactly this.

Coverage >= 80% on the changed surface.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
OPEN QUESTION FOR THE TEST BEAD, raised by the coordinator 2026-09-03 and deliberately NOT filed as a finding, because it could not be attributed.

WHAT `guard --liveness` says after .31: 'surface (claude): 3 of 3 write path(s) bound, matcher(s) Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash', plus two honest lines in the other direction — MultiEdit and NotebookEdit are named by a matcher and granted by no role adapter, so those entries protect nothing here. The reverse check was not asked for and is the better half.

THE QUESTION: that surface is derived from .claude/settings.json ON DISK. A harness that reads its hook configuration once at session start would still be enforcing the OLD matcher while the report claims the new one — a claim about a declaration read as a claim about enforcement, which is this epic's subject applied to its own instrument. If true, the widened matcher is inert in the very session that widened it, and nothing says so.

WHY IT IS NOT FILED: I tried to measure it by writing a file through Bash and watching the counters. They moved 678->681 in twenty seconds — but a dev subagent was running concurrently and firing guards of its own, so the increment is unattributable. That is exactly the shape of BDL-UX #233, met while trying to measure something else. An unattributable measurement is not evidence.

HOW TO SETTLE IT: with no subagent running, record fired= for both guards, make one Bash-only write, record again. If the counters do not move, the matcher is declared and not enforced, and the surface line needs a word for that — 'bound' is a fact about the file, not about the harness.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
DELIBERATE MEASUREMENT FOR THE TEST/REVIEW BEADS, set up by the coordinator 2026-09-04.

Every launch prompt in BDL-067 and BDL-068 up to and including wave 3 carried the clean-room conventions typed by hand: the two different claims (#181), name the room, the bead-id room path (#235), check a filename before writing (#224), merge-slot, checkpoint cadence, python3 heredoc for commit messages. Roughly twenty-five prompts. That is the fact BDL-UX #228 names.

beadloom-67t1 landed in wave 3 and put the duty into the composed role cores: .claude/agents/dev.md now carries it at lines 177, 183 and 192, including the #235 room-naming rule, and beadloom-0mdo.27's check enforces that a declared duty reaches the core of every role it names.

SO FROM WAVE 4 ONWARD THE LAUNCH PROMPTS OMIT ALL OF IT. beadloom-en0x's prompt carries only bead-specific content: no clean-room instruction, no room-naming rule, no reporting-words rule, no checkpoint cadence. If the agent still separates 'green in a clean room over N files' from 'green on the tree', names its room, and builds at room-<bead-id>, the duty is carried by the role core rather than by the coordinator's typing, and #228 is answered by measurement instead of by inspection.

THE HONEST LIMIT OF THIS TEST: it is one agent, and a negative would be strong while a positive is only suggestive -- a model may produce the right words from the epic's documents, which it also reads. Whoever reviews S4 should weigh it as evidence, not as proof, and should say which. The stronger check is beadloom-0mdo.27's, which reads the artifacts rather than the behaviour.

title: [BDL-068.S4.x][dev] the commit gate judges the paths a commit stages and calls a neighbour's hunk clean — wire scope-check into the hook
description:
THE RESIDUE OF `beadloom-mr2l.81`, which was closed 2026-08-31 in a tracker cleanup as unfinished work rather than as done. Read its description via `bd show beadloom-mr2l.81` — the analysis there stands and is not to be redone.

THE DEFECT, measured by `mr2l.22`: the installed pre-commit hook judges the paths a commit STAGES. A neighbour's hunk swept into that commit — inside a file the committer legitimately touches, because `git add -p` is unavailable to an agent — is INSIDE the region the gate judges. `outside` reads 0, `staged_py` names the file, and the hook prints a confident "0 file(s) outside this commit were not judged" over a commit containing someone else's work.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE `.81` WAS WRITTEN, and it is most of the bead: BDL-068 S1 shipped `beadloom scope-check`, which answers whether a commit touched a path outside the WORK ITEM's declared axes and names which axis. `.81` asked for that mechanism and had to design it; it now exists. This bead is the wiring plus the four decisions `.81` said must be made BEFORE building, three of which the epic has since answered.

ANSWERED ALREADY — do not re-litigate:
- WHOSE scope. CONTEXT Q2: the comparison is against the WORK ITEM's axes, not the bead's. That was chosen precisely because the claimed in-progress bead is wrong the moment two agents share a tree, which is the mode this exists for.
- WHERE THE SCOPE COMES FROM. CONTEXT Q1: derived by `beadloom impact`, recorded in the document, generated into the bead's `refs:`.

STILL TO DECIDE, and each one is a line of the bead's own report:
- THE EXEMPT SET. A work item scoped to one node legitimately touches its own tests, its own docs and the tracker export. Decide the exempt set and MEASURE it against real commits on this branch BEFORE the check goes live; a check that is noise within a day is a check that is turned off within two.
- WARN OR BLOCK. Warn is the honest default until the exempt set has been measured. A false positive here blocks a correct commit in a shared tree, which is the failure #118 itself was.
- A COMMIT WITH NO ATTRIBUTABLE WORK ITEM IS `unjudged`, and says so. A commit nobody could attribute reading as clean is the false green this epic exists to remove.

DO NOT SHIP A COUNT NOBODY CHECKED. `.22`'s standing rule: whatever number this prints is a count of paths actually compared, and a comparison that could not be made prints a different word from one that passed.

NOTE THE BRANCH-NAME COUPLING: BDL-UX #230 / `beadloom-bdnv` — `declared_scope` matches a branch segment that EQUALS a work-item key, so a branch named `features/BDL-068-S4` attributes to no work item and this check would read `unjudged` for a whole slice. That bug is filed separately; this bead must at minimum not make its consequence silent.

title: [BDL-068.S4.x][dev] the guard binding sees one of three write paths, and reports the firings rather than the surface
description:
BDL-UX #170, filed 2026-08-22, never carried a bead. It is the entry the whole slice is named after: "the enforcement surface is narrower than the promise".

MEASURED THEN: the shipped hook binds PreToolUse with matcher "Edit|Write|NotebookEdit". An agent that writes through `python3 - <<EOF`, `sed -i` or a heredoc goes through Bash and fires no guard at all. Not hypothetical — the session that found it was operating under an instruction to prefer Bash for file edits, so a whole class of edits to THIS repository was unguarded while `--liveness` showed the guards healthy and firing. This session is under the same instruction today.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A MISSING MATCHER: the failure is shaped like success. `bead-claimed` cannot warn about an edit it was never told about, so a session that edits exclusively through Bash produces a clean liveness report and zero warnings — byte-identical to the output of a session that complied perfectly.

THREE SEPARABLE PIECES, and the third is the real one.
1. Add Bash to the emitted matcher and derive the edit target from the command line where it can be derived. Necessarily partial: a shell command's write targets are not decidable in general.
2. BECAUSE it is partial, the verdict must say so. A Bash invocation whose target cannot be determined is `not_covered`, never `pass`. This is the unknown-is-not-zero rule turned on the enforcement surface itself.
3. REPORT THE SURFACE, NOT JUST THE FIRINGS. `--liveness` answers "did each declared guard fire?". It must also answer "what fraction of edit events could this binding have seen?" — a guard healthy on a matcher covering one of three write paths is a third of a guard, and nothing says so today.

TECHNIQUE: the same one S1 shipped four times over. Derive the surface from the instrument's own matcher, compare it against the write paths that exist, report the gap. Do not hand-write the list of write paths — enumerate it from the harness settings the flow emits, so a matcher added later is covered without anyone remembering to.

DO NOT ship piece 1 without pieces 2 and 3. A matcher widened to Bash with no `not_covered` verdict makes the false green WIDER, because more events now report `pass` on a target nobody resolved.

DESIGN, three pieces:
P1 matcher — EDIT_MATCHER gains Bash; _claude_code_context reads tool_input.command for a Bash
   event. A new module derives WRITE TARGETS from the command line over a declared set of
   shapes (redirection, tee, sed -i, cp/mv/install, dd of=, touch), tokenised with shlex.
P2 the verdict says it is partial — DECISION, and the load-bearing one: a derived target NEVER
   feeds exclusion matching. The derivation is a LOWER BOUND on the writes, never the set, so
   letting one derived target grant an exclusion skip would exempt a command that also writes
   elsewhere. A Bash event therefore carries a NEW PathScope.UNDETERMINED: relative is None, so
   no exclusion applies (fail-closed), and not_covered_note names the derived targets and says
   the rest was not determined. The evaluator already appends not_covered_note to EVERY verdict
   including pass, so a pass on a Bash event can no longer read as coverage.
   Outcome stays what the check decides — turning it into skip would make the surface NARROWER,
   which is the opposite of the bead.
P3 the surface — new module application/guards/surface.py, one responsibility: what fraction of
   the harness's write paths the emitted binding can see. POPULATION IS DERIVED, not written:
   matchers come from .claude/settings.json hooks[PreToolUse][].matcher (so a matcher added
   later is covered), tool grants from the 'tools:' frontmatter of the emitted role adapters
   (.claude/agents/*.md, path from role_adapters.TOOL_AGENT_DIRS). The only declared table is

comments.text:
COMPLETED — commit 5fd9636 on features/BDL-068.

WHAT: BDL-UX #170, all three pieces, and piece 1 was never shipped without 2 and 3.
1. EDIT_MATCHER names Bash. hook_payload reads tool_input.command (bounded, COMMAND_LIMIT=2000).
   New module shell_targets.derive_write_targets reads write targets over a declared set of
   shapes — >/>>/>| redirection, tee, touch, truncate, sed -i, the destination of
   cp/mv/install/ln, dd of= — tokenised with shlex(punctuation_chars=True), so >f, > f and 1> f
   are one shape. Value-taking options are declared per writer, because without that
   'truncate -s 0 log' named '0' and 'sed -i \'\' -e s/a/b/ f' named the script.
2. The derivation is a LOWER BOUND, so a shell edit resolves to the new PathScope.UNDETERMINED:
   relative stays None -> exclusion_for(None) -> no exclusion applies (fail-closed), and the
   derived targets travel in not_covered with the statement that the rest was not derived. The
   evaluator already appends not_covered_note to EVERY verdict including pass, so a pass on a
   shell command can no longer read as coverage.
3. surface.build_surface answers what fraction of the write paths the binding could see, derived
   from artifacts and never from a list: matchers from .claude/settings.json hooks[PreToolUse][],
   the tool population from the 'tools:' grant of every emitted role adapter, and one declared
   OPEN-WORLD table of which tools write. A tool it cannot classify is 'unclassified', never a
   non-writer. An unreadable source is 'unresolved' and suppresses the fraction. It also reports a
   matcher naming a tool no role is granted — the dead-glob rule applied to a matcher.

DECISIONS
- A derived target NEVER feeds exclusion matching. 'sed -i docs/a.md && python3 write_src.py'
  names one write and performs two, so an exclusion applied to the visible half would exempt the
  invisible one. Stated in the module docstring and the SPEC.
- The outcome stays whatever the check decides. Turning a shell event into 'skip' would have made
  the surface NARROWER, which is the opposite of the bead.
- The matcher is read off DISK, not off EDIT_MATCHER. scaffold_guard_hooks merges on the command
  string, so a project scaffolded before this release keeps its narrow matcher across the
  upgrade. The merge stays (it must not rewrite an adopter's settings) and the gap is now
  reported instead of silent.

MEASURED on this repository: 3 of 3 write paths bound; 2 of 3 before the fix.

title: [BDL-UX #233] the read-only guard test reports a `bd` export burst as the guard's own write
description:
ATTRIBUTED BY beadloom-0mdo.26 after beadloom-0mdo.22 recorded it as non-reproducing and .23 and .24 each looked for it across four full-suite runs without meeting it. The attribution is the contribution; .26 deliberately did not allocate a number, because the log's open numbering was being used by beads that never reached the file and inventing one beside that is how mr2l.91's duplicate happened.

THE TEST: tests/test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation. It failed on two of .26's four full-suite runs and passed on the other two with no change to anything between them.

WHAT NOBODY COULD SAY BEFORE: the differing digest is '.beads/issues.jsonl', NEVER 'beadloom.db'. Both occurrences, the same file. So it is not the index and not a concurrent `beadloom lint`, which is the candidate the test's own docstring is built around.

THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE, not flakiness: `_moved_with_nothing_running` opens a control window of the same duration as the measurement window and skips only if the repository moves DURING it. A `bd` tracker export is a single burst of a few milliseconds rather than a continuous writer, so the burst lands inside the measurement window and misses the control window entirely. The test's attribution guard therefore does not fire and the failure is reported as the guard's.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TEST: a wave makes it LIKELIER, because both agents in a two-writer wave run `bd comments add`. So the check is least reliable exactly when the flow is most parallel — which is the condition under which a check teaches its reader to discount it. This project already has the principle: an always-red check is an ignored check, and an intermittently-red one is worse because it trains the discount without ever being wrong enough to fix.

EXPECTED: the control window must be able to observe a burst, not only a continuous writer — sample it repeatedly across the measurement window, or attribute by FILE (the digest already names which path differed) rather than by timing. The second is cheaper and the information is already in hand.

RELATED: BDL-UX #168 (pytest-randomly produces failures no seed reproduces) is the same reader-facing symptom from a different cause; #207 (the pre-commit hook re-stages .beads/issues.jsonl) is the same file being written by tooling outside the test's model.
notes: SCOPE DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED (BDL-068 S4, 2026-09-03). The axes derivation for this slice ran beadloom impact over tests/ and attributed a node to NONE of the 148 caller sites it found; the run reported sweep-narrower-than-the-project, which is BDL-UX #225 named by the instrument rather than inferred. This bead's whole scope is tests/test_guards_parity.py. flow-guards is the node under test, but no derivation says so, and writing 'refs: flow-guards' here would be an AUTHORED scope dressed as a derived one — which is precisely the defect beadloom-en0x / BDL-UX #232 is filed against, sitting in the same slice. beadloom waves will therefore serialise this bead against every other, and that is the correct answer, not a penalty: an unknown scope is not an empty scope. DO NOT 'fix' this by inventing a ref. It resolves when impact can attribute a node to a test file.

title: [BDL-UX #232] `waves` plans from an authored `refs:` line, so two beads editing one document read as independent
description:
FOUND BY beadloom-0mdo.21 during the first documentation wave run in parallel, and sharpened by the coordinator's own measurement.

WHAT HAPPENED: beadloom-0mdo.21 and beadloom-0mdo.26 ran concurrently and BOTH edited docs/services/cli.md — .21 the review-brief section, .26 the mutation and rooms sections. `beadloom waves` reported 1 wave, 2 beads, 0 serialisations, 0 findings. In .21's words: 'both sets of edits survived by luck, not design.' It recovered by rebuilding the file from HEAD plus its own edits and staging only its hunks.

THE CAUSE IS NOT THAT THE GRAPH DOES NOT KNOW THE FILE. It does: docs/services/cli.md is the spec document of the `cli` node, and `beadloom search` resolves it to the `cli-commands` component. The cause is that `waves` compares the `refs:` each bead DECLARES, and both declarations were authored by the coordinator from the CODE each bead would touch — `refs: review-brief` and `refs: mutation-scope, ci-gate` — while the collision was in a DOCUMENT owned by a node neither named.

SO THE SHAPE IS THIS EPIC'S OWN, IN THE PLANNER ITSELF: `waves`'s scope input is AUTHORED while everything BDL-068 built is DERIVED. `beadloom impact` now derives the axes a change ranges over from the source and names the population it could not resolve; `waves` still reads a hand-written line and, when that line is short, reports 0 findings with the confidence of a measurement. A wave plan is acted on, so a planner whose errors WIDEN a wave is the dangerous direction — which is the same argument the parser in `waves` already makes for itself when it says an unreadable declaration serialises against everything.

TWO FIXES, and they are not alternatives:
 (a) IMMEDIATE, the coordinator's: a bead's `refs:` must name the nodes that own the DOCUMENTS it will edit, not only the code. A tech-writer bead editing a node's spec declares that node. This costs nothing and would have caught this instance.
 (b) THE REAL ONE: feed the planner a derived scope rather than an authored one. `beadloom impact <target> --section` already produces the axes and their boundary nodes; a bead whose Axes section exists should have its wave scope taken from there, and a bead whose declaration and derivation DISAGREE is a finding — which is exactly the rule BDL-068 CONTEXT.md Q1 already states for the axes table, the document and the bead's refs.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE IF UNFIXED: every wave this epic ran was planned from an authored declaration. Five of them were parallel. Four were safe by construction (a read-only reviewer, or a single writer); this one had two writers on one file and nothing reported it.

RELATED: BDL-UX #181 (a clean room cannot see a cross-bead interaction — this is the planner failing to predict one), and the `waves` media report itself, which names working-tree, commit-gate, doc-baseline and tracker-ids as shared media and correctly reported all four as passing here. The medium that collided was not among them because it was not in scope.
notes:
refs: wave-plan, cli-commands
ALSO COVERS BDL-UX #234 (filed 2026-09-03, same session, found while planning S4's wave): the remedy printed beside an unresolved_scope finding does not follow the cause down as far as the reason does. beadloom-nn4c has NO declaration; its note is prose explaining why writing one would be dishonest, the parser matched the refs: inside that explanation, and the printed remedy told the reader to promote it to a real declaration -- which would have manufactured exactly the authored scope this bead is filed against. The serialisation and the exit code were both correct. Fix the remedy alongside the derivation: derive it from the cause, and where the tool genuinely cannot tell prose about refs: from a careless refs:, say that rather than guessing which.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: design settled, before any code.

#232. The declaration keeps deciding the shape; what is added is the COMPARISON Q1 states. A new `WorkItemAxes` (the work item's recorded derivation, composed at the services edge from the SAME read `scope-check` makes, so the commit gate and the wave plan cannot disagree about one approval) is held against every bead's declared refs. Four verdicts per ref: agrees / ruled_out_of_scope / no_scope_decision / not_derived. And one over the wave: a node the work item APPROVES (kept rows plus the `Derived by` targets, exactly `DeclaredScope.inside`) that no bead of the wave declares is `unguarded_axis`.

WHY THE FINDING IS PER-WAVE AND NOT PER-PLAN, measured rather than guessed: BDL-068's RFC keeps 8 axis nodes. A plan of one bead declaring one of them would print 7 findings, every time, for the whole epic — an always-red check is an ignored check, which is this project's own rule and nn4c's bead quotes it. The claim the check actually makes is about a PAIR: the pairwise verdict for these two beads did not compare those nodes. Over a wave of one there is no pair, so nothing is claimed and nothing is printed — the same way `conflicts` is empty for a wave of one and nobody calls that suppression. This is NOT `media_for(wave_size)`, which 67t1 removed: that suppressed a STATEMENT about a medium shared regardless of width.

Q2 IS THE UNIT, per the launch note's point 2: `0mdo.27` edited `cli-commands` outside its own refs and that is CORRECT because `cli-commands` is a kept row of this epic's axes. So the comparison is never `bead touched outside its refs`.

POINT 1 (`.32`: 41 of 52 paths have no owning node) has its shape here as the axis row whose Node cell names none — no declaration can name it and no comparison can reach it, so it is `not compared`, printed, never a finding.

POINT 3 (#225, `impact` under-reports) is `not_derived`: a declared ref the table does not mention is the derivation not reaching, not the declaration being wrong. Reported, NOT a finding. The section's own `Unresolved:` field is carried verbatim beside it.

#234. `UNRESOLVED_REMEDIES` stops being a dict lookup and becomes `remedy_for(cause, axes=...)`. The unanchored remedy states BOTH branches and says the check cannot tell them apart; the no-declaration remedy sends the author to the axes document when there is one.

DEFAULT IS A FINDING, NOT A PASS: a caller that gathers no axes gets a `WorkItemAxes` carrying a reason, and a wave of two beads whose declarations were compared against nothing says so. Same rule as `unmeasured` in the media checks.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: both halves implemented and measured on the beads that produced them.

#234, ON THE LIVE CASE. `beadloom waves beadloom-nn4c` now prints, under the SAME correct reason `declaration_not_at_a_line_start`: "a `refs:` token appears in the text but never at the start of a line, and this check cannot tell a declaration written mid-sentence from prose ABOUT declarations. If it is a declaration, move it to the start of its own line. If it is prose — which is how a bead that declares no scope on purpose says so — nothing needs moving, and promoting the sentence would author the scope this check exists to derive." nn4c was not touched. `UNRESOLVED_REMEDIES` is now the base text and `remedy_for(cause, axes=...)` is what every caller spends, including `review-brief`, which had the same one-sentence lookup.

#232, ON THE MEASURED CASE. `beadloom waves beadloom-0mdo.21 beadloom-0mdo.26` reported 1 wave, 2 beads, 0 findings before. It now reports: `unguarded_axis: wave 1 runs beadloom-0mdo.21, beadloom-0mdo.26 together and BDL-068 approves 9 node(s) none of them declares (axes-section, cli-commands, config-check, flow-guards, impact, planning-report, role-adapters, role-composer, work-item-type)`. `cli-commands` is in that list, and `cli-commands` is the node that owns `docs/services/cli.md` — the document both beads edited.

WHAT THE COMPARISON MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, which is also the answer to whether it is noise. BDL-068's RFC approves 10 nodes (8 kept rows plus 3 `Derived by` targets, one of which is also a kept row). Of `.26`'s two declared refs, `ci-gate` AGREES and `mutation-scope` is `not_derived`; `.21`'s `review-brief` is `not_derived` as well. That is not the declarations being wrong — it is the RFC's own statement coming true, that S2–S6 would add their axes at their own start and did not. 0 `ruled_out_of_scope` on this repository today, because the only out-of-scope row (`co-writers`) attributes no node, which is reported as `not_attributed` and is exactly point 1's shape at table scale.

THE ONE DESIGN CALL WORTH REVIEWING. The gap is reported PER WAVE and only for a wave holding two beads or more, because the sentence it makes is about a pairwise verdict and a wave of one makes no pair. Reported per plan it would print 9 findings on every single-bead plan of this epic, forever. This is deliberately NOT `media_for(wave_size)`, which `67t1` removed: that suppressed a STATEMENT about a medium shared whatever the width. The same gate governs `declarations_not_compared`, so `beadloom waves <one bead>` off a work-item branch does not exit 1 on every run.

FOUR EXISTING TESTS WENT RED AND WERE UPDATED RATHER THAN THE RULE WEAKENED, which is the same move `beadloom-mr2l.80` made when the environment default stopped meaning clean: each now SAYS what its declarations were held against (`_approving(*nodes)`), and `test_cli_waves`'s measured project gained a real work item on a real branch, so the CLI path is exercised end to end.

RED SEEN, AND WHERE IT WAS NOT. 7 of the 8 new acceptance scenarios were run against the restored old behaviour and all 7 failed. The 8th ("a wave whose beads together declare every approved node reports no gap") is the false-positive guard: it asserts a CLEAN plan, so it cannot go red under the absence of the rule, and that is stated here rather than left implied.

DOCS: wave-plan SPEC (new section + structure + API + invariants), declared-scope DOC (`work_item_axes`), cli-commands DOC. Five pairs attested per `--pair`/`--code`, never `--all`, since a neighbour's `setup.py` change is in the tree. `sync-check` rc 0, `lint --strict` rc 0, `doctor` clean, `mypy` clean, `ruff` clean. Clean-room and combined-tree measurements still to come.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
API CHANGE: `beadloom waves` gained a fourth thing every plan rests on, in both output shapes, and `plan_waves` gained a keyword argument.

CLI: the human output prints a `Declared axes (<work item>, <document>)` block — nodes approved, declared refs that agree, refs the derivation did not reach, axis rows naming no node — plus the seed, the section's own `Unresolved` statement, and one line per non-agreeing verdict. A work item nothing can be read from prints `Declared axes: NOT COMPARED — <reason>` instead. Two new findings reach exit 1: `unguarded_axis` and `declared_outside_the_axes`, plus `declarations_not_compared` where a wave holds a pair and nothing was gathered. Exit codes are unchanged in number and meaning.

`--json`: three new top-level keys — `axes` (work_item, document, seed, unresolved, approved, reason), `agreements` (bead, ref, verdict, detail) and `unguarded_axes` (wave, beads, nodes); and `scopes[].declared`, the refs a bead's own words named before `part_of` expanded them.

Python API: `plan_waves(..., axes: WorkItemAxes | None = None)`. Leaving it out is allowed and is REPORTED, so an existing caller that plans a concurrent wave now reaches exit 1 where it reached 0 — the same break `beadloom-mr2l.80` made when `environment` stopped defaulting to clean, and for the same reason. New exports from `beadloom.application.waves`: `WorkItemAxes`, `ScopeAgreement`, `UnguardedAxis`, `compare_declarations`, `unguarded_axes`, `derivation_findings`, `remedy_for`, the `AXIS_*` and `FINDING_*` constants, `AXES_NOT_GATHERED`, `UNKNOWN_REMEDY`. `UNRESOLVED_REMEDIES` still exists but is now the base text rather than what a caller spends: `remedy_for(cause, axes=...)` is, and the printed wording for `declaration_not_at_a_line_start` and `no_declared_refs` has CHANGED. `BeadScope` gained `declared`; `WavePlan` gained `axes`, `agreements`, `unguarded_axes`. New: `beadloom.application.declared_scope.work_item_axes(project_root, *, branch)`.

Docs to check: docs/domains/application/features/wave-plan/SPEC.md and docs/domains/application/components/declared-scope/DOC.md and docs/services/components/cli-commands/DOC.md (all three updated in this bead); docs/guides/parallel-waves.md and docs/services/cli.md (NOT updated here — both carry the `waves` surface and both already read `surface drift` at HEAD, so they are the tech-writer's, `beadloom-0mdo.36`).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED. beadloom-en0x — BDL-UX #232 and #234, both measured on the beads that produced them. Commits ded748d (code, docs, tests) and dcf9338 (ACTIVE).

WHAT. #232: the wave planner's scope input was a `refs:` line the bead's AUTHOR wrote, while everything else this epic built is derived. The declaration still DECIDES the shape — CONTEXT Q1's direction is not "stop reading it" — and what is added is the comparison against the derivation the work item recorded, with the gap reported. #234: the printed remedy did not follow the cause as far as the reason did, and told a bead that declares no scope on purpose to promote its own explanatory prose into a declaration.

DECISIONS.
1. The unit is the WORK ITEM's axes (Q2), never the bead's, so `0mdo.27` editing `cli-commands` outside its own refs stays correct and raises nothing.
2. `WorkItemAxes` is composed at the services edge from the SAME read `scope_of_branch` makes for the commit gate — a second RENDERING, never a second read — so the gate and the plan cannot disagree about one approval. It adds the two things the gate has no use for: the rows attributing no node, and the section's own `Unresolved` statement.
3. Four verdicts per declared ref and only ONE of them accuses anybody. `not_derived` is the derivation not reaching (#225, still open), `not_attributed` is the table-scale shape of `.32`'s 41-of-52 unowned paths, `no_scope_decision` belongs to `axis-without-a-scope-decision`. Only `ruled_out_of_scope` is a finding.
4. `unguarded_axis` is per WAVE and only where a wave holds two beads or more. The sentence it makes is about a pairwise verdict, and a wave of one makes no pair. Per plan it would print 9 findings on every single-bead plan of this epic, forever, and an always-red check is an ignored check — this project's own rule, quoted in `nn4c`'s own bead. This is NOT `media_for(wave_size)`, which `67t1` removed: that suppressed a STATEMENT about a medium shared whatever the width.
5. A caller gathering no axes gets a reason rather than silence, under the same rule that makes `unmeasured` a medium verdict — and under the same pair gate, so `beadloom waves <one bead>` off a work-item branch does not exit 1 on every run.
6. `UNRESOLVED_REMEDIES` becomes the base text and `remedy_for(cause, axes=...)` is what every caller spends, `review-brief` included. Where the two sub-cases of an unanchored `refs:` cannot be told apart, both are stated and so is the ambiguity.

TESTS. 8 new acceptance scenarios in `tests/acceptance/features/wave_plan.feature`, all bound `@bead:beadloom-en0x`; 27 new cases in `tests/test_wave_derivation.py`. RED VERIFIED: the old behaviour was restored under all three claims and 7 of the 8 scenarios failed. The 8th asserts a CLEAN plan (the false-positive guard) and cannot go red under the absence of the rule — stated rather than left implied. Four EXISTING tests went red and were updated rather than the rule weakened, each now saying what its declarations were held against; `test_cli_waves`'s measured project gained a real work item on a real branch, so the CLI path is exercised end to end.

FILES. src/beadloom/application/waves/{derivation.py NEW, models.py, planner.py, scope.py, __init__.py}, src/beadloom/application/declared_scope.py, src/beadloom/application/review_brief/assembly.py, src/beadloom/services/commands/waves.py, docs/domains/application/features/wave-plan/SPEC.md, docs/domains/application/components/declared-scope/DOC.md, docs/services/components/cli-commands/DOC.md, tests/acceptance/features/wave_plan.feature, tests/acceptance/steps/test_wave_plan_steps.py, tests/test_wave_derivation.py NEW, tests/test_wave_plan.py, tests/test_wave_media_checks.py, tests/test_bead22_wave_guarantee.py, tests/test_cli_waves.py.

MEASUREMENTS, EACH IN THE ROOM IT WAS TAKEN IN.
- Clean room `room-beadloom-en0x` over 18 files: 8 626 passed, 1 failed. That failure (`TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh`) is the room's stated property — no `.git`, so 420 pairs read `unverified` — and it was confirmed red at PURE HEAD in an identically-built control room. `beadloom ci` rc 0 there, in Darwin arm64 / CPython 3.12.12, which is NOT the tree's interpreter: #236's shape, a room's verdict decided by what it installed.
- AS ITS OWN GATE OWNER (`beadloom waves` names this bead the owner of its wave of one): the combined tree at ded748d is green — 8 657 passed, 0 failed, `beadloom ci` rc 0 in the FOREGROUND and unpiped, `HEAD` verified unchanged before and after. Darwin arm64 / CPython 3.13.7, 0 of the 21 declared rooms, so it is a claim about this machine and about no CI leg.
- `mypy --python-version` over all four declared target versions (3.10-3.13): clean on each. That varies the version the checker is ASKED about, not the interpreter it RUNS under, so a per-interpreter difference in what is installed is still measured only in CI.
- The tree carries four files from outside this bead (`onboarding/bootstrap.py`, `doc_classify.py`, `services/commands/setup.py`, two tests), uncommitted before this bead began and deliberately left that way. Doc pairs were attested with `--pair`/`--code` and never `--all`, so the neighbour's `setup.py` pair keeps its own baseline.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, AND WHY. `beadloom-nn4c` was NOT edited: its note is deliberate and it is the next wave's work, so it stands as a live regression case for both defects. `docs/guides/parallel-waves.md` and `docs/services/cli.md` were not updated — both carry the `waves` surface, both already read `surface drift` at HEAD, and both are `beadloom-0mdo.36`'s. The commit hook printed 8 mypy errors in two test files; all 8 are present at HEAD~1 in the same files, so none is new — they are `beadloom-gsal` / #231's subject, which is that same hook type-checking an undeclared surface and never blocking.

The `unguarded_axis` line on this branch names 9 of 10 approved nodes because BDL-068's `## Axes` were derived once, at S1, over S1's three surfaces — the RFC says S2-S6 add theirs at their own start and they did not. That is the check's first real output being a true statement about a real gap, not a false positive, but it means the finding will keep firing until the later slices' axes are derived. Deriving them is a coordinator action, not this bead's.

CORRECTION, after the close, to a claim this bead made about the room its own verdict was taken in.

The completion comment and ACTIVE.md both said the combined tree carried four uncommitted files from outside this bead (`onboarding/scanner/bootstrap.py`, `doc_classify.py`, `services/commands/setup.py` and two tests). IT DID NOT. All four are byte-identical to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` over them is empty, and their mtimes (2026-09-03 09:14:51 and 23:05:07) predate this bead's first command by hours. The launch context's `git status` snapshot listed them as modified, that snapshot is documented as not updating during a session, and it was RESTATED rather than re-derived — which is this bead's own defect one layer up: a report resting on an authored snapshot instead of a measurement.

WHAT IS UNAFFECTED. The verdict itself: 8 657 passed, 0 failed, `beadloom ci` rc 0, `HEAD` verified unchanged at ded748d before and after. If anything the claim was too WEAK — the tree measured was clean of any neighbour's work, so the combined-tree verdict is a claim about exactly this bead's three commits and nothing else. And `git show --stat` on each commit confirms only this bead's files landed: ded748d carries the 18 files plus the two tracker exports, dcf9338 carries ACTIVE.md plus issues.jsonl, 1924776 carries the two tracker files.

WHAT IT COST, so the next reader can weigh it: nothing was lost and nothing was measured wrong. The cost is that a sentence about a room was published without the one command that would have decided it, in a bead whose whole subject is a plan resting on a declaration nobody compared against a derivation. ACTIVE.md now carries the withdrawal in the entry itself rather than only here.

title: [BDL-UX #231] the commit hook warns about type errors on an undeclared surface, discards the output, and never blocks
description:
FLAGGED BY beadloom-0mdo.28 as a shared-medium fact for its wave's gate owner, then measured by the coordinator. A sharper statement of mr2l.82, which the ROADMAP records as 'the commit-scoped hook type-checks a surface the project never declared typed'.

THE HOOK, .git/hooks/pre-commit:41-48, verbatim:

    echo "$staged_py" | xargs uv run mypy 2>/dev/null
    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "Warning: mypy type errors in this commit"
    fi

THREE PROPERTIES, ANY ONE OF WHICH MAKES IT IGNORABLE:
 1. It type-checks a surface the project NEVER DECLARED. pyproject's [tool.mypy] sets packages = ["beadloom"] — src/beadloom and nothing else. ruff deliberately covers both (src = ["src", "tests"], and the completion checklist runs `ruff check src/ tests/` beside `mypy src/`), so the asymmetry is a decision, not an oversight. MEASURED: `uv run mypy tests/` reports 970 errors in 90 files over 338 source files. None is a violation of a declared standard.
 2. It DISCARDS mypy's output (2>/dev/null) and prints one contentless sentence. A committer is told errors exist and not which, where, or whether they matter.
 3. It never blocks.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS, and it is not the noise: a real error inside src/ produces THE IDENTICAL SENTENCE. The one case where this check earns its place is indistinguishable from the 970 that are expected — so the signal that matters is drowned by the signal that does not, and the whole thing is trained to be scrolled past. This project already has the principle: an always-red check is an ignored check, which is why `beadloom-0mdo.6`'s acceptance required that a commit INSIDE the declared axes be silent, verified on one that is.

EXPECTED, and either is defensible so long as it is stated:
 - scope the hook to the declared typed surface, so a warning means a violation of something the project claims; or
 - declare tests/ typed and pay the 970 down, which is a decision about the standard rather than about the hook.
Whichever is chosen, the hook must print WHAT mypy said. A check that reports its own existence and not its finding is the shape this epic exists to remove.

FILED SEPARATELY FROM mr2l.82 rather than reopening it: that bead is closed with the ROADMAP carrying the one-line record, and this adds the measurement (970/90), the discarded-output half, and the drowning argument, which the one-liner does not.

Belongs with beadloom-0mdo.12 (S4 — the guards' enforcement surface is narrower than their promise): this is a guard whose surface is WIDER than the promise and whose signal carries nothing, which is the same family read from the other end.

title: [BDL-UX #230] a branch whose name carries a suffix after the work-item key names no work item, and the channel goes silent
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-0mdo.20, MAJOR 2. Filed rather than fixed in the cycle, by the reviewer's judgement: 'nothing about it is a wrong claim about the product; the instrument understates itself and the SPEC discloses it.'

MEASURED on features/BDL-068-S2S3: the work-item channel reads 'NOT INSPECTED — the branch names no work item among the project's planning documents, so no folder could be read'. THE FOLDER EXISTS AND THE REVIEWER READ FROM IT — RFC.md and CONTEXT.md under .claude/development/docs/features/BDL-068/, which is step 4 of the review protocol. So the report FAILED TO NAME A CHANNEL THE REVIEWER REACHED, and it is the channel BDL-UX #212 is about.

The report also contradicts itself inside one page: its own CHANGE inventory lists .claude/development/docs/features/BDL-068/ACTIVE.md.

Under the Channel docstring's own rule — a channel nobody could inspect must never read like one that was inspected and found empty — this is the same class in the other direction.

CAUSE: declared_scope.py:142 matches a work-item key that a branch segment EQUALS. FIX, per the reviewer: match a key that a segment BEGINS WITH, longest key wins, so `features/BDL-068-S2S3` names BDL-068 while a segment that merely CONTAINS a key still names none. One home, not two — the SPEC is right that a second reader of the branch convention would be two sources of truth.

TEST GAP: tests/test_review_brief_reachability.py has no case for a branch carrying a suffix after the key; every case is `features/ALPHA-1` exactly.

COORDINATOR'S NOTE, recorded because the cause is upstream of the code: the branch is named features/BDL-068-S2S3 because the coordinator chose to carry two slices on one branch. Every remaining slice of this epic runs on a branch of that shape, so THIS CHANNEL STAYS BLIND FOR THE REST OF THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN DEVELOPMENT unless either the fix lands or later slice branches are named features/BDL-068 with no suffix. The cheap mitigation costs nothing and is the coordinator's to take; the defect is still real for any adopter whose branch names carry a suffix, which is the ordinary shape.

title: [BDL-UX #229] the brief sends the reviewer to the tracker export and does not name it as a channel
description:
REVIEW FINDING beadloom-0mdo.20, MAJOR 1 parts (b) and (c). Filed by the reviewer's own judgement: part (a) is one sentence and rides the fix cycle; these two widen the report.

THIS IS THE ASSIGNMENT'S ANSWER — the channel that carries an author's account and that the new report does not name is THE TRACKER EXPORT INSIDE THE REVIEWED DIFF.

MEASURED: `git diff main...HEAD -- .beads/issues.jsonl` adds 16 record lines carrying 30 author comments and 81,270 characters of comment text (beads .18, .19, .22, .23 and mj2o). The brief's own CHANGE inventory lists .beads/issues.jsonl and then prints `read it: git diff main...HEAD -- <path>`.

So the report names the commit bodies its protocol sends the reviewer to (BDL-UX #219, answered) and does not name the tracker export it sends the reviewer to IN THE SAME BREATH. That is #219's mechanism one step further along.

(b) Add a channel for the tracker export when the reviewed range changes it. Its population is derivable exactly as the commit range is, from the change inventory the brief already holds, and a COUNT of comment records in the added lines needs no comment text — so the channel can be named without the brief reading what it withholds.

(c) Either count the slice's sibling beads — reachable through `waves` — or say in the statement that they are not counted.

RELATED: #204 (the brief cannot know what the coordinator's prompt contained — now answered by naming the launch prompt as an uninspectable channel), #212, #219. This is the fourth channel in the family and the first one the instrument itself points at.

title: [BDL-068.S4.x][dev] a duty declared for a role is carried by that role's composed core — checked in both directions
description:
A CLASS CHECK, proposed after the same shape was measured four times in two epics. Belongs to S4 because the technique is S4's: derive the surface an instrument actually reaches, compare it against what it promises, report the gap.

THE CLASS, stated as narrowly as the evidence supports: a duty an agent is obliged to perform is written somewhere the performer does not read.

THE FOUR INSTANCES, and they are NOT all the same sub-shape — the distinction decides what is checkable:
 (a) THE DUTY DOES NOT REACH THE PERFORMER. #228: the clean-room duty lives in the coordinator's prose and in waves/media.py (only for waves of more than one bead). ZERO occurrences in .claude/agents/{dev,test,review,tech-writer}.md and zero in the role templates setup-agentic-flow composes for an adopter. Across two epics every agent said the right words because the coordinator typed them into every launch prompt.
 (b) THE DUTY REACHES THE PERFORMER AND NOTHING CAN CHECK PERFORMANCE. BDL-061 S4 put mutation testing into every role core and shipped no runner; four beads in BDL-067 then reported four different hand methods as prose. S3 of this epic is closing that half.
 (c) A GUARANTEE IS STATED OVER ONE CHANNEL AND DEFEATED BY ANOTHER THE SAME PLAYBOOK NAMES. #212 (the review's withholding defeated through ACTIVE.md, which the role prompt is told to read) and #219 (through commit bodies, which the review protocol tells the reviewer to read). S2 is closing that half.

THIS BEAD IS (a) ONLY. Naming the three sub-shapes is half the deliverable: they were read as one finding four times, and a check built over all three would be a check over nothing.

THE DESIGN, and the trap it must avoid. Do NOT derive 'duties' from free prose. This project has already filed that failure three times — docs audit's English-keyword-proximity classifier binds 'supports 11 languages' to a fact counting the languages the project is WRITTEN in (#205), reads a version cited as an example as a claim (#190), and verifies nothing in a non-English document while counting it as scanned (#209). A duty detector over prose would be the fourth instance, shipped as the fix for the third.

MAKE DUTIES DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED, the way this repository already made scenarios declared. A scenario carries @bead: and @node: tags and scenario-coverage checks the binding in BOTH directions — a scenario naming a dead node, and a node carrying none. The same technique applies: a duty in a composed flow artifact carries the role(s) that must perform it, and the check asserts that every named role's COMPOSED core contains it, and that every duty in a role core is declared somewhere.

THE LIMIT, to be stated in the check's own output rather than discovered later: a duty carried only by a coordinator's launch prompt is unreachable by any file-based check, because a prompt is not an artifact. The check can cover composed artifacts and nothing else. That limit is itself the argument for moving a duty out of the prompt and into a composed core — which is what #228 does for the clean-room rule — and the check should say what it could not see, the way beadloom impact names its unresolved population.

DONE WHEN a duty declared for a role and absent from that role's composed core is a finding; a duty in a role core that no artifact declares is a finding; and the output names the population it cannot inspect.

refs: role-composer, role-adapters, config-check
