title: [BDL-UX #228] the clean-room duty reaches the roles that must perform it only through the coordinator's typing
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03, by grep, after the owner asked where the discipline comes from.

    .claude/agents/{dev,test,review,tech-writer}.md          0 occurrences of 'clean room'
    src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/roles/**               0  <- what setup-agentic-flow composes for an ADOPTER
    .claude/CLAUDE.md                                        2  <- the PROJECT layer, explicitly never distributed
    src/beadloom/application/waves/media.py                  yes <- a machine
    templates/agentic_flow/commands/coordinator.md.txt       yes <- prose, coordinator only

THE RULE: 'green in a clean room over N files' is a different claim from 'green on the tree'; verify with git archive HEAD plus only your files, and say which you measured. It exists because four agents in BDL-067 each reported green on a tree that was RED and none of them was wrong — each measured its own room (BDL-UX #181).

THE DEFECT: the roles that must perform it carry nothing. Across BDL-067 and BDL-068 every agent reported the correct words, and the only reason is that the coordinator typed the requirement into every launch prompt by hand. A role exists so the coordinator's prompt stops mattering; for this duty the prompt is the entire mechanism.

THE MACHINE HALF FIRES IN THE WRONG CASE. waves/media.py emits the working-tree note and names a combined-tree gate owner only for a wave of MORE THAN ONE BEAD; a single-bead wave prints 'not_applicable'. Roughly twenty of the waves across the two epics were single-bead, and in every one of them the rule travelled by prompt alone. So the instrument speaks exactly where the coordinator is already thinking about it and is silent where it is not.

AN ADOPTER GETS NEITHER HALF: no role template carries it, and the project layer that does carry it is by construction not distributed.

SAME CLASS AS BDL-061 S4, and worse. There the mutation duty at least reached the role cores with no runner behind it. Here the duty does not reach the role at all.

EXPECTED: the clean-room duty is stated in the role cores that compose to every adopter — the same place BDL-061 S4 put the mutation duty — AND a single-bead wave says which room its one bead owes, so the machine half stops being conditional on wave size. The two halves answer different questions and this project has already learned that shipping only one of them is how a rule reads as held while nothing holds it.

RELATED: #212 and #219 (the review's withholding defeated through channels the playbook itself names), BDL-061 S4 (a duty with no runner), #227 (a verdict that does not name its room). This is the same family and belongs with S2/S4 of BDL-068 rather than on its own.

title: [BDL-UX #227] mypy --strict is run on one Python version locally and four in CI, so an unused-ignore lands as a red PR
description:
MEASURED on PR #59: tests (3.10) and tests (3.11) failed in 18 and 21 SECONDS while 3.12 and 3.13 passed in ~6.5 minutes. Not a test failure — `uv run mypy src/` at the step before:

    src/beadloom/application/gate.py:581: error: Unused "type: ignore" comment  [unused-ignore]
    src/beadloom/application/gate.py:582: error: Unused "type: ignore" comment  [unused-ignore]

The ignores were needed under the interpreter the work was written on and unnecessary under 3.10/3.11, and `--strict` reports an unnecessary ignore as an error. Every local measurement in BDL-068 — and every one in BDL-067 before it — ran `uv run mypy src/` with no --python-version, i.e. against the developer's own interpreter only.

THIS IS THE THIRD TIME CI HAS CAUGHT WHAT EVERY LOCAL MEASUREMENT MISSED, and all three are one shape: a claim true of the room it was measured in, read as a claim about the product.
 - BDL-067: nine 'green on the tree' measurements, all macOS; the CI legs are Ubuntu and the tenth was red on six of them (a path hard-wrapped mid-token at a width only the runner's path length produces).
 - mr2l.61, already filed: fifteen tests skip on Linux that do not skip on macOS.
 - This: four interpreters in CI, one locally.

EXPECTED, and it is cheap: the type check runs over the versions the project declares support for, in one command, so a version-conditional error cannot reach a PR. `uv run mypy --python-version 3.10 src/` through `3.13` takes seconds — measured here at four clean runs while writing this — and it belongs in the completion checklist beside `uv run mypy src/`, or replaces it.

WIDER SHAPE, worth stating once rather than filing again per instance: this repository's completion checklist names commands, and a command names no room. 'green' is not a verdict until it says on what. BDL-068's S3 slice already owns 'a verdict that does not name its platform is not a verdict'; this is that finding arriving from the typing side rather than the test side, and it should be closed with it.

FIXED IN PASSING on features/BDL-068: _convention_finding took `convention: object` and carried three type: ignore[attr-defined] on one f-string. It is now typed SectionConvention and carries none, which is version-independent and also removes a CLAUDE.md anti-pattern (a type: ignore with no stated reason). Verified with --python-version at 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13: clean on all four.

title: [BDL-UX #225] impact under-reports on `src/<one package>` beside code outside src/ — the commonest Python layout
description:
FOUND BY THE beadloom-0mdo.17 RE-REVIEW as a non-blocking major, with a red proof in the layout matrix's own form. Filed rather than fixed, by the reviewer's judgement and the slice's stop rule.

application/impact/answer.py:177-193 (source_root_of) and :460 (_sweep_gaps).

On an src/<one package> layout the narrowing gap is compared against src/<package> rather than against the PROJECT, so Python outside src/ is swept by nothing and declared by nothing. callers.resolved and co_writers.resolved are both True over a demonstrably partial answer.

THIS IS THE COMMONEST PYTHON LAYOUT THERE IS: src/pkg beside tests/, scripts/, tools/, noxfile.py, tasks.py, manage.py.

THE PROOF, in the matrix's own invariant ('found, or declared'), a sixth layout built in the scratchpad:

    assert names == ["run"] or "sweep-narrower-than-the-project" in kinds
    E  assert ([] == ['run'] ... or 'sweep-narrower-than-the-project' in
       {'no-graph-index', 'no-seed', 'unresolved-terminator-name'})

Red against the shipped package. Not committed — that review was read-only.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COMMAND: the ## Axes artifact that `impact --section` writes — consumed by `beadloom scope-check` and by `axes --refs` — carries the same silence in its Unresolved: field. So a commit-scope verdict on this layout can be clean over a partial derivation, which is the failure mode the whole slice exists to prevent, one layout over from the critical it just closed.

title: [BDL-UX #224] a new test file landing on an existing path deletes its scenarios and the suite goes GREEN over the wreckage
description:
FOUND BY beadloom-0mdo.6 ON ITSELF, by reading `git status --short` before staging rather than by any check in this repository.

WHAT HAPPENED. The bead named its acceptance files tests/acceptance/features/commit_scope.feature and tests/acceptance/steps/test_commit_scope_steps.py and OVERWROTE two that already existed: BDL-061 S6's, bead beadloom-mr2l.21, node sync-check, the scenarios for BDL-UX #118 ('the commit gate judges the commit, and names the tree it did not judge').

The two missing were the evidence for another bead's finding, and nothing reported them. beadloom ci was rc 0 throughout.

WHAT CAUGHT IT: ' M' in git status where '??' was expected. A tracked file the author believes they created is the whole signal, and it is available to a human reading two lines of output and to nothing else.

WHY THE EXISTING CHECKS CANNOT SEE IT. scenario-coverage asks that a scenario names a live node and that a behaviour-bearing node carries scenarios. It cannot see that a FILE which used to hold four scenarios under one @bead now holds nine different ones under another. The population it counts is satisfied either way.

title: [BDL-UX #222][bug] the independent cross-check states and computes the attribution rule the implementation stopped using
description:
FOUND BY THE beadloom-e8s4.28 REVIEWER (ninth pass), filed rather than fixed under the stop rule. NOT merge-blocking: the divergence tree IS covered by two sibling classes, so the epic is not uncovered.

tests/test_init_one_table_over_every_axis.py:41-46 (module docstring, invariant 3), :462-478 (RunOutcome.wrote_the_failing_graph_file / .corner), :788-800.

Invariant 3 reads: 'The bug-report request appears exactly where THIS run wrote both the rules and THE GRAPH FILE THE FAILING NODE CAME FROM.' That was the key until beadloom-e8s4.24. The shipped key is _this_run_wrote_the_node_that_fails — the NODE. RunOutcome.corner computes the FILE-grain answer, and three cases require the report to agree with it under a docstring saying it 'FAILS if the report and the tree disagree'. Both claims are now false: report and tree can disagree at the node grain in a way this measurement cannot see.

MEASURED by the reviewer over all ten red runs the table performs, computing both grains side by side: they AGREE in every cell. The agreement is a consequence of the ARRANGEMENTS, not of the rules — since .21, generate_skeletons annotates every node on disk, so whenever a cell rewrites legacy.yml it also rewrites the failing node's own entry. The one tree where the two rules diverge (the file moves for a SIBLING while the failing node does not) is exactly the tree the eighth review measured, and no cell of this table builds it.

SO THE ANSWER TO 'strongest test or coincidence' IS: coincidence — BECAUSE THE DIVERGENCE IS NOT STATED. An independent cross-check deriving its expectation by a different rule than the code is the strongest test in a suite only when that difference is declared; undeclared, it is an agreement waiting to break.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, in order of cost:
 - it cannot fail if the implementation regresses to the file grain, which is the defect .24 and .27 were both spent on;
 - it will fail FALSELY, blaming a correct implementation, the first time an arrangement stops annotating the failing node.

WHY NOT CRITICAL: TestTheGraphHalfIsAskedOfTheNodeAndNotOfTheFile and TestEachSentenceSpeaksAtTheGrainItsKeyIsReadAt do build the divergence tree and would go red.

FIX, either: compute the corner at the node grain here too (the module already digests .beadloom/_graph/ before and after; a {ref_id: node} digest is the same walk), OR keep the file-grain digest as a deliberately coarser instrument and SAY so — rename wrote_the_failing_graph_file, correct invariant 3 to name the node, and add one case asserting the two grains coincide on this table, so the day they stop coinciding is the day it is noticed.

title: [BDL-UX #221][bug] attribution should key on a rule-relevant projection of the node, not on the whole node
description:
RE-PLANNED OUT OF BDL-067 by the beadloom-e8s4.26 reviewer's own recommendation, adopted 2026-09-02. NEEDS /task-init.

THE OPEN QUESTION, ANSWERED. 'Is a node whose docs: field this run wrote a node this run wrote?' — NO, not for this instrument, and the grain was never the axis that decides it.

The reviewer's reasoning, which is the specification: the instrument exists to answer one question — did this run produce the property that makes this node FAIL. The failing rule is domain-needs-parent, which reads `kind` and `part_of` edges. `docs:` is not a field any rule in the failing finding can see. A run that annotated a node did not write anything the rule read, so answering 'yes' attributes to Beadloom a failure Beadloom did not cause. Bead .23 moved from file to node believing the annotation was a property of the FILE; .24 measured that it is a property of the NODE as well and said so. The variable that separates the two cases is not how coarse the sample is — it is WHETHER THE PART OF THE NODE THAT CHANGED IS A PART THE RULE READS.

STILL MEASURED FAILING on the commonest shape: an inherited legacy.yml holding ONE undocumented orphan still prints (True, True) — 'This is a defect in Beadloom's bootstrap rather than in your project — please report it' — about a node no writer in this run produced. Single-node inherited graph files are at least as ordinary as the two-node case cycle 8 did close, so the cost is still paid by the adopter in a bug report and by this project in triage.

THE FIX, and it is deliberately NOT the option .23 rejected. Do not exempt a docs:-only diff — a filter over one field is the shape init_flow.py's own docstring argues against, and it goes stale the next time the block gains a writer. Instead key the node sample on a RULE-RELEVANT PROJECTION of the node, DERIVED rather than hand-listed: digest the node restricted to the fields the rule engine can read, taken from graph/rules/loader.py's own authoring surface. Then a docs:-only annotation is not a change the failing rule can see and the corner stops firing, while a kind, source or edge rewrite still reads as ours — so the error direction .24 insisted on (created-or-CHANGED, never created) is preserved rather than traded away.

PRECEDENT ALREADY IN THIS REPOSITORY: test_every_authoring_key_the_loader_accepts_has_a_type holds _detect_rule_type to graph.rules.loader.AUTHORING_KEYS, so a rule dimension added later widens the projection by the same act instead of leaving a filter behind. A rule that one day reads docs: would then make a docs:-only annotation attributable to this run — the right answer, and the one a hand-written exemption would get wrong.

NOT A DEFECT IN CYCLE 8'S EXECUTION, and the reviewer said so explicitly: .24 was told to implement a decision, implemented it, measured that the decision's stated outcome did not follow, refused to write that it had, and put the measurement in the class docstring. Filing this against that bead would punish exactly the behaviour that made it visible.

title: [BDL-UX #220][bug] `init` still tracebacks on an unparseable graph file — N readers across four domains, each with its own policy
description:
MEASURED BY beadloom-e8s4.24 AFTER its own fix, and pinned rather than fixed — the honest residue of BDL-067's major 3.

WHAT IS FIXED: the traceback beadloom-e8s4.21 introduced. doc_generator._load_graph_from_yaml no longer raises; the four readers of .beadloom/_graph/*.yml under onboarding/ + setup.py now share one skip policy (onboarding/scanner/graph_files.py::each_graph_file).

WHAT IS NOT: on a project carrying one hand-edited .beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml that does not parse, `beadloom init --bootstrap` STILL ends in yaml.parser.ParserError. The frame moved: application/reindex/indexing.py:63 read_declared_docs, reached from setup.py:1217 do_reindex. That reader is in ANOTHER DOMAIN, was reachable before .21, and is not alone — graph/loader.py:186, graph/diff.py:220, reindex/change_detection.py:89 and services/commands/index_ops.py:235 walk the same directory with their own policies.

So the class is: N readers of the adopter's graph directory across four domains, each with its own answer to 'what if this file does not parse'. BDL-067 consolidated the four inside onboarding and could not reach the rest without crossing domain boundaries mid-fix-cycle.

PINNED, NOT SILENT: tests/test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py::test_the_traceback_the_review_measured_is_gone_and_a_second_one_is_not asserts BOTH halves — the fixed frame is gone AND the second one is still there. It fails the day somebody closes indexing.py, so no future reader of this repository can take 'init no longer tracebacks' as true. The dev bead refused to write that sentence.

NEEDS /task-init: the fix is a policy decision spanning onboarding, application, graph and services — the same shape as beadloom-6i5q / BDL-UX #218, and for the same reason it is not a fix cycle. Decide once what every reader of a graph file does with one that will not parse, then apply it.

ADOPTER IMPACT, stated plainly because it is user-facing: a hand-edited or truncated file under .beadloom/_graph/ makes `beadloom init --bootstrap` print a Python traceback instead of a message. It predates BDL-067 and BDL-067 did not close it.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
FINDING from BDL-067 .25, measured while covering .24 — the class is wider than one shape and one branch, and a fix scoped to 'unreadable YAML' would close two thirds of it.

MEASURED over init's own entry-point-by-mode table (8 cells, derived from the command's source in tests/test_init_one_table_over_every_axis.py) crossed with three shapes of hand-edited .beadloom/_graph/legacy.yml. 24 runs, pinned in tests/test_graph_files_are_read_under_one_policy.py::TestWhatEveryBranchOfInitDoesWithAFileItCannotHandle.

 * SHAPE 1, a file that does not parse -> yaml.parser.ParserError in application/reindex/indexing.read_declared_docs (this is what .24 pinned, for --bootstrap only).
 * SHAPE 2, a file holding a top-level LIST -> AttributeError, same reader, on every branch. It parses fine and dies on data.get, so no 'except yaml.YAMLError' catches it.
 * SHAPE 3, NEW and not in this bead's title: 'added: 2026-09-02' loads as a datetime.date and dies in graph/loader.py::load_graph with TypeError (json.dumps with no default). This file is NOT unreadable — onboarding.graph_files.each_graph_file yields it happily and every one of init's own four readers is fine with it — so a fix that only guards parsing leaves it open.

BRANCH COVERAGE: --bootstrap, --import and all three wizard modes traceback on all three shapes. --yes does not, on any shape, and not because a guard works: non_interactive_init returns 'skipped' when .beadloom/ already exists, so the file is never read. With --force the directory is deleted first. So the branch axis adds nothing to the diagnosis — every branch that reads the tree reaches the same two unguarded readers, which is why this is one decision and not four.

The pinned cases fail the day this bead closes, which is deliberate: they carry the measurement so the fix is checked against the whole class rather than against the one traceback the review of BDL-067 .23 reported.

title: [BDL-UX #218][bug] `init` holds three hand-written step sequences and no artifact states what the sequence is
description:
RE-PLANNED OUT OF BDL-067 by owner decision 2026-09-02, on the seventh review's diagnosis. NEEDS /task-init AND AN RFC BEFORE ANY CODE — the fix is a change to init's control flow, not a patch, and appending it as cycle 8 of a bug fix is exactly what the re-plan rule ranked P0 in the ROADMAP exists to prevent.

THE DIAGNOSIS, quoted from beadloom-e8s4.23:

  'Every instrument this epic has built ranges over ONE symbol's callers. Nothing ranges over one entry point's STEPS. init holds three hand-written step sequences — the --bootstrap branch inline in setup.py, non_interactive_init, interactive_init — and no artifact states what the sequence is. So the next divergence was a step that two sequences run and the third does not, and a step that runs once over one writer's output and is never revisited. Both were reachable through the whole epic; six reviews and two derived enumerators did not see them, because the question "which steps does this entry point run" has never been asked of the source.'

And its verdict on the approach: '.21's three fixes are each correct and each is the LAST FIX OF ITS KIND that a per-symbol enumeration can produce.'

THREE MEASURED INSTANCES:
 - MAJOR 1: auto_link_docs is run by two of the three entry points; doc-sync is off on the third.
 - MAJOR 2: generate_rules is the second whole-graph artifact rendered from ONE writer's node list.
 - MINOR (same root cause, named as such by the reviewer): setup.py:1210 — --bootstrap honours neither the existing-.beadloom check nor --force, unlike --yes, so it re-bootstraps over an existing graph silently.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN WORK ITEM: BDL-067 fixed six instances of 'a statement scoped to one shape while a neighbouring shape exists' and, on the seventh pass, the class moved from symbols to sequences. Fixing sequences means declaring what init's sequence IS — one artifact the three entry points share, or derive from — and that is a design decision about the command, with an RFC and an Axes section, not a fix cycle.

Review counts by pass on BDL-067, as the evidence that iteration had stopped paying: 2, 1, 1, 3, 4, 3, 5.

title: [BDL-UX #219][bug] the review's withholding does not cover commit messages, which is where this project writes its accounts
description:
FOUND AND DECLARED BY THE beadloom-e8s4.23 REVIEWER, unprompted. The second structural defeat of the same mechanism; #212 was the first.

THE FINDING, quoted:

  'git log main..HEAD on this branch carries the author's full account in the commit bodies — .21's and .22's messages are longer and more specific than any bead comment would be, including .22's explicit "FINDING for .23". Any reviewer who follows step 3 of the protocol (git diff <base>...HEAD) is one command away from them. The withholding mechanism covers bead comments and does not cover commit messages, which is where this project actually writes its accounts.'

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN #212. #212 was a coordinator handing over ACTIVE.md — fixable by changing the launch prompt, and it was. This one is not reachable by prompt discipline: the review protocol itself tells the reviewer to read the diff, and this project deliberately writes long, specific commit bodies. The better the commit message, the more completely the withholding is defeated.

review-brief reports '0 comments withheld' and is correct about bead comments while the account is fully available one command away. A number that is right about its own scope and wrong about the question the reader is asking is the class this repository exists to remove.

EXPECTED, and the choice is a decision rather than a patch:
 (a) review-brief also withholds or summarises commit bodies on the reviewed range, and says how many it withheld;
 (b) the mechanism stops claiming to withhold and instead REPORTS what is reachable, so the reviewer can declare it — which is what both the .16 and .23 reviewers did unprompted and is the only reason either leak is known;
 (c) accept it: independence on a re-review is not worth the cost, and the first pass is the only one where it matters.

RELATED: #212 (defeated through ACTIVE.md, fixed by prompt), #204 (review-brief reports '0 withheld' and cannot know what the coordinator's prompt contained). All three are the same shape: an instrument that measures its own scope and is read as measuring the question.

title: [BDL-UX #217][bug] an earlier `init --mode import` leaves domains that no later run will parent
description:
FOUND AND NAMED BY beadloom-e8s4.17 as its own stated limit, reported rather than absorbed — the same treatment the beadloom-e8s4.16 review gave major 4.

THE GAP. .17 made the verdict tree-level: every init branch that writes a graph file takes it, and attribution comes from a digest of .beadloom/_graph/ taken before any writer and again at verdict time. That removes the REASON for the --mode import carve-out rather than the check. What it does NOT do is parent the nodes an EARLIER --mode import run already left in imported.yml.

So the sequence the beadloom-e8s4.16 review measured is narrowed, not closed: an import-only run followed later by a bootstrap on the same tree still meets domain nodes that no run of this command parented. The report now names them honestly — it prints 'the graph already in .beadloom/_graph/' and asks for no bug report — but the graph is still one the adopter has to repair by hand.

WHY .17 STOPPED THERE, and the reason is worth keeping: making the bootstrap parent nodes it did not write means REWRITING A GRAPH FILE THE ADOPTER MAY HAVE AUTHORED. Every other fix in BDL-067 constrains what Beadloom writes about its own output; this one would have Beadloom edit an existing graph on the adopter's disk. That is a different kind of act and it deserves a decision rather than a fix cycle.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD NEEDS, before any code:
  (a) parent the orphans on a later run — structurally complete, and it edits a file the adopter may own;
  (b) report them and stop — honest, and leaves the adopter a manual repair with no reminder;
  (c) parent only nodes carrying provenance that Beadloom wrote them — needs provenance the graph does not record today.

This is the same shape as the (a)/(b) choice the owner decided for #192 itself on 2026-08-31, one layer out.

Recorded in the code, in two documents and in beadloom-e8s4.17's checkpoint 2 as a stated limit, so it is visible rather than silent.

title: [BDL-UX #215][bug] the Gate reports an index problem as a rules configuration error
description:
FOUND BY THE beadloom-e8s4.12 SWEEP, reported rather than fixed — the fourth instance of the class BDL-067 kept finding, and the first one outside init.

application/gate.py:242-248 stamps summary=RULES_CONFIG_ERROR on ALL THREE LintError raise sites in graph/linter.py. Two of them are INDEX problems, not rules problems.

MEASURED on a scratch adopter with a VALID rules.yml and no index:

    beadloom ci --no-reindex   ->  "lint FAIL: rules configuration error"
                                   while the same run's "why" field carries "index not found at ..."

So the headline names a file that is fine and the detail names the real cause. An adopter reads the headline.

The same prose appears in src/beadloom/application/gate.py:61, docs/domains/application/README.md and docs/domains/application/features/ci-gate/SPEC.md:23 — so the wrong summary is documented as the behaviour, which is how it survives review.

CLASS: a user-facing message asserting a fact the code knows to be false. BDL-067 found three instances inside init — a comment counting monkeypatch bindings and calling them branches; a message blaming Beadloom for the adopter's own rules; a withdrawal claiming a rule failed where none was evaluated. Each arrived the same way: careful reasoning about one shape, not carried across to the neighbouring shape. This is the same defect one layer up, in the Gate that every adopter runs.

FIX SHAPE: the summary must name what actually failed. Distinguish the rules-parse raise site from the index raise sites in graph/linter.py, or have gate.py derive the summary from the raise rather than stamping one constant on all three. Correct the two documents in the same change — they currently certify the defect.

FILED SEPARATELY from BDL-067 by the same reasoning the owner applied to BDL-UX #214 on 2026-08-31: a different defect, a different surface, and it deserves its own measurement rather than a line at the end of another PR.

title: [BDL-UX #214][bug] bootstrap writes two nodes with the same ref_id on the classic Python src-layout, and one is silently dropped
description:
MEASURED BY THE beadloom-e8s4.4 REVIEWER on a fresh 'ledger' project laid out as src/ledger/ — the standard Python src-layout:

    beadloom init --yes --mode bootstrap  ->  rc 0   Graph: 2 nodes, 0 edges
    services.yml holds TWO nodes with ref_id 'ledger' — one kind=service (the root), one kind=domain
    the loader keeps ONE
    lint --strict  ->  domain-needs-parent:rule_liveness:warn
    ci             ->  rc 0

NOT A REGRESSION and NOT caused by beadloom-e8s4.1: pre-fix behaviour is identical. The .1 invariant deliberately carves out a domain whose ref_id equals the root's (bootstrap.py:69), because a self-edge is not a parent — that carve-out is correct. The defect is upstream of it: the root ref_id comes from _detect_project_name (pyproject/package.json name) and the domain ref_id comes from the source directory, and on src/<project>/ those are the same string.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the most common Python layout there is, and the failure is silent — the graph loses a node, the rule goes inert rather than failing, and ci stays green. A green that describes the loader discarding a node is the exact class this project exists to remove.

FIX SHAPE: unique ref_ids, not an edge. Disambiguate the domain (or the root) when the two collide, and make a duplicate ref_id in a generated graph something the writer refuses rather than something the loader silently resolves.

FOUND: 2026-08-31, during the BDL-067 review. Filed separately by owner decision rather than folded into BDL-067, whose approved brief is about a missing edge.

title: [BDL-063] Speech style guide for all four roles — shipped as data, configurable, machine-checked
description:
SCOPE WIDENED BY OWNER DECISION 2026-08-28. The bead was filed as a style guide for the tech-writer role. It now covers ALL FOUR ROLES -- dev, test, review, tech-writer -- and must serve the Goose+Qwen tech-writer as well as the Claude/Cursor adapters. It ships with Beadloom and the end user can configure it.

WHY ALL FOUR. Every role emits text a human reads: bead comments and checkpoints, review findings, commit messages, PR bodies, API CHANGE notes. Today only prose in documentation is even nominally held to a standard, and that standard is one table row in the CORE tech-writer role: "Verbose prose | Concise, technical descriptions".

THE ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT, and it is the whole design. The style guide must reach a Claude markdown role adapter AND a Goose recipe AND a machine check. So it CANNOT live as prose inside .claude/agents/*.md. It has to be DATA that all three consume -- the roadmap's own principle 5, a canonical source composed into thin adapters. Prose in a role file is what BDL-065 measured failing: the word "проза" was rejected by the owner on 2026-08-27, agreed by the coordinator, and then written again by Qwen the same day, because the rejection lived in a session and nowhere a second writer could read it.

WHAT THE DATA HOLDS, and each item is measurable:
  - forbidden words, scoped by language. Already earned, RU: проза, популяция, базовая линия, объявленная поверхность, застава, знаменатель, матчер, субстрат, примитив.
  - the half-stated construction: an intensifier with no contrast named, a transitive verb with no object, a comparative with no second term. One diagnosis, three parses, one message: NAME THE OTHER HALF.
  - antithesis density, and the sharper signal, a paragraph ENDING on one.
  - semicolons in prose: zero.
  - em-dash density in FLOWING prose only. Definition dashes in bullet lists are correct Russian typography and counting them inflated the README diagnosis from 56 to 98.
  - internal jargon leaking into reader-facing text, against a project-declared list.

WHAT STAYS PROSE IN THE ROLE, because it is judgement: a heading promises a result rather than a thesis; a term is explained where first needed; N instances of one idea is a table; explain through consequence, not internal mechanism; do not invent precision.

CONFIGURABLE BY THE END USER. Shipped defaults plus a project layer, the same shape as .beadloom/flow/. A project must be able to add its own forbidden words and its own jargon list without editing the shipped core, and those additions must survive an upgrade.

THRESHOLDS ARE NOT SHIPPED AS ABSOLUTES. The coordinator set "no more than three antitheses" and it was wrong within the hour: five of the nine remaining carried real meaning and removing them would have cost precision. Ship the dial, keep our values in our config.

WARN, NOT ERROR, ON FIRST SHIP. Measured on the README sweep: seven intensifier hits, five legitimate. A rule that forces a writer to strip meaning is a rule they disable.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT PRETEND TO DO. It cannot judge whether Russian reads naturally. Measured twice in one session: the four style metrics caught ZERO of the twelve corrections the owner made to README.ru.md, and the coordinator then defended a construction ("Красить конвейер на обновлении") that the owner rejected as not being Russian at all. The check catches what can be counted. Natural language is judged by a native speaker, and after BDL-065 the first draft is written by a model with the language.

TARGET 3.1.0, not a patch: editing a CORE role template changes what setup-agentic-flow composes in every adopter's repository.

comments.author: coordinator
comments.text:
PATTERN FOUND WHILE REWRITING README.ru.md — the owner rejected the same construction three separate times in one session, so it is a class, not three slips.

THE HALF-STATED ANTITHESIS. The writer holds a contrast in mind and puts only one half of it on the page. The reader gets an emphatic qualifier with nothing to weigh it against:

  'это третье состояние, А НЕ ВЕЖЛИВЫЙ СИНОНИМ одного из двух других'
  'печатали то же слово, что и НАСТОЯЩИЙ успех'
  'порог входа здесь НАСТОЯЩИЙ'

Owner's verdict on the first, verbatim: 'какая-то галлюцинация... что это за бред'. On the third: 'снова звучит как бред'. That reaction is the signal -- the sentence is not wrong, it is unreadable, because the contrast it leans on was never written down.

Distinct from the plain 'X, а не Y' antithesis already in this bead. There BOTH halves are present and the objection is frequency. Here ONE half is missing and the objection is comprehension. Different defect, different fix, and the second is worse: frequency makes prose tiring, a missing half makes it meaningless.

MECHANICALLY DETECTABLE, which is why it belongs in the check rather than only in the role prose: an intensifier ('настоящий', 'вежливый', 'просто', 'обычный', 'сам по себе') qualifying a noun with no contrasting term named in the same sentence. Needs tuning to avoid false positives on ordinary emphatic use, so it likely ships warn-only and per-language.

Root cause worth recording: every one of the three came from a coordinator brief where the contrast WAS spelled out over many messages. In the README the reader has none of that context. This is the same failure as the jargon leak already recorded on this bead -- text that is complete for its author and incomplete for anyone else -- and it is the strongest argument for checking reader-facing docs by machine rather than by the author rereading their own words.

comments.text:
AMENDMENT to the half-stated-antithesis note above: the pattern is WIDER than the intensifier form I recorded, and a check built only for intensifiers would miss half of it.

Fourth instance, caught minutes later, different grammar:

  'тем больше Beadloom ВОЗВРАЩАЕТ.'   <- transitive verb, object never named. Returns WHAT?

So the four rejected sentences split into two grammatical families:

  (a) intensifier with no contrast named   'настоящий', 'вежливый синоним', 'настоящий успех'
  (b) transitive verb with no object named 'возвращает'

The common property is neither grammar nor vocabulary. It is: THE SENTENCE OPENS A SLOT AND NEVER FILLS IT. The author fills it silently from context the reader does not have.

That reframing matters for the check's design. Do not encode a list of constructions -- encode the slot. Candidate detections, all cheap: a transitive verb ending a clause with no object; a comparative ('больше', 'сильнее', 'быстрее') with no second term; an intensifying adjective with no contrast in the sentence. Each is a different parse, one diagnosis, one message to the writer: NAME THE OTHER HALF.

Also worth carrying into the role prose, because it explains WHY an author cannot self-catch this: rereading your own sentence, you supply the missing half from memory and it reads fine. Every one of these four survived my own rereading and was caught by the owner on first contact. A writer proofreading their own text is structurally the wrong instrument for this defect -- which is the same argument as REPORTS ARE NOT EVIDENCE, applied to prose.

title: [BDL-062] .10 dev: the review's cheap true fixes, including two that damage our own verification
description:
Five minor findings from .6 that are corrections rather than decisions. Two of them attack the apparatus this project verifies WITH, which is why they land before the release rather than after.

m6 (tests/test_ai_techwriter_seams.py:85,91) -- run_command(['python', ...]) instead of sys.executable. Two failures in any clean room whose venv is not on PATH, unrelated to whatever is under test. A clean room's greenness is currently PATH-sensitive, and the release process verifies in a clean room.

m4 (test_guards_parity.py::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation) -- NOT intermittent. The reviewer measured 3 failures in 4 consecutive runs with a plain beadloom lint running concurrently, and a pass once it stopped. It digests .beads/issues.jsonl and the live index, so any concurrent bd call reddens it. It cost .5 a lost failure identity today. Fix it to be concurrency-safe or quarantine it explicitly -- the reviewer disagrees with leaving it as is and so do I. A test that fails for reasons unrelated to the code teaches agents to ignore red.

m2 (summary_facts.py:215-218) -- the not_applicable.get fallback is unreachable: FACT_KEYWORDS and the registry's declare/decline sets are the same 9 names, set difference empty both ways. NO CALLER NO CAPABILITY: delete it or make it reachable, and say which.

m1 (summary_facts.py:270-282 + types.py:553-563) -- _unverifiable goes through liveness_finding which hardcodes from_ref_id=None, while _disagreement sets from_ref_id=claim.ref_id. Same rule, same node: a machine consumer can attribute a disagreement and cannot attribute an unverifiable claim.

m5 (test_gate_three_states.py:257) -- assert '18' not in line and '43' not in line pins Beadloom's current MCP tool and CLI command counts as literals. When either moves the assertion silently stops guarding the leak it was written for. Derive them from MCP_TOOL_CATALOG / the CLI group, or drop them -- the set-membership assertion above is what does the work.

NOT in scope: M2/M3/M5 and m3 are decisions with trade-offs and ship as BDL-UX #201/#202/#203. M1/M4/m7 are documentation and belong to .7.

comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 5 major

WITHHOLDING DEFEATED BEFORE I RAN. My launch prompt carried the authors' accounts in
detail — .4's "14 corrections, none of the 9 self-lint tests edited", .5's "113 JSON parses
across 49 files, git diff -U0 with zero non-stream lines", .5's two self-caught neutered-
passing tests, .9's severity fix, the #198 clean-room amendment with its 363/363 numbers, and
#199/#200 by number. review-brief reports "0 author comment(s) withheld"; in practice the
account arrived through the prompt instead. I am the only party that can see this, so it is on
the record: several of my checks below are verifications of stated claims rather than
independent discoveries. The findings I did derive independently are marked DERIVED.

--release also could not establish that the verdict was recorded by anyone other than the
bead's author — every role writes under one tracker identity here. Reported, not filed.

WHAT I MEASURED

CLEAN ROOM, built to the amended rule. `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a scratch dir,
`git init` + one commit inside it, `uv sync` so the room runs its OWN `src/` rather than the
editable install on PATH. 1021 files — the whole tree at HEAD, not one bead's slice.

  beadloom ci rc 0
  ::notice::sync-check PASS: 363 pair(s) fresh; declared surface grew 344 -> 363 pair(s)
  lint --strict rc 0 · doctor rc 0 · ruff clean · mypy: no issues in 225 source files
  7259 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed

Quoting the sync-check line, not the exit code: 363 fresh, 0 NOT VERIFIED. Green in a clean
room over 1021 files.

One caveat worth passing on. The room first reported 2 failures —
test_ai_techwriter_seams.py::test_run_command_invokes_real_subprocess and its sibling — which
spawn `"python"` from PATH (tests/test_ai_techwriter_seams.py:85,91) instead of
sys.executable. Unchanged on this branch; they pass once the room's venv is on PATH. A clean
room's greenness is PATH-sensitive today, which is the same shape as the git-work-tree
artifact and worth knowing before the next clean-room claim.

--- MAJOR ---

M1. docs/domains/graph/README.md:145 · Major · DERIVED
Issue: the bullet says liveness findings are "Always `warn` — a liveness finding is about the
configuration, not the code, so nothing green turns red on upgrade". That is false since `.9`,
and it contradicts line 117 OF THE SAME FILE, which `.9` rewrote in the same commit to say a
total stand-down carries the declared severity. Measured: c9f8325 changes exactly one line
(1 insertion, 1 deletion) in this file and does not touch line 145. This repository escalates
`doc-area-coherence` to `error`, so the sentence misdescribes live behaviour here today.
`.9`'s own note says it swept architecture.md, rule-engine/SPEC.md and services/cli.md for this
sentence and "had to find two by grep" — the grep missed the fourth occurrence, in the file it
was editing.
Recommendation: replace "Always `warn`" with the partial/total split already written at
line 117 and cross-reference it. Also check rule-engine/SPEC.md:886, whose "**Always `warn`.**"
heading is now a partial truth (the assertion under it is still correct).

M2. src/beadloom/graph/linter.py:459-480 · Major · DERIVED
Issue: `--format porcelain` emits no `message`, and porcelain is the format `lint` SELECTS BY
DEFAULT when stdout is not a terminal — i.e. what every pipe, script and CI capture gets.
Measured on a real adopter project I built from scratch (not a fixture: warehouse-svc, own
pyproject, own graph, `beadloom init -y --mode bootstrap`, run with the clean room's binary),
`summary_facts` declared at `severity: error`:

  state A — total stand-down, 0 of 5 summaries checked:
      summary-facts:rule_liveness:warn::::
  state B — 2 of 5 checked, one claim unverifiable:
      summary-facts:rule_liveness:warn::::

Byte-identical. This is the FOURTH instance of the class, after #198 (sync-check), #199 (the
Gate line) and #197 (the severity half). It is the worst-placed of the four because it is the
default machine path, and because it discards the whole of `.1`/`.2`/`.9`'s denominator work:
the population clause, the registry's verbatim decline reason and the remediation all exist and
none of them survives the formatter. `doc-area` at `error` renders as
`doc-area:rule_liveness:error::::` — a rule name, a type and a severity, and nothing that says
which of the three states it is.
Recommendation: open a BDL-UX issue and decide it, do not patch it blind. The cheapest honest
fix is a seventh field carrying the message (the format is already colon-delimited and already
gained `severity` in position three without ceremony). Not release-blocking by the standard
`.9` applied to #199: severity survives and `--strict` still exits 1, so this is an ambiguous
line, not a false verdict.

M3. src/beadloom/graph/rules/summary_facts.py:57 · Major · DERIVED
Issue: `from beadloom.doc_sync import DocScanner, FactRegistry, FactSet, compare_facts` is a
module-level peer domain import. It is resolved in the index (`code_imports` has the row), and
`edges` has no `graph -> doc-sync` row. Measured: `beadloom why doc-sync` lists doc-shape,
doc-quality, docs-audit and sync-check as dependents and does NOT list `graph`. So a feature
whose thesis is "graph metadata is an unchecked surface" left the graph wrong about its own
dependency structure, and the one command the workflow tells every agent to run for impact
under-reports the blast radius of a change to `DocScanner.scan_line`, `FactSet` or
`compare_facts` — the three seams `.1` deliberately reused rather than forked.
`.1`'s justification names `graph -> context_oracle` as precedent. That precedent is a second
undeclared peer import (import_resolver.py:15), not a warrant for a third.
Recommendation: declare `graph -> doc-sync` (and `graph -> context-oracle`) as `uses` edges so
`why` and `lint` can see them; or invert via an infrastructure port, which this codebase already
does for exactly this "a lower layer needs a higher layer's surface" problem in
`surface_registry`. Either is fine. Leaving the graph silent about it is the one option the
feature's own argument forbids.

M4. docs/architecture.md:387 and :380 · Major · DERIVED
Issue: line 387 reads "Rules support 7 authoring keys: `deny`, `require`, `forbid`, `layers`,
`forbid_cycles`, `forbid_import`, `check`". Measured: `loader.AUTHORING_KEYS` holds 12, and
line 133 of THIS FILE was corrected from "the ten authoring keys" to "the 12 authoring keys" by
`.4` this morning (746e0b9). The same fact, 254 lines apart in one document, corrected in one
place and left in the other. Line 380 has the same shape: "supports 9 languages:" followed by
ten language names, and "(16 file extensions total)" against `_CODE_EXTENSIONS` of 18
(application/reindex/models.py:57-78).
Both pre-exist on `main`, so this is not a regression. It is a gap in the correction pass whose
stated purpose was this exact class, and `.4`'s own note ("architecture.md:133 had TWO stale
numbers, not one") shows the file was read closely enough that a grep for the same claim would
have been cheap.
Recommendation: fix both lines, and grep the file for every remaining bare count before the
release rather than trusting `docs audit` — neither number is bound to a fact, so no check will
ever report them.

M5. application/doctor.py:529 vs doc_sync/audit.py:1013-1033 · Major · DERIVED
Issue: one `beadloom ci` run prints two different numbers for "CLI commands" under one name.
`doctor` prints "CLI has 34 commands registered" (top-level only); the audit computes
`cli_command_count: 43` (`_count_click_commands` recurses into groups). Both call it CLI
commands with no qualifier, and `docs/domains/doc-sync/README.md:95` states 43 and is verified
OK, so a reader of `doctor` and a reader of the audit get contradicting facts from the same run.
This is #193 exactly — "two unrelated meanings collide under one fact name" — which `.4`
resolved for `framework_count` by renaming it `nodes_with_framework`. The sibling was not looked
for. `language_count` is a third of the same family (computes 1, means "languages in this
project's index", while the docs use the phrase for "languages the tool parses"), already
recorded in the log as unverifiable but not as a naming defect.
Recommendation: make `doctor` say "top-level commands" or count recursively, and sweep the fact
registry once for names whose prose meaning differs from what they compute.

--- MINOR ---

m1. graph/rules/summary_facts.py:270-282 + types.py:553-563 · Minor · DERIVED
`_unverifiable` goes through `liveness_finding`, which hardcodes `from_ref_id=None`, while
`_disagreement` sets `from_ref_id=claim.ref_id`. Same rule, same node: a machine consumer can
attribute a disagreement and cannot attribute an unverifiable claim. Measured on the adopter,
the finding naming `warehouse-packing` in its prose carries `"from_ref_id": null`. The
unverifiable state is structurally poorer than pass and fail, which is the epic's own class in
miniature. Fix: give `liveness_finding` an optional `from_ref_id`, same shape as `.9` gave it
`severity`.

m2. graph/rules/summary_facts.py:215-218 · Minor · DERIVED — NO CALLER NO CAPABILITY
The `not_applicable.get(name, "`{name}` is not a fact this project declares")` fallback is
unreachable. Measured: `DocScanner.FACT_KEYWORDS` and the registry's declare/decline sets are
the SAME 9 names (set difference empty in both directions), every collector writes `facts` or
`declined`, and `_collect_extra_facts` only ever writes `facts`. Grep: the string appears once
in the whole repository, in that line — no test, no doc, no caller. A fifth sub-state that is
coded and cannot be reached. Fix: drop it, or make it reachable and test it.

m3. graph/rules/doc_area.py:262-280 and :83-91 · Minor · DERIVED
I ran the mutation testing `.5` did not. Eight mutations against the clean room; six killed,
two survived the FULL suite (the 2 residual failures under each are a hash artifact —
`TestSyncCheckNewPairs` goes red for any edit to a file in a sync pair, confirmed with a
comment-only control):
  M2 `_area_depth` tie-break flipped from shallower to deeper — 7257 passed, 0 behavioural kills
  M7 `_normalise` hyphen/underscore folding removed  — 7257 passed, 0 behavioural kills
Both are behaviours the docstrings state a rationale for and no test observes. M7 is the more
interesting: folding is not load-bearing on this repository because the rule learns a per-area
MAPPING rather than asserting equality, so `doc_sync -> doc-sync` is dominant either way. That
is worth knowing before someone deletes the line as dead.
Killed for the record: silent-count falsified (1), identity gate always matches (11),
min_support guard dropped (8), inert_reason always live (4), the two audit populations merged
(2), per-claim unverifiable reworded as the stand-down (2).

m4. tests/test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::
test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation · Minor · DERIVED
Not intermittent. It fails RELIABLY: measured 3 failures in 4 consecutive runs with a plain
`beadloom lint --project .` running concurrently on the same repository, and 1 pass once the
lint loop finished. It hashes four LIVE shared files it does not own — `.beadloom/beadloom.db`,
`-wal`, `-shm`, `.beads/issues.jsonl` — and this project's declared model is concurrent waves on
one working tree with every agent writing the tracker. `.5` was right to record the identity as
lost rather than call it flaky, and right that its own `bd` activity could redden it. My
judgement on the question asked: it cannot survive concurrent waves as written, and it will keep
costing sessions — worse, it teaches agents to read a red there as "concurrency", which is the
habit that would hide a real read-only violation. The property it wants is already proved in
isolation by its sibling `test_evaluating_every_guard_changes_nothing_but_the_firing_record`;
what this one adds is the real probes. Fix: copy the live index into `tmp_path` and run the real
probes against the copy, and drop `.beads/issues.jsonl` from the tracked set entirely — no guard
writes the tracker, so it contributes all of the flakiness and none of the coverage.

m5. tests/test_gate_three_states.py:257 · Minor · DERIVED
`assert "18" not in line and "43" not in line` pins Beadloom's current MCP tool and CLI command
counts as literals. When either moves the assertion silently stops guarding the leak it was
written for, and nothing will say so. The first assertion in that test (`{"mcp_tool_count",

`MCP_TOOL_CATALOG`/the CLI group, or drop them.

m6. tests/test_ai_techwriter_seams.py:85,91 · Minor · pre-existing
`run_command(["python", ...])` instead of `sys.executable`. Two failures in any clean room whose

The docstring states the porcelain format as `rule_name:rule_type:file_path:line:from_ref:to_ref`.

The bead table still shows `.5` and `.6` as `blocked` and `.9` as done, and the progress log has
no `.5` entry although `.5` closed and committed four times. Coordinator's, not a bead's.

--- THE THREE CLAIMS I WAS ASKED TO CHECK ---

C1. NO CALLER NO CAPABILITY on the unverifiable paths — BOTH REACHABLE, verified on a real
project with no fixture. warehouse-svc: own pyproject, three source areas, `beadloom init -y
--mode bootstrap`, the two rules declared at `severity: error`, linted with the clean room's own
binary. Both paths produced user-visible output:

  summary-facts | rule_liveness | warn | Rule 'summary-facts' could not be verified for
  `warehouse-packing`: its summary states mcp_tool_count 18, and this project declares no value
  to check it against — the MCP tool catalog describes the running beadloom package, not this
  project (this project declares itself as 'warehouse-svc', not 'beadloom'); declare
  docs_audit.extra_facts.mcp_tool_count in .beadloom/config.yml to audit this project's own.

  doc-area | rule_liveness | ERROR | Rule 'doc-area' checked nothing: no node/doc pair yields a

  and 3 have a doc path with no segment at the depth this project names areas.

The `.3` identity gate's reason crosses the seam verbatim into `.1`'s rule on a foreign project,
which is the whole contract, and `.9`'s severity escalation reaches the reader at `error`.
`lint`'s rich summary reads "3 rules evaluated, 1 of them unable to check anything" —
`rules_inert` counts the total stand-down and correctly does NOT count the per-claim
unverifiable. Coded is reachable. The one exception is m2 above.

C2. THE TWO CHECKABLE CLAIMS — BOTH HOLD, one file-count off by one.
`.4`: none of the 9 self-lint tests was edited by `.4`. `git log main..HEAD` on
test_integration_v1.py, test_s3_decomposition.py, test_module_coverage_hardening.py and
test_bead15_s3b_coverage.py names only a97caca, which is `.5`'s stream sweep. 746e0b9 and
875947f touch none of them. The 9 went green by the corrections.
`.5`: 113 removed `.output` lines across 48 files (claim says 49), and every single removed line
is a `json.loads(...)`/`_json.loads(...)` — no other `.output` use was touched. 48 of those 48
files have a diff containing NOTHING but the swap. The remaining changed files in a97caca are
four new files plus the tracker export, which cannot contain removed lines. Residual on HEAD:
three `json.loads(result.output)` strings, all inside test_cli_json_streams.py's own detector
fixtures. The AST guard is real and recognises five spellings.

C3. A FOURTH COLLAPSE — FOUND. See M2. Also m1, which is the same class one layer lower: the
`unverifiable` verdict loses the node identity that `disagrees` keeps.

--- THE OTHER FOUR QUESTIONS ---

Q4, a third neutered-passing test: I did not find a third test that PASSES under neutering of
what it names. I found two behaviours with no test at all (m3). Different defect, lower severity
— a missing test reports nothing, and `.5`'s two were tests reporting green. On the evidence
`.5`'s sweep was thorough.

Q5, the attestations: RECORDED, BUT THE JUDGEMENT WAS NOT MADE OVER THE WHOLE DOCUMENT, and M1
is the proof. `.1` attested `domains/graph/README.md <-> graph/scenarios.py`; `scenarios.py` is
unchanged on this branch, the pair went stale only because the README moved, and the README's
scenarios prose is still accurate — so that particular attestation is defensible. The structural
problem is what M1 exposes: that README was edited by `.2`, `.1` and `.9` and attested through
the feature, and it carries a sentence made false by `.9` twenty-eight lines below the line `.9`
changed. Attestation is being used as a hash re-baseline with a claim attached, and the claim
("a human-equivalent judgement checked this") is not true of the document as a whole. That is
not a reason to remove attestation — it is a reason to scope it. An attestation over a
900-line README is a promise nobody can keep.

Q6, the parity test: see m4. It cannot survive concurrent waves, and I disagree with leaving it
as is.

Q7, the mutation gap: it mattered less than it might have, and it did matter. `.1` ran 12 hand
neuterings, `.9` four, `.2` an AST layout-literal guard; my eight-mutation run killed six,
including every headline behaviour. What the missing run would have added is precisely m3 — the
supporting decisions nobody thought to neuter because they are not the headline. Low yield, real,
and cheap enough that it should become routine rather than a bead-by-bead choice.

--- WHAT SHOULD BLOCK ---

Nothing here blocks the release, and I want to be explicit rather than hedge. M1 is a one-line
correction of a false sentence about the behaviour this release changes, so I would fix it in
the release commit rather than defer it. M4 is two stale numbers in the primary architecture
document and is also a minutes-long fix. M2, M3 and M5 are decisions, not typos: each has a real
trade-off, none produces a false verdict, and shipping them as recorded BDL-UX issues with the
measurements above is the honest move. `.9` blocked correctly earlier today because `lint
--strict` exited 0 while a blocking rule checked nothing. Nothing I found has that shape.

title: [BDL-062] .2 dev: doc_area_coherence — convention derived from the graph, never hardcoded
description:

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: doc-area-coherence.

WHAT. A node should document itself where its own graph says nodes like it are documented. src/beadloom/graph/rules/doc_area.py derives the convention from the indexed graph (nodes.source JOIN docs.path) and names the nodes that contradict it. NO layout literal anywhere: the source area is the segment below the longest common prefix of every node source; the docs area is the segment at the derived AREA DEPTH.

DECISIONS.
1. Two-pass depth derivation, not vocabulary matching. The first cut located the docs area by matching each doc segment against the source-area names. That made drift INTO a directory naming no source area invisible - the commonest shape of the defect, and a scenario caught it before the code shipped. Now pass 1 asks each doc path where in it a source area is named and takes the modal depth; pass 2 reads THAT depth on every doc path, whatever the segment is called there.
2. Not the RFC's 'segment below the docs root'. A docs root cannot be derived by common prefix here: architecture.md sits at the docs root and collapses the prefix to empty, which would make the compared segment the domains/services bucket - precisely the segment that cannot disagree.
3. min_support added (default 2). Without it every area holding one documented node is unanimous at one observation and PLAN's 'graph of six nodes' reports a clean sweep having compared nothing. threshold <= 0.5 and min_support < 2 are rejected by the loader: both are configuration that reads as a rule and behaves as a silence.
4. unverifiable is its own state. Zero dominant mappings -> a rule_liveness finding saying 'checked nothing' plus the reason, AND the rule is counted in LintResult.rules_inert so the gate line reads 'N of them unable to check anything'. Counted by liveness.py through doc_area_inert_reason, reported by doc_area.py - the same split scenario_coverage uses, so the count cannot drift from the control flow.
5. Ships warn; this repository sets error in .beadloom/_graph/rules.yml (severity is a per-rule field there, not in config.yml).

MEASURED HERE. 83 node/doc pairs; 3 rootless (the package-root node), 3 with no segment at the area depth (services/{cli,mcp,tui}.md); 77 compared, all under a dominant mapping; 73 agree, 4 DIFFER: debt-report, doctor, reindex, watcher - all src/beadloom/application/... documented under domains/infrastructure/.... Exactly the four the bead names, at severity error. The bead's 69/73 baseline differs by the 7 domain-README pairs plus the 3 short services docs; the four violations are identical under either sample.

TESTS. 21 in tests/test_doc_area_coherence.py, 3 executable scenarios in tests/acceptance/features/doc_area_coherence.feature (RED first: ImportError on DocAreaCoherenceRule, captured). BITE PROVED by five neuterings, each captured on first sight: ignore min_support -> 2 fail; silence the unverifiable branch -> 5 fail; drop the liveness branch -> the 2 gate-line tests fail; introduce a 'domains' literal -> the AST layout-literal scan fails; replace the derived depth with vocabulary-first-match -> 3 fail.

OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-26: this is a MAJOR, not 2.3.0.

WHY, and the second reason is the one that decided it:
  (a) By semver it is breaking. `sync-check` now FAILS where it passed - a declared doc that is gone is `missing`, exit 2, and an adopter whose project is green today with a deleted doc goes red. `sync-update <ref>` no longer attests the whole ref by default, so a script relying on it now silently does LESS. `DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` went 7 -> 9, so `setup-branch-protection` requires a different set.
  (b) This is the release of a tool that spent an entire epic on 'do not claim more than you did'. Numbering a behaviour-changing release as a minor would be that same failure, in the version number.

WHAT TO DO:
- `src/beadloom/__init__.py` 2.2.0 -> 3.0.0. Check whether any other file states the version; `.87` measured that `get_actual_version()` reads `beadloom.__version__` and that #183's leak of OUR version into an adopter's CLAUDE.md was fixed in S3b - verify that still holds at 3.0.0 rather than assuming.

THE BREAKING SECTION IS THE DELIVERABLE. An adopter reading it must be able to answer, before upgrading: will my CI go red, and why. Specifically:
- A project with a declared doc that no longer exists WILL go red, and that is the intended fix - say so plainly and say the remedy is to restore the file or remove the declaration.
- A project scripting `sync-update <ref>` keeps working but attests less; `--all-pairs` restores the old scope, and the reason it is no longer default is BDL-UX #163 - re-baselining without reading is what the narrower default prevents.
- `setup-branch-protection` must not be re-run until every declared context reports green. The project layer already carries this warning; make sure the RELEASE notes carry it too, because an adopter upgrading is exactly who will run it.

DO NOT overstate what shipped. Six slices closed; eighteen debts remain open and are listed in the tracker, five of which the release notes should name because an adopter will meet them: #187 (`bd list --json` filtered silently), .60 (Windows path refusal, unverified by decision), .81 (the commit gate cannot see a neighbour's hunk), .82, and the doc-quality `measurable-goal` re-scope.

BDL-060's release was verified that way and it is the standing practice: build, install into a fresh venv, run `beadloom init` + `reindex` + `ci` on a scratch project, and confirm the version the installed package reports. `tests/adopter_project.py` exists now - use it.

title: [dev] ctx returns reality without intent — an agent asking what a node IS never learns what it is FOR
description:
MEASURED by the coordinator on 2026-08-25, after S5 landed.

`beadloom ctx flow-guards` returns the node's AS-IS documentation, its symbols and its edges. It returns NOTHING from the TO-BE space - no PRD, no CONTEXT, no acceptance criterion. The intent is indexed (190 TO-BE documents, searchable with a `[to_be]` label - verified: `beadloom search "acceptance criteria are executable"` returns BDL-061's own PRD) and the relation is checked in one direction (`docs spaces` holds an epic's declared intent against the AS-IS space, `relation_checked: True`, 17 declarations from 37 epics with closed beads). What is missing is the direction an agent actually travels.

THIS IS NOT A DEFECT IN S5. PLAN's S5 criteria were "the TO-BE space is indexed and searchable, bound to beads" and "an epic with closed beads whose criteria never reached AS-IS is reported". Both are met. Feeding intent back into `ctx` was never in scope. This bead exists because the gap is only visible once S5 shipped.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. CLAUDE.md tells every agent to run `beadloom ctx <ref-id>` before touching an area - it is step 4 of BEFORE ANY WORK, and it is the single most-executed instruction in this flow. So the one moment an agent is guaranteed to ask about a node is the moment it gets reality with no intent. It learns what the code IS and not what it is FOR, which is exactly the knowledge that stops a "fix" from removing a deliberate behaviour. This epic has six recorded cases of an honesty note understating what the code does; the inverse - code whose reason nobody re-read - has no detector at all.

It is also the missing half of the Spec-Driven claim. TO-BE and AS-IS are two artifacts and the checkable claim is the RELATION between them. Today that relation is computed for a REPORT and never delivered to the reader who is about to change one side of it.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and the reasons matter more than the outcome:
- WHICH intent belongs to a node. An epic's PRD may name ten nodes; a node may be named by six epics across two years. Dumping every mention would drown the useful one, and `ctx` has a token budget it exists to respect (`prime` is capped under 2K for the same reason). Judge whether it is the epic that DECLARED the node (the `Related Files` join `.17` already built), the most recent, the still-open ones, or something else - and say what a node with no declared intent shows, because that is the common case: only 5 of 37 epics declare nodes.
- ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE. A node no epic ever declared must read differently from one whose intent was never checked. That distinction has cost this epic two full slices (#174, #175); do not re-earn it.
- WHETHER IT IS DEFAULT OR OPT-IN. Default is more useful and risks bloating every call; a flag is honest but nobody will pass it. Measure the size on this repository before choosing, and state the number.

DO NOT re-implement the join. `.17` built `read_epic_intents`, `EpicIntent` and the `Related Files` declaration parse in `application/doc_spaces.py`; `context_oracle/builder.py` is where a bundle is assembled. This should be a read of an existing seam, not a second one.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE (prove it against `tests/adopter_project.py`, since an adopter's doc roots are configurable and their epics are not laid out like ours), CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

comments.text:
CHECKPOINT: implementation complete, Gate green. `beadloom ctx <ref-id>` now carries an `intent` section for the FOCUS nodes only. Three decisions, each with its reason.

WHICH INTENT BELONGS TO A NODE — the epics that DECLARED it in `Related Files`, and nothing else. `.17` already measured the alternative (backticked tokens anywhere in an epic's documents) over 60 epics and threw it away because it attributed the node `status` to nine epics whose prose used the English word. The join was NOT re-implemented: `context_oracle/intent.py` holds the port types and the policy, `application/intent_reader.py` fills them by calling `read_epic_intents`. The direction matters — `context_oracle` is a domain and `application` is the layer above, so the port types live in the domain and the adapter above it, the same shape `doc_roots` uses to let `doc_sync` resolve roots without importing application. Only the focus refs are looked up; the traversal reaches 20 nodes and the question was asked about one.

ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE — three statuses, and the last two are deliberately not one. `declared` names the epics with document and line. `none_declared` says the space was read and nothing declares this node, AND carries `epics_read` / `epics_declaring_nodes`, so on this repository it prints 'No epic declares this node. 61 epic(s) read, 5 of them declare a node' — a measurement, not a claim. `not_checked` has four distinct reasons: `intent_space_not_read` (--no-intent, or a caller with no project root), `no_intent_documents` (empty TO-BE space), `no_epic_declares_any_node` (documents read, none declares anything — the same vacuity `SpacesReport.relation_checked` reports) and `doc_roots_config_error`.

DEFAULT, NOT OPT-IN, and the numbers decided it. Section size measured on this repository: 306 B on `flow-guards` (1 epic), 713 B on `why` (3 epics), ~145 B when not checked, against bundles of 124 KB and 150 KB. Mean cost of turning it ON across all 84 nodes: 22 B per bundle, 0.015%; largest single delta 564 B. Time: reading the whole TO-BE space is 26 ms (61 epics) against a `build_context` of 8.5 ms — paid on a COLD bundle only, because `compute_bundle_mtimes` now folds the TO-BE tree into `docs_mtime` and `bundle_cache_key` gained a `with_intent` dimension so an opted-out caller cannot serve its 'not checked' answer to one that asked. THE TRACKER IS NOT READ, deliberately. `bd close` writes only the local database, so the committed 2.7 MB export and the live tracker disagree on a branch — a bead status inside `ctx` would be confidently wrong exactly where the work is happening — and parsing it costs 15 ms per cold bundle for a fact that does not change which epic declared the node. CAP: 5 declarations carry document and line; the rest keep their names in `also_declared_by`. Order is descending NATURAL key (ORD-31 above ORD-4), because a tracker allocates numbers in time order — a heuristic, stated as one, which is why the truncated epics are still named.

title: [BDL-061][bug] a document that SHOWS the watches syntax opts itself into surface drift — parse_watches matches inside a fenced code block
description:
MEASURED on this repository, 2026-08-24, while judging which reference documents to attest in beadloom-mr2l.24.

`beadloom sync-check` reports docs/domains/context-oracle/features/code-indexer/SPEC.md as a
reference document with watches=cli,graph. That SPEC declares no watch of its own: its header
carries no annotation. It opted in from an EXAMPLE inside a fenced python code block, whose own
caption reads '<!-- beadloom:watches=cli,graph --> <- also an example: not read'. The caption is
false, and the document it is written in is the one that proves it.

CAUSE: doc_sync/surface.py:parse_watches calls _WATCHES_RE.search(text) over the whole document,
with no line anchoring and no awareness of fenced content.

SAME CLASS AS THE ONE S6 JUST CLOSED: beadloom-mr2l.83 fixed exactly this shape for the wave
declaration — a 'refs:' written inside a sentence became a real scope — by anchoring the match to
the start of a line and reporting what it had to drop. The direction argument transfers: a false
positive here silently enrols a document in a check it never asked for, and the operator's only
remedies are to attest a declaration the document never made or to leave a permanent advisory
warning.

EXPECTED: (1) anchor the annotation to the start of a line, the way an annotation is required to
be elsewhere; (2) skip fenced code blocks; (3) the code-indexer SPEC then leaves the reference
population without an edit, and a document that genuinely wants to watch a surface says so in its
header like every other reference document does.

STATED, NOT FIXED, in docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md under the reference-drift
section, so the limit is visible where a reader meets the mechanism.

refs: sync-check

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit e6de765).

WHAT. parse_watches searched the whole document, so any occurrence of the syntax anywhere enrolled the document. Measured before the fix, reference_state held TWELVE documents and FOUR of them had made no declaration: CHANGELOG.md (an entry describing the feature), docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md (the syntax inside a sentence), docs/services/cli.md (a fenced example), and the code-indexer SPEC the bead names, whose caption reads 'also an example: not read'. The bead found one; the same search found four.

THE QUESTION THE BEAD ASKED. A document that DEMONSTRATES a declaration is not distinguishable from one that MAKES it by syntax — the two are byte-identical. What separates them is POSITION, and position decides three of the four shapes a real document uses: fenced, indented, and written inside a sentence. A declaration now opens a line (at most three spaces of indentation, markdown's own boundary) and is not inside a fenced block. The residual case position cannot decide is an unfenced, unindented example written in prose at column 0; that is read as a declaration, and the module docstring says so rather than hiding it. The proposal for that case is the one a markdown document follows anyway — fence the sample — rather than inventing an escape marker, which would add a second syntax to get wrong. The code-indexer SPEC's caption is now true instead of aspirational.

ONE JUDGEMENT. docs/services/cli.md was enrolled by its own fenced example and genuinely wants to watch the CLI surface, so it now DECLARES cli,graph,flow.yml in its header — the same set it was tracking, so build_reference_state preserves its baseline and no new drift appears. CHANGELOG.md and the two SPECs leave the population: a changelog and a specification of the mechanism are not overviews that go stale with the surface. Reversible in one line each if the owner disagrees.

MEASURED. Reference documents 12 -> 9, all nine declaring in their header. surface_drift entries that no operator could ever attest: 1 -> 0.

TESTS. tests/test_surface_watches_declaration.py, 11 rows, including the code-indexer SPEC read from disk rather than restated (a fixture copy could stay true after the SPEC changed) and the exact declaration set this repository makes. Mutation-checked: removing the anchor reddens 3.

FILES. src/beadloom/doc_sync/surface.py, docs/services/cli.md, tests/test_surface_watches_declaration.py.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: API CHANGE: doc_sync.surface.parse_watches() keeps its signature and changes behaviour — the annotation must open a line, at most three spaces indented, outside a fenced block; the first such line decides. Docs to check: docs/domains/doc-sync/README.md (the parse_watches line ~211 says 'the annotation', which is now 'a line-anchored declaration'), docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md (its reference-drift section STATES this limit as known-and-not-fixed — that paragraph is now false), docs/services/cli.md (the sync-check reference-drift block should say a declaration is read from a document's header).

title: [BDL-061][dev] attestation is per ref while the freshness fact is per file — a per-pair re-baseline has no CLI
description:
Filed from review beadloom-mr2l.23's minor n5, which named it and asked for it to be filed rather than left in a comment. beadloom-mr2l.78's own close comment names the same gap: 'A per-PAIR attestation has no CLI. That is the next honest step and it is unfiled.'

WHAT .78 CHANGED: the doc-freshness fact is now recorded per FILE (sync_state.file_symbols_hash),
so only the pair whose own code file moved is stale and its siblings are unverified.

WHAT IT DID NOT CHANGE: attestation is still per REF. `beadloom sync-update <ref> --yes`
re-baselines every pair that ref owns. MEASURED on .83's own doc fixpoint: 4 stale pairs were
cleared by two ref attestations that re-baselined 10 pairs, a 10-for-4 ratio. The six pairs
nobody read were re-attested as a by-product.

WHY IT MATTERS: that is exactly the hazard BDL-UX #163 is filed for — re-baselining a document
nobody read silences sync-check without evidence. #133 is CLOSED because the bulk re-attestation
is no longer REQUIRED by the tool. It is still the only re-attestation the tool offers.

EXPECTED: a per-pair attestation surface (for example `sync-update <ref> --pair <doc>`, or an
interactive mode that attests the pairs the operator confirms) so an operator who revised one
document does not have to record a claim about its siblings. Decisions that must precede it:
whether the pair is named by document path, by code path or by both, and what happens to a ref
whose remaining pairs stay stale after a partial attestation.

refs: sync-check

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: attestation split from the freshness fact. attest_ref(scope=) writes symbols_hash for every pair of the ref (a FACT about the index) and baseline_source=attested + synced_at only for the scoped pairs (a CLAIM about a document somebody read). CLI: sync-update <ref> --yes now scopes to the STALE pairs; --pair <doc_path> (repeatable) names a document read; --all-pairs is the deliberate whole-ref attestation. Reopened after a premature close; validation pending.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: attestation is scoped to what the run had grounds for.

DECISION (the 'something smaller'): a FACT and a CLAIM were one UPDATE, and they are now split.
- FACT: the node-level sync_state.symbols_hash is what the index saw. attest_ref() carries it
  forward for EVERY pair of the ref. Left behind, .78's unverified/sibling_symbols_changed verdict
  would stand forever on a pair whose mover has since been re-baselined and can no longer be named,
  and a signal reading cannot clear is a signal people clear with a bulk re-attestation.
- CLAIM: doc_hash_at_sync, code_hash_at_sync, file_symbols_hash, synced_at and
  baseline_source=attested are written ONLY inside the scope.
Withholding the claim is not cosmetic: check_sync corroborates an index_build baseline against git
instead of trusting it, so the bulk form used to switch the harder check off for every document
nobody had opened. Pinned by TestTheWithheldClaimIsObservable.

CLI. Default scope of 'sync-update <ref> --yes' is now the STALE pairs. A pair reported unverified
because a sibling moved is the pair .78 said nobody can revise, so it is left unclaimed and says so.
A ref with no stale pair now prints 'Nothing to attest for <ref>' and names the two ways to say more.
--pair DOC_PATH (repeatable) names a document read. --code CODE_PATH narrows to one file.
--all-pairs is the deliberate whole-ref attestation, kept because an operator who did read all of a
ref must be able to say so in one command; taking that away is its own cost.

WHY BOTH AXES (the bead asked: by doc, by code, or by both). Answered by measurement on this very
branch, not by taste: domains/doc-sync/README.md was stale against MY engine.py and the other
agent's surface.py in one run. Naming the document alone would have recorded a reading of a change
I had not seen. So: both, and either alone is a legitimate narrowing.

MEASURED HERE. This bead's own doc fixpoint: 7 pairs revised, 7 attested — 1-for-1, against the
1/27, 13/20, 26/56 and 15/10 this epic recorded. And unverified fell 107 -> 0, because the carried
FACT clears the sibling verdict without claiming anything.

WHAT WAS NOT CHANGED, deliberately: the MCP mark_synced tool and mark_synced_by_ref keep whole-ref
semantics. Narrowing an MCP tool's contract is a separate decision with its own callers; it is the
same hazard one layer over and is worth filing.

TESTS 15 (tests/test_attestation_scope.py) + 3 scenarios
(tests/acceptance/features/attestation_scope.feature). RED first; verified biting against the
previous HEAD in a clean room.
FILES src/beadloom/doc_sync/engine.py (Attestation, attest_ref, pairs_of_ref),
src/beadloom/services/commands/docsync.py, docs/domains/doc-sync/README.md,
docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md.
