New public engine API: attest_ref(), pairs_of_ref(), Attestation. mark_synced_by_ref() is unchanged (whole-ref). Docs to check: docs/domains/doc-sync/README.md (CLI table + engine API list, updated), docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md ('The scope of an attestation', added), docs/services/cli.md (sync-update flags — NOT updated by this bead, the other agent holds that file this wave).

title: [BDL-061][bug] the ACTIVE reconcile matches a full bead id against a table written with short ids, so it reports coherent while matching nothing
description:
MEASURED on this repository, 2026-08-24, while writing the S6 documentation pass.

`beadloom active-sync --check` prints 'ACTIVE tables already coherent.' and `--json` returns
{"changed_files": [], "drifted_rows": []} while BDL-061's own ACTIVE.md carries a row reading
'| .22 | In progress |' for a bead `bd` reports CLOSED. The row was corrected by hand in .24.

CAUSE: application/active_table.py:_reconcile_one looks up bd_statuses.get(cells[0]). The first
cell of this repository's bead-status table is the SHORT id ('.22'), while the injected keys are
full ids ('beadloom-mr2l.22'), so no row is ever matched. set_active_table_status has the same
whole-token comparison and the same blind spot.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW: the mechanism was built (BDL-053) precisely so the table would
not drift with manual discipline, and it has been inert on the repository that authored it. It
also violates this epic's own standing rule that absence is not evidence: 'already coherent' is
reported for a run that compared zero rows.

EXPECTED: (1) resolve a short row id against the epic directory's bead prefix before the lookup,
or state that only full ids are reconciled and report the rows it could not resolve; (2) a run
that matched NO row is a finding, not a pass — print how many rows it resolved out of how many
it read, so an inert reconcile cannot read the same as a clean one.

refs: active-table

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit e6de765).

WHAT. The reconcile was inert, and four faults kept it that way — the bead named one and the other three were measured while fixing it.
1. The id-form mismatch the bead reported: bd_statuses.get(cells[0]) compared a full id against a short cell. resolve_row_bead_id() is now the single mapping, used by _reconcile_one AND by set_active_table_status, which had the same blind spot.
2. _find_status_column returned None at the FIRST Bead-headed table without a Status column. BDL-061's own ACTIVE.md carries a deferral table headed '| Bead | What it is | Why it was not done here |' at line 203 and its status table at line 683, so the whole file was skipped before any row was read. Fixing only (1) would have left the mechanism just as inert here.
3. bd list --json returns OPEN beads capped at 50 rows: measured 41 of this repository's 709, every closed one missing. The reconcile could therefore never write '✓ done' — the exact correction this bead was filed for. The query is now bd list --all --json -n 0.
4. A short id is not unique: this tracker holds EIGHT beads numbered .17. With (1)-(3) fixed and the scope left global, BDL-061's .17-.24 rows resolved onto beadloom-8qqp.17-.24 and eight rows of one epic's table would have been rewritten from another epic's tracker state. Resolution is now scoped to the epic's own prefix, derived from the [KEY] in each epic-typed bead's title (_bd_epic_prefixes). Without a prefix the number must be unique in the whole tracker; an ambiguity is reported, never guessed.

THE SWEEP THE BEAD ASKED FOR. One other place, in this same module: set_active_table_status, reached by the MCP checkpoint/complete_bead tools, which pass the full id bd gave them into a table written in short form. Fixed by the same helper. Everywhere else that compares ids across the two conventions already does it deliberately — application/waves/media_checks.py compares only the trailing number and says why ('the prefixes deliberately differ... comparing whole ids would report every bead in the project'). review_brief/assembly.py and waves/planner.py compare full ids on both sides, and the .feature suite tags carry full ids. So: two occurrences of the defect, both here, and one correct precedent that shows the convention was known.

ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE (the bead's clause 2). ReconcileResult gains rows_read, rows_resolved, unresolved_rows((path, cell, reason)) and is_inert. Every output form states the fraction; --check exits 1 on an inert run as well as on drift, and does NOT fail on a partially resolved one, because a permanent failure over an old epic's table is how a channel stops being read. Unresolved rows are listed 5 at a time with the remainder stated; the COUNT is never truncated.

ONE JUDGEMENT NOT IN THE BEAD. 'Done' and '✓ done' are compared as one state (leading non-alphanumerics stripped, case-folded). Without it the first working run would have rewritten 78 of BDL-061's 79 rows purely to add a checkmark, which is a mechanism that gets switched off. The module's contract already said a richer cell is preserved when the STATE agrees; this makes that true for more than one spelling.

MEASURED, first working run, included in the commit: 191 of 283 rows resolved, 56 corrected across 12 ACTIVE.md files, 92 named as resolving to no bead. Two corrections are beadloom-mr2l.65 and .68 — CLOSED in the tracker, reading 'Pending' and 'Open' in the epic's own table.

TESTS. tests/test_active_table_id_forms.py, 20 rows. Each discriminator mutation-checked: removing the epic scope reddens 3, removing the list-marker exemption reddens 2.

FILES. src/beadloom/application/active_table.py, src/beadloom/services/commands/docsync.py, docs/domains/application/components/active-table/DOC.md, tests/test_active_table_id_forms.py.

TODO for someone. 92 unresolved rows are real and are now visible: BDL-008 numbers its rows '01'..'13' and BDL-038/040/041 put the title in the first cell ('.1 Contract model + ...'). Neither is a bug in the reconcile; both are tables no mechanism can read, and the run now says so instead of passing.

CLI: active-sync --json gains rows_read / rows_resolved / unresolved_rows, and --check now exits 1 on a run that resolved no row as well as on drift. docsync gains _query_bd_beads() and _bd_epic_prefixes(); _query_bd_statuses() keeps its signature and now queries 'bd list --all --json -n 0'. title: [dev] S6: the wave parser fails toward more parallelism, and the release gate toward less independence
description:
Review `.23`'s nine majors. Both clusters fail in the DANGEROUS direction, which is the thing to fix - not the individual parses.

=== CLUSTER 1: THE DECLARATION PARSER FAILS TOWARD MORE PARALLELISM.
The wave decision rests on it, and every way it is wrong makes beads MORE likely to share a wave:
- `refs: wave-plan; sync-check` beside `refs: sync-check` share one wave at exit 0 with ZERO findings. Two beads that touch the same node run concurrently and nothing says so.
- A PROSE MENTION of `refs:` adopts the next word as a real ref. A sentence about declarations becomes a declaration.
- `mcp_server.py` SPACE-joins the declaration fields where both CLI callers newline-join, defeating `.80`'s `[ \t]` fix. One caller of three has the old bug back, and it is the one an agent reaches through MCP.

A parser whose every failure mode increases parallelism is worse than no parser, because the wave shape is trusted. Fix the DIRECTION, not the three cases: an ambiguous or unparseable declaration must serialise, the way `no_declared_refs` already does. `.21` established that default and it is right - unknown scope is not independence.

=== CLUSTER 2: THE RELEASE GATE FAILS TOWARD LESS INDEPENDENCE.
- `_marker_in` matches without the colon, so a comment reading "REVIEW ISSUES are still open" RELEASES the author's account. The docstring names THAT EXACT STRING as the case it prevents. Verified by the coordinator: `stripped.startswith(marker)` on a line beginning with those words.
- `AuthorNote.author` is read from the tracker and NEVER COMPARED, so the author releases their own account. Verified: no comparison anywhere in `release.py`.

title: [dev] S6: the second half of the wave guarantee is prose, and waves holds both ids of a mis-wired edge without comparing them
description:
Review of `.21` by `.22`, which held the bead to its own stated guarantee. Five findings pinned as strict xfails (`FINDING BDL-061.22-1..5`) in `tests/test_bead22_wave_guarantee.py` — those are the acceptance criteria; do not delete one to make the suite green.

=== THE HEADLINE: CLAUSE TWO IS PRINTED, NOT ENFORCED.
`.21` stated the guarantee as: for any two beads in one wave, no shared medium can carry one bead's in-progress state into the other's result — AND where a medium cannot give that guarantee, the wave SAYS SO and names the bead that measures the combined outcome.

Clause one is genuinely enforced: `.22` tried containment either way, a `part_of` cycle, one absent ref among real ones, and a case mismatch — every sideways overlap serialises.

Clause two is a CONSTANT TUPLE. The four media are listed with a deterministic `gate_owner` that a serialised neighbour cannot silence — which is good — but NOTHING CHECKS that the tree was measured, that the gate ran scoped, that the baseline was reconciled, or that a tracker id matches the id in its title. The wave asserts a property it does not verify.

A guarantee whose second half is prose is worse than one that claims less, because the prose is what a reader trusts. Decide, and say which: either enforce the four (each medium gets a check that can fail), or restate the sentence so it claims only what the code does. Do not leave it as it is.

=== #171 IS NOT CAUGHT, AND THE DATA IS ALREADY IN HAND.
`waves` reproduces the mis-wired dependency edge faithfully at exit 0 — it holds BOTH the allocated id and the id written into the bead's title and NEVER COMPARES THEM. Same shape as `validate_rules()` computing the right answer while `linter.py:160` discarded it (`.48`): the diagnosis exists and is thrown away. One comparison closes it.
This matters because #171 is not hypothetical - it happened in this session, produced a well-formed accepted WRONG dependency edge, and was caught only because `bd dep add` echoes full titles and a human read the echo.

=== #118's HOOK FIX CANNOT CATCH THE SWEPT HUNK, AND THIS BEAD PROVED IT ON ITSELF.
The fix is real for a neighbour's SEPARATE file. It cannot catch a neighbour's hunk INSIDE a file the committer legitimately touches — which is the failure that actually happened twice this session, because `git add -p` is unavailable in this environment. And `.22`'s own pathspec commit swept `.beads/issues.jsonl` in through the hook's `active-sync --stage`: the same shape, from a direction its tests did not model. Judge whether that is fixable here or is a separate bead, and say which.

=== TWO MORE, FOUND BY THE TESTS RATHER THAN INHERITED.
- An empty `refs:` header adopts a LATER LINE as the bead's scope, because `\\s*` after the colon matches newlines. A scope silently taken from the wrong line is the worst possible failure for a mechanism whose whole job is deciding what may run beside what.
- A blank-but-present `reason`/`until` is accepted: the required-field check reads truthiness of presence, not content. CONTEXT requires every exclusion to carry a reason and an exit condition, and this epic has already shipped two exclusion mechanisms whose fields were decorative (`.48`'s dead entries, `.49`'s unparsed `until`).

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

title: [dev] S5: the population's third hole, a half-inert declaration, and two adjacent lines that contradict
description:
Review `.19`'s three majors. Found by ACTIVE PROBING - the reviewer planted a `README.md`-only planning directory rather than reading the code - which is why this is the third population hole after `.18`'s two.

=== M1. KIND WINS OVER ROOT, AND A DOCUMENT FALLS OUT OF EVERY COUNT.
When a document's KIND resolves to a space whose ROOT does not match it, the document drops out of every count rather than being reported. Same equation as #174 and #175 - a thing that cannot be classified is UNVERIFIABLE, not absent - now inside the classifier S5 shipped to enforce exactly that.

This is the population's THIRD failure: `.17`'s first denominator silently dropped 34 epics; `.18` found four directories falling out for carrying no `CONTEXT.md`/`BRIEF.md`; `.73` widened it; and a planted directory still finds a way out. Do not patch the third case. **Establish what the classifier does when kind and root disagree, once, and make the disagreement itself a finding.** A document that cannot be placed must appear in a count somewhere, or the count is not of documents.

=== M2. A HALF-INERT `working.kinds` DECLARATION REPORTS NOTHING.
A `working.kinds` declaration covering 39 SPEC files reports nothing, while the DOC promises per-item liveness. This is `.48`'s rule-liveness question in the doc-spaces layer, and `.49`'s expired-exemption question in the same breath: a declaration that suppresses nothing, or that suppresses far more than its author expected, must say so.

The standard is already set in this codebase - `rules_inert` qualifies lint's summary so a rule count cannot over-claim, and `.49` prints the suppressed count on every run. Do the same here rather than inventing a third vocabulary. And per CONTEXT, an exclusion carries `reason`; a declaration that covers 39 files with one line should have to justify itself at that scale.

=== M3. TWO ADJACENT LINES CONTRADICT.
One `beadloom ci` run prints `exempt: 0` and `55 WORKING document(s) exempt`. COORDINATOR'S NOTE: I did NOT reproduce this - on the current tree I see the `55 WORKING document(s) exempt` half and no `exempt: 0`, so it likely needs excused pairs present, which the tree does not have right now. Take the reviewer's measurement as the report and reproduce it yourself before fixing; if it does not reproduce, say so rather than fixing by inspection.

Whatever the cause, the fix is the one this epic keeps arriving at: two readers of the same fact must not be able to print different numbers for it. `.75` closed exactly that shape one layer down (a WORKING root meant two different things to `check_sync` and `check_spaces`), so look for the same seam before assuming a formatting slip.

=== NOT IN SCOPE
The 11 reference documents carrying advisory `surface_drift` are `.20`'s and need prose - do not silence them. `.75`'s two residuals (`ci` stays rc 0; only the default kind list stops a one-line whole-tree silencing) the reviewer explicitly routed to `.20`'s guide rather than to code.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE, CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

comments.text:
COMPLETED — one classification decision, not three patches.

M1, THE POPULATION'S THIRD HOLE. The rule established once: every document a declared root found is placed in exactly one bucket, so sum(populations) == |files any declared root matched| on ANY tree. DocSpaces.classify(project_root) globs every root once and classifies each file once; documents_in and working_documents read off it. WORKING never had this hole because it alone was computed by a full scan — that special case is now the rule, and the two spaces doing the wrong thing beside it are gone. Kind still wins over root (ACTIVE.md lives inside the TO-BE tree, so a root-first answer would exempt nothing), and the disagreement is itself a finding: document_outside_declared_root, ONE per kind with the count, up to five paths and the roots that failed to reach them — sixty directories named the same way are one convention decided once, not sixty lines. A space that declares NO root has said nothing about where its documents live and contradicts nothing, which is why the shipped 55 ACTIVE.md files stay silent.

MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL CLI on this repository, planting the reviewer's two probes and reverting them (--json only, #148): .claude/development/docs/features/ZALPHA/README.md + docs/PLAN.md took to_be 190 -> 191, as_is 93 -> 94, epics 61 -> 62 and printed 2 findings, where before both files were in NO population and nothing was reported. Reverted: 190 / 93 / 55, epics 61, 0 findings. TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE: the invariant is pinned on this repository (338 files found, 338 placed) AND on tests/adopter_project.py's TypeScript project, where a design/ORD-4/README.md is reported and goes quiet once README is declared a TO-BE kind — the remedy the finding recommends actually removes the finding.

M2, A HALF-INERT DECLARATION. Two causes, both closed. (a) space_of_kind walked SPACES, whose own docstring calls it 'the order a report reads best' — one constant asked to mean two things, so AS-IS's DEFAULT kind list beat a project's explicit working.kinds before liveness ever ran. _KIND_PRECEDENCE is now its own constant with its own reason: a kind declared for WORKING is the one declaration that changes what a check DOES rather than where it looks, and WORKING winning is visible three ways (contradiction findings, the reach line, sync-check's excused count). Safe by construction and asserted rather than claimed — the three shipped kind lists are disjoint, so no shipped classification depends on the order, and this repository's 190/93/55 are unchanged. (b) Liveness is per DECLARED item. working_reach names each declared kind and each declared root with how many documents it excused, so a one-line declaration covering 39 files prints 39, and a [ACTIVE, SPEC] line whose SPEC half is inert reports SPEC and not ACTIVE. Scoped to what the PROJECT wrote: WorkingExemption.kinds_declared/roots_declared distinguish a declaration from an inherited default, so a project that declared only exempt_from_freshness is still asked the old whole-space question and the existing pins (.75's and test_doc_spaces') keep their exact assertions. Vocabulary reused, not invented: rules_inert qualifying lint's count and .49's suppressed count are the two this codebase already had.

M3, REPRODUCED — and in the split form the coordinator suspected. On this tree sync-check --json summary reads exempt: 0 while docs spaces printed '55 WORKING document(s) exempt'; inside one beadloom ci run only the second half prints, because .76 deliberately omits the excused clause when nothing was excused. So the reviewer's two numbers are real and come from two commands, not two lines of one run — the ci line's contradiction is the weaker form, where a reader takes 55 as pairs while the sync-check line's denominator never moved. Cause: one word for two populations, and on this repository the 55 ACTIVE.md documents live outside the docs directory index_docs walks, so none of them is a sync pair at all. Fix: the two populations are named apart, and the pair count is CARRIED from the step that measured it — GateStep.pairs_excused is set by the sync-check step and handed to _step_doc_spaces, never recomputed. beadloom docs spaces runs no freshness check and states pairs_excused: null rather than a number it did not measure. The gate line now reads '55 WORKING document(s) in the exempt space, 0 sync pair(s) excused'.

ONE DEFECT MY OWN CHANGE INTRODUCED, found by the FULL-SUITE run and stated rather than hidden: hoisting the sync-check step out of the step list made it run BEFORE reindex, so a fresh project's gate reported 'database missing'. Six tests reddened (test_gate.py x4, test_f3_gate_coverage, test_sync_unverifiable). The list is built in execution order now, with the reason in a comment. This is exactly the cost .76 recorded for targeted-only runs.

TESTS. 30 new in tests/test_bead77_kind_and_root_disagree.py + 3 acceptance scenarios (@bead:beadloom-mr2l.77, doc_spaces.feature). Suite 6669 -> 6702 passed, 0 failed, 4 xfailed (all pre-existing), captured to a file and read (CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN). description:

So 'FROM 37 OF 57 EPIC(S) WITH CLOSED BEADS' is really 'from 37 of 57 epics the export still names', and the 20 are finished work (BDL-001..BDL-030) whose intent-to-AS-IS relation is never checked.

IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. bd close writes only the local Dolt database, so the export drifts from the tracker by ordinary use. .18-3 — ONE NUMBER, TWO SOURCES OF TRUTH. docs spaces prefers 'bd list --all --json' and falls back to the export; _step_doc_spaces reads the export only. In the measurement above the command reported 17 declarations and one finding while the gate reported 4 and none, at the same commit. Whichever is right they cannot both be, and a check whose answer depends on which entry point ran is not a gate (BDL-UX #171's shape).

DONE WHEN: an epic absent from the tracker is counted in epics_without_bead_status and named in the summary; the command and the gate give the same answer on one tree, or the difference is itself reported. The four xfail(strict=True) tests turn green.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COORDINATOR — raised P2 -> P1, because it drifts by ORDINARY USE rather than by mistake.

.18 measured that removing an epic's records from `.beads/issues.jsonl` takes `_step_doc_spaces` from 1 finding to 0 with `passed=True`, and `not_verified` unchanged — it was already True for an unrelated reason, so the one honest signal is saturated and cannot carry this.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED — three states where there was one, and the state has its own channel.

WHAT. `_bead_statuses(key, beads_by_epic, tracker_source)` replaces `beads_by_epic.get(key, ())`. An epic is now one of three: statuses known; statuses unknown because a READABLE tracker does not name it; statuses unknown because no tracker answered at all. `EpicIntent.unknown_status_reason` carries which — the source string for the middle case, `TRACKER_UNREADABLE` for the global one — and `SpacesReport.epics_unknown_to_tracker` names the middle case's epics.

THE FINDING IS SCOPED, deliberately. `epic_not_in_tracker` fires only for an epic that DECLARES a node. An epic that declares nothing is already counted and named in the *declare no node* clause; reporting it a second time under another name would say one thing twice and, on this repository, add 19 findings that repeat an existing line. And when the WHOLE tracker is unreadable no per-epic finding fires — that is one global cause, already reported once.

WHY IT IS NOT `not_verified`. That boolean was already True here because 52 epics declare no node, so it could not carry the deletion (`.18`'s measurement). The channel is a count, a name list, a finding and a clause in the gate line.

.18-3, THE TWO TRACKERS. They still read different ones ON PURPOSE — the gate the committed export, so it answers the same in a fresh CI checkout with no `bd` installed, and the command the live database, which is the more current. `TrackerRead(statuses, source)` carries the source with the answer and both surfaces print it (`tracker read from …`, and `tracker_source` in `--json`). title: [dev] re-scope measurable-goal before the debt is paid — it is a numeral detector, not a measurability detector
description:
Review `.15` measured this and it blocks `beadloom-mr2l.65`, which the owner has already decided to do.

THE MEASUREMENT: `measurable-goal` reports 154 findings over 235 goal statements, and its precision on a random sample is about **1 in 18**. It flags, among others:
  "`beadloom lint --strict` fails (non-zero)..."
  "`beadloom federate --fail-on` exits non-zero..."
  "**G6 - Graph-write safety.** Graph YAML writes are atomic (temp + `os.replace`)..."
The first two are EXACTLY the exit-code form BDL-UX #148 exists to demand, and the third states a property (atomicity) that is measurable by any reasonable reading. The check is looking for a NUMERAL, not for measurability.

THE REVIEWER'S PROPOSED FIX, measured: accepting a backticked artifact or an observable verb takes 154 -> **87**, and the remaining 87 are the genuine "make it better" class. Verify that number yourself rather than adopting it - and if your own criterion lands somewhere else, say what it is and why.

WHY THIS COMES FIRST. The owner chose to PAY this debt rather than live with a standing warn, and the reason was that a large permanent number stops being read. Paying 154 when ~67 of them are the check's fault would rewrite correct sentences to satisfy a regex - the worst possible outcome, because it teaches everyone to write for the checker. That failure has a precedent in this epic: BDL-UX #169, where the fix was explicitly NOT to reword the document.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not lower the count by adding a tolerance, by excluding documents without a stated reason, or by weakening the check until it fires on nothing. The three sibling checks that report 0 over populations of 269/138/243 are proof that a real check CAN read a large population and find it clean; this one must earn the same standing.

REQUIRED: after re-scoping, run the five checks and publish the new counts, including which of the previously-reported 154 are now accepted and a sample showing why. `beadloom-mr2l.65` starts from your number.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE (prove the narrowed check still fires on a genuine "make it better" goal), A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

=== THE CRITERION, and why it is not the reviewer's
A goal is reported when BOTH legs hold:
  (1) states_an_unbounded_improvement — the predicate is a quality, not an outcome: improve / enhance / optimize / polish / streamline / modernize / strengthen / establish / clean up / tidy up, or make|keep|render|leave <something> <better|faster|simpler|useful|intuitive|...>;
  (2) not names_a_witness — nothing an observer could go and look at: no quantity (the old _NUMBER_RE, unchanged), no named artifact (an inline code span, a --flag, a file name, a snake_case identifier) and no observable outcome (exits / non-zero / rc / fails / passes / catches / detects / reports / renders / produces / shows / works / builds / generates / blocks / refuses / emits / green / red / no longer).
This is the construction the three sibling checks already use — name the empty form, do not guess at the good one. risk-mitigation's list of non-mitigations is the same shape one check over. The shipped check was the outlier: it tried to PROVE measurability from a positive signal (a digit), which is why its precision was 1 in 18.

I did NOT adopt the reviewer's criterion, because its number does not reproduce. 'accept a backticked artifact or an observable verb' was measured on the same 154 under five literal readings:

None is 87. I then read every statement in the closest remainder sets by hand: at 33-49 remaining, most are not the 'make it better' class — BDL-046's seven menu-structure bullets, 'G7 — Docs. Guide for ... + CHANGELOG + ROADMAP', 'Route extraction has no self-matching false positives', 'Create Agent Prime — ... working identically across all IDEs (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline)'. Paying those would be the same defect one notch quieter. So the criterion shipped is a different one, and its remainder I can defend line by line: all four are the standard's own example.

  145  no unbounded-improvement form  (123 of them also name a witness; 27 do not — see the limit)
    3  not a statement at all: a markdown horizontal rule closing a Goal section (review .15 m1)
    2  improvement form, but names a witness

Precision was bought with recall. Of the 150 statements newly accepted, 27 name no witness either; about those this check now decides nothing ('Turn prose into mechanisms', 'Clear separation between policy and fact sections', 'Doc Sync Engine — tracking doc<->code relationships'). title: [dev] the decode family has 29 live candidates and no mechanism — one ruff line closes half of it
description:
ANSWER to .66's open question: can a mechanism make the SIXTH instance of the decode family fail rather than ship? YES, in two halves, and both are cheap. MEASURED on HEAD 4d167cb, not argued.

=== HALF ONE — the explicit encoding. ONE CONFIG LINE, ZERO MIGRATION.
ruff's PLW1514 (`unspecified-encoding`) flags `Path.read_text()`, `open()` and friends in text mode with no `encoding=`. This repo does not select `PL`, so it has never run.
MEASURED: `ruff check --preview --select PLW1514 src/ tests/` reports ZERO on this repo — .42's ~40-site sweep already paid the whole debt. And the rule BITES: a probe module with `p.read_text()` and `open(p)` gets 2 findings. So the cost of enabling it is one line in `[tool.ruff.lint].select` and no code change at all.
CAVEAT to check before enabling: PLW1514 is `--preview` in ruff 0.16.3. Either pin preview for that rule or wait for it to stabilise; a preview rule in the Gate is its own kind of drift.

=== HALF TWO — the handler as wide as the call. AN AST LEDGER, THE SHAPE THIS REPO ALREADY SHIPS.
No linter checks 'the except clause covers what the try body can raise'. An AST scan does, in ~40 lines: for every `ast.Try` whose body calls `.read_text(` / `open(` / `.decode(`, flag every handler whose caught set contains neither `UnicodeDecodeError` nor `ValueError` nor `Exception`.
MEASURED with that prototype over `src/`: 29 SITES TODAY. Not hypothetical — the sixth instance already exists, 29 times over. A sample:
  application/active_table.py:73,183       catches OSError
  application/doctor.py:363,369            catches OSError
  application/guards/config.py:440         catches YAMLError only
  context_oracle/test_mapper.py:266,385    catches OSError
  doc_sync/audit.py:634,662                catches OSError
  doc_sync/doc_shape.py:111                catches OSError   <- .15's own C1 sibling, still open
  graph/loader.py:459                      catches OSError
  onboarding/config_sync.py:210,293,472,646  catches OSError
  onboarding/scanner/project_scan.py:218,247 catches JSONDecodeError,KeyError
  services/commands/docsync.py:839         catches OSError
29 is NOT 29 defects. Each needs .42's per-site judgement: is this stream a UTF-8 CONTRACT (a planning document, our own index, a file we wrote) or the user's locale, and what is the honest behaviour on a failure. That is exactly why the mechanism is a LEDGER and not a verdict: every site is listed with a stated reason, a NEW narrow handler fails the suite, and an existing one is a decision on the record rather than an accident.

=== WHY THIS IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE MISSING EXCEPT CLAUSE
`tests/test_windows_dimension.py` ALREADY implements this exact shape for `sys.platform` — an `ast` visitor, a ledger of every occurrence with a reason, and `test_the_scan_finds_things` as the non-vacuity guard. So the mechanism was not merely possible: it was already in the repository, one test file over, and nobody pointed it at this family. `doc_quality.py` was written after .36, .37, .40 and .42 all fixed the same shape.
The honest conclusion is that a cheap mechanism EXISTS and was never built. Note review .15 M7's warning about this class of ledger: the `sys.platform` one was evaded in one line because the ledger only looks for conditions naming `sys.platform`. A decode ledger must key on the CALL (`read_text`), which cannot be renamed away, not on the exception name.

=== DONE WHEN
- `PL` (or `PLW1514` explicitly) is selected in `[tool.ruff.lint]` and `ruff check src/ tests/` still exits 0.
- `tests/test_decode_handlers.py` holds the AST scan, the ledger of the 29 sites each with a judged reason, and a non-vacuity guard that fails if the scan finds nothing.
- Injecting `except OSError` around a `read_text` in any src module reddens the suite; restoring it goes green, byte identity verified.
- Each of the 29 is judged per .42's framework, and the ones that are defects are fixed rather than ledgered — starting with `doc_shape.py:111`, which review .15 C1 named and which is still open.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — both halves built and RED first, and the sabotages found a limit the bead did not know about.

HALF ONE GOES IN, on stated terms. PLW1514 is selected in pyproject.toml together with lint.preview = true and lint.explicit-preview-rules = true, because a preview rule selected WITHOUT preview is not an error: ruff prints "Selection PLW1514 has no effect because preview is not enabled" and exits 0 (measured with --isolated). That is a gate that reads as configured and checks nothing, so the three settings travel together and the test file fails if any is removed.

Answered with a line noqa carrying its reason, never by editing the measurement that row records. ruff is pinned by uv.lock, so further preview drift arrives with a reviewed lockfile bump. When PLW1514 graduates, the two knobs can be deleted and the select line keeps working.

THE FINDING FROM SABOTAGE 5, which changes the bead's premise: PLW1514 IS TYPE-INFERENCE BOUND. Planting path.read_text() behind an UNANNOTATED parameter in graph/linter.py left ruff check src/ tests/ at exit 0 and only .42's AST sweep reddened; annotating the same parameter as path: Path made ruff report it. open() has no receiver and is reported either way. So "one config line closes half of it" is too strong: over src/ the reach is broad because mypy --strict makes annotations mandatory, over tests/ (type-checked by nothing) it is partial, and .42's receiver-agnostic sweep is what actually covers the package. PLW1514 also does not look at subprocess(text=True) at all. Neither instrument contains the other; both facts are now pinned by test_the_reach_of_the_rule_is_the_one_that_was_measured, framed so a later ruff that widens the rule is a signal to re-scope rather than a failure to paper over.

HALF TWO: tests/test_decode_handlers.py, an AST ledger keyed on the CALL. 203 modules parsed (the same 203 mypy reports), 55 try/suppress blocks whose body decodes text, 28 of them narrow. Each of the 28 carries the stream it reads, the caught set as the source spells it (machine-checked), what the handler answers today with what happens instead, and one until naming .67.
FOUR DEFINITION DECISIONS, each one a way the ledger could have gone vacuous: the verdict is over the whole try, not per handler, so except OSError beside except Exception is NOT a row; a call with errors="replace" cannot raise and is not a site (this is what removes context_oracle/test_mapper.py, two of .66's sample rows); contextlib.suppress and subprocess(text=True) are in the definition though neither matches src/ today, each held open by a planted fixture; and the ordinal in a key counts ALL guarded blocks in a scope, so repairing the first does not renumber the second.

At 30cf11f the file has except OSError: continue and no UnicodeDecodeError anywhere in it, and git show says doc_shape.py was ADDED in that commit carrying this handler (183 insertions, one file). So review .15's C1 is still open. Not fixed here — fixing is .67's — but its ledger row says it in as many words so the next reader does not inherit the claim.

SABOTAGES so far, FAILED never ERROR, every restore by reverse edit and sha256-verified OK: (1) inject a new narrow site in graph/linter.py -> 1 FAILED / 15 passed, and the failure names _sabotage_probe; (2) drop preview = true -> 2 FAILED / 14 passed (the planted-site row and the not-inert row); (3) drop the PLW1514 selection, keep preview -> 1 FAILED / 15 passed while ruff check src/ tests/ stays at rc 0, which is the pure false green this row exists for; (4) widen a ledgered handler without deleting its row -> 1 FAILED naming 'judged but no longer narrow (1)'; (5) an unstated-encoding read in the package -> see the finding above; (6) blind the scan (called_name answers None) -> 11 FAILED / 25 passed including test_the_scan_reads_a_live_population, so a ledger over a broken scan cannot go green.

WHEN IT GRADUATES: delete the two knobs, keep the select line — and the noqa becomes unused, which RUF100 will say out loud.

=== 2. THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE BEAD'S CLAIM (sabotage 5)
"One ruff line closes half of it" is too strong, and this is measured, not read off the rule description. PLW1514 IS TYPE-INFERENCE BOUND: planting path.read_text() behind an UNANNOTATED parameter in graph/linter.py left `ruff check src/ tests/` at exit 0 and only .42's AST sweep reddened; annotating the same parameter `path: Path` made ruff report it. open() has no receiver and is reported either way. It also does not look at subprocess(text=True) at all — which is the shape .40 actually found in git_activity.
So over src/ the reach is broad because mypy --strict makes annotations mandatory there; over tests/ (type-checked by nothing) it is partial, and .42's receiver-agnostic sweep is what actually covers the package. Neither instrument contains the other. Both facts are pinned by test_the_reach_of_the_rule_is_the_one_that_was_measured, written so that a later ruff which widens the rule is a signal to re-scope the sweep deliberately, not a red to paper over.

=== 3. THE LEDGER: 28 ROWS, and the four decisions that keep it from going vacuous
tests/test_decode_handlers.py. 203 modules parsed (the same 203 mypy --strict reports), 55 try/suppress blocks whose body decodes text, 28 of them narrow. Each row: the STREAM it reads (the fact that decides contract-or-locale), the caught set as the source spells it (machine-checked), what the handler answers TODAY and what happens instead, and one until naming .67.
(a) Keyed on the CALL, never the exception name — review .15 M7's evasion of the sys.platform ledger was a rename; read_text cannot be renamed away.
(b) The verdict is over the whole try, not per handler: `except OSError` beside `except Exception` is covered, and listing it would put a non-defect on the ledger.
(c) A call with errors="replace" cannot raise and is not a site — this is what removes context_oracle/test_mapper.py, two rows .66's sample listed.
(d) contextlib.suppress and subprocess(text=True) are IN the definition though neither matches src/ today, each held open by a planted fixture, so a leg with no live instance cannot rot.
Plus: the ordinal in a key counts ALL guarded blocks in a scope, so repairing the first does not renumber the second; and test_the_package_uses_no_except_star_the_scan_would_walk_past turns the scan's one known blind spot (ast.TryStar, 3.11) into an assertion instead of a sentence, so raising target-version reddens rather than silently widening the hole.
I do NOT claim "29 minus one". .66's definition is not reproduced here and I did not reconcile row by row; the docstring says so and names the count this file recomputes on every run.
NON-VACUITY: test_the_scan_reads_a_live_population asserts the DENOMINATOR (modules parsed, guarded blocks found), never the guilt — .67 will drive the narrow count to zero and a guard reading "the scan must find something wrong" would then redden on success and be deleted.

=== 4. A REPORTED FIX THAT IS NOT IN THE TREE
.66's checkpoint 1 says doc_shape.py _documents_by_node_kind "now reports the document as status=unverified reason=unreadable". At 30cf11f the function is `except OSError: continue`, the file contains no UnicodeDecodeError anywhere, and `git show 30cf11f -- doc_shape.py` says the file was ADDED in that commit (183 insertions, one file) carrying this handler. So review .15's C1 is still open. Not fixed here — that is .67's — but its ledger row states it in as many words so the next reader does not inherit the claim.

=== 5. TESTS MUST BITE — six sabotages, FAILED never ERROR, numbers not colour, every restore by reverse edit and sha256-verified OK
(1) inject a new narrow site in graph/linter.py -> 1 FAILED / 15 passed, failure names _sabotage_probe.
(2) drop preview = true -> 2 FAILED / 14 passed (planted-site row + not-inert row).
(3) drop the PLW1514 selection, keep preview -> 1 FAILED / 15 passed WHILE `ruff check src/ tests/` stays rc 0 — the pure false green.
(4) widen a ledgered handler without deleting its row -> 1 FAILED, "judged but no longer narrow (1)" naming the key. This is the row that stops .67 closing a site silently.
(5) an unstated-encoding read in the package -> the type-inference finding in section 2.
(6) blind the scan (called_name answers None) -> 11 FAILED / 25 passed, including test_the_scan_reads_a_live_population, so a ledger over a broken scan cannot be green.
Honest caveat recorded in the code: on THIS tree, dropping preview also reddens lint through RUF100 on the new noqa. That coupling is an accident of one comment, so the guarantee rests on the planted site and not on it.

=== 6. GATES / VERIFIED
- Full suite captured ONCE on the shared tree: 6491 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped, 4 xfailed (153s).
- GREEN IN A CLEAN ROOM OVER 925 FILES (git archive HEAD + only my six): 6485 passed, 1 failed, 16 skipped, 4 xfailed. The one failure is test_bead15_s3b_coverage::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh, ATTRIBUTED by measurement: it fails identically on a pristine HEAD extraction with none of my files. Two earlier ai_techwriter_seams failures were "python" not on PATH under that invocation and vanish with the venv bin on PATH. The six shipped files are sha256-identical between the tree and the clean room, and the three affected test modules were re-run there on the final bytes: 60 passed.
- ruff check src/ tests/ clean; mypy --strict clean (203 files).
- beadloom ci rc 0, all steps: reindex PASS, lint PASS 0 errors / 68 warnings (the same 68 baseline .66 measured, so no new violation), sync-check PASS 322 fresh, docs-audit PASS 15 mentions fresh, docs-quality WARN (pre-existing), config-check PASS, doctor PASS.
- Fact coverage is NOT quietly lowered by my doc: 3 of 9 declared facts verified both WITH and WITHOUT my section (measured by removing it, reindexing and restoring, sha256 OK). The transient 4/9 in between was two FALSE mentions — "0.16.3" read as the beadloom version and "203" as node_count — now spelled `ruff==0.16.3` (a pin, which the scanner correctly skips) and backticked.

=== 7. FILES
pyproject.toml; tests/test_decode_handlers.py (NEW, 18 tests + the 28-row ledger); tests/decoding_calls.py (NEW — the ONE definition of "a call whose codec somebody chooses", so the .42 sweep and this ledger cannot drift; .42's four private copies deleted and imported instead); tests/test_locale_independent_io.py (imports the shared module; its docstring now states which leg it owns and which PLW1514 owns); tests/test_decoding_symmetry.py (one noqa line); docs/domains/infrastructure/components/console-streams/DOC.md (the SPEC statement — that DOC already owned "which stream gets which codec", and this extends it from writes to reads and from the codec to the handler).
.beads/issues.jsonl rode along, re-added by the pre-commit coherence hook: tracker state for .70, .65 and the merge slot, none of it mine. The commit message names it so the diff is not wider than the message.

Start with doc_sync/doc_shape.py::_documents_by_node_kind#1 (review .15 C1, still open) and application/guards/config.py + onboarding/flow_config.py, which are narrow in TWO directions because their caught set omits OSError as well.

title: [tech-writer] pay the measurable-goal debt — 4 goal statements of 232 (re-scoped by .70; was 154 of 235)
description:
OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-24: pay the debt rather than accept it as a standing warn.

MEASURED by the S4 doc-quality work: `measurable-goal` reports **154 findings over 235 goal statements read** across this repository's 243 planning documents. Two thirds of our goals carry no measurable clause. The check is not wrong - CONTEXT's writing standard has said "a goal carries an explicit measurable clause; 'make it better' is not a goal" since this epic began, and nothing enforced it until now.

WHY THE OWNER CHOSE TO PAY RATHER THAN LIVE WITH IT: a large permanent number stops being read. A warn that everybody has learned to scroll past is the same failure as a check that cannot fire - the subject of this entire epic - arriving by habit instead of by code.

HOW TO DO IT, and the order matters:
1. **Read the review verdict first.** `beadloom-mr2l.15` was asked whether the criterion is too strict to be actionable, because a check nobody can satisfy gets disabled. If review says the criterion needs narrowing, that changes this bead's size and possibly its scope - do not start rewriting before you have that answer.
2. **Do not rewrite a goal you cannot make true.** Some of these documents are historical - a closed epic's PRD from months ago. For those, the honest move is not to invent a measurable clause retroactively; it is to mark the document as historical and exclude it from the population with a stated reason, the way this epic has handled every other "cannot check" case. Say how many fell into each bucket.
3. For live documents, rewrite the goal so the clause is real. A number, a threshold, an observable state - not a rephrasing that satisfies the regex.

FORBIDDEN: making the count go down by weakening the check, by excluding documents without a reason, or by adding a tolerance. The number is the point; if it ends at zero because the rule stopped looking, nothing was paid.

REPORT: how many goals were genuinely rewritten, how many documents were marked historical and why, and what the count is at the end. If the honest floor is not zero, say what it is and what holds it there.

Standing rules by name: A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TESTS MUST BITE.

COORDINATOR — the debt is 4, not 154, and all four are historical. Resolution proposed, not executed.

AFTER `.70`'s re-scope, verified by me through the gate: `measurable-goal` reports **4 findings over 232 goal statements** (was 154 over 235; three of the old 235 were a markdown horizontal rule). So 150 of the original 154 were the check looking for a NUMERAL rather than for measurability - it flagged "`beadloom lint --strict` fails (non-zero)", which is exactly the exit-code form #148 exists to demand.

THE FOUR SURVIVORS, and they are all from CLOSED epics:
  BDL-002/CONTEXT.md:12 - "Establish the agent-native architecture and clean up the codebase before building new features"
  BDL-004/CONTEXT.md:12 - "Make Beadloom useful for the whole team, not just the person who set it up"
  BDL-005/CONTEXT.md:13 - "Make Beadloom fast, searchable, and fully agent-native - with no LLM API dependency"
  BDL-006/CONTEXT.md:13 - "Make Beadloom enjoyable and intuitive - visual graph exploration, impact analysis, change visibility"
Every one is a genuine unbounded-improvement predicate. The check is right about all four.

WHY I AM NOT REWRITING THEM. This bead's own text forbids it: "do not rewrite a goal you cannot make true ... for historical documents the honest move is not to invent a measurable clause retroactively". Adding "measured: N nodes, zero outbound LLM calls" to a goal written before that work existed would be fabricating the record of intent - and CONTEXT's TO-BE/AS-IS decision says a planning document stays the record of what was intended, precisely so a later artifact can be checked against it.

WHAT THE HONEST PAYMENT IS: a `historical` exclusion carrying `reason` and `until` (or a permanent equivalent, since a closed epic has no exit condition), the way every other exclusion in this codebase now works. That is a small mechanism change, not a documentation pass - so it is dev work and belongs in its own bead rather than here.

WHAT THIS BEAD BECOMES: nothing to pay. Recommend closing it as "debt measured at 4, all historical, superseded by the exclusion bead". The owner's decision to pay rather than live with a standing warn was correct on the information available and cost almost nothing once the check stopped lying about the size of the debt.

title: [dev] withdraw the Windows CI leg by owner decision — keep what it taught, drop what it costs
description:
OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-24: the Windows leg is NOT shipped. The cost is not technical - ~16-28 runner-minutes per PR and, unlike the locale rows, it becomes the CRITICAL PATH, roughly tripling PR-to-merge latency. Windows is not in the target audience.

WHAT TO REMOVE:
- The `tests-windows` job from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and from the vendored template.
- `DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` back from ten to nine. Live protection on `main` still has seven; the declared set stays ahead until someone runs `setup-branch-protection`, which is the owner's call and is documented in the project layer.

WHAT TO KEEP, and this is most of `.39`'s value:
- **All six formerly-`skipif(win32)` guard tests stay non-vacuous.** `.39` established that the mark named the wrong obstacle - Windows has symlinks and `Path.resolve` follows them; what a PROCESS may lack is `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege`. They are gated on a measured capability probe and run on any runner that holds it, which is true regardless of whether a Windows leg exists. Removing the leg must not put a platform name back.
- The ledger that fails the suite when an unjudged platform skip is added. It is the mechanism that keeps this from silently rotting back.

WHAT MUST BE STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED:
`beadloom-mr2l.60` - the backslash refusal refuses every native edit target on Windows and its stated reason is false there - was pinned as a strict xfail **for the leg to adjudicate**. With no leg, nothing adjudicates it. So:
  - Say in the SPEC that the Windows behaviour of the path refusal is **UNVERIFIED BY DECISION**, not verified and not broken - the distinction this epic spent two slices on (unverifiable is not clean).
  - Decide what to do with `.60`'s xfail. A strict xfail that no runner can ever flip is a pin nobody can close; either keep it with that fact written next to it, or convert it to a documented residual. Judge and state the reason.
  - `#170`'s enforcement-surface note and anything else claiming Windows support should say what is actually true: the refusal exists FOR Windows harnesses and has never executed on one, and now by decision will not.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, ONE PLATFORM IS NOT VERIFIED (which is exactly what this decision accepts, deliberately, with the cost stated).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.64] — commit 02bd162 on features/BDL-061-S4 (19 files mine; a 20th, .beads/issues.jsonl, was swept in by the repo's own pre-commit coherence hook — see §9).

=== 1. THE DECISION, EXECUTED IN ONE CHANGE (and it had to be one)
`tests-windows` left `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the vendored `ai_techwriter/github-workflow.yml` AND `DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` (10 -> 9) together. Not tidiness: I deleted the job first and MEASURED the consequence — `test_required_contexts_match_ci_yml_check_runs` went red with "required but absent from ci.yml (LOCKOUT): ['tests-windows']". That is .38's lockout in the withdrawal direction, and it is the reason a job deletion is never a job deletion. Sabotage 1 and 3 below re-measure both halves.
`setup.py`'s `--check` help + docstring dropped the context. The one number I did NOT have to touch: ci.yml's locale block already said "not the 9 that setup-branch-protection would apply" — .39 left it stale at 9 and the withdrawal makes it true again.

=== 2. WHAT HAPPENED TO .60's PIN, which is the judgement this bead was for
CONVERTED TO A MEASUREMENT, NOT DROPPED. .60 stays OPEN and its defect is unchanged.
The pin was `@pytest.mark.xfail(sys.platform == "win32", strict=True)` on `test_the_guard_is_told_the_file_the_writer_will_touch`, and strict was RIGHT while a leg was landing — the runner adjudicates, an unexpected PASS fails the suite. With no leg the same mark is inert on every runner: it cannot flip in either direction, so it is a pin nobody can close that reads exactly like a tracked question. Keeping it with a note attached would have left the suite carrying a marker whose only function is to look diligent.
It could be converted because the prediction was never a mystery — it is DERIVABLE, and derivable is only as good as the two facts it composes, both of which I asserted:
  (a) `ntpath.join("src","app.py") == "src\\app.py"` and `PureWindowsPath` reads it as ("src","app.py") — the spelling a Windows harness produces names a real file there (already pinned by .39; I extended the row to assert the full verdict, `MALFORMED` + `BACKSLASH_REJECTION` + `relative is None`, not merely the reason);
  (b) NEW `test_the_module_that_refuses_contains_no_platform_branch` — `paths.py` reads no `sys.platform` and no `os.name` (nor does anything in `src/`, re-measured), so the refusal is ONE code path on every OS; and NEW `test_the_backslash_verdict_is_reached_before_any_call_the_platform_owns` — `os.fsencode` (the one line whose codec a Windows kernel owns) is monkeypatched to raise if reached, and the backslash verdict still comes back, so the answer cannot depend on it.
(a)+(b) is the composition. It is stronger than the xfail was: the xfail could only ever have been settled by a runner that no longer exists, and these run on every leg of every PR. THE REVIEWER'S POINT SHARPENS THIS: .60's false justification is decidable by READING, so paying ~16-28 runner-minutes and 3x PR latency to adjudicate it was never a good trade. We are not skipping a measurement we needed; we are skipping an expensive way to learn something cheap.
THE RULE MOVED WITH IT. `test_a_win32_xfail_is_always_strict` became `test_no_platform_xfail_waits_for_a_runner_that_will_not_come`: while no leg runs another platform, NO platform xfail is allowed at all — measure it, or write it down as a residual. The old rule is quoted in the failure message and returns with the leg if the leg ever returns.
AND THE NEW RULE'S POPULATION IS EMPTY, WHICH I DID NOT LEAVE SILENT. An assertion over an empty set passes identically when the scan is broken, so `TestTheScannerItselfBites` gained a parametrised row that builds a module carrying a platform xfail in BOTH spellings (strict and lax) and asserts the scanner finds it. Sabotage 7 breaks the scan and 2 rows fail.

=== 3. UNVERIFIED BY DECISION — the wording, and where it lives
`docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md` gained `#### Windows: unverified by decision`, placed at the end of the accepted-shape section: what is measured (PureWindowsPath/ntpath + a branchless refusal => on Windows EVERY edit target is MALFORMED and every guarded edit an `error` at exit 2, fail-closed, unusable, with a remediation the harness cannot perform), what is NOT and now will not be (`Path.resolve` over real links, volume case-folding, `os.fsencode`'s codec, whether a Windows harness truly sends backslashes), and why nothing pins the second list. The third state is named in those words: not verified, not known broken.
#170's enforcement-surface section gained the same honesty one axis out: the adapter, the matcher and every recorded firing come from macOS/Linux; the path rules are written FOR a Windows harness and have never run under one; the gap is permanent by decision rather than pending.
THE SPEC's OWN FALSE SENTENCE FIXED: the drive-letter paragraph blamed "this build of Beadloom" for what is the PLATFORM. It now says platform and states that the documented answer is not the answer on Windows. That is .60 scope item 4, done here because it is a doc claim; items 1-3 and 5 (the product change) remain .60's.

=== 4. M7 (review .15), taken because the withdrawal makes it load-bearing
REPRODUCED FIRST, not accepted on report: `SYMLINKS_UNAVAILABLE = True` in place of `not SYMLINK_CAPABILITY.both` -> 133 passed / 6 skipped / 0 failed / rc 0 across test_guards_paths + test_windows_dimension + test_bead14_s4_binding, with the reader told only "could not create a symbolic link ... no reason recorded". Every assertion in that class was about the CAPABILITY object; none was about the joint between the capability and the condition the marks read, so the chain could be cut exactly there.
FIXED IN TWO LAYERS, because I judged the mechanism rather than the line:
  (i) `test_the_skip_condition_is_the_measurement_and_not_a_value` — the flag must BE `not SYMLINK_CAPABILITY.both`. Closes the cut joint precisely.
  (ii) `test_the_six_rows_are_observed_to_run_rather_than_inferred_to` — the six, BY NODE ID, are run in a child pytest and the OUTCOME is read (`rc == 0`, no "skipped" in the report, "6 passed"). It does not care where the cut is: a constant condition, an edited mark, a module-level `pytestmark`, a deselecting conftest or a RENAMED row all redden it. Sabotages M7a-d, four different mechanisms, all bit.
(ii) also mechanically forbids this bead's forbidden action: deleting one of the six now fails a row that names it.
A machine that genuinely cannot link fails here rather than skipping six guard tests quietly elsewhere. Deliberate, and the same stance the file already took one row above.

=== 5. SABOTAGES — 13, all FAILED, never ERROR; every restore sha256-verified
1 re-add the job only -> 3 FAILED (incl. the lockout guard) | 2 re-add it under ANOTHER NAME (`tests-platform`) -> 1 FAILED, proving the check reads `runs-on`/matrix and is not a name test | 3 re-add the context only -> 2 FAILED | 4 drop the price + bead id from ci.yml -> 1 | 5 vendor the leg back into the adopter template -> 1 | 6 re-pin .60 as a strict platform xfail -> 1 | 7 break the marker scan -> 2 | 8 add a `sys.platform` branch to paths.py -> 3 | 9 decide the backslash AFTER os.fsencode -> 1 | M7a the reviewer's one-line edit -> 2 | M7b hard-skip ONE mark, flag left honest -> 2 | M7c rename one of the six -> 1 | M7d module-level skip -> 1.
Two sabotages initially reported "no tests ran" (rc 4) — my harness passed a multi-target string as one argv element — and one produced an ERROR because the sabotage itself referenced `sys` after I had removed the now-unused import. Both were defects in the sabotage, not weak tests; re-run correctly, all three bit. A sabotage that does not bite is a claim about the sabotage first.

=== 6. WHAT I DID NOT DO
- Did not delete any of the six, did not re-add a platform name to a mark, did not close .60.
- Did not touch `.claude/development/BDL-UX-Issues.md`. #170's own entry makes no Windows claim (the claim was in the SPEC section it produced, which I fixed), and the file carried another agent's uncommitted edits earlier in this session — editing it would have meant staging their work.
- Did not run `beadloom setup-branch-protection`. Live protection on `main` is still the seven pre-.38 contexts; the declared set is now nine and the two it lacks (`tests-locale`) have both been observed green, so the gap is finally closeable — the owner's call, and the sequencing note in `docs/services/cli.md` now says "compare against what reports green" instead of "wait for the Windows leg".
- Did not re-baseline any ref I do not own (see §9).

=== 7. GATES
Local suite 6421 passed / 11 skipped / 4 xfailed. ruff rc 0 over src/ + tests/, mypy --strict clean (203 files).
GREEN IN A CLEAN ROOM OVER 19 FILES (#181): `git archive HEAD` into an isolated checkout + only my files, `uv sync`, then ruff rc 0, mypy 203 files clean, pytest 6416 passed / 16 skipped / 4 xfailed with 2 failures, and `beadloom ci` rc 0 (reindex PASS, lint PASS 0 errors, sync-check WARN "no baseline — index rebuilt", docs-audit PASS, docs-quality PASS, config-check PASS, doctor PASS 0 errors). Exit codes and `--json` throughout, never line counts (#148).
THE TWO CLEAN-ROOM REDS ARE NOT MINE AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: built a second clean room from PRISTINE HEAD with none of my files and ran the same three files — it fails THREE rows there (`test_our_approved_rfc_still_carries_pending_questions`, which the coordinator owns because paying the RFC debt is what reddens it, plus BOTH `TestSyncCheckNewPairs` rows). My tree fails strictly FEWER, and the parity row passes in both.

=== 8. ONE FLAKE, MEASURED RATHER THAN WAVED AT
`test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation` failed ONCE in the last full run. The differing file was `.beads/issues.jsonl`, not the index: `bd` flushed an export mid-run (my earlier `--claim` among the rows). It passes alone, passed in the earlier full run and passes in the fixed-order clean room. Same family as #168 (order + shared on-disk state) and the reason that test's own docstring already argues about relative `-wal` checks — except the shared file here is the tracker log, which no guard writes and `bd` does.

=== 9. SHARED-TREE NOTES, flagged not hidden
(a) The final `beadloom ci` on the SHARED tree is rc 1 with 13 stale pairs — every one of them under `doc_sync/`, `application/gate.py` and `services/commands/docs.py`, files another wave is editing right now and I never touched. I did NOT run `sync-update` on `doc-sync`/`application`: re-baselining their docs mid-edit is the masking failure mode. My own evidence is the clean-room gate (rc 0).
(b) I DID re-baseline exactly one pair: `mcp-server` <- `services/commands/setup.py`, because my edit changed only the `setup-branch-protection` help string and `mcp.md` documents that module's SIGNATURES, which did not move. `docs/domains/onboarding/features/branch-protection/SPEC.md` was genuinely revised instead (it now states the nine-context default, the withdrawal and the both-directions invariant) — it was already stale at session start and is fresh now. sync-check re-run to fixpoint after: 0 stale, rc 0.
(c) The pre-commit coherence hook staged and committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` alongside my 19 files. It was already staged by another agent before I started; the delta is bd state only (my claim, the merge slot, .65/.66 appearing) and it moves the tracked log forward, losing nothing.
(d) Took `bd merge-slot acquire --wait` before committing and released after.

=== 10. FILES
ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml, src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/ai_techwriter/github-workflow.yml
src: onboarding/branch_protection.py (10 -> 9 + the reasoning), services/commands/setup.py

=== 11. TODO / NOT MINE
(1) .60 stays open, and its scope item 1 ("wait for the first tests-windows run") is now unreachable — the rest is unchanged, and the SPEC edit it asked for as item 4 is done.
(2) The GitLab side still carries neither dimension, unchanged from .39's note; the platform asymmetry there is now moot.

title: [BDL-061] A feature reclassified as a component leaves scenario-coverage's population with nothing reported
description:
Measured by beadloom-mr2l.14 while checking whether the 68 is honest.

THE POPULATION IS HONEST TODAY, and that is measured rather than asserted: the shipped rule uses for: {kind: feature} with no ref_id and no exclude, and tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py::TestThePopulationIsHonest compares the matcher's reach against services.yml itself — all 37 declared feature nodes are selected, and the same graph checked by a ref_id matcher instead reports 0 where the honest one reports 2.

THE HOLE: the population is defined by kind, and a node's kind is one line in services.yml. Changing 'kind: feature' to 'kind: component' removes the node from the rule's population with no finding of any sort — the count simply falls by one and the run stays the same colour. The architecture model says the feature/component distinction is 'intent, not weight', which makes it exactly the judgement a future author under time pressure can restate. 24 component nodes sit outside the population today, several of them plainly behaviour-bearing by any ordinary reading (guard-hooks, mcp-tools, cli-commands, graphql_breaking).

WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT IN .13: excluding plumbing is the model's own definition, and widening the rule to components would add 24 findings to 68 without a decision having been taken. The gap is that the EXIT is silent.

TWO OPTIONS, both stated because the trade-off is real:
(a) report a reclassification — the rule cannot see history, so this needs a stored population or a snapshot diff, which makes an evaluator a writer (the #147/#189 shape). Cheaper variant: 'beadloom snapshot compare' already diffs node kinds, so the check could live where history already lives.
(b) print the denominator with the verdict — 'N of M feature nodes carry a scenario; K nodes are outside this rule's population by kind'. It does not catch the reclassification, but it makes the population visible in the same breath as the number, so a shrinking denominator is on the same line as the improving fraction. Cost: one more line of output; benefit: no new writer.

NOT URGENT and stated as such: nothing is wrong today, the number is honest, and this is how it stops being honest in six months.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: leaving the scenario-coverage population is now visible.

DECISION: option (b) from the bead, and (a) is rejected with its reason. The rule cannot see
history, so it cannot report the reclassification itself; an evaluator that remembered its own past
population would be a WRITER, which is exactly the #147/#189 shape this epic keeps meeting. What it
can do is print the denominator in the same breath as the fraction, so a shrinking population and an
improving coverage figure land on the same screen.

NOT widened to components, and that is the bead's own point: excluding plumbing is the architecture
model's definition of the feature/component split, and 24 more findings is a decision nobody took.

WHAT IT PRINTS, measured on this repository: 'this rule's population is 42 of 82 graph node(s)
(kind=feature); the other 40 are outside it and no finding of this rule reaches them: component
(28), domain (7), service (4), site (1)'. Note the number is larger than the bead's 24 — the bead
counted components only, and the honest denominator includes domains, services and the site node.
warn whatever the rule declares (a statement about CONFIGURATION must not redden a pipeline), and
silent when the population is the whole graph, for the same reason the excused statement is silent
at zero: a line about nothing on every run is how a real one goes unread.

TWO EXISTING TESTS INVERTED, on purpose and with the reason written into them.
test_bead14_s4_binding's 'a node outside the population is not reported and is not counted covered'
asserted violations == []. Absent from the verdict was ALSO absent from the arithmetic, which is the
defect. It now asserts the node is still not reported as UNCOVERED and IS counted on the population
line. Same for 'a hand-picked population would report almost nothing' — the hand-picked matcher's
cost is now a printed number rather than an argument in a docstring.

TESTS 3 scenarios (tests/acceptance/features/rule_population.feature) + the two inverted assertions.
RED first; verified biting against the previous HEAD in a clean room.

title: [BDL-061] scenario-coverage reference leg: 'Example:' prose and indented code read as scenario references; an undecodable document reads as no intent
description:
Three findings measured by beadloom-mr2l.14 in the reference leg of scenario-coverage (src/beadloom/graph/scenarios.py), pinned as xfail(strict=True) in tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py::TestTheReferenceLegsWidestSurface so a fix reddens the suite and the mark must be removed with it.

1. FALSE POSITIVE — 'Example:' is a Gherkin scenario keyword (en dialect), so a bare prose line opening with it is read as a claim that a scenario exists. Measured: 'Example: a nested import inside a function is still an import.' yields the reference 'a nested import inside a function', which the rule then reports as a scenario the author must write under exactly that name. Zero false positives on this repo today (all 33 references come from 'Scenario:' lines) and a large one for any adopter, because 'Example:' opens an ordinary explanatory paragraph in a PRD. Every real reference in this project is backticked or bulleted, so that is the discriminator the shorter keywords need.

2. FALSE POSITIVE — an indented (four-space) code block is read as a reference while a fenced one is not. Markdown has two code-block syntaxes and _FENCE knows one. The module's own reason for skipping fences — a form is not a claim that a scenario exists — applies identically to indentation, and templates.md is exactly the kind of document that carries a Gherkin form.

3. ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE — load_references() swallows OSError and UnicodeDecodeError with a bare continue, so a document it cannot decode contributes zero references and NOTHING is reported: not a dead glob (the glob matched), not an unreadable file. Measured: a cp1251 PRD naming one scenario yields refs=() dead=(), i.e. the rule states that document's intent is fully met. load_suite() reports an undecodable .feature one function away, so the two halves of the same module disagree. This is BDL-061 CONTEXT's own rule (.57): nothing an editor does may make a check quieter.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit e6de765). All three of .14's strict xfails are ordinary assertions now.

1. FALSE POSITIVE, 'Example:'. Gherkin's Example (en) and Пример (ru) are scenario keywords and also ordinary words. A bare line opening with one is prose until the author marks it — bulleted, quoted or backticked, which is what every real reference in this repository already is. The keyword is not withdrawn: '- Example: an order is placed' and '`Example: an order is placed`' are still references. MEASURED: 33 references before the change and 33 after, so nothing an author wrote stopped being read.

2. FALSE POSITIVE, indented code. Markdown has two code syntaxes and the reader knew one. Four spaces (tabs expanded) is a form, on the module's own stated reason for skipping a fence. The discriminator against a deeply nested list item is the marker: a line that is indented AND opens with a bullet or quote marker is a list item, not code. That is narrower than CommonMark's real rule, which needs a block parser this reader is not, and the docstring says so.

3. ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE. load_references swallowed OSError and UnicodeDecodeError with a bare continue, so an undecodable document contributed nothing and NOTHING was reported. It now returns a ReferenceSet — references, dead_globs, unreadable — the same shape .66 gave the suite reader one function away, and scenario_coverage's reference leg reports each unreadable document with its reason. UnreadableFeatureFile is renamed UnreadableDocument (the name is now used by both readers) with the 2.2.0 name kept as an alias.

TESTS. The three xfails in tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py::TestTheReferenceLegsWidestSurface are assertions carrying their finding as a docstring, and tests/test_reference_leg_syntax.py adds 12 rows for the other half of each fix — the true positives that must survive a false-positive removal, plus the rule-level report. Mutation-checked: emptying the prose-keyword set reddens 2, removing the list-marker exemption reddens 2.

MEASURED after: beadloom lint --strict rc 0, 60 findings, 26 of them reference-leg — identical to the count before, so this repository gained and lost nothing.

FILES. src/beadloom/graph/scenarios.py, src/beadloom/graph/rules/scenario_coverage.py (reference leg only), docs/domains/graph/features/scenario-binding/SPEC.md, tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py, tests/test_scenario_binding.py, tests/test_reference_leg_syntax.py.

title: [BDL-061] The vendored agents snapshot is the #177 loop, one direction short of closed
description:
Measured while shipping beadloom-mr2l.13 (S4).

WHAT: src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/agentic_flow/agents/*.md.txt is a byte-snapshot of this repository's LIVE .claude/agents/*.md, refreshed by sync_agentic_flow() and asserted byte-identical by tests/test_core_roles.py::TestVendoringDriftGuard and tests/test_cli_setup_agentic_flow.py.

WHY IT IS A LOOP: it is exactly the shape .57 removed for CLAUDE.md and the commands (BDL-UX #177) — the shipped artifact is defined as a copy of one project's local file. Today it is harmless ONLY because this repository has no .beadloom/flow/roles/ fragment, so the live adapters happen to equal the pure shipped composition. The moment anyone adds a project role fragment here, the next sync_agentic_flow() writes that project's standing practice into the package and ships it to every adopter — silently, and byte-identically to what the tests expect.

EVIDENCE: sync_agentic_flow() has NO production caller (grep over src/ finds only its own module); it is invoked from tests and by hand. So the snapshot is maintained by a manual step that nobody is reminded of, guarding an artifact that scaffold_agentic_flow() only reads on the legacy include_agents=True path — the CLI has passed include_agents=False since BDL-052 S3.

EXPECTED, two candidates:
(a) delete the snapshot and the drift tests, and have the legacy path compose like everything else — the roles already have a composition, so the snapshot is a second source of truth for the same bytes (#171's shape as well);
(b) if the snapshot must stay, refresh it from compose_all_roles(config) with NO project_root, and assert that — never from the live directory.

(a) is preferred and is roughly the S3 fix applied to the one artifact it did not reach.

title: [BDL-061][bug] the backslash refusal makes the flow guard refuse every edit on Windows — and its stated reason is false there
description:
FOUND WHILE MAKING THE SIX skipif(win32) GUARD TESTS NON-VACUOUS (BDL-061.39). Reported rather than fixed, deliberately: the rule for this axis is that a Windows failure is a finding and a bead, never a test adjustment, and fixing it here would replace ONE unverified Windows claim with ANOTHER — which is the defect, not the remedy.

THE MEASUREMENT, made on Linux/macOS with PureWindowsPath (which implements Windows path semantics on every platform, and which `pathlib.Path` IS on a real Windows build):

    PureWindowsPath("src\\app.py").parts == ("src", "app.py")     # a separator
    PurePosixPath("src\\app.py").parts   == ("src\\app.py",)      # a name character
    PureWindowsPath("C:/Users/x/app.py").is_absolute() is True
    PurePosixPath("C:/Users/x/app.py").is_absolute()   is False

THE DEFECT. `application/guards/paths.py::rejection_reason` refuses ANY backslash, unconditionally and on every platform. On Windows that is the spelling a Windows harness natively produces (`os.path.join`, `str(Path(...))`, Claude Code's own `tool_input.file_path`), so EVERY edit target would be PathScope.MALFORMED -> an `error` verdict at exit 2. Fail-CLOSED, so it is not a bypass — but a guard that refuses every edit on a platform is not usable there, and its stated remediation ("supply the target as a POSIX path") is not something the harness can do.

THE JUSTIFICATION IS ALSO WRONG THERE, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART. BACKSLASH_REJECTION reads: "it contains a backslash, which separates directories on the harness's platform and is an ordinary file-name character on this one, so the guard and the writer would not be looking at the same file." Both clauses are true, but they describe TWO DIFFERENT platforms — and the guard runs in the harness's own process tree, on the harness's own machine. There is no deployment in which "the harness's platform" and "this one" differ. On Windows, `Path("src\\app.py")` names exactly the file the writer will touch, so it is the REFUSAL that stops the guard and the writer looking at the same file.

A SECOND, SMALLER ONE OF THE SAME SHAPE. docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md says a bare drive letter "is read as a relative directory called `C:`, because this build of Beadloom resolves paths with POSIX semantics". There is no such build property: it is the PLATFORM. On Windows the same string is absolute, so the branch taken in `resolve_edit_path` is the other one (OUTSIDE the root, unless the project lives on that drive) and the documented answer is false.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, so this bead starts from evidence rather than from scratch: tests/test_windows_dimension.py pins all of the above with PureWindowsPath, and `test_the_guard_is_told_the_file_the_writer_will_touch` carries a STRICT xfail on win32 stating this prediction. Strict is the point — on the new `tests-windows` leg the runner ADJUDICATES it: if the row unexpectedly PASSES on Windows, the prediction was wrong and the suite fails and says so.

SCOPE WHEN TAKEN:
1. Wait for (or read) the first `tests-windows` run. The strict xfail turns the prediction into a measurement.
2. Decide the rule. The obvious shape is to refuse a backslash only where it is NOT this platform's separator (`os.sep != "\\"`), which restores the rejection message's own sentence to something true on both platforms and lets `pathlib` do the interpreting it is already trusted for everywhere else. Consider `os.altsep` too: on Windows a mixed `src\sub/app.py` is legal and unambiguous.
3. Decide what the shape gate then owes on Windows that it does not owe on POSIX (a reserved device name — CON, PRN, NUL, COM1 — names no file the writer can create; a trailing dot or space is silently stripped by the Win32 layer, which is EXACTLY the "the guard and the writer see different files" condition the module exists for, and is a stronger argument for a refusal than the backslash ever was).
4. Fix the SPEC's drive-letter paragraph to say platform, not build.
5. Every new rule must be exercised without a Windows kernel where PureWindowsPath can settle it, and on the leg where it cannot.

ACCEPTANCE: the guard reaches a correct, non-MALFORMED verdict for the edit-target spelling a harness produces on the platform it runs on, asserted on both; no Windows-conditional behaviour rests on reasoning alone.
