title: [BDL-061][dev] The guard firing record is never rotated, and --liveness parses it whole on every run
description:
Review .3 minor m7, carried out of .35 rather than solved by it.

`.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl` is append-only with no rotation and no cap. `read_firings` parses the WHOLE file on every `beadloom guard --liveness`, so the cost of the report grows without bound with the number of guarded edits. Measured in .3: 9.5 KB after ~one day of dogfooding, on a repo where the binding only saw a fraction of the writes (#170) and where most edits went through Bash.

WHY IT IS FILED NOW, AND WHY .35 DID NOT FIX IT: .35 added the .gitignore entry for the record. Ignoring a file makes its growth INVISIBLE rather than absent - nobody sees it in `git status` any more. That interaction is named in the ignore block itself, in the flow-guards SPEC and in the ignore-block DOC, precisely so the entry does not read as a solution. This bead is the solution.

Decide with reasons, not outcomes:
- WHAT to bound: bytes, lines, or age. The report's questions are 'did it ever fire', 'how often', 'what was the last outcome' - a cap by AGE loses 'how often' for a long-lived project, a cap by SIZE loses the oldest evidence first, which is the evidence a never-fired claim depends on. State the trade.
- WHETHER rotation may lose a firing at all. A rotated-away firing is evidence that a gate ran; `--liveness` treats a gate that cannot demonstrate it ran as not having run, so silent truncation can turn a healthy guard into a false 'never-fired'. Whatever is dropped must be summarised, not deleted (a counter that survives rotation is the cheap shape).
- WHETHER --liveness should parse the whole file at all. An incremental tail or a materialised summary is a different fix from rotation, and may be the better one; the two are not the same decision.

Relevant when the Gate starts reading the record (S2+ per .1's note).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: the firing record is bounded, and rotation loses no count.

WHAT IS BOUNDED, with the trade the bead asked for stated: RECORDS, not bytes and not age.
A byte cap truncates mid-record. An age cap loses 'how often' on a long-lived project and makes a
quiet month read like a dead guard. A record cap bounds exactly what was measured — the parse.
ACTIVE_FIRINGS_CAP = 2000: at the measured rate (9.5 KB after ~one day, ~50 firings/day at ~200
bytes) that is about six weeks of full detail and ~400 KB to parse.

MAY ROTATION LOSE A FIRING? No count and no verdict. --liveness treats a gate that cannot
demonstrate it ran as not having run, so silent truncation could turn a healthy guard into a false
never-fired. The outgoing firings are folded into a CARRIED SUMMARY holding, per guard, count,
answered (error records excluded, so an error-only guard stays never-fired across a rotation),
first_at, last_at and last_outcome — every input liveness.py reads. fired_count, never_fired and
last_outcome are therefore the same numbers after a rollover as before it.
WHAT IT COSTS, named because a cost nobody names is a cost nobody weighs: per-firing 'why' text
older than one generation. The detail stays readable in guard-firings.1.jsonl until the next
rollover; after that only the counts remain. GuardLiveness.carried_count says how much of a count
rests on a summary rather than on readable lines, and the human row prints 'N carried from rotated
records' — the number is the same, the evidence behind it is not.

SHOULD --liveness PARSE THE WHOLE FILE? Yes, and that is now a decision rather than an oversight:
with a cap the whole file IS bounded. An incremental tail or a materialised counter would be a
SECOND source of truth for a number the file already holds, which is the #171 shape. read_firings
needed no change to stay correct — the summary line names no guard, so the existing parser skips it.

CONCURRENCY: rotation renames rather than rewrites, and the summary is APPENDED to the fresh record
rather than written over it. The archive is read for the summary AFTER the rename, so an appender
holding the old handle is still counted. The one uncovered window is a write into the archive after
that read: such a firing keeps its line on disk and is missing only from the counts.

INTERACTION WITH .35, which the bead was careful about: .35's ignore entry SAID the record is not
rotated. That sentence is now false, so it was rewritten in three places rather than left standing
(the block's own why, the flow-guards SPEC, the ignore-block DOC + onboarding README). The pattern
became .beadloom/guard-firings*.jsonl — ignoring the active record while leaving its archive
untracked would reintroduce exactly the churn the entry exists to remove. test_ignore_block's
'names that it is never rotated' was rewritten to pin the inverted fact, with the inversion stated.

TESTS 12 (tests/test_guard_firing_rotation.py) + 3 scenarios
(tests/acceptance/features/firing_record.feature) — flow-guards had no scenario before, so this also
removes one scenario-coverage finding. RED first; verified biting against the previous HEAD.
FILES src/beadloom/application/guards/firing.py, .../liveness.py,
src/beadloom/services/commands/guard.py, src/beadloom/onboarding/ignore_block.py, four docs.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: API CHANGE: GuardLiveness gains carried_count (and it appears in --liveness --json). New public API in guards.firing: ACTIVE_FIRINGS_CAP, ARCHIVE_RELPATH, CARRIED_KIND, Carried, CarriedGuard, read_carried(). The shipped .gitignore pattern changes from .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl to .beadloom/guard-firings*.jsonl — an existing project's block is written once and never rewritten, so an adopter who already has the old line keeps it and their archive shows as untracked until they widen it by hand. Docs to check: docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md (updated), docs/domains/application/README.md (updated), docs/domains/onboarding/components/ignore-block/DOC.md (updated), docs/domains/onboarding/README.md (updated).

title: [BDL-061.55][tech-writer] S2b: the docs for unverifiable-is-not-clean, and the onboarding README the wave left stale
description:
Documentation pass for slice S2b (beads .45 .46 .47 .48 .49). The gate is currently RED and this bead is what turns it green - honestly, not by re-attesting.

STATE MEASURED BY THE COORDINATOR on the combined tree: `beadloom ci` rc 1; sync-check reports 286 pairs, 258 ok, 28 stale, 4 unchecked, 6 surface_drift. All 28 stale pairs are ONE document - `docs/domains/onboarding/README.md` - 27 `symbols_changed` and 1 `hash_changed`.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW, and it is worth stating in the record: every agent in this slice verified in a CLEAN ROOM (HEAD plus only its own files) because they shared a working tree. That is the right technique for isolating one bead's effect, and it structurally cannot see an interaction between beads. The first combined run was the coordinator's. Do not treat the staleness as anyone's mistake; treat the pattern as the finding.

WHAT THIS SLICE CHANGED, and the docs must now say it in one voice - the four fixes are one sentence, *unverifiable is not clean*:
  .46/.47 - a deleted declared doc is `missing` (exit 2, gate FAIL); a rebuilt index with no baseline is `unverified`, named and never counted fresh. The BASELINE MOVED OUT OF THE DATABASE: freshness now rests on git provenance, and the declared surface on the committed ledger `.beadloom/sync-surface.json`. That is an architectural change adopters must understand - `beadloom.db` is a derived cache again, and `--record-surface` is a deliberate act.
  .48 - a rule that cannot match reports itself, across all NINE rule types (the SPEC said seven, #172 said six, the loader has dispatched nine since BDL-051); `rules_inert` qualifies the summary so the rule count cannot over-claim.
  .49 - an expired `until:` is a finding and the suppressed count is printed on every run; the same deadline logic is shared with guard exclusions so `flow.yml` and `rules.yml` cannot promise different things.
  .45 - `docs-audit` reports what it did NOT verify: 2 of 9 declared facts verified, the other seven named, and 46 scanned / 33 not read / 1 counts-suppressed.

DO NOT RE-ATTEST TO GET GREEN. #163 exists because `sync-update` can silence sync-check without evidence. Read what actually changed in `onboarding/` and revise the README to match; if some pairs are genuinely unaffected by a rename the doc never mentions, re-attest THOSE deliberately and say in your bead comment which and why.

ALSO YOURS: the six `surface_drift` entries (#166 - `sync-update --all --yes` does not cover that path); and note in the record that 28 identical-looking gate lines for ONE document is #167 at gate scale, since the reader cannot tell one doc from twenty-eight.

Verification: exit codes and `--json`, never line counts (#148). Run pytest SEPARATELY from any gate command - a reindex in the same shell perturbs it (measured twice by the coordinator today).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:

          43/43 — the two TestSyncCheckNewPairs tests that were red because the tree was

  All 28 stale pairs were ONE document, docs/domains/onboarding/README.md, and only ONE of
  them (hash_changed, src/beadloom/services/commands/docs.py) had a file that changed. The
  other 27 read symbols_changed because _compute_symbols_hash is per ref_id over EVERY symbol
  annotated to the node: .45's four new private helpers in docs.py moved the node's hash, so

title: [BDL-061.50][dev] annotations the extractor cannot see: docstring annotation, directory source without a slash, deny rule blind to both
description:
Review .7 MAJOR 3 plus `.5`'s unfiled findings (a), (b), (c). One bead because they are one root: what counts as an ANNOTATED symbol, and what silently owns nothing.

(c) THE ROOT. Module-level `# beadloom:` annotations placed inside a module DOCSTRING are invisible to `extract_symbols`, which reads comment nodes only.

MAJOR 3 - THE WRONG ANSWER IT PRODUCES TODAY. `sync-check` reports ref_id `graph-reads` unchecked with reason `no_indexed_code`, details `src/beadloom/application/graph_reads.py`. That file IS indexed: 2 rows in file_index, 2 in code_imports, ~250 lines. What is absent is ANNOTATED symbols - `code_symbols` has 0 rows for it - because its `# beadloom:domain=application` / `feature=graph-reads` lines sit inside the docstring. The branch keys on `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM code_symbols` and reports that as "no indexed code".
This matters more than an ordinary mislabel: naming the residue with a reason is the mechanism that made COMPONENT BLINDNESS retirable - "clean means checked, and where it cannot, it says so". The ONE place in this repo where that reason is exercised sends the reader hunting for missing code in a fully indexed file. Rename to `no_annotated_symbols` and let the details carry the real cause.

(a) A node whose `source:` is a directory written WITHOUT a trailing slash owns no files at all - no `depends_on` edge, no sync pair, no symbol count. Zero of this repo's 67 sourced nodes are affected, which is exactly why it is adopter-only and silent: it cannot fail here, so nothing here will ever catch it.

(b) `deny` rules resolve an import's SOURCE node through `code_symbols` annotations only, so a file whose annotation the extractor cannot read is invisible to every deny rule. The #146 disease in the linter.

COMMON SHAPE, worth stating in the fix: all three are "the thing was not there, so there was nothing to check, so it is clean". Same equation as #146, #174 and #175. Decide once what the system does when a declared thing owns nothing - and make that answer reportable rather than silent.

Standing rules by name: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT.

comments.text: CHECKPOINT: claimed. Four measurements taken BEFORE any edit, on the live index: (1) 5 modules in src/ carry their beadloom annotations inside the module docstring (doc_sync/surface.py, application/graph_reads.py, infrastructure/{surface_registry,repository,atomic_io}.py); (2) 22 of 128 distinct import-source files (17%) are attributable to NO node via code_symbols annotations and are therefore invisible to every deny rule — among them services/cli.py, tui/widgets/{domain_list,node_detail}.py and application/graph_reads.py; (3) get_owned_code_files — the #146 fallback itself — queries code_symbols, so a module with ZERO top-level symbols (graph_reads.py is a 75-line pure re-export facade, 0 defs, 0 classes) is unreachable by BOTH the annotation path and the source-owned fallback, which is the real reason MAJOR 3's node is unchecked; (4) 190 indexed code files, 165 of them with symbols — 25 files a symbol-keyed reader cannot see. comments.author: v.zoologov

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: BITE CHECK, seven sabotages, each reverted by reverse edit with sha256 verified identical (CLEAN-ROOM REVERT). (1) extractor blind to docstrings again -> 4 red; (2) owned files keyed on code_symbols again -> 5 red; (3) unchecked reason keyed on code_symbols again -> 1 red; (4) attribution by annotation only -> 4 red; (5) no directory-source normalisation -> 4 red; (6) no report for a source naming no path -> 1 red; (7) file_index populated after sync_state again -> 6 red. MEASURED ON THE LIVE REPO after the fix (exit codes and --json, never line counts): lint --no-reindex --format json => 12 rules, 0 violations, 0 inert, 6 suppressed, 187 files scanned, files_unattributed 0 — the same verdict as the pre-change baseline, reached with a check that now covers all 187 files instead of the 106 the annotation key could reach. sync-check --json => unchecked 0 (was 4, one of them the graph-reads mislabel); pairs 286 -> 303. A FALSE RED I INTRODUCED AND KILLED BEFORE IT SHIPPED, recorded because it is the anti-pattern the bead warns about: my first attribution ranked candidates and then tried EACH of them until a rule matched — rule-shopping. On services/commands/setup.py, whose individual commands are annotated domain=onboarding, that reported the CLI's own mcp-server import as a domain-to-service breach at error severity, on a file whose derived depends_on edge says 'service'. The fix is that attribution is CONTAINMENT, not mention: a node is a candidate only if its source covers the file or it declares no source of its own (which is what a feature node is). An annotation naming a node whose source lies elsewhere is a cross-reference and is not containment.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit 635f125 on features/BDL-061-S3; merge-slot acquired before the commit and released after).

THE SENTENCE, since the bead asked for one decision stated once: A DECLARATION THAT OWNS NOTHING IS NAMED, WITH THE REASON, AND NEVER COUNTED AS CHECKED — and its corollary for the extractor, AN ANNOTATION THE EXTRACTOR CANNOT SEE IS NOT AN ABSENT ANNOTATION. Consistent with .46/.47 for pairs (a verdict says what it was green against) and .48 for rules (what cannot fire says so): here it is what cannot be PLACED that says so.

WHAT, per defect. (c) extract_symbols reads a module docstring's annotation lines, in the strict form only — comment marker at column 0, every line of the docstring considered. The strictness is the fix's second half: prose SHOWS the syntax with an indented sample and doc_sync/surface.py documents the in-doc <!-- beadloom:watches=... --> form inside its own docstring, so a loose reader would have made four modules silently claim nodes they only mention. Only Python declares docstring_types; every other language's module documentation IS a comment and was already read. MAJOR 3: the fix is NOT the recommended rename. get_owned_code_files — #146's own fallback — read code_symbols, so a module with no top-level def was unreachable through BOTH keys; it reads file_index now, the facade is genuinely PAIRED, and the reason no_indexed_code stops being exercised on an indexed file rather than being relabelled. The reason vocabulary is unchanged and each of its three words is now true of the index. (a) source is STAT'ed at load: a directory without a trailing slash is normalised (a file source is never widened), and a source naming no path is a reindex warning. This also repaired module-coverage, which required the slash in _node_dir_source_prefixes — an adopter's whole subtree read as uncovered at error severity. (b) deny rules attribute the source end by containment (annotation OR ownership), most specific first, replacing 'the first annotation key that happened to name a node'.

MEASURED (exit codes and --json only, #148). Live repo: lint --strict rc 0 — 12 rules, 0 violations, 0 inert, 6 suppressed, 187 files scanned, files_unattributed 0 (before: 22 of 128 import-source files reachable by no deny rule). sync-check unchecked 4 -> 0; pairs 286 -> 303, and the gate NAMES the growth ('declared surface grew 286 -> 303 pair(s)'). doctor rc 0, ruff rc 0, mypy rc 0. Full suite 5935 passed.

CLEAN ROOM, in those words: verified GREEN IN A CLEAN ROOM OVER 21 FILES — git archive HEAD extracted into a fresh directory, uv sync, then ONLY my 21 files copied in (the 4 domain READMEs were revised after this run and are the only files not in it). pytest: 5904 passed, 1 failed; lint --strict rc 0 (184 files scanned, 0 unattributed, 0 inert); doctor rc 0. The one failure is test_bead15_s3b_coverage::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh, and it is NOT a regression: a clean room is not a git checkout, so every one of the 297 pairs reads 'unverified' rather than 'ok' — .47's mechanism working. CONTROL: a second clean room at HEAD ALONE fails the same test identically. This is a different claim from 'green on the tree' (#181) and both are recorded.

STALENESS WAVE (#182), reported rather than bulk re-attested. 56 pairs went stale, 51 of them symbols_changed on sibling files nobody touched, because symbols_hash is per NODE: graph 24, rule-engine 9, infrastructure 8, context-oracle 8, code-indexer 1, graph-loader 1. I re-attested exactly six refs, and only after genuinely revising each one's doc in this bead — including four domain READMEs I had not planned to touch, two of which stated something my change makes FALSE (context-oracle: 'Annotations are parsed from comments'; application: the reindex step order ending '... take health snapshot -> populate file index'). Nothing was re-attested whose doc I did not read and change. Left alone and NOT mine: one stale pair, services/mcp.md <-> src/beadloom/services/commands/setup.py (hash_changed), from the concurrent agent's uncommitted 18-line edit — it is the only reason 'beadloom ci' is rc 1 on the shared tree; every other gate step PASSes. Also left alone: 6 surface_drift warnings (advisory, never a hard failure) — the 'graph' surface signature is a node+edge identity set and the concurrent wave added three nodes, so I did not re-record .beadloom/sync-surface.json while the surface is still moving.

FILES: see the commit. ACTIVE.md deliberately NOT edited — it is the coordinator's reconcile-from-bd surface and the tree is shared.

TODO / handed to review: (1) build_sync_state still pairs a node's owned files only when the node has NO annotated file at all ('annotated or owned', not 'annotated and owned'), so an unannotated module inside a node that HAS annotated files is indexed, owned, and paired with nothing. Same family, deliberately not absorbed: unioning them widens every domain's pair set and the staleness wave with it, and that is a scoping decision, not a correctness patch. (2) Attribution is per FILE, not per symbol — an import is attributed to the module rather than to the symbol whose lines enclose it; named as a limit in the rule-engine SPEC. (3) Found while measuring, unfiled: a fresh-DB rebuild re-baselines reference_state too, so surface_drift reads 0 on a clean database by construction — the #175 shape for the Layer-2 reference surface.

title: [BDL-061.45][dev] docs-audit is silently blind: three measured false-negative classes, and the audit reports green about facts it never checked
description:
Sweep result from beadloom-mr2l.44 (BDL-UX #169 fix). That bead fixed the extractor's
token boundary; this one is what the sweep found while looking for the SILENT half.

A false POSITIVE announces itself by failing the Gate — that is how #169 was found, twice.
A false NEGATIVE is silent. Three classes were MEASURED on this repo on 2026-08-23:

1. GROUPED NUMBERS WERE READ BY THEIR TAIL (fixed in .44, recorded here because it is the
   proof the class exists). "The graph holds 1,067 nodes." extracted as 067, compared equal
   to the project's node_count of 67, and was printed under "Fresh (verified)". The audit
   stamped a false claim VERIFIED. Symmetrically "The suite has 6,390 tests." — the TRUE
   statement — extracted as 390 and was reported stale.

2. COUNTS BELOW 10 ARE NEVER EXTRACTED for any *_count fact (scanner.py skips
   number_val < 10; also number_val <= 1 for every fact). Consequence measured here:
   language_count is 1, so that fact CANNOT be audited at all — any doc claim about it,
   right or wrong, is invisible, and the Gate reads green about it. rule_type_count (12)
   is one refactor away from the same fate.

3. A LAYER-1 MODIFIER WORD ANYWHERE IN THE +/-3 WORD WINDOW SUPPRESSES A GENUINE COUNT,
   even when it modifies a different noun: "The graph holds 316 edges, one per import."
   yields nothing, because "per" is in the window. The blocklist cannot tell what the
   modifier modifies.

Also measured, by design but silent: SPEC.md / CONTRIBUTING.md suppress all count facts and
docs/**/features/*/SPEC.md is excluded outright (26 of 72 doc files under docs/ are not
scanned at all). Nothing in the output says which files or which facts went unchecked.

WHOLE-REPO MEASUREMENT that makes the shape plain: the audit reports "13 mention(s) fresh"
and prints a Ground Truth block of NINE facts. All 13 verifications are the SAME fact
(mcp_tool_count). cli_command_count (39), edge_count (316), node_count (67),
rule_type_count (12), test_count (6390) and version (2.2.0) have ZERO findings — no doc in
the repo states the current version at all. A green docs-audit today means "one fact out of
nine was checked", and the output presents it as a clean bill of health.

THE FIX IS NOT MORE HEURISTICS, IT IS REPORTING THE SURFACE. Same shape as #170's third
piece and the S1 "unknown is not zero" rule:
- Report per-fact coverage: for every fact in the registry, how many mentions were found.
  A fact with zero mentions is NOT_COVERED, printed, and never counted as passing.
- Report the files whose counts were suppressed by the file-type heuristic, and why.
- Only then reconsider the <10 threshold and the modifier window, because with coverage
  reported their cost is visible instead of invisible.

Classes 2 and 3 are pinned as strict xfail tests in
tests/test_doc_scanner_tokenization.py::TestKnownBlindSpots, so they go LOUD (XPASS-strict
failure) the day the extractor stops being blind, instead of staying invisible. The
follow-up must delete those pins together with the fix.

Standing rules 1, 5.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: Filed as BDL-UX #173 in .claude/development/BDL-UX-Issues.md (measured 2026-08-23 during the beadloom-mr2l.44 sweep). Classes 2 and 3 are pinned as strict xfail in tests/test_doc_scanner_tokenization.py::TestKnownBlindSpots — delete the pins together with the fix.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: RED->GREEN. New tests/test_docs_audit_coverage.py (21 tests, 19 were red). Fixes: (1) per-fact coverage channel (verified/not_covered/unreadable) in new doc_sync/audit_coverage.py, surfaced in AuditResult, docs audit --json/rich, and the beadloom ci docs-audit line; (2) clause-scoped modifier AND keyword windows in scanner.py (fixes #173 class 3); (3) ScanSurface — every skipped doc named with its reason. MEASURED: repo audit 0 stale, 14 fresh, 2/9 facts verified (was: 9 declared, all 13 verifications of one fact and nothing said so). Separator set chosen by measurement: parens EXCLUDED because they cost the true verification in 'MCP tools (18):'. 3 more docs_audit.ignore entries retired (0 matches). Single-digit floor KEPT after re-measurement (14 extra mentions, 13 FPs) and now REPORTED as unreadable instead of silent.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED (commit 189d92f).

WHAT. The audit reports what it did NOT verify. Not three parser fixes — the same equation as
.46/.47 (unverifiable is not clean) and .48 (a rule that cannot match reports itself).

1. PER-FACT COVERAGE (new src/beadloom/doc_sync/audit_coverage.py, ~97 lines, feature=docs-audit).
   Every declared fact carries verified / not_covered (no document states it) / unreadable (the
   extractor cannot read a claim of that value, with the reason). Printed AGAINST the fact in the
   Ground Truth block, summarised in one line, exposed as AuditResult.coverage +
   .unverified_facts, in --json as coverage/unverified_facts/summary.{declared_fact_count,
   verified_fact_count,unverified_count,unreadable_count}, and on the beadloom ci step line:
   "14 mention(s) fresh; 2/9 declared fact(s) verified, NOT VERIFIED: cli_command_count, ...".
   A mention hidden by a docs_audit.ignore rule is deliberately NOT coverage (.44's lesson).
2. THE SCAN SURFACE IS PUBLISHED (DocScanner.resolve_surface -> ScanSurface). 33 unread documents
   named with the pattern that skipped them + the count-suppressed ones (--verbose, --json).
   resolve_paths is now a projection of it, so the two can never disagree.
3. CLAUSE-SCOPED MATCHING fixes #173 class 3. Both the modifier window AND the keyword window stop
   at , ; : and the dashes.

DECISIONS, each made by measurement and written into the code + SPEC:

* PARENTHESES ARE NOT SEPARATORS. Including them removes 2 more false positives but COSTS the
  true verification in ".beadloom/README.md:53  MCP tools (18):" — an appositive restates its
  noun. A lost true positive is the very silent false negative this bead exists to remove.
  Measured both ways: with parens 13 fresh (one genuine verification lost); without, 14 fresh,
  0 gained, 5 lost, all five confirmed FPs.
* THE SINGLE-DIGIT FLOOR STAYS. Re-measured the alternative (bind a small number to an
  immediately-following keyword): 14 extra mentions repo-wide, 13 of them ordinals ("5. Domain
  list"), table cells ("| 5 | tests |") and category breakdowns ("(4 tools):") — several would
  have failed the Gate, and quieting them would need exactly the ignore entries this bead was
  told not to add. So the floor is KEPT and REPORTED: language_count (value 1) reads unreadable
  by name. The strict xfail pinning it is retired because its premise ("someone will fix this")
  was wrong, not because the behaviour changed; the tokenization file now records why.
* NO WARN, NO FAIL FOR COVERAGE. Silence in the docs about a fact is not a defect in the code,
  and a WARN every project would carry on every run would spend the channel .47 just built for
  sync-check's missing baseline. The number rides on the line everybody reads instead, and
  --fail-if unverified>N (new metric, shared evaluator so the printed number and the exit code
  cannot disagree) is the opt-in.
* NO TOLERANCE, NO IGNORE ADDED. Three more docs_audit.ignore entries went dead under clause
  scoping (README.ru cli_command_count=14, getting-started + SECURITY mcp_tool_count=14, all
  "N tools: 14 over the graph" breakdowns) and were RETIRED, measured at 0 matches. 15 -> 12.

THE COVERAGE NUMBER, HONESTLY (the bead asked for this on the record). After the fix, on this
repo: 9 declared facts, 2 verified (mcp_tool_count x13, version x1), 6 not_covered — no document
states node_count, edge_count, test_count, framework_count, cli_command_count or rule_type_count
— and 1 unreadable (language_count = 1). So 8 of 9 are verifiABLE (a doc stating them would be
checked); exactly ONE is structurally unverifiable, and only because its true value is 1: the
extractor never reads 0/1, for the measured reason above. The residual, stated in the SPEC: a
claim written BELOW the floor is invisible whether right or wrong, whatever the fact's own value.
A green docs-audit now means "no document contradicted a fact, and here is which facts that
covers" — not "the documentation is current".

#179 -> ITS OWN BEAD (beadloom-mr2l.53, P2), and the coverage work is why. Two things make it
more than a registration: (a) the existing rule_type_count is a MISNOMER — it counts ROWS in the
rules table (12), not the loader's nine dispatch KINDS, and FACT_KEYWORDS maps rule/rule type/
rule kind all to it, so registering #179's number means splitting keywords and renaming a fact,
which breaks docs_audit.tolerances/ignore keys in every adopter's config; (b) the document that
states it, docs/domains/graph/features/rule-engine/SPEC.md, matches docs/**/features/*/SPEC.md
and is NEVER SCANNED — a registered fact would read not_covered forever while the SPEC drifted.
Both recorded in #179 as a MEASURED note.

FILED: BDL-UX #180 (MEDIUM) — a fact that fails to COLLECT is silently dropped from the declared
list, so coverage cannot report it (reproduced: cli_command_count vanishes in-process and the

title: [BDL-061.42][dev] S2/S3: the locale dimension's first run — 97 ASCII / 73 8-bit failures from text I/O without an explicit encoding
description:
WHAT THE DIMENSION FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN. BDL-061.38 added a CI leg that runs the whole suite with the locale VARIED. Before pushing it, I ran the same three legs locally in one Linux container (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim, tree = `git archive HEAD` + .38's files), changing nothing between runs but the locale, so the number that matters is the DELTA, not any leg's colour:

  LEG BASE  LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, no knobs        ENC utf-8    utf-8      ->  2 failed / 5611 passed / 115s
  LEG C     LC_ALL=C      + the two knobs   ENC ascii    ascii      -> 99 failed / 5514 passed / 110s
  LEG L1    LC_ALL=en_US.ISO-8859-1 + knobs ENC iso8859-1 iso8859-1 -> 75 failed / 5538 passed / 109s

The 2 baseline failures are ROOT-USER artifacts of running in a container (test_atomic_io_call_sites::test_nonwritable_dir_raises_and_leaves_no_partial, test_setup_rules_fix::test_returns_none_for_unreadable_file — root ignores the permission bits those tests set). They appear in all three legs and will NOT appear on ubuntu-latest, which does not run as root. So the locale-attributable delta is 97 (ASCII) and 73 (8-bit).

THE TWO ROWS FIND DIFFERENT DEFECTS — this is the measurement that settles .38's open question about whether the second row earns its cost, and the answer is yes, empirically rather than by argument. The sets are NOT nested: the entire `test_cli_hooks.py` block (18 rows) and `test_cli_active_sync_hardening` fail ONLY under the 8-bit locale; `test_e2e_wave3`, `test_doc_generator`, `test_mcp_process_tools`, `test_guards_parity` and most of `test_onboarding` (11 rows vs 1) fail ONLY under ASCII; `test_config_sync::TestAgenticFlowDrift` fails on 2 of 8 parametrised rows under ASCII and on all 8 under 8-bit. That is exactly the predicted shape: ASCII RAISES on an undecodable byte (loud), an 8-bit codec accepts every byte and MANGLES it (silent), so each row reaches code the other cannot.

THE LIKELY ROOT CAUSE, one sentence: text I/O without an explicit `encoding=`. `Path.write_text()` / `Path.read_text()` / `open()` default to `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`, so every generator that writes UTF-8 content (AGENTS.md and the MCP tool table, the doc generator, the rules/adapter writers, `install-hooks`, the bootstrap YAML + README ingestion) and every reader that reads it back is locale-dependent today. This is the SAME family as .36's defect (which was fixed at one call site), and the same family as .37's probe decode — but at ~40 call sites rather than one.

SCOPE. Not "make the leg green" — that invites the pin. Per file/site: decide whether the byte stream is a CONTRACT (UTF-8 by definition: JSON, YAML, generated markdown, hook scripts — pass `encoding="utf-8"` explicitly) or genuinely the user's LOCALE (almost nothing here is). Then fix the site, not the test. Where a TEST rather than the product is locale-assuming, say so explicitly in the test.

SUGGESTED ORDER (highest blast radius first):
1. The generators/writers: onboarding/scanner/agents_md.py + rules_gen.py, onboarding/doc_generator.py, onboarding/role_adapters.py, guard_hooks.py, config_sync.py, and the install-hooks writer — these produce files an adopter's repo keeps.
2. The graph/YAML readers behind test_s2_move_regression + test_onboarding::test_generated_yaml_is_valid + test_readme_ingestion.
3. The guard rows for non-ASCII targets (src/файл.py, emoji, homoglyphs, Unicode whitespace) — overlaps .36's item 2 (the shape gate's own criterion is ambient: `os.fsencode` uses the filesystem encoding, so the ACCEPTED SET changes with the locale). Decide the intended answer in the SPEC first; this is the one place where the current behaviour might be correct and the TEST is what assumes UTF-8.
4. Re-run the three legs and report the new delta, not the new total.

SEQUENCING WITH BRANCH PROTECTION — READ BEFORE RUNNING `beadloom setup-branch-protection`. .38 added `tests-locale (C)` and `tests-locale (en_US.ISO-8859-1)` to DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS, but a constant is not live protection: the repo's actual required checks only change when someone RUNS that command. Do not run it until these legs have been observed green at least once, or `main` becomes unmergeable on this backlog. The leg landing red on the PR is the intended signal and blocks nothing by itself.

ACCEPTANCE: the delta between the UTF-8 leg and each locale leg is zero, and every fix is at a call site with a stated reason for its encoding rather than a test that was taught to expect the mangling.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT — THE DELTA IS ZERO ON BOTH LEGS, AND IT TOOK THREE DIFFERENT DECISIONS RATHER THAN ONE. Final three-leg run, same container, same method, tree = the clean room committed at 9acfd8d + only my 40 files:
  BASE  utf-8/utf-8      -> 4 failed / 6156 tests / 27 skipped / 131s
  C     ascii/ascii      -> 4 failed / 113s   => 0 locale-attributable (was 108)
  L1    iso8859-1/…      -> 4 failed / 113s   => 0 locale-attributable (was 83)
The 4 are the SAME set in all three legs (the 2 root-user container artifacts + 2 sync-check pairs that were stale mid-work and are now re-baselined), so the delta — the only number that means anything here — is 0/0.
THE POPULATION SPLIT IN THREE, and the split is the finding rather than the count:
(1) 72 rows = TEXT I/O WITH NO STATED CODEC, contract = UTF-8. One product call site did 24 of them on its own: install-hooks' _write_hook, whose template carries an em dash, so on an ASCII image the command ABORTED having written no hook and on an 8-bit one it would have written a mojibake byte into an executable script an adopter keeps. Plus 4 subprocess(text=True) seams and ~45 test-side reads of artifacts the product had already written correctly as UTF-8.
(2) 36 rows = THE FILESYSTEM'S ENCODING, and here the PRODUCT WAS RIGHT ON EVERY IMAGE while the tests hard-coded the answer a UTF-8 machine gives. The guard's accepted path shape ends in 'encodable for this filesystem' (os.fsencode) BY DESIGN — a string the filesystem cannot encode names no file. Fixed in the tests, both directions asserted, never skipped: tests/filesystem_names.py::filesystem_can_name asks the codec by name (not os.fsencode, so it cannot agree by sharing the defect) and each row asserts INSIDE where the name is spellable and MALFORMED-with-the-stated-cause where it is not.
(3) 4 rows = THE TERMINAL, where UTF-8 is the WRONG answer — see the next comment. Different decision again: keep the operator's codec, fix the error handler.
ALSO MEASURED AND WORTH CARRYING: through the REAL binary a non-ASCII argv value never fails — argv arrives surrogate-escaped and os.fsencode round-trips it, so 'guard --context path=src/файл.py' is ACCEPTED under LC_ALL=C. Only a str built INSIDE the process is refused. Several fixtures were asserting the second while only the first can happen in production; they now build their branch/author/directory from the BYTES a real caller sends (as_the_process_receives), which makes them image-independent instead of image-dependent.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TWO PRODUCT DEFECTS THE DIMENSION FOUND THAT NOBODY HAD NAMED, both measured before being fixed, both outside 'pass encoding=utf-8'.
A. THE INVERSE OF .40, in graph/federation/export.py — .40's own fix created it. That module decodes every git answer as utf-8+surrogateescape, and its note claims 'it is what os.fsdecode uses, so ... both sides of that comparison are decoded alike'. That sentence is true ONLY where the filesystem encoding IS utf-8, i.e. everywhere except the images the locale legs exist for. MEASURED on a real LC_ALL=C Linux image with the repo at .../проект: rev-parse --show-toplevel came back as real Cyrillic while Python's own project_root held the surrogate-escaped form of the SAME bytes, and Path(toplevel).resolve() raised UnicodeEncodeError OUT OF beadloom export — past the 'except OSError', which cannot see a raise that happens in its caller. FIX: the git seam now captures BYTES and each caller states its own rule — a sha/URL is text (utf-8), a PATH is read with os.fsdecode, which is the only rule under which both sides of that comparison agree. Container sabotage (_git_path -> _run_git): 3 rows FAILED under the ASCII leg, 0 with the fix; on macOS both pass either way, which is exactly why it was invisible.
B. THE CLI DIES ON A TERMINAL THAT CANNOT SPELL A GLYPH — the 8-bit row's unique yield, and the reason that row keeps earning its cost. MEASURED under LC_ALL=en_US.ISO-8859-1 on BOTH Debian and this macOS: 'python -m beadloom.ai_agents.ai_techwriter --help' exits 1 with UnicodeEncodeError on the → in its own help text, and a PASSING 'beadloom guard working-branch' writes NOTHING to stdout because the verdict line carries an em dash — a guard whose PASS is silent cannot be told from one that never ran, which is the exact failure this epic exists to remove. WHY THE ASCII ROW IS GREEN AND THE 8-BIT ONE IS NOT: under the C/POSIX locale CPython already hands sys.stdout the backslashreplace handler; a NAMED 8-bit locale is a real locale, gets strict, and raises. 'Non-UTF-8' and 'ASCII' are not the same environment, and this is the first defect that could ONLY be found by the second row.
THE DECISION, stated because it is the opposite of the rest of the bead: a terminal is the ONE stream whose codec genuinely belongs to the operator, so writing utf-8 into a latin-1 terminal would only move the damage. The codec is untouched; the ERROR HANDLER goes strict -> backslashreplace (CPython's own C-locale policy, applied everywhere). New component infrastructure/console_streams.py, applied at each Click ENTRY OBJECT (services/commands/_root.TolerantOutputGroup, ai_techwriter/cli._TolerantOutputCommand) rather than in a callback — Click answers --help while PARSING, so a callback never runs for it, and --help is one of the two measured failures. beadloom.services.cli:main stays the console-script target, so no import path an adopter or a test uses moved. backslashreplace not replace: U+FFFD says a character was there and nothing about which; \uXXXX names it and can be grepped.

title: [BDL-061.39][chore] S2/S3: a Windows CI leg — but only after the six skipif(win32) guard tests are made non-vacuous
description:
WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT PART OF .38. .38 added an environment DIMENSION by VARYING the locale: same runner, same interpreter, one variable changed, and the leg is cheap (~4 runner-minutes, 0 added wall-clock because it fans out in parallel). Windows is a different kind of change and is priced differently, so bundling it would have made .38 unmergeable for reasons that have nothing to do with the locale.

THE DEFECT IT ADDRESSES (item 3 of .36's environment-dependence deliverable): six guard tests carry `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')` and CI has no Windows leg, so EVERY Windows claim rests on reasoning. The backslash refusal in `application/guards/paths.py` exists FOR Windows harnesses and has never executed on one. A skip that can never fail is the same shape as the vacuous loop test .36 repaired — and the same shape as the vacuous `LC_ALL=C` leg .38 measured.

WHY IT IS NOT CHEAP, stated so the cost is visible rather than discovered:
1. ADDING THE LEG DOES NOT UN-VACUUM THE SKIPS. Those six tests would still SKIP on windows-latest — that is what `skipif(win32)` means. Someone must first decide, per test, what the correct Windows behaviour IS and rewrite the assertion; that is dev work on `src/`+`tests/`, not CI configuration. A Windows leg added without that work buys a green check that proves nothing, which is exactly the failure mode this family of beads exists to stop.
2. windows-latest bills at 2x minutes and is the slowest runner; the suite is 5599 tests. Expect ~8-12 minutes, i.e. it becomes the pipeline's critical path — .38's legs did not change wall-clock at all.
3. The first run is very likely red for reasons unrelated to the guards (path separators, sqlite/WAL file locking — .36 already found cross-test connection leaks — tree-sitter grammar wheels, `BEADLOOM_REQUIRE_LANGUAGE_GRAMMARS=1`, temp-dir cleanup on locked files). Triaging that is the bulk of the work and none of it is the thing we came for.

SCOPE WHEN TAKEN, in this order (the order matters — 3 before 4, or the leg is theatre):
1. Judge each of the six `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')` tests: state the Windows behaviour it should assert, or delete it as a test that cannot be written.
2. Rewrite them to assert that behaviour (the backslash refusal first — it is the one that exists FOR Windows).
3. Add a `windows-latest` leg, ONE python version, whole suite, `fail-fast: false`. Triage the fallout; anything not a guard defect gets a named, reasoned xfail or a fix.
4. Only once observed green: add its check-run name to `branch_protection.DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` (a required context that never reports leaves main unmergeable — the lockout guard `test_required_contexts_match_ci_yml_check_runs` will demand it as soon as the job exists, so steps 3 and 4 land together).
5. Also decide there whether the vendored `onboarding/templates/ai_techwriter/*` pipelines and `.gitlab-ci.yml` should mirror the platform dimension; .38 deliberately left the templates alone (see its final comment).

ACCEPTANCE: no guard test skips on the Windows leg for a reason nobody has judged; the backslash refusal has executed on a real Windows runner at least once; the leg is either required or its absence from the required set is argued in writing.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: RED->GREEN done, and the ORDER the bead insisted on was honoured. (1) THE SIX ARE NON-VACUOUS: all six were platform-INDEPENDENT in their assertions; the mark's reason ('POSIX symlink semantics') misnamed the obstacle. Windows HAS symlinks and Path.resolve follows them; what a process may lack is SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege — a per-PROCESS capability, measurable in ~1ms. New tests/symlink_capability.py probes it for real (creates a file link AND a directory link, reads both back) and the five marks (six collected rows — one is parametrised x2) now skip on the MEASURED refusal, carrying the OS's own words. So 6/6 RUN on a runner that holds the privilege. Zero needed a Windows kernel; zero were deleted. (2) THE LEG GOES IN: ci.yml job tests-windows (windows-latest, py3.13, extras byte-identical to tests, whole suite, no --cov, REQUIRE_LANGUAGE_GRAMMARS=1, not in ai-techwriter's needs) + DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS 9->10 + the vendored template (else adopter lockout, .38 §5). (3) ANTI-VACUITY, the half that is this bead's whole point: the in-CI probe fails the leg TWO ways — VACUOUS (not Windows at all) and DEGRADED (it IS Windows but cannot create a link, in which case the six rows capability-skip again and ~6000 unrelated tests carry the green). tests/test_ci_windows_dimension.py EXECUTES that heredoc out of ci.yml. 10 sabotages, all FAILED never ERROR, each hitting its own row, every restore sha256-verified.

comments.text: API CHANGE: `onboarding.branch_protection.DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` grew from 9 to 10 entries — `tests-windows` added. Adopter-visible twice: it is the payload `beadloom setup-branch-protection` PUTs in ANY repo, and it is the documented default of the repeatable `--check` option. NOT auto-applied — the live protection changes only when the owner re-runs the command, which is the whole sequencing note (see below). Forced, not chosen: the repo's lockout guard test_required_contexts_match_ci_yml_check_runs DERIVES the check-run names from ci.yml and asserts derived == required, so the constant had to move the moment the job existed; and .38 §5's lesson made the vendored template move with it, or every scaffolded repo gets a required check its pipeline never produces. SEQUENCING, the one thing that must not be missed: tests-windows WILL BE RED on the first push and that blocks nothing by itself, because the constant is not live protection. DO NOT run `beadloom setup-branch-protection` on this repo until the leg is observed green — main's live set is still the seven pre-.38 contexts. No `continue-on-error` was added to avoid this (a check that cannot fail is theatre, which is the thing being fixed), and the suite fails if anyone adds one. Docs updated in this bead: docs/domains/onboarding/README.md (x3 incl. the literal tuple), docs/services/cli.md (the --check default + the 'live constraint' paragraph, whose REASON has moved — the locale legs are green since .42, tests-windows is now the red one), docs/guides/agentic-flow.md, docs/guides/ai-techwriter.md (+ a new paragraph on the sixth verify job and how a Linux-only adopter drops it), docs/guides/multi-agent-development.md + .ru.md (9 → 10 in the enumeration, the table row, the job-order row and the live-protection paragraph, in both languages). Docs the tech-writer should still CHECK, deliberately not rewritten: the pipeline mermaid diagrams in multi-agent-development.md/.ru.md (~lines 162, 270, 483) still draw the parallel verify set as gate/tests/tests-locale/site-build — there is now a FIFTH parallel verify job — and ai-techwriter.md's prose still calls tests-locale 'a fifth verify job' in one place where the count is now visibly a series.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.39] — commit 98bcb0d on features/BDL-061-S4 (18 files, +1389/-53). NOT pushed; the coordinator pushes and reads CI.

=== 1. THE SPLIT THE BEAD ASKED FOR, PER TEST. Six of six became non-vacuous; NONE genuinely needed a Windows kernel and none was deleted.
The mark named the wrong obstacle, and naming it wrongly is what made the skip permanent. Windows HAS symbolic links, os.symlink has taken target_is_directory since 3.2 (these tests already passed it), and Path.resolve follows them there exactly as here. What a Windows PROCESS may lack is SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege — granted by Developer Mode or an elevated shell, different between two Windows machines, decidable in ~1ms. So 'POSIX symlink semantics' was a claim about the OS model where the true statement was about this process's capability.
  1. TestTraversalCannotBypassAnExclusion::test_a_symlink_out_of_an_excluded_directory_is_guarded — capability, not semantics.
  2. TestSymlinksInBothDirections::test_a_link_into_the_excluded_tree_is_excluded — same.
  3. TestSymlinksInBothDirections::test_an_exclusion_stops_applying_when_its_directory_is_a_symlink — same; it already passed target_is_directory=True, i.e. the author had ALREADY written it for Windows and then marked it off.
  4/5. TestASymlinkLoopEndsInAVerdictAndNeverInATraceback::test_a_real_loop_comes_back_as_a_scope_whatever_this_platform_does[a] and [a/x.py] — the strongest case: the test NAME asserts platform-independence and the mark denied it. (These two are why five marks are six collected rows.)
  6. ...::test_the_guard_reaches_a_verdict_through_a_real_loop — same.
NEW tests/symlink_capability.py takes the skip on a MEASURED refusal: it creates a real file link AND a real directory link in a temp dir and READS BOTH BACK, so a filesystem that 'supports' links by copying is refused too (that state is worse than a skip — the rows would RUN and assert the wrong thing). The reason a reader sees carries the OS's own error text plus what to do about it. FAKES PROVE FAKES applied to a predicate: it never asks sys.platform or os.name anything.
WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: add monkeypatched-resolve doubles so the rows 'run' where links are unavailable. Injecting Path.resolve would replace the very thing under test — the existing injected rows in that class are justified because an interpreter genuinely will not RAISE, which is a different case from an OS that genuinely will not LINK.

=== 2. THE THREE SKIPS THAT DO NEED A POSIX KERNEL, judged rather than left
test_decoding_symmetry.py (module, 23 rows) and test_guard_probes_encoding.py (module, 19 rows): the fixtures write a raw 0xFF byte into file names, git ref names and commit metadata and replace PATH with a shebang stub. NTFS stores names as UTF-16 and cannot hold a lone byte; Windows has no shebang mechanism. The FIXTURE cannot be built — a different fact from an assertion being wrong.
test_atomic_io_call_sites.py::TestEdgeCases::test_nonwritable_dir_raises_and_leaves_no_partial: Windows derives directory writability from ACLs, not from the mode bits Path.chmod sets, so the row cannot reproduce its own precondition. (Same reason it already FAILS as root in a container — .38 measured it.)
Plus one darwin row from .38 (test_shipped_env_is_genuinely_non_utf8_on_linux), kept in the same ledger because it is the same question.
So the Windows-skip surface is 49 rows, not six — 43 of them added AFTER .36 counted, by .37/S3b, and each is now stated.

=== 3. THE LEDGER, so the class cannot come back
tests/test_windows_dimension.py AST-scans tests/ for any pytest.mark.skipif whose condition mentions sys.platform and requires an entry in JUDGED_WINDOWS_SKIPS naming the facility. There is NO 'convenience' verdict — re-entering that state requires deleting an assertion, not adding a line. Parsed from SOURCE rather than collected from pytest on purpose: a mark that is inert on this platform is invisible to collection, which is exactly the property that let six sit unexamined. A companion requires strict=True on any platform xfail (a lax xfail passes whether the prediction holds or not — the skip's failure mode wearing a different word).

=== 4. THE LEG: YES, AND WHAT IT COSTS
ONE row, windows-latest, python 3.13, extras byte-identical to the tests leg, whole suite, no --cov, REQUIRE_LANGUAGE_GRAMMARS=1, no continue-on-error, outside ai-techwriter's needs. No matrix, so there is no fail-fast question — there is no sibling to cancel.
COST, priced like .38 priced the locale rows: ~8-14 min (6100 tests, heavy tempdir+sqlite work, which is where Windows is slowest) at GitHub's 2x Windows multiplier => ~16-28 runner-minutes per PR against ~8 for both locale rows. Unlike those rows it is NOT free in wall-clock: the ubuntu legs finish in ~4 min, so this is the new critical path and PR-to-merge latency roughly triples. Keeping it out of ai-techwriter's needs puts that cost on the MERGE, not on the doc refresh.
DOES IT EARN IT: yes, and on evidence rather than principle. The locale dimension has already repaid its own cost (.42: 108 ASCII / 83 8-bit locale-attributable failures fixed, a git-hook writer that could not write on a non-UTF-8 image, a federation export raising past its own handler, a --help exiting 1). Windows is a LARGER delta than a locale — separators, absolute-path parsing, case-folding, file locking and process spawning all change at once — over a src/ that contains ZERO sys.platform and ZERO os.name branches anywhere (measured). A product with no platform branches is either genuinely portable or has never been asked, and an all-green Linux pipeline cannot tell those apart.
THE ONE HONEST OBJECTION, stated because it is real: the leg is not on-thesis for every ADOPTER the way a non-UTF-8 container is. The lockout invariant forces the vendored template to carry it, so the template comment names the cost and spells the exact two-part opt-out (delete the job AND drop the --check context; deleting the job alone IS the lockout).

=== 5. THE LEG CANNOT GO VACUOUS — the lock this bead is actually about
The in-CI probe fails two ways. VACUOUS: not Windows at all (a runs-on edit) — everyone would catch that. DEGRADED: it IS Windows but this process cannot create a link, in which case the six rows capability-skip AGAIN, ~6000 unrelated tests carry the green, and NOBODY is told the leg stopped covering the thing it was bought for. That second half is the whole bead, restated at the CI layer. Third state also covered: a link that is created but does not follow. tests/test_ci_windows_dimension.py EXECUTES that heredoc (parsed out of ci.yml) against injected platforms and injected WinError 1314, so a shell script inside a YAML string is covered and cannot drift from the workflow. shell: bash is asserted too and is load-bearing, not style — the DEFAULT shell on windows-latest is pwsh, which has no POSIX heredoc.
EXPECT IT RED ON THE FIRST RUN, and the legend is in ci.yml next to the job so a reader of the PR meets it: the value is the delta between legs, never any leg's colour.

=== 6. FINDINGS FILED, NOT FIXED (the standing rule: a Windows failure is a bead, never a test adjustment)
.60 (P1, bug) — rejection_reason refuses ANY backslash unconditionally, so on Windows the guard refuses the spelling every Windows harness natively produces: every edit becomes MALFORMED -> error/exit 2, and the stated remediation ('supply the target as a POSIX path') is not something the harness can do. Its own justification is false there: 'separates directories on the harness's platform and is an ordinary file-name character on this one' describes TWO platforms, and the guard runs in the harness's own process tree — there is no deployment where they differ. Measured BY PROXY with PureWindowsPath (win parts ('src','app.py') vs posix ('src\\app.py',)), pinned, and carried as a STRICT xfail so the runner ADJUDICATES the prediction — if it unexpectedly PASSES on Windows my reasoning was wrong and the suite says so. Same bead carries the SPEC's drive-letter paragraph, which blames 'this build of Beadloom' for what is the platform.
.61 (P2, task) — .6's uncounted 26-skipped-vs-11 delta. MY DECISION: its OWN bead, not this one, and the reason is mechanical rather than tidiness — my ledger reaches skips whose condition names sys.platform, and those fifteen are CAPABILITY/ENVIRONMENT-conditional (root ignoring mode bits, an absent binary, an ungenerated dogfood artifact). Widening the ledger to every conditional skip would have put a hundred entries in one dict and blurred 'the platform leg exists' with 'every skip is judged'. The bead asks for the right thing instead: diff the skip POPULATION between legs (the data already exists on 7 legs and nobody looks at it), classify each row, and decide in writing whether the delta becomes a ratchet or a printed number.

=== 7. SABOTAGES (rule 5: FAILED never ERROR, numbers, reverse-edit restore sha256-verified) — 10, all bit
revert one capability mark to skipif(win32) -> 2 FAILED/34 passed; xfail strict=False -> 1/35; drop the probe's read-back -> 1/35; delete ci.yml's DEGRADED half -> 1/35; delete its VACUOUS half -> 1/35; narrow the leg to '-k guard --cov' -> 1 FAILED/16; drop shell: bash -> 1/35; diverge the extras -> 1/35; rename the template's job -> 2 FAILED/34; continue-on-error: true -> 1/35. No sabotage produced an ERROR or 'no tests ran'. NOTE ON MY OWN PROCESS: the -k narrowing sabotage passed 36/36 on its first two anchors because both matched the tests-locale job (identical text, earlier in the file) — the sabotage was testing the wrong job, not a weak assertion. Re-run against the tests-windows block explicitly, it bit. A sabotage that passes is a claim about the sabotage before it is a claim about the test.

=== 8. GATES
Local suite 6250 passed / 11 skipped / 1 xfailed / 0 failed. ruff clean, mypy --strict clean (198 files) on my files.
GREEN IN A CLEAN ROOM OVER 16 FILES (#181), then re-verified on the COMMITTED tree: git archive HEAD into an isolated checkout -> ruff rc 0 over all of src/ and tests/, mypy 196 files clean, pytest 6174 passed / 16 skipped / 1 xfailed, beadloom ci rc 0 (reindex PASS, lint PASS 12 rules 0 violations, sync-check WARN 'no baseline — index rebuilt', docs-audit PASS, config-check PASS, doctor PASS 13 checks 0 errors).
THE ONE CLEAN-ROOM RED IS NOT MINE AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: test_bead15_s3b_coverage::TestSyncCheckNewPairs::test_all_new_node_pairs_are_fresh reads the live sync_state, which lives in the gitignored index, so a from-scratch checkout reports every pair 'unverified'. Built a second clean room from PRISTINE HEAD with none of my files: it fails TWO rows there (test_new_node_docs_are_tracked_pairs as well), i.e. my tree fails strictly FEWER. Exit codes and --json throughout, never line counts (#148); pytest run separately from the gate.
SHARED-TREE NOTE, flagged not hidden (.38's mistake, not repeated): the shared index reports symbols_changed across onboarding/ and graph/ against files I never touched — that is the sibling's in-flight symbol extraction. I did NOT run sync-update on any ref: re-baselining 'onboarding' would tell them composer.py/role_composer.py docs are fresh mid-edit, which is the masking failure mode. My evidence does not depend on the shared index. Nothing outside my 18 paths was staged; no git add -A.

=== 9. FILES
ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml, src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/ai_techwriter/github-workflow.yml
src: onboarding/branch_protection.py (contexts 9->10 + the reasoning), services/commands/setup.py (--check help + docstring)

title: [BDL-061.38][chore] S2: add an environment DIMENSION to CI — vary the locale rather than pin it
description:
The one-line recommendation closing .36's deliverable, filed so it is not lost: 'the cheapest structural defence is a CI matrix leg that runs the existing suite with LC_ALL=C - VARYING the locale, NOT pinning it. Everything in that list except the Windows item would have been caught by an environment DIMENSION rather than by a new test.'

WHY VARY AND NOT PIN. Pinning a UTF-8 locale in CI would have made .36's defect invisible to us while shipping it to every adopter running in a container - which is the default deployment. The value is in the DIFFERENCE between legs, not in any one leg being green.

WHAT THIS BUYS, measured rather than argued: .36's locale defect failed on all four Python versions and was invisible to a 5574-test local suite; the symlink-loop defect was invisible because the one Python the owner runs (3.13) does not raise where 3.10-3.12 do. Both are dimension failures, not coverage failures - more tests on one platform would not have found either.

SCOPE TO DECIDE, with reasons:
- Which legs. `LC_ALL=C` is the cheap high-value one. A genuinely non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. one where `locale.getpreferredencoding` is not UTF-8) is what .37 needs and is harder to arrange, since PEP 538/540 coercion defeats the obvious spellings - say whether it is worth the cost.
- Whether the whole suite or the guard subset. The whole suite is the honest answer and .36 measured it at ~110s locally; a subset is cheaper and silently narrows the dimension to the code we already suspect.
- Windows (item 3 of the deliverable): six guard tests carry `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')` and CI has no Windows leg, so every Windows claim rests on reasoning - including the backslash refusal, which exists FOR Windows harnesses and has never executed on one. A skip that can never fail is the same shape as the vacuous loop test .36 just fixed. Decide whether a Windows leg is in scope here or is its own bead; do not leave it implied.

comments.text: CHECKPOINT: RED->GREEN done. tests/test_ci_locale_dimension.py (10 tests) written first, 7 failed against the unchanged ci.yml. ci.yml now declares job `tests-locale` — single axis locale: [C, en_US.ISO-8859-1], python 3.13, byte-identical extras to the `tests` leg, locale env on the SUITE step only, whole suite (no -k/-m/--cov). MEASURED on python:3.12-slim, which is the load-bearing fact: bare LC_ALL=C gives preferred=utf-8 fs=utf-8 utf8_mode=1 (PEP 540 auto-enable) — the bead's own one-line recommendation, spelled naively, is a VACUOUS leg. LC_ALL=C + PYTHONUTF8=0 gives ANSI_X3.4-1968/ascii/utf8_mode=0. PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 kept as belt-and-braces for images where the PEP 538 half bites. 6 sabotages, all FAILED never ERROR, each hitting exactly its own test, restored sha256 OK: drop PYTHONUTF8=0 (2 failed), pin LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 (2), narrow to -k guard (1), drop the 8-bit row (1), neuter the probe step (1), diverge the extras (1).

comments.text: API CHANGE: `onboarding.branch_protection.DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS` grew from 7 to 9 entries — `tests-locale (C)` and `tests-locale (en_US.ISO-8859-1)` added. NOT auto-applied: the live protection only changes when the owner re-runs the command, which matters here — see the SEQUENCING note in the completion comment. Why required at all: the repo's own lockout guard (test_required_contexts_match_ci_yml_check_runs) DERIVES the check-run names from ci.yml and asserts derived == required, so a real check that gates nothing is a failure by construction; and a dimension leg that cannot block a merge is advisory, which is the shape .36's defect slipped through. comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT — SHARED-TREE SIDE EFFECT, FLAGGING IT RATHER THAN HIDING IT. After committing 906a818 I ran `beadloom reindex` on the SHARED working tree to reach the sync-check fixpoint for my two changed source files. That was a mistake in a three-agent wave and I am recording it: the reindex ran against .5's in-flight changes to application/reindex/* and graph/import_resolver.py, and the resulting index now reports the ENTIRE onboarding domain (and agent-prime, role-adapters, flow-config, guard-hooks…) as `symbols_changed` against files nobody in this wave has touched. That is the sibling's in-progress symbol extraction, not doc drift. I did NOT try to repair it by mass re-baselining — marking those pairs synced would tell .5 their docs are fresh when they have not been written yet, which is precisely the masking failure mode in the sync-check reason-masking rule. The index (.beadloom/beadloom.db) is gitignored, so nothing of this is in the commit; it will settle when .5 reindexes on their finished code. ALSO: `beadloom sync-update <ref>` is INTERACTIVE — it prompts 'Open <doc> in editor? [Y/n]' and aborts under a non-tty agent, so it cannot be used to re-baseline non-interactively. That is a real UX gap for the agentic flow (a sibling of BDL-UX #147 'lint mutates the index') and is worth its own BDL-UX entry. MY OWN EVIDENCE does not depend on the shared index: a clean-DB `beadloom ci` on an isolated `git archive HEAD` + only my files gave rc 0 — reindex PASS, lint PASS 12 rules 0 violations, sync-check PASS 272 pairs fresh, docs-audit PASS 13 mentions fresh, config-check PASS, doctor PASS 20 checks clean.
