comments.text: CHECKPOINT — THE EXPERIMENT THE BEAD IS ABOUT, RUN LOCALLY BEFORE ANY PUSH. I ran the whole suite THREE times inside one Linux container (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.13-bookworm-slim, the tree = git archive HEAD + only my files), changing nothing but the locale, so the DELTA between legs is the measurement rather than any leg's colour. LEG BASE (LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, no knobs): ENC utf-8 utf-8 utf8_mode=0 -> 2 failed / 5611 passed / 115s. Both failures are ROOT-USER artifacts of running in a container (test_atomic_io_call_sites::test_nonwritable_dir_raises_and_leaves_no_partial and test_setup_rules_fix::test_returns_none_for_unreadable_file — root ignores the permission bits those two tests create), they are present in EVERY leg, and they will not appear on ubuntu-latest, which does not run as root. They are the baseline noise the delta is taken against. LEG C (LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0): ENC ascii ascii utf8_mode=0 — i.e. the spelling shipped in ci.yml genuinely produces an ASCII interpreter on a real Linux image, which is the whole premise. Suite result for legs C and en_US.ISO-8859-1 lands in the completion comment.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CORRECTION to my earlier checkpoint — I was wrong about the tool, and the wrong claim should not sit in this bead's history. I wrote that 'beadloom sync-update <ref> is INTERACTIVE and cannot be used to re-baseline non-interactively'. It is not: `sync-update` has `-y/--yes` for exactly that (and `--all` for a fixpoint loop). I had simply invoked it without the flag and read the editor prompt as the only behaviour. Withdraw that as a UX finding; the real (much smaller) observation is only that the default is the interactive path, so an agent that guesses gets an abort rather than an error telling it the flag exists. Having established the shared index was healthy again (a sibling had reindexed), I then re-baselined ONLY my own refs: `sync-update onboarding -y` (28 pairs) and `sync-update branch-protection -y` (1 pair). Deliberately NOT `--all`, and deliberately NOT `mcp-server`: that ref's stale set includes `services/mcp.md <- bd_seam.py`, which is .37's in-flight change, and re-baselining it would tell them their doc is fresh when they have not written it. Two stale pairs therefore remain and BOTH are for .37 to settle: services/mcp.md against bd_seam.py (theirs) and against commands/setup.py (my one-line --check help-text update, which mcp.md does not describe — a re-baseline, not a rewrite).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.38] — CI now carries an environment DIMENSION, and the leg is built so it cannot quietly stop being one.

=== 1. THE THREE SCOPE DECISIONS, EACH WITH ITS REASON

(a) WHICH LEGS. One job, `tests-locale`, single axis `locale: ["C", "en_US.ISO-8859-1"]`, python 3.13, extras byte-identical to the `tests` leg, locale env on the SUITE step only (an install broken by the locale would confound the signal rather than produce it). Python 3.13 on purpose: it is the version the owner runs locally, so the ONLY difference from the known-green local suite is the locale and a red leg is attributable to it; the version dimension is already the `tests` matrix's job, and crossing the two would be 8 legs for an ambiguous signal.

    THE `LC_ALL=C` LEG AS RECOMMENDED IS VACUOUS, MEASURED. On python:3.12-slim a bare `LC_ALL=C` gives preferred=utf-8 fs=utf-8 utf8_mode=1 — PEP 540 auto-enables UTF-8 Mode under a C/POSIX LC_CTYPE. Adding PYTHONUTF8=0 gives ANSI_X3.4-1968/ascii/utf8_mode=0. PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 is carried too for images where the PEP 538 half is what bites. This is the single most important finding of the bead: the one-line recommendation, spelled the obvious way, would have shipped a green leg that asserted nothing.

    THE NON-UTF-8 LOCALE EARNS ITS COST, and this is measured rather than argued (it was the bead's open question). `locale-gen en_US.ISO-8859-1` is REJECTED on ubuntu:24.04 — /usr/share/i18n/SUPPORTED spells that entry `en_US ISO-8859-1` — so the leg builds it with `localedef -i en_US -f ISO-8859-1` (~0.25s), verified to give iso8859-1 for preferred AND filesystem encoding with a 'café.py' filename round-tripping. The -i/-f arguments are derived from the matrix value, so a third row needs no edit. Why it is worth a whole leg: the two rows find DIFFERENT defects, not more of the same — see §3.

(b) WHOLE SUITE, not the guard subset. A subset narrows the dimension to the code we already suspect, which is the exact mistake being corrected: .36's defect was invisible to the WHOLE suite, not to a small one. No `--cov` on this leg — coverage is a property of the code, not of the locale, and the `tests` legs already enforce the floor; keeping it would only add a second way for the leg to be red that has nothing to do with the dimension.

(c) WINDOWS IS ITS OWN BEAD — filed as beadloom-mr2l.39, not left implied. The decisive reason is not cost, it is that ADDING THE LEG DOES NOT UN-VACUUM THE SKIPS: six guard tests carry `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')` and would still SKIP on windows-latest. Someone must first decide, per test, what the correct Windows behaviour IS and rewrite the assertion — dev work on src/+tests/, not CI configuration — or the leg buys a green check that proves nothing, which is the failure mode this whole family of beads exists to stop. Secondary: windows-latest bills at 2x and becomes the pipeline's critical path (unlike these legs, which add 0 wall-clock), and the first run is red for reasons unrelated to the guards (path separators, sqlite/WAL locking, grammar wheels). The bead carries the ordered scope and the acceptance criterion.

=== 2. THE LEG CANNOT GO VACUOUS — THREE INDEPENDENT LOCKS
1. An in-CI probe step runs BEFORE the suite and fails the leg two ways: VACUOUS (the image put it back on UTF-8) and DEGRADED (LC_ALL names a locale the image lacks, glibc falls back to POSIX, and the 8-bit row silently becomes a SECOND ASCII row — still non-UTF-8, still green, and no longer covering the direction it was added for). I found the DEGRADED hole while writing the probe; non-UTF-8 is necessary but not sufficient, the row must be the codec it claims.
2. That probe script is EXECUTED by the suite (tests parse the heredoc out of ci.yml and run it against injected encodings), so the least-tested code in a repo — a shell script inside a YAML string — is covered, and cannot drift from the workflow because the test reads the workflow.
3. `test_ci_never_pins_a_utf8_locale` (+ the inline-shell variant) asserts no job may set LC_ALL/LC_CTYPE/LANG/LANGUAGE to a UTF-8 value anywhere in ci.yml. That is the tempting "fix" the first time the leg goes red, so it fails the suite rather than being left to reviewer memory.

=== 3. WHAT IT FOUND, BEFORE ANY PUSH — the three-leg experiment
One Linux container, tree = `git archive HEAD` + my files, nothing changed between runs but the locale, so the number that matters is the DELTA:
  BASE  LC_ALL=C.UTF-8            ENC utf-8/utf-8        ->  2 failed / 5611 passed / 115s
  C     LC_ALL=C + both knobs     ENC ascii/ascii        -> 99 failed / 5514 passed / 110s
  L1    LC_ALL=en_US.ISO-8859-1   ENC iso8859-1/iso8859-1-> 75 failed / 5538 passed / 109s
The 2 baseline failures are root-user container artifacts present in every leg and absent on ubuntu-latest. So 97 and 73 locale-attributable failures. THE TWO SETS ARE NOT NESTED — the whole `test_cli_hooks.py` block (18 rows) fails ONLY under the 8-bit locale; `test_e2e_wave3`, `test_doc_generator`, `test_mcp_process_tools`, `test_guards_parity` and most of `test_onboarding` fail ONLY under ASCII; `test_config_sync::TestAgenticFlowDrift` fails 2 of 8 rows under ASCII and 8 of 8 under 8-bit. Exactly the predicted shape: ASCII RAISES (loud), an 8-bit codec ACCEPTS EVERY BYTE and mangles (silent). That is the empirical answer to "does the second row earn its cost": yes. Population, likely root cause (text I/O without an explicit `encoding=`) and the suggested order are written up in beadloom-mr2l.42, cross-referenced with .37's .40/.41 which reached the same class from the code side.

=== 4. SEQUENCING — THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT BE MISSED
`tests-locale` WILL BE RED ON THE FIRST PUSH. That is the intended signal and it blocks nothing by itself: DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS is a constant, not live protection — the repo's actual required checks change only when someone RUNS `beadloom setup-branch-protection`. DO NOT RUN IT until the legs are observed green, or `main` becomes unmergeable on the .42 backlog. I did not weaken the leg to avoid this (no `continue-on-error` — a check that cannot fail is theatre, which is the thing being fixed).

=== 5. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FIRST COMMIT, FOUND AND FIXED (39a3275)
DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS is not this repo's config — it is what `setup-branch-protection` PUTs in ANY repo, while a scaffolded repo's pipeline is the VENDORED TEMPLATE. Requiring `tests-locale (...)` while the template declared no such job would have given every adopter two required checks that never report → their `main` permanently unmergeable: precisely the lockout the module docstring warns about, from the one direction nobody watches. Fixed by giving the template the same job (on-thesis anyway — a container is the default deployment and is usually not UTF-8) and by asserting the lockout invariant over the TEMPLATE as well, not only over this repo's ci.yml, which is the check that was structurally missing.

=== 6. SABOTAGES (rule 5: FAILED never ERROR, numbers, reverse-edit restore verified by sha256) — 9, all bit
drop PYTHONUTF8=0 -> 2 FAILED/7 passed (including the EXECUTED one, so the pin is about effect not spelling); pin LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 -> 2 FAILED/7; narrow to `-k guard` -> 1 FAILED/8; drop the 8-bit row -> 1 FAILED/8; neuter the probe step -> 1 FAILED/8; diverge the extras from the `tests` leg -> 1 FAILED/8; delete the DEGRADED half of the probe -> 1 FAILED/13; delete the VACUOUS half -> 1 FAILED/13; swap localedef back to locale-gen -> 1 FAILED/13. Every restore sha256-verified; no sabotage produced an ERROR or "no tests ran". The two lockout tests were RED before the template job existed.

=== 7. WHAT I COULD AND COULD NOT VERIFY LOCALLY (nothing pushed)
COULD: actionlint (docker) on BOTH ci.yml and the vendored template — clean apart from the pre-existing self-hosted `ai-techwriter` runner-label warning, which is not mine and which an `.github/actionlint.yaml` would silence; both locale spellings measured on real Linux images; the three-leg suite experiment; 16 new tests, 9 sabotages; a clean-DB `beadloom ci` on an isolated `git archive HEAD` + only my files → rc 0, all six steps PASS, suite 5609 passed / 0 failed / 110s.
COULD NOT: the leg itself on a GitHub runner (only the owner's push does that), and `test_shipped_env_is_genuinely_non_utf8_on_linux` skips on this macOS because CPython FORCES a UTF-8 filesystem encoding there — that skip is stated as a platform where the assertion is false BY DESIGN, and it executes on every ubuntu leg of every PR, which is the opposite of a skip that can never fail.

=== 8. COST
2 rows x ~4 runner-minutes, fanned out in parallel with the four `tests` legs → pipeline WALL-CLOCK unchanged (~4 min); ~8 added runner-minutes per PR. Local whole-suite reference: 110-121s.

=== 9. FILES / TODO
ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml, src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/ai_techwriter/github-workflow.yml
src: onboarding/branch_protection.py (contexts 7->9 + docstrings), services/commands/setup.py (the `--check` help enumerated the old default)
tests: NEW tests/test_ci_locale_dimension.py (16 tests), test_ci_consolidated.py, test_branch_protection.py
docs: domains/onboarding/README.md, services/cli.md, guides/{agentic-flow,ai-techwriter,multi-agent-development,multi-agent-development.ru}.md
TODO / not mine: (1) beadloom-mr2l.42 — the 97/73 backlog; (2) beadloom-mr2l.39 — Windows; (3) the GitLab side (.gitlab-ci.yml + gitlab-ci-job.yml) does NOT carry the dimension — no lockout risk there since GitLab has no required-context mechanism, but it is a real asymmetry in BDL-050's "mirrors across GitHub + GitLab" property and belongs in .42 or its own bead; (4) the tech-writer should refresh the pipeline NARRATIVE and mermaid diagrams, which still show three parallel verify jobs — listed with line numbers in this bead's API CHANGE comment; (5) two stale sync pairs on services/mcp.md are left for .37 on purpose (re-baselining them would mask their in-flight doc drift).

title: [BDL-061.33][dev] S2: a guard that cannot answer must actually block — the exit-3 class is fail-open
description:
Review .3 finding N1(c). S2 scope - NOT S1. Filed because it was written as 'worth a bead in S2' twice (.27 FRICTION #1, .29 section 8) and filed zero times; the deferral had no owner and would have been lost.

THE DEFECT. SPEC.md Invariants states verbatim: 'A guard that cannot answer says so and blocks. I could not tell is a verdict (`error`), not an exception, and it never borrows the `warn` code.' Measured through the real binary, five cases all produce an ERROR verdict at exit 3: an unregistered guard name; an unparseable `guards:` block; `--liveness` with a name; a malformed `--context` pair; an unsupported `--hook` harness. Exit 3 does NOT block in Claude Code - the slice measured that itself.

Verified again by the coordinator on 2026-08-22 by appending invalid YAML to .beadloom/flow.yml: `beadloom guard bead-claimed --context path=app.py` returned an ERROR verdict naming the parse error, at exit 3. So the most likely failure an adopter will actually meet - a flow.yml that will not parse - SILENTLY DISABLES EVERY GUARD IN THE HARNESS while the Invariants section promises the opposite. Fail-open, on the one input the adopter edits by hand.

This belongs in S2 because S2 is 'stop the lying checks': a document asserting enforcement the product does not deliver is the same defect class as a check that reports clean without checking.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and the choice needs stating with its reason, not just its outcome:
  (a) map the exit-3 class to 2, i.e. a configuration defect blocks like any other 'cannot answer'. Simple and consistent with the invariant. Cost: a broken flow.yml then blocks ALL edits, which for an adopter who mistyped one line is a hard stop with a clear message - arguably correct, arguably hostile on upgrade.
  (b) keep 3 at the CLI and have the ADAPTER map it, so the CLI keeps its distinction (declared-config defect vs this-edit failure - a distinction .29 established deliberately and it is worth something) while the harness still blocks.
Weigh them against CONTEXT's constraint 'no adopter's green project turns red on upgrade' - note that this is not a new check going red, it is an existing check that was never enforcing.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, the docs must match afterwards: SPEC Invariants, the emitted adapter's comment in `onboarding/guard_hooks.py`, and `docs/services/cli.md` where 'deliberately not 2' currently reads as a pure win. Until this lands, .4 (tech-writer) qualifies the invariant rather than deleting it - that is deliberate: the sentence stays as the target, marked as not yet delivered, so the gap stays visible instead of being papered over.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: CHECKPOINT: RED->GREEN done. Chose (b), implemented at the CLI keyed on --hook rather than in the emitted script. New tests/test_guards_fail_closed.py (24 tests) failed 10/24 before the fix. Sabotage both directions: forcing 3 always -> 9 of the new tests red; forcing 2 always -> 6 red (the shell-distinction half). 5 pre-existing tests updated with stated reasons (the unsupported-harness rows + the flow.yml-through-a-hook row). Docs next.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text: API CHANGE: `beadloom guard` exit codes. The configuration/command-line class (unparseable `guards:` block, exclusion missing reason/until, unregistered guard name, no guard named, --liveness with a name, malformed --context pair, unsupported --hook harness) now exits 2 instead of 3 WHEN --hook names a harness. Unchanged (still 3) for every caller that does not pass --hook, i.e. every shell and CI caller. New application-layer function: beadloom.application.guards.models.harness_exit_code(harness). Docs updated in this commit: docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md (Verdict + Invariants), docs/services/cli.md (641/645/663), docs/guides/agentic-flow.md (exit-code table), docs/domains/onboarding/components/guard-hooks/DOC.md, and the emitted adapter's own comment in src/beadloom/onboarding/guard_hooks.py. Docs still to check by a reader: none found by sweep (grepped docs/ + README.md + README.ru.md + AGENTS.md for 'exit 3' / '3 = usage' / 'fail-open').

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.33] S2 dev — commit 71e31eb on features/BDL-061-S2. 13 files, +503/-96.

=== THE CHOICE, WITH ITS REASON
(b), and the mapping lives IN THE CLI keyed on the harness the adapter already declares — not in the emitted .sh. Three reasons, in order of weight:
  1. The distinction .29 established is worth keeping for the caller who can act on it and worthless to the one who cannot. From a shell, 3 says 'your declared configuration is broken' and separates that from Click's own usage exit 2. Through a hook, the exit code answers exactly one question — does this edit proceed — and 3 answers it 'yes'. So 3 is kept where it means something and dropped where it means 'unguarded'.
  2. Doing the mapping in the .sh (the literal reading of (b)) puts logic in an adapter, which is the rule guard_hooks.py's own docstring calls 'the rule the whole epic rests on'. It would also be re-implemented — and re-forgotten — by every future harness adapter: the same fail-open, one tool later. In the CLI it is one tested function, and a second harness inherits it the way it inherits the payload translator.
  3. Against CONTEXT's 'no adopter's green project turns red on upgrade': (b) changes nothing for a project whose flow.yml parses, and nothing at all for shell/CI callers. (a) — mapping the whole class to 2 — would additionally change the code every script already reads, which IS a contract change for adopters. And as the bead says, this is not a new check going red: a project whose flow.yml does not parse had no enforcement to lose.
Corollary, decided here: an unsupported --hook harness blocks too. It is a defect in the binding itself and Beadloom cannot learn the exit vocabulary of a tool it does not support, so it uses the code it knows stops work. That flipped 4 pre-existing test rows from 3 to 2.
NOT DONE deliberately: no per-harness exit-code table. Every harness Beadloom supports blocks on 2, and a one-entry table with a default is the 'permission without a caller' shape (standing rule 8). Stated in the docstring, with what to do the day a harness disagrees.

=== TESTS (rule 5, both directions)
NEW tests/test_guards_fail_closed.py, 24 tests, 4 classes. Before the fix: 10 failed / 14 passed — the 14 are the shell half plus the non-vacuity check, which must NOT move.
  - the five measured cases + 'no guard named', run under --hook: exit 2, and still an error verdict with a non-empty why and not_covered (a blocking code with no cause is a different bug);
  - the same six without --hook: still exit 3;
  - DERIVED, not hand-written: every row of tests/test_guards_invocation.py::_EXIT_PATHS whose expected code is 3 and which does not already pass --hook is re-run with --hook claude-code and must exit 2. A config-error path added later is covered on the day it is added, not on the day someone remembers this file. Guarded against vacuity by a test asserting the derivation finds >=5 rows;
  - the REAL emitted .sh, real subprocess, real CLI, against a flow.yml that will not parse -> rc 2 and 'bead-claimed: ERROR' on stderr. This is the coordinator's own 2026-08-22 measurement, now a test;
  - the adapter's comment names no exit code the adapter can no longer produce.
SABOTAGE, by reverse edit (rule 7), never git checkout:
  - force harness_exit_code -> 3 always: 14 red across the suite, 9 of them in the new file;
  - force -> 2 always (i.e. candidate (a)): 6 red, all in TestFromAShellTheDistinctionSurvives.
So both halves bite, and the second sabotage is a working demonstration that the tests would have caught (a) being applied by accident.

=== EXISTING TESTS CHANGED (5, each with the reason written into the test)
  test_guards_invocation.py  _EXIT_PATHS 'a harness nobody supports' 3 -> 2
  test_guards_adversarial.py the same row in two tables, 3 -> 2
  test_guards_cli.py         test_unknown_harness_exits_three -> ..._blocks_and_names_the_ones_it_knows
  test_guards_paths.py       test_a_config_error_is_recorded_and_keeps_its_own_exit_code -> ..._reaching_a_hook_is_recorded_and_blocks (it runs with --hook claude-code, so it IS the flow.yml case)
No test was weakened; every change is a code moving 3 -> 2 on a hooked invocation.

=== DOCS — the .4 qualification comes out because the gap closed
  SPEC Invariants: the sentence now states all three clauses as fact ('every code it can exit with, in the harness it is bound to, stops the edit') and records that the second half was not true until this bead.
  SPEC Verdict: the 'gap rather than a decision' paragraph is replaced by the decision, both rejected candidates with why, and the no-per-harness-table note.
  cli.md 641/645/663; guides/agentic-flow.md exit-code table now has a shell column and a hook column; guard-hooks/DOC.md's 'the script's comment does not carry the second one yet' is now 'both now carried'.
  The emitted adapter's comment no longer says '3 = usage or configuration error'; it says what this adapter can return and what the same command returns without --hook.

=== VERIFICATION
  ruff clean on src/beadloom/ + every test file I touched. mypy --strict clean, 183 files.
  Guard suite: 679 passed (test_guards_*, test_guard_hook_adapter, test_guards).

title: [BDL-061.32][test] S1: make the Click-validation pin about its sentence, not about click.Path
description:
Review .3 finding N2. One test file, no source change.

`tests/test_guards_invocation.py` :: `test_the_command_does_no_validation_click_would_exit_on` claims the wide sentence in its name and docstring - 'an option Click validates exits before the callback, and therefore before the boundary'. Its implementation asserts `click_path_keywords(...) == [["path_type"]]`, i.e. it walks the AST for calls unparsing to exactly `click.Path`.

Measured by the reviewer against click 8.4.2 in this venv, standalone dispatch: `type=click.Choice([...])` with a bad value exits 2 without reaching the callback, and `type=int` with a bad value does the same. Neither is a `click.Path`, so neither is visible to the pin. Neither of the other two mechanisms covers it either: the witness matrix imports `run_invocation` and runs BENEATH Click by construction, and every `_EXIT_PATHS` row is a hand-written argv, so a new option contributes no row.

COST TODAY IS ZERO - `--project` is the only typed option and carries no validator. This is about the guarantee, not a live defect. It matters because S2/S3 will plausibly add `--work-kind` as a `click.Choice` (strictness is already per work kind), and on that day `beadloom guard bead-claimed --work-kind epci` exits 2 with Click's usage message, no verdict and no record, with every pin green. That is exactly the round-six defect this re-review was called to look for, and the fifth cycle's lesson - a pin narrower than its invariant - one constructor over.

DO WHAT .31 DID FOR TERMINATORS: make the pin about the sentence. Assert an allowlist over the keywords of EVERY `type=` argument on the command's options, or assert the command declares no option whose `type` is a Click validator instance at all. Judge which of the two is the honest statement of the rule and say why in the test's docstring.

Then prove it bites: add a `click.Choice` option to the command as a sabotage and show the reddening is FAILED, never ERROR, comparing collected/passed NUMBERS. Restore by reverse edit (rule 9) and verify by sha256. Rule 1 for lint. pytest-randomly is active - pin a seed.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.32] S1 — the Click-validation pin is now about its sentence, and the
sentence was false when I measured it. Commit fb19e22. Suite 5561 -> 5574 passed / 10
skipped / 0 failed. DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD, stated first: it says "one test file, no
source change". It is one keyword of source change, because "cost today is zero" is wrong.

=== 1. THE FINDING THE WIDER PIN FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN
`click.Path` defaults `readable=True`, and that check runs INSIDE Click, before the
callback. So `--project` — "the only typed option, and it carries no validator" — carried
one: measured through the real binary, `beadloom guard bead-claimed --project <a directory
this process may not read> --json` was Click's usage exit 2, no verdict, no record, and
nothing on stdout for a `--json` consumer to parse. Fail-closed on the code, but the same
shape as the defect this whole slice is about. Fixed with `readable=False` (7 lines with
the reason as a comment); the directory is now refused BY THE BOUNDARY as an `error`
verdict, the same refusal a missing path / a file / an unmarked directory get since .31.
Note what this says about the retired pin: a keyword allowlist can only see keywords
SOMEBODY TYPED. The validator here was a default nobody typed, under a pin reading
`[["path_type"]]` and green.

=== 2. WHICH FORMULATION IS HONEST, AND WHY (the judgement the bead asked for)
NEITHER of the two proposed, and the reasoning is in the test's docstring, not just the
choice:
- "An allowlist over the KEYWORDS of every `type=`" is the same defect a third time. The
  two constructors that prompted the finding both satisfy it: `click.Choice(["a"])`
  carries no keyword at all, and `type=int` is not even a call. It also cannot see a
  rejecting DEFAULT, which is exactly what §1 was.
- "No option whose type is a Click validator INSTANCE" names the wrong property.
  `click.STRING` is a `ParamType` instance; so is the `click.Path` this command needs in
  order to take a path at all. Instance-hood is not what exits 2.
- What exits 2 is A CONVERSION THAT CAN REFUSE AN ARGV STRING. That is the rule, so that
  is what is quantified over: EVERY parameter Click converts on the way to this callback
  — the group's options as well as the command's, read from the command Click DISPATCHES
  (`main.commands["guard"]`) rather than from an imported symbol, so a parameter added
  through a shared decorator or an `add_command` is inside the pin the day it lands.

=== 3. THE MECHANISM (three parts, because one is a sample and one can be vacuous)
- MEASURED: every value-taking parameter x a 13-row corpus of hostile argv strings, run
  through `Command.make_context` — which is exactly the parse Click performs before
  `invoke`, and does NOT call the callback. So "this returned" IS "control reached the
  boundary", whatever the type is called. Corpus: empty, whitespace, `epci` (the finding's
  own typo), a non-number, a negative number, 400 digits, a lone dash, a newline, 4 KiB, a
  non-ascii name, an existing file, an existing directory, a missing path, + an unreadable
  directory when this process can be refused access.
- STRUCTURAL (closes the sampling residual): an exact table of the conversion each
  value-taking parameter declares, read from the RUNTIME object (so an alias or a variable
  is described as what it is), with `click.Path` written out as the refusals it can make
  rather than as its constructor name: `click.Path(nothing it can refuse, path_type=Path)`.
- SCOPE ACCOUNTING: probed ∪ valueless == every parameter, the valueless set pinned by
  name, and each asserted to be a flag (Click supplies a flag's value itself, so no argv
  string meets its type). Nothing leaves the pin's scope silently.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL (10 parametrised rows): the same probe on the option a later slice
  might write — `click.Choice`, `int`, `float`, `IntRange`, `Path(exists=True)`,
  `Path(dir_okay=False)`, `Path(file_okay=False)`, `DateTime`, `UUID`, and
  `Path(readable=True)` (the conversion this command shipped with). Each must be REFUSED,
  or the pin above is one that cannot fail.

=== 4. SABOTAGE (rule 5) — baseline 708 collected / 708 passed, 12 guard test files,
`-p no:randomly`, __pycache__ cleared both sides, each applied ALONE, removed by REVERSE
EDIT, and all three touched files verified BYTE-IDENTICAL by sha256 after every row.
 S1 `--work-kind` as a `click.Choice(["feature","bugfix"])` (the bead's required sabotage,
    + the callback parameter so it is a plausible edit)  -> 4 FAILED / 704 passed
    reddened: the probe, the conversions table, the scope accounting, and the retired-pin
    characterization in test_guards_boundary_escapes.py — three independent mechanisms.
 S2 `--depth` as `type=int` (not Choice-specific)        -> 3 FAILED / 705
 S3 revert `readable=False`                              -> 3 FAILED / 705
    reddened: the probe, the conversions table, AND the behavioural test through the real
    binary — the structural and behavioural halves catch it separately.
 S4 the corpus emptied (`yield []`) — the pin made vacuous -> 10 FAILED / 698, i.e. every
    negative-control row. A hollowed probe cannot pass.
Every row: ZERO ERROR, failed+passed == 708 exactly, so no test was lost to collection.
RED FIRST: with the new tests against the shipped source, 2 FAILED — the probe (on the
unreadable row) and the conversions table (`click.Path(readable, path_type=Path)`), i.e.
the source change was demanded by the tests before it was written.

=== 5. SECOND FILE, AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE ONE
`test_guards_boundary_escapes.py` IMPORTED `click_path_keywords`; removing the helper
would have been a collection ERROR. Keeping a dead helper alive to keep a stale
characterization green is the precedent this slice exists to stop, so its test is now
`test_the_retired_pin_is_blind_to_the_validator_a_later_option_would_use`: the `--work-kind`
Choice is applied to the REAL command source in memory and the retired pin is shown to read
it as UNCHANGED, beside the new mechanism refusing it. `.30`'s B5 row is preserved in the
docstring rather than deleted.

=== 6. WHAT I ALSO MEASURED, AND DID NOT ACT ON (rule 4 seams)
- A NUL in `--project` leaves `click.Path` as `ValueError: stat: embedded null character`,
  which is NOT the `UsageError` Click converts into a usage message — so an IN-PROCESS
  caller (`main(["guard", ...])`, a CliRunner, an embedder) gets a traceback and exit 1,
  the WARN code. NOT reachable through a real shell: `execve` takes NUL-terminated strings,
  so no argv value can carry one. Deliberately kept OUT of the corpus for that reason,
  stated in the fixture's docstring rather than silently dropped. Worth a BDL-UX line if
  anyone ever embeds the CLI.
- The group's three options (`--version/--verbose/--quiet`) are all flags, so including the
  parent chain in the scope costs nothing today and NO sabotage can prove those rows bite.
  Stated, not claimed.
- Residual in the structural half: a refusal a future Click adds under a new attribute name
  would be described here as absent. The probe is the mechanism that would still see it.
- `access_can_be_refused()` is MEASURED (a real `chmod 000` in a temp dir), not assumed from
  `geteuid`, so the unreadable rows skip with a reason as root or on a permissionless
  filesystem instead of passing in silence.

=== 7. DOCS (behaviour changed, so the docs say so)
flow-guards/SPEC.md: the unreadable directory is now named in the `--project` section, and
the "what remains outside the boundary" residual now carries the rule that keeps it true —
no parameter declares a conversion Click can refuse. cli.md `beadloom guard`: same, one
sentence. The callback docstring's claim "`--project` is deliberately not validated by
Click" — which was FALSE while `readable=True` — now names the keyword nobody typed.

=== 8. GATE
pytest 5574 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed, identical under `-p no:randomly` and
`--randomly-seed=20260822`; the touched files re-run under `--randomly-seed=1337` (249
passed). ruff clean; mypy --strict clean (183 files). Coverage: guards package 99.89%,
`services/commands/guard.py` 98%. Clean-DB gate: db removed -> reindex (67 nodes / 314
edges / 1242 symbols) -> `beadloom ci` rc=0 (lint 0 violations, sync-check 272 pairs fresh,
docs-audit 13 mentions, config-check, doctor 20 clean). Pre-commit hook green.
FILES: tests/test_guards_invocation.py (+1 test replaced by 4 tests incl. 10 parametrised
rows, + the corpus fixture and 7 helpers; +1 behavioural test in the project class),
tests/test_guards_boundary_escapes.py (1 test rewritten), guard.py (+7/-2),
flow-guards/SPEC.md, cli.md. Net +13 tests.

title: [BDL-061.31][dev] S1 fix-4: make the pin as wide as the invariant, and close the two ways past the boundary
description:
Fix cycle 5. Input: `bd comments beadloom-mr2l.30` (three escapes, method and measurements), `.29` (the boundary being repaired). The coordinator independently reproduced C through the real binary: `beadloom guard bead-claimed --project <existing-dir-without-marker> --context path=app.py` returned SKIP at exit 0, created `.beadloom/` there, and wrote the firing into it while the real project's record was untouched.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG: the boundary itself. `run_invocation` = `_record(_answer(...))` is the right shape and `.30` attacked it hard and failed to break the render step, the exit-code rule, the three recording exceptions, walk-up discovery and append atomicity. Do not redesign it.

WHAT IS WRONG, and the three are not equal:

B IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The structural pins were the deliverable that was supposed to make a regression impossible, and they check SPELLING, not behaviour. Measured: `if invocation.name == "": sys.exit(0)` placed inside `run_invocation` preserves one return, one record_firing call site and one `x.exit` in guard.py, ships 628/628 GREEN across the whole guard suite and all four pins, and makes `beadloom guard ""` exit 0 printing nothing and recording nothing. A total silent bypass invisible to the shipped suite. Also blind: `os._exit`, `os.abort`, a BARE `raise SystemExit` (exc is a Name, not a Call), `raise click.Abort()`; a `record_firing` anywhere in services/ outside guard.py; and pin D is the substring 'exists=True' while `dir_okay=False` exits before the callback just as surely.
  The fix is not four more substrings. Decide what the pin is ABOUT — 'no control leaves the boundary path except through the recording step' — and pin that: scan every module on the path (invocation.py, project_root.py, services/commands/guard.py, and whatever else control passes through), recognise terminators by what they DO rather than by how they are spelled, and assert an allowlist of Click validation keywords rather than the absence of one string. A pin narrower than its invariant is how this slice reached round five.

A IS A DEFECT, ONE WORD WIDE. `except Exception` + `except SystemExit` does not cover BaseException, so a KeyboardInterrupt during evaluation escapes and Click exits 1 — the non-blocking WARN code — with no verdict and no record. That is .28's F7 shape in a different exception class. Widening to BaseException is one line, but WRITE THE REASONING: converting an interrupt into a recorded 'I could not tell' at exit 2 means Ctrl-C now BLOCKS the edit. Argue that either way and state it in the SPEC; what is not acceptable is the current answer, where an interrupt is indistinguishable from a passing warn.

C IS THE HONESTY NOTE FAILING FOR THE THIRD TIME IN THIS SLICE. project_root.py's docstring says a guard 'does not create .beadloom/ where it stands'. True of discovery, false of --project: any `is_dir()` is honoured, no flow.yml is found, the project's declared `block` silently becomes the shipped default `warn`, and a self-entrenching `.beadloom/` is created there. .28 filed it as minor m3; .29's residual list does not name it and the docstring denies it. Require the marker for --project as for discovery, and make the docstring and the residual list say what the code does. An understating honesty note has now been the finding twice before this one — that pattern is the thing to stop, not just this instance.

ALSO, small and named so they are not lost: `name or UNNAMED_GUARD` swallows an empty string, so the not-recorded reason quotes a guard the caller never typed; a CLOSED stdin surfaces the raw \"AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'read'\" where a stated cause belongs; and the render step (`_emit`) is still structurally outside the boundary with nothing pinning that it cannot raise — .30 could not reach a raising case, so decide whether to move it inside or to pin the claim, and say which.

DELIVERABLE BAR: .30's characterization tests currently pin the DEFECTIVE behaviour and are green. Every one of them must be rewritten to assert the correct behaviour — a fix that leaves a characterization test pinning the old answer has not landed. Then re-run .30's own B2 sabotage and show it reddens.

Standing rules 1, 5, 9 apply. Do not widen not_covered to cover a gap.

A: _answer now SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt/BaseException (+_record widened, +_detail); C: --project requires the .beadloom/ marker (new _declared_project + DECLARED_PROJECT_UNMARKED), docstring/SPEC/cli.md rewritten; B: pin rewritten as scope-derived + effect-measured terminators + recording-witness matrix in a subprocess. Also: empty guard name no longer swallowed (_named), closed stdin states a cause, render wrapped so it cannot pick the exit code. A KeyboardInterrupt during an evaluation is now a recorded 'error' at exit 2 (was: escaped to Click, exit 1, no verdict, no record) — Ctrl-C during a guarded edit now BLOCKS that edit. `beadloom guard ""` now reports guard="" instead of "(no guard named)" in the verdict and in not_recorded_because. A closed stdin with --hook now reports 'no standard input ...' instead of the raw AttributeError. A failure while rendering the verdict no longer changes the exit code; it is reported on stderr. New public constant DECLARED_PROJECT_UNMARKED in application/guards/project_root.py. comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.31] S1 fix-4 — the pin is now as wide as the invariant, and the two
ways past the boundary are closed. Suite 5501 -> 5561 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed;
guard subset 653 -> 713. src/ touched in 3 files, +151/-26.

=== 1. B — THE PIN, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERED
The old pin checked a SPELLING of the sentence it was supposed to hold. The sentence,
stated once and now written at the head of section 2 of test_guards_invocation.py:

    CONTROL LEAVES THE GUARD'S BOUNDARY PATH IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE, AND ONLY AFTER THE
    RECORDING STEP HAS RUN.

Three axes, because .30's sabotage walked through three:
  SCOPE is DERIVED, not listed. `boundary_path_modules()` = the command module +
    `(_GUARDS_PACKAGE).rglob("*.py")` (15 modules today), so a module added to the
    package is inside the pin on the day it is added. The old scope was one file, and
    the boundary module itself was never read.
  TERMINATORS are recognised by MEASURED EFFECT. `process_terminators()` matches call
    targets on their LAST component ({exit, _exit, quit}, so sys.exit/os._exit/ctx.exit/
    a bare `exit` are one behaviour), plus whole dotted targets whose last component is
    too ordinary to match alone (os.abort/os.kill/os.exec*/signal.raise_signal), plus a
    `raise` read from its exception NODE rather than from a Call — which is why a bare
    `raise SystemExit` counts now and did not before. The table is not a list of
    guesses: 9 rows are each RUN IN A REAL SUBPROCESS and shown that a process does not
    continue past them, and each is measured a second time inside an
    `except BaseException` handler, which splits catchable terminators (the boundary
    converts them into verdicts) from uncatchable ones (nothing above them can). Stated
    and not hidden: os.abort and the os.exec* family are recognised but NOT measured,
    because SIGABRT writes a crash report on every run of the suite — os.abort is
    documented as SIGABRT-to-self, i.e. the mechanism of the measured os.kill row.
  The RECORDING STEP LEAVES A WITNESS. `_record` sets exactly one of `recorded_at` /
    `not_recorded_because` on every result, so a result that skipped it carries NEITHER.
    A matrix GENERATED from the argument axes (6 names x 4 project kinds x liveness x 3
    contexts x 3 harnesses = 432 rows, incl. "" and a trailing newline) runs in a CHILD
    PROCESS printing one JSON row each: a construct that ends the process is the named
    row that never arrived, not a dead test session. .30's bypass was placed on an argv
    nobody had written a row for; a generated matrix has no such argv.
Also widened: the one-writer pin now scans the WHOLE source tree (183 modules) for
`record_firing` calls AND for imports of it (an alias import would hide a call from a
name scan) — .30's B4; and the click.Path pin is an AST keyword ALLOWLIST
(`== [["path_type"]]`) instead of `"exists=True" not in source` — .30's B5, where
`dir_okay=False` exits before the callback just as surely and passed the substring.

=== 2. A — THE HANDLER, AND THE ARGUMENT FOR IT
`_answer` is now `except SystemExit` / `except KeyboardInterrupt` / `except BaseException`
(the two named clauses only so a reader gets a cause they can act on; the wide one so the
class nobody thought of is a verdict). `_record`'s handler is as wide, closing the
asymmetry .30 named. The reasoning is IN THE SPEC with both sides, because the fix is not
free: Ctrl-C during a guarded edit now BLOCKS that edit (recorded `error`, exit 2) instead
of waving it through (exit 1, no verdict, no record). Against: an interrupt is the
operator's escape hatch and this writes a firing they did not ask for. For, which is the
decision: SIGINT reaches the whole foreground process group, so the harness's own tool
call is interrupted with the guard and there is usually no edit left to let through; the
verdict is the honest one, because an interrupted guard checked nothing; and the
alternative leaves an interrupt indistinguishable from a passing warn, which is the exact
failure every cycle in this slice has been about.

=== 3. C — THE HONESTY NOTE, AND THE RECURRENCE
`--project` now requires the marker: `_declared_project()` refuses a missing path, a file,
AND an ordinary directory (new DECLARED_PROJECT_UNMARKED), all as the same "the project
could not be located" the discovery path gives. The docstring that denied it is rewritten
("manufacturing a root — by ANY route, including through --project ... it does not create
one where it was pointed"), the SPEC carries the requirement, its cost (--project cannot
point at a directory before `beadloom init`) and the residual list, and cli.md carries the
behaviour change.
THE RECURRENCE, treated as the thing to stop: an understating honesty note has now been
the finding three times, and each time it was TRUE OF THE WALK and FALSE THROUGH THE FLAG
— i.e. the claim was asserted about one path instead of quantified over the set. It is now
quantified: `_WAYS_A_ROOT_IS_NAMED` enumerates every way a root can be chosen (discovery
inside a project, discovery outside one, --project naming the project / a plain directory /
a subdirectory / a missing path / a file) and one parametrised test asserts, for each, that
the only directory carrying `.beadloom/` afterwards is the one that carried it before. The
same shape was added to the 20-row exit-path table: every row now also asserts that the
not-a-project directory gained no marker.

=== 4. THE SMALL ONES, NONE DROPPED
- `name or UNNAMED_GUARD` -> `_named(name)` (`UNNAMED_GUARD if name is None else name`), so
  `beadloom guard ""` reports guard="" and "'' is not a registered guard" instead of quoting
  "(no guard named)", a guard the caller never typed.
- A CLOSED stdin: `_read_stdin` states the cause ("this process has no standard input to
  read the payload from (the caller closed it)") instead of surfacing
  "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'read'". Measured through a real
  process with fd 0 actually closed (`/bin/sh -c '... 0<&-'`) — CliRunner installs a stream
  of its own and monkeypatching sys.stdin is undone by that installation, so neither can
  reproduce what CPython does at start-up. Stated as a seam (rule 4).
- `_detail(exc)` drops the empty tail, so an argument-less exception reads
  "KeyboardInterrupt" and not "KeyboardInterrupt: ".
- THE RENDER STEP: decided and stated — it stays OUTSIDE the boundary (click.echo in the
  application layer would break the DDD direction) and the CLAIM IS PINNED instead of
  trusted. `_emit` is now the body of a `try` whose handler is BaseException, with the one
  `sys.exit` outside it, so a failure while printing is reported on stderr and the code is
  still the verdict's. .30 honestly reported it could not reach a raising case; a claim
  nobody could break this round is not a guarantee.
- Repeated `--context k=v`: last-wins is now STATED (SPEC + cli.md) and a test reads the
  sentence back, rather than being an unstated rule that happened to be fail-closed.

=== 5. THE .30 CHARACTERIZATION TESTS — ALL REWRITTEN, NONE LEFT PINNING THE OLD ANSWER
Every class renamed and every assertion inverted (25 -> 44 tests in that file):
  TestAnInterruptEscapesTheBoundary       -> TestAnInterruptIsARecordedVerdictLikeAnyOtherFailure
  TestTheOneWayOutPinCannotSeeEveryWayOut -> TestControlLeavesTheBoundaryPathInExactlyOnePlace
  TestADeclaredProjectNeedNotBeAProject   -> TestADeclaredProjectMustBeAProject
  TestExitPathsTheEnumerationDoesNotList  -> TestTheRowsThisRoundAddedAreNowEnumerated
  (+ new TestTheRenderStepCannotChangeTheVerdict)
The disjointness assertion is INVERTED: the four argv-reachable rows .30 derived are now
rows of `_EXIT_PATHS` (16 -> 20) and the fifth is a row of the new `_INJECTED_FAILURES`
table, and the test asserts `_ROWS_ADDED_THIS_ROUND <= shipped`. Two latent defects in the
table harness were fixed to make that possible: `if name else []` folded an empty name into
"no name at all" (the very confusion .30 found in the product), now `if name is not None`;
and a `{not_a_project}` placeholder lets a row point --project somewhere that is not one,
with `project_located` derived from the row rather than hardcoded True.
`test_the_shipped_pin_does_not_look_inside_the_boundary_module` (which asserted the scope
was three named files) is now `test_every_module_of_the_package_is_scanned_not_only_the_
three_named`; the two "the pin stays green beside a second terminator" parametrisations are
now "the pin sees every terminator the table measures". .30's B2 edit is applied to the real
invocation.py source IN MEMORY and scanned, so the exact sabotage that shipped 628/628 green
is a test rather than a memory.

=== 6. SABOTAGE (rule 5) — 9 applied one at a time; EVERY reddening FAILED, zero ERROR
Baseline 713 collected / 713 passed (the 13 guard test files, `-p no:randomly`).
__pycache__ cleared on both sides of every run; each removed by REVERSE EDIT and the three
boundary files verified byte-identical by sha256 after every row.
 B2 `if invocation.name == "": sys.exit(0)` INSIDE run_invocation (.30's own edit, the one
    that shipped 628/628 green and all four pins)      -> 10 FAILED / 703, caught by THREE
    independent mechanisms: the AST scan over the package (2), the enumerated empty-name
    rows (3), and the witness matrix (3), plus the empty-name reporting test.
 M1 `os._exit(3)` in guard.py (invisible to the old pin) ->  6 FAILED / 707
 M3 `dir_okay=False` on the click.Path (passes the old substring) -> 154 FAILED / 559
 M4 revert the interrupt + BaseException clauses        ->  7 FAILED / 706
 M5 revert the --project marker requirement             ->  8 FAILED / 705
 M6 unwrap the render step                              ->  4 FAILED / 709
 M7 a second `record_firing` call site in services/     ->  3 FAILED / 710
 M8 a bare `raise SystemExit` in project_root.py        ->  3 FAILED / 710
 M9 narrow `_record`'s handler back to Exception        ->  1 FAILED / 712
Every row's failed+passed sums to 713, so no test was lost to collection.
HARNESS FIX FOUND BY THE SABOTAGE ITSELF: the first M4 run did not FAIL, it INTERRUPTED the
session ("184 passed", no summary) — an escaping KeyboardInterrupt aborts pytest, and "the
run stopped" is not "the test failed". The five tests that inject a BaseException now go
through `_must_not_escape(...)`, which turns an escape into `pytest.fail(...)`. That is rule
5 catching a defect in rule 5's own evidence; M4 above is the re-run.

RED FIRST: with the final tests against the shipped source, 16 FAILED / 156 passed for B and
C, and finding A could not be counted at all because the escaping interrupt aborted the
session — which is itself the measurement that it escaped `run_invocation`.

=== 7. GATE
pytest 5561 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed, IDENTICAL under `-p no:randomly` and
`--randomly-seed=20260822` (no ghost; .29 FRICTION #4). ruff clean. mypy --strict clean, 183
files. Clean-DB gate (rule 1): rm beadloom.db -> reindex (67 nodes / 94 edges / 673 chunks /
1242 symbols / 1311 imports / 12 rules) -> lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules ->
sync-check 279 pairs, 0 stale -> doctor 20 checks clean -> `beadloom ci` rc=0 (reindex, lint,
sync-check 272 pairs, docs-audit 13 mentions, config-check, doctor).
`git diff --stat -- src/`: 3 files, +151/-26, and nothing else.

=== 8. WHAT REMAINS, NAMED (not_covered NOT widened)
- The structural pin is still AST, so it cannot see a terminator reached through an alias
  (`_stop = os._exit; _stop(3)`) or through `getattr`. That residual is REAL but it is no
  longer the whole guarantee: the witness matrix is behavioural and would catch such an
  edit on any of its 432 rows, and a child process that dies names the row it died on.
- os.abort / os.exec* are recognised but not measured (crash-report cost, stated above).
- `.29`'s residuals are unchanged: an argv Click itself cannot parse never reaches the
  callback; a nested `.beadloom/` wins beneath itself; exit 3 still does not block in Claude
  Code (S2 owns that decision); a whitespace-only target is a path, not "absent".
- `--project` now refuses a directory that has no `.beadloom/`, which means it cannot be
  used to point at a project before `beadloom init` has run there. Intended, and stated in
  the SPEC as a cost rather than left to be discovered.

=== 9. FILES
src: application/guards/invocation.py (the three handlers, `_named`, `_detail`, the
  decision paragraph), application/guards/project_root.py (`_declared_project` +
  DECLARED_PROJECT_UNMARKED + the rewritten honesty paragraph), services/commands/guard.py
  (the wrapped render, the closed-stdin cause).
tests: test_guards_boundary_escapes.py (rewritten, 25 -> 44), test_guards_invocation.py
  (section 2 replaced, 4 enumeration rows, the injection table, the locating tests, 98 ->
  ~117), conftest.py (`guard_project` fixture), test_guards_cli.py / test_guards_parity.py /
  test_guards_liveness.py / test_guards_paths.py (the project under test is now a project).
docs: flow-guards/SPEC.md, services/cli.md; BDL-061/ACTIVE.md.

=== 10. FRICTION (for BDL-UX)
1. zsh does not word-split an unquoted parameter, so `pytest $FILES` silently runs nothing
   and reports "no tests ran in 0.00s" with exit 5 — a sabotage harness can look green by
   running zero tests. Rule 5's "compare NUMBERS, not colour" caught it; worth a line in the
   standing rules, since every agent here drives pytest from zsh.
2. pytest reports an uncaught BaseException from a test as a session INTERRUPT, not as a
   failure — see the M4 note in section 6. Any test asserting "this cannot escape" has to
   convert the escape itself, or the sabotage that proves it bites is uncountable.

title: [BDL-061.30][test] S1 fix-3: prove the boundary holds where three cycles did not
description:
Independently verify .29. Standing rule 6.

This slice has now shipped a hole in each of three consecutive rounds, and one of them was introduced by the fix that closed the previous one. Assume a fourth exists.

The claim under test is no longer about paths. It is: EVERY invocation of 'beadloom guard' ends with a verdict and a firing record, and never with exit 1 unless the verdict is genuinely 'warn'. Attack that claim, not the four symptoms.

1. ENUMERATE INDEPENDENTLY. Do not reuse .29's list of exit paths — build your own from the code and the CLI surface, then compare. A path present in your list and absent from theirs is the finding. Include: no arguments, an unknown guard name, --liveness with a broken store, unreadable/malformed/empty flow.yml, absent flow.yml, stdin closed, stdin empty, stdin non-UTF-8, stdin valid JSON of the wrong shape, --context with no equals sign, a repeated --context key, --project pointing at a non-project, a subdirectory, a read-only firing store, and a check that raises.

2. FOR EACH: assert the verdict exists, the record exists, and the exit code matches the documented contract end to end through the REAL binary. A verdict correct internally and wrong at the exit code is how this slice's worst defect survived two rounds.

3. THE ENUMERATION TEST ITSELF. .29 must ship a test that fails when a new exit path lands without a record. Verify it actually does that: add a deliberate record-less exit path, confirm the enumeration test REDDENS, then remove it by reverse edit. If it does not redden, the guard against regression does not exist and that is the headline finding.

4. THE SUBDIRECTORY DECISION. Whatever .29 chose, verify the SPEC's stated reasoning matches the code's behaviour, and that no discovery failure returns a silent skip at exit 0.

5. .29's named residuals — check each against its claimed width. An honesty note that understates has already been the finding twice in this slice.

Standing rule 5: sabotage what you assert, confirm it reddens as FAILED and never ERROR, compare collected/passed NUMBERS, name the reddened tests. Rule 9: reverse edit, never git checkout of a file. Rule 4: name where a test proves a seam rather than the real tool. Use bd import for bulk fixtures.

Report honestly if you find nothing. Three clean rounds would be evidence; one more forgotten path would be a different kind of evidence, and the coordinator wants to know which.

comments.text:
VERDICT [BDL-061.30] The boundary is REAL but NOT LOAD-BEARING. It holds at runtime for
Exception + SystemExit and its behaviour table is honest. Its *structural* guarantee — "an
exit added without a record is a diff that reddens" — does not hold, and one reachable
exit path escapes the handler entirely. Three findings, all measured, none manufactured.

=== 0. METHOD
Enumerated independently from invocation.py / project_root.py / guard.py / click 8.4.2's
main() BEFORE reading .29's table, then diffed. Baseline pinned at `-p no:randomly`; the
guard subset is 628 collected / 628 passed, which matches .29's stated baseline exactly.
Every sabotage: __pycache__ cleared both sides, reverse edit only, sha256 verified against
the pre-sabotage bytes, `git diff --stat -- src/` empty afterwards. No src/ change shipped.

=== 1. FINDING A (DEFECT, reachable) — the handler is not BaseException
`_answer` catches `SystemExit` and `Exception`. `KeyboardInterrupt` is neither, so it
escapes `run_invocation` — which the module docstring says "never raises". Click's main()
catches (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt) -> Abort -> **sys.exit(1)**.
MEASURED through real Click standalone dispatch in a subprocess (not CliRunner):
  rc=1, stderr "Aborted!", no verdict on any stream, guard-firings.jsonl absent.
That is .28's F7 shape exactly — exit 1 is the WARN code the shipped adapter reads as
"carry on" — in a different exception class. An interrupted guard therefore lets the edit
through AND leaves no trace, which is the one combination this slice exists to prevent.
.29 explicitly added `except SystemExit` because "a lower layer that terminates the process
without a verdict is the exact shape of every hole so far"; SystemExit is one of the five
BaseException subclasses and the other reachable one was not added. Section 8 does not name
it: the only pre/post-boundary escape listed is "an argv Click itself cannot parse".
REACHABILITY, honestly: Ctrl-C in the session delivers SIGINT to the foreground process
group, which includes a running hook. I could NOT reproduce it by SIGINT-ing the real
binary — the signal landed while the process was blocked in the `bd` subprocess and the run
resolved as "tracker unavailable" -> SKIP/0. So the escape is demonstrated by injecting
KeyboardInterrupt at the probe seam (rule 4: a seam, and the same seam .29 uses to inject
sys.exit and UnicodeDecodeError), while the exit CODE is measured through real click.main().
FIX: one line, `except Exception` -> `except BaseException` in `_answer`. Verified: with
that one edit applied, my 3 gap pins flip and ZERO of .29's 122 tests move; the interrupted
invocation becomes rc=2 with a recorded blocking error verdict. Reverse-edited.

=== 2. FINDING B (the deliverable's own guarantee) — the pins are spelling checks
`test_the_process_is_terminated_in_exactly_one_place` counts AST calls whose function is
NAMED `exit`, plus `raise SystemExit(...)` written as a Call, in `guard.py` ONLY.
  B1. Blind to the spelling. `os._exit(3)` (attr is `_exit`), `os.abort()`, a BARE
      `raise SystemExit` (node.exc is a Name, not a Call), and `raise click.Abort()` are all
      invisible. MEASURED: adding `os._exit(3)` to guard.py leaves all four .29 structural
      pins GREEN; only my wider pin reddens (1 FAILED / 122 passed).
  B2. Blind outside guard.py. Nothing scans invocation.py. MEASURED: adding
      `if invocation.name == "": sys.exit(0)` INSIDE `run_invocation` — one return
      preserved, one record_firing call site preserved, one `x.exit` call in guard.py
      preserved — ships **628/628 GREEN across the whole guard suite and all four pins**,
      while `beadloom guard ""` through the real binary exits 0, prints nothing and records
      nothing. A total silent bypass, invisible to the shipped suite. With my file added the
      same sabotage is 3 FAILED / 120 passed, all three mine.
      This is NOT S12 repeated: S12 put the exit where an enumerated row ran through it.
      This one is placed where the boundary module is unscanned and the argv unenumerated —
      which is precisely the failure mode of the last three rounds.
  B3. Pin B counts `Return` nodes in run_invocation; a terminator BEFORE the return is not
      a return, so the "exactly one return, and it is `_record(...)`" pin cannot see B2.
  B4. Pin C scans application/guards/** + guard.py; a `record_firing` call anywhere else in
      services/ is not counted.
  B5. Pin D is the substring `"exists=True" not in source`. .29's report states it as "no
      click.Path keyword other than path_type". `dir_okay=False` also exits before the
      callback (verified against click 8.4.2 directly) and passes the substring. Weight it
      honestly: the wider suite DOES catch it behaviourally (45 FAILED from the real-binary
      --project rows), so this is a pin-tightening, not a hole. Only mine reddens at the pin
      level (1 FAILED / 15 passed on the pin classes alone).
So: the boundary is one function at runtime, but "a new exit path cannot be added without
reddening" is true only for exits spelled `x.exit(...)` inside services/commands/guard.py.

=== 3. FINDING C (honesty note) — --project is not required to name a project
project_root.py: "What is deliberately NOT done: manufacturing a root. A guard that cannot
find a project ... does not create .beadloom/ where it stands." True of discovery, FALSE of
--project. `locate_project_root` accepts any `declared.is_dir()`. MEASURED through the real
binary against an existing directory with no .beadloom/:
  - honoured verbatim, no refusal;
  - no flow.yml found -> the project's declared `block` becomes the shipped default `warn`
    -> exit **1**, non-blocking (with a tracker that answers; SKIP/0 when it does not);
  - `.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl` CREATED in that directory.
That is the coordinator's measured F9 failure — wrong root, defaults instead of declared
strictness, a stray self-entrenching .beadloom/ — reachable through an explicit flag. .28
listed it as minor m3; .29's section 8 residual list does not name it and the module
docstring denies it. The bead warned that an understating honesty note has already been the
finding twice in this slice; this is the third.

=== 4. MY ENUMERATION vs .29's 16 ROWS (the diff, machine-checked in a test)
Present in mine, absent from theirs: an empty guard name `""`; a --project that exists but
is not a project; a hook payload of zero bytes; a --context key supplied twice; an interrupt
during the evaluation. Four of the five behave correctly — enumeration gaps, not defects:
  - `beadloom guard ""` -> exit 3, error verdict, "not recorded", nothing written. Correct,
    but the verdict's `guard` field reads "(no guard named)" while `why` says
    "unknown guard ''" (`name or UNNAMED_GUARD` swallows the empty string), so the
    not-recorded reason quotes a guard the caller never typed. Cosmetic.
  - empty stdin with --hook -> `{}` -> an ordinary evaluation, recorded, no crash.
  - repeated --context path= -> last wins, silently. Fail-closed in the order tested.
  - stdin CLOSED (`0<&-`) with --hook -> exit 2, recorded, no traceback — but the reason is
    the raw "AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'read'". Fail-closed and
    honest-ish; an internal repr where a stated cause belongs.
Also enumerated and NOT a gap: no arguments, unknown guard name, --liveness over a broken
store, unreadable/malformed/empty flow.yml, absent flow.yml, JSON of the wrong shape,
--context with no `=`, --project missing, a subdirectory, an unwritable record, a check that
raises — all present in .29's table or its injection class and all correct.

=== 5. ATTACKED AND HELD (reported so a clean result is not mistaken for a shallow one)
  - The RENDER step. `_emit` runs after the boundary returns and before `sys.exit`; an
    exception there is a traceback at exit 1 with the record already written. I could not
    reach one: PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii does not break the hard-coded em-dash (click re-wraps
    a non-UTF-8 stream), a lone surrogate from argv survives because `repr()` escapes it in
    not_covered and `json.dumps` is ensure_ascii, a closed fd 1 does not raise, and the
    output is far under the pipe buffer so `| head` never yields EPIPE. Structurally the
    render step is still outside the boundary and nothing pins that it cannot raise.
  - `_record` catches Exception around `record_firing` but NOT SystemExit, and
    `run_invocation`'s own body is inside no try — an asymmetry with `_answer`, unreachable
    today because record_firing only mkdirs and appends.
  - The exit-code rule (3 = declared-config defect / unusable command line, 2 = this edit)
    HOLDS on every path. All eleven `raise GuardConfigError` sites are in config.py, i.e.
    flow.yml parsing; every other exit-3 comes from argv. Nothing harness-supplied can land
    on 3. Re-verified by grep of the raise sites plus the real-binary rows.
  - `_should_record`'s three exceptions are each genuinely intrinsic. The weakest is
    "unregistered name", because it composes with "exit 3 does not block in Claude Code"
    into a mis-typed adapter that bypasses silently forever — but `--liveness` DOES surface
    that as never-fired, which is the honest reading, so it is a residual, not a gap wearing
    a reason. Verified live: `beadloom guard bead-clamed` -> exit 3, not recorded, and the
    liveness row for the real guard is unaffected.
  - Walk-up discovery cannot be pointed somewhere unintended beyond the named nested-marker
    residual: the marker must be a directory, Path.cwd() is already physical so resolve() is
    a no-op, and there is no user-level ~/.beadloom for the walk to hit.
  - firing.py claims "an append is atomic enough for parallel agents". 32 concurrent
    processes each writing a 20,853-byte record produced 32 physical lines and 32 parseable
    firings on APFS. Held.

=== 6. SPOT-CHECKS OF .29's SABOTAGE TABLE (3 of 17, chosen where failure would matter most)
Reproduced independently by reverse-engineering the edit from the row text. All FAILED, zero
ERROR, every failed+passed sums to the 628 baseline:
  S2  run_invocation returns without _record   -> 88 FAILED / 540  (.29 said 88; their sum
      is 627 because S1-S15 predate class (d)) — includes the one-return AST pin.
  S6  discovery stops at cwd                   ->  6 FAILED / 622  (.29 said 6) — exactly
      the F9 class; only 2 of the 6 run through the real binary.
  S14 payload error back to exit 3             -> 19 FAILED / 609  (.29 said 19) — the
      fail-open .28 flagged; reddens across invocation, adversarial, cli and parity.
.29's numbers are accurate where I checked them.

=== 7. WHAT I SHIPPED
tests/test_guards_boundary_escapes.py — 25 tests, all passing on the shipped source, in the
gap-pin style .28 used and .29 closed (each class is NAMED for the gap, so the fix is a
rename, not a deletion):
  TestAnInterruptEscapesTheBoundary (4)          — Finding A, incl. the real-click subprocess
    measurement and an AST read of the except clauses; plus a control proving the same seam
    IS caught for an ordinary exception.
  TestTheOneWayOutPinCannotSeeEveryWayOut (12)   — Finding B. Reproduces .29's predicate
    verbatim and shows it green beside four terminator spellings, and contributes the wider
    pin (`_terminators_of_any_spelling` over guard.py + invocation.py + project_root.py,
    asserting exactly `[("guard.py", "sys.exit(result.exit_code)")]`) plus an AST pin that
    the --project click.Path takes only `path_type`.
  TestADeclaredProjectNeedNotBeAProject (4)      — Finding C, incl. a test that reads the
    contradicted sentence out of project_root.py so the doc and the code cannot drift apart

  TestExitPathsTheEnumerationDoesNotList (5)     — the enumeration diff, with the disjointness
    against .29's `_EXIT_PATHS` asserted in code rather than in prose.
Each new pin verified to redden as FAILED under the sabotage it guards (M1 os._exit: 1 FAILED
/122; M2 in-boundary sys.exit: 3 FAILED/120; M3 dir_okay=False: 1 FAILED/15 on the pin
classes; M4 the BaseException fix: 3 FAILED/120, all mine).

title: [BDL-061.29][dev] S1 fix-3: make 'no invocation without a verdict and a record' structural
description:
Fourth cycle. The diagnosis changed, and the change is the point.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG: .27's path work holds. Traversal, backslash and NUL are closed, the accepted shape is stated in the SPEC, and the refusal explains the hazard rather than merely rejecting. Do not redo it.

WHAT IS WRONG: the invariant 'no invocation ends without a verdict AND a firing record' is honoured CASE BY CASE. The command has many entry paths — argument parsing, stdin read, project discovery from cwd, strip ordering, the checks themselves — and each new one is a fresh place to forget it. Three cycles have now each found a different forgotten place, and .27's own fix introduced one.

FOUR SYMPTOMS, both headline ones reproduced by the coordinator through the real CLI:
  - A non-UTF-8 byte on the hook's stdin gives a raw UnicodeDecodeError, exit 1 (the WARN code, which the harness reads as non-blocking), no verdict, no record. sys.stdin.read() sits outside both handlers .27 added.
  - Six invocations naming a REGISTERED guard leave no record, while the SPEC states exactly one exception.
  - Run from a subdirectory, a declared 'block' becomes a non-blocking outcome with exclusions dropped and the firing written where --liveness never reads it. Coordinator measured: from src/beadloom the guard returns skip/exit 0 'tracker unavailable'. An agent not sitting in the project root is silently unguarded.
  - The strip runs before the shape is judged, so nine C0 control characters turn a 'block' into a 'skip' whose reason names a pattern that does not cover the file. Residual (1) in .27 understates this.

THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT FOUR PATCHES. Put ONE boundary around every invocation so that any failure anywhere — including argument parsing and the stdin read, i.e. before a guard name is even known — produces a verdict and a record. A crash becomes a recorded verdict of 'I could not tell'. New failure modes will still exist; the requirement is that they become VISIBLE in --liveness instead of invisible in a traceback. Fix the four symptoms as a consequence of the boundary, and use them to prove it.

Make it hard to regress: add a test that ENUMERATES the command's exit paths and asserts each leaves a record, so adding a new exit without one fails rather than passes silently. That test is the deliverable as much as the boundary is.

ONE DESIGN DECISION TO MAKE AND DOCUMENT: project discovery from a subdirectory. Walking up to find the project root is the conventional behaviour and keeps legitimate work working; refusing is consistent with .27's narrow-the-input philosophy but breaks an agent that simply changed directory. Whatever you choose, a guard that cannot locate the project must NOT return a silent skip at exit 0 — that is the same 'looks like it ran' failure in yet another spelling. Write the reasoning into the SPEC, not just the choice.

Done when: every enumerated exit path produces a verdict and a record; no path exits 1 unless the verdict is genuinely 'warn'; the four symptoms are closed with tests that FAIL on d4bb618; the enumeration test exists; the SPEC states the discovery decision and its reason; not_covered is truthful and the remaining cases are named.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COORDINATOR — additional measured evidence for the subdirectory case (found by inspecting the tree after the probe, not by an agent report).

Running `beadloom guard bead-claimed --hook claude-code` from /Users/v.zoologov/beadloom/src/beadloom does more than skip silently. It CREATED src/beadloom/.beadloom/ containing guard-firings.jsonl with exactly one line:

  {"at": "2026-08-22T10:49:45Z", "context": {"path": "app.py"}, "guard": "bead-claimed",
   "outcome": "skip", "why": "the work tracker is unavailable - cannot tell whether a bead is claimed",
   "not_covered": ["whether the claimed bead's scope actually covers this path"]}

Three things follow, and they sharpen this bead's invariant:

1. A guard declared READ-ONLY wrote to the source tree. CONTEXT decision: 'Guards are read-only ... a check that writes to the artifact it checks cannot be trusted about it.' The firing record is a deliberate write, so the rule needs its honest wording (read-only w.r.t. the INDEX; the record is the one write) - and that write must land in the PROJECT's record, never wherever the process happened to start.

2. It manufactured a second project root INSIDE the real project. A record in the wrong place is indistinguishable from no record. Whatever boundary you build, the invariant is 'the PROJECT's record', located by discovery, not by cwd.

COMPLETED [BDL-061.29] S1 fix-3 — the invariant is now STRUCTURAL, and the four symptoms
closed as consequences of it. Commit 2a82dad on features/BDL-061. Suite 5376 -> 5476 passed /
10 skipped / 0 failed; guard subset 528 -> 628.

=== 1. THE DIRECTION: one boundary, not four patches
New `application/guards/invocation.py` owns one sentence: EVERY invocation of the guard
command returns through `run_invocation`, which is `_record(_answer(invocation))` and has
exactly ONE return statement. `_answer` decides and may fail in any way at all; `_record`
writes and is the only `record_firing` call site in the codebase. Argument parsing, the hook
payload read and project discovery all happen INSIDE `_answer`'s try — including the locate
step, which starts as 'no project' precisely so that a failure to locate one still reaches the
handler. `except SystemExit` is caught as well as `except Exception`: a lower layer that
terminates the process without a verdict is the exact shape of every hole so far (that is what
`_fail()` did on six paths), so inside the boundary it becomes a recorded 'I could not tell'.
services/commands/guard.py is now render + ONE sys.exit; it does no validation Click would
exit on (--project lost `exists=True`), because an option Click rejects exits before the
callback and therefore before the boundary.

RECORDING IS ONE PREDICATE, STATED ONCE: a firing is written when the invocation produced a
verdict, a project was located, and the verdict names a registered guard. Three exceptions,
each intrinsic and each REPORTED on the result ('not recorded: <reason>' on stderr, `recorded`
+ `not_recorded_because` under --json) rather than inferred from an absent line: a successful
--liveness evaluated nothing; an unlocatable project has nowhere to write (and manufacturing
one was the measured defect); an unregistered name has nothing to attribute the row to. A
fourth case is a failure, not an exception: a record that cannot be written still lets the
verdict reach the reader, carrying the reason.

=== 2. THE DESIGN DECISION, WITH ITS REASONING (SPEC 'The project a guard answers about')
Chosen: WALK UP from cwd to the nearest ancestor holding `.beadloom/`; --project is honoured
verbatim with no search. Rejected: refusing to run outside a project root (consistent with
.27's narrow-the-input, but it turns an agent that merely changed directory into one that
cannot edit anything for a reason it cannot fix from inside the harness — and it does not
remove the 'cannot locate' path, it makes it the common case). Walking up is also not the kind
of guess .27 removed: that was about repairing a MODEL-SUPPLIED STRING; a directory tree is
not model-supplied and `.beadloom/` is evidence, not inference. Marker is `.beadloom/` and not
`.git/` because it is where flow.yml and the record already live (and .git nests). A guard
that cannot locate a project answers `error` (exit 2, blocks) and CREATES NOTHING. Residual
named: a nested `.beadloom/` makes the inner directory the root beneath it — which is what a
nested project is.

=== 3. THE FOUR SYMPTOMS, MEASURED THROUGH THE REAL BINARY
F7 undecodable stdin: was rc=1 (the WARN code) + UnicodeDecodeError traceback + no record.
   Now rc=2, no traceback, one 'error' firing. Three byte payloads asserted.
F8 six unrecorded invocations naming a registered guard: all six now record. The two payload

F9 subdirectory: was BLOCK/rc2 at the root vs WARN/rc1 from src/deep, firing written to a NEW

F10 the strip: DELETED, not narrowed. The shape is judged on the string exactly as supplied,
   so all nine C0 characters str.strip() swallowed are refused, and `src/app.py` + U+00A0
   is BLOCKed (guarded) instead of skipped quoting a pattern that does not cover it. m2 fixed
   in the same change (glob anchor `$` -> `\\Z`) so the inner lock is not left open behind the
   outer one. m1: --project <missing> is now an 'error' verdict with a reason, not Click's
   bare exit 2.

=== 4. THE EXIT-CODE RULE (written into the SPEC + cli.md)
3 = a defect in the project's DECLARED CONFIGURATION (unparseable guards:, an exclusion with
no reason, an unregistered guard name) or a command line the CLI could not use at all (no
name, --liveness with a name, a malformed --context pair, an unsupported --hook harness) —
stable defects that fail identically every time and are not about any edit. 2 = everything
that goes wrong while answering about THIS edit (payload undecodable/unparseable, project not
located, any exception). That closes the fail-open path .28 flagged: a truncated pipe used to
exit 3, which the harness treats as non-blocking. No path exits 1 unless the verdict is
genuinely 'warn' — asserted as a property over the whole enumeration table.

=== 5. THE ENUMERATION TEST (tests/test_guards_invocation.py, 98 tests) — the deliverable
(a) 16-row table of every way the command can terminate; the 'records' expectation is DERIVED
    from `_should_record(name, project_located, produced_a_verdict)`, not written per row, so a
    new exit path cannot be added with a hand-written False. Three properties over the same
    table: it records iff the rule says so, it always says something (never a traceback), and
    it never exits 1 unless the JSON outcome is 'warn'.
(b) STRUCTURE (AST, the part a behaviour table cannot see): the process is terminated in
    exactly ONE place in the command module; `run_invocation` has exactly ONE return and it is
    `_record(...)`; `record_firing` has exactly ONE call site across the package + the command;
    no click.Path keyword other than path_type (an option Click validates exits before the
    boundary).
(c) INJECTION — a failure nobody enumerated is still a verdict: an exception in a check, a
    `sys.exit(7)` in a check, an unreadable stdin, an unwritable record, and a locate step
    that raises.
(d) In-process discovery + boundary tests, so the walk is covered without the console script.

=== 6. SABOTAGE (rule 5) — 17 applied one at a time; EVERY reddening FAILED, zero ERROR
Baseline 628 collected / 628 passed (627 for S1-S15, run before (d) was added); every row's
failed+passed sums to the baseline, so no test was lost to collection. __pycache__ cleared on
both sides of every run; each restored by REVERSE EDIT and verified by sha256 against the
pre-sabotage bytes; `git diff --stat -- src/` matches the intended change set.

 S11 a second way out of the command       -> 23 FAILED (incl. the one-exit AST pin)
 S12 a record-less exit inside the boundary-> 35 FAILED (.30's attack shape; the AST pin
     'the boundary returns through the recording step and nowhere else' is among them)
 S13 --project validated by Click again    ->  3 FAILED (m1 + the no-validation pin)
 S14 payload error back to exit 3          -> 19 FAILED
 S15 record a firing for an unregistered name -> 7 FAILED

RED FIRST, on d4bb618: the FINAL test file against .28's source = 51 FAILED / 46 passed, 0
collection errors (20 of the 51 fail with ModuleNotFoundError for modules that do not exist
there — stated rather than counted as assertions).

=== 7. .28's PINS: every gap pin rewritten as CLOSED, none deleted
TestTheStripHappensBeforeTheShapeIsJudged, TestAnEmptyTargetIsAbsent...(now
...AndTheSpecNowSaysSo), TestTheExclusionMatcherIsNotFullyAnchored (now ...IsAnchoredAtBothEnds),
TestAHookPayloadTheProcessCannotDecode, TestTheProjectRootIsWhereverTheShellIs (now
TestTheProjectIsDiscoveredNotTakenFromTheShell), the m1 row, residual (1), and the
EveryWayTheCommandCanTerminate table (records column flipped for the five rows the fix fixes).
The empty-target drift was F6's class and was fixed IN THE DOCUMENT (the code's behaviour was
the better one), with a test that reads the SPEC so the two cannot drift again.

=== 8. WHAT REMAINS, NAMED (not_covered NOT widened)
- An argv Click itself cannot parse (an unknown option) never reaches the callback: exit 2

- A whitespace-only target ('   ') is now a path naming a file of three spaces rather than

Coverage: invocation.py 100%, project_root.py 100%, services/commands/guard.py 100%, guards
