title: [BDL-061.28][test] S1 fix-2: adversarial path input, and no invocation without a record
description:
Independently verify .27. Standing rule 6: the fix author's own tests are not evidence.

Two fix cycles have now shipped a bypass each, both from model-controlled path strings, and the second cycle INTRODUCED one. Assume a third exists and go looking for it.

1. ADVERSARIAL INPUT. Build the table and state, per row, the verdict AND whether a firing was recorded: backslash separators (single and mixed), NUL and other control bytes, percent-encoded traversal ('%2e%2e'), Unicode separators and homoglyphs, an over-long path, a path that is only dots, an empty string, a path that normalises to the project root, a symlink pointing outside the project, an absolute path outside the project, and at least three you invent. The point is not to pass — it is to find the row where the guard is wrong and say so.

2. NO SILENT INVOCATION. For every row above, assert a firing record exists. An invocation that produces no record is invisible to --liveness, and --liveness is the report that must not lie. A crash must be a recorded verdict of 'I could not tell', not an absence.

3. EXIT-CODE CONTRACT. Assert the mapping end to end through the real CLI: 0 pass/skip, 1 warn, 2 block, 3 config-error. Any path that produces an exit code the harness will misread is a finding regardless of what the verdict says internally — that is exactly how F2 slipped through.

4. THE not_covered NOTE. After the fix, verify it is TRUE, not merely shorter. If a case is uncovered and the note is silent, that is the finding. Check the SPEC's stated path shape against what the code actually accepts.

5. Re-verify that F1 and F2 are closed by tests that FAIL on a3b0d4d / 6970d62.

Standing rule 5, and it has now been earned three times over: sabotage every fix, confirm THAT test reddens as FAILED and never ERROR, compare collected/passed NUMBERS, name the reddened tests. Restore by reverse edit, never 'git checkout <file>' (rule 9). Rule 4: say plainly where a test proves a seam's contract rather than the real tool's.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TESTS [BDL-061.28] S1 fix-2 re-verification — 151 new tests (tests/test_guards_adversarial.py),
suite 5225 -> 5376 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed, coverage 98.7% on application/guards.
Nothing taken on .27's word (rule 6). FOUR findings, all reachable, none in .27's residuals.
Committed on features/BDL-061 as d4bb618. No src/ or docs/ change: this bead verifies.

=== F7. THE F2 FAILURE MODE IS STILL REACHABLE — a byte, not a spelling  [the headline]
`--hook` reads sys.stdin.read(), which decodes strict UTF-8. A payload carrying one non-UTF-8
byte produces, measured through the REAL binary (not CliRunner — a CliRunner supplies an
already-decoded string and cannot reproduce a decoding failure at all):
    rc=1, raw UnicodeDecodeError traceback on stderr, NO verdict, NO firing record.
That is F2's four properties, from the same input class (the harness's stdin), reached by a
different byte. UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError but not a HookPayloadError, and the read
happens BEFORE the try that wraps evaluate_guard, so neither of .27's two handlers sees it.
rc=1 is the warn code, which the shipped adapter's own comment calls "shown, never blocking".
Sharpest part: .27 deliberately ADDED 'src/\udcff.py' to its accepted list ("a real non-UTF-8
byte ... so it names a file that can actually exist") — so the transport refuses, with a crash,
a name the shape gate one layer down says it accepts. Both halves asserted side by side.
Reachability: the emitted adapter is `exec beadloom guard "$1" --hook claude-code`, i.e. the
harness's stdin verbatim. Pinned: TestAHookPayloadTheProcessCannotDecode (4 tests).

=== F8. SIX INVOCATIONS THAT NAME A REGISTERED GUARD LEAVE NO RECORD
SPEC invariant, verbatim: "No invocation that names a registered guard ends without a firing
record. The single exception is a name that is not a registered guard." .27's COMPLETED comment
says the same ("One exception, stated in the docstring and pinned by a test"). Measured through
the real binary in an isolated project, guard name `bead-claimed`, records before/after:
    --context nonsense                     rc=3  records +0
    --context '=value'                     rc=3  records +0
    --hook no-such-harness                 rc=3  records +0
    --hook claude-code  + '{not json'      rc=3  records +0   <- harness-supplied, F2's class
    --hook claude-code  + '[1,2]'          rc=3  records +0
    --project <missing dir>                rc=2  records +0   <- see the exit-code note below
    --liveness bead-claimed                rc=3  records +0   (a report, not an evaluation —
                                                               listed for completeness)
Every one routes through _fail(), which sys.exit()s before record_firing is reached. The
consequence is asserted directly rather than argued: `--liveness --json` is byte-identical
before and after an unrecorded invocation, so the report goes on showing yesterday's healthy
verdict through today's unguarded edit. That is the one report whose whole product is honesty.
The unparseable-payload row is the one that matters — that string comes from the harness, so a
schema change or a truncated pipe silently disables the gate, loudly but fail-open (exit 3 does
not block in Claude Code either; .27's own FRICTION #1).
Pinned: TestEveryWayTheCommandCanTerminate — an 11-row parametrized table with an explicit
`records` column, so a fix flips exactly the rows it fixes.

=== F9. FROM A SUBDIRECTORY, A DECLARED `block` BECOMES A NON-BLOCKING `warn`
The emitted adapter passes no --project, so the DECISION root is Path.cwd(), and
load_guards_config does not walk upwards. hook_command anchors the SCRIPT with
$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and its docstring gives the reason — cwd "is not the project root for every
tool invocation" — then leaves the decision on cwd anyway. Measured, project flow.yml declaring
strictness block + one exclusion:
    from the project root   -> BLOCK, rc 2, recorded in <root>/.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl
    from <root>/src/deep    -> WARN,  rc 1, recorded in <root>/src/deep/.beadloom/...
Three things at once: the declared strictness is gone (blocking -> non-blocking), every declared
exclusion is gone with it, and the firing lands in a NEW .beadloom/ directory that --liveness at
the root never reads — measured: rows["working-branch"]["never_fired"] is True, fired_count 0,
after a real evaluation happened. A fourth way the report can be honest and wrong.
Pinned: TestTheProjectRootIsWhereverTheShellIs (4 tests, all real-process).

=== F10. THE STRIP RUNS BEFORE THE SHAPE IS JUDGED — residual (1) UNDERSTATES
resolve_edit_path does raw.strip() and THEN rejection_reason(). str.strip() removes every
character Python calls whitespace, which includes \t \n \v \f \r and U+001C-U+001F — nine code
points inside the U+0000-U+001F range the SAME SPEC paragraph says are refused. Two sentences of
the SPEC disagree and the code resolves it in the ACCEPTING direction. Also stripped: U+00A0,
U+0085, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028/9, U+3000 — each naming a real, creatable, DIFFERENT file.
.27 records the cost as "a file whose name genuinely ends in whitespace is guarded as though it
did not", which reads as harmless. Measured, with `src/*.py` excluded and strictness block:
    src/app.py        -> SKIP  "excluded by 'src/*.py'"    (correct)
    src/app.py + \n   -> SKIP  "excluded by 'src/*.py'"    exit 0
    src/app.py + \xa0 -> SKIP  "excluded by 'src/*.py'"    exit 0
and GuardExclusion("src/*.py").matches("src/app.py\xa0") is False — i.e. the guard exempts a file
the pattern it names does not cover, and prints a reason that is true about the stripped string
and false about the file the writer will create. That is F1's exact shape with a different
character, and it is the direction .27 says the shape gate exists to close.
Pinned: TestTheStripHappensBeforeTheShapeIsJudged (22 tests) + the counter-example kept next to
the residual it contradicts (test_the_whitespace_residual_is_wider_than_the_spec_states).

=== TWO MORE, SMALLER, BOTH STATED WITH THEIR DIRECTION
m1 A USAGE ERROR BORROWS THE BLOCK CODE. `--project <missing>` is validated by Click
   (exists=True), which exits 2 — the code the SPEC reserves for a block, "deliberately not 2,
   which is Click's own usage code and would otherwise be indistinguishable from a genuine
   block". So the collision the SPEC says was designed out is reachable from the command's own
   option, with no verdict and no record. Fail-CLOSED, so it costs work, not safety.
m2 THE EXCLUSION GLOB IS NOT FULLY ANCHORED. _glob_to_regex ends in '$' and calls .match(), and
   Python's '$' also matches before a trailing newline: GuardExclusion("src/*.py").matches(
   "src/app.py\n") is True. Latent today — the strip means the newline never reaches the matcher
   — so the module has two locks with the same hole and the outer one is what holds. Bounded
   honestly by a second test: one trailing newline, not any suffix. Pinned so that fixing F10
   does not silently leave this open.

=== THE FOUR QUESTIONS, ANSWERED
1. THE ACCEPTED SHAPE, BOTH SIDES. 17 rows the SPEC accepts are not refused (emoji, 4096-char
   component, 40x200-char path, %2e%2e, U+2044, a Cyrillic homoglyph, '...', '\udcff', a
   non-leading '~'); 17 rows it refuses do not slip through (UNC path, trailing backslash, NUL
   at start/middle/end, BEL, ESC, DEL, CR, bare '~'). One drift each way: F10 (accepts what it
   documents as refused) and an empty target, which the SPEC's "a non-empty string ... anything
   else is refused" makes an error and the code makes PathScope.ABSENT — safe direction, better
   behaviour, wrong document; that is F6's class exactly. A new test parses the SPEC's shape
   sentence and asserts each of its four clauses is enforced by rejection_reason, so the pair
   cannot drift in silence again.
2. EVERY REJECTION'S not_covered. There are exactly three routes to `error` and all three are
   asserted, on the full string not on non-emptiness: a refused path names "everything this
   guard checks ... refused as malformed before any exclusion or check was applied to it", and
   the note is verified TRUE rather than trusted — the exclusion matcher and the check are both
   instrumented and asserted never to have been called. A config error and an unexpected
   exception both name "everything guard 'X' checks: the evaluation did not complete", the
   config one across three different malformations. The GuardVerdict invariant that makes this
   structural (an error cannot be built without the note) is pinned separately.
3. NO SILENT INVOCATION. Enumerated, not sampled — see F8's table. The recorded routes are
   pass/warn/block/skip/error/config-error/missing-tracker plus an exception raised inside a
   CHECK (.27 pinned the evaluator; a real future defect lives two layers deeper).
4. THE EXIT-CODE CONTRACT, END TO END. Measured on the installed executable in a real git
   repo with no probe stubbed — pass 0, skip 0, warn 1, block 2, error 2, config 3, no traceback
   on any of them — plus which stream each reaches, because the harness reads stderr.

=== THE ADVERSARIAL TABLE (constant config: bead-claimed at `block`, 'src/**' excluded, tracker
    answers "nothing claimed"; every row driven through the CLI, so the exit code and the firing
    record are the real ones). 23 rows + 2 outside-the-project rows.
    spelling                          verdict  rc  recorded  note
    src\app.py                        error    2   yes       backslash
    src\sub/app.py                    error    2   yes       mixed separators (new)
    src/app.py + NUL                  error    2   yes
    src/\x1b[31mapp.py                error    2   yes       ANSI escape (new)
    src/app\x7f.py                    error    2   yes       DEL (new)
    ~/secrets.env                     error    2   yes
    %2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd          block    2   yes       never decoded; does not escape
    src\u2044app.py                   block    2   yes       U+2044 look-alike (new)
    \u0455rc/app.py                   block    2   yes       Cyrillic homoglyph (new)
    'a'*4096 + '.py'                  block    2   yes       no length limit, as documented
    '..'                              block    2   yes       outside root, named in not_covered
    '...'                             block    2   yes       a literal name (new)
    ''                                block    2   yes       ABSENT, not the documented refusal
    '.'                               block    2   yes       the root itself
    src/app.py                        skip     0   yes       honestly excluded
    docs/../src/app.py                skip     0   yes       traversal into the exclusion
    src/                              block    2   yes       'src/**' does not name the dir (new)
    ../<root>/src/app.py              skip     0   yes       leaves and returns (new)
    src/app.py + '\n'                 skip     0   yes       *** F10 ***
    src/app.py + U+00A0               skip     0   yes       *** F10 ***
    src/ap<U+200B>p.py                skip     0   yes       under src/, so genuinely excluded
    src/<U+202E>gpj.txt               skip     0   yes       see m3 below
    .beadloom/flow.yml                block    2   yes       the guard's own config (new)
    <abs path outside the project>    block    2   yes       not_covered names the target
    src/link.txt -> outside           block    2   yes       symlink out, not_covered names it
m3 A target inside the shape is echoed VERBATIM into `why`, so a bidirectional override or a
   zero-width character reorders what a human reads in the hook's stderr. Display-only, and every
   character that could inject a terminal control sequence is already outside the shape — but it
   is the un-named half of residual (3) ("a homoglyph names a different file, which the guard
   then reports accurately"): accurately about the file, not about what the reader sees. Both
   directions pinned, including the positive property that a REFUSED target is repr-escaped and
   truncated at 120 characters before it reaches stderr and the JSONL record.

=== .27's RESIDUALS, EACH CHECKED AGAINST THE WIDTH IT CLAIMS
  (1) whitespace strip              NOT AS NARROW AS CLAIMED -> F10.
  (2) bare drive letter 'C:/...'    AS CLAIMED. Reads as a relative directory 'C:', so the guard
      runs on a file that does not exist instead of skipping, and an exclusion written for the
      tree does not exempt it (measured: BLOCK). Over-guard, as stated.
  (3) homoglyphs name a different file  AS CLAIMED for the verdict (U+2044, U+FF0F, Cyrillic 's'
      all fall outside 'src/**' and are guarded, never exempted). Incomplete for the REPORT: m3.
  (4) no length limit               AS CLAIMED. 4096-char component, 40x200-char path, and 1000
      nested traversals all resolve without raising and land inside.
  (5) no percent-decoding           AS CLAIMED. '%2e%2e/...', 'src%2fapp.py', 'src/app.py%00' all
      resolve to themselves, so the guard sees the name the writer will use.

=== A NOTE ON WHICH LOCK IS HOLDING (rule 8, one level down)
The evaluator and the SPEC both explain the refusal by ORDER — malformed decided "before
exclusions, because matching a pattern against a string the guard has refused to interpret is
the bypass this order removes". Measured: moving the exclusion lookup AHEAD of the malformed
check reddens NOTHING (148 passed, 0 failed), because exclusion_for(None) returns None. Deleting
`relative is None` from the refusal reddens 18. The documented reason names the weaker of the
two guarantees. Not a defect — but the load-bearing lock now has its own test, and the property
"a refused target is never matched against an exclusion" is pinned against a declared '**'.

=== SABOTAGE (rule 5) — 15 applied one at a time; EVERY reddening FAILED, zero ERROR
Baseline 151 collected / 151 passed. __pycache__ cleared on both sides of every run (.27's
stale-.pyc trap). Restored by REVERSE EDIT (rule 9), each verified by sha256 against the
pre-sabotage bytes; `git diff --stat -- src/` empty at the end.
 S1  drop the backslash rule        -> 13 FAILED /135: 5 refusal rows, the exclusion-ordering row,
     the SPEC-clause test, 2 table rows, the not_covered test, the terminate-table row.
 S2  drop the control-char rule     ->  9 FAILED /137 (139 rows incl. 8 refusal params).  [11]
 S3  drop the leading-tilde rule    ->  6 FAILED /142.
 S4  drop the encodability rule     ->  2 FAILED /146.
 S5  exclusions before the refusal  ->  0 FAILED — see the note above; replaced by S5b.
 S5b match the RAW string first     -> 10 FAILED /138: all 4 ordering rows, the "nothing ran"
     assertion, 4 table rows, the refusal-note test. (F1's actual shape.)
 S6  ERROR exits 1 instead of 2     -> 14 FAILED /134, incl. the real-binary error row.
 S7  stop recording the firing      -> 35 FAILED /113 — the largest, as it should be.
 S8  remove the last-resort handler ->  2 FAILED /146: the exception-inside-a-check test and its
     not_covered pair (RuntimeError escapes to the runner, i.e. the traceback returns).
 S9  refusal names something else   ->  1 FAILED /147.
 S10 a refused path gets a relative ->  18 FAILED /133 (the lock that actually holds).
 S11 echo the refused target raw    ->  2 FAILED /149.
 S12 escape an accepted target      ->  1 FAILED /150.
A PIN THAT DOES NOT REDDEN WHEN THE GAP IS CLOSED PINS NOTHING — each gap's FIX applied:
 P1  judge the shape BEFORE strip   -> 13 FAILED /135: the whole F10 class + the residual test.
 P2  fullmatch instead of '$'       ->  1 FAILED /147: the m2 pin.
 P3  record on the --context route  ->  3 FAILED /145.   P3b same for the hook routes -> 6 FAILED.
 P4  decode stdin with surrogates   ->  3 FAILED /145: all three F7 rows.
 P5  walk upwards for the root      ->  4 FAILED /144: the whole F9 class.
 P6  an empty target is refused     ->  4 FAILED /144: the SPEC-drift class.

=== WHERE A TEST PROVES A SEAM AND NOT THE TOOL (rule 4)
The exit-code, stdin-decoding and project-root classes (19 tests) run the INSTALLED `beadloom`
in a subprocess with raw bytes on stdin, and skip with a reason if the console script is absent
— a CliRunner proves Click's dispatch and the SystemExit it raises, not the process's exit
status, and it cannot reproduce a decoding failure at all. The remaining CLI tests use CliRunner
and therefore prove the command's own logic, not the process contract; that is stated in the
module docstring. The `bead-claimed` probes are stubbed at the GuardProbes boundary — the real-bd
transport is covered by .26's TestRealProbes and is not re-proved here. The real-binary exit-code
rows use `working-branch`, which needs only git, so no probe is stubbed in any of them.

=== GATE
pytest 5376 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed (5225 at .27; +151, all mine). ruff clean. mypy
--strict clean (181 files). Coverage on application/guards + the guard command 98.7%
(paths.py, evaluation.py, config.py, firing.py, contract.py, bead_claimed.py all 100%).
Clean-DB gate (rule 1): rm beadloom.db -> reindex (665 chunks / 1220 symbols / 1298 imports /
12 rules) -> sync-check rc=0 -> lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules.

=== WHAT I WOULD NOT SHIP WITHOUT A DECISION
F7 first (it is F2 again, exit 1, unrecorded, harness-reachable), then F9 (a declared block that
silently is not one), then F8's payload row. F10 is a correctness-of-reporting bug and a
documentation bug at once; m1/m2/m3 can wait, but m2 must be fixed in the same change as F10 or
the second lock is left open behind the first.

=== FRICTION (for BDL-UX)
1. The .27 report names ONE exception to "no invocation without a record"; there are six. An
   invariant stated in a SPEC and enforced by exactly one test at one call site is how this
   keeps happening — the enumeration belongs in a table test, which is what this bead added.
2. `guard --liveness` reads only <cwd>/.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl, so any invocation from a
   subdirectory is invisible to it AND creates a stray .beadloom/. Worth a "this project root
   was inferred from cwd" line in the report, or refusing to record outside a project root.
3. Two spellings of the same class shipped in one slice (F2 = a byte in the path, F7 = a byte in
   the transport). A single test that feeds arbitrary BYTES end to end — argv, stdin, both —
   would have caught both at once; the suite tests strings everywhere.

title: [BDL-061.27][dev] S1 fix-2: narrow the guard's path input instead of normalising it
description:
Second fix cycle. Review .3 and test .26 both found that a model-supplied path defeats the guard, twice, from the same root: an arbitrary-shaped, model-controlled string is parsed on the guard's side.

BOTH REPRODUCED BY THE COORDINATOR through the real CLI:

F1 — a Windows-style separator still bypasses, AFTER the .25 fix.
  exclusion '*.py', strictness block:
    path=src/app.py  -> block
    path=src\app.py  -> skip, why: "excluded by '*.py'"
  A backslash is a legal POSIX filename character, so 'src\app.py' resolves to ONE component and
  '*.py' — correctly taught by .25 not to cross directories — matches it. The guard is switched off
  by a spelling, and the printed reason is FALSE about the file the harness will write. not_covered
  is silent. Reachable from Claude Code on Windows, from WSL, and from any model that types a
  Windows path.

F2 — a NUL byte produces no verdict at all, and this was INTRODUCED BY the .25 fix.
    ValueError: lstat: embedded null character in path   (unhandled traceback)
    real exit code = 1  -> the WARN code, which the harness reads as non-blocking
    no firing recorded  -> --liveness last shows 'skip'; the event does not exist in the honesty report
  So a model-controlled string both bypasses the guard AND leaves no trace. This is the same shape
  .2 already fixed in config loading: a failure indistinguishable from a warning by exit code.

DIRECTION (coordinator decision, owner-approved 2026-08-22): do NOT chase case three. Two bypasses
in a row came from the same place — the guard tries to NORMALISE whatever it is handed. Narrow the
input instead:
  - Define what a well-formed path is for this guard, in the SPEC, in one paragraph.
  - Anything outside that shape is REJECTED with an explicit verdict — never silently normalised,
    never a traceback. Rejecting is cheaper to reason about than guessing.
  - Decide and DOCUMENT which outcome a malformed path deserves. It must not be 'skip' (that reads
    as 'not applicable'), and exit 1 is the warn code, so a rejection that must stop work has to be
    block or config-error. State the reasoning, not just the choice.
  - No guard invocation may end without a verdict AND a firing record. A crash is a verdict of
    'I could not tell', and it must be recorded as one — an unrecorded failure is invisible to
    --liveness, which is the one report that must not lie.

Also judge F3-F6 from bd comments beadloom-mr2l.26 and either fix or record them with a reason.

Done when: F1 and F2 are closed and proven by tests that FAIL on a3b0d4d/6970d62; a malformed path
yields a recorded verdict and never a traceback; the SPEC states the accepted path shape and what
happens outside it; not_covered is truthful about what remains, and the remaining cases are named.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.27] S1 fix-2 — the guard's path input is NARROWED, not normalised. F1-F6 all
closed. Guard suite 335 -> 377; full suite 5183 -> 5225 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed.

=== 1. THE DIRECTION: a shape, not a third patch
paths.py now owns one sentence, and it is in the SPEC verbatim: a well-formed edit target is a
non-empty string with no C0 control character or DEL (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F), no backslash, no
leading '~', and encodable for this filesystem (os.fsencode); surrounding whitespace is stripped
as a transport artifact first. Anything else is PathScope.MALFORMED - refused with a stated
reason, never resolved, never matched against an exclusion. Each rule removes a spelling that
means one file to the guard and another to the writer: a NUL ends the name in the C layer, a
backslash separates directories on the harness's OS and not on this one, '~' is expanded by a
shell and not here, an unencodable string names nothing at all. The gate is purely lexical and
runs BEFORE anything touches the filesystem, which is where F2 came from.
DELIBERATELY NOT in the shape, with reasons in the SPEC: no length limit (a long path resolves to
exactly what it says and the OS enforces its own maximum) and no percent-decoding (nothing decodes
it, so '%2e%2e' names a directory called '%2e%2e' - the over-guard direction).

=== 2. THE TWO CONSTRAINTS THE OWNER SAID HE WOULD CHECK
(a) NEVER A TRACEBACK, NEVER EXIT 1. New GuardOutcome.ERROR = "the guard could not answer",
    exit code 2. The reasoning is written into models.py + SPEC + cli.md, not just the choice:
    'skip' reads as "not applicable" and the edit proceeds; 'warn' is exit 1, which the harness
    reads as non-blocking - that is exactly how F2 got through; exit 3 is reserved (BDL-061.2) so
    a broken flow.yml is not mistaken for a guard that fired, AND, measured against the adapter
    this project ships, Claude Code blocks the tool call on exit 2 and on nothing else. So an
    outcome that must stop work has exactly one code available. A malformed path is decided AFTER
    'strictness: off' (an opt-out is a human decision in flow.yml and an off guard never looks at
    the path) and BEFORE exclusions (matching a pattern against a string the guard has refused to
    interpret is the bypass this order removes).
(b) NO INVOCATION WITHOUT A FIRING RECORD. The CLI now turns every failure into a recorded
    verdict: a GuardConfigError (recorded, still exit 3) and ANY unexpected exception (recorded,
    exit 2, no traceback). One exception, stated in the docstring and pinned by a test: an
    unregistered guard NAME records nothing - there is no guard to record it against and the
    row would be invented. Liveness was also taught the difference: an 'error' counts in
    fired_count and is shown as last_outcome, but does NOT clear never-fired, because a gate that
    ran three times and answered none of them is not a live gate.

=== 3. LIVE THROUGH THE REAL CLI (isolated project, exclusion '*.py', strictness block)
    path=src/app.py   -> BLOCK, rc 2   (unchanged)
    path=src\app.py   -> ERROR, rc 2   (was SKIP "excluded by '*.py'", rc 0)
    NUL via --hook claude-code payload ("\u0000" in JSON) -> ERROR, rc 2, recorded
       (was: unhandled ValueError, rc 1 = the warn code, no verdict, no record)
    guard --liveness afterwards: fired=3, last error at <ts> - the events exist in the report.

=== 4. F3-F6: WHAT WAS FIXED AND WHAT WAS RECORDED
F3 dead 'except OSError' - FIXED by removing the claim, not by widening the catch. Resolution is
   wrapped in one try over (OSError, ValueError) that yields a refusal, and its comment no longer
   names a case ('e.g. a symlink loop') that cannot occur: it says it is unreachable for every
   input the shape gate admits, which is exactly why it is there. Covered by an injected-failure
   test rather than left uncovered - the property is "an unknown input becomes a refusal", and an
   unknown input cannot be written down. paths.py coverage 100%.
F4 two exclusions that together cover everything - FIXED. excluded_everywhere now asks whether
   ANY exclusion covers each probe path instead of whether ONE covers all of them; '*' + '*/**'
   is reported. GuardExclusion.covers_everything() was DELETED rather than left with no caller
   (standing rule 8).
F5 '**/' translated to an unanchored '.*' - FIXED as '(?:.*/)?' for '**/' followed by more
   pattern, so '**/app.py' no longer exempts 'src/myapp.py'. A TRAILING '**/' keeps its '.*'
   reading (it names no file of its own, and a pattern that silently stops exempting is how an
   author discovers their exclusion moved) - so test_a_catch_all_exclusion_is_reported['**/']
   stays green, which the naive edit reddens. 7 new parametrized semantics rows pin it.
F6 the SPEC quoted a matcher the scaffolder does not emit - FIXED in the SPEC (the scaffolder is
   the product; the three-tool spelling is this repo's hand-written settings.json, review .3 m5,
   still open and NOT touched here). The test now asserts SPEC == EDIT_MATCHER constant instead of
   a literal, so the two cannot drift apart in silence again.
.26 judgement (b), the whole-tree liveness flag - RECORDED, NOT ADDED, with the measurement that
   decides it: .26's own test has to filter '.beadloom/' out of the walk to make its point.
   Declaring an exclusion requires a .beadloom/flow.yml, which no realistic exclusion covers, so a
   flag computed from real files would read False in every project that could set it - and a flag
   that cannot fire teaches a reader to stop reading flags. The REACHABLE half of that gap is F4
   and it is fixed. Written into the test docstring and the SPEC.
MINOR from .26 ('~/secrets.env' resolving to <root>/~/secrets.env) - FIXED as a side effect: a
   leading '~' is outside the shape.

=== 5. WHAT REMAINS - named, not widened into not_covered
The SPEC's path section names three residuals explicitly: (1) a file whose name genuinely ends in
whitespace is guarded as though it did not (the strip is a transport-artifact decision, stated
with its cost); (2) a bare drive letter 'C:/Users/...' is well-formed POSIX and reads as a
relative directory called 'C:' - this build resolves with POSIX semantics; (3) a homoglyph names a
DIFFERENT file, which the guard then reports accurately - the over-guard direction, not a bypass.
not_covered itself was NOT widened: the malformed verdict's note says only what is true - the
target was refused before any exclusion or check was applied to it.
STILL OPEN, and it is not this bead's: a config error exits 3, and exit 3 does not block in Claude
Code either. It is loud, deterministic and repeats on every edit, unlike F2's single silent slip -
but a broken flow.yml is still fail-open in the harness. Worth a bead in S2 (see FRICTION).

=== 6. SABOTAGE (standing rule 5) - 9 applied one at a time, every reddening FAILED, never ERROR
Baselines: test_guards_paths 70, test_guards_config 68, test_guards_liveness 62,
test_guard_hook_adapter 15, test_guards 29. Each restored by REVERSE EDIT (rule 9), verified by
byte-comparison against the pre-sabotage text; 'git diff --stat' at the end matches the intended
change set exactly.
 S1 drop the backslash rule            -> 7 FAILED / 63 passed: the shape params [Windows
    separator, Windows absolute], TestARefusedPathIsAVerdictNotATraceback[answers_instead_of_
    raising, same_file_spelled_for_another_os, names_what_it_did_not_check, blocking_code],
    TestNoInvocationEndsWithoutARecord::a_backslash_path_blocks_instead_of_skipping.
 S2 drop the control-character rule    -> 4 FAILED / 66 passed: the shape params [NUL, newline,
    DEL, escape]. NOTE the NUL still reached a REFUSAL rather than a traceback, via the
    resolution fallback - the belt-and-braces layer measured, not assumed.
 S3 ERROR exit code 2 -> 1             -> 5 FAILED / 94 passed: blocking_code, the two CLI
    refusal tests, the unexpected-failure test, and test_an_error_blocks_because_it_is_the_only_
    code_that_blocks.
 S4 remove the last-resort handler     -> 1 FAILED: test_an_unexpected_failure_becomes_a_
    recorded_verdict (RuntimeError escapes to the runner - i.e. the traceback returns).
 S5 config error back to _fail()       -> 1 FAILED: test_a_config_error_is_recorded_and_keeps_
    its_own_exit_code.
 S6 never_fired back to 'not own'      -> 1 FAILED: test_a_guard_that_only_errored_is_not_
    reported_as_having_fired.
 S7 catch-all back to any(all(...))    -> 1 FAILED: TestTwoExclusionsThatTogetherCoverEverything.
 S8 '**/' back to '.*'                 -> 3 FAILED: both F5 pins + the semantics row
    ['**/app.py'-'a/myapp.py'-False].
 S9 SPEC matcher back to 3 tools       -> 1 FAILED: the SPEC/scaffolder agreement test.
HARNESS DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, worth knowing: S3 changes 'ERROR: 2' to 'ERROR: 1' - same
byte length, same mtime second - so CPython reused the STALE .pyc and the next two sabotage runs
reported 3 extra reddenings that were not real. Caught by reading the failure list instead of the
colour; the harness now clears __pycache__ on both sides of every sabotage, and S3/S4/S5 were
re-run clean. This is precisely the 'check the harness itself' half of rule 5.

=== 7. GATE
pytest 5225 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed. ruff clean. mypy --strict clean (181 files).
Coverage on application/guards 99% (paths.py, evaluation.py, models.py, config.py, liveness.py
all 100%; the single miss is contract.py's removed-property line region, see below).
Clean-DB gate (rule 1): rm beadloom.db -> reindex (67 nodes / 94 edges / 665 chunks / 1220
symbols / 1298 imports / 12 rules) -> lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules -> sync-check rc=0,
268 pairs [ok] -> doctor 20 checks clean -> 'beadloom ci' rc=0 (reindex, lint, sync-check,
docs-audit, config-check, doctor all PASS).
GuardRequest.relative_path was DELETED: the evaluator now reads resolved.relative directly, which
left the property with no caller (standing rule 8). Its docstring's job - that None means three
different things - moved to resolved_path, where the scope that distinguishes them lives.

=== 8. FILES
src: application/guards/paths.py (the shape + refusal), models.py (ERROR + exit map + invariant),
evaluation.py (refuse before exclusions), config.py (F4 union, F5 anchoring), liveness.py (error
!= fired), contract.py (property removed), checks/bead_claimed.py (docstring), services/commands/
guard.py (record every named-guard invocation, ERROR to stderr), onboarding/guard_hooks.py
(emitted script's exit-code comment).
tests: test_guards_paths.py (+ the two .26 pins rewritten as closed), test_guards_config.py,
test_guards_liveness.py, test_guards.py, test_guard_hook_adapter.py.
docs: flow-guards/SPEC.md (accepted shape + error outcome + liveness wording + invariants),
services/cli.md; .claude/development/docs/features/BDL-061/ACTIVE.md.

=== 9. FRICTION (for BDL-UX)
1. 'beadloom guard' config errors exit 3, which the Claude Code hook contract treats as
   non-blocking - so a flow.yml that will not parse disables every guard in the harness while
   looking like an error. Loud and repeatable (unlike F2), but still fail-open. Needs a decision
   in S2: either exit 2 for a config error, or an adapter that maps 3 -> block.
2. The stale-.pyc trap above is a real hazard for any same-length sabotage; worth one line in the
   dev/test role files ("clear __pycache__ around a sabotage, or change the byte length").
3. tests/test_guards_parity.py::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation
   fails if a '.beadloom/beadloom.db-wal' is lying around from an EARLIER command (standing rule 3,
   #147) - it is asserting the absence of a file it did not create. It should snapshot the -wal's
   presence first, or the rule-3 mutation should stop happening. Reproduced and then green after
   removing the stale -wal.

title: [BDL-061.26][test] S1 fix: independent re-verification of the bypass and the limit boundary
description:
Independently re-verify the .25 fixes. Do not trust the fix author's own tests — standing rule 6.

1. TRAVERSAL. Build the matrix rather than the one case: 'scripts/../src/app.py', './scripts/../src/app.py', 'scripts/./../src/app.py', an absolute path pointing outside the project, a symlinked path, a Windows-style separator, and a path with a redundant '//'. State explicitly which of these the guard covers and which it does not — the not_covered note must be truthful after the fix, not merely shorter.

2. LIMIT BOUNDARY. Prove the probe sees beads past bd's old default: create enough beads in an isolated project to cross 50 and assert bead-claimed still finds the claimed one. A test that only asserts 'no crash' repeats the vacuous assertion this fix exists to remove.

3. EXCLUDED_EVERYWHERE in both directions, including the two patterns named in review ('*' false positive, '**/**' false negative), plus at least two patterns nobody has thought about yet.

4. DEAD EXCLUSION reported.

5. Confirm 'on:' is gone from SPEC and flow.yml and that nothing silently depends on it.

Standing rule 5 applies with force here: for every test you add, sabotage the code and confirm THAT test reddens as FAILED and not ERROR; compare collected/passed NUMBERS; name the reddened tests in your bead comment. Two vacuous assertions already reached main in this slice — the point of this bead is that a third does not.

Restore sabotage by reverse edit, never 'git checkout <file>' (standing rule 9).

comments.text:
TESTS [BDL-061.26] S1 re-verification — 55 new tests (guard suite 280 -> 335), coverage 99.68% on
application/guards. Nothing taken on the author's word (rule 6): every row below was measured
through evaluate_guard or the real CLI before it was asserted.

=== 1. THE TRAVERSAL MATRIX (exclusion 'scripts/**' declared; WARN = guard ran, SKIP = exempted)

  spelling                         verdict  resolves to        guard covers it?
  scripts/../src/app.py            WARN     src/app.py         YES

                                                                      root as a STRING prefix —

                                                                      against a startswith rewrite)

Every spelling using '/' is now covered, in both the traversal and the symlink sense, and the

=== 2. THE FINDINGS — where the .25 honesty note is INCOMPLETE

F1. A WINDOWS-STYLE SEPARATOR STILL BYPASSES A SINGLE-COMPONENT EXCLUSION. Measured live through
    the real CLI in an isolated project, not only in-process:
       exclusion '*.py' declared, working-branch at strictness: block, sitting on the trunk
       path=src/app.py    -> BLOCK, exit 2
       path=src\app.py    -> SKIP  "excluded by '*.py'", exit 0
    A backslash is a legal POSIX filename character, so resolution reads 'src\app.py' as ONE
    top-level component, and '*' — which the fix correctly taught not to cross directories — then
    matches it. This is C1's exact shape surviving the fix: a model-supplied spelling turns the
    guard off and prints a reason that is false about the file the harness will write. Reachable
    from Claude Code on Windows, from WSL, and from any model that types a Windows path.
    not_covered says NOTHING about it. Against a directory pattern ('scripts/**') the direction is
    safe (over-guard), which is presumably why it was never noticed.
    Pinned: TestAWindowsStyleSeparator (2 tests). Fix = normalise separators before resolving, or
    a not_covered note when the target carries a backslash. Either reddens the pin.

F2. A NUL BYTE IN THE PATH CRASHES THE GUARD — AND THE FIX INTRODUCED IT. Path.resolve() calls
    lstat, which rejects an embedded NUL with ValueError; _resolved catches OSError only. The
    lexical matching resolve() replaced never touched the filesystem, so this route did not exist
    before a3b0d4d. Measured end-to-end through the real CLI with a hook payload (the path comes
    from tool_input.file_path, and JSON can carry a NUL as backslash-u0000):
       rc=1, traceback on stderr, NO verdict emitted, and record_firing never runs.
    rc=1 is the code reserved for warn, i.e. non-blocking in a harness — so a NUL downgrades a
    block to a message AND leaves no evidence in guard-firings.jsonl that the edit happened.
    Fail-open, silent, model-controlled. The fix is one exception type.
    Pinned: TestANullByteInTheSuppliedPath (3 tests, including the CLI route).

F3. THE 'except OSError' IN _resolved IS DEAD FOR THE REASON ITS COMMENT NAMES. Path.resolve()
    defaults to strict=False, which since 3.6 returns the longest resolvable prefix instead of
    raising ELOOP. Measured on 3.13.7: a -> b -> a resolves without raising, both for the link
    itself and for a path through it. So the handler catches a case that cannot occur while
    missing the one that does (F2). Standing rule 8, one level down.
    Pinned: TestASymlinkLoopDoesNotRaise (2 tests).

F4. TWO EXCLUSIONS THAT TOGETHER COVER EVERYTHING READ AS LIVE. excluded_everywhere asks whether
    ONE exclusion is a catch-all. Declare '*' (top level) and '*/**' (every subtree) together and
    no path in any project escapes them — measured: README.md, .gitignore, src/app.py and
    a/b/c/d/e.txt all match, and a real edit SKIPs — yet excluded_everywhere is False,
    dead_exclusions is empty (both patterns match real files) and the row reads healthy. A
    completely dead gate, unreported, from two ordinary-looking exclusions. Not in the review, and
    not in the fix's stated limits, which describe only the pattern-vs-project axis. Same defect
    class the fix removed. Fix = ask whether ANY exclusion covers each probe path.
    Pinned: TestTwoExclusionsThatTogetherCoverEverything (2 tests).

F5. '**' TRANSLATES TO AN UNANCHORED '.*', SO A PATTERN COVERS MORE THAN IT NAMES.
       '**/app.py'    -> ^.*app\.py$    also matches src/myapp.py
       '**/tests/**'  -> ^.*tests/.*$   also matches src/mytests/a.py
    config.py's own docstring states the standard this violates: "an exclusion that covers more
    than it says is exactly the failure this module exists to prevent". Wider than declared is the
    gate-off direction. Fix = '(?:.*/)?' for a '**/' prefix; note that it must keep a trailing
    '**/' a catch-all, which the naive edit does not (measured: it reddens the existing
    test_a_catch_all_exclusion_is_reported['**/']).
    Pinned: TestHowWideAnExclusionActuallyReaches (2 gap tests + 8 parametrized semantics rows).

F6. THE SPEC QUOTES A MATCHER THE SCAFFOLDER DOES NOT EMIT. SPEC.md:60-62 says routing lives in
    "the Edit|Write|NotebookEdit matcher in .claude/settings.json". scaffold_guard_hooks writes
    Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit; the three-tool spelling is this repo's HAND-WRITTEN
    settings.json (review .3 m5, still open). So the sentence a reader consults to learn what an
    adopter gets describes the dogfood instead. Pinned as a recorded gap: correcting either side
    reddens test_the_spec_quotes_a_matcher_the_scaffolder_does_not_emit.

MINOR, not pinned: a relative '~/secrets.env' resolves to <root>/~/secrets.env, so the verdict
names a file the harness did not mean. Over-guard, safe direction, silent.

=== 3. THE TWO DECLARATIONS THE FIX AUTHOR MADE — VERDICTS

(a) ">50 not tested against the real binary" — WAS TRUE, IS NOW COVERED, and the stated reason for
    skipping it does not survive contact. The cost was ~1 s per 'bd create' x51; 'bd import' seeds
    60 issues in ONE process in 0.88 s (measured), so the real-binary test costs ~4.8 s of
    module-scoped setup shared by two tests in tests/test_guards_cli.py::TestRealProbes: the probe
    finds the claimed bead, and the guard PASSes under work_kind=epic — the 'strictness: block'
    example the docs ship — instead of falsely BLOCKing.
    It bites regardless of bd's ordering: it reads bd's own default page at run time and claims an
    id that page does NOT contain (verified: after claiming, the bead is still absent from
    'bd list --json' and present in 'bd list --status in_progress --json --limit 0'). Sabotage back
    to ['list','--json'] -> both FAILED. Not a vacuous "no crash" assertion: it asserts
    [bead.id for bead in claimed] == [that id].

(b) "excluded_everywhere reads the PATTERN only, so 'src/**' in an all-src project is not
    reported" — TRUE (verified: excluded_everywhere False AND dead_exclusions empty, while every
    file the walk can see is in fact excluded), and NOT THE WHOLE TRUTH.
    JUDGEMENT: defensible as a property of GuardSpec, a hole in the --liveness REPORT.
    The predicate's argument is sound and I would keep it — an answer computed from today's files
    would flip under an unrelated commit. But --liveness is a report about THIS project and it
    ALREADY walks the tree (project_files, for dead_exclusions). It therefore answers "this pattern
    matches nothing that exists" and never "these patterns match everything that exists", though
    both are one pass over the same list it already holds. The docstring's framing — "the
    project-dependent half of the same question is answered by the liveness report" — reads as if
    the pair is complete; it covers one end of the range and not the other. With F4 the consequence
    is concrete: a guard that cannot fire at all, on a real tree, with a healthy-looking row. The
    command whose entire product is honesty about dead gates has the data to answer and does not.
    Pinned: TestAnExclusionThatSwallowsThisProject (2 tests).

=== 4. 'on:' IS GONE AND NOTHING DEPENDS ON IT — verified three ways
- .beadloom/flow.yml: no 'on' key and no YAML-1.1 boolean True key (existing test kept).
- SPEC.md: its yaml schema block is PARSED, not grepped — the prose legitimately contains the
  string "no `on:` key" — and no guard body declares 'on' or True. New test.
- The code: asserted as BEHAVIOUR, not as a grep. The same guard evaluated with
  {tool: Edit, event: PreToolUse} and with {tool: Bash, event: SessionStart} returns an IDENTICAL
  verdict (outcome, why, not_covered), and runs at all with no event key present. Sabotaging
  evaluate_guard to route on the event reddens it.
  So the SPEC's claim that event routing is the harness adapter's is TRUE of the code: the only
  routing decision that exists is the matcher string the scaffolder writes into settings.json, and
  no Beadloom code reads it back (asserted). Its one inaccuracy is F6, the string itself.
- context['event'] is still written by hook_payload and read by no decision, but it has a genuine
  consumer — it is echoed into the firing record as evidence — so it is not a repeat of the defect.

=== 5. SABOTAGE (rule 5) — every reddening FAILED, never ERROR; numbers, not colour
Applied one at a time, each reverted by reverse edit (rule 9). 'git diff --stat -- src/' is EMPTY
at the end: src/ is byte-identical to a3b0d4d, only tests/ changed.
 S1 resolve_edit_path stops resolving          -> 23 FAILED / 19 passed. New ones reddened:
    TestTheTraversalMatrix[bare traversal|dot-prefixed|dot inside|doubled separator|directory
    form], TestSymlinksInBothDirections[both], TestThePathOutsideTheProjectIsNamed[both],
    TestANullByteInTheSuppliedPath[all 3].
 S2 probe back to ['list','--json']            -> 5 FAILED / 36 passed, including the two REAL-bd
    ones: test_a_bead_claimed_past_bds_default_page_is_found_by_the_real_binary,
    test_a_project_past_bds_page_size_does_not_produce_a_false_violation.
 S3 covers_everything back to a spelling tuple -> 5 FAILED / 46 passed, including new
    TestPatternsNobodyHasClassifiedYet['**/**/**'] and the F4 pin.
 S4 dead_exclusions inverted                   -> 7 FAILED / 44 passed, including new
    test_a_project_entirely_under_the_excluded_directory_is_not_reported and the F4 pin.
 P1 APPLY the F1 fix (normalise backslashes)   -> 1 FAILED: the F1 pin. (A pin that does not redden
    when the defect is fixed pins nothing — checked for all four gaps.)
 P2 APPLY the F2 fix (catch ValueError)        -> 3 FAILED: all three NUL pins.
 P3 APPLY the F4 fix (any-exclusion coverage)  -> 1 FAILED: the F4 pin.
 P4 APPLY the F5 fix ('(?:.*/)?')              -> 4 FAILED: both F5 pins + the '**/' catch-all rows.
 P5 route on the event inside evaluate_guard   -> 1 FAILED: the event-identity test.
 P6 EDIT_MATCHER := the SPEC's string          -> 2 FAILED: both F6 tests.
 P7 a root-relative '.' treated as ABSENT      -> 3 FAILED: TestThePathThatIsTheProjectRoot[2] plus
    the existing TestResolveEditPath::test_the_project_root_itself_resolves_inside.

=== 6. GATE
pytest 5183 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed (5128 at .25). Guard suite 280 -> 335 across
test_guards_paths (21->44), test_guards_config (44->60), test_guards_liveness (33->56),
test_guards_cli (22->24), test_guard_hook_adapter (13->15). ruff clean; mypy --strict clean
(181 files). Coverage on application/guards 99.68% — the single miss is paths.py:88, the dead
OSError branch of F3, deliberately NOT covered by a mock that would prove nothing.
Clean-DB gate (rule 1): rm beadloom.db -> reindex (661 chunks / 1217 symbols / 1293 imports /
12 rules) -> sync-check rc=0, all pairs [ok] -> lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules.
Committed on features/BDL-061 as 6970d62. No src/ or docs/ change: this bead verifies, it does not
fix. F1/F2 are the two I would not ship without a decision.

=== 7. FRICTION (for BDL-UX)
1. bd bulk creation is O(N) PROCESSES: 'bd create' spawns an embedded-Dolt process each time
   (~1 s), so a 60-bead fixture is ~1 min of wall clock with no output — enough to trip an agent
   stream watchdog, and a hard limit on what test fixtures are practical. 'bd import <file.jsonl>'
   does the same 60 in ONE process in 0.88 s and is the answer; it is not discoverable from
   'bd create --help', and task-init.md advertises '--graph' instead. Worth documenting as THE
   bulk path. ('bd init' in a temp dir: 2.2 s, and it writes CLAUDE.md + .claude/settings.json +
   a git commit into that dir — confirms .25's note.)
2. 'bd list --json' still gives no signal that its answer was truncated at 50 — the defect behind
   M4. A "truncated": true field would have made it observable instead of requiring a doc read.
3. 'beadloom guard' crashes with a raw traceback on an unexpected exception (F2) instead of an
   exit-3 configuration error, and exit 1 then collides with the warn code. A guard's own failure
   should not be spelled like a warning.

title: [BDL-061.25][dev] S1 fix: path normalisation, probe limit, excluded_everywhere, dead `on:`
description:
Fix cycle after review .3 returned 1 critical + 5 major. RED first for every item — two of the defects below were pinned by GREEN tests, so the test change IS part of the fix.

CRITICAL — guard bypass (contract.py ~108-120). Paths are not normalised, so with an exclusion 'scripts/**' declared, 'scripts/../src/app.py' returns skip while src/app.py is edited. Reproduced by the coordinator on an isolated project. The path arrives from model-controlled tool_input.file_path, so every exclusion is a universal skeleton key. Normalise before matching; reject or normalise traversal; decide explicitly what an absolute path outside the project means.

MAJOR — silent failure at scale (services/guard_probes.py:54). 'bd list --json' carries bd's default --limit 50; this repo has 42 open beads. Past 50, bead-claimed stops seeing the claimed bead: false warn, and false BLOCK under the documented 'epic: block'. Use --limit 0. The only real-bd test asserts all(bead.id for bead in claimed) on what is currently an EMPTY tuple — all() of empty is True, so the test is vacuous and passed while covering nothing. Replace it with an assertion that fails when the probe returns nothing.

MAJOR — excluded_everywhere() is wrong in BOTH directions: '*' is a false positive and is PINNED AS CORRECT by a green test at tests/test_guards_liveness.py:168; '**/**' is a false negative. Both are errors in the honesty report, which is the one report that must not lie.

MAJOR — a dead exclusion (matching nothing) produces no signal. An exclusion that protects nothing should surface, like a guard that never fires.

MAJOR — remove the dead 'on:' declaration (owner decision 2026-08-22). Unquoted 'on' is a YAML 1.1 boolean, so the key parses as True and is dropped; GuardSpec.events has no consumer; event routing lives entirely in the harness matcher. Rather than wire it hastily, DELETE it from docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md and from .beadloom/flow.yml so the product stops promising a capability it does not have. It returns, wired, in S3 where composition and adapters are reworked. Say plainly in the SPEC that routing is currently owned by the harness adapter.

Done when: the traversal bypass is closed and proven by a test that FAILS on the old code; the probe has no limit and its test fails when the probe returns nothing; excluded_everywhere is correct in both directions and the test that pinned the wrong behaviour is corrected; a dead exclusion is reported; 'on:' is gone from SPEC and flow.yml with the harness-owned routing stated honestly.

comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.25] S1 fix cycle — C1 + M1/M2/M4/M5 + m1 closed, each RED first.

WHAT WAS FIXED (and how RED was obtained)

C1 traversal bypass. New module application/guards/paths.py owns resolving the caller-supplied
edit path; contract.GuardRequest delegates. resolve() (not lexical normpath) so the SYMLINK
route closes too, on both the candidate and the project root (/tmp is a symlink on macOS —
without resolving the root, every tmp path read as OUTSIDE).
RED was the shipped behaviour itself, not a mock of it: paths.py was first committed to disk
carrying the old lexical logic verbatim, so the 12 new end-to-end cases failed as FAILED, never
ERROR. 12 failed / 9 passed -> 21 passed.
DECISION, written into the SPEC because 'normalise' does not answer it: a path that resolves
OUTSIDE the project root is matched against NO exclusion, the guard still runs on its other
evidence, and not_covered names the resolved target ('the edit target <abs> resolves outside
the project root, so no exclusion in flow.yml was applied to it'). Rejected: inheriting a
pattern (an out-of-project write gets the same reassuring skip as an in-project one) and
refusing the path (turns a legitimate edit elsewhere into a guard error).
NOT WIDENED, deliberately: bead_claimed's not_covered keys on PathScope.ABSENT, not on
'relative_path is None'. Both are None now, and printing 'the harness supplied no path' about
a path the harness DID supply would have been a shorter note that is false.
NOT CLAIMED: no shipped guard decides whether editing outside the project is acceptable —
inventing that policy here would be a rule nobody declared. Said so in the SPEC.
Verified live through the real CLI on an isolated project, reproducing the coordinator's case:
scripts/deploy.sh -> SKIP 'excluded by scripts/**'; scripts/../src/app.py, ./scripts/../src/
app.py and the absolute form -> identical verdict to src/app.py (the exclusion no longer
applies).

M4 probe limit. guard_probes now runs bd list --status in_progress --json --limit 0, keeping the
client-side status check as belt-and-braces. RED: a fake honouring bd's documented paging
contract (--status + --limit, default 50, 0 = unlimited) with the claimed bead at index 63 of
80. 3 failed -> passed.

M5 vacuous test. tests/test_guards_cli.py's real-bd test replaced: bd init a throwaway project
in tmp_path, create two beads, claim one, assert THAT id comes back and the other does not, and
that the pre-claim answer is () and not None. ~5.7 s. It bites — sabotaged the probe to return
an empty tuple and it FAILED ('Right contains one more item: tt-tqp'), which is precisely the
state the old assertion tolerated.
LEFT UNCOVERED, stated in the test docstring rather than papered over: the >50 boundary against
the REAL binary. bd create costs ~1 s each on embedded Dolt, so 51 beads is ~1 min in the
default suite. The boundary is proved against bd's documented contract in the fake, and .26
owns the independent re-verification.

M1 excluded_everywhere. GuardExclusion.covers_everything() asks the matcher: does this pattern
match every path in CATCH_ALL_PROBE_PATHS (top-level / nested / deep / dotfile / extensionless /
doc)? Fixes '*' (false positive) and '**/**' (false negative) in one edit. The green test that
pinned '*' as a catch-all is CORRECTED, not deleted: it now parametrizes '*', '*.py', 'src/*'
and asserts False, and the '**/**' recorded-gap test asserts True.
LIMIT STATED, not hidden: this reads the pattern only, so 'src/**' in a project whose code is
entirely under src/ is NOT reported. That sentence is in the SPEC and in the docstring.

m1 dead exclusion. liveness.dead_exclusions(spec, files) names patterns matching no file that
currently exists; liveness.project_files walks the tree (vendor/build dirs pruned, symlinks not
followed, 20k cap — 1094 files / 0.03 s on this repo) and is skipped entirely when no guard
declares an exclusion. Reported as 'matches no file in the project: <pattern>' in text and
dead_exclusions[] in JSON. An empty file list yields NOTHING rather than everything (an
unreadable tree would otherwise call every pattern dead).
WORDING IS THE PRODUCT: it claims 'matches nothing that exists right now', NOT 'can never
match' — a directory added tomorrow revives it. Two predicates, two homes, neither pretending
to answer the other: catch-all is a question about the PATTERN (config.py), dead is a question
about the PROJECT (liveness.py). The matrix characterization test keeps its assertion (a typo'd
pattern still leaves the guard LIVE — the safe direction) and its docstring now says the
silence is gone.

M2 dead 'on:'. DELETED, not quoted, per the owner decision: GuardSpec.events, Guard.
default_events, _build_events, the schema example in config.py, and both 'on: [edit]' lines in
our own .beadloom/flow.yml. SPEC.md and cli.md now say plainly that event routing is owned by
the harness adapter today (Claude Code's Edit|Write|NotebookEdit matcher plus one settings entry
per guard) and that 'on:' returns wired in S3. Three RED tests replaced the four that pinned the
YAML 1.1 trap — including one that reads our own flow.yml and asserts neither 'on' NOR the
boolean True appears as a guard key, so the trap cannot come back by spelling.

SABOTAGE (standing rule 5) — each fix broken by reverse edit, one at a time, restored by reverse
edit (rule 9, never git checkout). Every reddening was FAILED, never ERROR:
- C1: paths.resolve_edit_path stops resolving -> 12 FAILED / 9 passed in test_guards_paths.py,
  incl. TestTraversalCannotBypassAnExclusion (all 4 params + absolute + symlink),
  TestAPathOutsideTheProject (all 4), TestResolveEditPath (3).
- M4: back to ['list','--json'] -> 3 FAILED / 14 passed: test_a_bead_claimed_beyond_the_first_
  page_is_still_seen, test_a_project_past_the_page_size_does_not_produce_a_false_violation,
  test_every_claimed_bead_is_reported_not_just_the_first_page_of_them.
- M5: tracker forced to () -> 1 FAILED:
  test_bd_tracker_reads_a_real_bead_claimed_in_a_real_bd_project.
- M1: back to the literal spelling tuple -> 4 FAILED / 37 passed:

  reported_too, test_a_catch_all_exclusion_is_reported['**/**'] and ['**/'].
- m1: dead_exclusions inverted -> 4 FAILED / 37 passed: test_a_dead_exclusion_is_reported,
  test_only_the_dead_pattern_of_several_is_named, test_nothing_is_called_dead_when_no_file_
  could_be_read, test_the_text_report_names_a_dead_exclusion_and_its_pattern.
- M2: events field restored on GuardSpec + 'on: [edit]' back in flow.yml -> 2 FAILED
  (test_the_effective_spec_carries_no_event_list, test_the_shipped_dogfood_config_declares_no_
  events); separately default_events restored on Guard -> 1 FAILED
  (test_a_registered_guard_declares_no_default_events).

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, named rather than silently skipped: M3 (the harness owns BOTH the
edit matcher and the guard list) is S3 — it is M2 seen from the other end, and wiring an event
selector inside a fix cycle would recreate the very shape M2 removes. Minors m2-m7 untouched.

NUMBERS: guard suite 242 -> 280 passed. Full suite 5128 passed / 10 skipped (0 failed). ruff
clean, mypy --strict clean (181 files). Clean-DB gate (standing rule 1): rm beadloom.db ->
reindex (67 nodes / 94 edges) -> lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules -> sync-check rc=0, 268
pairs fresh -> doctor: only the pre-existing unlinked-guide warns. beadloom ci exit 0.

liveness.py, checks/bead_claimed.py, checks/working_branch.py, services/guard_probes.py,
services/commands/guard.py, .beadloom/flow.yml; tests/test_guards_paths.py (new),
test_guard_probes.py, test_guards_cli.py, test_guards_config.py, test_guards_liveness.py,
test_guards_matrix.py, test_guards_checks.py; docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/
SPEC.md, docs/services/cli.md, docs/services/components/guard-probes/DOC.md;
.claude/development/docs/features/BDL-061/ACTIVE.md.

BEADLOOM/BD FRICTION: (1) rule 1 still bites — the first lint on the incremental index is not
trustworthy, so every check here ran on a freshly rebuilt DB; S2 owns it. (2) bd list's default
--limit 50 is invisible in --json output: nothing in the payload says it was truncated, which is
why the defect needed a doc read rather than an observation. (3) bd init in a temp dir takes
~3.4 s and writes CLAUDE.md + .claude/settings.json + a git commit into that dir — fine for a
throwaway, worth knowing before anyone runs it somewhere real.
