comments.text:
REVIEW [BDL-061.3] S1 — ISSUES: 1 critical, 5 major, 7 minor.

Verified independently on the working tree (standing rule 6): diff read before the .1/.2
reports; every claim below is measured, not quoted.

WHAT PASSED (measured)
- ruff clean; mypy --strict clean (180 files); 248 guard tests pass; 99.64% coverage on the
  guard modules.
- Clean-DB gate (standing rule 1): `git archive HEAD` -> fresh export -> `beadloom reindex`
  (67 nodes / 94 edges) -> `lint --strict` = 0 violations / 12 rules; `sync-check` rc=0
  (all pairs [ok], incl. all 9 flow-guards pairs + both new component DOCs); `doctor` shows
  only pre-existing warns.
- `diff --since 157d3fe`: +flow-guards (feature), +guard-hooks (component), +guard-probes
  (component), +3 part_of edges. Layering correct, all three annotated, all doc-linked.
- DDD holds: checks read through ports; probes wired at the CLI boundary; GUARD_NAMES passed
  as a parameter into onboarding rather than imported downward. No inward->outward leak.
- STRICTNESS DEFAULTS — constraint holds. Simulated an adopter upgrading from 2.2.0 (fresh
  repo, .beads/ present, no flow.yml, on trunk): bead-claimed -> SKIP exit 0, working-branch
  -> WARN exit 1. Nothing turns red.
- HONEST OUTCOMES — holds for all six reachable paths. Swept warn / block / off-skip /
  exclusion-skip / probe-skip / pass: every one carries a non-empty `why` AND a non-empty
  `not_covered`; the three skip reasons are distinguishable; warn+block carry remediation.
  The one exception is C1 below.
- READ-ONLY w.r.t. the index — holds, and I did not take the JSONL argument on trust.
  md5 of .beadloom/beadloom.db before/after a real `bead-claimed` + `working-branch` run in
  this repo: BYTE-IDENTICAL. No -wal/-shm left behind. See m4 for the two caveats.
- Test strength is real where it counts: parity compares the WHOLE verdict (JSON + rendered
  text + which stream) across all four outcomes, and runs the emitted .sh as a real
  subprocess against the real CLI in a real git repo. Read-only tests digest whole trees.
  The "Recorded gap" characterization tests with stated reasons are good practice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CRITICAL

C1. src/beadloom/application/guards/contract.py:108-120 (`GuardRequest.relative_path`)
    PATH-TRAVERSAL BYPASS: any guard can be silently disabled by a model-supplied path.
    `relative_path` never normalises the path — `Path(raw)` collapses `.` but not `..`.
    So an exclusion matches on a lexically-unresolved string. MEASURED, with a
    `scripts/**` exclusion declared:
        'src/app.py'                          -> warn
        'scripts/../src/app.py'               -> SKIP   <-- edits src/app.py
        '<root>/scripts/../src/app.py'        -> SKIP   <-- absolute form, same file
        './scripts/../src/app.py'             -> SKIP
    The path arrives from `tool_input.file_path`, i.e. from the model. CONTEXT's constraint
    is explicit: "No guard may depend on how compliant a given model is today." This is a
    guard that any caller can opt out of, and the skip reason it prints ("excluded by
    'scripts/**' ...") is false about the file being edited — an honest-looking skip for an
    unguarded write. It also lands in the firing record as evidence the gate ran.
    Zero test coverage: no test in the suite passes a path containing '..' (grepped).
    RECOMMENDATION: normalise + prefix-check before matching. Resolve the candidate and the
    project root, then `relative_to`; a path that resolves OUTSIDE the root must not be
    exclusion-matched at all — report it in `not_covered` instead of inheriting a pattern.
    `resolve()` also closes the symlink route; a purely lexical `os.path.normpath` fixes the
    '..' case but not symlinks. Add the four cases above as tests.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MAJOR

M1. src/beadloom/application/guards/config.py:146-155 (`excluded_everywhere`)
    The honesty report is wrong in BOTH directions, and the false positive is asserted as
    correct by a green test. Known defect 2 (`**/**` false negative) is only half of it.
    MEASURED against the module's own matcher:
        '**'    -> ^.*$        matches everything      excluded_everywhere=True   correct
        '**/*'  -> ^.*[^/]*$   matches everything      excluded_everywhere=True   correct
        '**/**' -> ^.*.*$      matches everything      excluded_everywhere=False  FALSE NEG
        '*'     -> ^[^/]*$     matches ONLY top-level  excluded_everywhere=True   FALSE POS
    The false positive is new — it is not in the known-defects list, and
    tests/test_guards_liveness.py:168 parametrizes `'*'` as a "catch-all" and asserts True,
    so a green test enshrines it. It also contradicts this slice's own SPEC.md, which says
    "`**` crosses directories and `*` does not, so `src/*.py` cannot silently exempt a
    subtree" — the doc and the liveness logic disagree about what `*` means.
    JUDGEMENT ON KNOWN DEFECT 2: BLOCKS S1. `--liveness` is the one artifact whose entire
    purpose is to be truthful about which gates are dead; a report that can be wrong either
    way, on patterns as ordinary as `*`, does not carry that weight. Pinning the false
    negative in a test was the right instinct, but pinning is not shipping.
    ROOT CAUSE, shared by both directions: the function compares literal pattern STRINGS
    against a hardcoded tuple instead of asking the matcher it already owns.
    RECOMMENDATION: make it a coverage question, not a spelling question — e.g. probe a
    fixed set of representative paths ('README.md', 'src/a/b.py', 'a/b/c/d/e.txt') through
    `exclusion.matches` and call it excluded-everywhere only when one exclusion covers all
    of them. That fixes `**/**` and `*` in one edit, needs no new vocabulary, and is the
    same computation that answers m1 (excludes-nothing).

M2. .beadloom/flow.yml:16,20 · docs/.../flow-guards/SPEC.md:44 · docs/services/cli.md:650 ·
    src/beadloom/application/guards/config.py:121,244-253 (`events` / `_build_events`)
    `on:` is a documented capability wired to nothing — and in our own flow.yml it does not
    even survive parsing. MEASURED: `yaml.safe_load('.beadloom/flow.yml')` gives the
    bead-claimed body keys `[(True, 'bool'), ('strictness', 'str')]` — YAML 1.1 reads bare
    `on` as boolean True, `body.get("on")` returns None, and the loader silently falls back
    to the default. Grepped the whole tree: `GuardSpec.events` is WRITTEN in config.py and
    READ nowhere. Event routing lives entirely in the harness matcher (M3).
    JUDGEMENT ON KNOWN DEFECT 1: BLOCKS S1, and on the epic's own authority. Standing rule
    8 says "A permission without a caller is not a capability — an allowlist entry, or a
    function nothing calls, reads as 'the feature exists'". This is precisely that shape,
    shipped into an adopter's config schema, our own config, the SPEC, the CLI reference and
    the RFC. It is also the second-worst kind of doc defect: not stale, but teaching an
    incantation that has never done anything.
    RECOMMENDATION: pick one and do it in this slice. Either (a) delete `events`,
    `default_events`, `_build_events` and every `on:` from flow.yml + SPEC.md:44 +
    cli.md:650 (RFC.md:90 is a historical record, leave it) — smallest honest change; or
    (b) wire it, which is M3's fix and pays for itself. Do not merely quote the key: a
    quoted `"on"` that still has no consumer is the same defect spelled correctly.

M3. src/beadloom/onboarding/guard_hooks.py:50 (`EDIT_MATCHER`) + .claude/settings.json:16
    PORTABILITY — the answer you asked for: YES, behaviour exists only inside Claude Code.
    The adapter script itself is clean; the claim survives for the .sh file and I verified
    it (`exec beadloom guard "$1" --hook claude-code`, one line, and the real script vs the
    real CLI agree byte-for-byte in a subprocess test). But "the adapter" is not the whole
    binding. Two decisions live only in .claude/settings.json:
      (a) WHICH TOOL INVOCATIONS COUNT AS AN EDIT — `EDIT_MATCHER` = "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|
          NotebookEdit". That is event routing, i.e. exactly what `on:` was meant to own,
          expressed in one harness's regex vocabulary. Nothing in Beadloom knows it.
      (b) WHICH GUARDS RUN — one settings entry per guard NAME (known defect 4). A guard
          added to flow.yml is inert until settings.json is edited; conversely a guard set
          to `strictness: off` still spawns a process on every edit to produce a SKIP.
    JUDGEMENT ON KNOWN DEFECT 4: BLOCKS S1, and it is the same defect as M2 seen from the
    other end. The dev's framing ("the guard NAME is the one coupling still present") is one
    coupling short: the matcher is the other, and it is the more portable-looking one because
    it is buried in the scaffolder rather than in a $comment.
    COST, MEASURED: 1.07 s per `beadloom guard` invocation in this repo (3 runs, +/-0.01),
    x2 guards = ~2.1 s added to every Edit/Write, growing linearly with the registry.
    RECOMMENDATION (fixes M2 and M3 together and removes the latency growth): make the
    adapter forward an EVENT, not a name — `exec beadloom guard --event edit --hook
    claude-code` — and have Beadloom select the guards whose `spec.events` contains it. One
    settings entry, one process per edit, `on:` gains its consumer, adding a guard to
    flow.yml activates it, and `strictness: off` costs nothing. The matcher stays in the
    harness because it must (it is Claude's tool vocabulary), but it then maps to a Beadloom
    event name rather than to a Beadloom guard list.

M4. src/beadloom/services/guard_probes.py:54 (`BdWorkTracker.claimed_beads`)
    `run_bd(["list", "--json"])` under-reads its evidence and can produce a FALSE VIOLATION.
    VERIFIED from `bd list --help`: `-n, --limit int   Limit results (default 50, use 0 for
    unlimited) (default 50)`. The probe takes the first 50 issues and filters for
    `status == in_progress` CLIENT-SIDE. On any project with more than 50 open issues, an
    in-progress bead outside that window is invisible and `bead-claimed` reports "no bead is
    in progress" — a false WARN, and under the `strictness: { epic: block }` configuration
    that the RFC, SPEC.md:45 and cli.md:653 all ship as THE example, a false BLOCK that stops
    an agent editing while a bead genuinely is claimed.
    This repo has 43 open beads (measured: `bd list --json --limit 0` -> 43). Seven short of
    the threshold, on the epic that will add beads.
    A guard that reports a violation of a condition that is satisfied is the exact failure
    mode S1 exists to remove, so this blocks even though today's default is warn.
    RECOMMENDATION: ask bd the question instead of filtering its answer —
    `run_bd(["list", "--status", CLAIMED_STATUS, "--json", "--limit", "0"])`. Keep the
    client-side status check as belt-and-braces. Add a test with >50 synthesised issues.

M5. tests/test_guards_cli.py:234 (`test_bd_tracker_reads_the_real_binary_in_this_repo`)
    The only real-`bd` test cannot fail on the behaviour its name claims. It asserts
    `isinstance(claimed, tuple)` and `all(bead.id for bead in claimed)` — both are vacuously
    true for `()`, and `()` is what it returns right now (measured: 0 in_progress in this
    repo). So the assertion holds whether the probe works, returns nothing, or silently
    truncates. Standing rule 4 demands a real-binary test at this boundary; this satisfies
    its letter and none of its force, which is why M4 survived 248 tests and 99.64%
    coverage. Coverage was a floor here, exactly as you said.
    RECOMMENDATION: make it bite — `bd init` a throwaway project in tmp_path, create and
    claim a bead, assert that ID comes back and that an unclaimed one does not; skip only
    when the binary is absent. If that is too slow for the default suite, mark it and run it
    per slice — but do not leave an assertion that passes on an empty tuple under a name
    that promises the opposite.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MINOR

m1. KNOWN DEFECT 3 (a dead exclusion produces no signal) — CORRECTLY DEFERRED. The
    behaviour is pinned by a characterization test with a stated reason
    (tests/test_guards_matrix.py:426), the guard stays LIVE (the safe direction), and a
    typo'd pattern therefore over-guards rather than under-guards. But it is the same
    computation as M1: once `excluded_everywhere` becomes a coverage probe, "covers nothing"
    is the other end of the same predicate. Fold it into M1's fix rather than carrying a
    separate bead.
m2. Adopters get no .gitignore entry for .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl — only THIS repo's
    was hand-edited (.gitignore:31). `scaffold_guard_hooks` writes the hook and edits
    settings.json but not the ignore file, so every adopter of setup-agentic-flow gets a
    file that grows on every edit and shows up as untracked churn. Add the entry where the
    hook is scaffolded.
m3. `beadloom guard` in a project with no Beadloom index CREATES .beadloom/ as a side effect
    of `record_firing` (firing.py:47, measured in a bare git repo). A read-only primitive
    that makes a directory in a project that does not use Beadloom is a surprise. Either
    record only when .beadloom/ exists, or say so in the docs.
m4. Read-only, stated precisely, since the SPEC asserts "the firing record is the only file
    guards write": beadloom.db is byte-identical (md5) after real runs — TRUE. Two caveats
    the tests do not cover: (i) `bd list` bumps MTIMES on
    .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/noms/{manifest,journal.idx,vvvv...} (content md5
    identical — measured, so no data change, but it defeats mtime-based caches); (ii)
    tests/test_guards_parity.py:357 digests only beadloom.db{,-wal,-shm} + .beads/
    issues.jsonl, not .beads/embeddeddolt/**, so its docstring ("the real database") claims
    a wider scope than the assertion. Widen the digest, or narrow the docstring.
m5. The dogfood and the scaffolder disagree. .claude/settings.json:16 registers the DIRECT
    CLI command with matcher "Edit|Write|NotebookEdit"; `scaffold_guard_hooks` emits
    .claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh with "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit". So the shipped
    scaffolder's own output is not what is running in this repo. Parity is covered by a real
    subprocess test so the risk is low, but "this epic is dogfooded under the flow it
    builds" (PLAN, Notes) is weaker than it reads. Make the dogfood use the emitted adapter,
    or drop the stale MultiEdit entry — pick one and make them match.
m6. KNOWN DEFECT 5 (.1 committed its own work, .2 did not) — CORRECTLY DEFERRED as a code
    matter; it is a protocol gap in /coordinator + .claude/agents/*.md, not an S1 defect.
    But file it as a bead NOW rather than "later": S1's dogfooding evidence is per-wave, and
    two waves in this slice were committed by different actors, which makes "what did wave N
    change" ambiguous the moment anyone reruns it. One line in the role files ("the
    coordinator owns the commit; a role never commits") settles it.
m7. guard-firings.jsonl has no rotation and `read_firings` parses it whole on every
    `--liveness` (9.5 KB after ~one day of dogfooding). Named by .1 as a known limitation;
    acceptable for S1, revisit when the Gate starts reading it (S2+).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DONE-WHEN (PLAN, S1)
  [x] verdict identical from CLI and hook adapter — verified, whole verdict, all 4 outcomes,
      plus the real .sh vs the real CLI in a subprocess
  [x] exclusion without reason/until is a configuration error
  [~] `skip` always carries a reason — true for all six reachable paths, but C1 produces a
      skip whose reason is FALSE about the file being edited
  [~] `--liveness` reports guards excluded everywhere — reports them wrongly in both
      directions (M1)
  [x] every guard has a test proving it FAILS on the condition it guards
  [x] no guard writes to the index — beadloom.db byte-identical, measured (see m4)

VERDICT: not passing. C1 and M1-M5 are fixable inside this slice and four of them (M1, M2,
M3, m1) collapse into two edits. Do NOT close .3; return for a fix cycle, then re-review C1,
M1 and M4 specifically — each needs a test that fails before the fix.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
RE-REVIEW [BDL-061.3] S1 after five fix cycles, on b2fc13c — NOT PASSING: 0 critical, 4 major,
3 minor. No code fix is required. Every finding below is a document or a mechanism claiming
more than the code delivers, which is the same defect class this slice spent five rounds
removing from the code — it has moved layer, not disappeared.

METHOD. Standing rule 6: nothing below is taken from a fix report. I built an isolated project
(git repo, .beadloom/flow.yml, working-branch at `block` with a `scripts/**` exclusion,
bead-claimed at `warn`) and drove the REAL binary (.venv/bin/beadloom, verified to import from
src/) for every row. Surface (5561 passed, ruff/mypy, `beadloom ci` rc 0, the B2 sabotage) was
re-verified by the owner and is not re-measured here.

================================================================================
THE ORIGINAL FINDINGS — JUDGED

C1 path traversal — CLOSED, measured, not accepted on report.
  exclusion 'scripts/**' declared, working-branch at block, sitting on trunk:
    scripts/deploy.sh            -> SKIP  "excluded by 'scripts/**'"        rc 0
    src/../scripts/deploy.sh     -> SKIP  (traversal INTO the exclusion still works) rc 0
    scripts/../src/app.py        -> BLOCK (the skeleton key is gone)        rc 2
    ../elsewhere/x.py            -> BLOCK, not_covered names the resolved target, no exclusion applied
    src\app.py                   -> ERROR rc 2, refused as malformed, recorded
  The fix is better than the one I asked for: the input is NARROWED (paths.py owns the accepted
  shape) rather than normalised, which is the correct answer to two consecutive bypasses from
  the same root. resolve() closes the symlink route; the shape gate runs lexically BEFORE the
  filesystem, which is where the NUL crash the first fix introduced came from.

M1 excluded_everywhere wrong in both directions — CLOSED, verified against the shipped matcher:
    '*'    -> False (the false positive is gone; the green test that pinned it was corrected)
    '**/**'-> True  (the false negative is gone)      '**' '**/*' '**/' -> True
    '*' + '*/**' together -> True   (F4, found by .26, fixed in .27)
    '**/app.py' vs 'src/myapp.py'   -> False  (F5 anchoring)
    'src/*.py' vs 'src/app.py\n'    -> False  (m2, the \Z anchor)
  The declared limit ('src/**' in an all-src project is not reported) is stated in the SPEC with
  the measurement that decides it, and it is a genuine limit, not a papered-over gap: a
  whole-tree flag would read False in every project that can declare an exclusion, because
  declaring one requires a .beadloom/flow.yml no realistic pattern covers. I agree with .27's
  decision to record rather than add it.

M2 dead `on:` — CLOSED. No `events` field, no `default_events`, no `_build_events`, no `on:` in
  our flow.yml; the only surviving mention is one docstring sentence explaining the deletion.
  Standing rule 8 satisfied, and the deletion is the honest half of M3.

M3 the harness owns event routing AND the guard list — OPEN BY DECISION (S3). Correct call for
  the code; NOT correct for the docs as they stand — see N3.

M4 `bd list` page limit — CLOSED. `["list","--status",CLAIMED_STATUS,"--json","--limit","0"]`
  with the client-side status check kept. Also good, and not in my original finding: the probe
  refuses to run `bd` at all unless `.beads/` exists, with the read-only reason stated.

M5 the vacuous real-bd test — CLOSED. `tests/test_guards_cli.py::TestRealProbes` — 6 tests, ran
  them, 12.06 s. The assertions are `[bead.id for bead in claimed] == [beyond]` against a real
  `bd init`ed project seeded past bd's 50-row page. Cannot pass on an empty tuple. The >50
  boundary I flagged as untestable in-suite is covered against the REAL binary via `bd import`
  (~5 s), which is better than I asked for.

THE SEVEN MINORS AS A SET — nobody had checked these, so here they are, all seven:
  m1 dead exclusion    LANDED (.25). liveness.dead_exclusions + project_files; surfaced in text
                       and as dead_exclusions[] in JSON; the wording claims "matches nothing
                       that exists right now", not "can never match". Correct.
  m2 .gitignore entry  NOT LANDED. Grepped the entire src/ tree: nothing in Beadloom writes a
                       .gitignore entry anywhere. `scaffold_guard_hooks` writes the adapter and
                       merges settings.json and nothing else. Every adopter of
                       setup-agentic-flow gets .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl growing as
                       untracked churn. Our own line .gitignore:31 is still hand-written. -> n2
  m3 creates .beadloom/ NOW CLOSED, as a side effect of .31's marker requirement rather than as
                       its own fix. Measured: `--project <existing dir, no marker>` -> ERROR
                       rc 2, and no .beadloom/ in that directory afterwards; the same from a
                       subdirectory of a real project -> BLOCK rc 2, firing at the ROOT, no
                       stray .beadloom/ in the subdirectory.
  m4 read-only precision PARTIALLY LANDED. The SPEC invariant is now honest in words. Measured
                       on this repo, sha256 + mtime over every file under .beadloom/ and
                       .beads/ before and after a real `beadloom guard bead-claimed`:
                         CONTENT CHANGED: ['.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl']   (only that)
                         MTIME-ONLY:      3 files under .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/noms/
                         NEW/GONE:        none
                       So the index is untouched and the record is the one write. The remaining
                       half is unfixed: test_guards_parity.py's live-repo digest still covers
                       only beadloom.db{,-wal,-shm} + .beads/issues.jsonl, not
                       .beads/embeddeddolt/**, and the mtime bump the `bd` probe causes in the
                       tracker's own store is stated in no document. -> n3
  m5 dogfood != scaffolder NOT LANDED, and it is now the weaker half of the #170 story.
                       .claude/settings.json in this repo registers the DIRECT CLI command with
                       matcher "Edit|Write|NotebookEdit"; the scaffolder emits a SCRIPT with
                       "Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit"; .claude/hooks/ does not exist here
                       at all. So the artifact adopters get has never run in this repo, and the
                       binding that produced #170's evidence is narrower than the shipped one.
                       .27 fixed the SPEC to quote the scaffolder (F6) and explicitly left this
                       side untouched. -> n1
  m6 role files own the commit NOT LANDED, and no bead filed. Grepped .claude/agents/*.md and
                       commands/coordinator.md: no rule saying a role never commits. Meanwhile
                       .28 and .30 (test role) each committed their own work this slice
                       (d4bb618, 8bbd84c). The ambiguity got wider, not narrower.
  m7 no rotation       OPEN by declaration, as agreed. Fine for S1.

================================================================================
MAJOR (new this round)

N1. docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md:423 (Invariants) ·
    src/beadloom/onboarding/guard_hooks.py:60-62 (the emitted adapter's comment) ·
    docs/services/cli.md:641
    THE SPEC ASSERTS AN INVARIANT THE SHIPPED ADAPTER DOES NOT DELIVER.
    Verbatim: "**A guard that cannot answer says so and blocks.** 'I could not tell' is a
    verdict (`error`), not an exception, and it never borrows the `warn` code."
    Measured through the real binary, all exit 3, all ERROR verdicts:
      unregistered guard name            rc 3   (SPEC: "the guard could not answer")
      unparseable `guards:` block        rc 3   (SPEC names this as an `error` explicitly)
      --liveness with a name             rc 3
      malformed --context pair           rc 3
      unsupported --hook harness         rc 3
    Exit 3 does NOT block in Claude Code — the slice measured this itself (.27 FRICTION #1,
    .29 §8, and SPEC:50 says so in passing while justifying moving the payload cases to 2).
    So the largest class of "could not answer" an adopter will actually meet — a flow.yml that
    will not parse — disables every guard in the harness while the invariant list says it
    blocks. The reader most likely to be misled is the adopter, who reads the Invariants
    section and the adapter's own comment ("3 = usage or configuration error", with no
    mention that 3 lets the edit through).
    WORSE: the deferral has no owner. PLAN.md's S2 is "#142 import edges, #146 component
    pairs, #147 read-only lint" — nothing about exit codes. `bd list --limit 0` has no bead for
    it and BDL-UX-Issues has no entry. "Worth a bead in S2" was written twice and filed zero
    times.
    RECOMMENDATION: (a) qualify the invariant — "…and blocks, except for the exit-3 class,
    which the Claude Code adapter treats as non-blocking; a broken flow.yml is therefore loud
    and fail-open"; (b) say the same in the emitted adapter's comment and in cli.md:641, where
    "deliberately not 2" currently reads as a pure win; (c) file the bead (map 3 -> 2, or have
    the adapter map it) and reference it. This is not a request to change behaviour in S1.

N2. tests/test_guards_invocation.py:702-711
    (`test_the_command_does_no_validation_click_would_exit_on`)
    THE PIN IS AGAIN NARROWER THAN THE INVARIANT IT NAMES — the round-five finding, one
    constructor over. The test's name and docstring claim the wide sentence ("An option Click
    validates exits before the callback — and the boundary"). Its implementation is
    `click_path_keywords(...) == [["path_type"]]`, which walks the AST for calls whose func
    unparses to exactly `click.Path`. MEASURED against click 8.4.2 in this venv, standalone
    dispatch:
      @click.option("--kind", type=click.Choice([...]))  bad value -> exit 2, callback NOT reached
      @click.option("--n", type=int)                     bad value -> exit 2, callback NOT reached
    Neither is a click.Path, so neither is visible to the pin. The other mechanism cannot cover
    it either: the 432-row witness matrix imports `run_invocation` and calls it in a child
    process, i.e. it runs BENEATH Click and can never observe a Click-level exit; and
    `_EXIT_PATHS` does go through CliRunner but every row is a hand-written argv, so a new
    option contributes no row (the derived `records` expectation only helps once a row exists).
    Nothing in the suite would redden. The SPEC:244-249 residual names only "an unknown
    option".
    COST TODAY: zero — `--project` is the only typed option and it carries no validator. The
    finding is about the guarantee, not about a live defect. But S2/S3 will plausibly add
    `--work-kind` as a `click.Choice` (strictness is already per work kind), and on that day
    `beadloom guard bead-claimed --work-kind epci` exits 2 with Click's usage message, no
    verdict and no record, with all pins green. That is precisely a round-six defect the
    mechanisms would not catch, and it is the answer to the question this re-review was
    called to answer.
    RECOMMENDATION: make the pin about the sentence, the way .31 did for terminators — assert
    an allowlist over the keywords of EVERY `type=` argument on the command's options (or
    assert the command declares no option whose `type` is a click validator instance at all),
    rather than over one constructor name. One test edit, no source change.

N3. docs/.../flow-guards/SPEC.md (the harness-routing section) ·
    docs/domains/onboarding/components/guard-hooks/DOC.md · docs/services/cli.md:661
    THE ENFORCEMENT SURFACE IS NOWHERE IN THE SHIPPED DOCS — #170, and it bounds what S1 may
    claim. All three documents state that which tool invocations count as an edit is the
    adapter's decision, and the SPEC quotes the matcher. None of them says the consequence:
    a file written through `Bash` (`sed -i`, a heredoc, `python3 - <<EOF`) fires no guard, and
    `--liveness` after such a session is byte-identical to `--liveness` after a compliant one.
    guard-hooks/DOC.md lists `EDIT_MATCHER` under "Public surface" without its value or its
    limit; its Invariants section names "merge, never rewrite" and "guard names are a
    parameter" and says nothing about coverage.
    This is the "unknown is not zero" rule — the rule S1 applies to every verdict — not being
    applied to S1's own enforcement surface. The slice measured the hole on this very repo
    (#170: "a whole class of edits to this very repository was unguarded while --liveness
    showed the guards healthy and firing"), and m5 above means our binding was narrower still.
    RECOMMENDATION: one paragraph in the SPEC and one in guard-hooks/DOC.md, stating the tools
    the emitted matcher covers, that a write reaching the filesystem by any other tool is
    unguarded, and that the liveness report cannot distinguish that from compliance. Do NOT
    widen `not_covered` to say it — this is a property of the binding, not of a verdict, and
    the verdict has no way to know. Cross-reference #170 and M3/S3.

N4. README.md:267
    STALE, after three API CHANGE notes naming it. The row reads: "`guard NAME` | Evaluate one
    flow guard — `pass`/`warn`/`block`/`skip` in the exit code". `error` has been the fifth
    outcome since .27 and is the outcome the whole boundary was built to produce; the .27, .29
    and .31 API CHANGE comments each list "README/getting-started if they quote guard exit
    codes" and none was actioned. sync-check and docs-audit cannot see this — README is not
    paired to the guard nodes — which is exactly why the API-CHANGE-note channel exists.
    RECOMMENDATION: `pass`/`warn`/`block`/`skip`/`error`. One cell. cli.md:631-671 is
    excellent and current by comparison, including the three recording exceptions.

================================================================================
MINOR

n1. `.claude/settings.json` vs `guard_hooks.EDIT_MATCHER` — original m5, unchanged after five
    cycles. Pick one: either register the emitted `.claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh` here (which
    would make the dogfood claim true and would have caught #170's narrower binding earlier),
    or drop `MultiEdit` from the scaffolder. Today the shipped artifact has never run here.

n2. `scaffold_guard_hooks` writes no `.gitignore` entry for `.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl` —
    original m2, unchanged. Verified by grepping the whole of src/: Beadloom writes a
    .gitignore entry nowhere. Adopters get untracked churn from the first guarded edit.

n3. Two small honesty leftovers, both in the "reason misdescribes the case" family that .31
    fixed one instance of:
    (a) src/beadloom/application/guards/invocation.py:271-277 — `beadloom guard` with NO name
        reports `not_recorded_because: "'(no guard named)' is not a registered guard, so there
        is nothing to record it against"`. Measured. The `why` is correct ("no guard was
        named"); the not-recorded reason quotes a pseudo-name as though the caller typed it.
        That is `name or UNNAMED_GUARD` one case over from the `""` swallow .31 fixed —
        `_named(None)` legitimately returns the placeholder, but `_record` then routes the
        no-name case through the unregistered-name exception. The module docstring lists three
        exceptions; the code has four cases and folds one into another's wording.
    (b) src/beadloom/application/guards/config.py:306-323 (`_build_spec`) — an unknown key in a
        guard body is silently ignored. Measured: I wrote `exclude:` instead of `exclusions:`
        and got a clean parse with zero exclusions and no signal (the guard then over-guards,
        the safe direction). `option:` for `options:` is the unsafe direction: working-branch
        silently falls back to `trunk = "main"`. The module rejects unknown guard NAMES and
        unknown strictness VALUES for exactly this reason and does not reject unknown KEYS.
        Mitigated by the verdict printing the trunk it compared against.

n4. .claude/development/docs/features/BDL-061/ACTIVE.md — the Progress list carries DUPLICATE
    entries for .28, .29, .30 and .31, and the duplicates disagree on their own numbers
    ("suite 5376 -> 5476" vs "5376 -> 5475"; "guard tests 528 -> 627" vs "628"). The epic's own
    tracking file should not need a reader to decide which copy is true.

================================================================================
THE THREE QUESTIONS I WAS ASKED, ANSWERED DIRECTLY

1. `not_covered` HONESTY — HOLDS, in both directions, and it was not widened.
   Evidence that it was not widened: `git diff 370aa53..HEAD -- checks/` shows the two shipped
   guards' not_covered STRINGS are byte-identical to the first S1 commit. The only change is
   the KEYING (`request.relative_path is None` -> `PathScope.ABSENT`), which NARROWED the note:
   .25 explicitly refused to print "the harness supplied no path" about an outside-root or
   malformed target, where `relative` is also None. Five cycles, three of which added new
   failure states, and nobody reached for the escape hatch. The three notes that WERE added
   (OUTSIDE_ROOT, MALFORMED, UNANSWERED) each name a state in which genuinely nothing was
   checked.
   Claim-vs-code, both directions, for each shipped guard:
     bead-claimed  claims not covered: whether the claimed bead's scope covers this path; and
       (only when the scope is ABSENT) that no target was supplied. Code checks exactly one
       thing: does the tracker report anything `in_progress`. Nothing it claims not to check is
       checked; nothing it checks is omitted.
     working-branch claims not covered: whether the branch is named after the work item;
       whether the trunk is actually protected on the remote. Code compares the checked-out
       branch to `options.trunk`. Both claims are true, and the second one honestly covers the
       misconfigured-trunk case I went looking for (a project whose trunk is `develop` and who
       never set `options.trunk` gets a PASS on `develop` — and the `why` prints "(trunk is
       'main')", so the reader can see what was compared).
   The reverse direction, the one you asked me to check: I found exactly one over-claim and it
   is a nitpick, not a finding. `_NO_PATH_NOT_COVERED` appears only when no path was supplied,
   which implies that when one IS supplied the target was considered; bead-claimed's DECISION
   never looks at the path (only exclusion matching, one layer up, does). The substantive gap
   is still named by the other note, so no reader is misled about coverage.
   Structural backing: GuardVerdict.__post_init__ refuses to construct a WARN or an ERROR with
   an empty `not_covered`, and a SKIP without a reason. BLOCK and PASS are not covered by the
   constructor — the evaluator's `_not_covered` fallback fills them — which is a narrower
   guarantee than the code's behaviour, but the SPEC states the invariant exactly as narrow
   ("a `warn` always names…"), so document and mechanism agree. Noted, not filed.

2. THE READ-ONLY CONSTRAINT — the prose is now true, and it says what the code does.
   CONTEXT's constraint has always been qualified ("read-only **with respect to the index they
   inspect**"); the SPEC's invariant was rewritten to state the write explicitly: "No guard
   writes to the index it inspects. The firing record is the one deliberate write, it is not
   the index, and it goes to the project's own `.beadloom/` — a guard never creates a project
   root as a side effect of recording." Measured against that sentence, clause by clause:
     - index untouched: yes, byte-identical; `beadloom.db` is not even opened on the guard path.
     - one deliberate write: yes, `guard-firings.jsonl` is the only file whose CONTENT changed.
     - the project's own `.beadloom/`: yes — from a subdirectory the firing lands at the root
       and no marker is created below it; `--project` at an unmarked directory refuses.
     - never creates a root: yes, by any of the seven routes .31 enumerated; I re-measured two
       of them and found no stray directory.
   The two cases of a guard writing where it should not have (the subdirectory root and the
   `--project` root) are both closed at the source rather than papered over, and the SPEC now
   carries the "by ANY route, including through --project" quantifier that the docstring
   previously asserted only about the walk.
   The single residual is m4's, and it is real: the `bd` subprocess bumps mtimes on three files
   under `.beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/noms/` (content sha256 unchanged — measured). That is
   a write to the artifact `bead-claimed` inspects, which is the exact wording of CONTEXT's own
   reason for the rule. Content-neutral, so trust is not at stake, but it is stated nowhere and
   the parity test's digest does not cover that tree. One sentence in the SPEC settles it.
   I do not think the prose needs to change beyond that sentence — the honest rewording you
   were worried about has already happened.

3. THE THREE RECORDING EXCEPTIONS — none of them is a gap wearing a reason, but the
   enumeration is off by one.
     `--liveness` — intrinsic. A report performs no evaluation; recording one would inflate the
       count it prints. Structurally sound: `verdict is None` is reachable only from a
       successful `_report`.
     no project located — intrinsic. There is nowhere to write, and manufacturing somewhere was
       the measured defect. Fail-CLOSED (error, exit 2, blocks) and the reason is printed, so
       the invocation is not invisible — it is just not in the JSONL, because there is no JSONL.
     an unregistered name — I attacked this one hardest, because it is the one that composes
       with "exit 3 does not block" into a mistyped adapter that bypasses forever. It survives:
       `build_liveness` builds a row for every REGISTERED guard from `GUARD_NAMES`, so a typo'd
       adapter entry leaves the real guard's row reading `never_fired: true`, which is the
       honest reading and is exactly what a reader needs. Verified live. Residual, not gap —
       and its severity now lives in N1, where it belongs.
   OFF BY ONE: the code has a fourth case, "no guard was named", and folds it into the third
   with wording that misdescribes it (n3a). The docstring says three. That is cosmetic, but it
   is the same shape as the `""` swallow .31 fixed in this very round, one case over — which is
   itself a small piece of evidence for the answer to your real question.

================================================================================
WOULD THESE MECHANISMS CATCH A ROUND-SIX DEFECT?

Mostly yes, and that is a real change. Three things now hold that did not:
  - The runtime boundary is genuinely wide. `_answer` catches SystemExit / KeyboardInterrupt /
    BaseException and `_record` matches it; a `sys.exit` in `services/guard_probes.py` (which
    is on the boundary path but outside the AST pin's scope) would still become a recorded
    verdict, because the handler does not care where it came from.
  - The structural pin stopped being a spelling check: the scope is DERIVED from the package
    (a module added tomorrow is in scope on the day it is added), terminators are recognised by
    measured effect in real subprocesses, the one-writer scan covers the whole source tree
    including alias imports, and the recording witness is a property of the returned object
    rather than an inference from an absent line.
  - The behavioural matrix is GENERATED from argument axes rather than hand-listed, which is
    the specific reason .30's B2 bypass — placed on an argv nobody had written a row for — now
    reddens through three independent mechanisms.
Where they are still narrower than their claim: N2, and it is the same shape as the last three
rounds — a guarantee stated as a sentence and implemented as one constructor name. The AST
residual .31 named honestly (an aliased or getattr'd terminator) is the smaller one; the Click
validator class is the reachable one, and unlike the AST residual it is covered by NEITHER
mechanism, because the witness matrix runs beneath Click by construction.

================================================================================
DONE-WHEN (PLAN, S1) — re-judged
  [x] verdict identical from CLI and hook adapter
  [x] an exclusion without reason/until is a configuration error
  [x] `skip` always carries a reason — and the C1 case that made one FALSE is gone; measured
      across skip-off / skip-exclusion / skip-probe / skip-no-path
  [x] `--liveness` reports guards excluded everywhere — correct in both directions now, plus
      dead exclusions, with the pattern-vs-project split stated
  [x] every guard has a test proving it FAILS on the condition it guards
  [x] no guard writes to the index — measured byte-identical; the one write is the record and
      it goes to the project's own root
  [~] the flow the guards enforce is the flow this repo runs — n1: the shipped adapter has
      never run here, and #170 says the binding misses a whole class of writes

================================================================================
VERDICT AND ROUTING

The CODE is shippable. I could not find a reachable defect in it, and I looked in the two
places this slice has failed before (the path input and the exits) plus one it has not (the
Click layer). C1 and M1/M2/M4/M5 are closed on measurement, not on report; m1 and m3 landed;
M3 is correctly deferred.

The SLICE is not, and the reason is worth naming precisely: three of my four majors are
documents claiming enforcement the product does not deliver (N1 exit 3, N3 the matcher, N4
the README) and the fourth is a test claiming a guarantee wider than it checks (N2). That is
the identical failure mode of rounds one through five — a claim wider than its mechanism —
relocated from src/ to docs/ and tests/. Shipping it would put S1's own thesis, "unknown is
never reported as zero", in the position of being false about S1.

ROUTING — do NOT open a sixth dev cycle. None of this needs a source change:
  - N1, N3, N4 and n1-n4's doc halves belong in `.4` (tech-writer), whose scope is already
    "guards guide + flow.yml reference". Add to its brief: the exit-3 qualification in the
    SPEC's Invariants + the emitted adapter comment + cli.md; the enforcement-surface paragraph
    in SPEC + guard-hooks/DOC.md cross-referencing #170; the README outcome list.
  - N2 is a one-file test change; give it to `.4` as well or fold it into S2's first dev bead.
  - File the exit-3 bead now (it is currently deferred to an S2 that has no such scope item,
    with no bead and no BDL-UX entry), and file m6's one-line role-file rule.
  - n1 (make the dogfood use the emitted adapter) is worth doing before S3, since S3 reworks
    adapters and would otherwise rework something we have never run.
S1 ships with `.4` as planned, provided `.4` carries the four doc items above. Nothing here
belongs in S2 except the exit-3 decision, which already did.

title: [BDL-061.2][test] S1: verdict matrix, exclusion validation, liveness
description: Verdict matrix across outcomes and work kinds; exclusion validation (missing reason/until rejected); liveness reporting; CLI-vs-adapter verdict parity. Every guard gets a test proving it FAILS on the condition it guards — a guard whose bite is not shown does not ship.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TESTS [BDL-061.2] S1 verdict matrix, exclusion validation, liveness, parity, read-only.

NUMBERS: 180 new tests (suite 4926 -> 5106 collected; 5096 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed).
Guard suite now 248 (68 from .1 + 180 here). Split: test_guards_matrix.py 52, test_guards_config.py 48,
test_guards_liveness.py 32, test_guards_parity.py 29, test_guard_probes.py 14, +5 appended to
test_guard_hook_adapter.py. Shared factories (write_flow_yml, make_guard_probes incl. an exploding
tracker) added to tests/conftest.py so a matrix test states only its cell.

COVERAGE on the guard code (statements + branches, --cov-fail-under=80): 99.64% overall
(665 stmts / 3 missed, 176 branches / 0 partial). application/guards/* = 100% stmts AND 100% branches
on every module; services/guard_probes.py 100%; onboarding/guard_hooks.py 100%;
services/commands/guard.py 97% - the 3 misses are the `return` statements after `_fail()`, which
calls sys.exit and makes them unreachable.

WHAT WAS WIDENED
1. Verdict matrix: all 9 cells of strictness{off,warn,block} x check-outcome{satisfied,violated,
   unavailable} parameterised (.1 proved 6 of 18 combinations). The cell that mattered most:
   an unavailable probe under `block` must SKIP, not BLOCK - strictness raises the price of a
   *violation*, never of "cannot tell". Plus: the three skips (off / excluded / probe-unavailable)
   all exit 0 and are asserted to be distinguishable only by `why`.
2. Exclusion precedence (untested before): an exclusion beats `block`; `off` is resolved BEFORE the
   exclusion so the recorded reason names the work kind, not the pattern; an excluded path never runs
   the check at all (proved with a probe that raises if consulted, not by inspecting a flag);
   first declared match wins; a satisfied check under an exclusion still reads SKIP, never PASS.
3. Path resolution: a harness-supplied ABSOLUTE path must match a project-relative exclusion pattern.
   Nothing tested this; without relativisation every exclusion in a real hook session is dead.
   Also ./-prefix normalisation, an absolute path outside the project inheriting nothing, and a
   catch-all `**` NOT covering an invocation with no path.
4. options: plumbing end-to-end: `options: {trunk: develop}` in flow.yml changes which branch violates.
   Untested before - silently dropped options would have made working-branch lie on every non-main trunk.
5. Exclusion validation: both fields missing, `path` missing, all three missing, present-but-empty
   ('' / whitespace / null) per field, entry not a mapping, exclusions not a list, whitespace stripping,
   an unquoted YAML date as `until`, first-match order. Plus the whole malformed-file surface:
   invalid YAML -> GuardConfigError (not YAMLError), top-level list, guards not a mapping, guard body
   not a mapping, empty body still `declared=True`, options/strictness not mappings, unknown-name error
   listing the registry.
6. Liveness: never-fired (per guard, and declared-but-never-run), fired-then-stopped, misconfigured,
   excluded-everywhere via `**`/`*`/`**\/*`, off-for-every-kind vs off-for-one-kind-only, last_outcome
   = most recent not first, cross-talk (one guard firing must not mark another as run), a firing for a
   retired guard name, junk/blank/wrong-shape JSONL lines never manufacturing evidence, text+JSON
   rendering incl. the strictness source column.
7. CLI/hook parity: full-verdict parity over all four outcomes - identical JSON payload AND identical
   rendered text AND the same stream AND the same exit code (parity that compares only exit codes is
   not parity: 3 of 4 outcomes share 2 codes). Plus notebook_path == file_path, empty payload ==
   no-context call, explicit --context overriding a hook field, and 6 unreadable payloads -> exit 3.
8. Real emitted adapter (standing rule 4): .claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh is scaffolded into a real
   `git init -b main` repo and EXECUTED as a subprocess with a real Claude PreToolUse payload on stdin,
   then compared byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr, returncode) against a direct `beadloom guard` subprocess.
   Real binaries, real probes, non-zero code (WARN=1). It ran; it did not skip.
9. Read-only invariant: proved by DIGEST, not by absence of a write. (a) whole-tree sha256 of a project
   containing a real Beadloom-schema DB, before/after evaluating every guard across every outcome ->
   identical; (b) the same via the CLI -> the ONLY delta is the addition of .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl,
   every other file byte-identical; (c) the LIVE repo's real .beadloom/beadloom.db + .beads/issues.jsonl
   digested before/after a real evaluation with the real bd+git probes -> byte-identical, and no
   -wal/-shm file appears.
10. Probe failure surface (new file, boundary-stubbed): bd missing / bd exit!=0 / bd printing junk /
   bd printing a non-list all return None -> guard SKIPS. Any of them returning () would turn a broken
   tool into a false violation. Also: bd is never invoked in a project without .beads/ (asserted with an
   exploding stub, not by reading the code), only in_progress counts as claimed, git OSError/Timeout and
   a detached HEAD read as "no branch".

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (src touched, minimally, RED first)
application/guards/config.py `_as_str_map` coerced YAML booleans with a lookup KEYED BY THE VALUE:
`{True: "on", False: "off"}.get(raw_val, raw_val)`. Two consequences, both verified against the real CLI:
 - an unhashable value (`strictness: {default: [warn]}`) raised TypeError, which is not GuardConfigError,
   so the command never reached its exit-3 path and Click exited **1 - the WARN code**. A malformed
   flow.yml was indistinguishable from a warning verdict for any adapter that reads only the exit code,
   i.e. every adapter. Reproduced end-to-end: `beadloom guard bead-claimed --project p` -> traceback, EXIT=1.
 - `0 == False` and `1 == True` in a dict lookup, so `strictness: {default: 0}` silently resolved to
   "off" - an integer switching a gate off, exactly what the reason/until rule exists to prevent.
Fix: coerce only real `isinstance(raw_val, bool)`; everything else falls through to the existing
"must map strings to strings" error. 7 lines, comment explains why. Pinned by
test_a_non_string_strictness_value_is_rejected[[warn]|{a: b}|7|1.5],
test_an_integer_strictness_is_rejected_rather_than_read_as_on_or_off[0|1] and
test_a_config_error_never_borrows_the_warn_or_block_code (CLI-level, exit 3).

DEFECTS FOUND, NOT FIXED (for review .3 / S2) - each pinned by a named test with a DEFECT docstring
 - `on: [edit]` UNQUOTED is a YAML 1.1 boolean key (`True`), so `body.get("on")` is None and the declared
   events are silently dropped. This is the form used in the shipped SPEC example
   (docs/domains/application/features/flow-guards/SPEC.md:43) AND in this repo's own .beadloom/flow.yml
   for both guards. Harmless only because `GuardSpec.events` is consumed by NOTHING today (grep: the one
   reference is its own default). Two items really: a documented key that does nothing, and a field with
   no consumer (standing rule 8 - a capability without a caller). Test:
   test_an_unquoted_on_key_is_a_yaml_boolean_and_is_silently_dropped.
 - `excluded_everywhere()` matches a literal pattern list ("**", "*", "**/*"). `**/**` demonstrably
   matches every path (asserted in the test) yet reports the guard as live - a FALSE NEGATIVE in the
   one number the liveness command exists to produce. Test:
   test_a_catch_all_spelled_another_way_is_not_recognised.
 - An exclusion that can never match anything is accepted silently; there is no "excludes-nothing"
   counterpart to "excluded-everywhere", so a typo'd pattern is indistinguishable from no exclusion.
   Guard stays live (safe direction), so the test pins the behaviour, not the missing warning:
   test_an_exclusion_matching_nothing_is_accepted_and_leaves_the_guard_live.
 - "fired then stopped" has no threshold, only a timestamp. Deliberate per .1 (a fresh clone is
   legitimately idle) - test asserts the EVIDENCE is carried (last_fired_at) so the Gate can judge later:
   test_a_guard_that_fired_long_ago_carries_the_evidence_of_when.

SABOTAGE (standing rule 5) - 13 cases, harness compares COLLECTED/PASSED/FAILED/ERROR numbers over all
9 guard test files, every edit removed by reverse string replacement (rule 7) and the file's sha256
compared before/after (restored=True in all 13). BASELINE 248 passed / 0 failed / 0 ERROR.
Every case produced FAILED, never ERROR, never "no tests ran":
 S1 `off` branch removed (248->241, 7 FAILED): verdict_matrix[off-satisfied], verdict_matrix[off-violated],
    off_is_resolved_before_the_exclusion_so_its_reason_names_the_work_kind, off_strictness_skips_and_says_so,
    one_config_yields_a_different_verdict_per_work_kind[chore-skip],
    a_guard_switched_off_for_chores_still_blocks_for_epics, the_three_skips_are_distinguishable_by_their_reason
 S2 strictness ignores work_kind (7 FAILED): + one_config...[epic-block], block_strictness_turns_the_same_violation_into_block
 S3 a check skip treated as a pass (15 FAILED): verdict_matrix[warn-unavailable], verdict_matrix[block-unavailable],
    an_unavailable_probe_never_hardens_into_a_violation[warn|block], a_check_skip_reason_is_passed_through_verbatim,
    unwired_probes_report_unavailable_so_the_guard_skips, a_broken_tracker_skips_the_guard_instead_of_failing_it,
    an_unknown_branch_skips_the_guard_rather_than_assuming_the_trunk, the_hook_and_the_shell_produce_the_same_json_verdict[skip], ...
 S4 edit path not relativised (2 FAILED): an_absolute_path_inside_the_project_matches_a_relative_exclusion,
    an_exclusion_declared_relatively_also_exempts_the_hook_absolute_path
 S5 exclusion field may be empty (9 FAILED): a_present_but_empty_field_counts_as_missing[path|reason|until x ''|'   '|null]
 S6 the value-keyed bool lookup restored (5 FAILED): the 5 regression tests named above
 S7 liveness counts every guard's firings (2 FAILED): one_guard_firing_does_not_mark_another_as_having_run,
    a_firing_for_a_name_no_longer_registered_is_not_reported
 S8 warn/block rendered on stdout (4 FAILED): the_hook_and_the_shell_render_the_same_text_on_the_same_stream[warn|block],
    the_generated_hook_script_and_a_direct_call_agree_byte_for_byte, a_blocking_verdict_reaches_stderr
 S9 liveness swallows a broken flow.yml (3 FAILED): a_broken_flow_yml_makes_liveness_raise_rather_than_report_all_idle,
    the_cli_reports_a_broken_flow_yml_on_the_config_error_code, an_unknown_guard_name_in_flow_yml_fails_the_liveness_report
 S10 firing record never written (2 FAILED): the_cli_adds_the_firing_record_and_touches_nothing_else,
    cli_evaluation_is_recorded_and_shows_up_in_liveness
 S11 missing bd reads as 'no bead claimed' (2 FAILED): an_unanswerable_tracker_reports_none_not_an_empty_result[bd not installed],
    a_broken_tracker_skips_the_guard_instead_of_failing_it[bd not installed]
 S12 non-object hook payload yields empty context (4 FAILED): a_payload_that_is_not_an_event_object_is_a_config_error_not_a_verdict[[]|\"a string\"|3|null]
 S13 settings rewritten when its shape is wrong (2 FAILED): a_settings_file_that_is_a_json_array_is_reported_and_left_untouched,
    unreadable_settings_are_reported_never_clobbered

FAKES DECLARED (standing rule 4 - a test on a fake proves the fake's contract)
 - tests/test_guard_probes.py stubs the bd SEAM (beadloom.services.bd_seam.run_bd) and
   guard_probes.subprocess.run. Its module docstring says so explicitly: it proves the seam's contract
   (unanswerable -> None -> skip), NOT bd's or git's own behaviour. The happy paths run against the real
   binaries in test_guards_cli.py::TestRealProbes, and the parity test runs the real emitted shell script
   against the real CLI in a real git repo.
 - The CLI parity tests stub probes at the CLI seam only (guard_cmd._probes) - the boundary, never the
   evaluator - so both callers under comparison traverse the identical decision path.
 - Everything else uses real files (tmp_path), real YAML, a real SQLite Beadloom schema and the real
   Click command.

DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED, and why
 - `beadloom guard --liveness` exit code is 0 even when every guard is idle. Asserted as-is with the
   reason (a fresh clone is legitimately idle); turning an idle gate red is the Gate's job (S2+), so
   testing for red here would encode the wrong policy.
 - Concurrent appends to guard-firings.jsonl from parallel agents. The design rests on O_APPEND of a
   single short line; a test that spawns writers would be timing-dependent and would pass for the wrong
   reason. Named as a limitation rather than covered vacuously.
 - Firing-file rotation/growth (.1's known limitation) - no behaviour exists to test.
 - Windows path separators in exclusions - the loader is POSIX-normalised via Path.as_posix(); asserting
   on a platform we do not run CI on would be a fake.
 - Whether the claimed bead's SCOPE covers the edited path - not implemented (needs S6 bead<->node
   binding); it is stated in not_covered and I assert THAT, rather than a coverage that does not exist.
 - lint-based guards - none exist (#147), as instructed.

GATE (all after `rm -f .beadloom/beadloom.db && beadloom reindex`, standing rule 1)
 uv run pytest: 5096 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed. ruff check src/ tests/: clean. mypy --strict: clean

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED [BDL-061.1] S1 guard primitive.

WHAT: application/guards/ = models.py (GuardVerdict + EXIT_CODE_BY_OUTCOME), contract.py (GuardRequest/GuardFinding/Guard + WorkTracker/Workspace ports), config.py (guards: block of flow.yml), evaluation.py (the single decision point), firing.py (append-only .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl), liveness.py, hook_payload.py (harness event -> context), checks/{bead_claimed,working_branch}.py. Plus services/guard_probes.py (real bd+git adapters), services/commands/guard.py (CLI), onboarding/guard_hooks.py (emitted adapter + settings merge), wired into setup-agentic-flow.

DECISIONS (with reasons):
1. Ports+adapters instead of guards calling bd directly: bd_seam lives in the SERVICES layer and application must not import services (architecture-layers, severity=error). Probes are injected at the CLI boundary; unavailable probe returns None -> guard SKIPS with a reason, never passes.
2. Exit code 3 for usage/config errors: click's UsageError already exits 2, which is our BLOCK. Without the split a malformed flow.yml would read to a hook as a genuine block.
3. warn/block -> stderr, pass/skip -> stdout: stderr is the stream a Claude Code hook shows the agent; a warning printed to stdout would be invisible where it matters.
4. Firing record is a JSONL beside the index, NOT a table in beadloom.db, and evaluate_guard does no writes at all (the CLI records). Keeps the decision path literally read-only. Deviates from the RFC's 'infrastructure/: guard-firing store' — a second node with one consumer was YAGNI; the module lives in the guards package, one nameable responsibility.
5. Own glob->regex (** crosses directories, * does not) instead of fnmatch: under fnmatch, 'src/*.py' silently exempts the whole subtree — an exclusion covering more than it says is exactly the failure the reason/until rule exists to stop.
6. Guard names are a PARAMETER to onboarding/guard_hooks.py, not an import: the registry is in the application layer above that domain. The CLI (above both) supplies GUARD_NAMES, so a guard added later is wired by re-running setup-agentic-flow.
7. bd is queried only when .beads/ exists — invoking bd in an unrelated repo could initialise state there, and a guard must not change what it inspects.
8. An undeclared guard name in flow.yml is a config ERROR, not a no-op: a typo would otherwise be a silently dead gate.

TESTS (numbers, TDD RED->GREEN each step): tests/test_guards.py 27, test_guards_cli.py 22, test_guards_checks.py 11, test_guard_hook_adapter.py 8 = 68 new. Full suite 4916 passed / 10 skipped (was 4915 collected before this bead; the 3 failures seen mid-work were the CLI-surface test and two sync-pair tests, both fixed by declaring the new command + docs, not by relaxing them).

SABOTAGE (standing rule 5 — each reverted by reverse edit, never git checkout):
- bead-claimed forced to always return ok -> 7 FAILED (test_fails_when_no_bead_is_in_progress, warn-default, block-strictness, warn/block exit codes, json payload, liveness last_outcome).
- reason/until requirement dropped from exclusion validation -> 3 FAILED (exclusion_without_reason, exclusion_without_until, config_error_exits_three).
- 'if ... fi' added to the emitted hook script -> 1 FAILED (the_adapter_is_a_single_exec_of_the_beadloom_cli).
All 68 green again after revert.

REAL-BINARY TESTS (standing rule 4 — a stub proves the stub): GitWorkspace against a real 'git init -b features/real' repo and against a non-repo dir; BdWorkTracker against the real bd binary in this repo (skips if bd absent) plus the no-.beads case.

GATE: clean-DB lint --strict 0 violations / 12 rules (standing rule 1 honoured, #142 still open); sync-check rc=0, 266 pairs fresh; docs-audit 13 fresh; config-check in sync; doctor 20 clean; beadloom ci rc=0. ruff + mypy --strict clean.

DOGFOOD (real run in this repo): 'beadloom guard bead-claimed' -> PASS 'in progress: beadloom-mr2l.1'; 'working-branch' -> PASS on features/BDL-061; hook path with a real Claude PreToolUse payload -> identical verdict; --liveness shows fired counts.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS / carried:
- The guards are NOT yet wired into Beadloom's own .claude/settings.json (no such file exists here). Deliberate: installing a PreToolUse hook changes the owner's live session. Enable with 'beadloom setup-agentic-flow' when the owner wants it — that is the only remaining step to dogfood the hook path in-session.
- .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl grows without rotation (gitignored, one line per evaluation). Not trimmed in S1; revisit if a long-lived repo notices.
- bead-claimed cannot tell whether the claimed bead's scope covers the edited path — stated in not_covered rather than implied; needs bead<->node binding (S6).
- --liveness always exits 0. Turning an idle gate red belongs to the Gate (S2+); a fresh clone is legitimately idle, so failing here would be a false gate.

title: [BDL-UX #162] doctor: audit the PRODUCED graph, not just the code — island / unexplained-leaf / claim-without-evidence checks
description:
Turns 'a green gate is not verification' into machine checks.

Four graph defects shipped past dev + test + review + tech-writer beads and a 6/6 gate (BDL-UX #144, #157, #159, plus dropped 'uses' edges). They share one shape: every test verified a FUNCTION, and none verified the CLAIM the produced graph makes. The graph said 'this node depends on nothing' and nothing asked whether that was true.

All four were found by a human clicking a node and asking 'is that true?'. During that session I wrote the audits by hand, ad hoc, and they took ten lines each. They should be doctor checks.

Proposed checks (each measured on this repo during BDL-060 S4):
1. CODE ISLAND — a node with no first-party dependency in EITHER direction whose files nothing references. doctor's isolated_nodes does NOT catch this, because part_of makes such a node look connected. Would have caught #160 (AsyncAPI adapter reachable from no code path). Measured: exactly one true island; ai_agents/ai-techwriter are reached by subprocess and vitepress-site is not Python, so the check needs to respect declared 'uses' edges and non-code sources or it will cry wolf.
2. UNEXPLAINED LEAF — a node reporting no outgoing dependency where its own files DO contain first-party imports. Every legitimate case is explainable (a true leaf imports nothing first-party; a container's only such imports are its __init__ re-exporting its own parts). Anything else is an attribution bug. Measured: 30 of 64 nodes empty, all explained, zero unexplained.
3. CLAIM WITHOUT EVIDENCE — the inverse: a node claiming a dependency with no first-party import behind it.

Design notes:
- These are assertions about the ARTIFACT, so they belong in doctor (graph integrity), not lint (architecture rules).
- Severity WARNING first, not ERROR: on an unfamiliar graph the island check will have false positives until 'uses' declarations catch up, and turning an existing project red on upgrade is the failure mode we keep filing against ourselves.
- The audits must NOT reuse the same attribution helper they are auditing, or a bug hides in both. During the session the manual cross-check was done with grep for exactly this reason.

title: [BDL-UX #157] Node source for a package-annotated `__init__.py` resolves to the FILE, so 5 nodes report 0 symbols (228 invisible) and max_symbols can never fire on them
description:
After BDL-059's cohesion-driven decomposition, a package carries its '# beadloom:feature=' / '# beadloom:component=' annotation in __init__.py — the natural place. The indexer records the node's source as that FILE. The facade only re-exports, so every symbol-based read sees an empty node.

Measured on Beadloom's own graph (5 nodes, 228 symbols invisible):
  cli-commands  component  shown 0 / actual 71
  federation    feature    shown 0 / actual 57
  agent-prime   feature    shown 0 / actual 43
  reindex       feature    shown 0 / actual 31
  debt-report   feature    shown 0 / actual 26

All five readers agree on 0 (repository.get_symbols_for_source, architecture_view._symbol_count, site_pages._load_symbols, graph/rules/evaluators max_symbols, debt_report/collect), so this must be fixed at the SOURCE, not in a reader — a per-reader patch would make the arch pop-up disagree with the node page.

Impact:
- the interactive architecture pop-up shows '0 symbols' for real packages
- the node page's 'Public symbols' section is empty for all five
- the debt report's complexity signal reads them as zero-cost
- max_symbols can never fire on them: a size rule reporting clean because it is looking at nothing (the #146 shape). It also distorts the domain-size-limit discussion — 'application' measures 283/290 while 57 of its own symbols belong to no node's count.

Proposed fix: when an annotation is found in a package's __init__.py, resolve the node source to the package DIRECTORY (with trailing slash) rather than the file. Add a regression test seeding a package facade + sibling modules and asserting the node's symbol count equals the package total, plus a guard that no node's source ends in __init__.py.

Found during BDL-060.15 review (2026-08-19).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
PART 1 SHIPPED (3eff4a8): doctor check `facade_sources` — WARNING naming the node, the hidden/total symbol counts and the package directory to repoint at. 5 tests, RED first. On this repo it finds all 5 nodes / 228 symbols. Non-blocking by design (only ERROR-severity doctor checks fail the gate), so an existing project does not go red on upgrade.

PART 2 BLOCKED ON A RULE DECISION — repointing this repo's own 5 sources to their package directories. I did it, ran a FULL reindex, and it turns `beadloom lint --strict` RED with two `no-dependency-cycles` errors:
  graph <-> federation
  beadloom <-> cli-commands

Both are ATTRIBUTION ARTIFACTS, not real cycles. Verified at file level:
  src/beadloom/graph/loader.py            -> beadloom.graph.federation   (parent file uses the child package)
  src/beadloom/graph/federation/reconcile.py -> beadloom.graph.{amqp_body, contracts}  (child uses parent siblings)
and neither amqp_body nor contracts imports anything leading back to loader — 'import beadloom.graph.loader, beadloom.graph.federation, beadloom.graph.amqp_body, beadloom.graph.contracts' succeeds, so there is no import cycle at runtime at all.

ROOT: a parent node's source PREFIX subsumes its children's files. The moment a child node is sourced at its real package (which is the whole point of this fix), any healthy two-way file-level import between the child and its parent's other files becomes a node-level A->B->A. That is normal package structure, not a design fault — and it is the same prefix-without-subtracting-nested-nodes root as #144, hitting a different rule.

Why nobody saw it: the facade sources were masking it. The child's import edges were only __init__.py's.

OPTIONS (owner decision — this changes what a HIGH-stakes gate rule means for every user):
  A. Exclude containment pairs from cycle adjacency — a node and its part_of ancestor cannot form a cycle. ~20 lines in graph/rules/cycles.py::_build_adjacency + tests. Removes a false-positive CLASS. Risk: a genuine long cycle that routes through a parent->child edge would no longer be found.
  B. Fix #144 properly — subtract nested nodes' files from a parent's attribution, for symbols AND imports. Fixes max_symbols, the symbol counts and this cycle coherently, in one place. Much larger; changes numbers across the whole product.
  C. Ship Part 1 only; leave the 5 sources as facades with the warning firing on our own repo, and repoint later behind A or B.

RECOMMENDATION: A for the 2.2.0 release (it is the narrow, provable false-positive fix and unblocks the repoint), with B filed as the real #144 work item. C is honest but leaves 228 symbols hidden in our own dogfood graph while the tool tells us about it.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
FIXED — variant B, in full (4ac244d). Owner chose 'no half-measures', and tracing the mechanism showed B and #144 were the same bug, so they were fixed together in one place.

THE RULE: a file belongs to exactly one node — the most specific one whose source covers it. Lives in infrastructure/repository (get_owning_ref_id / owns_file / count_symbols_owned_by_node / count_files_owned_by_node / get_owned_symbols); a package facade resolves to its package. Consumed by max_symbols, max_files, the architecture view, node pages and import_resolver, so no two surfaces can disagree — the unanimity of five wrong readers is what made #157 invisible.

CORRECTION to my earlier framing: I told the owner B would not remove the cycles. That was wrong in one respect — the cycles do go away, but not through symbol attribution. They went away because derived depends_on edges between a node and its part_of ancestor are a category error and are no longer emitted at all. 5 of 14 edges were exactly that noise (all machine-derived from imports, none authored in YAML), and they were manufacturing node-level cycles with no module-level counterpart.

MEASURED: application 284 -> 150, graph 257 -> 61, root service 1154 -> 0; the 228 hidden symbols restored; depends_on 14 -> 24 edges, now showing real feature-level dependencies that prefix attribution had collapsed into parents (graph-loader -> federation, mcp-server -> reindex, site-generation -> graph, import-resolver -> context-oracle). lint --strict 0 violations with the 5 sources repointed.

ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: a node whose source IS a file never owned that file (_find_node_for_file walked up from the PARENT directory), so its imports were credited to the enclosing directory's node.

REMOVED: the facade_sources doctor check I shipped earlier in this branch. Ownership makes the condition structurally impossible, and a check that can never fire is worse than none.

RECALIBRATION, stated openly: domain-size-limit 290 -> 180. Not a threshold tweak — the metric changed meaning, the observed maximum fell 284 -> 150, so 290 could never fire again. The signal the new metric does NOT carry (bounded-context size by subtree; context-oracle/ai_agents/infrastructure now own 0 while their subtrees hold 99/108/63) is filed as BDL-UX #158 rather than folded into the number.

15 new ownership tests, RED first. Gate: 4822 passed both orders, ruff, mypy strict, beadloom ci 6/6.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW (read-only) — S5 CI ai-techwriter parallel + cache (commit aa1c30e on features/BDL-052; the brief's c9e929c is stale — S5 actually landed in aa1c30e alongside S4+S6).

VERDICTS GREEN: full suite 4220 passed; mypy --strict clean (98 files); ruff clean; beadloom ci rc 0 (only 2 PRE-EXISTING domain-size warnings: graph 214, application 249 — unrelated to S5). backoff.py is classified (module-coverage 0 errors). Targeted 13 tests pass.

DIM 1 — parallel == sequential (the key invariant): MOSTLY VERIFIED, with one honest, documented nuance.
- Aggregation is order-deterministic: each session writes its own _DocWork; _fold_doc merges in stale (FIFO) order; docs_refreshed preserves stale order (test_docs_refreshed_preserve_stale_order). Verdict order-independent. turns count one-per-attempt (back-off retries are inside one turn) — matches sequential. The {ok/flagged/infra} classify_verdict is unchanged.
- NUANCE (acceptable, but real): the runaway-budget gate is NOT bit-identical under a mid-window overrun. Sequential checks the LIVE cumulative result before each attempt; parallel sessions share a FROZEN _Budget snapshot captured at submit time, so concurrent docs in one window do not see each other's tokens. _flag_if_budget_overrun catches the overrun after folding and preserves the FLAGGED verdict, but the token/turn TOTALS can diverge from sequential when the cap is crossed mid-window. This is a runaway safety net (flag, not precise budget), and the docstrings call it out — so it is honest, not a bug. The 'parallel==sequential aggregate' equality holds EXACTLY only when the budget is not tripped.

DIM 2 — rate-limit + RAM safety: PASS. retry_with_backoff is exponential (base*2**n), capped at 30s, gives up within the attempt budget and re-raises (caller treats give-up as a no-edit attempt = old failed-agent behaviour). Cap is doubly bounded (pool max_workers AND the submit window both = max_parallel); test_pool_never_exceeds_max_parallel proves peak==cap via a Barrier probe. Default max_parallel=3 is RAM-aware for the 8GB VPS and documented.

DIM 3 — cache correctness: PASS. Index cache key = hashFiles('.beadloom/_graph/**','src/**','docs/**') → any graph/src/docs change rotates the key → miss → reindex (reindex step gated on cache-hit != 'true'). uv setup-uv enable-cache:true. fetch-depth:0 + loop-guard + AI_TW_PAT token UNCHANGED (test_unchanged_invariants_preserved). Never serves a stale index.

DIM 4 — tests: SUFFICIENT FOR THE HAPPY PATHS, THIN ON THE PARALLEL BUDGET GATE.
- Covered well: parallel==sequential aggregate; stale-order fold; 429 retry-then-succeed; give-up-in-budget (→ infra verdict, tokens==0); back-off exponential+cap unit; non-rate-limit pass-through; concurrency cap (Barrier); all 4 cache/invariant CI assertions.
- GAP (Minor): runner coverage 95%, but the NEW parallel-specific runaway-budget paths are UNCOVERED across the entire ai-techwriter suite — lines 288-289 (_budget_stop invocation in the submit loop) and 336-338 (_budget_stop body: drain in-flight window + flag 'budget exceeded before repairing <ref>'). i.e. 'budget trips between docs in a multi-doc parallel run' has never executed in a test. The per-doc mid-retry budget (_doc_budget_exceeded) IS tested (test_ai_techwriter_hardening). No acceptance criterion from .14 is fully untested, but this branch is.

DIM 5 — honesty/quality: PASS. No Any/type:ignore/bare-except in runner.py or backoff.py (sole 'Any' is docstring prose). FakeAgentRunner is lock-guarded + thread-safe; sleep seam injected → instant/deterministic, no real network/Goose. Logic/verdict/trigger/loop-guard/AI_TW_PAT all unchanged.

Minor:
1. No test drives the runaway-budget gate in PARALLEL (lines 288-289, 336-338 uncovered). Add a multi-doc run with a tight max_total_tokens/turns + max_parallel>1 asserting the 'budget exceeded before repairing' flag and the in-flight window still folds.
2. (doc/nuance) Consider one line in SPEC.md noting the budget cap is a per-window safety net, so token/turn totals are NOT guaranteed bit-identical to sequential when the cap trips mid-window (the equality is exact only below the cap).

Nitpick: brief referenced commit c9e929c; actual S5 commit is aa1c30e.

OVERALL: PASS-WITH-FIXES (no Critical, no Major; 2 Minor). The behavior-change invariant (dim 1) holds for the verdict and for totals below the budget cap; the only divergence is the documented runaway-safety-net edge, which is honest. Tests are sufficient except for the parallel budget-gate branch (dim 4 = thin there). SPEC/doc freshness OK (sync-check PASS; SPEC.md documents parallel+backoff).
