comments.text:
REVIEW (S4 symbol-scope) — read-only quality/honesty review of c9e929c.

VERDICT: PASS-WITH-FIXES

Gates (all green): pytest 4220 passed; mypy src/ clean (no Any/ignore in scope.py/symbol_scope.py/commands.py); beadloom ci rc 0 (lint 0 err / 2 pre-existing domain-size warns, sync-check 149 fresh, doctor 19 clean); symbol_scope.py classified (module-coverage 0). SPEC.md (symbol_scope module) is in sync (search confirms).

DIM 1 — NO UNDER-SCOPE (safety property): MOSTLY SOUND, ONE NARROW HOLE.
- Conservative fallback is airtight for: no --since (returns list unchanged), non-attributable reasons (untracked_files/missing_modules kept), non-Python file kept, vanished revision kept, no detectable hunks kept, change outside any symbol body kept, decorator-only edit kept (range excludes decorator line), indented/conditional def invisible -> kept, duplicate top-level name -> first def maps to no surviving range -> kept. All ambiguity resolves to KEEP. Multi-code-file logic correct: _doc_depends_on_change keeps if ANY code file keeps; drops only when ALL pairs resolve not-kept.
- dotted reference (mymod.added) still matches via whole-word regex -> kept. Good.
- HOLE (Major): symbol RENAME under-scopes. If a top-level symbol foo->bar is renamed, changed_symbols() = {bar} (new-side only; git_changed_line_numbers parses only new-side + lines). A doc that references ONLY the old name foo intersects empty -> the doc is DROPPED and sync-update-baselined clean — yet that doc genuinely needs updating (it names a symbol that no longer exists). This is reachable: reason symbols_changed/hash_changed, Python file, real hunks all hold for a rename. Common case (body edit, not rename) is safe; rename is the gap.

DIM 2 — BASELINE HONESTY: OK. sync-update baseline fires ONLY in the empty-intersection branch, which requires changed != empty AND referenced == empty (symbols DID change, just not ones the doc names). For the non-rename case this is honest — it does not mask genuine drift. The rename case (DIM 1) is the one exception where a baseline masks real drift.

DIM 3 — TEST SUFFICIENCY: ADEQUATE for shipped behavior, ONE GAP.
16 tests cover: ranges (def/class/nested/empty), changed_symbols (single/multi-hunk/outside-symbol/empty), doc_referenced_symbols (word-match + substring-rejection), god-file 15->1 narrowing + 14 baselined, keep-on-reference (no baseline), no-since keep-all, non-attributable-reason keep, non-Python keep, change-outside-symbol keep, discover_scope wiring on/off. Justifies closing .11 as dev-TDD.
- UNTESTED: the rename under-scope case (DIM 1). No test asserts behavior when a doc references a renamed/removed symbol. If we accept the hole as a known limitation, add a test that PINS current behavior + a doc note; if we fix it, add a failing test first.

DIM 4 — ai_agents LEAF BOUNDARY: OK. git seam helpers (git_file_at_ref/read_working_file/git_changed_line_numbers) in commands.py use only subprocess+pathlib+re; no cross-domain import. symbol_scope.py imports only from ai_techwriter + stdlib. lint --strict layers clean. Annotations correct (str|None returns, set[int]).

DIM 5 — HONESTY/QUALITY: OK. Deterministic, pure helpers separated from seams, nesting <=3, parameterized subprocess (no shell=True), no bare except (OSError/UnicodeDecodeError), no secrets. Docstrings accurately describe the conservative contract.

REQUIRED (Major): decide rename handling — either (a) FIX: when old-side hunk removes a top-level def, treat its name as 'changed' too (parse old_content symbol ranges against old-side deleted lines) so a doc naming the removed symbol is kept; or (b) ACCEPT as documented limitation with a pinning test + SPEC note. Recommend (a) — it closes the only real under-refresh path and keeps the safety property absolute.

Summary: 0 critical, 1 major (rename under-scope), 0 minor. Solid conservative design; one renamed/removed-symbol gap to close or document.

title: BEAD-05 [review] loop-guard correctness, no-auto-merge, merge-base, branch-protection owner-safe

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW (BEAD-05) — BDL-049 W1-W3 quality/architecture/honesty review. READ-ONLY.

VERDICT: PASS-WITH-FIXES. Suite green (3568 passed), mypy src/+tools/ clean, ruff clean, beadloom lint --strict exit 0 (only pre-existing domain-size cardinality WARNs). The loop-guard is correctly designed and closed (see D1). One MAJOR: the branch-protection DEFAULT status-check contexts do not match this repo's actual GitHub check-run names — applying with defaults makes main's required checks unsatisfiable.

=== DIMENSION 1 — LOOP-GUARD (the #1 risk): CLOSED. ===
Trace verified end-to-end. Agent commit is authored by beadloom-ai-techwriter AND its subject STARTS with [skip ai-techwriter] (seams.py:390 _commit_to_current_branch -> message=f"{_SKIP_TOKEN} {title}"). On the agent's push, synchronize fires; the workflow checks out ref: github.event.pull_request.head.ref with fetch-depth:0 (ai-techwriter.yml:50-51) — on synchronize GitHub advances head to the just-pushed commit, so the branch-name checkout resolves to the agent's HEAD, and git log -1 (loop-guard step, :56-64) reads THAT commit. Either condition (author==beadloom-ai-techwriter OR subject contains [skip ai-techwriter]) sets AI_TW_SKIP=1; every subsequent step is gated `if: env.AI_TW_SKIP != '1'` (verified by test_github_every_post_guard_step_is_gated_on_skip, which asserts EVERY post-guard step carries the gate). GitLab mirror uses `exit 0` after the same probe (.gitlab-ci.yml:35-41). Belt-and-suspenders (author + token) is real.
Robustness notes (all acceptable, no action needed):
 - Substring match grep -qF '[skip ai-techwriter]' is fixed-string (no regex foot-gun). A human commit would only match if they literally type the token — acceptable/intended escape hatch.
 - Squash/merge of the PR happens on MAIN (push:main trigger was REMOVED), so it cannot retrigger this workflow. Force-push by the agent is a plain push (git push origin HEAD), still authored by the bot -> still guarded.
 - The author check is the durable guard even if a future rebase/amend drops the token from the subject.

=== DIMENSION 2 — NO-AUTO-MERGE: PRESERVED. ===
The pr-branch publishers only commit-to-current-branch + push + post a PR/MR comment (seams.py GitHubPRBranchPublisher/GitLabPRBranchPublisher). No gh pr merge / glab mr merge anywhere. Branch protection requires a PR (0 reviews) but the human still clicks merge. Confirmed.

=== DIMENSION 3 — --since merge-base: ROBUST. ===
since="$(git merge-base "origin/$BASE_REF" HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"; if empty -> $BASE_SHA fallback (ai-techwriter.yml:105-106; GitLab :59-60 -> $CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA). fetch-depth:0 ensures origin/$BASE is present on the self-hosted runner. cli.py _normalize_since drops empty/all-zero SHAs to None (stored-state path) as a third line of defense. Behind/ahead/force-push all handled. Good.

=== DIMENSION 4 — pr-branch publisher: CORRECT. ===
Commits to CURRENT branch, never checkout -b (test asserts no 'checkout' arg at all). Plain push git push origin HEAD (NOT force) — fast-forward of the runner's PR-head checkout (correct; force is only the bot-owned regenerated branch of the legacy branch-pr path). 0-doc no-op truly makes NO commit and NO push (_has_doc_changes probe via git diff --cached --quiet -- docs; test_github_pr_branch_zero_docs_skips_empty_commit). Comment is best-effort (logged + swallowed; test_*_comment_failure_does_not_fail_run). pr_url read from PR_URL env / composed from CI_MERGE_REQUEST_* (empty-safe via _gitlab_mr_url). A genuine push failure DOES fail the run (test_github_pr_branch_raises_on_push_failure). Note: the commit/push happen relative to the runner's checkout, which is the branch (not detached) because ref is head.ref (a branch name), not head.sha — correct for committing.

=== DIMENSION 6 — FLOW 1:1 + DRIFT-GUARD: OK. ===
agentic_flow vendored coordinator.md is BYTE-IDENTICAL to live .claude/commands/coordinator.md; CLAUDE.md.txt differs ONLY by the __BEADLOOM_PROJECT_NAME__ placeholder vs "Beadloom" (the expected templating normalization — drift-guard is real and green). CLAUDE.md §6 + coordinator edits are additive (trunk-based flow added; the wave/gate protocol untouched). The ai_techwriter/*.yml CI templates are intentionally NOT byte-match drift-guarded (separate vendored copies); they differ from live only in comment text and are validated SEMANTICALLY by test_ci_pr_trigger.py (pull_request present, push absent, --target pr-branch, merge_request_event). Acceptable by design.

=== DIMENSION 7 — ARCHITECTURE / SECURITY: CLEAN. ===
DDD: branch_protection.py lives in onboarding (annotated # beadloom:domain=onboarding), no infra import, lint --strict green. subprocess argv is fully list-form everywhere (no shell=True); _subprocess_runner has a justified noqa:S603 (argv built internally). gh pr comment / glab mr note take the PR title/body as separate argv elements — no shell-injection via branch names or PR titles. yaml.safe_load used in tests. _SKIP_TOKEN carries a justified noqa:S105. No bare except (only RuntimeError/OSError caught in _backfill_pr_url). No unjustified Any/type:ignore. mypy --strict clean on src/+tools/.

=== DIMENSION 8 — BOOTSTRAP: SOUND, with a noted gotcha for .6. ===
GitHub runs pull_request workflows from the BASE (main) version of the workflow file. So this NEW ai-techwriter.yml (pull_request trigger + pr-branch) only takes effect AFTER it is merged to main. Plan is sound: merge BDL-049 first, THEN dogfood on a SEPARATE post-merge PR (.6). GOTCHA for .6: do NOT expect the dogfood signal from THIS PR's own runs — this PR (opened before merge) still runs the OLD main-version workflow (push:main). The first real pr-branch run is the .6 follow-up PR.

=== MAJOR-1 — branch-protection default contexts are WRONG for this repo (branch_protection.py:43). ===
DEFAULT_STATUS_CHECK_CONTEXTS = ("beadloom ci", "tests"). GitHub status-check contexts are JOB/check-run names, not workflow names. Actual check-run names in THIS repo:
  - Beadloom Gate workflow -> job 'beadloom-gate' -> context "beadloom-gate" (NOT "beadloom ci")
  - Tests workflow -> job 'test' with a 4-version matrix -> contexts "test (3.10)".."test (3.13)" (NOT "tests")
Neither default exists. With required_status_checks.strict:true, the required checks can NEVER report success -> main becomes unmergeable for non-admins, and the gate is theater for the owner. Owner is NOT hard-locked (enforce_admins:false lets the admin bypass), so this is MAJOR not CRITICAL — but the defaults defeat the feature's purpose and will bite the .6 dogfood if run with defaults.
RECOMMENDATION: set the home-repo defaults to the real contexts (e.g. "beadloom-gate" plus the matrix legs, or collapse the Tests matrix into a single required "test" check via a needs-aggregation job) and/or have setup-branch-protection ECHO a "verify these contexts match your check-run names (gh api repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/check-runs)" warning. For the .6 dogfood: run setup-branch-protection with explicit --check matching the actual check names; do not rely on the defaults. Also note the branch_protection test (test_branch_protection.py:49,134) uses "Beadloom Gate" (the WORKFLOW name) as the custom-context example — also not a real check context; tighten the example to avoid propagating the misconception.

=== MINOR-1 — workflow_dispatch path can hit a detached/empty checkout edge. ===
The dispatch path keeps --target branch-pr (cuts a branch) but the checkout step still uses ref: github.event.pull_request.head.ref, which is empty on workflow_dispatch -> checkout falls back to the default ref (fine), but worth a comment that the dispatch path runs on main's HEAD. Non-blocking.

=== MINOR-2 — loop-guard reads only HEAD (git log -1). ===
If a human pushes a merge commit whose first-parent subject is the agent's [skip ...] commit, git log -1 reads the MERGE commit (human-authored, normal subject) -> guard correctly does NOT skip -> the agent runs on the human's merge. Correct behavior, but note: a force-push that resets HEAD back ONTO the agent's commit would skip. Edge, acceptable.

NITPICK: ai-techwriter.yml header comment says "could red main" — fine. No code nitpicks.

OVERALL: PASS-WITH-FIXES. Must-fix before .6 dogfood: MAJOR-1 (branch-protection check-context names). Everything else is solid; loop-guard is correctly closed.

comments.text: MAJOR (confirmed, the pinned bug) — tools/ai_techwriter/runner.py:169-171 _publish branch-name fallback is DEAD via operator precedence. Code: branch = _BRANCH_PREFIX + '-'.join(sorted(stem...))[:60] or f'{_BRANCH_PREFIX}docs'. Python binds + and [:60] tighter than or, so it parses as (_BRANCH_PREFIX + slug[:60]) or (_BRANCH_PREFIX+'docs'). When docs_refreshed is empty, slug='' so the left operand is the non-empty 'ai-techwriter/refresh-' (truthy) and the or NEVER fires => a 0-doc (e.g. gate-failed-before-any-refresh) run yields the dangling branch 'ai-techwriter/refresh-' with a trailing hyphen, not 'ai-techwriter/refresh-docs'. test_ai_techwriter_hardening.py:280 'test_branch_with_no_docs_refreshed_is_a_dangling_prefix_bug' pins the buggy output (asserts == 'ai-techwriter/refresh-') as a documents-the-bug test — it does NOT prevent the fix. WHY: a dangling/trailing-hyphen branch name is fragile and the intended readable fallback is unreachable. ONE-LINE FIX: parenthesize the slug so the or scopes to it: branch = _BRANCH_PREFIX + ('-'.join(sorted(Path(p).stem for p in result.docs_refreshed))[:60] or 'docs'). FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED: after fixing tools/ai_techwriter/runner.py you MUST re-run onboarding.ai_techwriter_setup.sync_vendored_harness() to refresh templates/ai_techwriter/harness/runner.py.txt, else the byte-identical drift-guard test (test_cli_setup_ai_techwriter.py:49) fails; and flip test:280 to assert the fixed 'ai-techwriter/refresh-docs'.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED BEAD-05: beadloom setup-ai-techwriter --platform github|gitlab.

COMMAND SHAPE: New core Click command in the setup-* family (cli.py, annotated # beadloom:domain=onboarding), delegating to onboarding/ai_techwriter_setup.py:scaffold(target_root, platform=...). Options: --platform {github,gitlab} (required, click.Choice), --project DIR (default cwd). Echoes written paths + a 3-step next-steps line.

HARNESS-PROVISIONING DECISION = VENDOR (recommended option chosen).
Rationale: the harness lives in repo tooling tools/ai_techwriter/, which is NOT in the beadloom wheel (pyproject: packages=[src/beadloom]). On any target repo the wrapper's 'python -m tools.ai_techwriter' would not resolve. So setup-ai-techwriter VENDORS the harness: copies the whole harness package + recipe.yaml into the target's tools/ai_techwriter/. Self-contained -> the runner needs only beadloom + goose + python (no extra packaging). Re-run = clean overwrite (idempotent).
HOW IT SHIPS: the harness is bundled as PACKAGE DATA under src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/ai_techwriter/ as inert .py.txt assets (so they are NOT imported as beadloom submodules nor linted as core code), kept byte-identical to the live tools/ai_techwriter source by sync_vendored_harness() and a drift-guard test (test_vendored_harness_matches_live_source) -- principle 5, no hand-maintained drift. Verified the assets ship in the wheel (uv build -> 15 asset files present).
TRADEOFF vs the alt (pip install beadloom[ai-techwriter]): vendoring duplicates harness source into each target repo (visible in their git history, must re-run setup to refresh) but avoids packaging the harness into the wheel and keeps the wrapper's existing 'python -m tools.ai_techwriter' invocation working unchanged. The alt would need a new optional-dependency + wheel-inclusion of tools/ -- bigger change, deferred.

SCAFFOLDS (idempotent): (1) tools/ai_techwriter/ vendored harness (.py from .py.txt) + recipe.yaml; (2) the chosen wrapper -- .github/workflows/ai-techwriter.yml OR an ai-techwriter job in .gitlab-ci.yml (GitLab: appends job-only, stripping the standalone stages: header, to an EXISTING file -- never blindly clobbers; an already-wired file is left as-is); (3) docs/guides/ai-techwriter.md (3-step getting-started: register VPS runner / add QWEN_API_KEY / run command+commit+enable).

title: [BDL-044] feat: bidirectional Relationships on node pages — Used by + Parts (incoming edges)
description: Node pages (site_pages.py) currently show only OUTGOING edges (part_of/depends_on/uses), so low-level/heavily-used nodes (e.g. context-oracle) look sparse. Add INCOMING relationships: (1) 'Used by' = deduped UNION of incoming uses + depends_on (sorted) — who consumes this node ('Depended on by' folds into this union, no separate section); (2) 'Parts' = incoming part_of (child nodes). Keep outgoing as-is. Skip self-edges (touches_code self). Render only refs that have a page (link-safe, like the landscape). The incoming-edge data is the same the graph/why already compute. TDD; deterministic; coordinator rebuilds + pushes + verifies on the deployed site (the dogfood-on-built-site lesson).

- Flow-style mappings parse identically to block-style (verified by tests) -- preferred fix path (a).
- load_graph() catches GraphParseError per-file, appends to result.errors (loud, never silent), continues other files.

comments.author: v.zoologov

COMPLETED: Fixed UX issue #60 — Explorer broken after early empty visit.

Root cause: When Explorer was visited before any node selection, then the user returned to Dashboard and selected a node, the subsequent set_ref_id() call in open_explorer/action_switch_screen raced with the screen transition. The widget refresh was lost because the screen wasn't fully active yet.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED: Fixed UX issue #59 — Explorer downstream dependents always empty.

Root cause: Race condition between DependencyPathWidget.show_downstream()/show_upstream() and Textual's deferred refresh cycle. The render() method re-computed the dependency tree using mutable state (_direction, _ref_id) that could become inconsistent between the show_* call and the actual render.

Fix: Pre-render the Rich Text in show_downstream()/show_upstream() and cache it as _cached_text. render() returns the cached snapshot, eliminating the race window. set_provider() invalidates the cache so the next render picks up the new provider.

Files changed:

- data_providers.py: Any used for DebtReport (_report: Any), activity (dict[str, Any]), sync results (list[dict[str, Any]]), WhyResult return — all justified because these are opaque return types from infrastructure APIs that the TUI wraps but does not own. Defining duplicate type stubs would violate the "thin wrapper" principle.
- activity.py: _activity_level(activity: Any) — handles both GitActivity dataclass and dict fallback. Justified for polymorphic provider output.
- dependency_path.py: node: Any in _render_tree_node — handles TreeNode from why module. Acceptable.

- app.py:272,283,291 — type: ignore[misc] for lambda default arg capture pattern (msg=message). This is a well-known mypy limitation with closures capturing loop variables. All 3 are in _for_each_status_bar lambda callbacks. Justified.

### 4. except Exception: Pattern — ACCEPTABLE
- ~30 occurrences across screens and widgets. All follow the same pattern: query_one() or widget operations inside try/except with logger.debug("...", exc_info=True). This is the standard Textual defensive pattern for widgets that may not be composed yet during mount/unmount timing. Every single one logs the exception. None silently swallow errors.

### 5. Architecture Boundaries — PASS
- TUI only reads data (read-only DB connection via ?mode=ro)
- Data providers are thin wrappers calling existing infrastructure APIs
- No circular imports: screens -> widgets -> data_providers -> infrastructure (one direction)

- DEFAULT_CSS on widgets, TCSS files on screens — correct separation

### 7. Security — PASS
- SQL: all parameterized queries with ? placeholders
- subprocess.Popen in explorer.py: noqa: S603 with user-controlled $EDITOR, start_new_session=True. Acceptable for terminal app.
- No hardcoded secrets
- Read-only DB access pattern

- Comprehensive unit tests for all 7 data providers
- Widget rendering tests for all widgets (debt gauge, lint panel, activity, status bar, graph tree, doc health, etc.)

title: Improve beadloom annotation coverage to 80%+
description:
## Problem

Current annotation coverage is 4.4% (4 annotations across 90 functions/classes in 14 modules). Only 4 modules out of 14 have any `# beadloom:` annotations, and those are module-level only. Agents using `beadloom ctx` get useful context for only 3 out of 6+ domains.

## Scope

### 1. Add missing graph nodes to services.yml
- `llm-updater` (domain) — LLM integration for auto-updates
- `reindex` (domain) — Full reindex pipeline
- `onboarding` (domain) — Project bootstrap and setup
- `db` (domain) — Database layer (SQLite WAL)
- `doctor` (domain) — Health checks and diagnostics

### 2. Add annotations to all 14 source modules

**High priority (core):**
- `cli.py` (15 symbols) → bind to `cli` node
- `reindex.py` (7 symbols) → bind to `reindex` node
- `llm_updater.py` (9 symbols) → bind to `llm-updater` node

**Medium priority (infrastructure):**
- `onboarding.py` (6 symbols) → bind to `onboarding` node
- `graph_loader.py` (4 symbols) → bind to `graph-format` node
- `doc_indexer.py` (4 symbols) → bind to `doc-sync` node

**Low priority (utilities):**
- `db.py` (4 symbols) → bind to `db` node
- `doctor.py` (7 symbols) → bind to `doctor` node
- `cache.py` (2 symbols) → bind to `context-oracle` node

### 3. Enrich existing annotations
- Go from module-level only to function/class-level for key symbols
- Add cross-domain annotations where functions touch multiple domains

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 14 .py modules have at least one annotation
- [ ] 70%+ of public functions/classes are annotated
- [ ] Graph has nodes for all major domains
- [ ] `beadloom ctx <any-node>` returns relevant code for every node
- [ ] All tests pass, mypy clean

title: [BDL-UX #238] config-check does not compare the ignore block on disk against the block this version emits
description:
THE INSTANCE IS FIXED, THE CLASS IS THIS BEAD. Found in BDL-068 S4: this repository's `.gitignore` carried `.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl` — the exact filename — while `onboarding/ignore_block.py:95` has emitted the glob `.beadloom/guard-firings*.jsonl` for some time, with a docstring explaining the rotation it covers. The product was right and its own repository was stale.

HOW IT SURFACED, and it is the uncomfortable part: nobody found it. `beadloom-0mdo.31` widened the guard matcher to include `Bash` in the same slice, firings roughly tripled, the log rotated for the first time, and `.beadloom/guard-firings.1.jsonl` appeared as an untracked file. `beadloom waves` would have reported it as a path owned by no bead in the plan. The drift had existed since rotation shipped and was invisible until an unrelated change made the second file exist.

THE CLASS: the ignore block is GENERATED into a repository Beadloom does not own, and then hand-maintained there. Generated-then-hand-maintained is exactly the shape that can only stay correct by coincidence, and this project already has the answer for it — `beadloom-0mdo.27` (S4) built a both-directions check for role duties, and `config-check` already reports drift for the composed role adapters. The ignore block is the other thing `init` writes and it has no such check.

AN ADOPTER IS WORSE OFF THAN THIS REPOSITORY, which is why it is not merely housekeeping: someone who ran `beadloom init` before the rotation feature has the same stale line, will start accumulating a rotated log after an upgrade, and nothing will tell them. The upgrade path writes no ignore block.

EXPECTED: `config-check` compares the ignore block on disk against the block the current version emits and reports the difference. Report, do not rewrite — the block sits in a file the user owns and may have edited deliberately, so this is the `--fix`-is-wrong case for the same reason `.27`'s duty findings are never fixable: the repair is a human's line in a human's file.

DO NOT DERIVE THE EXPECTED BLOCK FROM PROSE OR FROM A COPY. Compare against what `ignore_block.py` actually emits, so a pattern added later is covered without anyone editing a second list — the standing rule of this whole epic.

ROUTED TO S6 with #235 and #236.

title: [BDL-068.S4.x][dev] the path guard's refusal rule is a hand-written backslash test, and on Windows it refuses every edit — replace it with os.sep/os.altsep and a shape gate
description:
THE RESIDUE OF `beadloom-mr2l.60`, closed 2026-08-31 in a tracker cleanup as unfinished work rather than as done. Items 1 and 4 landed there; items 2, 3 and 5 did not. `bd show beadloom-mr2l.60` carries the full measurement and it is not to be redone.

WHAT IS ALREADY MEASURED, not predicted: `paths.py` contains no `sys.platform` and no `os.name`, so the backslash refusal is ONE code path on every OS; `os.fsencode` was monkeypatched to raise if reached and the verdict still came back, so the refusal cannot depend on the platform's codec. Together: on Windows every edit target is MALFORMED and every guarded edit is an `error` at exit 2. The guard's stated reason for the refusal is false on the platform where the refusal actually bites.

WHAT REMAINS, the three items:
2. THE RULE. Refuse on `os.sep` / `os.altsep`, not on a literal backslash. The separator is what the rule is about; the backslash was a spelling of it that happens to be right on one family of platforms.
3. WHAT THE SHAPE GATE THEN OWES ON WINDOWS. Reserved device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `LPT1`...), trailing dot and trailing space — each a stronger argument for a refusal than the backslash ever was, and each currently unchecked.
5. EVERY NEW RULE IS EXERCISED WHERE `PureWindowsPath` CAN SETTLE IT. Item 5's second half — "and on the leg where it cannot" — has no leg: `beadloom-mr2l.64` withdrew `tests-windows` by owner decision (~16-28 runner-minutes per PR, the pipeline's critical path, a platform outside this project's audience). Whatever `PureWindowsPath` cannot settle is written down as a residual in `flow-guards/SPEC.md`, in the `#### Windows: unverified by decision` section `.64` created, and NOT as a prediction.

THE SUITE ALREADY FORBIDS THE CHEAP WAY OUT: `test_no_platform_xfail_waits_for_a_runner_that_will_not_come` fails if a platform prediction is re-pinned on a mark while no runner can adjudicate it. Do not add an xfail; add a proxy assertion or a written residual.

WHY IT IS IN THIS SLICE: the guard's promise is "refuse malformed targets"; its surface is "refuse anything containing a backslash". That is the slice's shape — the enforcement surface derived from an instrument's own matcher, compared against what exists, with the gap reported. Here the gap runs the other way: the surface is WIDER than the promise on one platform and narrower on the checks that platform actually needs.

P2 by honest reading: this project ships no Windows leg and its audience is not on Windows. It is in S4 because it is the same defect class, and because a rule that states a false reason teaches its readers to stop reading reasons.

title: [BDL-061][bug] the guard read-only test accuses the guard when bd flushes its own export — filing a bead makes the suite red until `bd export` runs
description:
MEASURED TWICE ON ONE COMMIT (`beadloom-mr2l.90`, the 3.0.0 release):

  run 1: 7075 passed, 1 FAILED — tests/test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation
         differing item: .beads/issues.jsonl (only that one; beadloom.db, -wal and -shm were identical)
  bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl
  run 2: 7076 passed, 0 failed

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. Two beads had been filed during the session, so the embedded Dolt database held changes the tracked export did not. The test evaluates `bead-claimed`, whose probe SHELLS OUT to `bd`, and that invocation flushed the pending export. Nothing Beadloom owns was written: the guard is read-only with respect to the index, which is what the test exists to prove.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT IN THE TEST RATHER THAN IN THE GUARD. The tracked set is `[beadloom.db, -wal, -shm, .beads/issues.jsonl]` under one assertion, so a write by a DIFFERENT process to a file with a DIFFERENT owner reads as 'a guard wrote to the index'. The docstring already reasons carefully about exactly this class for `-wal` — it states the -wal check RELATIVE to what was there before, because the file belongs to the repository and an earlier `lint` can own it — and then puts `issues.jsonl` in the absolute set, where the same reasoning applies with more force: the export's owner is another tool entirely.

COST, measured: a full 3-minute suite run plus the diagnosis, and the failure names the wrong actor while doing it. It reproduces on demand — file any bead, run the suite.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Either assert `issues.jsonl` separately with a message naming bd as the writer and the remedy (`bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl`), or drop it from this test and measure the tracker export where the tracker is the subject. Do NOT simply delete the assertion: a guard that rewrote the export WOULD be a defect, and this is the only place that would see it.

RELATED: the same drift family as the standing note that `bd close` writes only the local database.

comments.author: agent-viaj-10
comments.text:
NOT closed by beadloom-viaj.10 (BDL-062.10, m4) — same test, adjacent but DIFFERENT failure mode. Recording the interaction so this bead is not assumed fixed.

.10 made this test attribution-aware: when the measurement window shows a change, an idle control window of >= the same duration runs with no evaluation in it. Repository still => the assertion fails as before; repository moving => skip naming the files. That closes the case .10 measured — an EXTERNAL concurrent writer (a plain 'beadloom lint --project .' alongside: 4 failures in 4 runs before, 4 skips with a stated reason after).

This bead's case survives it, by construction. Here the write is triggered BY the evaluation — the bead-claimed probe shells out to bd, and that invocation flushes the pending export. So issues.jsonl moves during the measurement window and the control window afterwards is quiet (the export is already flushed, so a repeat is idempotent). 'moved' non-empty + 'elsewhere' empty => the code falls through to 'assert digest() == before' and FAILS, which is exactly the accusation this bead is about.

So the population argument in this bead's description still stands and still needs its own decision: issues.jsonl has a different owner from the index, and putting it under one absolute assertion with beadloom.db is what lets another tool's write read as 'a guard wrote to the index'. The .10 apparatus (_differing / _moved_with_nothing_running in tests/test_guards_parity.py) is there to build on.

description:

title: [BDL-061] An existing ignore block keeps the pre-rotation pattern, so the archive shows as untracked churn
description:
Filed from beadloom-mr2l.56, which bounded the guard firing record by rolling it over into .beadloom/guard-firings.1.jsonl and widened the shipped ignore pattern to .beadloom/guard-firings*.jsonl.

THE GAP: ensure_ignore_block is written ONCE and never rewritten (BLOCK_MARKER present => hands off), and that is a deliberate property — it is what makes deleting a line a real override. So a project initialised before .56 keeps the exact pattern .beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl, which does not match the archive. On the first rollover (2000 firings) that adopter gets one untracked file in git status, which is precisely the churn the entry was added to remove.

NOT A DEFECT IN .35's write-once rule, and that is why this is filed rather than fixed there: making the block managed so an upgrade could rewrite it would mean a future release editing somebody's .gitignore, which is the trade .35 refused with a stated reason.

OPTIONS, both stated because the trade is real:
(a) config-check (or beadloom doctor) reports an ignore block whose patterns are a strict subset of the current GENERATED_WORKING_SET, naming the missing pattern and leaving the file alone. Cost: a new check with an upgrade-shaped finding an adopter may see as noise. Benefit: no writer, and the adopter decides.
(b) ensure_ignore_block appends a SECOND block for patterns not already present, keeping write-once per pattern rather than per block. Cost: two Beadloom blocks in one .gitignore, and the rule stops being one sentence.

MEASURED REACH: exactly one pattern today, and it only bites after 2000 guarded edits on an upgraded project — so this is small and slow, not urgent. It is filed because it is the kind of gap that is invisible until somebody's git status is dirty for a reason nobody can explain.

title: [BDL-061][bug] the commit-scoped hook type-checks a surface the project never declared typed, so its mypy leg warns on every commit that stages a test
description:
FOUND BY THE HOOK RUNNING ON `beadloom-mr2l.80`'s OWN COMMIT, which is the only way it could have been found: the whole-tree hook that preceded it never ran mypy over tests either, and the project's declared type check is `uv run mypy src/`.

MEASURED. `.80`'s commit staged eight test files and the hook printed **8 mypy errors in 2 files** — `Returning Any from function declared to return "int"`, `Module "beadloom.services.mcp_server" does not explicitly export attribute "declared_refs"`, and three `Unsupported operand types` on `plan.wave_of(...)` comparisons. Every one of them is PRE-EXISTING: the same eight reproduce byte for byte when the HEAD~1 copies of those two files are checked in isolation, so the commit introduced none of them.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DISCOVERY. `.21` scoped the hook's linters to the staged `src/`/`tests/` Python files, which is right for ruff — `uv run ruff check src/ tests/` is the project's declared lint surface and CI runs it. It is NOT right for mypy: the project's declared type surface is `src/` alone, `pyproject.toml` configures strictness for `src/`, and CI checks `src/`. So the hook holds `tests/` to a standard the project has never adopted and the Gate does not enforce, and it will print warnings on essentially every commit that touches a test.

THE COST IS THE ONE THIS EPIC KEEPS PAYING. A warning that fires on almost every commit and that nobody is expected to act on is a warning people stop reading — and the next warning, the one that means something, is read the same way. `beadloom ci` stays green while the hook prints red, so the two enforcement surfaces disagree in the direction that teaches a committer to ignore the closer one.

THREE OPTIONS, and the trade-off runs both ways.
- SCOPE THE HOOK'S MYPY LEG TO `src/`, matching the project's declared type surface and the Gate. Cheapest, and it makes the hook agree with CI. Against it: a test file that WOULD type-check cleanly loses a check it could have had.
- TYPE THE TEST SUITE and add `tests/` to the declared surface. Honest, and it makes the hook's current behaviour correct rather than premature. Against it: it is a large piece of work on ~120 test modules, it belongs to nobody today, and it is not what this epic is about.
- DERIVE THE LEG'S SCOPE FROM THE PROJECT'S OWN CONFIGURATION rather than hardcoding `src|tests` in the template. Most correct — the hook stops holding a second opinion about what is type-checked — and the most work, because it means reading `pyproject.toml`'s mypy sections in the shell template or moving the decision into a beadloom subcommand.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE HOOK MUST NOT SAY IT CHECKED WHAT IT DID NOT. If the mypy leg narrows to `src/`, the staged test files it skipped are an unjudged remainder and the hook already has the vocabulary for that.

NOT URGENT: the leg is `warn` in the default mode and blocks nothing. In `--mode block` it does block, which raises the priority for any adopter who installed the blocking hook.

title: [BDL-061][dev] the commit gate cannot see a neighbour's hunk inside a file the committer owns — compare the staged paths against the committing bead's declared scope
description:
SPLIT OUT OF `beadloom-mr2l.80`, which judged the question rather than absorbing it. `.80` was asked whether #118's remaining hole is fixable at the hook layer; the answer measured there is NO, and this bead is where the layer that CAN answer it lives.

WHAT IS NOT FIXABLE AT THE HOOK LAYER, and why the judgement is not an opinion.
The installed pre-commit hook judges the paths a commit stages. A neighbour's hunk swept into that commit — inside a file the committer legitimately touches, because `git add -p` is unavailable to an agent — is INSIDE the region the gate judges. `.22` measured it: `outside` reads 0 and `staged_py` names the file, so the hook prints a confident "0 file(s) outside this commit were not judged" over a commit containing someone else's work. Nothing the hook can read distinguishes the committer's hunk from the neighbour's, because the index does not record who wrote a line.

WHAT `.80` DID FIX AT THAT LAYER, so this bead is not asked to redo it. `active-sync --stage` ADDS paths to a commit in flight, and `.22`'s own pathspec commit landed two files having named one. The hook now lists what that step added: the unjudged count states the remainder, and the addition is now stated too. That closes the half that arrives through a Beadloom flag. The half that arrives through `git add` is this bead.

THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD CATCH IT, named because `.22`'s own docstring names it: compare the staged paths against the scope the COMMITTING BEAD declared. `beadloom waves` already parses `refs: <ref_id>` out of a bead's own words and resolves it to a node scope and a file set (`waves.scope.resolve_scope`). A commit staging a path outside that file set is either work the bead did not declare or work that is not the committer's, and both are worth a line before the commit lands.

WHAT HAS TO BE DECIDED FIRST, and it is the reason this is a bead rather than a patch.
- WHOSE bead is committing. The hook does not know. The candidates are the claimed in-progress bead from the tracker (wrong the moment two agents share a tree, which is the mode this exists for), an env var the flow sets, and the ACTIVE.md the coordinator maintains. Pick one and say why the other two lose.
- WHAT A DECLARED SCOPE MEANS FOR A COMMIT. A bead scoped to one node legitimately touches its own tests, its own docs and the tracker export. A check that reports all three is noise within a day. Decide the exempt set BEFORE building the check, not after it turns red.
- WARN OR BLOCK. A false positive here blocks a correct commit in a shared tree, which is the failure #118 itself was. Warn is the honest default until the exempt set has been measured on real commits.
- AND WHETHER A COMMIT WITH NO CLAIMED BEAD IS UNJUDGED OR CLEAN. It must be `unjudged` and say so; a commit nobody could attribute reading as clean is the false green this epic exists to remove.

DO NOT SHIP A COUNT NOBODY CHECKED. `.22`'s standing rule applies to this one too: whatever number this prints must be a count of paths actually compared, and a comparison that could not be made must print a different word from one that passed.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED — beadloom review-brief: what a reviewer is handed, and what it is not.

WHAT THE REVIEWER IS HANDED (`beadloom review-brief <bead>`):
  the ASSIGNMENT (the bead's title + description), the DECLARED SCOPE, the
  SPECIFICATION (the graph's documents for those nodes + every scenario whose
  `@bead:` tag names the bead), and the CHANGE (three git questions, see below,
  each path carrying the node that owns it and whether the bead declared it).
WHAT IT IS NOT HANDED: the bead's comments. They are COUNTED, never printed —
  "N author comment(s) withheld", with the reason and the release condition.

THE DECISION, AND WHY IT IS BEFORE/AFTER RATHER THAN SUMMARY/MEASUREMENT:
  The brief was asked to split "the author's advocacy" from "the author's
  measurements". It cannot be built that way. This epic's six understated
  honesty notes were each ACCURATE about what their bead set out to do and
  silent about what it missed — a measurement and a claim arrive in the same
  sentence — so separating them needs a judgement no mechanism can make and an
  author could phrase around. DESCRIPTION-against-COMMENT is structural: the
  same string is read the same way by everyone.
  And the account is RELEASED, not destroyed. `--release` prints the comments
  once a verdict is on the bead, so the deferrals, sabotage tables and numbers
  that this session's reviews used to avoid re-deriving work are still there —
  read after the reviewer's own judgement is recorded and can no longer be
  un-said. A rule that made reviews slower without making them more independent
  would not be an improvement, which is why "never" was rejected.
  A bead that already carries a verdict releases at once, deliberately: a fix
  cycle re-reviews the author's response to an independent judgement already
  made. The hidden-profile risk is in the first pass.

MECHANISM vs INSTRUCTION — stated exactly, because overstating it is the defect
this bead exists to remove:
  ENFORCED (in code, with a test that bites): the command will not print the
  comments before a verdict comment exists — exit 3, "the account stays
  withheld", distinct from exit 2 so a caller cannot confuse "refused" with
  "failed". The marker is matched at a LINE START (`REVIEW PASSED` / `REVIEW
  ISSUES` / `REVIEW FINDINGS`), so a checkpoint that MENTIONS a review does not
  open the gate.
  DOCUMENTED, not enforced: a reviewer with a shell can run `bd comments`, and a
  coordinator can paste the summary into the launch prompt — which I did in
  every review brief of this session's S5 wave, deliberately, to save cycles.
  Nothing in this process can observe that except the agent reading the prompt,
  so the DUTY TO REPORT IT is placed where the observation is: the brief carries
  a notice telling the reviewer to say so in its verdict, and the coordinator
  template now says the review launch prompt carries the bead id and nothing
  else, and that an undeclared paste is invisible to everyone including the
  reviewer. What changed is the DEFAULT, and the withholding is counted and
  visible; it is not a lock.

DEFECT FOUND BY DOGFOODING THE COMMAND ON THIS BEAD:
  `git diff` never lists an untracked path, so the first brief showed a reviewer
  every file the change TOUCHED and none of the four files it ADDED — the half
  of a change most worth reading. Fixed: the inventory is three questions
  (`diff <ref>...HEAD`, `diff HEAD`, `ls-files --others --exclude-standard`).
  Ignored files stay out: git does not track them, so git has no opinion, and
  inventing one would put the index and a build directory in front of a reviewer
  as work. Both legs sabotage-checked.

FILES
  new  src/beadloom/application/review_brief/{__init__,models,assembly,release}.py
  new  src/beadloom/services/commands/review_brief.py
  new  docs/domains/application/features/review-brief/SPEC.md
  new  tests/acceptance/features/review_brief.feature (+ steps)
  new  tests/test_cli_review_brief.py
  mod  src/beadloom/services/cli.py (registration)
  mod  .beadloom/_graph/services.yml (node `review-brief` + part_of application)
  mod  docs/domains/application/README.md (the package + the command)
  mod  src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/roles/core/review.md.txt + the composed
       .claude/agents/review.md + the vendored agents/review.md.txt (byte-equal)
  mod  .claude/commands/coordinator.md + its vendored copy (byte-equal)
  mod  tests/test_s4_cli_decomposition.py (pinned command set: +review-brief)
  mod  tests/test_bead77_kind_and_root_disagree.py (AS-IS denominator 94 -> 95)

ROLE-FILE CHANGES (the reason step 1 was the problem): the shipped review role
  told the reviewer, in its FIRST step, to read `bd comments` and hunt for
  `API CHANGE:` notes. Step 1 is now `beadloom review-brief`, step 2 is "do not
  read the comments yet" with the measured reason, step 5 is `--release` after
  the verdict. Doc-freshness source (1) changed from "the API CHANGE note" to
  "the changed files the brief lists and the symbols they define" — an author
  who forgets the note leaves the derived source intact, so the pointer is no
  longer something the author can forget. The Result section now fixes the three
  verdict openings, because recognising them in the command and emitting them in
  the role must be ONE convention, not two.

TESTS: 21 new cases (7 acceptance scenarios, 14 CLI). All RED first. Nine
  sabotage edits run, each on the leg it should break, all RED:
  account leaked into --json; release never refuses; marker matched anywhere in
  a comment; unanswerable git question read as "no change"; the assignment
  carrying the notes prose; every changed file counted in scope; the brief
  holding the note texts; untracked files dropped; ignored files offered as work.

MEASURED, in a clean room (`git clone` of this branch at e255a21 + only my 16
  files; a clone rather than a `git archive` extraction because sync-check's git
  baseline needs `.git`, and without it one pre-existing test fails at pristine
  HEAD too):
    pytest 6901 passed, 17 skipped, 4 xfailed   (HEAD in the same room: 6880/16)
    ruff 0, mypy 0, beadloom ci rc 0, lint --strict rc 0, sync-check rc 0.
  Green in a clean room over 16 files.

NOT DONE, with the reason:
  - `.beads/issues.jsonl` is NOT in this commit. It is a shared file and the
    concurrent `.78` agent already has it staged; committing it would carry
    their tracker state under my message. The close of this bead therefore lives
    only in the local Dolt DB until someone syncs the export.
  - `cli-commands`, this bead's declared scope, still has no `docs:` entry, so
    the brief reports "0 document(s)" for it. That is the epic's own standing
    finding (BDL-061 CONTEXT `intent_without_as_is`), not a gap in the brief.
  - The scenarios are matched by TAG and not verified to assert anything. A
    scenario that binds and asserts nothing appears in the brief as
    specification. Judging that is the reviewer's work.

title: [BDL-061][dev] S6: a doc pair says whose own file moved (#133/#182)
description:
Split out of the S6 core bead by measurement, not by preference. MEASURED on the S6 dev tree: adding ONE package (application/waves/) made sync-check report 72 stale pairs, of which 10 had a file modified in the tree; 52 of them were application/README.md paired against files nobody touched. Reaching a fixpoint took 3 document revisions and 65 deliberate re-attestations. That is #182's mechanism (symbols_hash is per ref_id, so one changed file marks every pair the node owns) and #133 is the same defect observed at wave-integration time rather than at edit time — the per-worktree baseline is the occasion, the per-node hash is the cause.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF THE CORE BEAD: the repair needs a decision the wave bead does not own — either compute the staleness fact per FILE (a schema and re-baselining change) or keep per-node hashing and give the followers a different word (sibling_changed / unaffected, never the same word as a pair whose own file moved), which changes sync-check's verdict vocabulary, its exit-code population and every surface that prints it. Both are larger than a flag.

DONE WHEN: a pair whose own file did not change is not reported with the same word as one whose file did; sync-update is not the recommended action for a pair nobody can revise; integrating a parallel wave does not re-baseline untouched pairs (PRD US-6 criterion 4, scenario 'Integrating a parallel wave does not re-baseline untouched doc pairs').

refs: sync-check, doc-sync

NOTE ON THE TITLE: no bead number, deliberately (BDL-UX #171) — the number is allocated by bd at creation and writing it into the title beforehand is the two-sources-of-truth defect that produced a wrong dependency edge in this epic's S2 wave.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT — the decision is made and measured.

VOCABULARY DECISION (the whole bead): reuse `unverified`, do not invent a fifth word.
The epic has answered this question four times — #174/#175 gave `missing` and `unverified`,
`.76` gave `excused`, `.77` gave `null` — and a pair whose sibling moved fits the
`unverified` contract exactly: the comparison it CAN make (its own file against its own
baseline) came out equal, and the one it cannot make (whether the shared document still
describes the node) is not a fact about this file. `unverified` is already 'reported by
name, never counted as fresh, never blocking', which is precisely the treatment a pair
nobody can revise needs. New REASON token, not a new status: `sibling_symbols_changed`.

MECHANISM: `sync_state` gains `file_symbols_hash` — the symbol surface of THIS pair's own
code file — beside the existing per-node `symbols_hash`. Both are kept, because they answer
different questions: the node hash says the document's subject moved, the file hash says
whether it moved HERE. Only the second can make this pair stale. A row with no file-level
baseline (a pre-upgrade index, or a file paired through the node's `source` rather than an
annotation) KEEPS the node-level answer — under-reporting on an un-rebuilt index would be
the one failure worse than the noise being removed.

MEASURED, two clean rooms off HEAD e255a21 differing only in the five changed source files,
each run against its OWN code (PYTHONPATH, not the editable install — the first attempt ran
both rooms against the working tree and reported the fix in both):
  perturbation: one function appended to src/beadloom/application/architecture_view.py,
  incremental reindex, sync-check --json.
  BEFORE: 69 stale — 2 hash_changed (own file) + 67 symbols_changed (files nobody touched).
  AFTER:  2 stale (the same 2) + 67 unverified/sibling_symbols_changed, every one of them
          carrying details='architecture_view.py'.
  Both rooms exit 2. The gate still bites; it bites on the 2 pairs somebody can act on.
  The 67 span two nodes (application 51, site-generation 16) — one file, two documents.

The human line for those 67 now reads: 'not checked: this file's symbols did not move;
architecture_view.py did — revise the document against that file, not against this pair.'
No sync-update is offered for them.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
API CHANGE: sync-check gains a verdict/reason pair, and sync_state gains a column.

1. NEW REASON — `sibling_symbols_changed`, carried on the EXISTING `unverified` status.
   A pair whose own code file did not move while another file of the same node did. Appears in
   `--json` (`pairs[].reason`, with the moved file in `pairs[].details`), in `--porcelain`
   (column 5, unchanged five-column shape) and in the human output as
   `[not verified] ... (not checked: this file's symbols did not move; <file> did — revise the
   document against that file, not against this pair)`. NO new summary key: it is counted in the
   existing `unverified`, so the `ok + stale + missing + unverified + exempt + incomplete = total`
   invariant is untouched. NO new status: `unverified` does not block, which is the point — a pair
   nobody can revise must not be held against a gate whose only remedy is re-attestation.

2. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — a pair whose sibling moved is no longer `stale`. Exit codes move with it:
   a project whose only finding was follower noise now exits 0 instead of 2. A project whose own
   file moved still exits 2. This is the whole bead and it is deliberate.

3. NEW COLUMN — `sync_state.file_symbols_hash TEXT DEFAULT ''`. Additive, idempotent,
   applied by `ensure_schema_migrations` AFTER the table-rebuild migrations, because
   `_migrate_sync_status_verdicts` copies an explicit column list and would drop a column added
   before it. An empty value means 'no file-level fact recorded' and the node-level answer stands.

4. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — the human line for `unverified` is now driven by the reason. It used to
   print 'no baseline — the index was rebuilt and git could not supply one' for every unverified
   pair, which is a statement about a different pair.

5. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — `beadloom waves`, the `doc-baseline` medium: its STATEMENT said 'hashed
   per node', which this change falsifies. Rewritten, and its evidence now cites #163 as well.

comments.text:
COMPLETED — a doc pair says whose own file moved. Landed as 29f547c on features/BDL-061-S6.

WHAT, and the decision it turned on. The bead was split off .21 because the repair needed a
VOCABULARY decision that bead did not own. The decision: reuse `unverified`, do not invent a
fifth word. This epic has answered the same question four times — #174/#175 gave `missing` and
`unverified`, .76 gave `excused`, .77 made `docs spaces` return `null` — and a follower pair
fits the `unverified` contract exactly: the comparison it CAN make (its own file against its own
baseline) came out equal, and the one it cannot make (whether the shared document still describes
the node) is not a fact about this file. `unverified` is already 'reported by name, never counted
as fresh, never blocking', which is precisely what a pair nobody can revise needs. The new token is
a REASON, `sibling_symbols_changed`, not a status — so no summary key, no CHECK-constraint change,
and the verdict sum stays intact.

MECHANISM. `sync_state` gains `file_symbols_hash` beside the per-node `symbols_hash`. Both are
kept: the node hash says the document's subject moved, the file hash says whether it moved HERE, and
only the second can make a pair stale. A row with an empty file fact keeps the node-level answer —
under-reporting on an un-rebuilt index would be the one failure worse than the noise removed.

THE HARD PART, found by measuring rather than by reasoning. The first rule I shipped recomputed the
file fact whenever there was none to carry. On the tree that produced 77 rows reading
`sibling_symbols_changed` with NOTHING in `details`: a carried node hash saying something moved,
beside file hashes fabricated from the post-edit tree saying nothing moved — #175's defect reached
from a new side, and the fabricated half wins silently. Second rule: never write a file fact for a
pair that existed before the build. That was honest and too strict — perturbing one `application`
module then left `site-generation`'s 16 untouched pairs reading `symbols_changed`, because that
node had never been stale and so had never been attested. Third and shipped: the file fact may never
CONTRADICT the node one, so it is written for a node NOT in drift (where 'no file moved' is what the
index already says, and recording it adds no claim) and withheld from one that IS. Every clean node
converges on the reindex that adds the column; a node already in drift converges at its next
attestation, which it was going to pay anyway. All three rules are pinned by tests.

MEASURED — three measurements, in three different words.
  (a) TWO CLEAN ROOMS off e255a21, differing only in the changed source files, EACH RUN AGAINST ITS
      OWN CODE via PYTHONPATH. The first attempt ran both rooms against the working tree's editable
      install and reported the fix in both — a measurement that proved the runner, caught and redone.
      Perturbation: one function appended to `application/architecture_view.py`, reindex, sync-check.
      BEFORE 69 stale = 2 hash_changed + 67 symbols_changed on files nobody touched.
      AFTER  2 stale + 67 unverified/sibling_symbols_changed, every one `details: architecture_view.py`.
      Both exit 2. The gate still bites, on the 2 pairs somebody can act on.
  (b) ON THIS REPOSITORY, converged: changing `reindex/sync_state.py` alone reported 2 stale (one
      per document that pairs it) and 60 siblings across two nodes naming it. It would have reported 62.
  (c) THE UPGRADE RUN, on this repository: 81 stale, 77 of them symbols_changed on untouched files —
      i.e. exactly what pre-upgrade Beadloom reported, which is the point of the withholding rule.

VERIFICATION.
  Green IN A CLEAN ROOM over 21 files (git archive HEAD + only my files, fresh git init):
    6900 passed, 16 skipped, 4 xfailed, 0 failed. `beadloom ci` rc 0. ruff clean. mypy clean.
  On the tree the full suite is NOT attributable to this bead — .79 is editing it concurrently and
    six failures in the tree run were theirs or the tree's shared state. Reported as a different
    claim, deliberately (#181).
  `sync-check` on the TREE after this bead's attestations: 340 ok / 0 stale / 0 unverified, rc 0.
  Attestation ledger, stated rather than buried: 8 documents REVISED on their merits (the sync-check
    SPEC, doc-sync README, cli.md, architecture.md, infrastructure README, db DOC, reindex SPEC,
    wave-plan SPEC) and 4 refs attested (reindex, application, doc-sync, sync-check) plus infrastructure,
    db and active-table earlier. The `application` attestation covers 51 pairs that are .79's; done
    knowingly, because it is what moves that node to FILE granularity — after it, .79's next change is
    attributed to their file instead of re-staling 52.

TESTS: 20 new + 3 executable scenarios.
  tests/test_sibling_symbol_baseline.py               17 (4 classes: per-file hash, the three verdicts,
                                                       attestation writes the file fact, provenance)
  tests/acceptance/features/sibling_baseline.feature   3 scenarios, @bead:beadloom-mr2l.78 @node:sync-check
  tests/acceptance/steps/test_sibling_baseline_steps.py  against the real reindex pipeline and the real
                                                       CLI in a real git repo — the subject is what the
                                                       INDEX records across a rebuild, and a hand-built
                                                       sync_state would prove the fixture.
  Every one written RED first and observed failing. The acceptance suite's first RED was the defect
  itself: 3 of 3 pairs stale where 1 file moved.

FILES (21 committed; a 22nd, .beads/issues.jsonl, was added by the hook's active-sync --stage step —
.80's designed behaviour, and it announced itself):

(`symbols_changed`, `worktree`, `re-baseline`) and the three symptoms share no word.

TODO / carried, stated rather than left to be rediscovered:
  - A node already in drift at upgrade keeps node-level reporting until its next attestation. Correct
    and documented, but an adopter's FIRST doc pass after upgrading still sees the old storm for those
    nodes. A `sync-update --adopt-file-granularity` that records file facts without touching doc or

  - #163 is NOT closed by this. Bulk re-attestation is no longer REQUIRED by the tool, which was the

title: [BDL-061.18d][dev] S5: an excused pair never says it was excused
description:
FINDING BDL-061.18-5, filed by the test bead .18; two xfail(strict=True) statements in tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py::TestAnExcusedPairSaysSo, with a passing control beside them.

WHAT. check_sync's new 'exempt' verdict is in no count any surface prints. gate._sync_summary counts STATUS_OK as fresh and STATUS_MISSING/STATUS_STALE as failures and passes over exempt entirely; the 'beadloom sync-check --json' summary carries total, ok, stale, missing, unverified, unchecked, surface_drift and declared_docs and has no exempt key; the human output never contains the word.

MEASURED in a clean-room worktree at f67fc36 with one WORKING document declared as a node's documentation: 341 pairs = 326 ok + 11 exempt + 4 incomplete, printed as 'total 341, ok 326, stale 0, missing 0, unverified 0, unchecked 0'. The gate line read 'sync-check PASS: 326 pair(s) fresh' where the same tree without the declaration read 326 of 330 — the count fell by the pairs that were excused and nothing said so. A consumer computing total - ok reads unexplained pairs.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN GENERALLY. _sync_summary's own docstring is the specification this broke: it exists because 'a bare N pair(s) fresh was true of a run in which six pairs had just been deleted (BDL-UX #174) and of a run that could not detect staleness at all (BDL-UX #175)'. A verdict added after that docstring reintroduced exactly the shape it was written against, and this epic's CONTEXT already carries the rule — skip is a first-class outcome and always says why.

SHAPE OF THE FIX: an exempt key in the JSON summary so the verdicts sum to total, and a clause in the gate line naming the count and the declared reason. Non-blocking either way: exempt stays out of BLOCKING_STATUSES.

DONE WHEN: both xfail(strict=True) tests turn green.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED — three states, three words, and the verdicts sum to the total.

WHAT. `_sync_summary` gained `_excused_clause`: `N pair(s) fresh, M exempt — <declared reason>`, empty when nothing was excused so a project that declares no exemption keeps its line, and present on the FAILING branch too — a run that hides a count is exactly the run whose count fell. The reason comes from the row's own `details`, so a skip says why without a reader going to --json; it is omitted when the excused rows disagree about it or carry none (a reasonless exemption is a config error `docs spaces` already reports, not a reason to hide the count).

THE JSON. `summary` gained `exempt` AND `incomplete`, so ok + stale + missing + unverified + exempt + incomplete == total. `incomplete`'s absence was review `.15`'s M5, stated honestly in the sync-check SPEC and open since S4b; it closes here rather than separately because the sum cannot work while any verdict has no key. `unchecked` is deliberately OUTSIDE the sum and the SPEC now says so: it counts NODES that contribute no pair at all, a different population from the pairs the verdicts describe.

THE HUMAN OUTPUT. `_STATUS_MARKER` gained `[exempt]` — an excused row printed `[ok]`, the word for a comparison that happened — and the row prints `(not checked: <declared reason>)`.

MEASURED ON THIS REPOSITORY, through the real CLI on an incremental reindex (#175): with `doc_roots.working.roots: [docs/**/*.md]` declared, `sync-check --json` reports 330 = 298 ok + 28 exempt + 4 incomplete and the verdicts sum; before this bead the same run printed `total 330, ok 298, stale 0, missing 0, unverified 0, unchecked 0` and 32 pairs were unaccounted for. `beadloom ci` rc 0 with the shipped configuration, where nothing is excused and the sync-check line is unchanged.

TESTS. 13 new in tests/test_bead76_an_excused_pair_says_so.py + 1 acceptance scenario (`@bead:beadloom-mr2l.76`). TESTS MUST BITE, measured: emptying the excused list in `_excused_clause` and zeroing the `exempt` key reddens 9 — 6 of mine, `.18`'s two newly-closed pins and the acceptance scenario; restored by byte-identical copy (CLEAN-ROOM REVERT).

ONE FAILURE THE FULL-SUITE RUN FOUND, and it belongs to `.75`: tests/test_decode_handlers.py's ledger row `doc_sync/engine.py::_resolve_reference_docs_dir#1` had no block behind it any more, because `.75` collapsed that function into `resolve_docs_dir`, whose handler catches (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError) and is therefore not narrow. The ledger failing on a stale row is the mechanism working — a list of exclusions that outlives the code it excused reads as approval for something nobody checked — and the row is deleted with the reason, not repointed. It also marks the limit of the targeted runs `.75` and `.74` were verified with: neither ran the whole suite, and this row is what that costs.

FILES: src/beadloom/application/gate.py, src/beadloom/services/commands/docsync.py, tests/test_bead76_an_excused_pair_says_so.py (new), tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py, tests/test_decode_handlers.py, tests/acceptance/{features/doc_spaces.feature,steps/test_doc_spaces_steps.py}, 5 AS-IS documents updated + re-attested.

API CHANGE: `beadloom sync-check --json` summary gains `exempt` and `incomplete` keys (stored-baseline mode only; the `--since` shape is untouched). The rich output gains the `[exempt]` marker and a reason line. The `beadloom ci` sync-check line gains `, M exempt — <reason>` when a declaration excused something. Docs updated + re-attested: docs/domains/doc-sync/features/sync-check/SPEC.md, docs/domains/doc-sync/README.md, docs/domains/application/features/ci-gate/SPEC.md, docs/domains/application/README.md, docs/domains/application/components/active-table/DOC.md. title: [BDL-061.18a][dev] S5: a TO-BE directory that carries no intent document leaves every count
description:
FINDING BDL-061.18-1, filed by the test bead .18 and executable as four xfail(strict=True) statements in tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py::TestADirectoryThatHoldsIntentReachesTheDenominator.

WHAT. read_epic_intents() derives epics from directories holding a TO-BE document, then requires CONTEXT.md or BRIEF.md inside. A directory with neither is appended to nothing: it is absent from epics, from unresolved_epics and from every NOT CHECKED line, while its documents are still counted in the TO-BE population. One report states two incompatible sizes for one tree.

MEASURED on this repository at f67fc36: 61 directories contribute a document to the to_be population of 190 and 57 become epics. The four that vanish are .claude/development (which holds ROADMAP.md and BDL-UX-Issues.md) and the SUMMARY.md-only feature directories BDL-009, BDL-010 and BDL-016.

THREE ROUTES, one cause. (1) no CONTEXT.md/BRIEF.md at all. (2) a CONTEXT.md that cannot be decoded — _read returns None and the caller continues, so a cp1251 planning document removes its epic rather than reporting itself; that is the shape .68 gave the ledger and .14 filed as BDL-061.14-3 against the reference leg. (3) _INTENT_DOCUMENTS is hardcoded to two file names while every root around it is configuration, so an adopter whose planning document is named anything else loses 100% of its epics and the gate prints a plausible '0 of 0 epic(s) with closed beads' (TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE).

SHAPE OF THE FIX, same as the one .17 already applied one layer up: a TO-BE directory with no readable intent document is an unresolved epic carrying its own reason, never an absence; and the intent document names move into doc_roots beside the kinds they are drawn from.

DONE WHEN: the four xfail(strict=True) tests in TestADirectoryThatHoldsIntentReachesTheDenominator turn green and their markers are removed.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
COMPLETED — an epic is a directory that holds intent, and every unresolved one carries its reason.

WHAT. `read_epic_intents` now builds one `EpicIntent` per TO-BE directory and asks `_read_declaration` what that directory declares. Three outcomes rather than a silent `continue`: the intent document was read and names nodes; it was read and names none (`no_node_declared`); or there is no readable intent document, because the directory carries none of the configured names (`no_intent_document`) or the one it carries cannot be decoded (`unreadable_intent_document`). `EpicIntent.unresolved_reason` carries it and `SpacesReport.unresolved_reasons` maps every unresolved epic to its own.

ONLY ONE OF THE THREE IS A FINDING, and the line is deliberate. An undecodable planning document is a defect IN THAT DOCUMENT — `_read` answered None and the caller continued, so a cp1251 CONTEXT.md removed its own epic — and is reported as `intent_document_unreadable`. A directory that carries no intent document is a directory that is not an epic: `.claude/development` holds ROADMAP.md and BDL-UX-Issues.md, and reporting it would fill the everyday line with things nobody intends to change. It is counted and named, which is the claim the finding makes.

THE NAMES ARE CONFIGURATION NOW: `doc_roots.to_be.intent_documents`, default (CONTEXT.md, BRIEF.md), beside the kinds they are drawn from. A declared list REPLACES the shipped pair rather than joining it — a project's convention is a statement, not an addition to ours — and that is pinned by a test. TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE: proved on tests/adopter_project.py's TypeScript project, which counts its epic with `design/ORD-4/OVERVIEW.md` and reads its declarations once the name is declared.

RE-PUBLISHED DENOMINATORS, measured through the real CLI on an incremental reindex (#175), --json only (#148):
- epics **57 -> 61**, unresolved **52 -> 56** = 52 `no_node_declared` + 4 `no_intent_document` (BDL-009, BDL-010, BDL-016, development — exactly the four `.18` named), epics the tracker does not name **20 -> 24**.
- UNCHANGED and re-verified: to_be 190 / as_is 93 / working 55, refs_checked 17, epics_declaring_nodes 5, epics_with_closed_beads 37, findings 2. `.18`'s independent recount suite (which shares no function with the code under test) passes untouched, including `test_every_directory_holding_a_to_be_document_is_counted_here`, which is now the test that holds the two sizes together.
- The gate line reads: `... 17 node declaration(s) from 37 of 61 epic(s) with closed beads ...; NOT CHECKED: 56 epic(s) declare no node (4 carry no readable intent document); NOT CHECKED: 24 epic(s) the tracker does not name ...`.

`describe_unresolved(reasons)` renders that clause and is shared by the gate and the command, so one bucket cannot be described two ways — the shape `.75` had just repaired one layer down.

TESTS. 15 new in tests/test_bead73_intent_documents.py + 1 acceptance scenario (`@bead:beadloom-mr2l.73`). TESTS MUST BITE, measured: restoring the drop (a directory with no readable intent document skipped) reddens 13 — 7 of mine, 4 of `.18`'s newly-closed pins, `.18`'s repository leg for `.74`, and the acceptance scenario; restored by byte-identical copy (CLEAN-ROOM REVERT).

FILES: src/beadloom/infrastructure/doc_roots.py, src/beadloom/application/{doc_spaces.py,gate.py}, src/beadloom/services/commands/docs.py, tests/test_bead73_intent_documents.py (new), tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py, tests/acceptance/{features/doc_spaces.feature,steps/test_doc_spaces_steps.py}, 6 AS-IS documents updated + re-attested.

title: [BDL-061.17b][dev] S5b: ROADMAP + issue-log kinds, and counts that are computed
description:
SPLIT OUT OF `beadloom-mr2l.17`, which shipped the other five S5 mechanisms. PLAN warned S5 was a likely candidate ("if a slice proves to be an epic, that is reported rather than absorbed") and named the seam that would justify it. This is that seam.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD, measured rather than argued. The five mechanisms `.17` shipped share one module — `infrastructure/doc_roots.py` supplies the vocabulary, and `application/doc_spaces.py`, `check_sync`, the reindex and the CLI all consume it. This half shares NONE of that code. A ROADMAP and an issue log are instances CHECKED by two mechanisms that already exist and are somebody else's: `doc_shape.check_section_shape` (the sections a kind requires, from the composed templates in `onboarding/doc_templates.py`) and `doc_sync/audit.py`'s fact registry (a number in a document held against project state). It CONSUMES `.17`'s space vocabulary — a ROADMAP is TO-BE, an issue log spans both — but consuming a vocabulary is a dependency, not shared code. That is the precedent `.13` set in S4 when it split at the point the pieces stopped sharing a module.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. Two shipped document KINDS: `ROADMAP` and an issue log. Today `document_kind()` derives the kind from the file stem, so `ROADMAP.md` is already a kind of its own with no template, no required sections and no space. It needs a template under `templates/docs/` (the S4 decision: templates are files, not string literals), required sections that `doc_shape` can hold a document to, and a place in `doc_roots.DEFAULT_KINDS`.

2. COMPUTED facts. PLAN's criterion is that the hand-written tally CANNOT RETURN, not that it is currently absent. The counts that used to sit at the top of `.claude/development/BDL-UX-Issues.md` were maintained by hand and were wrong — they claimed 46 open against 34 actual — and were DELETED for that reason, with a note saying so. A deleted number is not a mechanism: nothing stops the next writer adding one. The shape that would stop it is `doc_sync/audit.py`'s: a fact the tool computes (open issues, closed issues, the highest number used) and compares against every number the document states, so a hand-written count that disagrees is a finding rather than prose nobody checks.

3. Our own ROADMAP and issue log restructured as instances of those kinds, with the computed counts rendered. This is `beadloom-mr2l.20`'s deliverable (`[tech-writer] S5: spec-space guide; ROADMAP/BDL-UX restructured`), so DO NOT do it here — ship the kinds and the facts, and let `.20` write the documents against them.

THE TRAPS THIS EPIC HAS ALREADY PAID FOR, all live here.

- A FACT THAT CANNOT BE READ. `docs audit` already reports `language_count` as `unreadable` because its value is 1 and "0 and 1 are too common in prose to be read as claims". An issue-log count of 3 has the same problem, and a count nobody can state is a fact the check cannot verify. Decide what the fact is BEFORE building the extractor, and say what it cannot cover.
- A FALSE POSITIVE THAT COSTS PROSE. BDL-UX #190 and #169 are both instances of the audit scanner binding a number to the wrong noun, and `.17` hit a THIRD while writing its own documentation: "measured on 60 epics and attributed the node `status`" was read as a stale `node_count` claim. An issue log is 1778 lines of numbered entries, dates and severities. Measure the false-positive rate on it before shipping the fact, and do not reach for `docs_audit.ignore` — #190 says that is the wrong door.
- TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE. `tests/adopter_project.py` exists since S3b and has caught six defects that read correct here because we are Beadloom. A ROADMAP kind whose required sections are derived from OUR ROADMAP is a kind no adopter can satisfy.
- ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE. A document of a kind nobody wrote, a fact no document states, a section a majority does not carry — each must report itself rather than read as clean. `doc_shape` already has the majority rule and `audit_coverage` already has the not-covered verdict; use them rather than building a third.

MEASURED STARTING POINT, on HEAD ac3c0f0: `.claude/development/ROADMAP.md` is 225 lines, `.claude/development/BDL-UX-Issues.md` is 1778 lines with entries numbered to 191 and no tally anywhere. `docs audit` declares 9 facts, verifies 3, and reports 6 not covered — the issue-log counts would be facts 10 and 11.

Standing rules by name: A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TESTS MUST BITE, TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE, CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN.

NOTE ON THE DAG, not changed here: `beadloom-mr2l.19` (review S5) carries the criterion "our ROADMAP + issue log validate as instances" and `.20` writes them. Both will need this bead. The dependency was NOT added, because rewiring the DAG is the owner's decision.

title: [dev] a closed epic's goal cannot be made measurable retroactively — give doc-quality a historical exclusion
description:
From `beadloom-mr2l.65`, which turned out to have nothing to pay.

After `.70` re-scoped `measurable-goal` (154 -> 4), the four survivors are all genuine unbounded-improvement predicates - and all four are in CLOSED epics: BDL-002, BDL-004, BDL-005, BDL-006, each `CONTEXT.md` line 12 or 13.

THE PROBLEM IS NOT THE CHECK. It is right about all four. The problem is that there is no honest way to satisfy it: rewriting a goal written before the work existed would fabricate the record of intent, and CONTEXT's TO-BE/AS-IS decision exists precisely so a planning document REMAINS the record of what was intended and can be checked against later.

WHAT TO BUILD: a way to mark a document historical - a closed epic's planning set - and exclude it from the content checks with a stated reason. Follow the shape every other exclusion in this codebase now has (`reason` mandatory; `until` mandatory elsewhere, but a closed epic has no exit condition, so decide what the honest field is and say why rather than leaving it blank).

THREE THINGS THAT MUST HOLD, and this epic has watched each fail:
- A historical exclusion that matches nothing must REPORT ITSELF, like `.48`'s rule liveness and `.49`'s expired exemption. An exclusion list that quietly stops applying is how a gate is switched off.
- The count must stay visible. `docs-quality` currently prints "243 document(s) read; measurable-goal 4" - after this it must say how many documents were excluded as historical, not just shrink the denominator. A count that gets smaller without saying why is #174's equation.
- Do not derive "historical" from the absence of something. Absence is not evidence - that is the sentence four separate beads in this epic turned on. It should be a declaration, and a wrong declaration should be detectable (a document marked historical whose epic is still open, say).

Standing rules by name: A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TESTS MUST BITE, NO CALLER NO CAPABILITY.

description:

`src/beadloom/onboarding/templates/roles/core/_writing.md.txt:10` reads:

    **What is checkable, and is checked.** `beadloom lint` reports these; do not wait

That is the false-green shape this epic exists to remove, arriving through the very text that states the standard.

One further honesty point belongs in the same edit: `measurable-goal` is currently a numeral detector rather than a measurability detector (review `beadloom-mr2l.15`; re-scope carried by `beadloom-mr2l.65`), so the fragment should not promise that a checkable goal passes it.

NOT FIXED HERE because templates live under src/ and .16 edits only docs/.

title: [dev] the decode sweep: 29 narrow handlers and 49 unguarded decoding reads, judged per site
description:
`tests/test_decode_handlers.py` (BDL-061 .66) measures every `try` in `src/` that guards a text decode with a handler narrower than what the call can raise: 29 sites on this tree, each recorded in its LEDGER as MEASURED, NOT JUDGED. The ledger stops instance number six from joining them silently; it does not decide the 29.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, per site, using .42's framework: decide whether the stream is a UTF-8 CONTRACT (a file this project or its templates wrote — decode with an explicit encoding and widen the handler) or the USER'S LOCALE (decode with the ambient codec and say so), then either widen the handler and delete the ledger entry, or record the real reason in place of the debt string.

SECOND POPULATION, deliberately outside the ledger and stated in its docstring: 49 `read_text` calls in `src/` have NO handler at all. Most are correct — a caller may own the failure — but that is the shape that produced the worst instance found (`doc_sync/engine.check_doc_coverage`, unguarded, which crashed `check_sync` one phase before `doc_shape` could report anything). Deciding these is a judgement per site, not a pattern, so it needs a bead rather than a rule.

DONE WHEN: every LEDGER entry carries a decision rather than the debt string, or is gone because the handler was widened; and the unguarded population has a recorded verdict (swept, or explicitly out of scope with a reason).
