title: [BDL-061][task] fifteen tests skip on Linux that do not skip on macOS — measure the skip POPULATION per leg, not just the pass count
description:
ROUTED HERE BY BDL-061.39, WHICH MEASURED THE WINDOWS AXIS AND DECIDED THIS IS A DIFFERENT ONE. .6 recorded the observation and nobody took it: the Linux container reports 26 SKIPPED where this macOS reports 11. Fifteen tests do not run on one of the two images we actually ship against, and no leg says which fifteen or why.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD AND NOT PART OF .39. .39's ledger (tests/test_windows_dimension.py::test_no_win32_skip_is_unjudged) covers skips whose condition mentions `sys.platform` — an AST scan over tests/, with a judgement required per entry and no "convenience" verdict available. That mechanism does NOT reach these fifteen, because they are not platform-conditional at all: they are CAPABILITY- and ENVIRONMENT-conditional (root ignoring permission bits, an absent binary, a missing grammar wheel, a dogfood artifact that was never generated in that checkout, a filesystem that can or cannot name something). Two of them are already known by name from .38's baseline — test_atomic_io_call_sites::test_nonwritable_dir_raises_and_leaves_no_partial and test_setup_rules_fix::test_returns_none_for_unreadable_file both FAIL as root because root ignores the mode bits they create, which is the same fact wearing a failure instead of a skip. Widening .39's ledger to every conditional skip in the suite would have put a hundred-odd entries in one dict and blurred "the platform leg exists" with "every skip in the suite is judged", so it was left as a scan that bites for exactly one class.

THE THING WORTH BUILDING, and it is a measurement rather than a rule: a skip is invisible by construction — it reads as a pass, it has no owner, and nothing compares the skip POPULATION between two legs. The pipeline now runs the same whole suite on four ubuntu pythons, two locales and (BDL-061.39) windows-latest, so the data already exists and nobody looks at it.

SCOPE WHEN TAKEN:
1. Get the numbers instead of the anecdote: `pytest -rs --json-report` (or parse `-rs`) on each leg, and DIFF the skip sets. The measurement is the SYMMETRIC DIFFERENCE between legs, exactly as the locale legs' value is the delta and not any leg's colour.
2. Classify each row that skips on one image and not another: (a) the facility genuinely does not exist there — legitimate, wants a stated reason like .39's; (b) the test asserts a POSIX/UTF-8/non-root answer that is simply different there — the .42 class, a test defect; (c) the precondition is not reproduced and the row therefore asserts nothing anywhere — a vacuous test, the class this whole family of beads exists to close. Root-vs-user is likely to dominate (b) and (c).
3. Decide whether the skip-set delta should be a CHECK. Recorded as a baseline it becomes a ratchet: a PR that makes a test stop running on a leg fails, which is the only defence against the failure mode where a green leg quietly covers less than it did last week. Weigh that against baseline-file churn; a cheaper first step is to have the CI legs simply PRINT `-rs` and the counts, so the number is visible before it is enforced.
4. Judge whether ubuntu-as-root is even the right image: GitHub's ubuntu-latest does NOT run as root, so two of the fifteen are artifacts of running the suite in a container locally and would not appear on the leg at all. That is itself worth stating — the local container and the CI runner are a THIRD pair of environments that disagree.

ACCEPTANCE: the skip population of every CI leg is measured and diffed against the others; each row that skips on one leg and runs on another is classified into one of the three buckets above; and it is decided in writing whether the delta becomes an enforced ratchet or a printed number.

title: [BDL-061][dev] S4b: doc templates out of the generator; missing_sections + section-quality checks
description:
Split out of beadloom-mr2l.13, which PLAN sized as one slice and which is six distinct mechanisms. .13 delivers the scenario half (the owner's request: BDD + Gherkin ported and improved) plus the role-template layer. This bead carries the DOCUMENT-SHAPE half, a different subject in a different domain:

1. Doc templates move from onboarding/doc_generator.py string literals into templates/docs/ and compose via onboarding.composer.compose(core, architecture, stack, project) — the S3 mechanism, reused rather than duplicated.
2. New staleness reason missing_sections (warn) in doc_sync, beside the existing five: they all compare CONTENT, never STRUCTURE.
3. Section-quality checks (all warn): a goal with no measurable clause; a decision row with an empty reason; a risk row with no mitigation; a Pending open question in an Approved document; an unfilled shipped placeholder ([Name], Criterion 1).
4. A project overlay can add required sections.

Also deferred here from .13 and stated rather than dropped: the MUTATION-SCOPE check (a declared mutation target outside the configured source paths is reported). The role DUTY text ships in .13; the check is a mechanism with its own config and belongs with this bead.

Depends on .13 for nothing structural — the two halves do not share code — but PLAN sequences S4 dev before .14 test.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — two of four mechanisms green.

1. DOC TEMPLATES OUT OF THE GENERATOR. Five templates now ship as package data under onboarding/templates/docs/core/ (overview, domain, service, feature, beadloom-readme) and compose through S3's compose(core, architecture, stack, project) as a new 'docs' ArtifactKind. doc_generator.py's five string literals are gone; the render functions build a values dict and call render_doc(). Extraction is BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING and pinned by two byte-identity tests (with and without the conditional ## Public API block), so the 52 existing doc-generator/CLI/init tests stayed green without an edit.

Decisions:
- Placeholders are {{name}}, not str.format's single brace: a generated document carries Mermaid, JSON and shell fragments, and a lone { in any of them either raises from the formatter or is silently eaten.
- A placeholder with no value RAISES. A silently-empty substitution is how a document ships half-written, which is the class the placeholder quality check exists for.
- A doc composition carries NO flow-suppression notice (new ArtifactKind.carries_suppressions, False for docs). A suppression stands down a rule addressed to an agent; appending it to a generated README publishes flow configuration as documentation.
- REQUIRED SECTIONS ARE DERIVED from the composed template's literal '## ' headings, with placeholders erased first. So a project fragment at .beadloom/flow/docs/domain.md appending '## Runbook' makes Runbook required by the same act — PLAN's 'a project overlay can add required sections', with one source of truth rather than two. A heading that arrives THROUGH a placeholder (## Public API) is conditional by construction and cannot be required of a node with no public symbols.

2. missing_sections. New doc_sync/doc_shape.py + phase 5 in check_sync, new status 'incomplete' (deliberately NOT in BLOCKING_STATUSES) with reasons missing_sections and section_not_in_use.

Two design decisions, both forced by MEASUREMENT on this repo rather than chosen:
- PEER-RELATIVE BY MAJORITY. First cut said 'in use if any document carries it' and reported 38 documents. Measured: ## Parent is carried by 1 feature SPEC of 36, so a presence-of-one rule reports the 35 that follow the actual convention — the finding inverted. A section below a majority is now reported ONCE against the KIND, with its ratio ('Source (5/36)'), because it is a statement about the convention and is fixed in the template, not in 35 files. A tie is not yet a convention. Same shape as .13's 'a features glob matching zero files reports the glob, not every node'.
- A SECTION IS MATCHED BY ITS NAME AS A WHOLE-WORD PHRASE, not by string equality. '## Features and components' is not a document that lost its Features section; equality reported two domain READMEs of ours that carry it under a wider title. Whole-word, so '## Featureset' is still a different heading.

MEASURED ON THIS REPO after both corrections: 4 rows. One real document finding — docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md has no Features section while its 6 peers do — and three convention statements with denominators (domain: Source 0/7, Dependencies 0/7; feature: Source 5/36, Dependencies 0/36, Parent 1/36; service: Source 0/4, Dependencies 0/4).

Layering: doc_sync and onboarding are PEER DOMAINS and this repo's graph declares no domain->domain edge, so the requirements are injected. application/doc_shape.py joins the two and four reporting surfaces pass them in (gate, sync-check CLI, MCP sync_check, TUI dashboard). Three call sites deliberately do NOT: sync-update x2 (re-baselining cannot fix a missing section) and site_published (publishing does not judge one).

Tests: +33 (15 doc templates, 18 missing_sections). ruff + mypy --strict clean.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 2 — all four mechanisms in, and the concurrent collision it caused.

3. THE FIVE SECTION-QUALITY CHECKS: new doc_sync/doc_quality.py, surfaced by 'beadloom docs quality' (warn, exit 0; --strict turns findings into exit 1) and a new gate step 'docs-quality' that reports and never blocks.

MEASURED ON THIS REPO'S OWN 243 PLANNING DOCUMENTS:
  measurable-goal       154 findings over 235 goal statements read
  decision-reason         0 over 261 decision rows read
  risk-mitigation         0 over 138 risk rows read
  pending-in-approved     6 over  69 open-question rows read
  unfilled-placeholder    0 over 243 documents read
checks_that_read_nothing = () — every check found a real population here.

The 6 pending-in-approved are genuine and named: BDL-061's OWN Approved RFC leaves Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5 Pending, every one of them decided in CONTEXT and never resolved back, plus BDL-021 Q4 and BDL-034 Q1.

Two false-positive classes were MEASURED and removed rather than tuned away:
- A placeholder inside an INLINE CODE SPAN is a command's metavariable ('beadloom ctx <ref-id>'), not an unfilled field. Applied symmetrically to the derivation and to the scan, or the check flags the correct documentation of every command we ship.
- An ENUMERATED stub ('Goal 1', 'Step 2') counts only as the WHOLE bullet/cell/heading, bar a trailing parenthetical. Substring matching reported three real headings of BDL-030's RFC ('Step 1 (12.12.1): Detection').

THE PLACEHOLDER VOCABULARY IS DERIVED, not listed: 44 tokens read from the composed /templates command's fenced blocks. A hand-kept list is a second source of truth that goes stale the first time a template gains a field, and the check would then pass documents nobody filled in.

Stated limits (in the SPEC and the module docstring, not left to be discovered): a number is NECESSARY for a measurable clause and not sufficient; a reason is checked for EXISTENCE, not for explaining rather than restating; a mitigation is judged against a named set of empty ones ('monitor it'), not on whether it would work.

4. THE MUTATION-SCOPE CHECK: new application/mutation_scope.py, three findings (mutation-outside-source / mutation-target-missing / mutation-zero-mutants), all warn, surfaced by config-check (CLI + gate). Config is 'mutation.targets' in .beadloom/flow.yml; 'inside' is decided by .beadloom/config.yml's scan_paths and languages, so an adopter whose code lives in lib/ is judged against lib/.
- It lives in application, not onboarding: it joins flow.yml to config.yml's scan paths, and scan_paths is read through the infrastructure seam onboarding may not import. Same precedent as application/guards/config.py owning the guards: block.
- It runs BEFORE the gate step's database guard. A declaration is checkable against the tree whether or not the index was built; dropping it on a missing database makes the finding vanish exactly when it is least likely to be noticed.
- DOGFOODED: .beadloom/flow.yml now declares three real targets (doc_quality.py, doc_shape.py, graph/rules/), so the check has a live population here. It reports 0 on this repo — a correct declaration is what a passing check looks like — and the sabotage pass measures that it fires.

SCENARIOS FIRST-CLASS: 12 new executable scenarios across 4 .feature files (document_shape, document_quality, mutation_scope, doc_templates), bound by @bead:beadloom-b0xl and @node:. lint's scenario-coverage went 68 -> 69 warns: +3 new feature nodes, of which doc-shape and doc-quality (and the mutation-scope component and doc-templates) now carry scenarios.

GRAPH + DOCS: 5 new nodes (doc-templates feature, doc-shape + doc-quality features, doc-shape-requirements + mutation-scope components) each with a doc. module-coverage stays at 0 errors; lint --strict rc 0.

CONCURRENT-TREE COLLISION, reported rather than worked around: .14's tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py hardcoded the acceptance suite at SEVEN scenarios in two places ('len(passed) == 7', 'len(survivors) < 7'). Adding scenarios reddened both. I changed the constant into a COUNT read from the suite via the project's own parser (load_suite + DEFAULT_FEATURE_GLOB), and strengthened the sabotage test to also assert the failures are the sabotaged FILE's rather than collateral. That is the minimum edit that makes the property survive any later slice; flagged here because it is another agent's file.

  pending-in-approved     6 over  69 open-question rows read
  unfilled-placeholder    0 over 243 documents read
No check reads nothing: checks_that_read_nothing == (), and a test asserts it, so a check that goes blind here is a failure rather than a silence.

THREE FIRE ON NOTHING HERE, AND THAT IS NOT VACUITY — each was proved to fire on a REAL document under one reverse-editable edit, in memory, nothing written:
  decision-reason      blanked the reason cell of BDL-061/CONTEXT.md's 'A guard is data' row  -> 0 before, 1 after
  risk-mitigation      replaced BDL-040/RFC.md's 'Rendering polish' mitigation with 'Monitor it' -> 0 before, 1 after
  unfilled-placeholder put '[Name]' back into BDL-061/PRD.md's title                          -> 0 before, 1 after
Two of the three read a large real population (261 decision rows, 138 risk rows) and found it clean; that is a CHECKED green, not an unchecked one, and the denominators are printed on every run so it cannot be mistaken for the other kind.

The 6 pending-in-approved are real debt, not noise: four are BDL-061's OWN Approved RFC (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5), every one of them decided in CONTEXT and never resolved back into the RFC, plus BDL-021 Q4 and BDL-034 Q1. The 154 measurable-goal findings are the same shape as .13's 33 missing scenarios — our PRDs state goals as deliverables, and the standard asks for a measurable clause. Not tuned away.

DECISIONS (each with its reason)
1. The doc templates compose through S3's compose() as a FOURTH artifact kind rather than through a second mechanism. A second assembly is a second thing that can drift from config-check.
2. Required sections are DERIVED from the composed template's literal headings, placeholders erased first. A project fragment appending '## Runbook' makes Runbook required by the same act — PLAN's overlay criterion with one source of truth instead of two — and a heading arriving through a placeholder (## Public API) stays conditional by construction.
3. A doc composition carries NO suppression notice (new ArtifactKind.carries_suppressions). A suppression stands down a rule addressed to an agent; a generated README has none, and appending it publishes flow configuration as documentation.
4. A missing placeholder RAISES rather than substituting empty. A silently-empty substitution is how a document ships half-written — the class check 5 exists for.
5. missing_sections is PEER-RELATIVE BY MAJORITY. Measured: '## Parent' is carried by 1 feature SPEC of 36, so a presence-of-one rule reported the 35 that follow the actual convention. Below a majority the KIND is reported once with its ratio, because the fix is in the template, not in 35 files. A tie is not yet a convention.
6. A section is matched by its name as a WHOLE-WORD PHRASE, not by equality. '## Features and components' is not a document that lost its Features section; equality reported two of our domain READMEs that carry it under a wider title. Whole-word, so '## Featureset' is still different.
7. Status 'incomplete', outside BLOCKING_STATUSES and never written to sync_state. The column would otherwise mean two things, and a check that writes to what it inspects cannot be trusted about it.
8. The requirements are INJECTED. doc_sync and onboarding are peer domains and this repo's graph declares no domain->domain edge. application/doc_shape.py joins them; four reporting surfaces pass them in; three deliberately do not (sync-update x2, site_published) and the SPEC names them.
9. A placeholder inside an INLINE CODE SPAN is a metavariable, not an unfilled field, on both the derivation and the scan side. Without it the check flags the correct documentation of every command we ship.
10. An ENUMERATED stub counts only as a whole bullet/cell/heading. Substring matching reported three real headings of BDL-030's RFC ('Step 1 (12.12.1): Detection').
11. Only an AGREED status (approved/accepted) is held to 'no Pending question'. A Draft is supposed to have open questions and reporting them teaches an author to ignore the check. A 'Pending' outside ## Open Questions is not a finding — PLAN's bead table uses it as a status.
12. The mutation-scope check lives in application, not onboarding: it joins flow.yml to config.yml's scan_paths, read through the infrastructure seam onboarding may not import. Same precedent as application/guards/config.py.
13. It runs BEFORE the config-check gate step's database guard. A declaration is checkable against the tree whether or not an index exists.
14. beadloom docs quality exits 0 with findings; --strict is the opt-in enforcement. No adopter's green project turns red on upgrade, and a project that wants the bar can have it.

TESTS: +90 unit (15 doc templates, 20 missing_sections, 43 doc quality, 16 mutation scope, minus overlap) + 12 executable scenarios in 4 .feature files. Suite 6428 passed / 2 known failures (TestSyncCheckNewPairs, .16's criterion, caused by the pre-existing branch-protection doc pair that predates this bead at commit 98bcb0d).

TESTS MUST BITE: 14 sabotages, each a single reverse-editable edit, against the four new test files + tests/acceptance (baseline 109 passed). TWELVE reddened first time (1-3 failures each, all FAILED and never ERROR/no-tests-ran). TWO did not, and both were real test gaps rather than reassurance:
  S3  an unreadable doc counted as empty  -> silent, because the fixture had only 2 documents and the MAJORITY rule then masked the defect. Fixture now has 3; S3 reddens.
  S12 a file target counted as mutable    -> silent, because every wrong-language case tested a DIRECTORY and the is_file branch was unreached. New test for the file branch; S12 reddens.
CLEAN-ROOM REVERT by reverse edit, byte identity re-verified by sha256 on all seven touched files; 109 -> 110 green afterwards.

ADOPTER AXIS (tests/adopter_project.py, S3b): a typescript project renders every doc kind; its own .beadloom/flow/docs/domain.md defines the required sections checked against it; its own scan_paths decide what is inside the mutation scope. beadloom_local_facts_in() is asserted empty on the rendered .beadloom README.

Clean-room pytest: 6422 passed, 3 failed — the same known TestSyncCheckNewPairs one, plus two ai_techwriter seam tests that shell out to a bare 'python' the clean-room venv has no PATH entry for. title: [BDL-061][dev] the Gate's lint line carries neither counter: '12 rules, 0 violations' over inert rules and suppressed crossings
description:
Found while closing beadloom-mr2l.49 and NOT fixed there, because application/gate.py was open in the concurrent agent's wave (beadloom-mr2l.45) and the coordinator's rule for a shared tree is to commit only one's own files.

MEASURED on this repo, 2026-08-23, after .49 landed: `beadloom ci` prints `lint PASS: 12 rules, 0 violations` while `beadloom lint` on the same tree prints `No violations found (12 rules evaluated, 6 crossings suppressed by an exemption)`. The Gate's own summary is the one surface that drops both qualifiers.

application/gate.py:_step_lint builds its summary itself:
    summary = (f"{result.error_count} error(s), {result.warning_count} warning(s)"
               if result.violations
               else f"{result.rules_evaluated} rules, 0 violations")
Two counters already exist on LintResult and are already rendered by the linter's own formatters: rules_inert (BDL-061.48, '13 rules evaluated, 2 of them unable to check anything') and violations_suppressed (BDL-061.49, ', 6 crossings suppressed by an exemption'). Both are dropped here.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN lint: the Gate line is what a pre-push hook and a CI log show, and it is the line a reviewer quotes. .48 named this gap and deferred it ('the gate line still never says the word inert'); .49 named it again. Twice deferred is how a class stays open.

FIX: reuse the linter's existing helpers rather than restating the clauses — `from beadloom.graph.linter import _inert_note, _suppressed_note` (or promote them to public names in the same edit) so the Gate cannot drift from the command it summarises. Both clauses are absent when their count is zero, so the common green line keeps its shape.

TEST: a gate step over a project with (a) one inert rule and (b) one exemption suppressing a real crossing must have both numbers in step.summary; a clean project's summary must be byte-identical to today's.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CLOSED BY beadloom-mr2l.49 (commit e244568), and the bead's own premise was half wrong — measured, not inferred.

THE SUPPRESSED HALF: fixed. application/gate.py:_step_lint now appends the linter's own _suppressed_note(result) to both summary branches, so the Gate reads 'lint PASS: 12 rules, 0 violations, 6 crossings suppressed by an exemption' on this repo. Taken from the formatter rather than restated, so the Gate line cannot drift from the command it summarises.

THE INERT HALF: no clause needed, and this is the correction. An inert rule ALWAYS emits a rule_liveness finding, so rules_inert > 0 implies result.violations is non-empty, which already flips the summary to the '0 error(s), N warning(s)' branch. The clean '<N> rules, 0 violations' branch is unreachable while a rule is inert. .48 observed the same thing from the other side ('an inert rule already flips it'); this bead's framing forgot it. A suppressed crossing is the only counter that can be non-zero with nothing to report — which is exactly why it was the one that hid.

WHY IT WAS FILED AND THEN CLOSED WITHIN THE HOUR: gate.py was the concurrent agent's open file when .49 started, so the finding was filed rather than absorbed. Their commit 189d92f landed mid-bead and left the file uncontended; deferring a third time (.48 named this gap and deferred, .49 named it again) is how a class stays open. Test: TestTheGateSaysItToo in tests/test_exit_condition_expiry.py — one assertion per branch, the clean-line one asserting byte-equality with today's shape so the everyday green line cannot grow a permanent clause.

title: [BDL-061][dev] Register the rule-type count as an audited fact — and fix the misnomer + the unscanned SPEC that would keep it not_covered
description:
BDL-UX #179 asks for the rule-type count to become a docs-audit fact. Measured against the
FIXED audit (beadloom-mr2l.45, 2026-08-24), registering it is necessary but NOT sufficient,
and the two extra pieces are why this is its own bead.

1. THE EXISTING FACT IS A MISNOMER. `rule_type_count` counts ROWS in the `rules` table
   (12 configured rules on this repo), not the loader's NINE dispatch kinds. #179's number
   is the second thing. `DocScanner.FACT_KEYWORDS` maps `rule`, `rule type` AND `rule kind`
   all to that one fact, so registering the dispatch count means splitting the keywords and
   renaming the existing fact — a BREAKING change to `docs_audit.tolerances` and
   `docs_audit.ignore` keys in every adopter's config. Decide the migration deliberately.

2. THE DOCUMENT THAT STATES IT IS NEVER SCANNED. `docs/domains/graph/features/rule-engine/
   SPEC.md` matches the built-in exclude pattern `docs/**/features/*/SPEC.md`. A registered
   fact would read `not_covered` forever while the SPEC drifted — the exact silence #179
   is about. Either the fact must be stated somewhere scanned, or the exclusion must be
   revisited for the file that owns the number. The exclusion is load-bearing (measured:
   shadow-scanning the 33 hidden files yields 17 matches, all false), so this is a real
   design question, not a config tweak.

Both facts are visible today only because BDL-061.45 published the coverage and the scan
surface: `beadloom docs audit --json` -> `coverage.rule_type_count` and `scan_surface`.

Standing rules: TESTS MUST BITE, A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT. Do not solve the
`not_covered` reading with an ignore entry or a tolerance.

title: [BDL-061.52][dev] read-only lint never says the index is older than the tree, and the incremental counter prints zeros for work it did
description:
Two leftovers named by `.6` (F6) and `.7` (MINOR 4) that reached the end of S2 without an owner. Filed together because both are a command reporting a number that is not about what the reader thinks.

F6 - `lint --no-reindex` never says the index is older than the tree. It is the read-only path S2 created (and it IS byte-identical, verified twice), so it is now the honest way to lint - but it answers about the INDEX, not about the working tree, and nothing in its output says which. An adopter wiring it into a gate action gets a verdict about a snapshot of unknown age. Related to #175 in shape: a result that is true about something other than what the caller asked.
FIX DIRECTION: report the index's age or its source revision alongside the verdict, or refuse when the tree has moved since the index was built. Decide which and state the reason - refusing is safer and noisier; reporting is honest and requires the reader to look.

MINOR 4 - the incremental reindex prints a misleading counter. On the run that genuinely re-extracted imports and caught an injected boundary violation, the summary printed `Imports: 0 / Rules: 0`. Cosmetic in isolation, but it is a zero printed by the very command whose honesty this slice restored, and the reader most likely to see it is an agent deciding whether the reindex did anything. Same family as #148: a number that is not about what it appears to be about.

Both want the same question answered once: what is a counter in this tool counting - work done on this run, or total state? Answer it, then make every counter obey the answer.

Standing rules by name: A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT, TESTS MUST BITE.

title: [BDL-061.51][dev] three modules past 1000 lines with many responsibilities each, self-flagged and owned by nobody
description:

  graph/rules/evaluators.py    1019 -> 1181 lines (nine evaluators in one module)
  graph/import_resolver.py     1010 -> 1099 lines (nine language extractors + resolution + edge generation)

title: [BDL-061.41][dev] S3: three more ambient-decode sites, plus an MCP test runner with no timeout
description:
The lower-blast-radius half of `.37`'s 17-call-site sweep (`bd comments beadloom-mr2l.37`). `.37` measured the family but did not measure these three individually and says so - re-measure before fixing, and drop any that does not hold.

- `ai_agents/ai_techwriter/commands.py:54` (`run_command`): `text=True`, no handler. Decodes model and beadloom output - i.e. the AI tech-writer's own inputs, in a repo whose docs are full of em dashes.
- `services/mcp_server.py:731` (`_run_test_suite`): `text=True`, `except FileNotFoundError` only. Decodes pytest output, which in THIS repo contains em dashes and Cyrillic in test names. **It also has NO timeout**, so a wedged pytest hangs the MCP call forever - `bd_seam` bounds its subprocess at 60 s and this does not. The missing timeout is a separate defect from the decode and is arguably the worse of the two; judge it on its own and do not let it ride along as a footnote.
- `onboarding/branch_protection.py:165`: `text=True`, `check=True`, no handler. Decodes a `gh api` JSON response.

ALSO FROM THE SWEEP, worth doing while the file is open: `services/commands/docsync.py:531` (`git ls-files`) has the pattern but cannot bite today - only the returncode is read and the output is one fixed ASCII path. One keyword would make that independent of the content rather than dependent on it staying ASCII. That is cheap insurance against the exact drift this family keeps producing.

CHECKED AND CLEAN in the sweep, recorded so nobody re-checks them: `tui/screens/explorer.py:277` (Popen, no capture, nothing decoded in-process; its `except OSError` is correct) and `services/commands/docsync.py:586` (`git add` - `capture_output` with no `text`, so bytes, no decode).

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
OVERLAP NOTICE from beadloom-mr2l.42 (closed): THE DECODE HALF OF THIS BEAD IS DONE — all four call sites it names are fixed and committed (64cf4f4). THE TIMEOUT IS NOT, and this bead's own sentence about it stands unanswered.

.42 swept src/ with an AST instrument rather than by grep, and the population it found was exactly this bead's four (nothing else in the package omits a codec today), so the sites were fixed at the same time as the ~40 the locale legs reddened. What landed, each with its reason in the code:

- ai_techwriter/commands.py::run_command — encoding="utf-8", errors="replace". `replace` and not `surrogateescape` because this text is DISPLAYED and re-encoded (logs, a PR comment, a JSON parse): a surrogate survives the decode losslessly and then raises on the way OUT, at a site that cannot explain where the byte came from.
- services/mcp_server.py::_run_test_suite — encoding="utf-8", errors="replace" (only the summary line is kept and it is shown to an agent as prose). THE MISSING TIMEOUT IS UNTOUCHED. I judged it out of scope on purpose rather than letting it ride along: it is not a locale defect, .42's acceptance criterion could not see it, and this bead says explicitly it should be judged on its own. A wedged pytest still hangs the MCP call forever while bd_seam bounds its subprocess at 60 s. THIS BEAD SHOULD STAY OPEN FOR IT.
- onboarding/branch_protection.py::_subprocess_runner — encoding="utf-8", errors STRICT, and the load-bearing half turned out to be the one this bead does not mention: `input=stdin` is the protection payload we PUT, so `text=True` was ENCODING it in the image's locale too. A check-run context with one non-ASCII character would raise on an ASCII image and be silently ALTERED on an 8-bit one — i.e. the branch protected with a required check whose name nobody declared. Strict because an outbound payload must never be made lossy to keep a call alive.
- services/commands/docsync.py::_jsonl_is_tracked — this bead's "cheap insurance" suggestion was declined in favour of a smaller change: the call lost text=True altogether. Only the exit status is read, so the decode bought nothing and cost a codec; bytes are the honest type for an answer nobody reads. (That hunk is in 9acfd8d, committed by .58 — it could not be split from a neighbouring change without an interactive add.)

The two sites this bead recorded as CHECKED AND CLEAN were re-checked by the AST sweep and are still clean; the sweep now fails the suite the day any site in src/ omits a codec, so the family cannot come back silently.

title: [BDL-061.35][dev] S3: the scaffolder leaves adopters with untracked churn — no .gitignore entry for the firing record
description:
Review .3 minor n2 (originally m2, unchanged across five fix cycles). S3 scope, alongside M3 and n1.

`scaffold_guard_hooks` writes no `.gitignore` entry for `.beadloom/guard-firings.jsonl`. Verified by the reviewer by grepping the whole of src/: Beadloom writes a .gitignore entry NOWHERE. So from the first guarded edit an adopter gets untracked churn in a file that is append-only and never rotated (m7, also still open).

Two decisions to make and state with reasons, not just outcomes:
- WHERE the entry belongs. Beadloom currently writes none anywhere, so adding one to the guard scaffolder alone makes the flow guards a special case. Either the scaffolder owns it, or `beadloom init` does for the whole `.beadloom/` working set - and the second is the larger change with the better shape.
- WHETHER the record should be ignored at all. It is evidence about what the flow did; a team might reasonably want it committed. If it is ignorable by default, the default needs its reason written down, and it should be overridable.

RELATED AND NOT TO BE FIXED HERE: m7 - `guard-firings.jsonl` has no rotation and `read_firings` parses it whole on every `--liveness`. Ignoring the file makes the growth invisible rather than absent. Name the interaction; do not solve it by hiding it.

ALSO IN S3 AND ADJACENT (n1, original m5): `.claude/settings.json` registers the DIRECT command while the scaffolder emits `.claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh`, so the artifact we ship has never run in this repo. The reviewer's judgement, which the coordinator accepts: that is why #170's narrower binding went unnoticed for five cycles - our dogfood exercises a path adopters do not use. Whoever takes M3 should take n1 with it.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT (pre-commit): both halves implemented and measured.

DECISION 1 - WHERE THE ENTRY BELONGS: `beadloom init`, for the whole `.beadloom/` working set, in a new onboarding component `ignore_block.py` (node `ignore-block`). NOT in the guard scaffolder, and the reason is not tidiness: the entry is a property of the directory Beadloom creates, not of any one feature. Putting it in `scaffold_guard_hooks` would have made the flow guards a special case while leaving the BIGGER churn - the SQLite index - unignored for every adopter, and it would have required EDITING a block written earlier each time a feature is enabled, i.e. Beadloom managing a file it does not own. Measured set, not assumed: on this repo the only paths under `.beadloom/` git does not track are the .db family and guard-firings.jsonl (`git status --ignored`); _graph/, flow.yml, config.yml, flow/, sync-surface.json, metrics_history.json are all SOURCE and stay committable, so the block never covers `.beadloom/` wholesale. Callers: `bootstrap_project` (creates the working set; returns `ignore_added`) and `setup-agentic-flow` (identical whole-set call, for a project initialised by an older Beadloom - which is how a guard adopter on an older init still gets the entry without the scaffolder knowing anything about it). Both PRINT what they wrote; silently editing someone's .gitignore is its own surprise.

DECISION 2 - WHETHER TO IGNORE IT AT ALL: ignored by default, reason written into the adopter's own file rather than only into our docs. Reason: the record is machine-local and append-only, so committing it makes every guarded edit a working-tree change and every branch a conflict on the same last line. It IS evidence and a team may want it committed - so the override is real: the block is written ONCE and a run that finds BLOCK_MARKER does nothing at all, so deleting the line means it never comes back. Rejected alternative and why: a flow.yml key would be the opposite trade - it forces the block to become MANAGED so that flipping the key rewrites somebody's .gitignore, which is the behaviour being avoided. Stated cost of the choice: a pattern added by a later release will not reach a project that already has the block - which is exactly why the block covers the whole working set from the first write.

m7 NAMED, NOT HIDDEN: the ignore entry's own comment says the record is not rotated and `guard --liveness` parses it whole, so ignoring it keeps the growth out of git, NOT off the disk. Same sentence in the flow-guards SPEC and the ignore-block DOC. Filed as bead beadloom-mr2l.56 (P2, parent epic) with the three decisions it has to make (what to bound - bytes/lines/age; whether rotation may lose a firing at all, given that --liveness reads a missing firing as never-fired; and whether the whole-file parse is a separate fix from rotation). Its title carries no bead number (#171).

n1 - THE DOGFOOD NOW RUNS WHAT WE SHIP: chose 'register the emitted script here' over 'drop MultiEdit from the scaffolder', because the divergence was never about the matcher - it was that the shipped artifact had never executed in this repository. `.claude/settings.json` was rewritten BY RUNNING `scaffold_guard_hooks` (direct-command entries removed first), so the file is literally the scaffolder's output, and `.claude/hooks/beadloom-guard.sh` is now committed. Measured live through the emitted adapter, not asserted: `bead-claimed` -> PASS 'in progress: beadloom-mr2l.10, beadloom-mr2l.35' exit 0, `working-branch` -> PASS on 'features/BDL-061-S3' exit 0, both with their not-checked notes, and both appended a firing to the record. Consequence accepted deliberately: this repo now inherits EDIT_MATCHER in full, so #170's surface gap is one we run under rather than one only adopters meet.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT (evidence): TESTS MUST BITE + CLEAN-ROOM REVERT, with numbers.

RED FIRST, per surface:
- tests/test_ignore_block.py: 15 tests. First run was a collection ERROR (no module) - recorded as such, not as a bite; the real bites are below.
- tests/test_guard_hook_adapter.py: the five n1 tests ran RED against the live repo before any fix - 5 failed / 15 passed, named: every_shipped_guard_is_bound_through_the_emitted_adapter, no_guard_is_bound_by_the_direct_command_instead, committed_adapter_is_byte_identical_to_the_emitted_one, committed_adapter_is_executable, live_matcher_is_the_one_the_scaffolder_emits. After the rebinding: 20 passed.
- The three caller tests ran RED before the wiring: 3 failed / 12 passed -> 15 passed after.

SABOTAGE (each reverted by REVERSE EDIT, byte-identity verified by sha256, never git checkout - a neighbour is live in this tree):
1. Marker check disabled (`if False and BLOCK_MARKER in existing`): 1 failed / 14 passed - test_a_deleted_entry_does_not_come_back. That is the OVERRIDE reddening, which is the point. Note test_a_second_run_leaves_the_file_byte_identical did NOT redden, because the already-declared check catches the second run independently - two locks, and the data says which one holds which claim.

title: [BDL-061.34][dev] S2: an unknown key in a guard body is silently ignored — and one not-recorded reason quotes a name nobody typed
description:
Review .3 minor n3, filed as its own bead rather than folded into .5 because this slice just demonstrated how a deferral with no bead disappears: 'worth a bead in S2' was written twice for the exit-3 class and filed zero times.

(b) IS THE REAL ONE. `application/guards/config.py` `_build_spec` silently ignores an unknown key in a guard body. Measured by the reviewer: writing `exclude:` instead of `exclusions:` parses clean with zero exclusions and no signal - the guard then OVER-guards, which is the safe direction. `option:` for `options:` is the UNSAFE direction: working-branch silently falls back to `trunk = \"main\"` and compares against a trunk the project never declared.

The module already rejects unknown guard NAMES and unknown strictness VALUES, for exactly this reason. It does not reject unknown KEYS. That inconsistency is the finding: a typo in the one file an adopter edits by hand quietly changes what is enforced, which is the same family as CONTEXT's decision that an exclusion without `reason`/`until` is a configuration error - 'an unnamed exclusion is how a gate is quietly switched off'.

Mitigation that exists today and should be weighed rather than assumed sufficient: the verdict prints the trunk it compared against, so an attentive reader can notice. Decide whether that is enough for a warn or whether an unknown key is a config error like the others, and state the reason.

(a) IS SMALLER AND IS WORDING. `application/guards/invocation.py` - `beadloom guard` with NO name reports `not_recorded_because: \"'(no guard named)' is not a registered guard, so there is nothing to record it against\"`. The `why` is correct ('no guard was named'); the not-recorded reason quotes a pseudo-name as though the caller typed it. `_named(None)` legitimately returns the placeholder, but `_record` routes the no-name case through the unregistered-name exception. The module docstring lists three recording exceptions; the code has four cases and folds one into another's wording. Fix the routing or fix the docstring - and note the review's own conclusion that none of the three exceptions is a gap wearing a reason, but that the enumeration is off by one.

ALSO CARRIED HERE (coordinator, from .32): the `why` string surfaces raw exception reprs - 'PermissionError: [Errno 13] ...' for an unreadable --project, and \"AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'read'\" for a closed stdin. Fail-closed and honest, but an internal repr sits where a stated cause belongs. Same family as (a).

Standing rules 1, 5, 9 apply. Every behaviour changed needs a test proving it FAILS on the condition it guards.

Your report: two consecutive `sync-check --json` runs on an unchanged tree read 60 stale then 0, with no sync-update between. I could not reproduce that, and while trying I twice reached a WRONG conclusion of my own.

That is BDL-UX #148, filed on 2026-08-05 as a MEDIUM cosmetic issue about `lint`. It is neither cosmetic nor limited to lint: a monitoring surface whose shape depends on whether a human is watching gets sampled by programs and agents and silently hands them the wrong number. I have escalated the entry with this measurement and the rule that follows — the exit code and --json are the only trustworthy contracts today, and any instruction to 'count the stale lines' is unsound.

Your 60-then-0 remains unexplained but is now much less likely to be a product defect: the likeliest cause is that commits landed between your two runs (.44's and your own doc updates), or the same output-shape trap. Not filed as a defect; recorded here so that if it recurs, the next investigator starts from the exit code rather than from the text.

Your decision on the unknown key — configuration ERROR rather than warn — is accepted, and the reason is the right one: the mitigation rode a stdout path the harness shows to nobody, and an unreleased feature cannot turn an adopter's green project red.

comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 10 major

S6 review of .21 / .22 / .78 / .79 / .80. Independently verified: 6927 passed / 11 skipped / 4 xfailed (none of them a BDL-061.22 finding — all five are closed and pinned by passing tests plus a meta-test that they cannot silently become xfail again); `beadloom lint --strict` rc 0; `doctor` rc 0; `sync-check` rc 0; `beadloom ci` rc 0; `diff --since main` = 2 added nodes (review-brief, wave-plan), 2 added edges, 0 removed. Coverage over the new packages 98% (547 stmts, 7 missed). Suite run ONCE and captured (CAPTURE, DON'T RE-RUN).

Standing rules cited by NAME: TESTS MUST BITE · A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT · ABSENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE · CLEAN-ROOM REVERT · CAPTURE, DON'T RE-RUN.

== ON THE MECHANISM I AM THE FIRST USER OF ==
`review-brief` did what it promised for what it can see. Five briefs, withheld counts 5/4/4/4/3 reported rather than hidden, release condition and defeat notice printed each time, and I formed every finding below before running --release. The withholding was NOT defeated by my launch prompt: it carried the bead id, the scope and standing-rule reminders and no author summary — the first review prompt this session written under the new coordinator rule. Two structural defeats found anyway (M1, M2) and one gap the mechanism does not model (see 'Honest limits' at the end).

== MAJOR (10) ==

M1. src/beadloom/application/review_brief/release.py:70-82 — `_marker_in`
ISSUE: the marker is matched at a line start but the COLON is not required, so a checkpoint that merely mentions a review releases the account. The docstring names the exact defeating string as the case it prevents: 'so a checkpoint that MENTIONS a review ("REVIEW ISSUES are still open") does not read as one being recorded.' MEASURED: `release_notes([AuthorNote('REVIEW ISSUES are still open, will fix')])` -> marker='REVIEW ISSUES', released=1, refused=False. A code comment asserting a property the code does not have, in the module whose whole subject is not printing what you did not check.
WHY THE TEST DID NOT BITE: tests/test_cli_review_brief.py:236 uses '... — the REVIEW PASSED comment is still to come', a MID-LINE mention, which the anchor does catch. The test was written to the implementation, not to the stated property (TESTS MUST BITE).
FIX: require the punctuation the role file and REFUSED_NO_VERDICT both instruct — `startswith(f'{marker}:')` — and add the docstring's own string as the regression case.

M2. src/beadloom/application/review_brief/release.py:85-91 — `verdict_recorded`
ISSUE: every comment is scanned regardless of who wrote it, so the AUTHOR releases the author's own account by writing 'REVIEW PASSED:' in a checkpoint. MEASURED: `AuthorNote('COMPLETED: x\nREVIEW PASSED: I checked my own work', author='dev-agent')` -> released. `AuthorNote.author` is populated by _author_notes() from the tracker and never compared — the same shape .80 filed against `waves` ('holds BOTH ids and NEVER COMPARES THEM') and against linter.py:160 ('the diagnosis exists and is thrown away'). One comparison closes it.
FIX: recognise a verdict only from a comment whose author is not the bead's assignee/claimant, or state in release.py's 'Honest limit' section that the gate does not check WHO recorded the verdict. Do not leave the data in hand and unread.

M3. src/beadloom/application/waves/scope.py:53 — `_DECLARATION` narrows a scope silently. RULING ON OBSERVATION BDL-061.22-A, which .80 referred to .23.
ISSUE: this is a defect, not shippable pinned behaviour. `[^\n.;]+` ends the list at ';', '.' or a space, so a second REAL ref is dropped and the bead compares independent of more beads than its true scope does. MEASURED on this repository's own graph: BeadRecord('a','refs: wave-plan; sync-check') and BeadRecord('b','refs: sync-check') -> plan.conflicts == (), ONE wave, 0 findings, exit 0. Two beads that both declared sync-check are placed side by side and the command reports nothing.
This fails OPEN while every other unknown in the same command fails closed (no declaration -> serialise; unknown ref -> serialise). The SPEC's strongest claim, 'An unknown scope is not an empty scope', is defeated by a KNOWN-but-WRONG scope arriving through a separator this project's own prose uses. Same door: `refs: svc.billing` truncates to 'svc' (_REF_TOKEN admits '.', _DECLARATION can never deliver one) — a dotted ref id is unusable, and if 'svc' happens to be a node the bead gets a scope it did not name.
FIX (the repair the test's own docstring already identifies): report a dropped word that IS a node in the graph. That is checkable without guessing at prose, and it turns the silent narrowing into a finding.

M4. src/beadloom/application/waves/scope.py:44-53 — a prose MENTION of `refs:` becomes a declaration.
ISSUE: the comment claims 'a declaration embedded in prose cannot silently swallow the rest of the paragraph as ref ids'. It swallows the next word of the current clause. LIVE ON THIS SLICE: bead .80's description discusses the parser ('An empty `refs:` header adopts a LATER LINE as the bead's scope, because ...') and `review-brief beadloom-mr2l.80` printed `FINDING: unknown-ref: because`. Harmless there only because 'because' is not a node. MEASURED with a real node: the sentence 'It is serialised until it declares `refs: <ref_id>`, sync-check being the example.' resolves to refs=('sync-check',) with unresolved=None — a bead acquires a genuine scope it never declared, reported as fully RESOLVED, and every pairwise verdict then rests on it.
FIX: require the declaration to start a line (or be the whole of a bullet), the way an annotation is required to. Then M3's dropped-word report is the only remaining prose ambiguity.

M5. src/beadloom/services/mcp_server.py:693-701 — one parser, two inputs.
ISSUE: the new comment says 'ONE parser for a bead's declared scope, shared with `beadloom waves` ... Two readings of one declaration is how a tool and a planner come to disagree about what a bead said.' The parser is shared; the COMPOSITION of its input is not. MCP joins the four fields with ' ' while services/commands/waves.py:52-56 and review_brief.py:159-161 join with '\n'. .80's fix (\s -> [ \t] so a dangling `refs:` stops instead of adopting the next line) depends on that newline, and the space-join removes it at the field boundary. The field ORDER differs too (design/description/title/notes vs title/description/design/notes).
MEASURED, identical bead record: newline-join -> declared_refs() == () ('no declaration', correct); space-join -> ('sync-check',). The tool and the planner disagree about what the bead said, which is the exact defect the comment claims to have removed.
FIX: one helper that composes the declaration, imported by all three call sites.

M6. docs/services/cli.md — `beadloom review-brief` is not documented at all.
ISSUE: cli.md is the exhaustive reference (every command carries a '### beadloom X' section; 'review-brief' appears zero times in the file). A new user-facing command with four distinct exit codes (0/1/2/3), --release, --since, --json and a --json payload is absent, while the same slice edited this same file to add a full `waves` section. sync-check flags it — '[warn] docs/services/cli.md (surface drift: watches=cli,graph,flow.yml)' — and surface drift is advisory, so nothing stopped it. Stale docs -> Major.

M7. docs/services/cli.md:1059-1073 — the `waves` worked example predates .80 in its own slice.
ISSUE: the transcript ends at 'No wave runs more than one bead, so nothing is shared concurrently.' Since .80 every plan prints a 'Plan-time precondition of each shared medium:' block, including a fully serial one (three not_applicable + the unconditional tracker-ids verdict). VERIFIED by running `beadloom waves beadloom-mr2l.21 beadloom-mr2l.78 beadloom-mr2l.79`, which prints the block. The prose above the transcript IS updated for the checks; the transcript beneath it was not. This is the class this bead was asked to look for: a later bead in the same slice made an earlier statement false.

M8. src/beadloom/services/commands/review_brief.py:93-132 + application/review_brief/assembly.py:122 — `changed-outside-scope` is measured over the BRANCH and reported as if measured over the BEAD.
ISSUE: `_changed_since` asks git about `<trunk>...HEAD` plus the worktree plus untracked files, i.e. everything the whole slice did. MEASURED on this slice's first real use: all five briefs report the identical 65 files, and four of them raise `changed-outside-scope` naming ~23 files written by a SIBLING bead — .79's brief accuses it of application/waves/*.py (which is .21's work), .22's brief accuses it of everything. The finding cannot distinguish 'this bead went out of scope' from 'this bead has siblings on the branch', and a reviewer who trusts it files a scope finding against the wrong author. That inverts the standing rule the module elsewhere honours: here an UNATTRIBUTABLE fact is printed as an attributed finding.
FIX: no per-bead data exists in the commits, so either narrow it (`--since <the sibling's landing point>`, already available) and say so, or rename the finding for what it measures ('changed-outside-scope, measured over the branch since <ref>: a sibling bead's file appears here'). Do not leave it claiming per-bead attribution it cannot make.

M9. TESTS MUST BITE — two of the five brief findings have no test anywhere.
ISSUE: `grep -rn 'no-declared-scope|FINDING_NO_SCOPE|unknown-ref|FINDING_UNKNOWN_REF' tests/` returns nothing, and coverage confirms it: application/review_brief/assembly.py is 91% with lines 113 and 115 — precisely `findings.append(FINDING_NO_SCOPE)` and `findings.append(f'{FINDING_UNKNOWN_REF}: ...')` — unexecuted. Both are exit-1-bearing outputs, and `unknown-ref` is the one that actually misfired in production on .80 (M4). Every other branch of this package is covered, which is what makes the two gaps notable rather than incidental.

M10. src/beadloom/application/waves/planner.py:197-201 — a finding that the same output contradicts.
ISSUE: the unresolved-scope finding ends 'it is serialised against every bead until it declares `refs: <ref_id>`'. MEASURED: two beads with no declaration plus one `parallel` override -> the plan places both in wave 1 AND prints that sentence for each of them. The override is legitimate and its effect is correctly counted (changed=1, not inert), so the shape is right and only the sentence is wrong. In a command whose subject is not printing claims it does not honour, a finding contradicted by the wave list beside it is the failure in miniature.
FIX: make the clause conditional on the pair not having been overridden, or state the remedy without asserting the current placement.

== MINOR (4) ==
n1. src/beadloom/services/commands/waves.py:12-14 — the module docstring still enumerates exit 1 as 'a bead that did not declare its scope, an override past its exit condition, an override that changed nothing'. .80 added `medium_failed` and `medium_unmeasured` to that population. cli.md and the SPEC were both updated; the docstring was not. Same class as M7, smaller blast radius.
n2. docs/services/mcp.md:403 — 'the first declared ref is the one this tool builds a bundle for'. `declared_refs` returns a SORTED tuple, so `declared[0]` is the alphabetically first ref, not the author's first. MEASURED: 'refs: wave-plan, sync-check' -> ('sync-check','wave-plan'), first = 'sync-check'. Say 'the alphabetically first', or sort at the display layer and preserve author order in the parser.
n3. tests/acceptance/features/wave_plan.feature:42-48 — the scenario is titled 'recorded with its reason and exit condition' and its Then observes only the wave placement and `changed 1 decision`. Neither the reason nor the exit condition is observed anywhere in the suite, and no scenario covers an expired or a blank-field override. The unit tests in test_bead22_wave_guarantee.py DO bite on all of that, so this is a scenario naming more than it asserts, not an untested behaviour.
n4. media_checks._check_working_tree treats `owned` as the nodes' CODE files only, so a wave planned in this repository will report working-tree failed for .beads/*.jsonl and ACTIVE.md on essentially every run. It errs toward safety, which is right, but a check that is always red is a check people learn to scroll past. Consider naming tracker/session files as a stated exclusion rather than letting them accumulate in the failure detail.

== WHAT I CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND ==
- The override path, verified by running it rather than reading about it: parallel flips the decision and reports changed=1; an override the tracker overrules is reported inert (`_earliest_wave` still honours blockers, so a parallel override cannot outrank `bd`); an expired override still applies and says so — which MATCHES the sibling mechanism (graph/rules/exemptions.is_expired keeps applying and files `_expired_finding`), so this is convention, not leniency; blank reason/until are rejected by content via `_is_blank`, closing BDL-061.22-3; unknown keys rejected; `load_overrides` uses yaml.safe_load and reports an undecodable flow.yml as a declaration error rather than a traceback.
- Clause two is genuinely enforced now. `WaveEnvironment` defaults every field to None, None means not observed, and an unobserved medium is `unmeasured` -> a finding -> exit 1. VERIFIED: plan_waves with no environment over a concurrent wave returns exit 1 with three medium_unmeasured findings. `unmeasured` is a fourth verdict rather than a lenient `passed`, which is the point.
- .78's repair is real and is the schema option, not the vocabulary-only option: sync_state.file_symbols_hash added, migration ordered LAST with a stated reason (_migrate_sync_status_verdicts rebuilds from an explicit column list), empty means 'never recorded' and keeps the node-level answer so an un-rebuilt index is not quieter than a rebuilt one, and a file fact is refused where the node is already in drift so the two baselines cannot contradict each other. The exit-code population does not lose signal: the pair naming the NEW file is stale/symbols_changed, only the untouched siblings go unverified/sibling_symbols_changed. media.py, the sync-check SPEC, doc-sync/README, infrastructure/README and reindex/SPEC all describe this accurately, including the measured limit '77 pairs read sibling_symbols_changed with nothing named in details'.
- The commit-scope repair states what it did not judge (`describe()`), refuses to narrow when git is silent (GIT_SILENT), keeps either side of a pair so the doc-only fix commit is not refused, and the hunk it CANNOT catch is both tested (test_a_neighbours_hunk_swept_into_a_staged_file_reads_as_this_commits_work) and written down at sync-check/SPEC.md:342.
- test_bead22_wave_guarantee.py carries a meta-test that every closed FINDING is still named by a PASSING test and is not an xfail. That is the right shape for a findings ledger and I would like to see it copied.
- The scenarios are behaviour-bearing, in the user's vocabulary, with Thens that can fail. No ceremony found.

== HONEST LIMITS OF THE MECHANISM, WHICH ONLY THE REVIEWER CAN REPORT ==
(a) The launch prompt carried no author summary — the coordinator's new rule held on its first outing. But it did carry the coordinator's own observation that 'one such case was caught and fixed inside the slice, which suggests the class is live', which pointed me at M5 and M7. That is author-side knowledge arriving in a wrapper nothing withholds. The mechanism models the AUTHOR's account and the COORDINATOR's paste of it; it does not model the coordinator's own observations of the wave. Naming the paste is a real mechanism because the reviewer is the only observer and now has a duty to report — it worked here — but it is scoped to a summary, and a directed hint is not a summary.
(b) release.py argues 'description-against-comment is structural'. For a FIX bead it is not. Bead .80's description IS a review report of .21 — five numbered findings with their diagnoses — and the brief handed me all of it under 'THE ASSIGNMENT'. That is correct (it is the assignment) and it also means a fix bead's reviewer is converged on the previous reviewer's framing by design. Worth stating in that docstring beside the shell and the paste, rather than leaving 'structural' unqualified.
(c) The three FINDING lines the brief emits go to stderr while the body goes to stdout, so a reviewer piping the brief to a file loses the findings. Not filed — every other command here does the same — but on this command the findings are the part a reviewer is least able to re-derive.

VERDICT: the wave decision is honest in the direction that matters (unknown serialises, media are checked not merely stated, the override carries a reason, an exit condition and a measured effect, and the tracker outranks it). The two open holes are both in the PARSER the decision rests on (M3, M4, and M5 downstream of them), where the failure is toward MORE parallelism, and both in the release gate (M1, M2), where the failure is toward LESS independence. Neither is a redesign. Not passing until they are closed or explicitly deferred with a stated reason.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
REVIEW FINDINGS: amendment after `--release`, per the role file's step 5.

The withheld accounts were read only after the verdict above was on the record. They changed exactly one finding, added three rulings the authors explicitly deferred to this bead, and strengthened one. Revised count: 0 critical, 9 major.

== AMENDED ==
M6 (docs/services/cli.md carries no `beadloom review-brief` section) — WITHDRAWN as a Major against .79 and restated as an outstanding hand-off. .79's account names it precisely: 'docs/services/cli.md (NOT written — the command is absent from the CLI reference and from README/CHANGELOG; that is the tech-writer's surface and it is left open deliberately rather than half-done)', repeated in the close comment. A deliberate deferral with a stated reason and a named owner is a decision, not a defect. It remains OUTSTANDING and must land before the slice ships: the CLI reference is the only surface where a user meets exit code 3, and README/CHANGELOG do not mention the command either. Carry it into the tech-writer wave by name.
This is also the clearest evidence for the mechanism under review: the ordering cost me nothing (the finding was already recorded and cannot be un-said) and the release corrected it, which is exactly what release.py's 'released, not destroyed' paragraph argues for. It worked.

== STRENGTHENED ==
M1 (the verdict marker matches without its colon) — the account raises this from a code-comment error to a claim in the honesty note itself. Under a heading reading 'MECHANISM vs INSTRUCTION — stated exactly, because overstating it is the defect this bead exists to remove', .79 lists under ENFORCED: 'The marker is matched at a LINE START ... so a checkpoint that MENTIONS a review does not open the gate.' MEASURED, before I read that: 'REVIEW ISSUES are still open, will fix' releases the account. The sabotage table confirms why the suite did not catch it — the edit run was 'marker matched anywhere in a comment', which proves the line anchor and never tests the colon.
So this is occurrence number seven of the pattern .79's own description cites as its justification ('six occurrences of an honesty note understating what the code does — every one caught by someone who read the code instead of the summary'). Here the note OVERSTATES rather than understates, in the paragraph written to prevent overstating, and it was caught the same way. The withholding is what made that catchable: had the note been in my prompt I would most likely have accepted 'matched at a LINE START' as the specification instead of probing it.

== THE THREE RULINGS HANDED TO .23, DECIDED ==
R1 — OBSERVATION BDL-061.22-A (the declaration parser narrows rather than refuses), referred here by .22, .21 and .80. RULED: fix it. See M3 above. The trade-off the observation states is real but asymmetric — reading every following word as a ref id found nothing, but the repair the observation itself identifies (report a dropped word that IS a node in the graph) has neither horn: it needs no guess at prose and it fails closed. MEASURED consequence of leaving it: 'refs: wave-plan; sync-check' beside 'refs: sync-check' shares one wave at exit 0 with 0 findings. A command whose one claim is that it DECIDES cannot ship a path where a bead's own declaration is read narrower than it was written and nothing says so.
R2 — OBSERVATION BDL-061.22-B (the tracker-id CHECK is unconditional; should `media_for` also STATE that medium for a wave of one?). RULED: no — leave the statement conditional, as it is. `media_for` answers 'what does CONCURRENCY share', and the id-space race is not carried between concurrent beads: #171 happens at bead CREATION, upstream of any wave, which is precisely why the check is unconditional. Stating it for a wave of one would return the list to the banner that media_for's docstring correctly refuses. The asymmetry is already explained where a reader meets it (_check_tracker_ids' docstring: 'what is stated and what is checked are separate questions'). No change; record the ruling so it is not re-opened.
R3 — .79 left the reviewer this: 'The scenarios are matched by TAG and not verified to assert anything. A scenario that binds and asserts nothing appears in the brief as specification. Judging that is the reviewer's work.' RULED: the 13 bound scenarios assert. Each names something an observer could see in the user's vocabulary ('are in the same wave', 'names "shared_node" over "billing"', 'the brief carries no author comment', 'the plan is not clean'), none restates an implementation call, none has an empty Then. The one weakness is n3 above — a title claiming more than its Then observes — which is a naming defect, not a scenario that cannot fail. The general point stands as a real gap in the BRIEF, though: tag-binding proves a scenario exists, not that it bites, so 'N bound scenario(s)' is a count the reviewer must still open. Worth a line in the review-brief SPEC's honest-limits section.

== ONE FINDING ADDED FROM THE ACCOUNTS (Minor) ==
n5. .78's account states: 'A per-PAIR attestation has no CLI. That is the next honest step and it is unfiled.' The repair makes the freshness fact per-file while attestation stays per-ref, so `sync-update <ref>` still re-baselines every pair of that node — the exact residue #133 is about, now correctly diagnosed and deliberately not closed. A named gap that lives only in a bead comment is a gap that gets lost. File it, the way .80 filed beadloom-mr2l.81 for the swept hunk instead of leaving it in prose.

== WHAT THE ACCOUNTS CONFIRMED, AND WHAT THEY DID NOT TOUCH ==

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TESTS: 46 collected in tests/test_bead22_wave_guarantee.py (37 functions, 41 passing outcomes, 5 strict xfails), unit only — the wave decision is a pure function over an in-memory index, and the CLI surface is already covered by tests/test_cli_waves.py. Coverage on the code under test: application/waves 94% (config.py 78 -> 80+ after the malformed-shape parametrisation), doc_sync/commit_scope.py 95%. Full suite CAPTURED ONCE (CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN): rc 0, 6831 passed / 11 skipped / 9 xfailed, 162 s — 6790 was the baseline, +41 is this file's passing outcomes. Green ON THE TREE, not in a clean room: git status at the time held only .beads/*.jsonl and this one untracked file, so the stronger claim was available and is the one made (#181's typed-green rule).

VERDICT ON THE GUARANTEE — the first clause is ENFORCED, the second is PRINTED.
  First clause (no shared medium carries state between two beads in one wave, for the media the graph decides): holds under every sideways attack tried. Containment serialises in either declaration order; a part_of cycle terminates and still reports the overlap; one absent ref among real ones leaves the WHOLE scope unresolved rather than just the name that was wrong; a ref differing only in case is absent, not matched. Two boundaries are stated and now pinned rather than left in a module docstring: sibling components of one domain are independent (part_of expands downward only, and the most-specific-source rule keeps their files disjoint), and a node BOTH beads reach through depends_on but NEITHER declares is not judged at all.
  Second clause (where a medium cannot give the guarantee, the wave says so and names the one bead that measures the combined outcome): the naming half is enforced — every wave of more than one bead carries a gate_owner drawn from its own members, deterministically, and a sabotage that took the owner from outside the wave reddened it. The saying half is a constant tuple printed by media_for(widest_wave), and it cannot be silenced by adding a serialised neighbour or by an override that BUYS the concurrency. But it is prose: nothing in the plan checks that the working tree was measured, that the commit gate ran scoped, that the doc baseline was reconciled, or that a tracker id matches the id written in its title. The command states four risks and enforces none of them. That is the honest reading of clause two, and it is the answer to the question the bead was written to ask.

WOULD IT HAVE CAUGHT THIS SESSION'S OWN FAILURES?
  #181 (four agents green, tree red): REPORTED, not prevented — and prevention was never the claim. Replayed with four disjoint beads: one wave, one named gate owner, exit 0, and the working-tree statement distinguishes 'clean room over N files' from 'green on the tree'. The step that was in nobody's bead is now in exactly one bead.
  #171 (a valid-but-wrong dependency edge): NOT CAUGHT. Replayed: waves reads blocked_by from the tracker and reproduces the mis-wiring faithfully — right reason (blocked_by_bead), right shape, wrong pair, zero findings, exit 0. There is nothing malformed for it to reject. Worth naming: the CLI already reads the bead's TITLE into the declaration, so it holds both the id the tracker allocated and the id the author wrote into the title, and never compares them. That comparison is the check that would have caught #171 mechanically.
  #118 (parallel agents colliding on the shared hook): the hook fix is real and is pinned against the shipped template rather than a retyped copy — a neighbour's unstaged edit is counted as not judged, and a clean neighbour reads 0. But the concrete failure this session had — a neighbour's hunk swept into a commit because git add -p is unavailable to an agent — is NOT caught and cannot be at this layer: the swept hunk is INSIDE the commit, which is the region the gate judges. Measured on the hook's own scope block: outside reads 0 and staged_py names the file, so the hook prints a confident '0 modified file(s) outside this commit were not judged' over a commit containing someone else's work.
  The two beads this session actually ran concurrently (.21 and .72): replayed with the declarations they carried — none — the command serialises them at exit 1 with one finding per bead. The command was right and was not consulted.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
FINDINGS — five, each measured, each shipped as a strict xfail whose docstring names it (the convention .18 set). A strict xfail turns red the moment it is fixed, so none of these can be closed silently, and none of them is prose in a report nobody re-measures.

BDL-061.22-1 — an override the tracker overrules reports 'changed 1 decision(s)'.
  _apply_overrides deletes a blocked_by_bead conflict and counts one change. _assign then places the blocked bead after its blocker anyway, through _earliest_wave, which reads the blockers directly rather than the conflict set. MEASURED: the wave shape is byte-identical with and without the override, and it is reported as effective, is not inert, and raises no finding. OverrideOutcome.inert exists because 'an override nobody can see doing anything is how a check gets switched off without anybody saying so' — this is one nobody can see doing anything. Fix: count decisions the SHAPE changed, or compare the shape with and without.

BDL-061.22-2 — the same dead override is caught in one direction and not the other.
  A parallel override about beads the plan does not contain finds no conflict to delete, counts zero, and is correctly inert. A serial one about the SAME absent beads CREATES a conflict, counts it, and is reported as having changed a decision. MEASURED: plan.conflicts then carries a pair nobody asked about, and beadloom waves prints it under 'Serialised because:' beside the real serialisations, where a reader cannot tell them apart. A stale override left behind after its beads closed is the ordinary route in — the entry .48 had to learn to report.

BDL-061.22-3 — a blank-but-present reason and until are accepted.
  config.py rejects a missing key with 'not entry.get(key)', which catches '' and null and passes '   '. The value is then stripped to '', so the loader returns an override whose reason is empty and whose until has no deadline — and no deadline means WaveOverride.expired is False forever. The error message the loader would have printed names this exact outcome: 'an unnamed, undated override outranks the graph permanently by accident'. MEASURED: it loads, and the CLI renders '(until )'. This is .49's shape on a third surface: an exit condition present in the file and absent in effect.

BDL-061.22-4 — the hook's unjudged count omits a neighbour's new file.
  outside=$(git diff --name-only | wc -l) lists tracked files with unstaged modifications. A neighbouring agent's brand-new module is untracked and is not listed. MEASURED in a real git repository with one tracked neighbour edit and one untracked neighbour module: the hook reports 1. Both sides: the word printed is 'modified', and an untracked file is literally not modified, so the line is not a lie — but the line exists to state the unjudged remainder, and a new module is the largest unjudged thing a neighbour can leave in a shared tree. git status --porcelain answers both in one call. A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT applies to this count too.

BDL-061.22-5 — an empty 'refs:' header adopts a later line as the bead's scope. NEW, found by the test rather than by reading.
  _DECLARATION is \b(?:refs?|area)\s*:\s*([^\n.;]+). The comment above it says the list ends at the first newline, and the CAPTURE does — but the \s* between the colon and the capture matches newlines, so a dangling refs: skips forward to the next non-empty line, across a blank line, and reads THAT as the declaration. MEASURED: 'Scope\nrefs:\nbilling is the one we mean' resolves to ('billing',), and 'refs:\n\nshipping' resolves to ('shipping',). The harmless case is an adopted word that is not a node — unresolved, serialised, fail-closed. The case that costs is the one measured: the adopted word IS a node, so the bead is handed a RESOLVED scope it never declared and every pairwise verdict rests on it. A dangling refs: left by a template is the ordinary way a bead acquires one. Fix: anchor the separator to spaces and tabs rather than \s.

TWO OBSERVATIONS, pinned as behaviour rather than filed as defects because the trade-off runs both ways. .23 is where they are ruled on.
  A — the declaration parser NARROWS a scope rather than refusing it. 'refs: billing; shipping' and 'refs: billing shipping' both resolve to ('billing',). Every other unknown in this command fails closed; this one fails open, and a narrower scope compares independent of more beads than the true one does. Against fixing it: a declaration is written inside prose, and reading every following word as a ref id found nothing at all — which is why the first-word rule exists. The narrow repair available is to report a dropped word that IS a node in the graph, which is checkable without guessing at prose.
  B — serialising a wave withdraws the only caution about the id space. media_for returns nothing for a wave of one. For three of the four media that is right. It is not right for tracker-ids: #171's mis-wiring happened at bead CREATION, before any wave ran, and a plan that serialises the beads it mis-wired is exactly the plan whose ids most need checking. The caution is withdrawn by the failure it describes. Against fixing it: a command that decides concurrency should state what concurrency costs, and printing a creation-time caution on a fully serial plan is scope creep.

TESTS MUST BITE — six sabotages, each reddening named tests, each reverted by REVERSE EDIT (never git checkout, the tree is shared) and verified sha256-identical against a pre-recorded manifest:
  1. media_for threshold >1 -> >2                       -> 2 FAILED (both silencing tests)
  2. part_of expansion stops at the roots               -> 4 FAILED (containment both orders + 2)
  3. unresolved scopes stop being findings              -> 2 FAILED (.21/.72 replay + forced-parallel)
  4. the hook counts the commit instead of the tree     -> 2 FAILED (both real-git scope tests)
  5. a medium cites an issue absent from the UX log     -> 2 FAILED (log cross-check + #181 replay)
  6. gate_owner taken from outside the wave             -> 1 FAILED (the gate-owner test)
  All six reverts byte-identical (shasum -a 256 -c, four files, OK).

MUTATION TESTING: ZERO mutants ran. No runner is installed (mutmut and cosmic-ray both absent) and Beadloom deliberately ships none. Reported as zero, never as clean. The six hand-applied mutations above are stated as hand-applied and are not a substitute for a run.

NOT COVERED, stated so it is not mistaken for covered: no test drives the real bd binary (the CLI seam is a double, and tests/test_bd_seam.py owns the real one); no test runs the installed pre-commit hook end to end — the two commit-gate tests execute the hook's OWN scope block, imported from _HOOK_COMMIT_SCOPE rather than retyped, so a copy cannot stay green while the hook drifts, but the ruff/mypy/sync-check legs below it are not exercised; concurrency is simulated as data, never as two real processes.

title: [BDL-061.21][dev] S6: beadloom waves decides; review isolation; #118, #133
description: beadloom waves <bead>... DECIDES parallelism from code-level independence of the beads' node scopes (Q6 — advisory is the failure this epic removes). A human override is recorded as an exclusion with reason and exit condition.
