comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT — S6 core: `beadloom waves` + #118, and the two beads this one was split into.

THE SENTENCE THE SHAPE GUARANTEES (written into `application/waves/__init__.py`, the SPEC and ACTIVE.md, because half of it is not decidable from the graph):
  For any two beads placed in the same wave, no medium they share can carry one bead's
  in-progress state into the other's result — and where a medium cannot give that guarantee,
  the wave says so and names the one bead that measures the combined outcome.

Code independence is the half the graph decides (#155 A). The other half is what THIS session
measured: one working tree (#181), one pre-commit hook (#118), one doc baseline (#182/#133),
one tracker id space (#171). No choice of shape makes any of those independent, so a wave of
more than one bead PRINTS them with their evidence and assigns a `gate_owner`.

SIZE JUDGEMENT, MADE BEFORE WRITING CODE AND CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT — three beads, not one.
  .21 (this one): the wave decision + #118. They ship together because a wave the tooling then
      breaks IS an advisory wave shape, which is the failure the decision exists to remove.
  .78: #133/#182 — the doc-baseline vocabulary. Split on a measurement taken here (below).
  .79: #155 C reviewer isolation — shares no module with the wave decision; it changes what a
      role is HANDED, not which beads may run at once.

WHAT SHIPPED
  src/beadloom/application/waves/  — six cohesive modules, one nameable responsibility each:
    models.py       the vocabulary (records, scopes, conflicts, overrides, waves, media)
    scope.py        resolve a bead to the nodes and files it occupies
    independence.py decide whether one pair may run together, and say why not
    media.py        what a wave shares no matter how independent its code is
    planner.py      assign beads to waves, apply overrides, report findings
    config.py       read and validate the declared `waves:` overrides
  src/beadloom/services/commands/waves.py — the CLI: `beadloom waves <bead>... [--json]`
  src/beadloom/doc_sync/commit_scope.py   — which pairs a commit is about (#118)
  `beadloom sync-check --staged`          — the commit-scoped run, with the count it left out
  both pre-commit hook templates          — judge the commit; state the tree they did not judge

DECISIONS TAKEN (each with its reason)
1. A bead declares its scope in the tracker: `refs: <ref_id>[, <ref_id>]` (also `ref:`, `area:`).
   Reason: it is the convention the MCP `bead_context` tool already reads, and it makes "declare
   what you occupy" the price of running in parallel. `bead_context` now reads through the SAME
   parser (`application.waves.declared_refs`) rather than its own — one fact, one source, which
   is the defect #171/#177/#179 all record.
2. A scope expands DOWNWARD through `part_of`. Reason: a node's own file set deliberately
   excludes a nested node's files, so without the expansion a domain-scoped bead and a
   component-scoped bead compare independent while editing the same package.
3. An unresolved scope serialises against EVERY bead, and is a finding with its remedy.
   Reason: an unknown scope is not an empty scope, and an empty one compares independent of
   everything — the command's whole claim would rest on silence. This is the single most
   load-bearing line in the bead.
4. One reason per serialised pair, from a closed named vocabulary, tried in reader order:
   blocked_by_bead > unresolved_scope > shared_node > shared_file > dependency_edge >
   override_serial. Reason: the pair is already serialised and a second reason changes nothing;
   a verdict spelled at its call site becomes several spellings of one fact.
5. Only `depends_on` makes two scopes non-independent — not `touches_code`, not contracts.
   Reason: it is the only edge kind that says one node's change reaches the other. Stated as
   what was NOT checked: transitive reach through an unchanged intermediate node is not judged,
   because on a real graph everything reaches infrastructure and the answer would be "serialise
   everything".
6. Greedy colouring in tracker-topological order (Kahn, sorted ready set), NOT optimal packing.
   Reason: the shape has to be the SAME shape every time it is computed, so two agents reading
   one plan act on one decision. A pinned determinism test holds it.
7. `gate_owner` per wave, assigned deterministically (last bead in sorted order).
   Reason: #181 — the combined-tree run "is currently in nobody's bead". Assigned wisely is not
   available; assigned to a NAMED bead is, and that is the whole content of the fix.
8. A human override is an exclusion with `reason` + `until`, and reuses `exit_condition_deadline`
   — the third surface making that promise, after the guard exclusions and the `forbid_import`
   exemptions. An override that changed NO decision is reported inert and is a finding, the same
   rule as `rules_inert` and `working_reach`.
9. Exit codes, never line counts (#148): 0 clean, 1 decided-with-findings, 2 undecidable. The
   human shape and `--json` carry the same counts, and neither depends on a TTY.
10. #118 is repaired with a BOUNDARY, not a tolerance: the commit gate judges the commit, the
   push gate judges the tree. Nothing stops being enforced — `beadloom ci` still runs over
   everything pre-push — what moves is WHEN a pair is judged.
11. What #118's fix does NOT check is stated in the hook itself: the content read is the
   WORKING-TREE content of the staged paths, not the staged blobs, so a partially staged file is
   judged including the part the commit leaves behind.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT — measurements, sabotage results, and one defect found on the way.

MEASURED, ON THIS BEAD'S OWN TREE — the evidence that split .78 out:
  Adding ONE package (`application/waves/`) made `beadloom sync-check` report 72 stale pairs.
  Ten of them had a file this tree had modified. Fifty-two were `docs/domains/application/README.md`
  paired against files nobody touched, because `symbols_hash` is stored per `ref_id`.
  Reaching a fixpoint cost 3 genuine document revisions and 65 deliberate re-attestations
  (`sync-update application/doc-sync/sync-check --yes`, pointwise, never `--all`).
  That is #182's mechanism exactly, and #133 is the same defect seen at wave-integration time:
  the per-worktree baseline is the OCCASION, the per-node hash is the CAUSE. The repair needs a
  verdict-vocabulary decision (per-file hashing, or `sibling_changed`/`unaffected` as a distinct
  word) that changes sync-check's exit-code population and every surface that prints it.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED WHILE WIRING `--staged` (not in the bead's scope, one line, worth naming):
  `pair_count` — the DECLARED surface compared against the committed `.beadloom/sync-surface.json`
  — was computed AFTER the `--ref` filter. Measured: `beadloom sync-check --ref sync-check` on
  this repository printed `declared surface SHRANK since it was recorded: 322 -> 6 pair(s)`, and
  `--record-surface` would have written that 6 into the committed ledger. `--staged` would have
  done the same on every commit. The count is now taken BEFORE any narrowing; both flags restrict
  what is REPORTED and neither says the project declared less. Pinned by
  `TestTheDeclaredSurfaceIsNotNarrowedByAReportFilter`.

TESTS MUST BITE — five sabotages, each reddening named tests, each reverted by REVERSE EDIT and
verified sha256-identical (never `git checkout`, the tree is shared):
  1. unresolved scopes stop conflicting -> 3 FAILED (TestUnresolvedScope + 2 scenarios)
  2. `staged is None` reads as "nothing staged" -> 1 FAILED (test_a_silent_git_narrows_nothing)
  3. the hook drops `--staged` -> 2 FAILED (both hook modes)
  4. `beadloom ci` invoked inside pre-commit -> 1 FAILED (the sharpened Gate-absence assertion)
  5. the tracker-topological order dropped -> 2 FAILED (both ordering tests)
  All five reverts: byte-identical. A collection ERROR was the first RED (the module did not
  exist); every later RED was a FAILED with named tests and compared counts.

ONE EXISTING ASSERTION SHARPENED, NOT WEAKENED (stated because editing a test to pass is the
thing this project forbids): `test_pre_commit_*_still_has_full_checks` asserted
`"beadloom ci" not in content`, a substring proxy for "the Gate is not invoked here". The hook's
new remediation line NAMES `beadloom ci` while not running it, so the proxy could no longer tell
the two apart. It is now `_runs_the_gate(content)`, which reads the COMMAND POSITION and also
catches `uv run beadloom ci` — a case the substring proxy would have passed. Sabotage 4 above is
the proof it bites.

TWO NUMBERS UPDATED IN EXISTING TESTS, both real consequences of this bead:
  - `tests/test_bead77...`: AS-IS population 93 -> 94 (the new `wave-plan/SPEC.md`). It is a
    denominator, not a constant, and it moves when the repository gains a document.
  - `tests/test_s4_cli_decomposition.py`: `waves` added to EXPECTED_COMMANDS. It caught the new
    command, which is what the surface test is for.

TWO PRD CRITERIA NOW RESOLVE, TWO DELIBERATELY DO NOT. The S6 scenarios were named to match
PRD US-6's referenced criteria exactly ("Two beads touching independent subgraphs are allowed to
run in parallel", "Two beads touching the same node are serialised"), so `scenario-coverage`
stops reporting them. US-6's other two references — the reviewer's input, and the wave-integration
re-baseline — still report, and that is correct: they are `.79` and `.78`, and the Gate naming
what has not shipped is the mechanism working.
  NOTE FOR REVIEW: PRD US-6 classifies #118 as "Non-behavioral". It is not — `sync-check --staged`
  has observable behaviour and now carries three executable scenarios in
  `tests/acceptance/features/commit_scope.feature`. The PRD is an approved TO-BE document, so the
  classification is left for `.24`/review to correct rather than edited here.

DOGFOODED ON THIS EPIC'S OWN BEADS:
  `beadloom waves beadloom-mr2l.21 beadloom-mr2l.72` -> exit 1, two waves, and the reason was
  `unresolved_scope` for BOTH: neither bead had declared what it occupies. The coordinator ran
  them concurrently anyway. That is the command refusing to bless a wave it cannot justify.
  `beadloom waves beadloom-mr2l.78 beadloom-mr2l.79` -> exit 0, `.78` then `.79`, serialised on
  `dependency_edge: cli-commands -> doc-quality` — `.79` edits the CLI, which depends on the
  doc-sync domain `.78` rewrites. A decision no tracker could have made.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
API CHANGE: three additions and one behaviour change on an existing flag path.

NEW COMMAND — `beadloom waves BEAD [BEAD ...] [--json] [--project DIR]`
  Exit 0 = decided and clean; 1 = decided with findings (unresolved scope / expired override /
  inert override), visible and non-blocking; 2 = undecidable (no index, no tracker answer, an
  unknown bead, a `waves:` block that will not parse).
  `--json` keys: beads, waves[{index,beads,gate_owner}], scopes[], conflicts[], overrides[],
  shared_media[], findings[], exit_code.

COMPLETED — commit acdd725 on features/BDL-061-S5. 16 files, docs only; no src/, no tests/.

=== THE GUIDE LEADS WITH THE DECISION, because every mechanism follows from it
docs/guides/document-kinds.md now opens on the three spaces and is retitled "Document Kinds,
Documentation Spaces and the Writing Standard". The lead is the decision, not the vocabulary:
TO-BE / AS-IS / WORKING deliberately not TODO/DONE, because NOTHING CHANGES STATUS. A PRD is
not a task that becomes done; it stays the record of what was intended while a DIFFERENT
artifact is written to describe the new reality. Hence the checkable claim is a RELATION
between two artifacts rather than a flag on one — a flag has nothing to be verified against
(`status: done` is true because somebody typed it and no later change to the code can make it
false), a relation has both ends on disk and in the graph.
Nine sub-sections follow from it, in the order the decision forces: what each space is for;
kind wins over root and a disagreement is a finding; configuring the spaces; the relation;
what the relation does NOT check; the WORKING exemption as a declaration; two stated limits;
and an adopter checklist for a project that is not Beadloom.

REVIEW BDL-061.19 (S5) — NOT PASSING: 0 critical, 3 major, 3 minor. `.75`'s resolution: I would ship it.

Verified read-only at HEAD aed43c9, plus a clean room built from `git archive HEAD` with its own
git history (`beadloom` driven with `--project`). Exit codes and `--json` only (#148).

=== WHAT HOLDS, RECOUNTED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED ===

THE POPULATION, third independent recount. I recomputed all nine denominators from `os.walk`,
`.beads/issues.jsonl` and a read-only sqlite read of `.beadloom/beadloom.db`, spelling out
kind-then-root and the glob semantics myself — no import of `doc_roots` or `doc_spaces`. Exact
match on every one: to_be 190 / as_is 93 / working 55; epics 61; declaring 5; unresolved 56
(52 `no_node_declared` + 4 `no_intent_document`: BDL-009, BDL-010, BDL-016, development);
tracker-unnamed 24; epics_with_closed_beads 37; refs_checked 17; findings 2 (BDL-030
`epic_not_in_tracker`, BDL-061 `intent_without_as_is`). `.73`'s three moved numbers (57->61,
52->56, 20->24) are correct. Reproduced identically in the clean room, so the recount is not
repo-path-dependent.

`.claude/development` IS INSIDE THE POPULATION NOW. Its two documents are among the 190, its
directory is the 61st epic, and it is named in both NOT CHECKED clauses (`4 carry no readable
intent document`, and by key in `24 epic(s) the tracker does not name`). The half of this bead's
criterion the population question was about is delivered. The other half — ROADMAP and issue log
as validated KINDS with computed facts — is `.72` and is not built, so the bead's own sentence
is still not satisfiable by this branch. That is the split `.17` made, not a defect of it.

PLW1514 IS CONFIGURED, NOT ONLY DOCUMENTED. `preview = true`, `explicit-preview-rules = true` and
the `PLW1514` selection are all live in pyproject.toml. Measured, not read: a probe module with
`open(p)` + `p.read_text()` gets 2 `unspecified-encoding` findings from `uv run ruff check`;
`test_the_selection_is_not_inert` asserts ruff's `has no effect because preview is not enabled`
is absent from stderr, which is the exact false-green the three settings exist against.

`.70` DID NOT UNDERSTATE — this is the one place in this epic where the honesty note is exact. I
recomputed the corpus: 232 goal statements read, 31 name no witness, 11 state an unbounded
improvement, 4 flagged, so the recall gap is 27. The SPEC says "27 name no witness either" and
names the trade. Measured number matches the published number.

Suite: 195 passed over the eight slice files, 0 xfail left (all 12 filed findings closed).
ruff rc 0, mypy --strict rc 0 (205 files), lint --strict rc 0, doctor rc 0. New modules carry
`# beadloom:domain`/`component` and both have component docs. No bare except, no `os.path`, no
`yaml.load`, no f-string SQL. Acceptance scenarios are behaviour in an observer's vocabulary with
real assertions, tagged per bead — not ceremony. The 11 advisory `surface_drift` reference
documents were not counted against this slice.

=== MAJOR 1 — the population's THIRD hole. Kind wins over root, and a document whose kind's space has no matching root falls out of EVERY count ===

FILE: src/beadloom/infrastructure/doc_roots.py:212 (`documents_in`) with :179 (`space_of`).

ISSUE. `documents_in(root, space)` globs a space's own roots and then KEEPS only what
`space_of` returns to that same space. When kind moves a file to a space whose roots do not match
it, no other space's glob will find it either, so the file is in no population, its directory is
in no epic list, and nothing reports the drop. `.73` fixed "a TO-BE directory with a TO-BE
document but no intent document"; this is one classification step earlier and it is worse,
because there the documents at least stayed in the 190.

MEASURED in the clean room at HEAD, both directions, each with a passing control:
  - `.claude/development/docs/features/ZALPHA/README.md` (a planning directory whose only
    document is an AS-IS kind): to_be 190 -> 190, as_is 93 -> 93, working 55 -> 55, epics
    61 -> 61, absent from `unresolved_epics`. CONTROL: the same file renamed `CONTEXT.md`
    -> to_be 191, epics 62. The only thing holding that directory in the population is a stem.
  - `docs/PLAN.md` (a TO-BE kind under the AS-IS root): to_be 190, as_is 93 — in nothing.
    CONTROL: `docs/notes.md` -> as_is 94.

WHY IT MATTERS TO AN ADOPTER, not to us. Feature folders named `README.md` / `SPEC.md` /
`DOC.md` are an ordinary convention. Such a project loses 100% of its epics AND their documents,
and the gate prints either a plausible small count or the NAMED skip `skipped — no TO-BE
document matches …` — which reads as a correctly-configured project with no intent recorded.
That is the same sentence `.73` wrote about `_INTENT_DOCUMENTS` being hardcoded, and TRUE HERE IS
NOT TRUE: it is invisible on this repository because our stems happen to agree with our roots.

WHY `.18`'S RECOUNT SUITE CANNOT SEE IT. `TestTheDenominatorsAreRecomputable` recomputes
kind-then-root independently, so it reproduces the drop faithfully and agrees. An independent
recount of the same RULE cannot find a hole in the rule. So can mine — I found this by planting
a file, not by counting.

RECOMMENDATION. Pin the invariant the counts must satisfy, not the counts:
`sum(populations) == |files matched by any declared root|` on any tree. Today it does not hold.
Then either keep a file its root FOUND when kind sends it to a space with no matching root, or
report it — a `document_in_no_space` finding with a count, the way every other absence in this
slice now reports itself. Absence is not evidence.

=== MAJOR 2 — a HALF-inert WORKING declaration reports nothing, and the DOC says it does ===

FILES: src/beadloom/application/doc_spaces.py:570 (`... and not working_docs`);
docs/domains/application/components/doc-spaces/DOC.md ("declared kinds **or roots** that no
document matches").

ISSUE. Liveness is asked of the declaration as a whole, not of each declared item. If ANY
document lands in WORKING, every other half of the declaration is silently inert.

MEASURED in a fresh clean room, with 39 `SPEC.md` documents in the tree:
`doc_roots.working: {exempt_from_freshness: true, reason: "...", kinds: [ACTIVE, SPEC]}`
-> as_is 93 (unchanged), working 55 (unchanged), `sync-check --json` `exempt: 0`, and
`docs spaces --json` reports ZERO `working_exemption_inert`. The SPEC half does nothing and
nothing says so. CONTROL that passes: `kinds: [SPEC]` alone -> working 0 -> the finding fires.
So the check only ever sees the all-or-nothing case, while its documentation promises per-item.

CAUSE — and it is the saturated signal you asked me to look for. `DocSpaces.space_of_kind`
iterates `SPACES`, whose own docstring says it is "every space, in the order a report reads best",
and returns the first space claiming the kind. So AS-IS's DEFAULT kind list shadows a project's
explicit WORKING declaration. `.75` gave roots a deliberate `_ROOT_PRECEDENCE` with a paragraph
of rationale ("if the catch-all won, a declaration a project wrote in the file we tell it to edit
would be silently inert"). Kinds got no such decision and reuse a reporting-order constant as a
classification precedence — one constant asked to mean two things, which is `.74`'s `not_verified`
one module over. It fails CLOSED here rather than open, which is why it is Major and not P0.

RECOMMENDATION. A `_KIND_PRECEDENCE` constant with its own stated reason, separate from `SPACES`;
and liveness per declared item — name each declared kind and each declared root that matched no
document, rather than firing only when the whole declaration matched nothing.

=== MAJOR 3 — one `beadloom ci` run prints two incompatible readings of the word "exempt" ===

FILES: src/beadloom/application/gate.py:596; src/beadloom/services/commands/docs.py:863;
docs/domains/application/features/ci-gate/SPEC.md (which reproduces the line verbatim).

MEASURED on this repository: `sync-check --json` summary is `exempt: 0` — 0 of 330 pairs were
excused — while the `doc-spaces` line of the same gate reads `55 WORKING document(s) exempt`
and `docs spaces` prints `55 WORKING document(s) exempt from freshness — <reason>`. Two adjacent
lines of one run; one says nothing was excused (by omission, correctly, since `.76`), the other
says 55.

`.75`'s own comment named this — "a count of documents, not of excused pairs … it is true and it
is not the number a reader will take from it" — and it was neither fixed nor filed as a bead, so
it survives only in a closed bead's prose. This is the shape `_sync_summary`'s docstring exists
against (#174/#175) reappearing one line below the place `.76` just repaired it, and the SPEC now
documents the misleading line without the caveat.

RECOMMENDATION. Say what the number is: `55 WORKING document(s) in the exempt space; 0 sync
pair(s) excused`. The pair count is already computed by the sync-check step in the same run.

=== MINOR ===

MINOR 1 — src/beadloom/services/commands/docs.py:820,856. `_spaces_json`/`_spaces_rich` take
`report: object` and pay 27 `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` for it — 27 of the repository's 61
total, added by this branch. The file already imports `TYPE_CHECKING` (line 9) and has a block at
line 13; importing `SpacesReport` there removes all 27. There is in-file precedent
(`surface: object`, `result: object`) but no stated reason, and CONTEXT forbids an escape hatch
without one.

MINOR 2 — the `docs-quality` gate line prints `measurable-goal 4` and never the 27 goals the
re-scope stopped deciding about. The SPEC states it and my recount confirms it exactly, so this
is not an understatement — it is a report that omits what its own SPEC admits, which is A GREEN
COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT. The line already has the machinery: `NO CHECK READS: BRIEF, PLAN,
SUMMARY` is the same clause shape.

MINOR 3 — docs/domains/application/components/doc-spaces/DOC.md closes with "Public surface
verified against `doc_spaces.py`", and the list is short of it: `check_spaces` and
`spaces_report` are shown without the `tracker_source` argument `.74` added, and the constants
omit `FINDING_INTENT_UNREADABLE`, `FINDING_EPIC_NOT_IN_TRACKER`, `TRACKER_BD`/`TRACKER_EXPORT`/
`TRACKER_UNREADABLE`, the three `UNRESOLVED_*` and `jsonl_records`.

=== `.75` — SECOND OPINION, ASKED FOR EXPLICITLY. SHIP IT ===

The design question is whether honouring a declaration is right and the defect was only that no
reader objected. It is right, and the fix reaches the whole silenced set rather than part of it —
which is the thing worth checking and which I measured rather than reasoned about.

CLEAN ROOM, `doc_roots.working.roots: [docs/**/*.md]` with a reason: 28 of 330 pairs go `exempt`,
and `docs spaces --json` names 6 `working_declaration_contradicted` — exactly the 6 documents
behind those 28 pairs. Coverage is COMPLETE, not partial, and structurally so: a sync pair exists
only for a document the graph declares, and the contradiction fires on precisely
`working_documents ∩ declared_doc_paths`. Both readers agree on the spelling now, which is what
was broken. Before `.75` the same configuration reported 0.

TWO RESIDUALS I would state in `.20` rather than block on.

(a) `beadloom ci` stays rc 0, because `_step_doc_spaces` is `passed=True` unconditionally
(gate.py:600). So an adopter who declares a WORKING root gets a green gate and a warn. That is
the epic's own shipped-as-warn constraint applied consistently, not a regression — but it means
the answer to "does an adopter still get a green gate they should not have" is YES, with the
objection printed. I accept that trade because the alternative breaks "no adopter's green project
turns red on upgrade", and because the sync-check line — the step that DOES block — now states
the count and the reason instead of letting it fall silently, which is the actual `.76` repair.

(b) The only thing stopping a one-line `working.roots: [docs/**/*.md]` from taking a whole
project's freshness gate to warn-only is that kind wins for `SPEC`/`DOC`/`README`. That is a
property of the shipped kind list, not a guard. An adopter whose documents are `architecture.md`,
`getting-started.md`, `ci-setup.md` — no AS-IS stem anywhere — has every one of them excused by
that single line. Worth a sentence in the kinds guide.

=== NOT CLOSING ===

Three Major findings, and this bead's own criterion still needs `.72`. Recommend: fix Major 1 and
Major 2 in `application/doc_spaces.py` + `infrastructure/doc_roots.py` (they share the
classification seam and belong in one bead), Major 3 in `gate.py`/`docs.py` with the SPEC line,
and let `.20` carry the two `.75` residuals into the kinds guide.

comments.text:
COORDINATOR — verdict, and it is mine to give because the reviewer left the bead open deliberately.

ALL THREE MAJORS ARE CLOSED BY .77, and I verified the two that mattered myself through the CLI:

M1 (kind wins over root, document falls out of every count) — closed as an INVARIANT rather than as the third patch, which is what I asked for and the reason I asked: this population had already failed three times (.17's first denominator silently dropped 34 epics; .18 found four directories falling out for carrying no intent document; you planted a README-only directory and found a third route). It now holds `sum(populations) == |files any declared root matched|` on any tree, and the disagreement is itself a `document_outside_declared_root` finding. Your two probes were re-planted and measured: to_be 190→191, as_is 93→94, epics 61→62, two findings, where both files had previously been in nothing. And a space that declares no root contradicts nothing, so our 55 ACTIVE.md stay silent — the invariant did not become noise.

M3 — reproduced, in the split form I suspected and could not produce myself: `sync-check --json` read `exempt: 0` while `docs spaces` printed 55, and inside one `ci` run only the second half appeared. Fixed at the seam rather than in the formatting: the gate line now carries both numbers under different names (`55 WORKING document(s) in the exempt space, 0 sync pair(s) excused`) because they are different facts, and `docs spaces` — which runs no freshness check — returns `null` instead of a number it never measured. That is 'unknown is not zero' reaching the tool's own output.

M2 (half-inert working.kinds) closed reusing the existing vocabulary rather than inventing a third, as required.

YOUR VERDICT ON .75 IS ACCEPTED, and the reason you gave is better than the one I had. I accepted it on 'honouring a declaration is the design'; you measured that the 28 excused pairs map onto exactly the 6 documents it names, so the coverage is STRUCTURAL rather than partial. That is a different quality of argument and it settles the residual doubt I had.

Your two routed residuals — `ci` stays rc 0, and only the default kind list stops a one-line whole-tree silencing — are in .20's guide as stated limits, not omissions.

Closing. Tree: 6702 passed, 0 failed, `beadloom ci` rc 0.

comments.text:
TESTS: 62 new in tests/test_bead18_s5_relation.py — 50 unit/integration passing + 12 xfail(strict=True) findings. Suite 6544 -> 6594 passed, 0 failed, 16 xfailed (4 pre-existing), captured to a file and read (CAPTURE DON'T RE-RUN). Coverage on the slice's two modules: application/doc_spaces.py 97%, infrastructure/doc_roots.py 96%, combined 96% statements+branches over 320 statements / 110 branches.

THE POPULATION IS HONEST IN WHAT IT PRINTS, AND I RECOUNTED IT. Every denominator .17 reported is recomputed in TestTheDenominatorsAreRecomputable from the filesystem and .beads/issues.jsonl by code that shares no function with the code under test, spelling out kind-then-root itself so a defect in the classifier cannot agree with itself: to_be 190 / as_is 93 / working 55 (exact), refs_checked 17 (exact, recounted from the Related Files sections), epics_with_closed_beads 37 (exact), epics 57, declaring 5, unresolved 52, and declaring + unresolved == epics. The corrected denominator in .17's comment is correct. The one finding it reports is true and I did not re-establish it.

WHAT IS STILL EXCLUDED — two populations, both invisible, both filed.

.18-1 (bead .73): a TO-BE directory carrying no CONTEXT.md/BRIEF.md is in NO field of the report — not epics, not unresolved_epics, not a NOT CHECKED line — while its documents stay in the to_be population, so one report states two sizes for one tree. Measured: 61 directories hold a TO-BE document, 57 become epics; the four lost are .claude/development (which holds ROADMAP.md and BDL-UX-Issues.md — the very documents .19/.20/.72 are about) and the SUMMARY.md-only BDL-009/010/016. Three routes to the same drop: no intent document, an undecodable one (_read returns None and the caller continues), and _INTENT_DOCUMENTS being hardcoded while every root around it is configuration — an adopter whose planning document has another name loses 100% of its epics and the gate prints a plausible '0 of 0'.

.18-2/.18-3 (bead .74): beads_by_epic.get(key, ()) makes 'the export never heard of this epic' identical to 'its beads are all open'. Measured: 23 of the 60 feature directories are absent from the export (20 of them among the 57 counted), and every one of the 37 the export DOES name has a closed bead — so '37 of 57 epic(s) with closed beads' is really '37 of 57 the export still names', and the missing 20 are BDL-001..BDL-030, finished work. YES, THE RELATION CAN BE MADE TO REPORT ZERO: removing BDL-061's 68 records from the export took _step_doc_spaces from 1 finding to 0, passed stayed True, and not_verified DID NOT MOVE — it was already True because 52 epics declare no node, so the one honest signal is saturated and carries no information about the deletion. bd close writes only the local Dolt DB, so this drifts by ordinary use rather than by sabotage. And at that same commit the CLI (which prefers bd) said 17 declarations / 1 finding while the gate (which reads only the export) said 4 / 0.

.18-4 (bead .75): A WRONG WORKING DECLARATION CAN HIDE. check_sync classifies the docs-dir-relative doc_path the indexer writes; check_spaces classifies the project-relative one. Kind agrees on both spellings (a stem has no prefix), which is why every shipped case works and why this was invisible; roots do not. Measured in a clean-room git worktree at f67fc36 through the real CLI: three stale documents, doc_roots.working.roots=[*.md, guides/*.md] with a stated reason, beadloom sync-check rc 2 -> rc 0, six pairs exempt, and beadloom docs spaces --json reported ZERO working_declaration_contradicted — the detector built for exactly this cannot see it. The other direction is equally wrong: a working root spelled project-relative like every other root in the file has no effect on freshness at all. Where the project-relative spelling matches nothing, the liveness leg fires and says the exemption 'excused nothing' while six pairs were being excused, which is worse than silence. .71 carries the same requirement for historical documents and inherits this spelling.

.18-5 (bead .76): an exempt pair is in no count any surface prints. Measured in the clean room with one WORKING document declared: 341 pairs = 326 ok + 11 exempt + 4 incomplete, printed as 'total 341, ok 326, stale 0, missing 0, unverified 0, unchecked 0'; the gate line read '326 pair(s) fresh' where the same tree without the declaration read 326 of 330. This is the shape _sync_summary's own docstring was written against (BDL-UX #174/#175) reintroduced by a verdict added after it. Related and stated so it is not rediscovered: index_docs walks the docs directory alone, so the SHIPPED ACTIVE.md never enters sync_state and the shipped exemption excuses 0 of 330 pairs here, while the report prints '55 WORKING document(s) exempt' — documents, not excused pairs.

WHAT HOLDS, ATTACKED AND NOT BROKEN. Repointing the roots does not buy silence: the relation follows the configured tree, a decoy at the shipped default is not read, and an empty TO-BE population is a NAMED skip that prints the glob it looked under (including 'no root declared'), never a pass — .14's 68 -> 1 analogue holds. tests/adopter_project.py's TypeScript project carries five of these tests, and the three that pass there prove the relation on a project with no .claude/ at all. Unverifiable is not clean for the COMPOSITE gate though not for docs spaces alone: a node whose declared document does not exist reads clean to the relation and 'missing' to sync-check (rc 2), and an empty one reads 'stale' (rc 2) — pinned in TestATOBEDocumentWithNoAsIsCounterpart so a later change that makes the relation the only reader is caught. The 11 advisory surface_drift documents were NOT touched; they are .20's.

TESTS MUST BITE, measured in two rounds, each reverted by reverse edit with sha256 byte-identity verified (CLEAN-ROOM REVERT; git status clean on src/). Round 1 — root-first instead of kind-first, plus re-filtering epics with no Related Files section: 13 reddened, 5 of them mine (TestTheDenominatorsAreRecomputable::{test_the_three_populations_match_an_independent_count, test_the_epics_with_closed_beads_are_recountable_from_the_export}, TestAWrongWorkingDeclarationIsDetectable::test_a_kind_declared_exemption_silences_a_pair_and_is_reported, TestTheVocabularyEdges::test_a_working_document_under_an_as_is_root_is_still_working, TestAnExcusedPairSaysSo::test_the_shipped_layout_excuses_no_pair_at_all) and 8 in .17's own suite; no xfail turned green. Round 2 — the doc-spaces skip becoming a pass and the exempt branch removed: 4 reddened (TestRepointingTheRootsDoesNotBuySilence::{test_an_empty_population_is_a_named_skip_and_not_a_pass, test_the_skip_names_the_root_it_looked_under_even_when_there_is_none}, the kind-declared control, and .17's acceptance scenario). Every xfail was additionally run under --runxfail and its failure read: each fails on the assertion its reason predicts, not incidentally — the one that did not (a root-declared exemption fired working_exemption_inert rather than nothing) had its fixture and its reason corrected to the measured behaviour.

MUTATION: zero mutants run, reported as zero rather than as clean. No runner is installed in this environment (mutmut and cosmic-ray both absent) and Beadloom ships none by design (CONTEXT Q5, the tool is the project's choice); adding one is not this bead's call. The strength check that DID run is the two sabotage rounds above, named test by test.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS OF THIS BEAD. (1) Zero mutants, above. (2) The repo-level recount tests read REPO_ROOT, so they measure whatever tree they run in — verified portable by running them in the clean-room worktree, but they are assertions about a real tree and will move with it by design. (3) No acceptance scenario was added: the five findings describe behaviour that does not exist yet, and a .feature scenario for absent behaviour is the ceremony .15 warned about. comments.text:
COMPLETED (HEAD 4010bb6).

WHAT SHIPPED — five of S5's six mechanisms; the sixth was REPORTED AS A SEPARATE BEAD (.72), not absorbed.
1. Configurable doc roots — `doc_roots` in .beadloom/config.yml, nested per space (roots / kinds / working exemption). infrastructure/doc_roots.py, beside scan_paths, so doc_sync resolves them without importing application.
2. Kinds for all three spaces — TO-BE (PRD/RFC/BRIEF/CONTEXT/PLAN), AS-IS (SPEC/DOC/README), WORKING (ACTIVE). KIND WINS OVER ROOT, and it is load-bearing: ACTIVE.md lives inside the TO-BE tree, so a root-first answer would classify every WORKING document as intent and exempt nothing.
3. .claude/development/ indexed IN PLACE (Q4) and searchable — docs.space column (additive ALTER), 190 TO-BE rows, an FTS row per document bound to no node, and `beadloom search --kind to_be`. On BOTH reindex paths: the full path was wired first and the incremental one — the path `beadloom ci` runs — was left behind, which is BDL-UX #142/#146's shape and was fixed before commit.
4. The TO-BE -> AS-IS relation — application/doc_spaces.py, `beadloom docs spaces`, and a warn-only doc-spaces gate step.
5. WORKING exempt from freshness BY DECLARATION — check_sync verdict `exempt` with reason `working_space` and the declared reason in details.

WHAT THE RELATION REPORTS HERE, and it fires on a real epic: ONE finding. BDL-061 declares `cli-commands` in its CONTEXT's Related Files, has 60+ closed beads, and `cli-commands` has no docs: entry at all. True — the `cli` service node declares docs/services/cli.md while the component holding every command implementation declares nothing, and neither lint --strict nor module-coverage can see it (both ask whether modules reach nodes, not whether nodes reach documents). Population: to_be 190 / as_is 93 / working 55 documents; 37 of 57 epics have closed beads; 5 declare a node; 17 node declarations held against the AS-IS space; 52 epics declare no node and are named NOT CHECKED.

THE JOIN WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. The obvious version — every backticked token in an epic's documents matching a ref id — was written, run over 60 epics, and thrown away: it attributed the node `status` to nine epics whose documents merely used the English word (BDL-UX #169/#190's class). The declared Related Files section is what shipped.

THE THREE TRAPS, each answered:
- A check that cannot fire: it fires on BDL-061 today, and `relation_checked` is False when nothing was related — reported as NOT CHECKED, not as clean. Three separate not_verified causes on the gate step (no tracker readable / no epic with closed beads declared a node / some epics declare none).
- Absence is not evidence: the WORKING exemption is a config DECLARATION, never inferred from a missing pair. A wrong declaration is detectable two ways — an exemption a project declared that matches no document (working_exemption_inert), and a document the graph declares as a node's documentation while the config declares its kind ephemeral (working_declaration_contradicted). And the check's own denominator was caught shrinking: requiring a Related Files heading removed 34 of 57 epics and made the report read '16 of 23'. Fixed in 4010bb6 with a test.
- True here is not true: tests/adopter_project.py's TypeScript project, with roots configured away from the shipped defaults and a decoy at the default path, asserting no Beadloom path reaches the answer.

TWO DEFECTS THE TESTS FOUND: root globs matched with fnmatch (which lets * cross a separator, so `*.md` classified vendor/lib/notes.md as top-level) and the WORKING liveness finding firing on the shipped DEFAULT rather than on a project's declaration.

TESTS MUST BITE, measured: unscoping the related-files read and making root beat kind reddens 7 — TestSpaceOf::test_kind_beats_root, TestWorkingExemption::{test_it_goes_quiet_once_it_excuses_something,test_a_declaration_the_graph_contradicts_is_reported}, TestRelatedFilesIsADeclaration::test_a_ref_outside_the_section_is_not_read, TestRelation::test_a_working_document_is_not_in_the_to_be_population, and the two acceptance scenarios for the exemption and the contradiction.

- 11 reference documents carry advisory surface_drift from the new CLI command (CHANGELOG, README, README.ru, docs/architecture.md, code-indexer + sync-check SPECs, getting-started, and the bdd-scenarios, document-kinds and project-overlays guides). They need prose, not a re-baseline; re-attesting without evidence is BDL-UX #163/#189's shape. They are .20's.

COMPLETED beadloom-mr2l.16 (2026-08-24) on features/BDL-061-S4. Gate rc 0. Everything below is
measured with exit codes and `--json`, never line counts (#148), on the FINAL tree.

=== GATE, before and after
BEFORE: `beadloom ci` rc 1 — sync-check FAIL, 82 stale pairs; docs-quality WARN.
AFTER:  `beadloom ci` rc 0 — reindex PASS, lint PASS (0 errors, 68 warnings, 6 crossings
suppressed), sync-check PASS (322 pair(s) fresh, 0 stale, 0 surface drift), docs-audit PASS
(15 mentions fresh, 3/9 declared facts verified — up from 2/9), docs-quality WARN (does not
block), config-check PASS, doctor PASS.
Full suite ONCE on the final tree, captured to a file: **6455 passed, 0 failed, 11 skipped,
4 xfailed** in 154 s. The three failures the coordinator measured are gone: the two
`TestSyncCheckNewPairs` rows fail only while `sync-check` exits non-zero (they assert
`exit_code == 0`), and the third did not reproduce — it was one of the environment-dependent
pair `.15` M6 named (a bare `python` on PATH / a concurrent `bd` rewriting `.beads/issues.jsonl`).
Sync-check was verified on an INCREMENTAL reindex throughout (#175); no clean database was used.

=== THE 82, REVISED vs RE-ATTESTED — the whole point of #163
Attribution measured per pair against `git diff --name-only main...HEAD`, not estimated:
**26 of 82 name a code file this branch changed; 56 name a file the branch never touched.**
Per ref: application 1/0, ci-gate 1/0, doc-quality 1/0, doc-sync 4/5, graph 6/20,
onboarding 8/26, rule-engine 5/5 (changed/untouched).
The 56 are #182: `symbols_hash` is per ref_id over every symbol annotated to the node, so ONE new
module makes every pair of that node stale — `graph` gained `scenarios.py` +
`scenario_coverage.py`, `onboarding` gained `doc_templates.py`, `doc-sync` gained `doc_shape.py`
+ `doc_quality.py`. Those pairs cannot be "revised": the file they name did not move.

**REVISED (6 documents, read against the code first):**
- graph/README.md — `evaluate_rule_liveness` said "all types except `forbid_import`"; it now skips
  `scenario_coverage` too, and `inert_rule_names` COUNTS it. `load_rules`'s union was 7 of 10 rule
  types. `evaluate_all`'s list omitted scenario-coverage. The `rules/` module list omitted
  `liveness.py`, `exemptions.py`, `attribution.py`. Added a `scenarios.py` API section and six
  dataclass rows. "nine rule types" -> ten.
- doc-sync/README.md — `check_sync`'s signature (the `section_requirements` keyword and what
  `None` means), and two whole modules with no API section at all (`doc_shape.py`,
  `doc_quality.py`).
- application/README.md + ci-gate/SPEC.md — the docs-quality step's summary gained three silence
  channels in `.66` (`NOT CHECKED` / `NO CHECK READS` / `UNREADABLE: N`) and reports WARN where
  the SPEC still said a single condition set `not_verified`.
- doc-quality/SPEC.md — the `measurable-goal` limit (below), plus the per-check measured table.
- onboarding/README.md — "the rule loader dispatches nine keys" -> ten (measured: AGENTS.md now
  lists `**scenario-coverage** (unknown)` beside `**module-coverage** (unknown)`);
  `SHARED_ROLE_FRAGMENTS` and `MAX_LISTED_FINDINGS` had no entry; `compose`'s layer order was
  missing the shared layer.
**RE-ATTESTED DELIBERATELY (1 document): rule-engine/SPEC.md.** `.66` wrote it and said it was
current; I did not take that on report. I re-read it against `scenario_coverage.py`,
`liveness.py` and `loader.py` and checked five claims by hand: the four legs + the excused
statement, the mandatory `reason` with no `until`, the `for.exclude` rejection scoped to this
rule type, the `references` default (empty — confirmed in the loader), and the
"all four legs stand down / counted in `rules_inert`" sentence. All true. Nothing to revise, so
the 10 pairs were re-baselined rather than edited.

=== THE THREE LIMITS, STATED AS LIMITS
1. `measurable-goal` — the SPEC still asserted "a number is NECESSARY for a measurable clause",
   which `.15` refuted. Rewritten: it is closer to a numeral detector than a measurability
   detector; ~1-in-18 precision on a sample of 18; it flags `beadloom lint --strict fails
   (non-zero)` and `beadloom federate --fail-on` exits non-zero, the exit-code form #148 demands.
   Read the COUNT, not the row, until the criterion is re-scoped; `.65` carries it and the
   owner's decision is to re-scope BEFORE paying. Said in the SPEC, in cli.md, in the new
   doc-kind guide, in CHANGELOG's known-limitations and in CONTEXT/PLAN.
2. Windows unverified by decision — I checked that nothing outside the flow-guards SPEC implies
   support (grep over docs/, README, README.ru: every other hit is the guides' correct
   withdrawal prose or the unrelated word "window" in docs-audit). `.64`'s care is intact and I
   added no Windows claim; CHANGELOG's Changed section states the 10 -> 9 context default and
   that no released version ever carried the leg.
3. BRIEF/PLAN/SUMMARY — reported, NOT decided. `.66`'s refusal stands: the doc-kind guide, the
   SPEC, CHANGELOG and CONTEXT all state the measured 56 of 243 (23%) and name the decision as
   open, with both sides of the trade-off written out in CONTEXT. Nothing anywhere says "BRIEF is
   outside these checks".

=== NEW DOCUMENTS (the bead's three deliverables)
- `docs/guides/bdd-scenarios.md` — the decision and what it rules out; the scenario shape and the
  tag binding; the runner note (a tag is a pytest marker unless you tell the runner otherwise —
  ten lines of `pytest_bdd_apply_tag`); where the suite lives and how to move it; the four legs;
  non-behavioural work; the honest limits; and the honesty block: **68 = 35 + 33**, repointing the
  glob takes it to **1**, and the two mechanisms that ship INERT here (`non_behavioural` and the
  `for.exclude` rejection both have no live instance on this repo's `rules.yml`).
- `docs/guides/document-kinds.md` — both document families in one place, the five generated doc
  kinds with their paths and required sections, the project overlay, the majority rule, the five
  checks with what each cannot decide, the two denominators, and the `unreadable` channel.
- Role duties: a new "What each role is held to" table in the agentic-flow guide — dev's BDD duty,
  test's mutation duty, review's "BDD is not ceremony", tech-writer's two staleness sources, and
  the shared writing standard — with the mechanism behind each named, and the mutation duty's
  deliberate absence of one.

=== MEASURED MYSELF RATHER THAN QUOTED
- 68 = 35 + 33 reproduced from `lint --format json`; 35 of **40** feature nodes, not 35 of 37 —
  `beadloom-b0xl` added three feature nodes and three scenarios after `.13` and `.14` wrote 37,
  so both sides of the fraction moved by three and the finding count did not. Corrected in the
  guide, in CONTEXT and in ACTIVE.
- `pending-in-approved` is **2 over 69**, not the 6 in the brief and in three earlier reports:
  commit 2ddbcf9 paid four of them (BDL-061 RFC Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5). The two survivors are BDL-021 Q4
  and BDL-034 Q1. Every published table now carries 2.
- `decision-reason` read moved **261 -> 269** because MY edits added decision rows (CONTEXT +1,
  ACTIVE +7). Found by re-measuring to a fixpoint after editing, and every published table was
  corrected. Both guides now carry a note that the corpus includes the documents publishing the
  numbers, and that the durable thing is the report's SHAPE.
- 0 `Example:`-derived references on this repo today — re-derived with `load_references` plus a
  hand scan of the reference globs, not taken from `.14`'s report.
- 19 scenarios in 6 files (the guide's population line), not `.13`'s 7 in 2.

=== TWO THINGS I DID NOT DO
- I did not satisfy the one `missing_sections` row. `docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md` has
  no heading naming `Features` and six of its seven peers do — because `infrastructure` has eight
  components and no feature, so it announces its children under `## Components`. Renaming a
  heading to match a matcher trades a true finding for a false green. The row stands, and the
  doc-shape SPEC now records it as a live instance of that check's stated limit.
- I did not add a `docs_audit.ignore` entry. `docs-audit` went FAIL on my first pass with 4 stale
  facts, all false matches of the keyword-proximity class: `rule_type_count` (the fact counts
  ROWS in the `rules` table, 13 — the misnomer `.53` owns) and three `node_count` matches on
  "35 ... nodes" / "33". `.beadloom/config.yml` is outside this bead's edit scope and `.53` warns
  that renaming the fact is a breaking change to every adopter's `docs_audit.ignore` keys, so I
  fixed it in the prose instead — and the architecture.md rewrite is strictly better than a
  suppression: it now states "the ten authoring keys `load_rules` dispatches ... this repository
  configures 13 rules across them", which makes `rule_type_count` a VERIFIED mention where it was
  NOT VERIFIED before. That is why declared facts verified went 2/9 -> 3/9.

=== FILED
`beadloom-mr2l.69` (P2, bug) — the shared writing standard tells all four roles, in both
localisations, that "`beadloom lint` reports these" directly above the five section-quality
checks. It reports NONE of them: measured, `lint --format json` returns 68 violations, all
`rule_type: scenario_coverage`, and the 156 doc-quality findings come from the other command. The
fragment composes into every scaffolded repository, so an agent told to run `beadloom lint` runs
a command that is green about the standard by construction. Found by writing the doc-kind
reference from the shipped templates rather than from a report. Fix is in `src/`, so not mine.

=== ALSO CLOSED FROM `.15`'s MINORS AND `.66`'s NOTES
m4 — `.13` decision 7 was argued in a SPEC and a bead comment and never written back into
CONTEXT's Architectural Decisions table, which still read "Every exclusion carries `reason` and
`until`". A dated row now refines it and says why a classification has no expiry and what keeps
it honest instead. That was the exact pattern the pending-in-approved check measured on our RFC.
M8 — ACTIVE's bead table contradicted the tracker on five rows (`.35` duplicated Pending+Done,
`.39`/`.42`/`.50` closed but Pending, `.13–.16` a single Pending row). All repaired, plus rows for
`.60`, `.62`, `.63`, `.65`, `.67`, `.69` and per-bead rows for the S4 four. `active-sync --check`
still prints "already coherent" over them because the table's ids are short-form and an unmatched
row is indistinguishable from an agreeing one — M8's mechanism half is unfixed and still open.
M5 — the `incomplete` verdict has no counter in `sync-check --json`. Not fixable in docs, so it is
now DOCUMENTED as a limit in three places with the arithmetic: total 326 = 240 ok + 82 stale +
4 incomplete, and the summary accounted for 322.

=== FILES (20 changed, 2 new; docs/, README*, CHANGELOG and the epic's planning documents only)
new: docs/guides/{bdd-scenarios,document-kinds}.md
docs: architecture, getting-started, services/cli, guides/agentic-flow, domains/graph/README,
domains/doc-sync/README, domains/doc-sync/features/{doc-quality,doc-shape,sync-check}/SPEC,
domains/application/README, domains/application/features/ci-gate/SPEC, domains/onboarding/README
root: README.md, README.ru.md, CHANGELOG.md (S4 Added/Changed/Fixed + the known-limitations
section rewritten — it still listed BDL-UX #183/#187/#188 as open, and all three were closed by
`.58`/`.59` inside this same unreleased cycle)
planning: BDL-061/{CONTEXT,PLAN,ACTIVE}.md
No file under `src/` or `tests/` was touched. PLAN's approved bead table was deliberately left
alone after an edit was reverted: rows `.1`–`.12` read Pending though they are done, so marking
only S4 would have made the table inconsistent, and its own header says live status lives in
ACTIVE and the tracker.

title: [BDL-061.15][review] S4: BDD is not ceremony; mutation scope is honest
description: Scenarios assert observable behaviour through a boundary, never private state. Non-behavioural work can opt out with a named reason. Mutation scope is pure domain cores only, and a declared target running zero mutants is caught.

comments.text:
REVIEW .15 — NOT PASSING: 1 critical, 8 major, 6 minor, 1 nitpick. Read-only; nothing edited.
Everything below is measured on HEAD 2ddbcf9 or in a `git archive HEAD` clean room (921 files, the
directory proved empty before extraction — `.13`'s trap, not repeated). Exit codes and `--json`
throughout, never line counts (#148 — see the correction at the end, which I earned).

=== WHAT I RE-DERIVED AND FOUND HONEST (before the findings) ===
- 68 = 35 uncovered feature nodes + 33 PRD-referenced scenarios. Reproduced in the clean room
  from tracked files with a from-scratch index: identical split, `13 rules, 0 inert`.
- Repointing `features:` to a directory that does not exist: 68 -> **1**, and that 1 is the
  liveness finding naming the dead glob. `.14`'s claim confirmed independently on the product.
- The b0xl half has the same property and I checked it because nobody had: repointing
  `doc_quality.paths` at `docs/rfcs/*.md` gives CLI `No planning documents found under
  docs/rfcs/*.md — nothing checked` (rc 0) and gate `docs-quality SKIP: skipped — no planning
  document matches docs/rfcs/*.md`. Neither half can be made silently quiet by moving a path.
- The scenarios EXECUTE: 19 cases, 0 skipped, read per-row from a JUnit report. And
  `test_the_shipped_acceptance_suite_runs_every_scenario_and_skips_none` binds `passed` to the
  project's own parser count, so a 7th `.feature` with no step module reddens. That closes
  "a scenario that never runs still counts as coverage" for this repo.
- BDD IS NOT CEREMONY HERE. All 19 scenarios are in the user's vocabulary, observable through a
  boundary, every `Then` asserts something, and the negative cases are present ("a draft is
  allowed its open questions", "a section stated under a wider heading is not missing"). Not one
  restates an implementation. This is the best BDD surface the epic has produced.
- Clean-room `beadloom ci` rc 0; `lint --strict` rc 0; ruff clean; `mypy --strict` clean (203 files).
- 6 new nodes, correctly layered, each with a doc. `doc-shape-requirements` and `mutation-scope`
  are correctly application components (they join two PEER domains / read the infra seam
  `onboarding` may not import). No peer edge, no new cycle, module-coverage 0 errors.
- `_migrate_drop_rule_type_check` is probe-gated, idempotent and copies every row verbatim — no
  data-loss path in the DB CHECK removal.
- The 6 `surface_drift` docs match the dev's routed list exactly (README, README.ru, CHANGELOG,
  architecture, getting-started, code-indexer SPEC). Advisory, no exit-code effect. Honest.
- The `not_covered` notes are accurate in the direction that usually goes wrong: `BEAD_NOT_VERIFIED`,
  "a scenario with no steps counts as coverage", `mutation-zero-mutants` = "holds no file in an
  indexed language" (not "a runner produced zero"), and each quality check's stated limit. Nothing
  claims MORE than the code does. The understatements are all about how far a SILENCE reaches.

=== CRITICAL ===
C1 · src/beadloom/doc_sync/doc_quality.py:503-506 · one undecodable planning document takes down
the WHOLE `beadloom ci` gate with a traceback.
`check_documents` catches `OSError`. `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`,
which is a `ValueError`, so it is not caught. MEASURED, twice: `beadloom docs quality` -> rc 1,
traceback, no JSON; `beadloom ci` -> rc 1, traceback out of `application/gate.py:449`, and because
the step list at gate.py:171 is built eagerly, the reindex / lint / sync-check / docs-audit results
of that run are lost with it. A step b0xl documented as "reports and never blocks" is the loudest
possible blocker.
This is the same defect `.14` filed as `.62`(3) against `load_references` — and `scenarios.py:366`
and `:499`, one module over in the sibling half, both catch `(OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)`. The
population it hits is not hypothetical: it is #136's own — a team writing planning documents in
Russian with one legacy-encoded file. It also breaks the standing constraint "no adopter's green
project turns red on upgrade" in the hardest way available.
RECOMMENDATION: catch `(OSError, UnicodeDecodeError)`, COUNT the document, and emit a named
`unreadable` finding — a document nobody can read is not a document with no findings; that is
CONTEXT's `.57` rule ("nothing an editor does may make a check quieter") with the sign flipped.
Same one-line class at `doc_sync/doc_shape.py:110` (currently masked because the pre-existing
`engine.py:1303` crashes first — that one is NOT S4's and I checked before attributing).

=== MAJOR ===

M1 · graph/rules/types.py:128 + rules/scenario_coverage.py:58-69, 133-134 · TWO silent population
exits beyond `.63`.
(a) `NodeMatcher.exclude` removes a node from `for:` with NO reason, NO report and NO expiry, and
    `_matcher_description()` does not even print `exclude`, so a matcher excluded down to nothing
    reports "the `for` matcher (kind=feature) selects no node" without saying why. This directly
    contradicts CONTEXT's own decision row "**Every exclusion carries `reason` and `until`**; one
    with neither is a config error" — which `non_behavioural` honours and `exclude` does not.
    `.14` locked the SHIPPED rule against it (S6/S7 sabotages); an adopter has no such lock.
(b) A LIVE `non_behavioural` declaration is silent: `_coverage_leg` skips it and nothing anywhere
    prints how many nodes are excused. `_population()` is the SUITE denominator
    (`19 scenarios in 6 files`), never the node population. So `.63`'s option 2 — "print the
    denominator beside the fraction" — is not implemented in ANY form, and the improving numerator
    is never shown next to the population it is a fraction of.
RECOMMENDATION: `exclude` on a `scenario_coverage` `for:` matcher should require a reason (reuse
`_parse_non_behavioural`'s error text), and every run should state the population
("35 of 40 feature nodes carry no scenario; 0 excused, 0 excluded").

M2 · doc_sync/doc_quality.py + application/doc_shape.py · THE ANSWER TO THE SHARPER QUESTION:
whole populations were never ENTERED, and `checks_that_read_nothing` cannot see it.
Measured per document over this repo's 243, by document kind:
  measurable-goal      reads   60 of 243 documents   (PRD 29/41, CONTEXT 30/46, ACTIVE 1/55)
  decision-reason      reads   40 of 243             (CONTEXT 31/46, RFC 6/45, PRD 2/41)
  risk-mitigation      reads   31 of 243             (RFC 27/45, PRD 4/41)
  pending-in-approved  reads   19 of 243             (RFC 18/45, PRD 1/41)
And the finding inside the finding: **all 11 BRIEF.md documents contribute ZERO to all four
content checks** — and so will every BRIEF in every adopting project, because the SHIPPED BRIEF
template (`templates/agentic_flow/commands/templates.md.txt:317-352`) carries no Goal section, no
decision table with a Reason/Rationale/Why column, no Risks and no Open Questions. The document
kind used for every `bug`, `task` and `chore` is unjudged BY CONSTRUCTION. All 42 PLAN.md
contribute zero as well, though PLAN's "Done when" list is where the epic's own criteria live.
Therefore, on your question about b0xl's proof: **the single-edit demonstrations are sound for what
they prove and are not the property the numbers imply.** Each proves the check CAN fire on a real
document — that half is solid, and 0/261 decision rows and 0/138 risk rows are a genuinely CHECKED
green. What they do not prove is that the population is complete, and
`checks_that_read_nothing == ()` cannot help: it is a **global OR over 243 documents**, so it goes
permanently silent the moment ONE document carries ONE row. It can detect a check that is blind
everywhere. It cannot detect a check that is blind on 203 of 243 documents and on an entire
shipped doc kind.
RECOMMENDATION: report applicability PER DOC KIND, which is one line of reporting and no new
mechanism — and it is the shape b0xl ALREADY chose for `missing_sections` ("Source (5/39)"). Then
either give the BRIEF template a Goal/Risks row or state in the SPEC that BRIEF is outside these
four checks, so the exclusion is a decision rather than an accident.

M3 · graph/rules/liveness.py (UNTOUCHED by S4) + rule-engine SPEC:180,228 · `rules_inert` does not
count `scenario_coverage`, and the SPEC sentence that says it does is now false.
MEASURED in the clean room with `features:` repointed: `13 rules evaluated, 0 inert` while the rule
had stood four legs down and printed its own liveness finding. `_reasons_for_rule` has no branch
for `ScenarioCoverageRule`, so it falls through to `validate_rules`. `.14` reported this as "one
nuance, not a defect"; it is a defect, of the class named A GREEN COUNT IS NOT A CHECKED COUNT.
Two documentation consequences, both stale:
- rule-engine SPEC:228 still reads "`LintResult.rules_inert` qualifies the rule count on the
  summary line ... **so a green run cannot advertise checks that never looked**" — directly under
  the new `scenario_coverage` liveness row S4 added, for which it is false.
- `liveness.py`'s module docstring still says "closes it for the remaining **eight** rule types"
  and still carries the per-type table it declares is "**the same table** [as] the SPEC". S4 added
  the tenth type and the SPEC row and did not touch `liveness.py` at all. One identifier, two
  sources of truth — BDL-UX #171's exact shape, which `.13` cited when removing the DB CHECK.
RECOMMENDATION: name the exception the way `forbid_import` is named (it has the same carve-out and
says so), in BOTH tables; or dispatch `ScenarioCoverageRule` so the counter is simply true.

M4 · rules/scenario_coverage.py:22-25 (module docstring) + rule-engine SPEC:219-221 · the honesty
note understates the silence — the fifth recurrence of this class in the epic.
The docstring says "**One deliberate silence:** when the `features` glob matches no file at all,
**the coverage leg** is skipped"; the SPEC says the same. MEASURED: `_evaluate_one` returns early
at line 346, so the **suite leg, the declaration leg AND the reference leg are skipped too** —
68 -> 1, and the 33 reference findings that an empty suite makes definitionally true vanish along
with any dead `non_behavioural` declaration. The same docstring's headline claim, three paragraphs
up, is "**Liveness is per LEG, not per rule** ... they fail independently" — contradicted by its
own control flow. The one-line liveness finding IS printed, so nothing is hidden from a reader who
looks; what is wrong is the note that tells them how far to look.
RECOMMENDATION: say what the code does ("an empty suite stands the whole rule down and reports the
glob"), or run the declaration and reference legs against the empty suite, which are both
answerable without a suite.

M5 · services/commands/docsync.py:158-164, 192-197 · the new `incomplete` status has no counter.
`sync-check --json` reports `total: 326` and `ok 321 + stale 1 + missing 0 + unverified 0 +
unchecked 0 = 322`. The four `incomplete` rows the same run PRINTS are in no counter at all. The
rich output shows them as `[warn]`, so the human is fine and the machine consumer is not — and the
TUI, MCP and any adopter script read the summary. One key, in the epic whose thesis is that a
count must describe what was checked.

M6 · tests/test_doc_quality.py::TestOnThisRepositorysOwnDocuments::
test_our_approved_rfc_still_carries_pending_questions · a test that REDDENS WHEN THE DEBT IS PAID,
and the branch is red because of it.
Full suite on HEAD, captured once: **5 failed / 6416 passed / 11 skipped / 4 xfailed**, not the 2
the brief accounts for. Two of the extra three are environment (`test_ai_techwriter_seams` shells
out to a bare `python`, absent from this PATH — `.14` saw the same pair in its clean room, not
S4's). The third is deterministic and is S4's own: the test asserts
`any("BDL-061" in f.path for f in pending)`, and commit 2ddbcf9 — "pay the debt the new
pending-in-approved check found in our own RFC" — paid exactly that debt. pending-in-approved is
now **2 over 69** (BDL-021 Q4, BDL-034 Q1), not the 6 every report still records.
So the last commit on the branch did the right thing and the suite punished it. The assertion is
pinned to a transient content state of this repository — TRUE HERE IS NOT TRUE, inverted.
RECOMMENDATION: assert the MECHANISM (the check fires on a constructed Approved document with a
Pending row — which the acceptance scenario already does) and drop the repo-content clause. Note
`assert pending, "the check read nothing on this repo"` in the same test has the same fate the day
the last two are paid.

M7 · tests/symlink_capability.py:113 · the vacuous skip `.39` removed can be re-created in ONE
line, with a green suite — and the ledger built to prevent recurrence does not reach it.
Baseline in a clean room: `tests/test_guards_paths.py tests/test_windows_dimension.py` -> 96 passed,
0 skipped. Single reverse-editable edit `SYMLINKS_UNAVAILABLE = True` -> **90 passed, 6 skipped,
0 failed**, and the six skips read "...: **no reason recorded**" — the tell that the constant and
the measurement disagree. Nothing fails: `test_this_machine_can_link_so_the_six_guard_rows_actually_run`
asserts `SYMLINK_CAPABILITY.both`, which is still honest, and the `test_windows_dimension` ledger
AST-scans only for conditions naming `sys.platform`, which these marks deliberately no longer do.
So the fix moved the condition to a place the anti-recurrence mechanism does not look.
CLEAN-ROOM REVERT by reverse edit, byte identity re-verified by sha256 (6d52f86cd9f31625, equal to
the repo file).
RECOMMENDATION: one line — `assert SYMLINKS_UNAVAILABLE == (not SYMLINK_CAPABILITY.both)`, or
better, have the ledger require that any capability-gated skip's condition be DERIVED from a probe
in the same module. Otherwise: the probe itself is SOUND. It measures a real link in both shapes,
reads both back (so a filesystem that degrades a link to a copy is refused), never asks
`sys.platform`, and `.14`'s two-sided cross-check against `tmp_path` closes the wrong-volume case.
It cannot silently answer "no capability" — that was your question, and the answer is no, except
through M7's one line.

M8 · `beadloom active-sync --check` reports "ACTIVE tables already coherent" over five stale rows.
Measured on the tree: BDL-061's own ACTIVE.md bead table says `Pending` for `.39`, `.42`, `.50` and
`.13–.16` — all CLOSED in the tracker — plus a duplicate `.35` row (one Done, one Pending). The
reconcile finds the table correctly (header `| Bead | Status | Details |` parses); it fails on the
row ids, which are short-form (`.39`, not `beadloom-mr2l.39`). `reconcile_active_tables`'s own
docstring: "Rows whose bead-id is absent ... are left untouched" — so an unmatched row is
indistinguishable from an agreeing one and the command prints green. This is BDL-053's mechanism
reporting a false green about S4's own state, and the fix is `.13`'s own `_declaration_leg` pattern
one domain over: an unmatched row is itself a finding ("4 rows name a bead the tracker does not
know"). Not S4's code; in scope because ACTIVE is the durable state all four beads write to.

=== MINOR ===
m1 · doc_quality.py `_check_goals` reports 3 markdown horizontal rules (`---`) as goal statements
     ("the goal states no measurable clause: ---"). `_paragraphs` does not skip separator lines.
m2 · .github/workflows/ci.yml, the DEGRADED probe creates only a FILE link, while
     `SYMLINKS_UNAVAILABLE` requires file AND directory. A runner that could do one and not the
     other passes the probe and capability-skips the six. Caught downstream by
     `test_this_machine_can_link`, so the leg still fails — but the comment claims the probe covers
     the condition, and it measures half of it. One line: add the `target_is_directory=True` link.
m3 · `shipped_placeholders` returning a PARTIAL vocabulary (44 tokens today) is invisible:
     `checks_that_read_nothing` only fires at zero, and `applicable` is 243 regardless. If the
     `/templates` fences change shape and the derivation drops to 3 tokens, nothing says so.
     Pin the count, or report it beside the denominator.
m4 · `.13` decision 7 (mandatory `reason`, deliberately no `until`) is argued in the SPEC and in a
     bead comment, and NO row was written back into CONTEXT's Architectural Decisions table, whose
     standing row still reads "Every exclusion carries `reason` and `until`". This is precisely the
     "decided in planning, recorded elsewhere, never written back to the document that asked"
     pattern that b0xl's own pending-in-approved check just measured on the RFC.
m5 · `onboarding` is now 15 `part_of` children (14 at review `.11` m8, "carried to S4 as the signal
     `domain-size-limit` cannot give"). S4 added `doc-templates` — correctly placed, no objection to
     the placement — without re-stating the carried signal. It should be decided in S5, not drift.
n1 · `unfilled-placeholder: 0 findings over 243 read` counts DOCUMENTS OPENED; the other four count
     ITEMS. Five denominators of two different kinds on one summary block.

=== VERDICT: `measurable-goal` at 154 of 235 — RE-SCOPE THE RULE, DO NOT PAY THE DEBT AS WRITTEN ===
The criterion is WRONG, not merely strict. As shipped it is a numeral detector: `_NUMBER_RE` finds a
digit not preceded by a word character, dot or hyphen, and calls its absence "no measurable clause".
Two findings from this repo's own run settle it:
  BDL-036/PRD.md:26  "`beadloom lint --strict` **fails** (non-zero) on real cycle/layer violations"
  BDL-039/PRD.md:22  "`beadloom federate --fail-on <verdicts>` exits non-zero ..."
Both are EXIT-CODE criteria — the most checkable goal this project knows how to write, and the exact
form standing note #148 exists to insist on — and both are reported as unmeasurable. On a random
sample of 18 of the 154 I could defend exactly ONE as a true positive ("Make Beadloom useful for the
whole team, not just the person who set it up"). The module docstring's stated limit — "a number is
NECESSARY for a measurable clause and not sufficient" — asserts a necessity that is false: an exit
code, a named artifact that either exists or does not, and a binary capability are all measurable
without a digit.
A check firing on 66% of a corpus at roughly 1-in-18 precision does not get satisfied; it gets
`--check`-excluded inside a slice, which is worse than not shipping it. And b0xl's handoff line —
"if a future slice wants them lower, the honest move is to write measurable goals, not to widen the
check" — would have us insert numerals into 154 goal statements that are already checkable.
CONCRETE, MEASURED RE-SCOPE: accept as a measurable clause either a number OR an observable
predicate — a backticked artifact, or one of `exits / rc / green / reported / produces / passes /
fails / no longer`. Measured on this corpus that takes **154 -> 87**, and the 87 that remain are
exactly the class the check exists for ("Make Beadloom fast, searchable and fully agent-native",
"Establish the agent-native architecture", "Make Beadloom enjoyable and intuitive"). If that
heuristic is judged too fuzzy to ship, the alternative is honest rather than clever: keep the
numeral rule, RENAME the check `goal-without-a-number`, and drop it below `warn`. A check whose NAME
over-claims what it decides is this epic's own recurring defect. Do not disable it — it caught a
real one.

=== VERDICT: THE WINDOWS LEG'S COST — I WOULD NOT PAY IT, AND `.64` HAS ALREADY WITHDRAWN IT ===
(The project layer of CLAUDE.md changed under me mid-review: `beadloom-mr2l.64` withdrew
`tests-windows` by owner decision. I agree with it, and here is the reasoning independent of that.)
The case FOR is the strongest in the epic on principle: `src/` contains zero `sys.platform` and zero
`os.name` branches, so the product is either genuinely portable or has never been asked, and an
all-green Linux pipeline cannot tell those two states apart. But the price is asymmetric with the
locale legs in the one dimension that matters. The locale rows cost ~8 runner-minutes and ZERO
wall-clock, because they fan out beside legs that are already slower. This one costs ~16-28
runner-minutes AND becomes the critical path, roughly tripling PR-to-merge latency — on a
single-maintainer trunk-based repo where every change integrates through a PR and latency, not
runner-minutes, is the scarce resource.
And the thing it exists to adjudicate does not need it. `.60`'s defect is decidable by reading:
`rejection_reason` refuses ANY backslash under a justification — "separates directories on the
harness's platform and is an ordinary file-name character on this one" — that describes two
platforms, while the guard runs inside the harness's own process tree, where there is exactly one.
`.39` measured it by proxy with `PureWindowsPath` and pinned it as a STRICT xfail, so if the
reasoning is wrong a runner would say so. A leg bought to confirm a conclusion already reached, at
the cost of every PR forever, is not a dimension — it is a receipt.
IF Windows ever becomes an audience, the honest middle is a `workflow_dispatch` (or release-tag)
Windows leg: the delta is measurable when someone wants it and is not on the merge path.
WHAT MUST NOT BE LOST WITH THE WITHDRAWAL, and this is `.39`'s real deliverable: the six guard rows
are non-vacuous NOW, independent of any leg, and the `sys.platform` ledger stays. That was always
worth more than the runner. Two consequences to sequence: the `--check` context and the ci.yml job
must be withdrawn together or the lockout guard is the thing that breaks; and M7 above must be
closed, because without the leg the ONLY thing standing between the repo and six vacuous skips is a
one-line constant nothing pins.

=== CONTRADICTIONS ACROSS THE FOUR BEADS ===
Nothing where a bead claims MORE capability than the code delivers — the COMPLETED comments are
accurate and the stated limits are real limits. What I found is drift in the reports and in the
silences:
- M4 (the deliberate-silence note names one leg, the code skips four) and M3 (the SPEC sentence and
  `liveness.py`'s untouched table). Both are the "understates what the code does" class you said has
  recurred five times; these are six and seven.
- b0xl's CHECKPOINT 2 records "scenario-coverage went 68 -> 69 warns"; the tree measures 68.
- pending-in-approved is recorded as 6 in b0xl's COMPLETED comment, in ACTIVE's b0xl row and in the
  review brief; it is 2 since 2ddbcf9. M6 is what that change cost.
- ACTIVE's bead table (M8) contradicts the tracker on five rows.
- `.13` said "a chore may declare itself non-behavioural ... [x] delivered" while its own decision 8
  says "Opted THIS repo in on the honest population". The shipped `rules.yml` has ZERO
  `non_behavioural` entries, so unlike the mutation targets — which b0xl deliberately dogfooded —
  that mechanism has no live instance here. Not a false claim (the unit rows and an acceptance
  scenario cover it), but it is the one S4 mechanism proved only in tests.

=== ONE CORRECTION ON MYSELF, since the epic's rule is that a wrong measurement is reported ===
I first recorded `beadloom docs quality --check no-such-check` as printing an error and exiting 0.
That was `tail`'s exit code, not the command's. Re-measured without a pipeline: rc 1, correct.
#148 applies to the reviewer too.
