comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
TESTS: 39 rows in tests/test_bead14_s4_binding.py (36 passed + 3 xfail(strict=True) findings). Coverage on the two S4 modules: scenario_coverage.py 100% statements AND 100% branches, scenarios.py 100%/100% (317 statements, 122 branches, 0 missed) — measured with the S4 test files plus tests/acceptance. Commit e14fd79 on features/BDL-061-S4.

=== 1. IS THE 68 HONEST? YES, AND IT REPRODUCES FROM TRACKED FILES ALONE.
35 uncovered feature nodes + 33 PRD-referenced scenarios absent from the suite = 68, and the same 35/33 split comes out of a `git archive HEAD` clean room with a from-scratch index and a from-scratch venv. So the number is a property of the repository, not of my working index.

THE POPULATION. `.13`'s claim checks out and is now measured rather than asserted. The shipped rule is `for: {kind: feature}` — no `ref_id`, no `exclude` — and test_every_feature_node_the_graph_declares_is_in_the_population compares the matcher's reach against services.yml itself: all 37 declared feature nodes are selected, 35 of them uncovered. Beside it, test_a_hand_picked_population_would_report_almost_nothing measures the alternative on the same graph and the same suite: a `ref_id` matcher reports 0 where the honest one reports 2. That is what the row above is protecting, priced.

WHAT IS EXCLUDED, and whether it should be. 24 `component`, 7 `domain`, 4 `service`, 1 `site` are outside the population. Components are excluded by the architecture model's own definition (`architecture-model.md`: a feature is a capability, a component is plumbing) — but that guide also says the distinction is "intent, not weight", and several components read as behaviour-bearing on any ordinary reading (guard-hooks, mcp-tools, cli-commands, graphql_breaking). Not a defect in `.13`; the DEFECT-SHAPED part is that the exit is silent — changing one line from `kind: feature` to `kind: component` removes a node from the population with no finding of any kind. FILED as beadloom-mr2l.63 with both options and their costs (report the reclassification, which needs stored history and makes an evaluator a writer; or print the denominator beside the fraction, which does not catch it but puts the shrinking population on the same line as the improving number).

THE 33, checked one by one rather than counted. All 33 come from ONE document (BDL-061's own PRD); the reference globs match 52 documents (41 PRD + 11 BRIEF) and the other 51 contain no scenario reference at all, which is honest — they predate the convention. Exactly ONE of the 33 exists in the suite under a different capitalisation ("A scenario naming no bead is reported" vs "a scenario naming no bead is reported"); the other 32 do not exist in any spelling. So the 33 is honest to within one row, and that row is still a real disagreement between the PRD and the suite. Locked test_the_shipped_reference_globs_read_more_than_the_document_that_added_them so narrowing `references:` to the one PRD that uses the convention — which would leave the 33 unchanged while making the leg unable to find a new document — reddens.

=== 2. CAN A PATH CHANGE MAKE scenario-coverage QUIET? NOT TO ZERO. TO ONE.
Measured on the PRODUCT, in the clean room, by editing the shipped rules.yml there: `features:` repointed to a directory that does not exist takes `lint` from 68 warnings to 1, and that 1 is the rule_liveness finding naming the dead glob by its text. Exit codes unchanged (0 both ways — severity is warn, per CONTEXT). The unit rows cover the same thing three ways: a moved-and-empty location reports the glob; the location FOLLOWED to a non-default directory works (a `qa/gherkin/**` layout is read); a glob that stops recursing (`*.feature` for `**/*.feature`) stays alive and reports the now-invisible node as uncovered, with the denominator falling to "in 1 file". A fourth row does it end-to-end through the real `lint --format json` on a two-node project that is not this one and asserts violations_count does not fall to 0.

ONE NUANCE FOR .15, not a defect: `liveness.py` — which computes the `rules_inert` counter in the summary line — has no knowledge of ScenarioCoverageRule, because `.13` put liveness per-LEG inside the rule module. So in the moved-path state the headline reads "Errors: 0, Warnings: 1 (13 rules evaluated, ...)" with NO "N of them unable to check anything" clause, while one of the 13 has stood two of its four legs down. The finding itself is printed and unmissable, and the Gate keys off `result.violations` (gate.py:219) so it does flip — the blind spot is the counter, not the report.

=== 3. BINDING, BOTH WAYS, INCLUDING THE CASES NOBODY HAD WRITTEN
Reported and tested: a scenario naming no bead; a `@node:` left behind by a deleted node (both halves — the dangling tag AND the node it stopped covering); a dangling tag that must not spend its coverage on a similarly-named node; a `.feature` file one directory outside the configured glob (covers nothing, the node is still reported); two scenarios claiming one node (covered once, reported zero times).
TWO LIMITS PINNED rather than described, because a stated limit nothing measures drifts into an unstated one: (a) the bead id is never verified against the tracker — a scenario tagged `@bead:no-such-bead-anywhere-42` is accepted, and BEAD_NOT_VERIFIED is asserted to travel on the finding's own remediation; (b) a scenario with NO steps counts as coverage — only structure is parsed, which is `scenarios.py`'s own statement and the mutation duty's job.

=== 4. THE SCENARIOS EXECUTE. CONFIRMED, AND A BROKEN STEP REDDENS.
Seven scenarios, and each one RAN — per-row outcomes read from a JUnit report rather than from a terminal count, because collected-and-skipped produces the same green and telling those apart is the whole question. 0 skipped. Then the sabotage-as-a-test: the shipped suite is copied out, one step's text is changed so the Gherkin no longer matches it, and the copy is run — it goes red with StepDefinitionNotFound and fewer than 7 rows survive. The assertion names the REASON, so a run that reddens for an unrelated import error does not count as proof.

=== 5. .39 VERIFIED — THE PROBE CANNOT SILENTLY ANSWER "NO" AND THE LEDGER BITES
The probe is non-vacuous here: tests/test_guards_paths.py runs 77 passed / 0 SKIPPED, so all six formerly-skipped rows execute. `.39` already asserts SYMLINK_CAPABILITY.both loudly; I added the direction it was missing — test_the_probe_agrees_with_the_directory_the_guard_rows_actually_use cross-checks the probe (which measures a `tempfile` directory) against `tmp_path` (which is what the six rows actually link in), so a TMPDIR on a mount without symlink support, or a `--basetemp` elsewhere, cannot make six live tests skip on a measurement taken on the wrong volume. Two-sided, so a probe that always answered the same thing fails it either way.
THE LEDGER: its scanner had tests, its VERDICT did not. Added both branches — an unjudged skip and a stale entry — executed against a redirected TESTS_DIR. And the bead's own request, done for real on the live tree: a `skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="not worth it")` added to tests/test_scenario_binding.py made test_no_win32_skip_is_unjudged FAIL, naming the row (sabotage S11).

=== 6. TESTS MUST BITE — 11 sabotages, all FAILED, never ERROR, never "no tests ran"
Baseline over the S4 surface: 104 passed / 0 failed. Each sabotage is one reverse-editable edit; each restore is sha256-verified; each hit its OWN row.
S1  coverage leg never reports              -> 14 failed / 90 passed
S2  a moved glob reports nothing            ->  5 / 99   (both path rows + the CLI e2e + .13's liveness row + the acceptance scenario)
S3  a scenario naming no bead is silent     ->  8 / 96
S4  an unknown @node: is silent             ->  4 / 100

S6  population narrowed by an exclude       ->  2 / 102  (both population rows)
S7  population pinned to one ref_id         ->  2 / 102

CLEAN-ROOM REVERT: scenario_coverage.py b3512be132f6..., scenarios.py fe0545cf8a6a... byte-identical afterwards, and `git status` over every sabotaged path is empty.

=== 7. FINDINGS FILED, NOT FIXED
beadloom-mr2l.62 (bug, P2) — three in the reference leg, the widest surface as `.13` predicted, each pinned as xfail(strict=True) so a fix reddens the suite and the mark must come out with it:
 (1) `Example:` is a Gherkin scenario keyword, so a bare prose line opening with it is read as a claim a scenario exists. Measured: "Example: a nested import inside a function is still an import." yields the reference 'a nested import inside a function'. ZERO false positives on this repo today and a large class of them for any adopter.
 (2) an indented (four-space) code block is read as a reference while a fenced one is not — markdown has two code-block syntaxes and _FENCE knows one; the module's own reason for skipping fences applies identically.
 (3) load_references() swallows OSError/UnicodeDecodeError with a bare `continue`, so a document it cannot DECODE contributes zero references and nothing is reported — not a dead glob (the glob matched), not an unreadable file. Measured: a cp1251 PRD naming one scenario yields refs=() dead=(), i.e. that document's intent reads as fully met. load_suite() reports an undecodable .feature one function away. This is CONTEXT's own `.57` rule: nothing an editor does may make a check quieter.
beadloom-mr2l.63 (task, P2) — the silent population exit, above.
NOT FILED, reported here: tests/test_guards_parity.py::TestGuardsAreReadOnly::test_the_live_repo_index_is_byte_identical_after_a_real_evaluation hashes `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which any concurrent `bd` process rewrites. It went red in my full-suite run and passes in isolation — the row can fail for a reason that has nothing to do with a guard being read-only. Same class as the `-wal` problem its own docstring already solved for the index.

Full suite ONCE, captured: 6348 passed / 6 failed / 11 skipped / 4 xfailed. TWO are the pair the coordinator measured and owns (.16's acceptance criterion). `beadloom lint --no-reindex --strict` rc 0 — 13 rules, 0 inert, 68 warnings, unchanged, as it must be: I touched no src and no graph YAML, so no reindex was due and I ran none against the shared index (the sibling has undeclared nodes in flight; reindexing would bake their half-state in). Same reason `sync-update` was not run on any ref.
GREEN IN A CLEAN ROOM OVER 897 FILES (#181): fresh directory PROVED EMPTY BEFORE EXTRACTION (`.13`'s trap, not repeated), `git archive HEAD`, `uv venv` + `uv pip install -e .[dev]` — 200 passed / 3 xfailed / 0 skipped over the S4 surface + guards_paths + the acceptance suite, and `beadloom lint` there reproduces 68 = 35 + 33 exactly.
Exit codes and `--json` throughout, never line counts (#148). Nothing outside my one path was staged; no `git add -A`. `.beads/issues.jsonl` rode along in the commit because it was ALREADY staged when this session began (8 lines: my two new beads, my claim, and the sibling's own open->in_progress transition) — stated rather than hidden; no source of theirs is in the commit.

comments.author: v.zoologov
comments.text:
CHECKPOINT 1 — the scenario half is green.

NEW: src/beadloom/graph/scenarios.py (parse .feature: Gherkin tags @bead:/@node: with Feature/Rule inheritance, doc-string payloads excluded, en+ru dialects, an unknown dialect REPORTED not counted as zero) and src/beadloom/graph/rules/scenario_coverage.py (the rule; per-LEG liveness).

Decisions taken and why:
- BINDING BY GHERKIN TAGS, not the header comment the RFC sketched. A tag is part of the Gherkin language — every parser, runner and IDE reads it, pytest-bdd selects on it, and Gherkin's own Feature/Rule inheritance gives 'one file binds to a node once' for free. A comment is understood by nobody but us. Recorded as a deviation from the RFC rather than done silently.
- LOCALISED GHERKIN IS A FIRST-CLASS CASE (#136's population). A Russian team writing 'Сценарий:' would otherwise have every node reported uncovered by a parser that read nothing — the exact 'true only here' defect S3b caught. en + ru ship; any other declared dialect is an UNREADABLE finding naming the shipped set, never silence.
- THE DB CHECK ON rule_type IS GONE (#171's shape). It restated the loader's vocabulary and its real effect was that a new rule type raised IntegrityError on every EXISTING beadloom.db — on the adopter's machine, not ours. Added _migrate_drop_rule_type_check (same rename-copy-drop mechanism as the kind/lifecycle CHECK migrations) and replaced the test that guarded the CHECK with two that pin where the vocabulary IS enforced (the loader) and that the schema no longer enumerates it.
- PER-LEG LIVENESS, a refinement of .48's model: a dead 'for' matcher must not stand down the two scenario legs, and a dead references glob must not stand down the other three. Each dead leg reports itself and the rest run.
- ONE DELIBERATE SILENCE: a features glob matching zero files reports the glob and does NOT then report every node. One configuration error printing as N architecture findings buries the finding that fixes it.

Tests: 54 (26 parser + 28 rule), all passing. Sabotage pass still to run.

THE SCENARIOS RUN. pytest-bdd added to the dev extra (not a second [dependency-groups] block — one place for dev deps). Without a runner a .feature file is prose and scenario-coverage would be checking the existence of TEXT; the decision it enforces only holds while the artifact executes. 7 scenarios execute in 'uv run pytest'.

Two defects the REAL runner found that my own tests would not have:
- pytest-bdd refuses a file with two Feature: blocks. My parser accepted it, which would have counted scenarios as covering their nodes while nothing executed — a false green. The parser now reports it as unreadable.
- pytest-bdd turns every Gherkin tag into a pytest marker and this repo runs --strict-markers, so @bead:/@node: broke collection. tests/acceptance/conftest.py consumes the two binding prefixes via pytest_bdd_apply_tag and leaves every other tag its usual selector meaning.

comments.text:
API CHANGE: a new public rule type and a new graph feature.

NEW PUBLIC SURFACE
- beadloom.graph.scenarios (new module, feature node 'scenario-binding'): Scenario, ScenarioSuite, ScenarioReference, UnreadableFeatureFile, parse_feature, load_suite, parse_scenario_references, load_references, DEFAULT_FEATURE_GLOB, DEFAULT_STEPS_DIRNAME, BEAD_TAG_PREFIX, NODE_TAG_PREFIX.

title: [BDL-UX #163] sync-update can re-attest a doc nobody read — re-baselining silences sync-check without evidence
description:
Turns 'a green sync-check does not mean the prose is true' into something checkable.

sync-check compares hashes. 'beadloom sync-update <ref>' re-baselines them. Nothing anywhere records whether the DOC was actually read or revised — so a re-baseline after a code change makes the pair green with zero evidence the prose still describes reality. This happened repeatedly during BDL-060 S4: a dev change re-stales a domain doc, the baseline is reset to keep the gate moving, and the prose silently drifts.

Concrete instance from the same session: the vitepress-site guide still described the landscape as 'an interactive Mermaid diagram' and called Cytoscape 'a follow-up' — after the slice that shipped Cytoscape. sync-check read 0 stale the whole time, because that guide is prose no symbol pair anchors.

Two distinct holes, and they need different answers:

A. PROSE WITH NO PAIR. A guide anchored to no symbol can never go stale. Today the only signal is the 'reference'/'watches' mechanism (BDL-057), which is opt-in and coarse. Options: make watches discoverable (warn when a docs/guides/*.md declares no watches), or let a doc watch a NODE rather than a symbol surface.

B. BLIND RE-BASELINE. Re-attesting without touching the doc is sometimes legitimate (an internal rename the doc never mentions), so this cannot be forbidden outright. Proposal: RECORD it. Track, per pair, how many times it was re-baselined while its code symbols changed and its doc file did NOT change. A pair with a high count is 'attested but never revised' — a staleness SUSPICION the gate can surface as advisory, without blocking. That is honest: it does not claim the prose is wrong, it says nobody has looked in a long time while the code moved underneath.

Relates to #161 (the audit checks numbers but not whether a documented symbol exists) — same family, different mechanism. #161 catches a phantom name; this catches prose that quietly stopped being true while every number in it stayed correct.

title: [BDL-UX #161] docs audit checks numeric facts but never that a documented identifier still exists
description:
While narrowing the surface_registry port from CLI+MCP to CLI-only, register_mcp_tools and get_mcp_tools were deleted from the code and left documented in docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md and the surface-registry component DOC. Both passed 'beadloom ci' 6/6 on the release branch.

Why nothing caught it:
- sync-check compares hashes and the pair had been re-baselined after the edit;
- docs audit verifies numeric claims (version, node/edge counts, CLI-command and MCP-tool counts) and has no notion of a named symbol.

Found by a ten-line ad-hoc script written for an unrelated reason.

The audit answers 'is this number still true?' but not 'does this name still exist?'. The second is cheaper and catches a worse class: a stale number misleads, a phantom symbol sends a reader — or an agent — after something that is not there.

Proposal: for each backticked 'name(' in a tracked doc, verify a matching def/class exists in the indexed symbols; report doc + name + node. Must tolerate legitimate framework references (e.g. Textual's pop_screen) and deliberate mentions of removed symbols — likely reusing the docs_audit.ignore escape hatch with a named reason.

Measured: an ad-hoc version over the release branch's 13 changed docs produced exactly ONE hit, and it was a correct framework reference — the false-positive rate on a real tree looks workable.

title: [BDL-UX #160] AsyncAPI ingestion is documented as a capability but wired to nothing — extract_payload_body is called by no code path in src/
description:
Found by the honest dependency graph (BDL-060 S4 dogfood): the 'asyncapi' node has no dependency in EITHER direction. Verified independently by grep — 'src/beadloom/graph/asyncapi.py' is referenced by ZERO other files under src/. Only its two test files import it.

The docs claim a capability:
  federation/SPEC.md:353 — 'teams on AsyncAPI ingest the payload schema via the source-only asyncapi.extract_payload_body adapter'
  components/asyncapi/DOC.md — 'Teams that already describe their AMQP messages with an AsyncAPI document ... it extracts the message payload JSON-Schema'

What is actually true: extract_payload_body() works and is well tested (test_asyncapi_ingest.py, test_asyncapi_fidelity.py). What is NOT true: that a team 'ingests' anything. There is no path from an AsyncAPI document to a contract body — the loader never reads AsyncAPI documents, and nothing calls the adapter. A user who points Beadloom at a project described with AsyncAPI gets exactly nothing.

This is the house failure mode one level up: not a check reporting success for work it did not do, but DOCUMENTATION claiming a capability the product does not deliver. It survived a dev bead, a test bead, a review bead, a tech-writer bead and a green gate — because every one of those verified the FUNCTION, and none asked whether anything calls it.

Scope to decide:
  (a) wire it — loader reads a configured AsyncAPI document per service and feeds extract_payload_body into the contract body, closing the claim; or
  (b) correct the claim — mark it explicitly as an unwired building block until (a) ships.
(b) is honest but leaves BDL-060 S3 delivering less than its SPEC says, so (a) is the real close.

Related: this is why an 'island' check is worth having — a node with no first-party dependency in either direction, whose files nothing references. doctor's isolated_nodes check does not catch it, because part_of makes the node look connected. Measured on this repo, asyncapi is the ONLY true island (ai_agents/ai-techwriter are reached by subprocess, vitepress-site is not Python).

comments.text:
DEFERRED by owner 2026-08-20 — real but outranked; more important work first. Planned in .claude/development/ROADMAP.md under P1 -> '⏸ Deferred (planned, not scheduled) — wire the AsyncAPI ingestion path', with the implementation plan recorded so picking it up does not need re-discovery:

4. Determinism: an extracted body must serialize byte-stably through export -> federate, like an authored one.
5. Tests: end-to-end golden (AsyncAPI doc -> contract body -> BREAKING verdict), payload-less doc keeps name-level, two-run determinism, plus a guard that the adapter is reachable from a code path so it cannot become an island again.

Priority lowered P1 -> P2 to match the deferral: the adapter is inert, so nothing regresses while it waits. What is NOT deferred is the honesty of the claim.

title: [BDL-UX #158] No signal for a bounded context too large by SUBTREE — max_symbols now measures a node's own code only
description:
Fixing #144 changed what max_symbols means: it counts the symbols a node OWNS (nested nodes excluded) instead of everything under its path prefix. That is what makes the rule's own remedy work — carving a subpackage out now genuinely relieves the parent.

But the old metric carried a SECOND legitimate signal: 'this bounded context has grown too large overall'. A domain decomposed into many features owns very little and will never trip the rule however large its subtree becomes.

Measured on Beadloom after the fix: context-oracle, ai_agents and infrastructure own 0 symbols each (every file belongs to a component/feature node) while their subtrees hold 99, 108 and 63.

Two different questions were riding on one number:
  'is this node's own code too big?'      -> own count (the re-scoping prompt) — still expressible
  'is this bounded context too big?'      -> subtree count (the split-the-domain prompt) — now unmeasured

Proposed: a separate cardinality key rather than overloading max_symbols — max_subtree_symbols (all symbols under the node's source, the old semantics) and/or max_children (how many nodes are part_of it). Keeping them distinct is the point: a threshold that silently answers whichever question is convenient is how a metric stops meaning anything.

Deliberately NOT folded into the domain-size-limit threshold when it was recalibrated 290 -> 180 (BDL-060, 2026-08-19).

## Fix #58 (Threading error on quit)
- app.py: _shutting_down flag added as bool attribute, set in on_unmount() BEFORE worker.cancel() — correct ordering prevents race window
- file_watcher.py: getattr(app, '_shutting_down', False) check before post_message + try/except RuntimeError around post_message — double defense, both paths covered
- Thread safety: CPython bool read/write is atomic under GIL, sufficient for a flag pattern. No need for threading.Event here.
- Verdict: CORRECT, minimal, focused

## Fix #59 (Downstream dependents empty)
- dependency_path.py: _cached_text pattern pre-renders in show_downstream()/show_upstream() via _build_text(), render() returns cached snapshot
- set_provider() correctly invalidates cache (_cached_text = None) so next render recomputes

- Verdict: CORRECT, clean solution to Textual deferred-refresh race

## Fix #60 (Explorer broken after empty visit)
- explorer.py: on_screen_resume() checks app._selected_ref_id, calls set_ref_id() only when pending != current — prevents redundant reloads
- Guards: returns early when app is None or pending is empty
- action_switch_screen already calls set_ref_id; on_screen_resume is a safety net for edge cases — no double-load risk because of the != check
- Verdict: CORRECT, covers all navigation paths (dashboard->explorer, doc_status->explorer)

- 10+ new tests across 3 test classes (TestFileWatcherShutdownFlag, TestDependencyPathCacheConsistency, TestExplorerScreenResume)

- Test names are descriptive and map to specific scenarios

- Footer moved from App.compose to per-screen compose (DashboardScreen, ExplorerScreen, DocStatusScreen) — correct, each screen owns its Footer
- Custom action-bar Labels replaced with Textual Footer widget — consistent UX

All changes are minimal, focused, correctly implemented, and well-tested. No issues found.

title: [BDL-UX #164] The beads git-hook prints a remediation command that does not exist (`bd import -i`)
description:
After a merge that changes .beads/issues.jsonl, the hook prints:

  Warning: Failed to import bd changes after merge
  Run 'bd import -i .beads/issues.jsonl' manually to see the error

Running it prints the help text instead: bd 1.0.4's 'bd import' takes the file as a positional argument (or defaults to .beads/issues.jsonl), and has no '-i' flag.

Impact is small but the shape is the one this log keeps recording: a remediation string that reads authoritative and does not work, so the operator concludes something is wrong with their state rather than with the advice. Same family as #140 (sync-check told the operator to run a command that could not clear the condition).

Observed on the 2.2.0 release merge. State was actually consistent — jsonl held 15 open + 1 deferred and 'bd list' agreed — so the warning itself was also a false alarm, which makes the wrong command doubly misleading.

Fix: correct the hook's message to the real invocation, and only warn when the import genuinely failed rather than on any non-zero from the wrapper. Verify against the pinned bd version rather than assuming the flag set.

description: _format_markdown uses ### for chunk headers, but chunk content may also contain ### headings (from H3 in docs). This makes output visually confusing. Fix: use a different heading level (##) or separator format for chunk boundaries.
